articles.title: Vie privée, neutralité, DNS : voici ce qu'il reste des DNS publics en France
articles.text:
Quad9 a quitté ses activités en France cette semaine, comme OpenDNS en 2024. Google et DNS4EU appliquent des blocages, tandis que Cloudflare tient tête à Canal+. Voici ce qu’il reste des DNS publics.
Changer de DNS pour contourner le blocage d’un site pirate ne marche plus comme avant. Depuis 2024, la justice française impose la même restriction aux résolveurs publics.
Pourquoi les DNS publics sont dans le viseur
Tout a commencé avec les fournisseurs d’accès. Ils reçoivent des ordonnances de blocage depuis 2022, dans le cadre de l’injonction dynamique créée par la loi du 25 octobre 2021. Certains abonnés ont alors reconfiguré leurs appareils pour passer par les DNS de Cloudflare, Google ou Cisco. C’est donc vers ces derniers que s’est tourné Canal+. La chaîne de télévision se base sur l’article L.333-10 du Code du sport, lequel permet de demander un blocage à toute entité capable d’y contribuer, si les ayants droit prouvent une atteinte grave et répétée.
Le 27 mars, la cour d’appel de Paris a rejeté les cinq recours de Google, Cloudflare et Cisco. Pour elle, la neutralité d’un DNS n’y change rien, et si un filtrage peut être contourné, cela ne le rend pas inefficace. Les ordonnances sont dynamiques et l’Arcom peut valider de nouveaux domaines en cours de saison. Celles du 17 juillet, au nombre de quatorze, visent la Premier League et la Ligue des champions. Une loi adoptée quatre jours plus tard doit remplacer la vérification de l’Arcom par un processus automatisé, mais elle n’est pas encore appliquée.
Ceux qui sont partis
Cisco a retiré OpenDNS de France le 28 juin 2024, en citant une décision fondée sur l’article L.333-10.
Depuis le 24 novembre, l’adresse 9.9.9.9 ne répond plus depuis la France. La fondation suisse Quad9 avait annoncé son départ le 22 octobre, au lendemain d’un jugement du tribunal de Paris. Dans cette affaire lancée par beIN Sports contre des sites diffusant le tennis féminin (WTA), la liste de domaines à bloquer est passée de 6 à 58. Google et DNS4EU ont obtempéré, mais pas Quad9. Le tribunal a fixé l’astreinte à 1 000 euros par jour au total, jusqu’au 14 novembre, soit 24 000 euros au maximum selon la fondation. Si le montant reste limité, Quad9 met surtout en avant une question de principe. Elle a fait appel, mais explique ne pas pouvoir savoir de façon fiable si une requête vient de France, contrairement à Google et Cloudflare qui eux peuvent limiter un blocage à la France. Quad9 a donc décidé de retirer tous ses résolveurs du pays, avec ou sans filtrage des sites malveillants. La SNCF, EDF, France Travail et RENATER figuraient parmi ses utilisateurs. Une vingtaine d’autres procédures sont en cours contre elle et d’autres résolveurs.
Deux autres services sont partis, cette fois, sans pression judiciaire. Dns0.eu, un projet associatif français lancé en 2023 par les fondateurs de NextDNS, a fermé en octobre 2025. L’équipe invoquait un manque de temps et de ressources. Mullvad a fermé ses DNS publics chiffrés le 2 novembre, parce qu’il préférait soutenir Quad9 plutôt que de maintenir son propre résolveur. Mullvad Browser envoyait donc par défaut ses requêtes DNS à Quad9, et ses utilisateurs ont dû revoir leurs réglages.
Ceux qui appliquent les blocages : Google et DNS4EU
Lorsque l’on passe par le DNS de Google (8.8.8.8), les sites pirates visés par les ordonnances de juillet sur la Premier League sont inaccessibles. Le résolveur refuse de renvoyer leur adresse et invoque une injonction judiciaire. Sans adresse, le navigateur ne peut donc pas ouvrir le site. Le tribunal lui a aussi ordonné de bloquer 19 domaines pour la Ligue des champions.
Le cas de DNS4EU est un peu plus gênant. Ce résolveur cofinancé par la Commission européenne était présenté comme l’alternative souveraine à Google et Cloudflare. C’est aussi vers lui que l’équipe de dns0.eu avait orienté ses utilisateurs en fermant. Le tribunal de Paris lui a ordonné de bloquer 37 domaines le 17 avril, 21 pour la Formule 1 et 16 pour le MotoGP. Whalebone, la société tchèque qui l’exploite, ne s’est pas présentée à l’audience du 19 février, et le jugement a été rendu par défaut.
Cloudflare tient tête à Canal+
Depuis l’ordonnance de 2024, Cloudflare était déjà tenu de bloquer sur son résolveur 1.1.1.1 des sites pirates diffusant la Premier League et la Ligue des champions, comme Google et Cisco. Son appel a été rejeté en mars. Les ordonnances du 17 juillet vont plus loin. Elles lui demandent de bloquer ces sites sur son résolveur, mais aussi sur son CDN et son proxy inversé, en le laissant libre de choisir les moyens techniques.
L’entreprise affirme avoir bloqué au niveau de son CDN plutôt que sur 1.1.1.1, une méthode qu’elle juge bien plus efficace. Canal+ réclamait 50 000 euros d’astreinte par jour dans les dossiers Formule 1 et MotoGP. Le tribunal a refusé le 17 septembre. Il a rappelé que les intermédiaires techniques ont une obligation de moyens, pas de résultat. Si un site change de CDN, c’est à Canal+ de signaler les miroirs à l’Arcom.
En Belgique, une ordonnance prévoit des sanctions contre Cloudflare, Google et Cisco s’ils ne bloquent pas de domaines d’ici début janvier 2027. Les trois entreprises ont fait appel.
Vie privée et neutralité du net : ce que ça change
Dans un billet consacré au départ de Quad9, Cloudflare s’inquiète des conséquences. Le résolveur de Quad9 sert à des administrations, des établissements scolaires, des hôpitaux et des services publics, et la fondation n’a aucun moyen de les prévenir directement. Les équipements configurés à la main, comme des systèmes de sécurité ou des thermostats connectés, peuvent aussi perdre la résolution des noms de domaine. Par ailleurs, un blocage DNS touche le domaine entier, contenus légaux compris, sans explication pour l’internaute, et il se contourne en changeant de résolveur.
Cloudflare craint aussi que les internautes se replient sur le résolveur de leur fournisseur d’accès ou sur des services moins connus, aux pratiques de confidentialité parfois floues. Pour l’entreprise, il faudrait viser directement les hébergeurs des contenus. Quad9 redoute de son côté une multiplication des demandes, pour des motifs commerciaux, moraux, religieux ou politiques.
Côté neutralité du net, il y a une nuance juridique. Le règlement européen de 2015 sur l’internet ouvert impose des obligations de neutralité aux réseaux, et l’Arcep en surveille le respect. Mais cela vise d’abord les fournisseurs d’accès, pas des résolveurs comme Quad9, Google ou Cloudflare. Surtout, ce principe n’est pas absolu puisque le règlement prévoit des exceptions, sur lesquelles reposent d’ailleurs les blocages ordonnés par la loi ou la justice.
Quad9 défend alors la neutralité de la résolution DNS, c’est-à-dire en retournant des réponses identiques pour tous ses utilisateurs. Cloudflare y voit de son côté une menace pour l’Internet ouvert. Bien évidemment, les ayants droit ne voient pas les choses ainsi et ils ont la justice de leur côté. La cour d’appel juge ces mesures techniquement réalisables et proportionnées.
Reste à savoir jusqu’où cela ira. Une étude commandée cet été par la commission des affaires juridiques du Parlement européen recommande un cadre contraignant, avec des blocages en moins de 30 minutes qui viseraient aussi les DNS, les VPN et les CDN. Cette étude n’a aucune valeur législative à ce stade, et propose des garde-fous comme la proportionnalité, le recours, le contrôle d’un juge ou d’une autorité. Reste qu’il devient alors facile de faire des bourdes avec le surblocage. En Italie, avec le Piracy Shield, un sous-domaine de Google signalé par erreur a rendu Google Drive inaccessible pendant plusieurs heures en octobre 2024.
Quel DNS choisir ?
Si vous utilisez encore Quad9 sur un ordinateur, un smartphone ou une box, il faut le remplacer, sans quoi certains sites risquent de ne plus se charger. Au-delà du navigateur et des applications, il faut aussi penser aux équipements qui ont leur propre réglage.
Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) répond normalement pour l’instant, mais reste donc dans le collimateur de Canal+. Google (8.8.8.8) applique les blocages, DNS4EU aussi dans le dossier beIN.
Trois services ne figurent, à notre connaissance, dans aucune décision française. À commencer par FDN, association française, également fournisseur d’accès à Internet. FDN propose des DNS gratuits (80.67.169.12 et 80.67.169.40) et défend la neutralité du net comme la vie privée de ses utilisateurs. De son côté, NextDNS peut être personnalisé par profil, avec filtrage et journaux réglables, et l’utilisateur peut choisir de ne rien enregistrer. Son service public en DNS-over-HTTPS suit par défaut une politique sans journalisation. C’est l’autre alternative que l’équipe de dns0.eu recommandait en fermant, et il est développé par les mêmes fondateurs. Pour sa part, Comodo Secure DNS (8.26.56.26 et 8.20.247.20) mise sur la sécurité. Il bloque les sites dangereux et protège contre les malwares grâce à ses renseignements sur les menaces. Cette absence d’injonction peut toutefois changer vite, la liste des résolveurs visés s’allongeant depuis 2024.
Un VPN dont le DNS interne traite vos requêtes dans le tunnel chiffré évite aussi de dépendre d’un résolveur public, mais les VPN sont eux aussi visés. Un jugement de mai 2025 les a obligés à bloquer environ 200 domaines.

articles.title: Save up to 36% on a some of the best PC speakers we've reviewed — deals starting at just $26 from AudioEngine, Creative, Edifier, and more
articles.text:
Save up to 36% on a some of the best PC speakers we've reviewed — deals starting at just $26 from AudioEngine, Creative, Edifier, and more
Upgrade your audio setup with a bit of savings.
If you want to upgrade your PC setup without paying high prices for new components, the best PC speakers, provide a tangible upgrade that isn't running at triple the typical price. Many of the sets we've reviewed are on sale for Black Friday, and we've tracked down five of the best deals on speakers we've tested, some of which are among the best we've tested on the market.
We're focused on typical 2.0 stereo speakers here, though some of the options include a subwoofer output so you can configure a 2.1 setup in the future. Although surround sound sets and soundbars are available as PC speakers, we weren't impressed with the deals available.
One of the best desktop speakers we've tested, now updated with USB-C and aptX Adaptive, aptX HD, aptX, AAC, and SBC for stellar wireless connectivity up to 100 feet, these are an excellent audio upgrade for any desk.
Read moreRead less▼
We've recommended the AudioEngine A2+ speakers for years, and the newer A2 GEN3 speakers only make them better. As usual, these speakers feature a 2.75-inch woofer and 0.75-inch tweeter, and they're among the best-sounding speakers in this class. They're expensive at $300, and even during shopping events, they don't always go on sale. That's what makes the 25% discount during Black Friday so attractive.
Although the cabinet and speakers remain unchanged, there are some updates under the hood. The GEN3 speakers support Bluetooth 5.3, adding support for various aptX codecs, and it uses a Class D amplifier, which should help the speakers run cooler. AudioEngine also swapped out the micro-USB port on the original speakers for a USB-C port.
The Creative Labs Pebble V2 is a set of stereo speakers that connect to your PC via USB and feature a minimalist design.
Read moreRead less▼
The Creative Labs Pebble V2 speakers are a go-to recommendation for cheap PC speakers here at Tom's Hardware, and for good reason. As you can read about in our review of the larger Creative Pebble Pro speakers, this range offers plenty of headroom, providing clean sound at higher volumes despite the tiny woofer size (just two inches). Like many Bluetooth speakers, the Pebble V2 set features passive radiators, capturing low-end frequencies to give the impression of a subwoofer. Of course, it's not the same as a subwoofer, but passive bass chambers help a lot with these smaller speakers.
You connect the speakers over a 3.5mm cable for audio, and power them with USB-C (the speakers call for a 10W port). Sustained RMS power is just 8W for the speakers, but they can peak a bit higher at 16W. They run lower by default, but a high-gain switch on the back will kick the power amp into full gear if you need the speakers louder.
The G2000 speakers from Edifier come with a peak power raing of 32W and a frequency response of 98 Hz up to 22 kHz, along with analog and Bluetooth connections.
Read moreRead less▼
The Edifer G2000 speakers double the power output of the Pebble V2's, and they feature larger 2.75-inch drivers (though no tweeter). At $80 on sale, they're much more expensive, but Edifier justifies the extra price with USB and Bluetooth output, alongside a standard 3.5mm connection, as well as a dedicated power adapter to avoid unwanted noise over USB power. If you want to expand your setup, there's also a subwoofer output.
RMS power here is 16W, giving you significantly more headroom at higher volumes to avoid any distortion. The 2.75-inch full range drivers offers decent low-end, though the frequency response cuts off just below 100 Hz, leaving precious sub-region frequencies out of the sonic picture. That gives you a good cutoff point to add a subwoofer, however.
The Edifier M60 speakers feature a 3-inch woofer and 1-inch tweeter, as well as 66W of total output across the four drivers.
Read moreRead less▼
Edifer's M60 speakers are larger, and they take some obvious notes from Audioengine. They're not quite the same as the A2+ speakers, however. The M60s feature a 3-inch woofer and 1-inch tweeter, with an average RMS of 66W across all four drivers (18W each for the woofers, and 15W for the tweeters).
The speakers come with a Hi-Res audio certification, extending the frequency response up from the typical 20 kHz to 40 kHz. Although the human ear typically can't hear about 20 kHz, extra harmonic information down in the audible range of frequencies can add richness to the sound. articles.title: Justiça condena oito pessoas por pirataria da Sky
articles.text:
Justiça condena oito pessoas por pirataria da Sky
Maior pena passou dos 15 anos de prisão. Grupo vendia receptores e chaves para liberar canais via satélite.
A Justiça Federal condenou oito pessoas envolvidas em um esquema que vendia receptores de TV via satélite e chaves para liberar canais pagos sem autorização. O grupo atuou entre 2013 e 2017, com fornecedores no Paraguai e revendedores em Porto Alegre. A Sky participou do processo como assistente de acusação.
A sentença foi assinada em 10 de novembro pelo juiz federal Lademiro Dors Filho, da 7ª Vara Federal de Porto Alegre. Todos os condenados poderão recorrer em liberdade. O chefe do núcleo fornecedor no Paraguai recebeu a maior pena: 15 anos, três meses e 20 dias de prisão, em regime inicial fechado.
O esquema utilizava o card sharing, ou compartilhamento de chaves. Segundo explicações da Sky anexadas ao processo, os decodificadores oficiais usam cartões criptográficos para liberar a programação transmitida via satélite. Na modalidade de pirataria, dados de cartões legítimos são copiados e distribuídos pela internet a vários usuários. Além dos aparelhos, o grupo oferecia suporte para renovar o acesso à programação.
As defesas sustentaram que os aparelhos eram receptores de canais abertos e questionaram sua capacidade de captar programação paga. O juiz considerou que o contrabando estava demonstrado pela entrada clandestina dos equipamentos sem homologação da Anatel. Já a venda de acesso aos canais foi comprovada por diálogos interceptados, códigos comercializados e depoimentos.
Os fornecedores mantinham uma empresa no Paraguai e abasteciam dois núcleos de revenda em Porto Alegre. Os receptores também entravam no Brasil sem documentação fiscal em remessas semanais ou quinzenais.
A sentença reconheceu 117 entradas clandestinas de mercadorias: 59 destinadas à Aztime e 58 à Azmegashop. Em um dos depósitos, a Polícia Federal apreendeu 446 receptores, além de planilhas de estoque, códigos de acesso e registros de vendas.
Os oito réus foram condenados por organização criminosa e contrabando. Os líderes dos núcleos também receberam penas por violação de direito autoral e estelionato. Três integrantes também foram punidos por lavagem de dinheiro: dois do núcleo fornecedor no Paraguai e o responsável pela Azmegashop.
As defesas negaram a existência de uma organização estruturada e sustentaram que os acusados mantinham relações comerciais ou profissionais. Os pedidos de absolvição dos oito condenados foram rejeitados e outros dois acusados foram absolvidos por falta de provas.
A decisão também determinou multas e a perda de bens e valores ligados aos crimes em favor da União. O juiz não fixou indenização mínima e os prejuízos das operadoras não foram estimados durante o processo. As empresas ainda poderão buscar compensação na Justiça cível.
A condenação ainda pode ser revista em segunda instância. A consulta ao processo registra apelações apresentadas em 23 de novembro. Esses recursos permitem pedir ao Tribunal Regional Federal da 4ª Região (TRF4) a revisão da sentença.
Em outro caso, divulgado em junho, dois irmãos receberam penas de nove anos e dois meses por operarem um serviço de IPTV pirata em Goiás.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Two GeoServer Flaws as Researchers Warn of Unauthenticated RCE Chains
articles.text:
Threat actors are actively exploiting two newly patched security flaws in GeoServer, according to watchTowr.
The vulnerabilities in question are CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243, details of which are below -
- CVE-2026-120705 (CVSS score: 8.6) - An arbitrary file read vulnerability that could enable an attacker to access local text files readable by the GeoServer process or fetch adversary-selected HTTP or HTTPS URLs by means of a single unauthenticated Web Feature Service (WFS) request.
- CVE-2026-129243 (CVSS score: 8.8) - An incorrect authorization vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to invoke OWS operations that are otherwise protected by service security rules.
Advisories for both the flaws were published on November 24, 2026, in the following versions -
- CVE-2026-120705: org.geoserver:gs-wfs-core - 3.0.2, 2.28.6, and 2.27.7
- CVE-2026-120705: org.geotools:gt-metadata - 35.2, 34.6, and 33.7
- CVE-2026-129243: org.geoserver:gs-ows - 3.0.2, 2.28.6, and 2.27.7
"Attackers sent error-based exploit probes to validate that the server is vulnerable by creating and invoking stored queries," the preemptive exposure management firm said in an X post today.
Yordan Ganchev, principal threat intelligence specialist at watchTowr, said the vulnerabilities can allow attackers to bypass security restrictions, interact with internal services, retrieve stored secrets, forge authentication credentials, and deserialize and run code on affected systems.
"On November 25, we observed in-the-wild exploitation against our global honeypot network in the early morning hours leveraging CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129244," Ganchev said. "Threat actors from multiple IP addresses were observed validating vulnerable systems on the internet by creating stored queries on GeoServer machines, checking whether they were created, and deleting them immediately afterward."
Eye Security, which discovered and reported CVE-2026-120705, said the flaw can be combined with two other vulnerabilities in the same product to create an unauthenticated remote code execution chain -
- CVE-2026-129245 (CVSS score: 9.2) - A use of a hard-coded signing key ("geoserver") vulnerability in the "remember me" functionality that could be exploited to forge administrator authentication. (Fixed in org.geoserver:gs-main versions 3.0.2, 2.28.6, and 2.27.7)
- CVE-2026-120704 (CVSS score: 7.2) - An improper control of the generation of code vulnerability that could allow an administrator, or anyone with access to an administrator session, to execute arbitrary code as the user running GeoServer. (Fixed in org.geoserver.security:gs-sec-jdbc versions 3.0.2, 2.28.6, and 2.27.7)
In a hypothetical attack chain, a bad actor can follow the steps below -
- Exploit CVE-2026-120705 to access "users.xml," a file containing GeoServer usernames and password hashes, and obtain the password representation along with the static signing key extracted from the security configuration ("security/config.xml").
- Exploit CVE-2026-129245 to forge a valid administrator authentication cookie by using the predictable signing key and the stored password representation without having to know the administrator password.
- Exploit CVE-2026-120704 to abuse an administrator-controlled JDBC configuration to execute code from an uploaded native library on both Linux and Windows versions of GeoServer.
According to the project maintainers, CVE-2026-129245 is also part of a five-step unauthenticated remote command execution chain that involves -
- CVE-2026-129244 (CVSS score: 6.9) - WFS stored query exception discloses data directory path
- CVE-2026-129243 (CVSS score: 8.8) - Service security rules bypassed with a prefixed service name such as x/WFS
- CVE-2026-120705 (CVSS score: 8.6) - Unauthenticated WFS GetFeatureById XML injection
- CVE-2026-129245 (CVSS score: 9.2) - Predictable "remember me" key allows administrator session forgery
- CVE-2026-129242 (CVSS score: 8.6) - Deserialization in JDBC user and role services allows administrator code execution
"An attacker who obtains an administrator password digest, through any file disclosure or a copy of the data directory, can log in as that administrator," GeoServer maintainers said. "Changing the key in security/config.xml does not help when the same file disclosure also reveals the key."
Jonah Burgess, a Senior Security Researcher at Rapid7, who goes by the online alias CryptoCat has been acknowledged for independently discovering and reporting the five-step unauthenticated remote command execution chain on August 2, 2026.
"Prefixing the Web Feature Service (WFS) name, as in x/WFS, slips past the admin-only rule for stored queries. GeoServer turns escaped text in a saved query into live xi:include elements, which leaks the files holding the remember-me key and the admin password digest," the researcher said.
"Those two values forge an administrator cookie without cracking the password. As admin, the attacker points a JDBC user service at an uploaded HSQLDB database, and the bundled driver deserialises a stored value that runs commands."
In light of active exploitation of two of the flaws, users are advised to update to GeoServer versions 2.27.7, 2.28.6, and 3.0.2 released over the past month as soon as possible.
The development comes a little over three months after another critical flaw in GeoServer (CVE-2026-76904, CVSS score: 9.8) witnessed active exploitation efforts as a zero-day.
"Organizations running publicly exposed GeoServer instances should prioritize patching them as soon as possible," Ganchev said. "Any exposed systems should be audited for signs of credentials leaking, unauthorized access and code execution on the host. Where patching is not immediately possible, restrict access to the host."
(The story has been updated after publication to include more details of the flaws and emphasize that advisories for the issues were released on November 24, 2026. The patches were originally released in October and early November 2026.)

articles.title: The lowest priced RAM in 2026 — price tracking on DDR5 and DDR4 memory of all capacities
articles.text:
The lowest priced RAM in 2026 — price tracking on DDR5 and DDR4 memory of all capacities
Check the best prices on DDR5 and DDR4 memory kits.
In today's market, memory has become one of the most critical and expensive components in any build, and prices have only worsened thanks to the ongoing global DRAM shortage. We're keeping an eye on the volatile memory pricing to help identify any good deals that may arise.
Now, even more so than before the shortage began, price tags are fluctuating significantly from day to day, and it's becoming increasingly complex to tell when you're getting a fair deal versus overpaying for the same memory kit. We've compiled this comprehensive RAM price tracker that monitors the availability and pricing of different DDR5 and DDR4 memory kits across major U.S. retailers. Our goal is to take the guesswork out of memory shopping and help you make an informed purchasing decision.
We update this index regularly with the lowest prices available in the U.S. market for each memory kit. Our tracker covers a range of capacities and speeds across both budget and premium brands. We list the lowest price for each available memory kit, regardless of manufacturer, so you see the absolute best deals currently on offer.
The general availability of many memory kits is limited, with truly exceptional deals scarce and often selling out within seconds of appearing. High-capacity kits, particularly DDR5, frequently show the most severe stock shortages and price premiums. articles.title: Typing 365 Turns PC Building, Technology and More into Typing Practice
articles.text:
Thursday, November 26th 2026
Typing 365 Turns PC Building, Technology and More into Typing Practice
Typing faster is useful, but what if practice could also teach you something? Typing 365 is a free native Windows app that combines structured typing lessons, educational content, and competitive challenges.
With over 100,000 installs and nearly 4 million typing races completed worldwide, Typing 365 has grown into more than a speed test. Its Albums Store offers themed collections covering technology, science, history, psychology, and more.Build Your PC: A Free Album for First-Time Builders
The new Build Your PC album features 40 free typing exercises about desktop hardware. It covers motherboards, component compatibility, assembly, first boot, operating system installation, and troubleshooting.
Here's the idea in practice: instead of just reading a guide, you type passages such as "Before buying a CPU, check that its socket matches your motherboard and that the board's BIOS supports it." By the end of the album, you've practiced thousands of keystrokes while picking up the fundamentals of building a PC.
You might already know your way around a PC case, but it's an easy recommendation for students, first-time builders, or that friend whose build you always end up helping with.
Why a Native Windows App?
Browser-based typing sites are great for a quick test. Typing 365 is designed for consistent practice, combining a dedicated Windows experience with structured courses, progress tracking, and detailed performance statistics.
Beginners can start with Typing 101, a free course that gradually introduces keys before moving on to complete sentences. Other courses cover keyboard rows, punctuation, and speed development.
During practice, an on-screen keyboard and optional hand guidance support finger placement. The app tracks words per minute (WPM), characters per minute (CPM), accuracy, and mistakes. You can also turn your own notes or technical material into typing exercises.Find Your Weak Spots with PRO Analytics
The free app offers plenty of practice material, while Typing 365 PRO adds detailed analytics for users who want to improve their skills. View speed trends, session history, and keyboard heatmaps, or identify slow words, characters, and letter pairs for targeted practice.
PRO also unlocks exclusive albums, advanced courses such as Typing 102, which focuses on building typing speed, plus additional fonts, keyboard sounds, avatars, and customization options.
PRO is available through a monthly subscription or a one-time lifetime purchase, with US pricing starting at $2.99/month or $29.99 lifetime. Prices may vary by region.
Race Against Other Typists
Prefer competition? Join ranked typing races, compare your results with other players, and climb the global leaderboards. Whether you're chasing a personal best or a higher rank, every race offers a new challenge.
Practice in Five Languages
Typing 365 supports English, German, Spanish, Russian, and Arabic, allowing users to practice across languages and keyboard layouts.
From learning keyboard basics to understanding how a PC comes together, Typing 365 turns everyday practice into something worth your time.
Download Typing 365 for free from the Microsoft Store and start typing.
Typing 365 is available for Windows PCs, with optional premium albums and PRO features.

articles.title: Steam suma 5 nuevos juegos gratis que puedes conservar para siempre
articles.text:
Steam incorpora cinco nuevos juegos gratis a su catálogo: Card Dice, The Temple, Lavender’s The One Stop Potion Shop, Amber Eyes y Might & Magic Fates TCG.
Los cinco títulos figuran como Free to Play en Steam y tienen fecha de lanzamiento reciente, según sus respectivas fichas en la plataforma.
La selección incluye propuestas de cartas, terror, simulación y novela visual. Cada juego presenta mecánicas y ambientaciones diferentes, desde duelos con dados hasta la gestión de una tienda de pociones.
Cuáles son los nuevos juegos de Steam
Card Dice es un juego de progresión con temática de casino. Los jugadores lanzan dados, compiten en duelos y reúnen gemas y grabados para crear distintas configuraciones, mejorar su equipo y avanzar hacia mesas de mayor nivel.
En The Temple, la propuesta se traslada a un planeta abandonado en un futuro lejano. El jugador puede recorrer el mar, el cielo y el espacio mientras evita peligros y busca descubrir la verdad en una aventura de terror cósmico que dura alrededor de dos horas.
Lavender’s The One Stop Potion Shop es un juego de simulación centrado en la administración de una tienda de pociones. La misión consiste en preparar brebajes mágicos para una variedad de personajes.
Por su parte, Amber Eyes es una novela visual ambientada en la Ciudad Libre de Danzig durante la década de 1930. La historia sigue a un taxista polaco enamorado de un alemán, en un relato atravesado por la nacionalidad, el prejuicio y el amor prohibido.
Finalmente, Might & Magic Fates TCG propone partidas de cartas estratégicas. Los jugadores lideran héroes, invocan criaturas, lanzan hechizos y construyen mazos para enfrentarse en combates tácticos.
Cómo acceder a estos juegos de Steam
Para obtenerlos, los usuarios deben ingresar a Steam y buscar los nombres de los cinco títulos: Card Dice, The Temple, Lavender’s The One Stop Potion Shop, Amber Eyes y Might & Magic Fates TCG.
En la ficha de cada juego aparece la opción Free to Play, que permite incorporarlo a la biblioteca sin costo de descarga.
Una vez añadidos, los juegos podrán instalarse desde la biblioteca de Steam en una computadora compatible.
CEO de Epic Games arremete contra los dueños de Steam
Tim Sweeney, CEO de Epic Games, reavivó su enfrentamiento con Valve, la compañía responsable de Steam, al acusarla de haber frenado durante años la expansión de la industria de videojuegos para PC.
El directivo cuestionó el modelo de la plataforma y defendió la necesidad de construir un ecosistema más abierto, con mayor comunicación entre usuarios y desarrolladores de distintas plataformas.
La controversia comenzó después de que Kiaran Ritchie, exprogramador principal de animación de Epic Games, criticara en X la comisión del 30% que Valve aplica sobre muchas de las ventas realizadas en Steam.
Ritchie consideró que sería posible crear una alternativa a la tienda, aunque admitió que Steam cuenta con una ventaja difícil de superar: la enorme cantidad de usuarios y sus bibliotecas digitales acumuladas durante años.
Sweeney respaldó esa postura y sostuvo que Valve mantiene los juegos de PC dentro de un sistema social que dificulta el vínculo entre jugadores de consolas, computadoras y dispositivos móviles.
Para el ejecutivo, los estudios deberían poder colaborar y conectar sus títulos sin depender de una única plataforma de distribución.
El CEO de Epic Games también planteó la posibilidad de que objetos o contenidos adquiridos en un juego puedan usarse en otros, como parte de una mayor interoperabilidad entre producciones. La empresa prevé explorar estas opciones con Unreal Engine 6.
Sus declaraciones generaron respuestas de usuarios que señalaron que numerosos estudios emplean Steamworks, las herramientas de Valve para publicar y gestionar juegos, incluso cuando sus lanzamientos también llegan a otras plataformas.
Sweeney rechazó esa comparación y aclaró que su crítica no estaba dirigida a las herramientas técnicas, sino a las funciones sociales y de comunicación entre comunidades.

articles.title: Europe's Mercury mission just suffered another thruster glitch at the finish line
articles.text:
The latest ESA mission to Mercury was nearly derailed by a last-minute 'software issue'
Europe and Japan's twin-probe spacecraft enter Mercury orbit
- BepiColombo reached Mercury despite an unexpected interruption during its orbital insertion
- A software malfunction shortened the spacecraft's planned propulsion operation
- Engineers are investigating the incident, but the spacecraft remains safe
Europe's latest spacecraft mission to Mercury has successfully reached its destination, although an unexpected computer problem complicated its orbital arrival.
The BepiColombo spacecraft, jointly developed by European and Japanese space agencies, experienced an unexpectedly shortened engine operation during its final approach.
Although the vehicle remains safe, investigators are examining the incident before its scientific operations can proceed as originally anticipated.
A software malfunction complicates BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury
The European Space Agency (ESA) confirmed the spacecraft entered Mercury's orbit after completing an exceptionally demanding journey through the inner solar system.
However, the agency subsequently disclosed that an onboard software problem interrupted the planned duration of an important propulsion operation during orbital insertion.
“The thruster burn was shorter than planned following a software issue,” said the European Space Agency in its initial statement.
The organization also confirmed that the spacecraft remained safe while engineers began examining the circumstances surrounding the unexpected interruption.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Reaching Mercury requires complex orbital maneuvers because the planet orbits the Sun rapidly, making direct spacecraft arrival particularly challenging.
BepiColombo therefore followed an extended trajectory involving one Earth encounter, two Venus encounters and six separate passages around Mercury.
These gravitational encounters helped reduce the spacecraft's speed sufficiently for eventual capture while accommodating the planet's unusually demanding orbital characteristics.
The mission had already encountered propulsion difficulties in 2024, when weaker-than-expected engine performance forced engineers to revise its planned flight trajectory.
That earlier complication also pushed the anticipated arrival from mid-2025 to November 2026, requiring additional adjustments to the mission schedule.
Two orbiters will investigate Mercury's unusual environment
BepiColombo carries two scientific spacecraft designed to investigate different characteristics of Mercury, including its internal structure, magnetic environment and surrounding particles.
ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) will examine surface materials, internal composition and magnetic conditions while collecting measurements for scientific investigations.
Researchers also intend to examine its gravitational effects, potentially providing unusually precise tests of Einstein's General Relativity predictions.
Japan's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MIO) will concentrate on studying the planet's magnetic environment, surrounding plasma, atmospheric material and interplanetary dust.
Both spacecraft face substantial engineering challenges because Mercury receives approximately ten times the sunlight reaching Earth, generating intense thermal exposure.
The Japanese orbiter relies on solar energy, while protective engineering helps the European spacecraft withstand heat radiating from Mercury's extremely hot surface.
ESA's thermal protection incorporates three to four multilayer blankets containing titanium, aluminum, and specialized Nextel ceramic fabric, collectively weighing 94 kilograms.
Scientific investigations are expected to begin in April 2027, although the agencies have not confirmed whether both orbiters currently meet every operational requirement.
Previous spacecraft visits produced important discoveries, including Mariner 10's observations in three encounters across 1974 and 1975, which covered less than half of Mercury's surface.
NASA's MESSENGER spacecraft subsequently entered Mercury's orbit in 2011, remaining there for more than four years before deliberately crashing onto its surface.
That mission mapped the entire planet and identified water ice near polar regions, providing discoveries unavailable through earlier spacecraft observations.
Via The Register

articles.title: U.S. Treasury's Financial Crimes Agency Takes Some Systems Offline After Cyber Intrusion
articles.text:
The U.S. Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has been hit by a cybersecurity incident that resulted in "unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems," the bureau said on Tuesday. As a precaution, it has taken some systems offline.
The bureau collects suspicious activity reports and other Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) filings from banks and other financial institutions and analyzes them to fight money laundering and terrorist financing.
The BSA E-Filing website is still up, although some services may be temporarily unavailable. The agency has not named the systems it reached or those it took offline.
To support filers affected by the disruption, the bureau is extending some filing deadlines: covered reports originally due between November 18 and December 29 can now be submitted until December 30.
A relief order issued the same day, FIN-2026-R002, applies to three groups:
- Financial institutions that used Secure Direct Transfer Mode (SDTM), the channel for sending batches of BSA reports directly from their own servers, as of November 18
- Companies required to file a beneficial ownership information report during the covered window
- Individuals required to update a FinCEN Identifier during the same window
All other Bank Secrecy Act obligations stay in force, including the duty to monitor for suspicious transactions. The service alert says urgent suspicious activity information can still reach law enforcement through the Financial Institutions Hotline, 1-866-556-3974, which is not affected by the disruption.
The disclosure followed days of filing trouble. Filing providers reported failures in automated batch submissions beginning November 18, and the bureau posted a notice about the disruption to SDTM late last week, according to a filing outages report by the markets news site The Deep Dive.
The bureau has not said whether the intrusion caused those outages. The order grants the relief because of a "service disruption" and does not mention the cybersecurity incident.
Nor has the agency said when the access began, whether any data was viewed or taken, or who was responsible. No group has publicly claimed the intrusion so far. Those answers matter because of what the bureau holds: reports of suspicious financial activity filed by financial institutions nationwide.
The incident is not Treasury's first in recent years: in December 2024, a China-linked group used a compromised BeyondTrust API key in an earlier Treasury breach that reached department systems and documents. No link between the two incidents has been reported.

articles.title: ATK Reveals Hex 80 V2 Hall Effect Gaming Keyboard in Collaboration with Qwertykeys
articles.text:
Thursday, November 26th 2026
ATK Reveals Hex 80 V2 Hall Effect Gaming Keyboard in Collaboration with Qwertykeys
The original ATK × Qwertykeys Hex 80 was something of a watershed moment for the Hall effect keyboard market, marking the first major collaboration between a premium mechanical keyboard maker and a gaming brand that played to the strong suits of both sides, delivering a keyboard that delivered gaming performance and the high-end build quality and feel of a Qwertykeys keyboard. The two brands have come together again to make an updated version of that same TKL keyboard, the Hex 80 V2. It features the same TKL layout with updated internals. 
ATK appears to be using a very slightly modified version of the CNC aluminium chassis of the original Hex 80 for the V2, so most of the updates are to the internals—this means that owners of the original Hex 80 shouldn't feel obligated to upgrade to the new version. The new internals feature an updated MCU, delivering a PCB scan rate of 600 kHz, compared to the previous version's 32 kHz. The Hex 80 v2 has a claimed end-to-end latency of as little as 0.28 ms. There is also now the option of the semi-transparent Silver Regent switches alongside the OwLab Ti switch—a choice that will mostly be aesthetics, allowing the keyboard backlighting to shine through the translucent keycaps. There are four different color variants of the Hex 80 V2, this time all anodized aluminium, instead of the e-coating.The ATK Hex 80 V2 will launch on November 26 with a retail price of $249.98 and a limited launch price of $199.98. For that price, ATK equips the Hex 80 with translucent polycarbonate keycaps UV-printed lettering and a soft-touch coating. The keyboard's case is also gasket mounted, and it has a carbon fiber switch plate.As with the previous version, the ATK Hex 80 V2 will be wired only, and it will have a polling rate of 8,000 mAh. It will, as is expected for a Hall effect keyboard, be fully customizable and remappable, and it will have support for adjustable actuation, rapid trigger, SOCD, among others, all in the ATK Hub web driver utility. ATK claims that the Hex 80 supports actuation distance customization in steps as small as 0.001 mm. It also comes with its own custom carrying case.
Source:
				ATK Gear			
	
	
	
		
	
		
2 Comments on ATK Reveals Hex 80 V2 Hall Effect Gaming Keyboard in Collaboration with Qwertykeys
You may have been confused while writing the article. I expect "8kHz" polling rate and it has no battery since it's wired-only.
Can't go wrong with Owlab Ti switches but it's 80%, they still have 20% to go for me. If they ever do that it will surpass Wooting's outdated offering of Two HE. Sadly it will probably still be priced very closely to it (ironically with higher build quality and materials).
Wooting should really feel threatened by brands like ATK and MChose because they really stepped their game up with these HE keyboards.

articles.title: Windows 11 : trop gourmandes en RAM, trois applications imposées par Microsoft vont disparaître
articles.text:
Un an après avoir commencé à installer trois nouvelles applications de productivité sur les PC professionnels équipés de Windows 11, Microsoft s'apprête à s'en débarrasser. L'entreprise reconnaît aujourd'hui que les services rendus ne justifiaient pas leur consommation de mémoire vive.
Microsoft poursuit son opération de dégraissage de Windows 11. Alors que l'entreprise s'est récemment félicitée d'avoir réduit de plus de 860 Mo la consommation de RAM de plusieurs de ses logiciels, d'autres n'auront pas droit au même traitement. Interrogée par l'un de ses clients lors de sa conférence Ignite 2026, la firme de Redmond a expliqué pourquoi elle avait décidé de se séparer des Microsoft 365 Companion Apps, dont elle avait pourtant organisé le déploiement automatique un peu plus d'un an auparavant.
Trois applications dont Windows 11 aurait bien pu se passer
À l'époque, Microsoft entendait faciliter l'accès aux ressources professionnelles depuis la barre des tâches de Windows 11. Baptisées People, Files et Calendar, ces trois applications permettaient de retrouver des contacts, de rechercher et de partager des documents ou encore de consulter son agenda sans avoir à ouvrir Outlook, Teams ou OneDrive. L'entreprise en avait aussi profité pour multiplier les points d'accès à Copilot, quitte à faire cohabiter plusieurs logiciels aux fonctionnalités redondantes.
Or, derrière ces petites interfaces se cachaient des applications reposant sur WebView2, une technologie qui s'appuie sur le moteur de rendu web de Microsoft Edge. D'après les mesures effectuées par Windows Latest, leur consommation de mémoire vive pouvait dépasser le gigaoctet. Et de fait, sans avancer de chiffre, Microsoft a reconnu lors de l'Ignite que ces applications mobilisaient beaucoup de mémoire et posaient divers problèmes techniques, pour un bénéfice fonctionnel qui ne justifiait pas un tel coût.
L'entreprise, qui avait acté leur abandon dès septembre dernier, invite désormais les services informatiques à désinstaller les trois logiciels avant leur mise hors service le 16 décembre prochain. Une opération sans incidence sur les données et les fonctionnalités de Microsoft 365, puisque les informations auxquelles ils donnaient accès peuvent toujours être consultées depuis les applications existantes, à savoir Outlook, Teams, OneDrive et SharePoint.

articles.title: Black Friday 2026 sin estafas: 5 ajustes que debes hacer en el celular antes de comprar
articles.text:
El Black Friday 2026 llega este viernes 27 de noviembre con una advertencia para quienes concentran sus compras en el celular: los ciberdelincuentes perfeccionaron sus métodos y ahora combinan tiendas clonadas con inteligencia artificial, anuncios patrocinados falsos y mensajes de texto que simulan problemas con la entrega de paquetes.
Antes de buscar ofertas, configurar cinco ajustes básicos en el teléfono puede reducir al mínimo el riesgo de fraude digital. La mayoría de las transacciones de esta jornada de descuentos ya se concretan desde dispositivos móviles, un dato que no pasa inadvertido para quienes diseñan estafas.
El sentido común sigue siendo una herramienta clave para evitar caer en engaños, pero no es la única disponible: los propios teléfonos cuentan con funciones integradas que operan como una barrera automática frente a intentos de robo de datos.
Actualizaciones de software: el primer filtro de seguridad
Una de las puertas de entrada más comunes para los ataques son las versiones desactualizadas de los sistemas operativos. Android, iOS y navegadores como Chrome o Safari acumulan fallas de seguridad que, una vez conocidas, quedan expuestas si no se instalan los parches correspondientes.
Revisar que no existan actualizaciones pendientes es el primer paso. Esto se hace desde el apartado de actualización de software del teléfono. Después conviene entrar a la tienda de aplicaciones, ya sea Play Store o App Store, para actualizar tanto el navegador como las aplicaciones bancarias que se usarán durante las compras.
Un sitio malicioso puede aprovechar una versión antigua de un navegador para robar datos de sesión sin que el usuario lo note. Mantener el sistema al día cierra ese margen de exposición antes de que comience la cacería de descuentos.
Cómo detectar tiendas falsas y bloquear apps maliciosas
Las páginas clonadas suelen imitar dominios casi idénticos a los de tiendas reconocidas, con diferencias mínimas que pasan desapercibidas a simple vista. Los navegadores modernos incluyen funciones capaces de detectar y bloquear estos sitios antes de que terminen de cargar, aunque solo si están activadas.
En Chrome, la opción se encuentra en el menú de privacidad y seguridad, dentro de navegación segura, donde debe seleccionarse la protección mejorada. En Safari, disponible en iPhone, el ajuste equivalente es el aviso de sitio web fraudulento, ubicado en la configuración de la aplicación.
A esto se suma otra amenaza frecuente en esta temporada: mensajes de texto o de WhatsApp que alertan sobre un paquete retenido y piden descargar una supuesta app de rastreo. Ese archivo, en realidad, suele estar diseñado para leer códigos bancarios.
En Android conviene revisar el acceso especial para instalar aplicaciones desconocidas y confirmar que navegadores y apps de mensajería tengan ese permiso desactivado. En iPhone, el sistema bloquea instalaciones externas por defecto, aunque es recomendable verificar que no haya perfiles desconocidos instalados en la gestión de dispositivos.
Alertas bancarias y tarjetas virtuales para blindar cada pago
Incluso con todas las precauciones, existe la posibilidad de ingresar datos en una página fraudulenta. En ese escenario, la diferencia entre un susto menor y una cuenta vacía depende de la velocidad de reacción y de evitar exponer la tarjeta física principal.
Activar las notificaciones push instantáneas para cada consumo, sin importar el monto, permite detectar movimientos sospechosos apenas ocurren. A esto se suma la posibilidad de configurar un límite diario de compras por internet acorde al presupuesto previsto para la jornada.
Cuando el banco lo permite, generar una tarjeta virtual o un CVV dinámico exclusivo para las compras del día añade una capa adicional de protección, ya que limita el uso de los datos reales de la tarjeta física.
Wi-Fi público, el riesgo oculto al pagar desde el celular
Completar una compra mientras se toma un café o se camina por un centro comercial resulta tentador, pero las redes Wi-Fi abiertas representan un blanco sencillo para interceptar información o para crear redes falsas que imitan el nombre del local.
Desactivar la conexión automática a redes públicas utilizadas con anterioridad, desde los ajustes de Wi-Fi del celular, reduce ese riesgo. Al momento de pagar o de abrir la aplicación bancaria, lo recomendable es desconectar el Wi-Fi y recurrir únicamente a los datos móviles.
Ningún ajuste técnico reemplaza, de todas formas, una pausa breve antes de actuar. Frente a una oferta demasiado buena para ser real o un aviso urgente sobre una entrega, la recomendación es cerrar el mensaje y acceder directamente desde la aplicación oficial de la tienda donde se realizó la compra original.

articles.title: Credential Remediation Is Slow When You Don’t Know What Will Break
articles.text:
TL;DR
- More than 64% still valid after four years: GitGuardian’s State of Secrets Sprawl 2026 found that most valid secrets discovered in 2022 still worked in January 2026, because teams stall on what a revoke will break.
- Validity-only triage misses 46% of critical secrets: Prioritize by impact instead, weighing what a credential can access and whether it leaked publicly, and update the risk score as new context arrives.
- Revoke last, never first: Issue a replacement, store it in the vault, switch every consumer to the vault call, deploy and monitor, then revoke the original and confirm it no longer authenticates.
Every modern enterprise depends on credentials. This is how humans, systems, and now AI connect securely to data, services, and each other. GitGuardian helps secure that credential layer through three connected capabilities: Detect, Remediate, and Prevent. The journey starts with detection, but credential remediation is where many secret security programs bog down. This is the second of three articles we are releasing to explain how we help address detection, remediation, and prevention.
The first article in this series, “The Credential Layer Is Expanding Faster Than Security Teams Can See It,” covered detection across every surface where credentials live. Just knowing they exist is not enough. Teams need to take action to remediate those findings. To do that, they need context around every credential they find.
Without the right context, it is impossible to know what risks the secret carries. It is also difficult to understand which systems rely on those secrets and the risk levels that revoking the secret brings. Nobody wants to break production, but we also cannot allow attackers to leverage those secrets.
The resulting decision paralysis leaves many teams struggling to rotate immediately. Sometimes it can take years for the secret to be revoked finally. That is actually all too common, as shown by GitGuardian’s State of Secrets Sprawl 2026 research that found that 64% of valid secrets discovered in 2022 still worked in January 2026, a full 4 years later.
It would be great if there were a one-size-fits-all solution for remediating every leak; in reality, each one is tied to a specific integration. What we can do is streamline the processes needed to get to the end, making it much easier for organizations of any size. And it does take the whole organization to properly deal with leaked secrets.
Why credential remediation is so hard for so many teams
A team that discovers an exposed credential rarely has all the authority or knowledge needed to fix it without causing further issues. A security engineer can see it’s valid and dangerous, but that security engineer usually cannot immediately tell which services will fail when it is revoked. Breaking production is considered a much higher risk than the possibility of a stolen and abused secret, so they need to go looking for answers, which is a time-consuming process.
The developers who know where and why a key is used and, hopefully, how to rotate it safely are often busy shipping new features and managing existing requests from the business. An alert in their email that shows only a file path and a secret type asks those busy devs to stop their workflow and launch their own investigation. These requests, all too often, sink into the backlog.
At the same time, the larger the organization, the harder it is to find the right person who knows the answer to “what breaks if this key is revoked?” Application security teams monitor code where keys are used, identity and access management (IAM) teams govern identities that were issued keys, and the Platform Engineering team runs the vaults holding the keys. They all have different perspectives and, in most organizations that are early in their secrets security maturity journey, can only tell part of the story.
Endpoint security teams are also watching what happens at the workstation level. They are beginning to track secrets stored there, as software supply chain attacks have increasingly targeted these plaintext credential stores over the last couple of years. A secret leaked here might even be the triggering event for the rotation in case of compromise from an infostealer. The endpoint team is historically not connected to AppSec or Platform teams.
One credential can touch all these teams while each individual, isolated group sees only its own slice of the credential layer. Now, multiply the communication and coordination issue across hundreds or thousands of potential leaks, and the scale of the remediation problem becomes clearer.
Action before investigation invites downtime
The risk of revoking before fully understanding the fallout is fairly high for the business. This is weighed against potential future abuse. Of course, this math changes during an active breach when the clock is ticking and when exfiltration or lateral movement is already occurring. Those emergencies do not get backlogged. Mature organizations understand that addressing leaks before an emergency arises is the better plan overall, but remediation times are still measured in weeks for most teams. How long a remediation process takes really boils down to how fast and accurately responders can gather and communicate information about the issue. Responders need to know a lot of things, starting with whether the credential works, what it can access, and who owns it before they can even ask questions like “where else does it appear?” and “which systems depend on it?”
For example, envision two valid cloud credentials. One grants read-only access to a single storage bucket, and the second one is a root-level key with administrative control over production. While their privileges and dependent workloads determine the appropriate level of urgency, both require the same level of insight and investigation to triage the remediation process and decide whether the response is a rotation next sprint or a revocation this very second.
The ultimate goal is to remove the leaked key rapidly, but in a way that does not interrupt production or break pipeline builds. Rotating secrets safely simply requires resources and a coordination plan. If this process is always piecemeal and manual, then mistakes are more likely to happen.
A security team that causes an outage once will face resistance the next time it asks to rotate anything.
Prioritize by impact, not just validity
Validity is the first and clearest signal most responders look at. Alone, this is an incomplete signal. GitGuardian research from the State of Secrets report found that validity-only triage misses 46% of critical secrets such as custom API tokens and SSH keys, because those secrets cannot be verified automatically.
While validity still matters, access to sensitive data or core systems raises urgency. If the leak happened publicly on the internet, that raises the urgency even further. Any risk scoring needs to explain which factors drove it. It also needs to be a living risk score, adjusting for new information as new context arrives. Scoring it once upon discovery is akin to trusting an initial CVSS score in a CVE disclosure. It is a helpful guide but needs to be updated based on what is really going on in your organization. The organization and its risk tolerance will decide what happens next. Having as much information centrally available as possible is key to a rapid response, as responders reach the boundaries of what systems they can actually touch.
Route the work to the right people who can push the change
Remediation requests should let the developer or platform team act immediately, without requiring the team to repeat the investigation that has already taken place.
Any request to replace a key for a production system should include validity and known exposure locations. It should list dependencies too, and where possible show how it connects to business operations. The more the person picking up the request understands about the issue, the sooner they can act. In an ideal world, all remediation requests would be routed to their named owners. In the messy reality of the enterprise, you will likely need to involve the developer who leaked the secret and gather data from commit attribution or source metadata. We need to establish communication because there is a probability that they will need further instructions or guidance.
Requests should not be ‘thrown over the fence’ and then forgotten about. Follow-up and confirmation about remediation progress should be centrally collected and shared so every department knows where the rotation process is at any given moment. This accountability proves resilience efforts when an auditor shows up.
Engineers need to be enabled with a clean way to communicate once they start the work and once their ticket is ready to close. Routing the work through existing ticketing tools keeps it alongside other engineering work, but those tickets also need to integrate with the responder’s security operational tooling.
Rotate, revoke, and vault: the order matters
Safe rotation means following a specific set of steps, in the right order, so you don’t break anything. Remember: “Availability” is one of the legs of the CIA (confidentiality, integrity, availability) security triad.
For mature organizations, this could be as straightforward as rotating the secret in a vault, since the production applications and systems relying on the credential are all already consuming it from the secrets manager. Any plaintext copies are then rendered harmless once the original offending secret is revoked.
For organizations and situations where no existing vaulted copy is in use, this process often starts with issuing a replacement credential. If the responder can do this, they should do so immediately and store it safely in the vault. Then, replace every occurrence of the plaintext secret with that vault call, across every known consumer. The remediation steps from there are to push the changed code or config live and monitor for any issues, ready to roll back if anything breaks. Only when all the new systems are safely consuming the new vaulted credential appropriately can the team revoke the original. Getting this out of order turns a security fix into an incident.
GitGuardian’s service account credential rotation checklist covers these steps in detail.
Verify the fix and keep the evidence
Only close the ticket when the key is safely revoked, and the danger is removed. There needs to be an audit trail about what you fixed and how you proved that. You need verifiable confirmation that the old credential no longer authenticates. Optionally, and depending on the circumstances, you can show that the old secret was removed from all surfaces.
Any incidents closed while the credential remains valid deserve their own review queue. This common case happens when a team rotates a key in one system while the old key remains active and valid in another. This means a siloed team only accounted for their one occurrence in their tooling that lacks a unified view or relies on manual tracking.
The incident record also serves auditors and security leaders. It shows what was found, who acted, and how long remediation took.
One credential, start to finish with GitGuardian
At GitGuardian, we have helped thousands of developers and organizations streamline their remediation process.
To help visualize how we can help, imagine a Kubernetes application that calls an external service with an API key stored in a secrets manager. During troubleshooting in our imagined scenario, a developer copies the key into a local configuration file and commits it. This is a fairly common scenario we have seen play out many times.
GitGuardian scanning finds the secret as soon as it is committed. The platform generates a new open incident and alerts the assigned team. An automatic validity check confirms the key is still active, and the Secret Analyzer lists its permissions. A presence check confirms the secret is still in the codebase. All these checks can be rerun as remediation progresses.
For customers with full platform integrations, the GitGuardian Exploration Map shows a production workload depending on it, and fingerprint matching ties the committed value to the vaulted copy. The security team can bring that context to the owning developer and operations team.
Once a replacement key is issued, everyone can track the progress of the rotation and see when the PR that accounts for the deployment configuration is pulling from the vault. There is no guessing about whether revoking the original will affect anything critical. GitGuardian then rechecks validity and confirms the committed copy is gone.
The incident might also expose a pattern worth investigating across other teams. Has this same codebase seen similar incidents? Has the same user caused the same issue before? Are vaulted credentials ending up in unmanaged files on developer laptops on a regular basis? These all point to a wider issue that needs to be addressed to prevent further incidents and an increased remediation backlog.
From fixing to preventing
Remediation reduces risk one credential at a time. It also shows where exposures keep coming from.
The third and final article in this series covers prevention, starting on developer machines and in AI coding workflows. Teams that want to see this remediation workflow can take an interactive tour of the GitGuardian platform.
Take a Guided Tour of GitGuardian
FAQ
What is credential remediation?
Credential remediation is the work of removing the risk from a leaked or exposed credential. The goal is to replace and revoke the leaked key quickly, in a way that does not interrupt production or break pipeline builds, and then to confirm the old credential no longer authenticates.
Why does credential remediation take so long?
The team that finds an exposed credential rarely has the authority or the knowledge to fix it alone. A security engineer can see the credential is valid and dangerous, but usually cannot tell which services will fail when it is revoked. The developers, identity, platform, and endpoint teams each see only their own slice of the credential layer, so responders spend their time gathering context instead of fixing the leak.
How do you prioritize which leaked credentials to fix first?
Prioritize by impact, not validity alone. GitGuardian’s State of Secrets Sprawl 2026 found that validation-only prioritization misses 46% of critical secrets, because some secrets cannot be verified automatically. Access to sensitive data or core systems raises urgency, and a public leak raises it further. The risk score should explain which factors drove it and change as new context arrives.
What is the safe order for rotating a leaked secret?
Issue a replacement credential and store it in the vault. Replace every plaintext copy of the old secret with a call to the vault, across every known consumer. Push the changed code or configuration live and monitor for issues, ready to roll back. Revoke the original only when every system is consuming the new vaulted credential. Getting this out of order turns a security fix into an incident.
How do you verify that a leaked credential has been remediated?
Close the ticket only when you have verifiable confirmation that the old credential no longer authenticates. Keep an audit trail of what was fixed and how it was proved, including who acted and how long remediation took. Incidents closed while the credential is still valid deserve their own review, since a team may have rotated the key in one system while it stayed active in another.

Esquenta Black: Galaxy Tab S11 para jogos sai por menos de R$ 5.000

Equipado com o processador Dimensity 9400+ de 3 nm e 12 GB de RAM, o tablet roda qualquer aplicativo sem engasgos, oferecendo alta performance para tarefas de produtividade e jogos. Sua GPU Immortalis-G925 conta com suporte para ray tracing, o que torna os efeitos de luz mais realistas ao jogar no tablet.
A tela Dynamic AMOLED 2X de 11 polegadas com 120 Hz garante imagens fluidas e cores vibrantes. Na prática, isso significa que você terá uma experiência visual rica e bastante confortável. articles.title: Save on a budget router with prices starting at just $39 — TP-Link Archer AX1450 and Netgear RAX5 Wi-Fi 6 routers go on low sale
articles.text:
Save on a budget router with prices starting at just $39 — TP-Link Archer AX1450 and Netgear RAX5 Wi-Fi 6 routers go on low sale
Walmart has some hot deals on budget Wi-Fi 6 routers
Suppose you don’t need the extra speed and capacity that Wi-Fi 7 offers, and you just want something cheap to give you decent coverage throughout your house? Well, that’s where something like the TP-Link Archer AX1450 comes into focus. Walmart has the router on sale this week for $39, a $10 discount off its regular asking price.
The Archer AX1450 is by no means a speed demon, delivering up to 250 Mbps over the 2.4 GHz band and up to 1,201 Mbps on the 5 GHz band. That should be more than sufficient if you have a 1 Gbps or lower broadband connection. You get one GbE WAN port and four GbE LAN ports for connecting your wired devices. The router features four antennas and four wireless streams.
You can manage the Archer AX1450 with the usual webGUI on a desktop/laptop or use the TP-Link Tether app to control the router from your smartphone or tablet.
There’s also the Netgear RAX5, which Walmart has on sale for $44.33 ($35 off its usual selling price). This is another Wi-Fi 6 router delivering up to 1.6 Gbps aggregate speeds. The router covers up to 1,500 square feet and includes a GbE WAN and four GbE LAN ports.
The TP-Link Archer AX1450 is a Wi-Fi 6 router with four GbE LAN ports and up to 1.45 Gbps aggregate wireless speeds across 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands.
The Netgear RAX5 is a Wi-Fi 6 router with four GbE LAN ports and up to 1.6 Gbps aggregate wireless speeds across 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands.
Keep in mind that the RAX5 isn’t meant for homes that have a ton of smartphones, computers, and smart home devices. It only reliably supports up to 20 wireless devices. So if you have a desktop, a laptop, a couple of TVs, and a couple of smartphones, the RAX5 should do perfectly fine handling the load. If you have more demanding needs, step up to one of the best Wi-Fi 7 routers.
As I previously mentioned, the TP-Link and Netgear routers are aimed at people who have less demanding wireless needs, and they’re priced to reflect this fact. They won’t win any throughput contests against their newer Wi-Fi 6E or Wi-Fi 7 competition, but those routers will also cost you around twice as much money.

articles.title: Séisme : NVIDIA suspend ses livraisons de serveurs IA vers l'Asie du Sud-Est, la Chine en ligne de mire
articles.text:
NVIDIA aurait brutalement coupé le robinet des serveurs IA à quatre pays d’Asie du Sud-Est. Washington veut barrer à la Chine tous les chemins vers les puces les plus avancées, et l’onde de choc secoue déjà la région.
Le moins que l’on puisse dire, c’est que NVIDIA est sous le feu des projecteurs. Il y a quelques jours, son emblématique patron Jensen Huang a démissionné après des révélations sur plusieurs liaisons extraconjugales. L’une d’elles a particulièrement alarmé les autorités américaines : sa relation avec Alice Huang, soupçonnée d’espionnage au profit de la Chine.
Mais le coup de théâtre est survenu ce 23 novembre avec le retour du P.-D.G à son poste. Désormais, l’entreprise doit absolument serrer la vis.
Empêcher la Chine d’utiliser les serveurs de la région
D’après des informations exclusives du Financial Times, Dell, Supermicro et d’autres partenaires industriels, chargés d’intégrer les puces NVIDIA dans des serveurs, ont prévenu leurs clients de Malaisie, de Singapour, de Thaïlande et d’Indonésie que leurs commandes n’aboutiraient pas. Et la consigne viendrait directement du géant des puces.
Pour l’heure, on ignore si ce blocage est provisoire afin de laisser le temps à l’entreprise et ses partenaires de comprendre comment appliquer les dernières restrictions américaines à l’exportation. Car la semaine dernière, le département du commerce a instauré une licence obligatoire pour exporter des puces d’IA avancées vers cinq pays : les quatre cités, ainsi que le Brésil. Son objectif est d’empêcher que ces territoires servent de porte d’entrée vers la Chine grâce au cloud.
Cette décision est tout sauf anodine : la maîtresse chinoise de Jensen Huang a justement dirigé Megaspeed, un néocloud singapourien pour qui elle a obtenu des puces d’IA avancées depuis 2023. Avides de puces de pointe, les développeurs chinois se ruent sur ces solutions pour entraîner leurs modèles.
C’est la pagaille dans la région
De quoi nourrir un boom des data centers, notamment en Malaisie et en Indonésie, où des milliards de dollars d’investissements se retrouvent fragilisés. À Singapour, la société Aolani comptait par exemple louer de la puissance de calcul à ByteDance, la maison mère de TikTok.
Cette dernière annonce sème la pagaille chez les opérateurs locaux, désormais contraints de prouver qu’aucune entité soumise à des restrictions ne figure parmi leurs utilisateurs finaux. D’autant qu’ils espéraient que le retour de Jensen Huang ouvrirait la voie à une application plus souple de ces règles. Mais le patron, fervent défenseur des ventes à la Chine, voit sa position clairement fragilisée.
L’enjeu est pourtant colossal pour NVIDIA. En 2025, sa filiale singapourienne a enregistré 104 milliards de dollars de chiffre d’affaires, soit un bond de 72 % en un an.

articles.title: Drupal Fail2Install Exploit Details Emerge as Critical RCE Flaw Faces Active Exploitation
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Tuesday added a critical flaw impacting Drupal to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring federal agencies to apply the fixes by November 27, 2026.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-132165 aka Fail2Install (CVSS score: 9.8), is a case of remote code execution (RCE) impacting Drupal core.
"Drupal Core contains a not failing securely vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to take over an existing site or execute arbitrary code via the Drupal installer," CISA said. "Under specific conditions, the attacker can use install.php to attempt to reinstall Drupal on the site."
As previously reported by The Hacker News, an attacker can use the installer to attempt to reinstall Drupal, resulting in site takeover or remote code execution under certain circumstances.
According to an independent analysis by Searchlight Cyber, it has emerged that ordinary server resource limits can be abused to trick Drupal into mistakenly believing that an existing website was not installed, enter its installation process via "install.php," create an administrator-controlled account, and execute arbitrary PHP code.
While Drupal has checks in place to determine whether the website is already installed before allowing installation to proceed, the research found that it's possible to bypass these checks by exhausting server resources.
As a result, a failed database connection to the configured database and a failed database check for an existing installation are interpreted as evidence that the website has not been installed, thereby opening the door to a scenario where Drupal allows the installation to proceed but only after winning a race condition that allows a second database connectivity check to pass.
"So if the database refuses the early connections and accepts the later one, all within one request, the installer concludes the site is new and shows its setup forms on a live site," StepSecurity said in an explainer. "
"The installer's database form saves the settings it receives to settings.php. Once an attacker submits that form with their own database settings, the live site points at the attacker's database. The attacker then creates the site's administrator account."
To achieve this, the three resource exhaustion techniques have been put to use -
- EMFILE, which refers to a limit on how many files a Linux process can open
- Database connection exhaustion
- TCP source-port exhaustion
"We started with EMFILE, then explored database and TCP limits to determine whether availability failures could become security primitives," the cybersecurity company said.
"Applying this methodology to Drupal uncovered a pre-authentication RCE affecting Drupal 8.9, 9, 10, and 11 across four common deployment combinations: Apache with PostgreSQL, Apache with MySQL, PHP-FPM with PostgreSQL, and PHP-FPM with MySQL."
This behavior can be turned into a pathway for code execution by taking advantage of the fact that Drupal's installer supports SQLite database files and allows the database path to be selected during installation. This is possible because the installer does not enforce restrictions on the file name extension.
"By selecting a path ending in .php under the document root, the installer creates an SQLite database with a PHP extension," Searchlight Cyber said. "Once the installation reaches the site configuration form, Drupal stores the submitted website name inside the SQLite database. By using PHP code as the website name, the payload bytes are written into the .php database file."
While direct access to the generated PHP file is blocked by Drupal's stock .htaccess on a stock Apache deployment, a path-handling weakness in the Apache RewriteRule could be exploited to achieve arbitrary PHP execution.
"Starting from three system-wide limits, we showed how errors that appear to affect only availability can become primitives for crossing a security boundary," Searchlight Cyber researchers Kevin Gervot and Adam Kues said.
"In Drupal, temporary database failures can produce a FAIL, FAIL, and then SUCCESS sequence that reopens the installer on an existing website and ultimately leads to pre-authentication RCE through an SQLite database containing PHP code."
The issue has been addressed in the following versions -
- Drupal 11.4.x - Update to Drupal 11.4.13
- Drupal 11.3.x - Update to Drupal 11.3.22
- Drupal 10.6.x - Update to Drupal 10.6.22
The addition of CVE-2026-132165 to the KEV catalog follows a report received by the Drupal Security Team that it "was exploited on live sites as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC."
It's worth noting that CVE-2026-132165 is the third Drupal flaw to come under active exploitation this year following CVE-2026-9082 (CVSS score: 6.5) and CVE-2026-118539 (CVSS score: 6.5).

articles.title: Thermal Grizzly Launches Delid Heat Mate for Lower-Risk DIY CPU Delidding
articles.text:
Thursday, November 26th 2026
Thermal Grizzly Launches Delid Heat Mate for Lower-Risk DIY CPU Delidding
Thermal Grizzly has just announced the Delid-Heat-Mate, the latest tool in its ever-expanding line-up of enthusiast delidding tools and accessories. The Delid-Heat-Mate is a CPU delidding tool built for AMD AM5 and Intel LGA 1700, 1851, and 1954 CPUs that aims to make the whole delidding process easier and less stressful. 
Instead of applying pressure to break the solder joint between the CPU and IHS and the adhesive bond between the IHS and the substrate, the Delid-Heat-Mate allows users to simply lay the CPU flat on the tool, put it into an oven, and heat the CPU up to melt the solder and free the silicon from its soldered heat spreader. If all goes well, the CPU's IHS should fall off the CPU under its own weight.The idea behind the Delid-Heat-Mate is that it reduces the stress on the CPU silicon, ostensibly reducing the risk to the CPU when delidding it. Once the CPU is delidded, it can then be cleaned and used with something like a direct-die cooling kit for significantly reduced thermals. The Thermal Grizzly Delid-Heat-Mate is available from the Thermal Grizzly online shop for $23.28.
Sources:
				Thermal Grizzly, 				via TweakTown
