articles.title: Com-Affiliated Hackers Hijack Cloud Accounts via Vishing for Data Theft and Extortion
articles.text:
Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 has disclosed that it's tracking and has responded to "numerous waves of vishing attacks" orchestrated by Com-affiliated threat actors since August 2026 that have led to data theft and extortion attempts.
The attacks have targeted financial services, healthcare, and legal services located in the U.S., the U.K., and Australia. Other targets include construction, high-technology, transportation, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, insurance, and real estate sectors.
"The victims share a common profile: they hold large volumes of high-impact corporate data where exposure carries severe regulatory, legal, or market consequences," Unit 42 said. "These attackers targeted financial services organizations about twice as often as healthcare organizations in August 2026, but healthcare overtook financial services in September."
The activity has been attributed to a number of threat clusters, including -
- Bling Libra (aka ShinyHunters)
- CL-CRI-1116 (aka Redact, formerly BlackFile), first observed in January 2026
- CL-CRI-1147 (aka Pink), first observed in May 2026
- CL-CRI-1182 (aka Falcon), first observed in mid-2026
- CL-CRI-1192 (aka Helix and UNC6671), first observed in June 2026
- CL-CRI-1264 (aka Vortex), first observed in September 2026
- CL-CRI-1274 (aka Cinder), first observed in September 2026
Intrusions typically commence with voice phishing, with the attackers posing as IT staff to resolve a purported authentication issue and direct the victim to a phishing page personalized to their organization.
Once the AiTM kit captures credentials and session tokens, the attackers quickly enroll their own multi-factor authentication (MFA) devices, abuse cloud utilities and, in a few instances, deploy malicious browser extensions to exfiltrate data and extort victims.
The harvested authentication data is used to authenticate to victim environments, typically by routing such requests through residential proxy networks and commercial VPNs. The adversaries then seek to establish multi-layered persistence by registering their MFA devices, generating cloud infrastructure temporary credentials, authorizing unapproved third-party OAuth applications; enumerate sensitive data; evade defenses by modifying mailbox rules and clearing security alert events; and harvest data from cloud platforms.
"Attackers associated with CL-CRI-1264 establish initial access through vishing, where they pose as internal IT support and direct employees to servers using subdomains tailored to each targeted organization," Unit 42 said.
"These servers act as adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) proxies that pass user credentials and multi-factor authentication (MFA) approvals to the attackers in real time. Attackers have targeted employees on both their corporate workstations and personal mobile devices."
CL-CRI-1264 has also been observed enrolling unauthorized MFA devices within minutes of authenticating to establish persistence, often reusing a single device named Pixel 10a across compromised accounts. The attack chains involve automated data exfiltration using Python scripts to harvest information from Microsoft 365 mailbox, OneDrive, and SharePoint.
Once data is exfiltrated, the threat actor sends Microsoft Teams messages directly to employees at victim organizations, claiming data theft and instructing them to visit a TOR-hosted ransom negotiation site.
The second new cluster to emerge around the same time is CL-CRI-1274, which has also leaned on vishing for initial access and leveraged the Microsoft Graph software development kit (SDK) to collect and exfiltrate data from the victim's SharePoint and OneDrive environments.
"Afterwards, the attackers used a compromised account to send extortion messages internally via email and Microsoft Teams, ultimately directing recipients to a Tor-hosted negotiation site," Unit 42 said.
The cybersecurity company said it also observed the CL-CRI-1192 attackers using a malicious browser extension named "Google Chrome" that's said to have been sideloaded onto the browser after enabling Developer Mode. The add-on performs a number of malicious actions, such as -
- Installing global keyloggers
- Stealing local/session storage and authentication cookies for Microsoft and Google accounts
- Scanning pages for QR codes to capture login/MFA tokens
- Streaming webcam feeds
- Implementing a command-and-control (C2) remote control module via Chrome DevTools Protocol to capture screenshots, dispatch input events, steal clipboard contents, and allow remote site navigation.
"We assess with moderate confidence that the attackers associated with CL-CRI-1192 developed this malicious browser extension as an alternative method to extract credentials from desktop and laptop devices running Chromium-based browsers such as Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge," Unit 42 said.
"The extension might also be shared with and used by other Com-affiliated attackers, although we currently have no evidence to suggest this."
One of the defining traits of the threat actors is their use of "apex" domains that impersonate single sign-on (SSO) portals, IT support pages, and passkey configuration services for each of the targeted organizations.
Also shared among the attackers is an AitM phishing kit called Doko's Panel that allows them to steal authenticated sessions and then abuse them to access connected software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms like SharePoint, Salesforce, DocuSign, and Slack to exfiltrate data of interest.
"The same persona behind Doko's Panel has been observed actively recruiting 'experienced callers' via Telegram, specifying requirements including fluent English with no accent, and advertising six-to-seven-figure weekly returns — evidence of the professionalized vishing-as-a-service model that complements the phishing kit ecosystem," Push Security noted in a report published earlier this May.
Microsoft has also revealed cloud-based intrusions in which threat actors have employed passkey and SSO lures to obtain unauthorized access and add their own authentication methods to set up persistence, as well as conduct high-volume Microsoft Graph activity, SharePoint and OneDrive downloads, and mailbox collection through REST APIs.
"Rather than employing custom tools, the threat actors primarily leveraged native cloud utilities and selectively limited executions and persistence deployments," Unit 42 said. "Cybercriminals like Bling Libra and other Com-affiliated threat actors are pivoting away from encryption, enabling them to move at greater speed across their intrusion lifecycle while still achieving their objectives."

articles.title: Bancos dos EUA criam “botão de emergência” contra agentes de IA
articles.text:
Bancos dos EUA criam “botão de emergência” contra agentes de IA
Instituições revisam acessos e mecanismos de desligamento após incidentes com modelos da OpenAI.
Bancos de grande e médio porte dos Estados Unidos estão revisando mecanismos de desligamento de emergência para seus agentes de inteligência artificial. Segundo uma reportagem recente da Reuters, a revisão foi motivada por incidentes em testes da OpenAI com modelos que driblaram restrições de segurança.
As instituições ouvidas não foram identificadas. Segundo a agência, nenhum banco foi atingido por episódios semelhantes.
Conhecidos como kill switches, esses mecanismos servem para desconectar agentes que apresentem falhas ou tenham sido comprometidos. Como o desligamento pode afetar as operações bancárias, as instituições testam alternativas para atividades como detecção de fraudes. O objetivo é manter os serviços funcionando enquanto o agente fica suspenso.
Os bancos também restringem permissões, separam os ambientes de testes das operações diárias e limitam o tempo de atividade dos agentes. Senhas e registros de atividade são mantidos fora do alcance desses sistemas.
Os agentes de IA conseguem planejar etapas, utilizar ferramentas e executar tarefas. Em um ambiente bancário, essa capacidade exige definir quais informações cada ferramenta pode acessar. Permissões amplas demais podem permitir ações que ultrapassem o objetivo da tarefa. Essa preocupação aparece em um documento publicado este mês pelo Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), órgão americano de supervisão bancária.
O documento cita os kill switches entre os recursos para conter agentes que continuem funcionando enquanto executam ações inadequadas. O impacto sobre clientes, a possibilidade de desfazer uma ação e o grau de autonomia também influenciam a avaliação do risco. Para preservar o atendimento, o material cita alternativas, como outro agente com funções limitadas.
O setor de tecnologia também desenvolve ferramentas de contenção. Em setembro, a Nvidia apresentou uma plataforma para limitar permissões de agentes e interromper comunicações quando eles tentarem ultrapassar restrições.
O episódio que motivou a revisão ocorreu em julho. A OpenAI confirmou que modelos usados em avaliações internas de cibersegurança contornaram o isolamento da internet e acessaram infraestrutura da própria empresa e da Hugging Face.
Os sistemas exploraram vulnerabilidades e estabeleceram comunicações não autorizadas. A investigação apontou como principal responsável um modelo experimental de pesquisa que não estava disponível ao público.
Esses testes tinham proteções reduzidas. Segundo a OpenAI, o incidente não afetou dados de clientes nem o funcionamento dos produtos. Após a investigação, a empresa anunciou medidas como ambientes de testes mais isolados e restrições adicionais de acesso.

articles.title: Samduo : jusqu’à 800 € de remise, mais le tirage iPhone exige une inscription
articles.text:
Le Black Friday entre dans sa dernière ligne droite chez Samduo ! Jusqu’au 30 novembre, les batteries solaires Nex E6000 et E6000H profitent de 400 € de remise, avec la possibilité d’opter pour des packs de deux unités (et ainsi économiser 800 €). Compteur intelligent offert, coffret cadeau et double participation à un tirage au sort de 12 iPhone : voici les avantages à ne pas manquer.
La facture d’électricité reste un poste de dépense important pour de nombreux foyers. Pour mieux maîtriser sa consommation, le stockage de l’énergie solaire peut constituer une piste très intéressante. Il permet de conserver une partie de sa production en journée pour l’utiliser lorsque les panneaux photovoltaïques ne fournissent plus d’électricité.
C’est précisément là que se positionne Samduo avec ses batteries Nex E6000 et E6000H. À l’occasion du Black Friday, la marque sort le grand jeu avec des remises allant jusqu’à 400 €, plusieurs cadeaux offerts et même un tirage au sort permettant de remporter l’un des 12 iPhone mis en jeu (dont le récent iPhone Duo). Le grand jeu on vous dit !
Batteries Samduo : jusqu’à 800 € de remise sur les modèles Nex E
Deux configurations sont proposées aux particuliers chez Samduo. La Nex E6000 adopte un format mural particulièrement fin, avec seulement 11,9 cm d’épaisseur pour une capacité de 6 kWh. Le modèle Nex E6000H, de son côté, privilégie un format compact à poser directement au sol, sans aucune fixation murale. Deux approches différentes, mais une base technique commune.
Pour le Black Friday, chacune est affichée à 1 599 € au lieu de 1 999 €, soit 400 € d’économie. Ceux qui souhaitent disposer de davantage de capacité peuvent également se tourner vers les packs de deux batteries, proposés dans trois configurations : deux E6000, deux E6000H ou un modèle de chaque. Dans les trois cas, la remise atteint 800 €, avec un tarif de 3 198 € au lieu de 3 998 €.
Deux unités permettent de disposer de 12 kWh de stockage, avec la possibilité de faire évoluer ensuite l’installation jusqu’à 90 kWh grâce au système PowerMesh. Le pack mixte permet quant à lui de profiter des deux formats, avec une batterie murale et une seconde installée au sol, avec les avantages qui en découlent.
Plus de confort au quotidien, avec un compteur intelligent offert
Au-delà du prix, l’intérêt d’une batterie domestique est avant tout de mieux exploiter sa production solaire. Plutôt que de réinjecter systématiquement son surplus d’électricité sur le réseau pendant les heures ensoleillées, la Nex E6000 ou la E6000H le conserve pour alimenter le logement lorsque les panneaux ne produisent plus suffisamment.
L’application Samduo accompagne cette gestion avec un plan énergétique sur 24 heures, qui prend notamment en compte les tarifs de l’électricité, peu importe que ceux-ci soient fixes ou dynamiques. Le système peut ainsi adapter les périodes de charge (et de restitution) pour mieux maîtriser sa consommation. La compatibilité avec Home Assistant et Homey complète l’ensemble pour ceux qui souhaitent intégrer leur batterie à leur installation domotique.
Un autre avantage du Black Friday, c’est le compteur intelligent Samduo Smart Meter, d’une valeur de 129 €, qui est offert avec chaque commande éligible. Celui-ci mesure les flux d’électricité entrants et sortants du logement, des données indispensables pour affiner le pilotage énergétique. Petite précision importante : un seul compteur est offert par commande, et non par appareil.
Samduo ajoute également un « coffret cadeau » spécial Black Friday, proposé dans la limite des stocks disponibles. De quoi compléter une offre déjà intéressante, sans supplément à prévoir.
Du 27 au 30 novembre, chaque commande compte double pour gagner un iPhone
C’est l’autre argument de cette dernière ligne droite. Du 27 au 30 novembre inclus, chaque commande éligible compte double en ce qui concerne le tirage au sort organisé par Samduo. Au total, 12 smartphones sont mis en jeu, avec 3 iPhone Duo 256 Go et 9 iPhone 18 Pro 256 Go.
Là encore, détail important : la participation n’est absolument pas automatique ! Après avoir passé commande, il faut donc impérativement se rendre sur la page dédiée au concours et renseigner son numéro de commande ainsi que l’adresse e-mail utilisée lors de l’achat. Sans cette inscription, aucune participation ne sera enregistrée (les commandes annulées ou intégralement remboursées perdent leurs participations).
Pour être éligible, il faudra également que la commande soit effectivement livrée avant le 19 décembre. Le tirage au sort aura lieu quant à lui le 21 décembre, avec une annonce des gagnants au plus tard le 23 décembre, parfait pour passer un très joyeux Noël donc.
Enfin, mieux vaut ne pas trop attendre puisque la marque précise d’ores et déjà que les tarifs promotionnels resteront identiques pendant le week-end du Black Friday, sans baisse supplémentaire annoncée. Les offres Samduo prendront fin ce 30 novembre, à 23 h 59.
Autrement dit, ces quatre jours constituent l’occasion idéale de profiter de belles remises d’une part, mais aussi des cadeaux offerts, ainsi que de deux chances de participation au tirage au sort pour chaque commande éligible.

articles.title: Pokémon GO en diciembre 2026: debut de Pyukumuku, mejora para Mega-Slowbro y evento con Pokémon Champions
articles.text:
Diciembre 2026 traerá tres novedades principales a Pokémon GO: el debut de Pyukumuku, una mejora para Mega-Slowbro y un evento de colaboración vinculado con Pokémon Champions.
Las actividades comenzarán el 1 de diciembre y se extenderán, con distintos contenidos, hasta el 21 de diciembre.
El primer evento será Paraíso tropical, disponible desde el martes 1 de diciembre a las 10.00 hasta el lunes 7 de diciembre a las 20.00, según la hora local.
Durante esos días, Pyukumuku, un Pokémon de la región de Alola, aparecerá por primera vez en incursiones y mediante el Pase de GO, una vía de progreso temporal que permite conseguir premios al reunir puntos dentro del juego.
La programación del mes incluirá la investigación temporal Escoge tu camino. Del 15 al 21 de diciembre, los jugadores podrán elegir una de tres rutas —Explorar, Capturar o Combatir—, que determinará las tareas y los bonus disponibles durante esa semana.
Las recompensas deberán completarse y reclamarse antes de que venza el plazo establecido.
Novedades en Pokémon GO: Pyukumuku y la mejora de Mega-Slowbro
El evento Paraíso tropical permitirá conseguir a Pyukumuku en incursiones de nivel tres.
Desde entonces, el Pokémon podrá aprender Anegar como ataque rápido. Además, habrá encuentros en estado salvaje con Slowpoke, Shellder, Wingull, Slakoth y Snorlax, entre otros.
Entre el 4 y el 7 de diciembre se sumarán Hoppip, Lotad, Shroomish y Exeggutor de Alola a los encuentros salvajes.
En las incursiones de nivel uno aparecerán Diglett de Alola, Frillish hembra, Frillish macho y Sandygast. Las tareas de investigación de campo, que son misiones para completar desde las Poképaradas, ofrecerán encuentros con Pokémon como Psyduck, Tentacool y Shellder.
La otra gran novedad será la posibilidad de aumentar el meganivel de Mega-Slowbro hasta el nivel supermáximo.
Para acceder a esta opción, será necesario llevar primero el meganivel del Pokémon al tercer nivel, el máximo habitual, y luego utilizar Megaenergía de Slowbro. Mientras esté megaevolucionado, Slowbro también podrá usar Agua Fría+ como ataque cargado adicional; su poder crecerá según el meganivel alcanzado.
El Pase de GO de Paraíso tropical estará disponible durante todo el evento. La versión gratuita se activará automáticamente para los jugadores, mientras que el Pase de GO deluxe tendrá un precio de USD 4,99.
Asimismo, habrá una opción de USD 6,99 que permitirá avanzar seis niveles de inmediato. Las recompensas obtenidas deberán reclamarse antes del 9 de diciembre a las 20.00, en la hora local.
El evento de celebración de Pokémon Champions
Del martes 8 de diciembre a las 10.00 al lunes 14 de diciembre a las 20.00 se realizará el Evento de celebración de Pokémon Champions.
Durante esa semana, los jugadores podrán encontrar a Charmander, Starly y Grookey en estado salvaje.
Las incursiones de nivel uno incluirán a Bagon, Litten y Frigibax. En las de nivel tres estarán Raichu, Garchomp y Rillaboom. La programación de nivel cinco reunirá a Latias, Latios, Heatran, Cobalion, Terrakion, Virizion, Regieleki y Regidrago, que formarán parte de las rotaciones de la temporada entre el 9 y el 15 de diciembre.
Los Pokémon destacados de las incursiones de nivel cinco podrán aparecer en versión variocolor, es decir, con una coloración diferente de la habitual.
Además, durante el evento tendrán la posibilidad de contar con un fondo especial. Ese diseño solo estará disponible mientras se desarrolle la celebración de Pokémon Champions.
La colaboración habilitará el envío de un Pokémon capturado en Pokémon GO hacia Pokémon HOME.
Después, los jugadores podrán enviarlo a Pokémon Champions para recibir un regalo en la bandeja de entrada de ese juego.
Las tareas de investigación de campo del evento entregarán Caramelos Raros, objetos que pueden utilizarse con cualquier especie de Pokémon.
El Pase de GO de la celebración estará disponible del 8 al 14 de diciembre. Su versión deluxe costará USD 4,99, mientras que la alternativa con seis niveles adicionales tendrá un valor de USD 6,99. Las recompensas de este Pase de GO vencerán el 16 de diciembre a las 20.00, en la hora local.

articles.title: A new malware network is generating 40 billion fake ad requests every day
articles.text:
BADBOX malware botnet returns — using hacked Android TV boxes to generate a record 40 billion fraudulent advertising bid requests every day
Your streaming device could be playing invisible ads 24/7
- BADBOX 3.0 generates 40 billion fraudulent advertising requests every day
- Cheap Android TV boxes have become tools for large-scale advertising fraud
- BADBOX 3.0 software has links to Chinese electronics manufacturer TXCZ
Cybercriminals have turned inexpensive television streaming equipment into tools for an advertising fraud operation generating unprecedented volumes of fraudulent transactions.
The operation, identified as BADBOX 3.0, compromises internet-connected devices and uses their computing capabilities to simulate advertising activity without owners knowing.
The original BADBOX operation was exposed in 2023, prompting investigations and disruption efforts against its infrastructure and infected devices.
Cheap streaming devices become a conduit for advertising fraud
At its height, the network produced approximately 40 billion advertising bid requests daily, exceeding the previous record holder VASTFLUX by more than threefold.
Research conducted by HUMAN Security's Satori Threat Intelligence team uncovered the operation through investigations involving compromised consumer electronics.
The affected products include cheap TV boxes manufactured in mainland China, running open source Android software without Google's official certification.
These devices differ from genuine Android TV products and lack the security verification associated with Google's certified hardware ecosystem.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Some of them reportedly contain malicious components before reaching customers, while other units acquire the malware after connecting to internet services.
Once activated, hidden programs communicate with remote control servers, downloading additional components responsible for generating fraudulent advertising activity.
These programs display commercial videos inside invisible windows, allowing advertisements to run without appearing on television screens.
The malicious software also manufactures advertising requests that imitate legitimate connected television applications, deceiving advertising systems into treating artificial traffic as genuine.
This allows operators to collect advertising revenue through activity that neither television owners nor legitimate advertisers knowingly authorized.
“BADBOX 3.0 is the largest ad fraud operation by bid volume ever publicly disclosed, and it ran on cheap TV boxes sitting in people’s living rooms,” said Gavin Reid, Chief Information Security Officer, HUMAN.
The investigation also found that criminals were secretly using infected devices to share their owners' internet connections with other people through proxy services.
Researchers identified 11 such networks, allowing criminals to make money from victims' internet connections in addition to fraudulent advertising.
BADBOX 3.0 links to a Chinese manufacturer and earlier attacks
HUMAN investigators traced parts of BADBOX 3.0's malicious software to TXCZ, a Chinese electronics manufacturer, through several technical links.
These included websites, remote control servers, preinstalled applications and online repositories associated with the manufacturer.
The investigation also connected the operation to IpMoYu, a residential proxy network previously linked to BADBOX 2.0.
Researchers believe the criminals have since developed a successor called PXYEDGE, which retains parts of IpMoYu's infrastructure and software.
Researchers from Nokia independently reached similar findings in their own investigation of the proxy network.
Google had already taken legal action against operators of BADBOX 2.0 in July 2025 after investigations uncovered infected consumer devices.
However, the discovery of BADBOX 3.0 shows that the criminals have continued their activities using updated malware and new methods of distributing it.
HUMAN said its security systems can still detect malicious activities even when criminals route internet traffic through residential proxy networks.
The company also claims its advertising protection services help customers defend against fraudulent advertising generated by BADBOX 3.0.
The exact number of devices infected by BADBOX 3.0 remains unknown, despite the operation's international reach.

articles.title: Windows Server 2028 Won't Run 32-Bit Apps Out of the Box
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Windows Server 2028 Won't Run 32-Bit Apps Out of the Box
At Ignite 2026, Microsoft confirmed that Windows Server 2028 won't be able to run 32-bit applications out of the box. According to Microsoft's Elden Christensen, the WoW64 (Windows 32-bit on Windows 64-bit) subsystem is being removed from default installs of Windows Server 2028. That is the compatibility layer that lets 32-bit software run on 64-bit Windows. He framed it as a "feature on demand," and apparently admins with an older 32-bit line-of-business app can still add it back manually. So it's not an outright removal, but it's still a change to how Windows Server approaches 32-bit applications.
The goal is to shut out 32-bit malware, which won't run on the OS without the WoW64 subsystem. This change is part of a bigger "secure by default" push for Windows Server 2028, which is in public preview. Christensen also said that AI tools are finding vulnerabilities at a worrying pace, which means that some legacy components are now on the chopping block. That apparently also includes SMBv1 and VBScript. Microsoft is also reportedly looking at dropping legacy BIOS support. Windows 11 isn't affected by this change, and Microsoft has announced no plans to end 32-bit support for that OS. Plenty of older PC games are still 32-bit, so that's probably for the best.
Sources:
				Microsoft Ignite, 				via Windows Central			
	
	
	
		
	
		
7 Comments on Windows Server 2028 Won't Run 32-Bit Apps Out of the Box
? Windows is a 64 bit operating system from the bootloader starting point. There's no 32 bit stuff during boot.Makes sense to me tbh. Anything running Windows Vista or later should be able to switch to SMBv2 at a minimum, and if you have anything running Windows 8 or older, that device should be in an isolated network without access to the Internet anyway.
VBScript is supposedly surpassed these days by PowerShell and seemingly hasn't gotten any relevant feature updates since v6 in the 90s so... it shouldn't be too problematic to remove.Honestly I am surprised they didn't remove it completely with Server 2022/2025 or Windows 11. They already require a bunch of stuff like TPM, Secure Boot, etc., so it's not like requiring UEFI-only mode would have been strange
Because there aren't any. 64-bit Windows does not require any 32-bit executables to run, and Windows Server has offered the ability to disable WoW64 for some time now. In a server context, disabling it is probably a good idea atp, if not overdue. 
The phaseout of 32-bit Windows has been in the works for a long time now. The last GPU drivers are 8 years old, the last kernel is 6 years old, and the last complete OS build is Windows 10 22H2 (which is now over 4 years old, and runs on the 2004 kernel anyways).
Is it also possible to remove, or disable completely, WoW64 on Windows 11 and 10?
No, this is not a supported configuration for client versions of Windows. On 2008 R2 and up, DISM [ICODE]dism /online /disable-feature /featurename:WoW64-Support[/ICODE] or PowerShell [ICODE]Uninstall-WindowsFeature -Name WoW64-Support -Restart[/ICODE]. Alternatively you can disable it on Server Manager if you have the GUI installed. 
Disabling WOW64 will make all 32-bit executable binaries incompatible with the OS.
Yeah, I am surprised as well. Modern hardware is so bound to UEFI that no reasonable Win 11 or Server hardware configuration would even want to run in legacy mode. ReBAR ain’t working without UEFI, as an example, either.

articles.title: WordPress Blocks Six Backdoored WP Connect Plugins Before Malicious Releases Go Live
articles.text:
WordPress has removed six WordPress plugins developed by WP Connect after they were backdoored on November 22, 2026, to enable arbitrary code execution on sites that have them installed, following a suspected compromise of the developer's account.
The WordPress plugins team has proactively detected and blocked the threat before it could be officially released. Visiting each plugin listing now serves the message: "This plugin has been closed as of November 22, 2026, and is not available for download. This closure is permanent."
The names of the affected plugins and the malicious versions are listed below -
- Air WP Sync – Airtable to WordPress (2.9.1 – 2.9.4)
- WP Sync for Notion – Notion to WordPress (1.7.4)
- Add-on Brevo for Gravity Forms (2.6.3)
- Add-On for Contact Form 7 to Airtable (2.5.4)
- Add-On for Contact Form 7 to Notion (1.6.4)
- Orders Sync to Airtable for WooCommerce (1.0.2)
These plugins have been collectively installed on more than 3,600 WordPress sites, according to WordPress security company Wordfence. The supply chain compromise is being tracked as CVE-2026-135202 (CVSS score: 9.8). It remains unpatched.
"Each release silently loaded the same remote-control module, which phones home to an attacker-controlled server, executes any PHP code it is sent, and exposes a full command set for running shell commands, stealing password hashes, and planting webshells," security researcher Chloe Chamberland said.
Specifically, the plugins come with a backdoor module ("includes/airwp-online.php") that runs on every request, sends site information (site URL, PHP, WordPress, and OS versions, and the server user) to a hard-coded command-and-control server ("tascredit-pay[.]com"), and runs PHP code returned by the server via eval().
It can also perform the following actions -
- Accept queued commands that run shell commands
- Read, write, and delete arbitrary files
- Query arbitrary database tables
- Dump the users table including login, email address, and password hashes
- Drop a web shell into the uploads directory or to a path of the attacker's choosing
- Register an hourly WP-Cron hook that runs attacker-supplied code
As a result, an unauthenticated attacker in control of the site can execute arbitrary code on the server and take complete control, facilitating credential theft and persistence through web shells and cron hooks that outlast the plugin removal.
Because the malicious versions were never released and blocked due to WordPress's new cooldown protections as part of its Protect The Shire initiative, sites running these plugins are unlikely to be affected. However, it's essential that site owners check their websites to make sure that they are not running one of the compromised versions and remove them as soon as possible.
"Unlike a typical vulnerability, this was not a coding mistake, and there is no patch: the malicious code was added deliberately and committed to each plugin's WordPress.org repository," Chamberland said. "Taken together, this strongly suggests that the developer's WordPress.org account was compromised and used to push the malicious releases, rather than that the vendor shipped this code intentionally."
The disclosure comes as URLscan.io revealed that an unspecified WordPress site had been infected by multiple cybercriminal campaigns, with attackers attempting to disable or remove scripts belonging to competing threat actors.
The site carried "thirteen separate ClickFix injections from three distinct kits [LOM, ErrTraffic, and Macfinger], alongside seven further malicious loaders," it said. "Several of the injections attempt to remove each other's code and overlays, and one injection disables another through a JavaScript naming collision. Five of the thirteen injections resolve their next-stage infrastructure from Polygon smart contracts, a technique known as EtherHiding."

articles.title: L’ANSM alerte sur les conseils de l’IA pour doser les médicaments
articles.text:
L'Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament a recensé en France huit cas d'effets indésirables chez des patients qui avaient suivi les conseils d'une intelligence artificielle, dont une hospitalisation. Elle vous demande de vérifier chaque réponse d'un chatbot dans la notice du médicament ou auprès d'un professionnel de santé.
Ces cas, déclarés entre 2024 et 2026, concernent des patients de 17 à 89 ans, et la moitié ont 18 ans ou moins. L'ANSM soupçonne une sous-déclaration, et son directeur général adjoint, Alexandre de la Volpilière, craint de « voir se multiplier ce genre de situation ». Selon OpenAI, plus de 300 millions de personnes posent chaque semaine des questions de santé à ChatGPT. Et d'après Alexandre de la Volpilière, les patients interrogent l'IA sur les médicaments qu'ils prennent sans ordonnance, mais aussi sur ceux que leur médecin leur a prescrits.
L'ANSM a surtout reçu des signalements d'erreurs de dose
Deux patients ont pris trop de paracétamol après avoir échangé avec une IA. Un surdosage de paracétamol peut abîmer gravement et définitivement le foie, et l'agence vous rappelle de toujours prendre la dose efficace la plus faible, le moins longtemps possible.
Une femme enceinte a avalé trop d'antimigraineux en suivant les indications d'une IA, rapporte franceinfo. L'ANSM évoque aussi des surdosages d'antiallergiques, d'antibiotiques, de sédatifs et d'anxiolytiques. Dans d'autres cas, le nom d'un médicament a été mal traduit dans des documents médicaux, et le patient a reçu le mauvais produit.
Selon l'agence, les réponses d'une IA peuvent être fausses, contradictoires ou mal adaptées à votre cas, y compris quand elles citent des sources qui ont l'air sérieuses. Et l'erreur est difficile à repérer. Dans une étude publiée en 2024, des spécialistes ont relevé quinze réponses potentiellement dangereuses de ChatGPT-4 à cent questions de vrais patients, et ces patients étaient incapables de les reconnaître.
L'ANSM vous renvoie à la notice et à votre pharmacien
Si vous interrogez un chatbot sur un médicament, l'ANSM vous demande de vérifier sa réponse dans une source officielle. Pour la dose, c'est l'ordonnance ou la notice qui fait foi. Vous avez perdu la notice ? Vous pouvez trouver sa version numérique sur la base de données publique des médicaments.
« Le patient peut se dire "Je vais mieux, j'arrête mon traitement" ou augmenter ses doses », explique Alexandre de la Volpilière. Pour changer une dose ou arrêter un traitement, l'agence vous renvoie vers votre médecin ou votre pharmacien, et elle vous demande de ne jamais confier à une IA le diagnostic de vos symptômes. « On n'augmente pas ses doses tout seul, ni en demandant à une IA. On demande à un professionnel de santé », insiste-t-il. Si vous êtes enceinte, vous devez demander l'avis d'un médecin, d'un pharmacien ou d'une sage-femme avant de prendre ou de modifier un traitement pendant la grossesse.
Après un effet indésirable ou un symptôme inhabituel, prévenez votre médecin. Vous pouvez aussi le déclarer directement sur le portail de signalement des effets indésirables du ministère de la Santé, ouvert aux patients.
OpenAI, de son côté, veut faire de ChatGPT Santé, son espace consacré aux questions médicales ouvert aux Américains, un simple complément du médecin.

articles.title: Lawsuit reveals Trump’s alleged strong-arming of Intel — troubled chipmaker allegedly forced to give White House 10% stake for release of CHIPS Act funds
articles.text:
Lawsuit alleges Trump strong-armed Intel — troubled chipmaker allegedly forced to give White House 10% stake for release of CHIPS Act funds
Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as the CEO of Nvidia wasn’t the first time that the president meddled in the business of private companies.
An Intel shareholder lawsuit against the company has revealed the extent to which President Donald Trump is allegedly willing to bend companies to his will. Richard Paisner sued the chipmaker earlier this year, saying that the White House’s 10% stake in exchange for the release of the previously granted CHIPS Act funds was unlawful. Now, Wired viewed unsealed documents from the case that allegedly showed how the president used his influence and position to strong-arm Intel’s board into accepting the deal.
Intel was already suffering from financial woes since July 2024, and its new CEO, Lip-Bu Tan, was facing scrutiny over his links to Chinese tech companies. Trump himself has called for Tan’s resignation in August 2025, calling him “highly conflicted.” The Intel chief eventually went to the White House and personally talked to the president, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. It was during this conversation that Trump said that he cooked up the 10% Intel deal. Intel was still waiting on $8.9 billion in funding from the U.S. government through the CHIPS and Science Act, but the White House allegedly wanted something in return. The president quoted himself to the Wall Street Journal telling Lip-Bu Tan, “You know what? I think the United States should be given 10% of Intel,” to which the Intel chief replied, “I would consider that.”
Court documents reveal how much pressure Intel’s leadership faced at that time. Internal notes show that a call between the company and Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro had the latter tell the former’s chief financial officer not to make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” and that “the president is expecting to announce a deal on Friday.” Furthermore, even though the government official said that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” it was also noted, “that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict.”
Because of this, Paisner and his attorney said in the complaint [PDF], “In extraordinary and expedited fashion, the Board, operating under the shadow of the President’s threat, and advised by legal counsel that itself was conflicted due to its pro bono promises to the president, caved to the government’s extortion.” Other sources also pointed out that Intel’s external legal counsel provided up to $100 million in free legal services to the Trump administration so it could avoid an executive order that would have prevented it from working with the federal government — something that the White House did to Anthropic after it refused to allow the Pentagon to use Claude for mass domestic surveillance or to control weapons systems.
Earlier this week, the president called the Nvidia board to pressure them into reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. This wasn’t the first time that Trump made a deal with the company. The AI chipmaker has previously agreed to pay 15% on its H20 sales to China so that it could be allowed to export them again, followed by an even larger 25% slice on H200 chips in December 2025.

articles.title: Windows 11 recebe atualização que muitos usuários não conseguem instalar
articles.text:
Windows 11 recebe atualização que muitos usuários não conseguem instalar
Microsoft liberou o pacote KB5132057 para os Windows 11 25H2 e 26H2, mas muitos usuários se deparam com um erro ao tentar concluir a instalação.
Uma vez por mês, a Microsoft lança um pacote opcional de atualizações para o Windows 11. Por não ser obrigatória, a sua instalação só é feita se o usuário acessar o Windows Update ou configurar a ferramenta para receber as atualizações mais recentes o quanto antes. O pacote de novembro de 2026 já foi liberado, mas há um problema: muitos usuários não conseguem instalá-lo.
O pacote em questão é o KB5132057, que é direcionado ao Windows 11 na versão 25H2, mas também pode ser instalado em PCs que já têm a atual versão 26H2. As suas principais novidades incluem (mas não se limitam a):
- experiência de busca renovada: o mecanismo de busca do Windows 11 (Windows Search) pode exibir recursos em lista única, tem ajustes de desempenho e consumo de memória, e pode lidar com erros de digitação mais facilmente;
- pesquisa aprimorada no Explorador de Arquivos: aqui, as buscas passam a ser baseadas em índices, tornando as pesquisas mais rápidas e consistentes;
- ajustes no Windows Hello: o reconhecimento facial agora pode aumentar temporariamente o brilho da tela em ambientes escuros, além de trazer melhorias na entrada com chaves de segurança.
Esses aprimoramentos justificam a instalação do pacote KB5132057. Mas é aí que os problemas começam: muitos usuários reclamam que, ao tentarem aplicar a atualização, o sistema operacional exibe uma mensagem de erro informando que o procedimento não pode ser realizado. Muitos deles seguiram a orientação de tentar de novo, mas, novamente, não tiveram sucesso.
Como a Microsoft não reconheceu o problema até o momento, não há nenhuma orientação formal sobre como proceder caso a tentativa de instalação do pacote KB5132057 resulte em uma mensagem de erro.
Houve quem conseguisse resolver o problema alterando o Registro do Windows e fazendo download manual de uma imagem do sistema operacional, mas esse é um procedimento complexo e que, talvez, não funcione para todo mundo.
Por isso, para a maioria dos usuários afetados, a recomendação é aguardar. Como o pacote KB5132057 é opcional, a sua ausência não deixará o Windows 11 perigosamente desatualizado.
Leve em conta também que os recursos de um pacote opcional costumam ser liberados pela Microsoft como parte do Patch Tuesday do mês seguinte, este sim um pacote de atualizações cumulativas de instalação obrigatória.
Isso sugere que, para quem tiver problemas com o pacote KB5132057, a solução chegará em dezembro. A gente só precisa torcer para não haver nada de errado com essa atualização (mas, convenhamos, não vai ser surpresa se houver).

articles.title: Today I learned why Tim Berners-Lee chose not to patent the World Wide Web
articles.text:
Today I learned why Tim Berners-Lee chose not to patent the World Wide Web
Giving the web away was the whole plan
Every website you've visited today runs on technology nobody owns. Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web at CERN in 1989, but he never patented it. On April 30, 1993, CERN put the web software into the public domain, giving up all rights to it.
Berners-Lee has always been blunt about why. He explained that the web only worked if everyone could use it. "In order to succeed, therefore, it would have to be free," he wrote in an op-ed for The Guardian.
The Gopher problem
In the 1990s, the World Wide Web wasn't the only way to browse the internet. A system called Gopher, built at the University of Minnesota, was actually growing faster than the web at the time, according to Berners-Lee's account on NPR.
Then in 1993, the university announced it would charge some users a fee to run Gopher servers. According to Berners-Lee, Gopher traffic dropped off almost immediately. People started asking him whether CERN would do the same to the web.
That scare pushed him to get a signed declaration from CERN guaranteeing the web would stay free. His colleague Robert Cailliau later wrote that CERN weighed licensing the software commercially before choosing the public domain. Open-source licences were still in their infancy, so giving up the rights entirely was the cleanest option.
The final document needed endorsement from CERN management and signatures from at least two directors. It was signed on April 30, 1993.
By the end of that year, more than 500 web servers were running worldwide. In November 1993, the University of Illinois' National Center for Supercomputing Applications released Mosaic, the browser that first brought the web to a mainstream audience.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Free by design
Money was never the main concern. In fact, Berners-Lee worried that a commercial stake would make it hard to stay neutral about how the web developed.
That thinking carried over into the World Wide Web Consortium, the standards body he founded at MIT in 1994 to keep the web's core technologies open. In February 2004, the consortium adopted a royalty-free patent policy, meaning companies that help write web standards must license any essential patents without charging royalties.
CERN itself credits that decision for the web's success. Rival systems like Gopher and WAIS were around too, but the web's simplicity and royalty-free status led to its rapid adoption, according to the lab.
Would a patented web have made Berners-Lee a billionaire? Possibly. It also might have gone the way of Gopher, which faded into obscurity.
In that 2025 Guardian piece, written alongside his memoir "This Is for Everyone", Berners-Lee admitted he can't picture a big tech company giving away something like the web today. The irony is that most of those companies only exist because he did.

articles.title: 1Password sufrió un ataque que expuso nombres y correos de clientes, pero no sus contraseñas
articles.text:
1Password informó que un atacante copió nombres y direcciones de correo electrónico de una parte de sus clientes tras acceder a sus sistemas internos. La empresa de gestión de contraseñas aseguró que las bóvedas de los usuarios, donde se guardan las claves, no fueron afectadas.
La compañía explicó en un comunicado publicado en su blog que la investigación comenzó el 19 de noviembre, cuando detectó indicios de que alguien había entrado en la cuenta corporativa de GitHub de un empleado. GitHub es la plataforma donde los programadores guardan y comparten el código de sus proyectos.
Con esa cuenta, el atacante accedió al código fuente y subió código malicioso a servicios internos, lo que permitió descargar datos administrativos de clientes. La empresa no informó cuántos usuarios resultaron afectados y se limitó a hablar de un subconjunto de ellos.
Qué datos se copiaron y cuáles no
Según la empresa, los registros descargados incluyen nombres y correos electrónicos, identificadores de cuenta y de usuario, y las fechas de creación de la cuenta y de su último inicio de sesión. También figuran claves públicas, que por diseño no son secretas, y parámetros técnicos del protocolo de inicio de sesión que, afirmó la compañía, no sirven para entrar en una cuenta.
El atacante copió además código fuente de repositorios privados y accedió al sistema que automatiza la construcción y publicación del software. 1Password sostuvo que el código no contiene secretos de usuarios, aunque ese sistema guarda credenciales de infraestructura, que ya fueron rotadas.
La empresa precisó que sus bóvedas, los elementos guardados en ellas y las claves que las protegen no se vieron afectados. Tampoco las claves de recuperación de cuenta, las aplicaciones ni las extensiones para navegadores. La compañía indicó que no almacena la contraseña de la cuenta ni la clave secreta de los usuarios.
Los enlaces de invitación y recuperación
Entre los datos copiados hay tokens, códigos incluidos en enlaces de correos de invitación, aprovisionamiento y recuperación de cuenta. Solo un número reducido de usuarios estaba en alguno de esos procesos durante el incidente, y fueron notificados de forma individual.
Esos tokens no dan acceso por sí solos: se necesitan además un inicio de sesión mediante SSO (acceso con las credenciales de la organización) o un código enviado al correo registrado del usuario. Como medida preventiva, 1Password amplió ese código de seis a diez caracteres alfanuméricos, lo que, según la empresa, vuelve prácticamente imposible adivinarlo por fuerza bruta.
1Password afirmó que no encontró pruebas de que se haya tomado el control de ninguna cuenta con los tokens expuestos, y que sus servicios funcionan con normalidad.
Cómo reaccionó la empresa
La compañía desactivó la cuenta de GitHub comprometida, revocó el token robado y eliminó el acceso que el atacante había creado. También rotó o revocó las credenciales internas que pudieron quedar expuestas, reforzó los controles del sistema de publicación de software y de los equipos de sus empleados, y sumó nuevas detecciones para este tipo de ataque.
Además, contrató a expertos independientes en ciberseguridad para validar las tareas de contención y reparación. La empresa aclaró que los usuarios no necesitan cambiar nada en su cuenta.
El riesgo que subraya la compañía es el phishing, mensajes falsos que buscan engañar a la víctima. Los nombres y correos copiados permiten enviar mensajes dirigidos. 1Password recomienda desconfiar de correos, mensajes o llamadas inesperados que mencionen la aplicación, invitaciones o intentos de recuperación de cuenta que el usuario no inició. La empresa recordó que nunca pide la contraseña de la cuenta ni la clave secreta, que solo deben escribirse en la aplicación oficial o en su sitio web, abierto por el propio usuario.

articles.title: Le Sénat va lancer une commission d’enquête sur les cyberattaques et les fuites de données
articles.text:
Le Sénat va créer une commission d'enquête sur les cyberattaques et les fuites de données subies depuis trois ans par l'État et les entreprises françaises. Ses 21 membres auront six mois pour établir les responsabilités et proposer de nouvelles règles, avec un rapport attendu en avril ou en mai 2027.
Nathalie Goulet, sénatrice centriste de l'Orne, réclamait cette enquête depuis le mois de mai, quelques semaines après le piratage de l'Agence nationale des titres sécurisés (ANTS) et de ses 11,7 millions de comptes. « C'est France passoire ! », lançait-elle alors à Public Sénat. Mais son groupe, l'Union centriste, avait consommé en février son droit de tirage, qui permet à chaque groupe du Sénat d'obtenir une commission d'enquête ou une mission par an. Il vient de l'utiliser pour ce projet, a fait savoir la sénatrice mercredi. Entre-temps, les fuites se sont enchaînées à la DGFiP et à l'Éducation nationale, au point de relancer le hashtag #FrancePassoire. Et en deux mois, l'ANSSI a reçu 99 signalements de fuites présumées dans les ministères.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Les sénateurs pourront interroger l'ANSSI et les ministères sous serment
La commission devra d'abord dresser le bilan des attaques subies par les administrations, les entreprises et les opérateurs d'importance vitale. Ces opérateurs sont les organismes, publics ou privés, dont la panne mettrait le pays en difficulté, dans l'énergie, les transports ou la santé. Les sénateurs mesureront ensuite les moyens de l'ANSSI et de son centre d'alerte, le CERT-FR, pour repérer une attaque, la contrer et réparer les dégâts. Ils étudieront aussi la dépendance de l'État aux prestataires informatiques non européens.
Nathalie Goulet dit observer dans les ministères et chez les opérateurs de l'État des « problèmes manifestes de priorisation et d'organisation du cyber ». Pour les comprendre, la commission dispose de pouvoirs plus larges qu'une simple mission d'information. Toute personne convoquée doit venir témoigner sous serment, et refuser est un délit, selon l'ordonnance de 1958 sur le fonctionnement des assemblées. Le président du groupe centriste, Hervé Marseille, a écrit le 23 novembre au président du Sénat pour obtenir cette commission, affirme le hacker éthique Clément Domingo, alias SaxX. Selon lui, la conférence des présidents, qui organise les travaux du Sénat, doit prendre acte de la demande la semaine prochaine, sans vote, et les premières auditions pourraient commencer vers la mi-décembre.
Le groupe centriste veut aussi que la commission prenne en compte les victimes d'usurpation d'identité, selon l'AFP. Si vos données ont fuité lors de l'un de ces piratages, sachez toutefois qu'une commission d'enquête rend un rapport et des propositions de loi, et que l'indemnisation des victimes relève des tribunaux.
La commission contrôlera l'application de NIS 2
Les sénateurs devront aussi vérifier si la France applique bien NIS 2, la directive européenne qui impose des règles de cybersécurité à près de 20 000 organismes, des hôpitaux aux collectivités, selon le gouvernement. Bruxelles demandait sa transposition avant octobre 2024. Le projet de loi Résilience, qui la transpose, a été reporté une nouvelle fois en octobre, avant d'être adopté par les députés le 17 novembre, par 464 voix contre 64. Avec ce texte, l'ANSSI pourrait obliger votre hôpital ou votre opérateur télécom victime d'une attaque à vous prévenir, voire annoncer l'incident à sa place.
La commission travaillera donc pendant que le gouvernement écrit les décrets d'application. Deux jours après le vote, le Premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu, a promis ces décrets dans les prochaines semaines, en présentant son plan de cybersécurité. Il impose aussi à chaque ministère de consacrer à la cybersécurité 5 % de son budget numérique dès 2027, puis 10 % en 2030. Il faut encore que députés et sénateurs s'accordent sur une version commune de la loi Résilience, en commission mixte paritaire, à une date encore inconnue.

articles.title: No Man's Sky Gets FSR 4 in Latest Update
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
No Man's Sky Gets FSR 4 in Latest Update
Following the launch of two massive content updates earlier in 2026, No Man's Sky has officially been updated to version 7.15S, bringing a bunch of new holiday content to the sci-fi exploration game. Arguably the most important change to land in No Man's Sky 7.15, however, is the addition of AMD FSR 4. As explained by No Man's Sky's engine programmer, Martin Griffiths, in a post on X, this update to FSR 4 was only made possible thanks to the recent release of AMD's FSR SDK 2.4, which added Vulkan support to FSR 4, where it previously only supported DirectX 12. This will ostensibly enable higher quality upscaling with fewer artifacts, while still maintaining many of the performance benefits of upscaling.

There are several potential performance pitfalls to consider when purchasing a new HDD, and the type of recording technology is one of the most crucial factors. Unless you are solely interested in cost and willing to sacrifice performance, we only recommend conventional magnetic recording (CMR) drives and not shingled (SMR), as the latter comes with performance and operational caveats.
- For performance, HDDs are also often gauged by rotations per minute (RPM), which is usually a direct indicator of performance. The RPM value affects both sequential transfers and random access latency. Lower RPM drives tend to be quieter and more efficient, while higher RPM drives have better performance. There are also variable RPM drives that try to achieve the best of both worlds. Power draw, heat, and noise are factors related to performance.
- HDDs also have a certain amount of DRAM to help temporarily cache data. This amount of cache typically scales with the drive's capacity. More cache is, of course, better, but if it comes at the expense of something else — for example, a support service — then you should carefully consider your priorities when making a purchase.
- You will want specialized drives for NAS, surveillance/DVR/NVR, raw storage for media and backups, or for heavier workloads. Certain drives will offer a better value for the money if you just want the extra capacity, or you may require a lower RPM drive to avoid the noise associated with faster drives.

articles.title: Pendant le Black Friday 2026, ce téléviseur OLED LG noté 5/5 perd 331,00 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le téléviseur LG 77G6 "5 étoiles" à 2 599,00 € (-11%)
Actuellement noté 5/5 par notre rédaction, le téléviseur LG 77G6 associe le contraste parfait de l'Oled à un filtre antireflet efficace et d'excellentes prestations pour le jeu vidéo. Le Black Friday 2026 est l'occasion de se l'offrir moins cher : il passe à 2 599,00 € chez Boulanger.com, soit une baisse d'environ 11 % et 331,00 € d'économie.
Le LG 77G6 perfectionne la formule Oled haut de gamme de la marque avec une dalle plus lumineuse, un traitement antireflet revu et une section sonore retravaillée. Conçu pour offrir une expérience cinéma et jeu vidéo sans compromis sur une grande diagonale, le successeur du G5 avait convaincu notre laboratoire.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, ce téléviseur descend à 2 599,00 € chez Boulanger.com, soit environ 11 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours. Cela représente une économie de 331,00 €.
Une dalle Oled lumineuse et taillée pour le jeu
Sur ce modèle 4K de 77 pouces, l'affichage profite du contraste absolu propre aux pixels auto-émissifs et d'une gestion efficace des reflets en pièce éclairée. Comme détaillé dans notre test complet, notre laboratoire a mesuré un pic de luminosité maximale à 2340 cd/m², assurant un rendu percutant des contenus en Dolby Vision ou HDR10.
Les amateurs de jeu vidéo profitent d'une réactivité exemplaire grâce aux quatre connecteurs HDMI 2.1 compatibles 165 Hz et G-Sync. Le banc d'essai a relevé un retard à l'affichage limité à 9.3 ms, ce qui garantit une excellente fluidité des commandes pour les parties rapides sur console ou PC.
LG 77G6
Points forts
- Contraste parfait de l’Oled.
- Forte luminosité HDR.
- Antireflet efficace.
- Colorimétrie HDR et qualité d'image remarquable.
- Très bonnes performances en jeu vidéo.
- Quatre ports HDMI 2.1, 165 Hz, G-Sync.
- Consommation très maîtrisée.
- Bon système son.
Points faibles
- Luminosité qui stagne par rapport au G5, hormis sur les petites fenêtres.
- Spatialisation audio encore limitée.
- Télécommande non rétroéclairée.
- Compte LG désormais obligatoire.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une image soignée malgré une ergonomie perfectible
La fidélité colorimétrique se montre irréprochable avec une consommation d'énergie mesurée à seulement 48.7 W/m², particulièrement sobre pour un écran de cette envergure. L'appareil demande toutefois la création d'un compte constructeur pour exploiter le système WebOS, et sa télécommande fait l'impasse sur le rétroéclairage des touches, des détails qui ne dérangeront pas ceux qui privilégient avant tout la qualité d'image brute.
LG 77C6 : l'autre option face au LG 77G6
Au sein du même catalogue, le LG 77C6 partage la diagonale de 77 pouces et la note maximale de 5 étoiles avec son grand frère. Il récupère d'ailleurs la technologie de dalle du G6 pour délivrer un contraste infini, une excellente colorimétrie et des prestations de premier ordre pour le jeu vidéo, tout en contenant son tarif.
Le LG 77G6 conserve néanmoins une luminosité supérieure et un meilleur contrôle des reflets, mais le LG 77C6 coûte 600,00 € de moins à son prix actuel.

Points forts
- Contraste parfait de l’Oled.

articles.title: Cómo compartir la ubicación exacta solo por un tiempo limitado en WhatsApp
articles.text:
WhatsApp permite compartir la ubicación exacta de un usuario durante un período determinado, tanto en chats individuales como en grupos, mediante una función cifrada de extremo a extremo que impide que terceros accedan a esos datos.
Quien envía la ubicación en tiempo real decide cuánto tiempo estará disponible esa información para sus contactos. Una vez cumplido ese plazo, o si la persona decide interrumpir el envío antes, los destinatarios dejan de ver la posición en el mapa, según indica el Centro de ayuda de WhatsApp.
Cómo activar los permisos de ubicación en Android
Para que WhatsApp pueda acceder a la ubicación del teléfono, primero hay que habilitar el permiso correspondiente desde el sistema operativo. El procedimiento comienza en Ajustes, dentro del menú Aplicaciones. Allí debe seleccionarse WhatsApp y luego ingresar a Permisos y a Ubicación.
Dentro de esa sección existen tres opciones disponibles: Permitir solo con la app en uso, Preguntar siempre y No permitir. La elección de cualquiera de estas alternativas condiciona el funcionamiento posterior de la ubicación en tiempo real.
Cómo habilitar la ubicación en dispositivos con iOS
En los equipos con sistema operativo de Apple, el camino para autorizar el acceso a la ubicación es distinto, aunque el objetivo es el mismo. Desde Configuración, hay que ingresar a Privacidad y seguridad y luego a Servicios de ubicación, donde debe buscarse la aplicación WhatsApp dentro del listado.
En ese punto se puede seleccionar entre dos modalidades: Siempre o Al usar la app. Esta configuración determina si WhatsApp puede acceder a la posición del dispositivo en todo momento o únicamente mientras la aplicación permanece abierta.
Pasos para compartir la ubicación en tiempo real desde un chat
Una vez otorgados los permisos, compartir la ubicación exacta requiere ingresar a una conversación individual o grupal dentro de la aplicación.
El siguiente paso consiste en tocar el ícono para adjuntar contenido, identificado con un clip de papel en Android y con un signo más en iOS. Dentro de ese menú debe elegirse la opción Ubicación y luego Compartir ubicación en tiempo real.
Ahora bien, en caso de que el sistema solicite una confirmación adicional, en Android aparece el botón Continuar, mientras que en iOS se presenta como OK.
Selección del tiempo y envío de la ubicación
El paso siguiente es elegir durante cuánto tiempo permanecerá activa la ubicación en tiempo real. Transcurrido ese período, el envío se corta de manera automática y los contactos dejan de visualizar la posición.
Antes de finalizar el envío, existe la posibilidad de añadir un comentario o emojis junto a la ubicación compartida, un detalle que puede resultar útil para quienes no conocen el mapa de la zona o no cuentan con una referencia clara del punto donde se encuentra la persona.
Para completar la acción, debe presionarse el ícono de enviar, representado por un avión de papel dentro de un círculo, que en iOS se distingue además por su color verde.
Cómo programar mensajes en WhatsApp con hasta dos semanas de anticipación en chats
WhatsApp sumó la posibilidad de programar mensajes, una función que permite redactar un texto en cualquier momento y definir que se envíe entre 10 minutos y 14 días más tarde.
La herramienta funciona tanto en chats individuales como en grupos, y acerca a la aplicación a prestaciones que ya existían en servicios de correo electrónico como Gmail y Outlook.
La función apunta a resolver situaciones habituales en las que el mensaje ya está escrito, pero conviene enviarlo en otro momento. Entre los usos posibles figura el envío de un saludo de cumpleaños justo a la medianoche en el huso horario del destinatario, el recordatorio de una reunión de trabajo o un mensaje de aliento antes de un examen, sin necesidad de estar atento al reloj para enviarlo manualmente.
Para programar un envío, el usuario debe escribir el mensaje dentro del chat individual o grupal correspondiente y luego mantener presionado el botón de enviar. En ese momento, WhatsApp despliega la opción de elegir la fecha y la hora en que se concretará la entrega.
El rango disponible para programar un mensaje va de 10 minutos a un máximo de 14 días. Una vez definido el horario, el mensaje queda almacenado en la plataforma y se envía de manera automática cuando se cumple el plazo establecido por quien lo redactó.
La incorporación de esta función no modificó el funcionamiento del envío de fotos y videos configurados para verse una sola vez, que mantiene el mismo proceso ya existente en la aplicación.

articles.title: Ubuntu Details AI Desktop Integration: "Optional, Local-First, Privacy and Security by Design"
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Ubuntu Details AI Desktop Integration: "Optional, Local-First, Privacy and Security by Design"
Generative AI has been a touchy subject in the vocal open-source community, and one proposed solution by those trying to toe the line but still use AI has been local models, and it seems as though Ubuntu will be taking that same approach with its new AI integration on the Linux desktop. According to a new announcement, Ubuntu will also be implementing AI in almost an opposite way compared to how Microsoft handled it in Windows. 
As Ubuntu's Didier Roche explains in the discussion post, Ubuntu will not be implementing AI on an app-by-app basis or by "scattering disconnected AI widgets across the desktop." Ubuntu's plan, instead, is to have a "unified, keyboard and speech-friendly entry point that bridges your apps, your local context, and smart assistance only when you explicitly ask for it." This will take the form of an app called warty, which features a UX similar to a typical launcher (like Krunner or the launcher in Gnome's Overview page).Roche also established four key principles for the development of Gnome's new AI interface:
- Strictly optional: It is your machine. All AI capabilities are strictly opt-in. If you want a pure, ultra-fast advanced launcher without enabling any AI features, that experience is first-class out of the box (and we aren't shipping gigabytes of models in the default install).
- Local-first: Our priority is on-device inference running against local models on your own hardware, rather than sending your queries to external cloud services by default.
- Privacy-first: Because processing happens locally, your files, local context, and daily habits stay where they belong: on your disk.
- Security-first: Leveraging Ubuntu's confinement and sandboxing architecture, the components powering these features are designed to run with strict isolation so that experimental or agentic capabilities cannot compromise your host system.
Judging by the wording, users will be able to use their own local AI models or connect Warty to a cloud AI provider, and it also sounds as though Ubuntu's default apps will all only have AI integrations through Warty, instead of Microsoft's mishmash of Copilot integrations throughout the Windows desktop. Ubuntu's dev team expects to be able to show off more of the AI integration in January 2027 alongside an installable version of the app.

articles.title: Uber et Nuro lancent les tests de robotaxis sans chauffeur avant 2027
articles.text:
Uber a depuis un certain temps annoncé son intention de lancer des robotaxis. Et ça se matérialise du côté de la Californie !
Pour ne pas finir en témoignage d'une autre époque, Uber souhaite faire un saut qualitatif qui lui permettra de proposer un service de taxi autonome. Et dans ce domaine, le géant américain a forgé un partenariat avec Lucid et Nuro, présenté en début d'année. Un partenariat qui donne rapidement ses fruits, comme on le voit du côté de l'ouest des États-Unis !
Uber et Nuro testent déjà les robotaxis à San Francisco actuellement
Uber et Nuro mettent déjà actuellement à l'essai la version du SUV Lucid Gravity bénéficiant de la conduite autonome dans les rues de San Francisco. Des essais qui ont lieu à peine six mois après avoir obtenu l'autorisation de mettre sur les routes des véhicules sans le chauffeur de sécurité.
Cette montée en puissance des robotaxis d'Uber devrait permettre d'ici peu de passer à une nouvelle étape, avec des trajets en robotaxis qui vont être offerts aux employés. Une rapidité qui peut au moins confirmer la pertinence des investissements consentis par Uber.
Un lancement commercial pour les premiers mois de 2027
La plateforme pour VTC a en effet à l'origine annoncé que ce partenariat entraînait de sa part un investissement de près de 500 millions de dollars dans Nuro, et de 300 millions de dollars dans Lucid (qui a depuis gonflé jusqu'à 500 millions de dollars). Après les essais, Uber compte avancer rapidement, et programme les premiers trajets commerciaux de ses robotaxis pour le premier trimestre 2027, dans l'agglomération de San Francisco.
À noter qu'au-delà de la Californie, Uber et Nuro sont aussi en train de tester des robotaxis sur les routes de Houston (Texas), avec cette fois la présence d'un chauffeur de sécurité encore au volant. Mais avec les progrès d'Uber dans le domaine, on imagine que le service va rapidement devenir un concurrent crédible dans ce domaine aux États-Unis. Et quand en Europe ?

articles.title: EU Rules Bring New Safety Requirements for Farm Robots
articles.text:
Digitalization and advancements in new technologies are making farming operations smarter, more automated, and more sustainable. But are these technologies explicitly safe to implement in agricultural settings?
There are already autonomous systems, including robots, drones, automated tractors, and AI-guided machines in the field that perform seed planting tasks, selective chemical spraying, mechanical weed control, milking, and feeding animals, and some prototype robots are now even picking apples in orchards. A lot of these are self-navigating and work with little-to-no human input.
These machines and robotic systems make farming operations more efficient and help reduce costs. But as machines ‘think’ and operate with less and less human input, an obvious question arises: Can they be trusted as much as when humans are fully in control?
The answer is not straightforward. While the technical aspects to consider are fairly well-established today, the definition of an autonomous system and who is responsible if something goes wrong is a lot more ambiguous and less clear-cut. Mandatory EU regulations coming into effect soon are set to quell this ambiguity and improve overall safety on farms where robots and other autonomous and AI-driven systems are part of everyday operations.
The AI and autonomous technologies being deployed
AI-driven and autonomous technologies are being deployed across a range of farming activities, from crop cultivation and soil analysis to irrigation management, fertilizer and pesticide spraying, weed removal, crop monitoring, field mapping, apple picking, and animal husbandry. Some tasks can be handled by a single robot, while others require a swarm of robots to cover a wider area. Applications include autonomous tractors that operate in fields at night, robotic sprayers that self-navigate rows of crops or trees, or a drone swarm overhead equipped with advanced sensors to monitor plant growth, identify growth-related problems, and spot potential threats to plant and soil health.
Many of these systems are driven by AI or have AI-enabled capabilities that help them navigate the field autonomously. AI allows these robotic and autonomous systems to process data a lot faster and handle larger volumes of data than systems without AI or machine learning (ML). This enables more efficient planning, earlier detection of potential problems before they become a big issue (including issues that might have otherwise been missed), and predictive capabilities that support a wide array of farming operations. However, replacing human workers in the field with AI-enabled machines doesn’t mean that there are fewer risks; it simply introduces different risks that need to be taken into account.
Lack of clarity could bring safety risks
Autonomous systems operating in the field face a number of inherent technical risks. What if fail-safes stop working and the robot hits a person? What if collision-free navigation is impacted by misaligned sensor fusion or dust on the sensor? Will the uneven terrain affect the locomotion and stability of some robots, making them unsafe?
Many of these technical aspects have been addressed, but anchoring the safety of autonomous systems in standards and regulations requires a lot more clarity around what an autonomous system actually is. More clarity is also needed on responsibility. Autonomous systems equipped with AI do not remove responsibility from the farm if something goes wrong, so farmers need clearer guidance and must understand that they are not immune to safety infractions if the technology goes awry.
The current EU Machinery Directive and harmonized standards, such as ISO 12100:2010, do not use the term ‘autonomous’. As with ‘artificial intelligence’, the term ‘autonomous’ is open to interpretation, and European regulations have suffered the same fate, with many different interpretations of what an ‘autonomous’ system is. In the automotive sector, there is a sliding scale created by the Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE), which has been widely adopted across industries, ranging from Level 0 to Level 5 based on the degree of driving automation. Therefore, one person’s perception of autonomy may be different from someone else’s.
Autonomy is typically defined in terms of the activity and behavior of a machine. There is also the argument that a machine is always automated because the activities are carried out by the machine regardless of whether there has been human input or not. More complex tasks typically require some level of human oversight, whereas more basic tasks do not.
To make automated machines safe, accountable, and responsible in the field, understanding what constitutes autonomy—and what doesn’t—is an important distinction that needs to be clarified through closer scrutiny. If machines are still meant to have human oversight, but workers allow them to operate on their own because they are ‘autonomous’, it could lead to various safety issues and hazardous situations.
So, a greater degree of clarity will enable farmers and their workers to better understand which systems can be left on their own with minimal oversight and which systems need more robust monitoring and oversight to ensure that all automated and semi-automated operations in the field remain safe and hazard-free.
For situations where humans are not responsible for oversight and spotting hazardous situations, the operating environment needs to be designed so that hazards don’t manifest, or there needs to be a separate monitoring system (such as a machine learning-based system or overhead drone imaging) in place to spot hazards and alert the autonomous robots/vehicles before they encounter them. Knowing which systems need this level of design and which don’t because humans will be looking over them is not only relevant from a safety perspective but also from a cost and infrastructure perspective, as the extra technology should only be installed where it is needed (as it increases the complexity of farming infrastructure).
How new European policies are looking to make autonomous farming safer
There are a couple of new regulations coming within the EU that should help clarify the ‘what is an autonomous machine’ situation and how they are deployed safely in the field. The first is the new EU 2023/1230 regulation on machinery. Although it came into effect in 2023, it will apply to all EU member states from Jan. 20, 2027, replacing the Machinery Directive that has governed machinery since 2006.
This regulation includes ‘autonomous mobile machinery’, which it defines in relation to machinery that performs safety functions while moving and operating without continuous operator intervention.
The regulation covers certain categories of machinery incorporating safety components with fully or partially self-evolving, machine-learning-based behavior that ensure safety functions, and machinery with embedded systems of this kind. These are listed in Annex I, Part A of the regulation and require conformity assessment by a notified body. This does not mean that all machinery using AI or ML is automatically classified as high risk or requires third-party certification.
But the regulation goes beyond this. Where relevant, autonomous mobile machinery will need to have a mandatory ‘supervisory function’ related to the autonomous mode, which will allow the machine to be stopped or started remotely to move it to a safe place where it cannot create further risk. If autonomous systems do not include this, they will no longer be compliant. However, machinery lawfully placed on the market before Jan. 20, 2027, stays lawful. The obligation applies to new machinery placed on the market from that date.
Farm owners also need to evaluate any risks when buying the equipment, especially AI technology, and be aware of any updates, changes, and new risk assessments released by the manufacturer. Finally, autonomous machines also need to log and store all data in case there is an accident or safety incident, as this increases transparency and accountability of the autonomous systems used on the farm.
The other key act is the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689). This came into effect on Aug. 1, 2024, and became generally applicable on Aug. 2, 2026. Compliance requirements are being added for high-risk AI systems in agricultural vehicles. This was initially planned for August 2027, but the deadline has recently been moved to Aug. 2, 2028. In this context, not all AI systems used in machinery are automatically classified as high risk. Under the EU AI Act, classification depends on specific criteria, including whether the AI system is a safety component of a regulated product under EU product safety law or is a regulated product itself, or whether the machine requires third-party conformity assessment before being placed on the EU market.
Machinery that is deemed to be high risk under EU product safety laws must meet requirements for transparency, documentation, and human oversight. Farmers who deploy high-risk AI systems will have to use them in line with the manufacturer’s instructions and implement human oversight.
These changes mean that farmers are going to need to be more robust in their documentation and compliance with stricter guidelines. This is going to include more formal risk assessments, maintaining stricter records, defining operating zones and protocols to ensure that autonomous machines work within clear and strict boundaries, and training staff to monitor the machinery and react if there is an incident. All these procedures will help to make farms that use autonomous machines safer.
These new regulations represent important steps toward defining autonomous systems and establishing the measures farms will need to put in place to keep personnel, visitors, and the robots themselves safe. The onus on workplace safety, however, has not changed. Farmers have been responsible for the safety of their personnel, and the onus is still on the farm to keep their workers safe even if the technology operates without direct human control. While the regulations go some way to improving the safety of autonomous machines in smart farms, there are still challenges to sort out about the allocation of liability if there is a failure with a machine. As regulations evolve alongside emerging and maturing technologies, it is almost certain that other issues and edge cases will be addressed in the coming years.

Gaming PC Specifications to look for
When looking for a new gaming PC, you need to pay special attention to specs. More recent and more powerful components are better, but this increases the overall price of the system. You can sometimes find gaming rigs that have last-generation parts that will still play games well and save some cash.
GPU: A choice between Nvidia, AMD, or Intel in your system will determine how well the computer game graphics are displayed on your monitor. Nvidia has the most powerful GPUs, with the likes of the RTX 5090 and RTX 5080, but AMD's RX 9070 XT is also a great mid-range card. See our GPU hierarchy for an idea of GPU performance.
CPU: Either AMD or Intel will get the job done, but AMD currently rules the roost in pure gaming benchmarks, with the 9000-series X3D processors providing the best performance.
Memory: At a minimum, you'll want 16GB of RAM. Operating systems and browsers can swallow a huge chunk of your available system RAM before you even boot your game. Having 32GB of memory is ideal for gaming if you can splurge.
Storage: With the size of AAA games constantly expanding, you ideally want a minimum of 1TB of storage, preferably in the form of a fast M.2 SSD. You can do better than a spinning hard drive.
