- Aucune limite d’envoi : Notre test relève des vitesses de transfert et une taille de fichier non plafonnées, utiles pour des rushs vidéo ou des images disque.
Photos, sauvegardes, mots de passe : ce que le pack couvre
Avec 3 To, le plan Premium absorbe une photothèque familiale, des vidéos lourdes et la sauvegarde d’un ordinateur. Sur mobile, l’envoi automatique copie la pellicule vers pCloud Photos, qui classe les clichés dans une chronologie. Notre test de pCloud décrit aussi une sauvegarde de dossiers sans limite de taille, tout en rappelant qu’elle ressemble plus à un miroir qu’à une archive figée.
Le pack vise surtout ceux qui comptent garder leur cloud plusieurs années : notre test situe le seuil de rentabilité d’un plan à vie 2 To autour de quatre ans face à l’abonnement annuel, et le ticket de 579 € demande ici plus de patience. Pass Premium ajoute un nombre illimité de mots de passe, le remplissage automatique et le partage chiffré. L’offre est moins pertinente si vous ne stockez que quelques gigaoctets, car des formules gratuites suffisent, ou si vous cherchez un cloud d’équipe, dont les fonctions avancées sont réservées à l’édition Business.
Face à kDrive, Proton Drive et aux clouds américains
Notre comparatif des meilleurs stockages en ligne place pCloud en tête, à 9,1/10, devant kDrive (8,7/10) et Proton Drive (8,3/10). Parmi les dix services comparés, seuls pCloud, Icedrive et Internxt vendent une licence à vie. Google Drive, OneDrive et Dropbox restent des abonnements soumis au Cloud Act américain, contrairement à la juridiction suisse de pCloud.
✅ Les points forts
- Trois licences à vie pour 579 €, soit 62 % de moins que le total affiché
- Chiffrement côté client inclus dans le pack
- Vitesses d’envoi et taille de fichier sans limite

- « À vie » signifie 99 ans de service et dépend de la pérennité de l’entreprise
- 579 € à payer d’un coup, avec un amortissement plus long que pour un plan 2 To
- Aucun audit indépendant du chiffrement publié par pCloud, selon notre test
- Offre non cumulable, remboursement possible pendant 14 jours seulement

Cette remise de 62 % ne vaut que si vous gardez le service longtemps, car « à vie » correspond à 99 ans et suppose que l’entreprise tienne dans la durée. Notre test attribue à pCloud 9,1/10 et la première place de sa sélection 2026, tout en notant l’absence d’audit indépendant du chiffrement.
Ce pack convient à qui veut en finir avec les abonnements de stockage et de mots de passe, et dispose de 579 € d’un coup. Il peut passer son chemin s’il stocke peu de données, s’il cherche un cloud d’équipe ou s’il veut un chiffrement de bout en bout sur tous ses fichiers sans supplément : notre test cite alors Proton Drive ou Internxt comme plus adaptés. articles.title: La Guardia Civil encuentra bajo un parque infantil de Granada un búnker de 180 metros con más de 2.000 plantas de marihuana
articles.text:
En una finca de Las Gabias, a las afueras de Granada, se construyó un rincón pensado para no levantar sospechas: césped artificial, un columpio, una casita de juegos y una colchoneta. Cualquier vecino, o cualquier agente, habría visto lo que era, el típico espacio para niños. Debajo, la Guardia Civil encontró una instalación subterránea de unos 180 metros cuadrados y 5 metros de altura con dos salas de cultivo de marihuana.
La operación, bautizada como Nazarí-Sabika 04, se ha saldado esta semana con con 13 registros, 5 detenidos, 3 investigados más y 2.479 plantas intervenidas. Según el instituto armado, es el zulo de cultivo más grande y sofisticado jamás visto en la provincia.
Parque infantil con rampa industrial. Parte del terreno estaba cubierto con césped artificial y varios juegos. El resto era piedra blanca decorativa. Bajo ese decorado se ocultaba un portón abatible de grandes dimensiones con un sistema de apertura hidráulico, que también se podía accionar a mano desde una pequeña trampilla cuadrada.
Tras retirar el césped y acceder a esa trampilla, los agentes accedieron a una rampa por la que podían entrar vehículos directamente. Ideal para cargar y descargar. No en vano, en el garaje cabía perfectamente una furgoneta. Dentro, dos habitaciones amplias albergaban 1.954 plantas de cannabis, con iluminación, ventilación y climatización pensadas para una producción intensiva. Las 525 restantes de las 2.479 intervenidas estaban ya en las otras dos plantaciones de la red.
Cuánto vale. La Guardia Civil no ha facilitado una valoración de la droga, pero se puede estimar con la cuenta habitual: con un rendimiento de entre 50 y 100 gramos aprovechables por planta, las 1.954 del zulo darían entre 98 y 195 kilos de cogollo por cosecha. Al precio medio de 6,42 euros el gramo que recoge la Monografía sobre Cannabis 2025, hablamos de entre 630.000 euros y 1,25 millones por ciclo. En un interior, con luz artificial y clima controlado, el ciclo se puede repetir perfectamente varias veces al año.
El enganche. Ninguna instalación así sobrevive con un contrato normal de luz. Los investigadores localizaron una torreta eléctrica desde la cual se hacía la conexión a la red. El consumo detectado en la finca equivalía al de alrededor de un centenar de viviendas. Es un patrón conocido: según datos de Endesa, las plantaciones ya concentran el 37% de la energía recuperada en fraudes eléctricos de la compañía, y cada una gasta de media como unas 80 viviendas. Los enganches directos, además, provocan sobrecargas que han incendiado centros de transformación en Sevilla y Granada.
La tienda. La operación incluyó también el precintado de una nave comercial especializada en material de cultivo de cannabis, un grow shop que la Guardia Civil estima en varios millones de euros y cuyo propietario sería el presunto responsable principal de la red. Los agentes sospechan que de ahí salía el equipamiento para la plantación de Las Gabias y que servía además para abastecer a otras organizaciones.
En los registros se intervinieron dos turismos, dos furgonetas, una caravana, un remolque, 22.970 euros en efectivo y una pistola eléctrica tipo táser. El juez ha decretado prisión provisional para el supuesto cabecilla. A los investigados se les atribuyen cultivo y elaboración de drogas, defraudación de fluido eléctrico, tenencia ilícita de arma prohibida y pertenencia a grupo criminal. Todo delito es presunto: la investigación sigue abierta.
Granada, otra vez. El caso no es una rareza en la provincia. En octubre de 2025, la operación Nazarí 64 Falla dejó 35 detenidos y 16.870 plantas incautadas en Granada, Málaga y Valencia. Entre finales de septiembre y principios de octubre de este año, otro despliegue se resolvió con 7.382 plantas y 17 detenidos en 15 localidades granadinas, con cultivos escondidos hasta tras una alacena de cocina.
En julio, Aduanas y Guardia Civil intervinieron 673 plantas en Padul y Cónchar-Villamena; en septiembre, 742 en Alhendín, donde un incendio por un cortocircuito en una instalación ilegal destapó la trama. A escala europea, según el último Informe Europeo sobre Drogas, España concentró en 2024 el 75% de todas las plantas de cannabis incautadas en la UE.
Lo novedoso de Las Gabias es el disfraz, absolutamente profesionalizado, lo cual requiere la ayuda implícita de electricistas, albañiles y operarios para sacar tanta tierra (recordemos: más de 5 metros de altura). Ante las posibles quejas por olor, aquí la organización apostó por esconderlas literalmente bajo un columpio y a vivir.

Lors des mesures effectuées pour notre test complet, la dalle a délivré un pic lumineux de 1400 cd/m², ce qui assure des reflets spéculaires intenses sur les contenus HDR. La fidélité colorimétrique se montre irréprochable avec un Delta E mesuré à 1,6 en SDR, une valeur inférieure au seuil de perception humaine qui garantit le respect total des teintes voulues par les réalisateurs.
LG 55C6
Points forts
- Qualité d’image globale très convaincante.
- Contraste parfait de l'Oled.
- Excellente colorimétrie.
- Très bonnes performances en jeu vidéo.
- Quatre ports HDMI 2.1.
- Système audio efficace.
Points faibles
- Les reflets sont visibles.
- Spatialisation audio encore limitée.
- Luminosité pas au niveau des meilleurs TV.
- Télécommande non rétroéclairée.
- Compte LG désormais obligatoire.
Fluidité à 165 Hz et équipement complet pour les joueurs
Ce modèle intègre quatre prises HDMI 2.1 capables de gérer un flux 4K jusqu'à 165 Hz, tout en maintenant un retard à l'affichage très bas mesuré à 9,3 ms. Ce temps de réponse court assure une réactivité sans décalage pour brancher simultanément un PC et les consoles actuelles. La dalle conserve toutefois une réflectance mesurée à 26 %, ce qui laissera apparaître des reflets gênants en pleine journée mais ne posera aucune difficulté dans une pièce aux rideaux tirés ou pour les séances nocturnes.
Philips 55OLED811 : l'autre option face au LG 55C6
Le Philips 55OLED811 partage la même note de 5/5 et propose lui aussi une dalle Oled à 165 Hz dotée de quatre ports HDMI 2.1. Il se distingue par l'intégration du système d'éclairage Ambilight, mais son interface Titan OS se montre moins fluide que le système WebOS de LG au quotidien.
Le Philips 55OLED811 coûte 100,00 € de plus que le LG 55C6, ce dernier conservant l'avantage d'une interface logicielle plus mature pour un tarif inférieur.
Philips 55OLED811
Points forts
- Excellente colorimétrie SDR et HDR
- Calibration globale.
- Contraste parfait et noirs profonds de l’Oled.
- Pic lumineux en nette hausse par rapport à l'OLED810.
- Quatre ports HDMI 2.1 et dalle 165 Hz.
- Pied orientable.
- Ambilight toujours sympathique.
Points faibles
- Titan OS encore loin d'être abouti.
- Reflets bien présents.
- Basses qui font grésiller le châssis.
- Consommation assez élevée.

articles.title: AI server giants including HPE, Dell and more are reportedly hiking prices by 45% months after contracts have been signed as memory shortage bites
articles.text:
AI server giants including HPE, Dell and more are reportedly hiking prices by 45% months after contracts have been signed as memory shortage bites
Signed an AI server deal last year? That could be costly
- Dell, HPE, Lenovo, and Supermicro are reportedly asking for 25% to 45% more on AI server orders months after signing, citing surging memory costs as a key issue
- GPU servers are reportedly up 20% to 30%, while memory-heavy CPU nodes have tripled or more, with memory prices up over 400% since 2024
- Buyers are mostly paying anyway, while four vendors either declined or did not respond to requests for comment
Buying AI servers used to be simple, if expensive: agree on a price, sign the contract, wait for the racks to arrive.
That dynamic has now changed considerably, with the last step becoming where the real negotiation takes place, reports from the Financial Times have claimed.
The FT reported Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro have been going back to customers months after deals were signed and asking for substantially more money before delivery, with insiders familiar with the developments telling it that increases between signing and delivery have reached 25%, 30% and, on some orders, as much as 45%, with suppliers blaming the cost of memory.
Paying up to avoid empty racks
The buyers named by FT are high-frequency and quantitative trading firms, including Jane Street, Optiver, and Hudson River Trading, all of which are expanding their data center footprints.
Most of those customers appear to be absorbing the increases. One person described "a significant disparity between the price initially agreed months in advance" and what firms end up paying on delivery, according to Seeking Alpha's summary of the FT report. Another, quoted by TechSpot, summed it up plainly: "the compute is valuable to us, and we'll pay for it."
For a trading firm, where idle capacity has a cost of its own, that is a rational calculation. It also tells suppliers exactly how much leverage they hold. The FT asked whether the affected buyers had contract clauses protecting them from post-signing changes, and Tom's Hardware reports that none would confirm or deny it.
HPE and Supermicro also declined to comment on the price adjustments, while Dell and Lenovo did not respond. Optiver and Hudson River Trading also declined to comment, and Jane Street did not respond.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The FT points to memory as the main driver, citing JPMorgan research that puts the rise in memory prices at more than 400% since the start of 2024. The impact varies sharply by machine type. GPU servers have reportedly risen by at least 20% to 30%, while CPU nodes, where memory makes up a much larger share of the bill, have tripled or more.
That split is what you would expect. In a GPU server, the accelerators dominate the cost, so even a dramatic DRAM increase gets diluted across the system. In a conventional CPU node, memory is one of the biggest cost components, so the same increase hits far harder.
Relief is not close, either. Nvidia told some of its largest customers in August 2026 that servers built around its chips would cost more than 15% more on systems shipping from early 2027.
Micron has warned that supply will be much tighter in 2027 and 2028 than it was this year, and SK Group chairman Chey Tae-won has said the shortage could run until 2030. Dell vice chairman and COO Jeff Clarke told analysts on November 24 2026, "We think that crunch continues clearly into 2027," according to Yahoo Finance.
The anonymous figures are hard to test, but one case has now become a courtroom affair: In June 2026, XTX Finland Oy, part of the London-based algorithmic trading group XTX Markets, sued Dell Products Unlimited Company in Ireland's High Court, the Irish Times reported.
According to XTX, it agreed in November 2025 to buy 1,680 servers for a 15,000-square-meter data center at a fixed price of about $549 million, and paid an extra $5 million on top of the quote specifically to avoid exposure to future price increases.
Delivery then slipped by two months, and Dell said higher component costs meant XTX would have to pay a further $62 million to $70 million. Some $70 million has been placed in escrow. In an affidavit, XTX director Cameron Scott Hill said Dell was "embarrassed" by the situation.
Dell disputes XTX's claims: It said it was not willing to lose tens of millions of dollars on the deal, that it could not deliver on the terms it believed applied when the agreement was signed, and that other customers facing increases had gone to rival suppliers before coming back and accepting the adjustments. The case has been admitted to the fast-track Commercial Court and is due back in December.
Repricing has been in the small print for a year
None of this is hidden policy: Last December, internal Dell guidance reviewed by Business Insider warned that "ordering today for future delivery does not lock in current prices," as TechRadar Pro reported, at a time when the major OEMs were already planning server price rises of around 15%.
HPE went further in March: CEO Antonio Neri said the company had amended its quoting terms "with the right to reprice existing orders for commodity cost increases," TechRadar Pro reported, noting that memory and storage make up around half of a traditional server's bill of materials.
In August, HPE partly reversed course, guaranteeing quotes on most compute, storage, and GreenLake Flex deals below $1 million net with no adjustment between order and shipment, and doubling quote validity from 15 to 30 days, according to SDxCentral. That helps smaller buyers, but it does nothing at AI cluster scale. For context, XTX's order alone is more than 500 times that threshold.
Suppliers argue they have no choice, and an OEM that committed to a fixed price a year ago and must now buy DRAM at today's rates can genuinely lose money on a deal. Dell's latest results, published two days after the FT report, cut both ways. Revenue more than doubled to $54.9 billion, the AI server backlog hit a record $132.3 billion, and the operating income rate climbed 490 basis points to 14.2%, a gain CFO David Kennedy said was "driven primarily by scale and pricing discipline," according to Dell.
Gross margin, an arguably better gauge of what Dell charges relative to what it pays for parts, rose just 10 basis points to 21.2%. That suggests Dell is largely passing costs through rather than widening its spread, which supports the vendors' argument. What it doesn't explain is why a customer who paid specifically for price certainty should still carry those costs and the risks they carry.
For now, the answer comes down to leverage. Supply trails demand; buyers would rather pay than leave data halls empty, and suppliers know it. The December hearing in Dublin may be the first real test of whether a price guarantee on an AI server order still means anything. Until memory supply catches up, a signed purchase order looks less like a price and more like an estimate.

Rahim Amir is a UAE-based tech writer who enjoys building PCs as much as he enjoys writing about them. He has been professionally writing about PC hardware since 2023, focusing on buyer’s guides, hardware reviews, and sponsored content and features related to tech.
Having built hundreds of gaming PCs and being an avid gamer in his spare time, Rahim tends to have stronger opinions about hardware than most. This is particularly on display when he gets his way with powerful, but minimalistic RGB builds even as Small Form Factor (SFF) PCs come a close second.

Save and start printing
You've been waiting for it all year, and now the Black Friday sales are finally here. It's that time of the year when your favorite 3D printer makers roll out huge discounts on some of their best products, and you can be sure that we will be here tracking them all for you live.

LIVE: Latest Updates
Keep your TPU and PETG safe with this $39 Sovol filament dryer
TPU and PETG (and to lesser degree, PLA) that's not properly dehydrated can seriously screw up your prints depending on how bad it is. To ensure your filament is fresh and ready for printing, you need a dehydrator. This filament dryer from Sovol is inexpensive at $39, 20% off its list price, and it can hold 2kg of filament across two spools.
Filament that has absorbed moisture just makes for a horrible printing experience. TPU and PETG become a mess on the print bed. Using this filament dryer will keep your filament dry, and it is ready to use via the feeder tube on the lid. Pop the spools in the dryer, set the timer and temperature, and your filament will be dehydrated and ready to print your next project.

The front display shows both temperature and humidity, and you can feed filament directly out of the dryer, so you don't need to constantly swap out spools. If you need more capacity, the 4kg version of this box (room for four spools) is also on sale for 27% off. — Jake Roach
Anycubic’s four-color Kobra X was my third 3D printer — but at its lowest-ever $279 sale price, it makes a great first machine

So if you are looking to get into the 3D printing game, or to step up to a multi-color model without spending a lot of money, the Anycubic Kobra X is a good option — especially while it’s on sale for just $279. -- Matt Safford
Print really big for less with Sovol's SV08 Max
Need to print big? Like, really big? Sovol's SV08 Max is one of the largest 3D printers this side of an Elegoo OrangeStorm Giga, and it'll let you print huge projects in one go that would otherwise need to be split into multiple jobs. You can get into its massive 500 x 500 x 500mm build volume for just $934 during the Black Friday frenzy at Amazon.
If you need to print big on a budget, Sovol's SV08 Max is the way to go. Its 500 x 500 x 500mm build volume is among the largest available, and if you're willing to tweak, you'll find awesome bang for the buck.

The SV08 Max ensures solid first layers with an eddy current sensor for automatic leveling across its huge build plate, and it includes a handy touch screen and 720p camera for managing and monitoring whatever massive jobs you might have in flight.
Although our review identified a few quirks that make this printer intimidating for novices, its open firmware and optional enclosure for handling high-temperature filaments make it a versatile tool for more seasoned enthusiasts. And where else are you going to find this much build volume for the dollar? If you need to print really big at a relatively modest price, hop on this deal while it's hot. -- Jeff Kampman
Our highest-rated 3D printer is on sale for $60 off during Black Friday
The Bambu Lab X2D is the best overall 3D printer we've reviewed, offering excellent value, speedy and high-quality prints, and a dual nozzle extruder. You can save an extra $60 off the printer itself right now, or an extra $110 if you bundle it with AMS 2 Pro.
The Bambu Lab X2D is the best 3D printer we've reviewed, offering a great value given its inexpensive price, dual nozzle extruder, and auto bed leveling.

The printer can gather models via USB, Bluetooth, or Wi-Fi with the Bambu Handy app on mobile or Studio app on desktop. The four-spool AMS 2 Pro, should you pick one up, doubles as a filament dryer to keep your materials in optimal shape. — Jake Roach
Elegoo’s 8-pack PLA basic 3D filament bundle is on sale for 15% off its typical price – stock up on basic PLA filament in a wide variety of colors
If I ever run into an issue with 3D printing, outside of clogged heads, it’s never having enough or the right filament available. Amazon’s Black Friday deal has Elegoo’s 8-pack (250g each) PLA basic 3D filament bundle on sale for just over $30 (15% discount). This bundle comes in eight colors: black, white, gray, transparent, red, cobalt, blue, orange, and green.
Elegoo's least expensive 8-pack 250g PLA basic filament comes in black, white, gray, transparent, red, cobalt, blue, orange, and green. There's also several other deals with different colors at a similar price.

The 250g spools are ideal for smaller projects and trying new colors without cracking open a full 1kg spool. Think printing out 3DBenchy a few times to test out new settings or colors without wasting the filament you plan to use on your project. The PLA basic mini bundle should work with most FDM 3D printers that use 1.75mm filament. If these aren’t the colors you want, Amazon has several more options at similar pricing. – Joe Shields

Start 3D printing for under $200🔥

Dip your toe into 3D-printed waters with the Elegoo Neptune 3 Pro for just $159

And, as you can read in our Elegoo Neptune 3 Pro review, it's an excellent printer that earned an Editor's Choice badge despite its budget price.

The open bed gives you a print volume of 225 x 225 x 280mm, and the direct drive extruder works with PLA, PETG, TPU, and ABS. Unlike many budget printers of years past, the Neptune 3 Pro comes mostly pre-assembled out of the box, allowing you to started printing within an hour.
Although this is a budget printer, it still comes with some premium trimmings including a touchscreen for navigation, auto bed leveling, and a built-in task light to illuminate your prints. — Jake Roach
Stock up on essential black and white PLA for 24% off — Creality bundle includes two 1kg spools
Black Friday is always a good time to stock up on filament, and Creality has a value bundle of basic white and black PLA available on Amazon for 24% off. The bundle comes with 2kg of filament total (1kg per spool), and you can get them both for $22.79.
Grab 2kg total of basic black and white PLA 1.75mm filament from Creality. This is a value pack, so it's standard PLA, not PLA+.

This is standard PLA with a printing temp between 190 and 230 degrees Celsius, and a hotbed temp between 25 and 60 degrees Celsius. It has a standard 1.75mm diameter, and although it's made by Creality, the filament should work with the nearly all FDM 3D printers. — Jake Roach
Save $80 on the Bambu Lab P1S with AMS — all-in-one solution gives you multi-color printer and minimal setup
If you want to upgrade to a multi-filament feeding system cheaply, you can save $80 on the Bambu Lab P1S with the AMS feeder. The printer comes (mostly) pre-assembled, so from unboxing to print shouldn't take more than 20 or 30 minutes.
Grab the same Bambu Lab P1S 3D printer as above, but with an AMS included. With AMS stock limited on Bambu Lab's website until August, this might be a good way to get both without waiting for stock to improve.
Read moreRead less▼
The P1S offers an enclosed 256 × 256 × 256 mm³ printing volume, giving you plenty of room for large prints. We called the printer the "new standard" in our Bambu Lab P1S review, and it remains a compelling choice on the back of several price drops. When it launched in 2023, the printer retailed for $699. Now, you can get it for $479, and you get the AMS four-color feeder.
A single AMS unit can hold four different colors of filament, but you can integrate four AMS units with a single printer, giving you access to up to 16 colors without any manual swapping. — Jake Roach
Save a whopping $200 on Creality's 16-color K2 Combo 3D printer in Black Friday stunner
Creality's K2 Combo is the smallest in the K2 family, with a print area of 260 x 260 x 260mm. Direct from Creality, you can save $200 on the printer itself, bringing its $549 list price down to $349 for Black Friday. Bundled with a Creality CFS quadruple-spool feeder, you'll also save $200 off the $699 list price, bringing the price down to $499.
Creality's K2 Combo is a formidable 3D printer. The smallest of the K2 family of printers, the K2 Combo still has a 260 x 260 x 260 mm print size, allowing users to print large objects inside its enclosed frame without worrying about having to glue together multiple prints. The ultra-sturdy frame holds an auto-leveling print bed and three step-servo motors for fast, consistent prints.
Read moreRead less▼
As with our K2 printers, such as the K2 Pro Combo we reviewed, you can pair up to four CFS cartridges together for a 16-color printer; though, with the smaller size here, it might be difficult to fit all those colors in. It also features auto print bed leveling, along with print failure detection. — Jake Roach
Starting at just $599, 3D printer tool changers are cheaper than ever
Snapmaker’s U1 kicked off the affordable tool changer craze around this time last year, with an early Kickstarter price of $799 and a full retail price of $999. But now it’s widely available and on sale for $100 less than ever. When we reviewed the U1, we praised its roomy build area (270 mm cubed), direct-drive tool heads, and its four-head tool-changing capabilities, earning it 4.5 stars and a spot on our best 3D printers list.
Last year, this tool-changer was the most anticipated upcoming printer around. With four heads for swapping colors or materials without the need to "poop," it can breeze through complex multicolor prints much faster than single-head printers, without wasting nearly as much filament.
Read moreRead less▼
This open CoreXY 3D printer has four toolheads, is rated for head swaps that take 7 seconds, and sports a 256 mm X3 build volume.
Read moreRead less▼
On the heels of the U1, Flashforge released the Creator 5, a tool changer that’s a bit more basic, but still a solid machine (we gave it 4 stars in our review), priced even lower than the Snapmaker, both when it launched (at $699) and now, when it’s on sale for $100 less. — Matt Safford

articles.title: ASUS ROG XG Station 3 Gets EU Launch and Immediately Sells Below MSRP
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
ASUS ROG XG Station 3 Gets EU Launch and Immediately Sells Below MSRP
ASUS announced the ROG Station 3 in early November, revealing that the new Thunderbolt 5 eGPU dock would go so far as to support ASUS's BTF 2.5 GPUs. It will also feature up to 140 W USB PD for laptop and handheld docking purposes. ASUS, however, did not announce pricing when it launched the XG Station 3. Its MSRP has now been revealed (via VideoCardz) to be €399 in the EU without a PSU. 
While the ASUS MSRP for the eGPU dock may be €399, the GPU has appeared online at European stores like Proshop for as little as €349, and that doesn't seem to be a result of any sort of deal. US pricing and an estimated launch date have not yet been revealed, although, given that it is already in stock at various retailers across Europe, it should launch in the US soon enough.

articles.title: “Debemos estar preparados para los próximos meses”: presidente de Microsoft advierte de más interrupciones tecnológicas masivas
articles.text:
El riesgo de que se repitan interrupciones tecnológicas masivas podría mantenerse elevado durante los próximos meses, mientras las organizaciones aceleran la actualización de software vulnerable y la modernización de infraestructura obsoleta, advirtió el presidente de Microsoft, Brad Smith.
“Creo que tenemos que estar preparados, francamente, para los próximos meses, porque esto no es el tipo de cosa que se resuelve en un par de semanas”, afirmó Smith en el programa Face the Nation, de CBS News, el domingo. “Toda la infraestructura de información del mundo está, en efecto, siendo actualizada en este momento”.
Una cadena de fallas técnicas sin relación entre sí
La advertencia llega luego de un período turbulento marcado por fallas técnicas independientes que afectaron a grandes bancos, aerolíneas, el control de tráfico aéreo y los propios servicios de nube global de Microsoft. Aunque las autoridades descartaron ataques cibernéticos coordinados, la sucesión de interrupciones expuso la dependencia de empresas, agencias gubernamentales y viajeros respecto de sistemas digitales interconectados.
La seguidilla de incidentes comenzó el 12 de noviembre y se extendió hasta el 13, cuando una falla global de Microsoft interrumpió los servicios de Microsoft 365, Exchange Online y Outlook para empresas y organismos gubernamentales en todo el mundo.
Smith explicó que esa falla no estuvo vinculada ni a un error de inteligencia artificial ni a un ciberataque, sino que fue producto de una “tormenta perfecta” generada por la interacción entre una actualización de software de cuatro meses atrás, una actualización más reciente y un cambio en el tráfico de red. Según precisó, Microsoft publicó dos informes sobre el episodio y ya completó nueve medidas correctivas, con 13 adicionales planificadas.
Ese mismo 13 de noviembre, la Administración Federal de Aviación (FAA) ordenó una infrecuente detención total de vuelos a escala nacional después de que una falla de telecomunicaciones interrumpiera durante unas cuatro horas su red de control de tráfico aéreo, lo que provocó demoras y cancelaciones generalizadas.
De acuerdo con la FAA, su red heredada se volvió inestable al recibir alrededor de 1.000 intentos de conexión cada cuatro o cinco segundos, lo que afectó las comunicaciones y las señales de radar en 17 de los 22 centros de control de tráfico aéreo de la agencia. Los investigadores señalaron dos posibles orígenes de ese pico de conexiones, entre ellos un sitio de comunicaciones en Arkansas donde el contratista de defensa L3Harris instalaba un enrutador.
El secretario de Transporte, Sean Duffy, atribuyó la interrupción a la antigüedad de la tecnología de control de tráfico aéreo del país y señaló que conmutadores y enrutadores sobrecargados comenzaron a generar datos inconsistentes.
Días después, United Airlines sufrió una falla tecnológica independiente que alteró las salidas de vuelos en toda su red en Estados Unidos. En paralelo, un problema técnico en JPMorgan Chase retrasó transacciones en distintos puntos del sistema bancario estadounidense, mientras miles de clientes reportaron dificultades para acceder a sus cuentas en línea en Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank y Capital One.
El secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, afirmó que no existe “ninguna prueba” que vincule los distintos episodios ni que sugiera la existencia de ciberataques coordinados.
La inteligencia artificial, motor de una carrera de parches sin precedentes
Smith sostuvo que la inteligencia artificial aceleró la detección de debilidades en el código informático. Si bien esto permite a los equipos de defensa corregir fallas con mayor rapidez, los actores maliciosos pueden emplear las mismas herramientas para atacar sistemas, lo que obliga a las organizaciones a desplegar actualizaciones a un ritmo acelerado que deja menos tiempo para las pruebas.
“Lo que hizo la inteligencia artificial a comienzos de este año fue básicamente facilitar mucho que la gente encuentre vulnerabilidades en el código, y entonces se puede usar ese conocimiento para parchear el código o, si uno es un actor malicioso, usar ese mismo conocimiento para intentar vulnerar sistemas”, explicó.
Debido a que las organizaciones corrigen vulnerabilidades “a un ritmo que nunca habíamos visto antes”, esa misma urgencia genera inestabilidad, en particular en los sistemas heredados, señaló Smith. “Especialmente cuando se tiene infraestructura más antigua, especialmente cuando se intenta parchear a ese ritmo, especialmente cuando hay que ir tan rápido que no se puede dedicar tanto tiempo a probar lo que se cambia en el código, se incrementa el riesgo de que algo salga mal”, agregó.
El directivo instó a los consumidores a instalar con prontitud las actualizaciones de seguridad y pidió a las empresas modernizar la infraestructura antigua y mejorar la coordinación con el gobierno. “Si reciben una actualización en su teléfono o su computadora con un parche, aplíquenlo, porque creo que eso va a mantener su tecnología mucho más segura”, dijo.
Smith remarcó que, si bien la falla de Microsoft tuvo causas propias, buena parte de las interrupciones registradas puede entenderse como un “efecto dominó de la inteligencia artificial” derivado de la carrera global por asegurar código vulnerable.

articles.title: Your AI agents can be fully authorized and still do damage
articles.text:
Your AI agents can be fully authorized and still do damage
For as long as we’ve had enterprise security, it’s been organized around one question: Who is allowed to do what?
Identity, zero trust and least privilege all exist to answer that question. The internet and mobile disrupted the landscape by bringing more people and devices onto the network, but the underlying problem remained.
Artificial intelligence agents expose the limits of that question. An agent can hold only the permissions it was given and still email a customer list to a stranger because it read an instruction buried on a web page or in a support ticket and treated it as a legitimate order. That is the problem Cato Networks Ltd. is trying to solve with its recent launch of AgentSense, a runtime capability built into its secure access service edge platform.
The news
AgentSense monitors an agent as it works and traces each proposed action back to its instruction source. Its first component, Untrusted Influence Detection, separates what the user asked for from content the agent encounters along the way, such as emails, documents and tool responses. If that external content steers the agent toward a risky step, the action is blocked before it runs. A second component, Drift Detection, is planned to check whether an agent’s steps still serve its original task.
With agentic agents, they can have the right permissions and still take harmful actions. The first release covers coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and GitHub Copilot. These are included at no extra charge in Cato AI Usage licenses, and Cato is offering $10,000 to each of the first three researchers who can beat it. This has clear value for security leaders. As organizations give AI more responsibility, they need visibility into what it is doing and when human intervention is required.
Why this matters
Language models read instructions and data in the same stream, and no patch will change that. Filters that look for known attack phrases catch poorly formed attempts, but a well-written injection will be interpreted as a valid business request. The control therefore must sit at the moment of action and ask where the instruction came from.
Permissions alone won’t close the gap because multiple actions, when executed individually, can still combine to produce an unauthorized outcome. Adoption is far ahead of control. A Gartner survey cited by Fierce Network found that 71% of organizations expect to deploy agentic AI within 12 months, while only 21% have governance in place.
Advice for IT pros
- Inventory your agents, starting with developers. Coding agents are among the most widely adopted and often run with developers’ own credentials, API keys and local files readily accessible. Find out which agents are installed, what they can access, and whether anyone is running them on a personal subscription. You can’t govern what you haven’t counted.
- Rank agents by the dangerous combination. The agents that deserve attention first are those with all three of the following: access to private data, exposure to external content, and the ability to send or change something externally. Security researchers call this the lethal trifecta, and Cato’s launch blog outlines the risk similarly. Removing any one of the three is often cheaper than buying a new tool.
- Scope permissions to the task. Most agents inherit everything their human owner can do, which is far more than any single job needs. Give agents their own identities with narrow, short-lived credentials, and keep root access and production secrets out of reach by default.
- Update your definitions of trusted sources and sensitive data. Runtime controls like AgentSense rely on you to specify which sources are trusted and which data is sensitive. If your data classification is stale, the tool will either block too much or miss what matters. This unglamorous work determines whether the technology pays off.
- Demand blocking before execution, then test it yourself. Ask every vendor whether the product stops an action or only alerts after the fact, which agents it covers, and how much delay it adds. Then plant your own instructions in a test ticket, document and web page and see what gets through. Vendor benchmarks and bounty programs are useful signals, but your own workflows are the test that counts.
- Assign an owner and an exception process. Agent behavior falls between the security, networking and development teams, which often leaves no one owning it. Name an owner, route blocked actions to the security operations team, and make it easy for developers to request exceptions. If the control only slows people down, they will turn it off.
- Keep a person in the loop for any irreversible action. Deleting data, changing production systems and sending information outside the company should require human approval until you trust the guardrails. Earn autonomy one workflow at a time.
Final thoughts
AgentSense is a single product from a single vendor, and it will take time and independent testing to prove itself. The more important point is the shift it represents. Zero trust taught us to verify who is asking. Agents also require us to verify why an action is happening and whose instruction is behind it.
The companies that get value from agents will be the ones that can let them run without watching every step, and that only happens when the controls are in place first. Start the inventory and the permission cleanup now. The tools to enforce the rest are arriving quickly, and they will work far better for the teams that did the groundwork.
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: Anatel nega recurso da TIM e antispam continua suspenso
articles.text:
Anatel nega recurso da TIM e antispam continua suspenso
Segundo a Anatel, a ferramenta de bloqueio de telemarketing da TIM ficará suspenso até que a operadora promova os ajustes necessários à reativação.
A Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações (Anatel) suspendeu o serviço antispam, da TIM, em 13 de novembro. A ferramenta, que bloqueia chamadas indesejadas, também estaria barrando ligações legítimas, de acordo com o órgão. A operadora tentou reativar o mecanismo, mas a Anatel decidiu manter a suspensão.
O antispam da TIM tem a proposta de fazer o bloqueio automático de chamadas massivas, frequentemente associadas a serviços de telemarketing que não seguem as boas práticas do segmento. Como as chamadas abusivas são barradas na rede da própria operadora, o usuário não precisa instalar aplicativos de bloqueio em seu celular ou executar ações manuais para esse fim.
A Anatel não é contra sistemas do tipo. Mas, no entendimento do órgão, o antispam da TIM também estaria bloqueando chamadas legítimas, inclusive de serviços essenciais, sem oferecer a transparência necessária para esse tipo de operação ou mecanismos adequados de contestação de bloqueios.
Discordando da suspensão do antispam, a TIM apresentou um recurso administrativo à Anatel para reativar o serviço. A companhia argumentou que medidas de ajustes da ferramenta já haviam sido adotadas, que a necessidade de fornecer informações adicionais não significa falta de transparência e que a suspensão poderia causar transtornos aos seus clientes.
Mas, como sabemos agora, a agência manteve a suspensão.
Vale relembrar que a TIM não chegou a divulgar à imprensa a ativação do serviço, embora tenha avisado clientes. De todo modo, o Tecnoblog noticiou, em setembro, que a TIM trabalhava em uma ferramenta de bloqueio de telemarketing. Esse mecanismo veio à tona após discordâncias com a Vivo, a primeira operadora a implementar um serviço do tipo.
De acordo com o Despacho Decisório nº 58/2026/PR, assinado em 24 de novembro de 2026 pelo presidente do Conselho Diretor da Anatel, Alexandre Freire, a suspensão do antispam será mantida até que a agência reconheça, formalmente, que as condições para a reativação tenham sido atendidas.
Em nota, a Anatel declarou o seguinte:
Ao analisar o pedido, Alexandre Freire considerou que os argumentos e as providências apresentados pela empresa não demonstraram, nesta avaliação preliminar, a superação dos riscos que fundamentaram a medida cautelar.
O presidente destacou que o risco de bloqueio indevido de comunicações essenciais ultrapassa os interesses individuais dos usuários afetados e pode comprometer a continuidade de serviços públicos.
O Tecnoblog pediu um posicionamento sobre o assunto à TIM. O texto será atualizado se obtivermos um retorno da operadora.

articles.title: Unikey Electronics Named RECOM Global Authorized Distributor at electronica 2026
articles.text:
The global electronic components distributor used its first electronica to sign a global distribution agreement with RECOM, demonstrate its online sourcing platform, and launch an industry interview series.
MUNICH, Germany — Unikey Electronics has been appointed a Global Authorized Distributor for RECOM Power, with the agreement signed at the company’s booth on the opening day of electronica 2026, held November 10–13 at Messe München.
RECOM Group CEO Karsten Bier attended the signing ceremony in Hall C2. The agreement gives Unikey’s customers worldwide authorized access to RECOM’s portfolio of power conversion products, which the company is currently expanding into discrete power.
Digital sourcing on the show floor
Unikey exhibited on a 150-square-meter booth together with its partners CJT and XSemitron, two component manufacturers that presented their own products and met visitors directly at the booth.
The Unikey booth also featured an experience zone for unikeyic.com, Unikey’s online sourcing platform. Visitors could run through the full digital purchasing workflow live, from part-number search and real-time availability checks to BOM upload and online ordering, with Unikey staff on hand to answer questions.
The demonstration reflects a broader shift in how engineers and purchasing teams buy components: buyers increasingly expect self-service tools for search, pricing and BOM management, alongside the global sourcing reach and personal support of a distributor. Unikey positions its platform as a combination of both.
Over the four days, the company’s team met with customers, manufacturers, engineers, purchasing teams and technology platforms to discuss sourcing challenges, market developments and new partnership opportunities in product distribution, digital sourcing and technical support. This year’s electronica drew more than 86,000 visitors and 3,512 exhibitors.
UniKey Connects interview series
Unikey also used the show to launch UniKey Connects — electronica 2026 Conversations, an interview series recorded at the booth under the theme “Where technology, data and supply chains connect.”
The first episode features Alyson Ong of Unikey Electronics in conversation with RECOM CEO Karsten Bier, covering RECOM’s latest developments, its move into discrete power, the outlook for power electronics and the role of distribution partnerships.
Further episodes feature SiTime, OEMsecrets, GlobalSpec, MDD (Microdiode Semiconductor), Sichuan Zhongxing Electronic, DAPU and other companies across the electronics value chain. They will be released in the coming weeks on the Unikey Electronics website, LinkedIn and YouTube.
During the show, Unikey representatives were also interviewed by several leading electronics industry media outlets.
About Unikey Electronics
Unikey Electronics is a Singapore-based global online distribution platform for electronic components, serving design engineers, sourcing professionals, ODMs, OEMs and EMS providers in 100+ countries and regions via www.unikeyic.com. 
Learn more at https://www.unikeyic.com

articles.title: Noté 5/5, ce téléviseur OLED Philips perd 291 € à l'occasion du Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le téléviseur Philips 77OLED811 "5 étoiles" à 1 899,00 € (-13%)
Actuellement noté 5/5 par notre rédaction, le téléviseur Philips 77OLED811 assure un contraste parfait avec ses noirs profonds tout en proposant l'éclairage d'ambiance Ambilight. Le Black Friday fait descendre son prix à 1 899,00 € chez Boulanger.com, soit une baisse d'environ 13 % et 291,00 € d'économie.
Le Philips 77OLED811 est un téléviseur OLED de 77 pouces pensé pour conjuguer grand spectacle et fluidité, avec son rétroéclairage Ambilight sur trois côtés et sa prise en charge des consoles actuelles. Positionné juste sous les modèles phares de la marque, il apporte une luminosité supérieure à celle de l'OLED810 tout en soignant sa connectique pour les cinéphiles comme pour les joueurs. Cet écran avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage sur notre banc de test.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, ce téléviseur descend à 1 899,00 € chez Boulanger.com, soit environ 13 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (2 190,00 €). Cela représente une économie de 291,00 €.
Calibration exemplaire et pic lumineux élevé
Ce modèle délivre une fidélité colorimétrique remarquable dès la sortie du carton, idéale pour apprécier vos films sans dérive de teinte. Comme le confirme notre test complet, le labo a relevé une luminosité maximale de 1672 cd/m², ce qui permet aux contenus HDR de conserver des reflets étincelants tout en maintenant les noirs absolus propres à la technologie OLED. Cette réserve lumineuse garantit un contraste saisissant même dans une pièce de vie modérément éclairée.
Philips 77OLED811
Points forts
- Excellente colorimétrie SDR et HDR
- Calibration globale.
- Contraste parfait et noirs profonds de l’Oled.
- Pic lumineux en nette hausse par rapport à l'OLED810.
- Quatre ports HDMI 2.1 et dalle 165 Hz.
- Pied orientable.
- Ambilight toujours sympathique.
Points faibles
- Titan OS encore loin d'être abouti.
- Reflets bien présents.
- Basses qui font grésiller le châssis.
- Consommation assez élevée.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Fluidité pour le jeu et limites de l'interface
Pour les joueurs, le diffuseur se montre particulièrement réactif grâce à un retard à l'affichage mesuré à 13,2 ms, évitant tout décalage perceptible manette en main. Le système d'exploitation Titan OS manque en revanche encore de maturité face à des interfaces plus fluides, un point qui dérangera peu les utilisateurs passant par un boîtier multimédia externe.
LG 77C6 : l'autre option face au Philips 77OLED811
Le LG 77C6 mise sur une dalle Tandem OLED lumineuse et un système audio plus stable dans les basses, le tout servi par une interface logicielle éprouvée. De son côté, le Philips 77OLED811 fait valoir son éclairage Ambilight intégré et son pied orientable, très pratique pour ajuster l'angle de vision dans un grand salon.
Le LG 77C6 est vendu 100,00 € plus cher que le Philips 77OLED811 au tarif du jour, ce dernier conservant l'avantage de la diffusion lumineuse immersive pour un tarif plus accessible.
LG 77C6
Points forts
- Contraste parfait de l’Oled.
- Pic lumineux HDR en très nette hausse.
- Couverture Rec.2020 au niveau du G6.
- Très bonnes performances en jeu vidéo.
- Quatre ports HDMI 2.1.
- Faible consommation.
- Bon système audio.
Points faibles
- Reflets encore visibles face aux haut de gamme.
- Spatialisation audio limitée.
- Télécommande non rétroéclairée.
- Compte LG désormais obligatoire.

articles.title: Canal+ enchaîne les bugs, et cette fois ce sont ses décodeurs qui ont un souci
articles.text:
Canal+ a confirmé mercredi subir une panne sur ses décodeurs. La lecture des replays avec publicités est perturbée par une erreur EESPT. Le groupe promet de rétablir le service « dans les meilleurs délais ».
Les abonnés Canal+ équipés d'un décodeur ont du mal à regarder leurs replays ces jours-ci. Une fois la lecture de la publicité terminée, une erreur EESPT empêche le programme de démarrer. Canal+ a reconnu l'incident le mercredi 25 novembre, sans en préciser la cause. Mais plusieurs abonnés affirment subir la panne depuis deux à trois jours et la rapprochent aux récentes hausses de tarifs.
Sur les décodeurs Canal+, le replay cale après la publicité
Mercredi, Canal+ a publié un message indiquant qu'« un incident technique perturbe actuellement la lecture des programmes en replay avec pub sur les décodeurs CANAL+ ». Ses équipes sont « mobilisées pour rétablir le service dans les meilleurs délais ». Pas plus d'infos donc, à ce stade, sur les causes ni même sur le calendrier d'une éventuelle résolution.
Pour les abonnés, le souci dure depuis deux à trois jours désormais. Certains décrivent une publicité qui se lance normalement, puis un programme qui refuse de démarrer. L'un a débranché sa télévision, comme Canal+ l'avait recommandé selon lui.
Un autre a éteint puis rallumé son décodeur. Mais rien n'y fait. Ce dernier raconte aussi avoir perdu le direct en fin d'après-midi mercredi, « écran noir », et avoir cru le problème réglé ce soir, avant que l'erreur revienne « au bout de 10 minutes ». Un troisième assure ne capter plus que CNews et Europe 1, sans savoir s'il joue de mauvaise foi ou s'il dit vrai.
Certains abonnés Canal perdent patience
Sur le forum d'assistance de Canal+, la colère monte. « Assurez d'abord un service correct ! », écrit un abonné, en majuscules dans le texte. Un autre réclame un « dédommagement financier », et un troisième multiplie les relances (« Alors Canal ?? ») sans réponse visible dans le fil. Joint par téléphone, le service client aurait promis à un abonné un retour à la normale dans la soirée.
On lui a aussi proposé quelques mois d'accès gratuit à Canal+ en clair. C'est « sympa », reconnaît-il, « mais il faudrait que le service fonctionne ». Les prix, comme souvent, nourrissent aussi la rancœur. Un client abonné depuis 22 ans affirme que la location de ses deux décodeurs est passée de 14 à 18 euros. S'y ajoutent selon lui la hausse de l'abonnement et des chaînes supprimées « à leur guise ».
Pas plus tard que lundi, le groupe a aussi reconnu que la version 6.3.1 de son appli ne se lançait plus sur certains iPad sous iPadOS 17.7.1. Reste à espérer que le correctif arrive vite, et qu'il referme une série de bugs dont Canal+ se passerait bien, tout comme ses abonnés.

articles.title: Resourceful PC owner repurposes CPU watercooler with dead pump as standalone LCD hardware monitor, vibecodes new software for module — NZXT Kraken’s LCD and controller board combined with 3D-printed stand for second chance at life
articles.text:
Resourceful PC owner repurposes CPU watercooler with dead pump as standalone LCD hardware monitor, vibecodes new software for module — NZXT Kraken’s LCD and controller board combined with 3D-printed stand for second chance at life
A clever way to save a dead cooler's LCD.
AIO liquid coolers are notorious for shorter lifespans due to pump failure or leaks, which usually results in having to replace the entire unit. However, one enthusiast decided to salvage theirs uniquely, at least a part of it. Sharing their DIY project on Reddit, u/BodeeHav repurposed the LCD screen from a dead NZXT Kraken AIO into a standalone desktop monitor that displays live CPU and GPU temperatures and utilization after vibecoding entirely new software.
According to the post, the pump on their NZXT Kraken AIO stopped working around a month ago. Rather than discarding a perfectly usable screen, they decided to dismantle the block and remove the LCD and its main board. They used the original black outer housing and 3D printed a stand to hold the LCD in place. To keep things tidy, they stripped the connector down to just its SATA power and USB pins. The display connects directly to the motherboard, presumably using the internal 9-pin USB header, although BodeeHav says they plan to adapt it for external USB.
Getting the display working properly required more than just pulling it out of the pump block. BodeeHav initially used NZXT’s CAM software; however, he kept running into issues whenever the PC entered sleep or standby. To overcome this hurdle, they turned to AI and vibe coded an entirely new software as a replacement that offers full control of the LCD with various customization options.
BodeeHav has graciously made his entire project available on GitHub, where you can access the DesktopKraken software and an STL file for the stand. According to the official GitHub page, the software is a standalone Windows application that communicates with compatible NZXT Kraken Elite LCDs over USB without requiring NZXT CAM.
The software currently only offers support for the 2023 Kraken Elite and 2024 Kraken Elite V2, which use circular LCDs with a 640x640 resolution. Apart from CPU and GPU temperatures and utilization, it can also display clock speeds, power consumption, memory usage, and VRAM information. Additionally, the software can be used for brightness control, screen orientation, sensor logging, and it even offers support for custom images, animated GIFs, thermal warning gauges, and automatic recovery after Windows sleep or a USB disconnect.
While it may cater to a very niche audience, the project is a great example of how a little ingenuity can give failed components a second life.

articles.title: I bought a refurbished iPhone 17e, and I'll never go back to buying new
articles.text:
Refurbished iPhone sales are on the rise — here's why buying pre-owned is a great idea (and why I'll never go back to buying new)
If you're thinking about upgrading your phone this November, take my advice: pick up a refurbished unit (and thank me later)
As a journalist who’s been covering the tech world for the better part of a decade, I can honestly say that I’ve never seen a worse time for consumers to buy a brand-new phone.
The race to build AI-fueling data centers (and the vast amounts of RAM they require) has wrought havoc on the cost of smartphones — the fact that Samsung’s entry-level flagship, the Galaxy S26, now has a starting price of $999 / £959 / AU$1,649 (a year-on-year increase of $200 / £160 / AU$100) should tell you everything you need to know.
And if, like me, you’re an iPhone user, then things aren’t much better. After keeping prices fairly steady for several years, Apple finally gave in and increased the cost of every iPhone it had on sale in September. We’re now in a situation where Apple’s cheapest handset, the iPhone 17e, costs an eye-watering $699 / £699 / AU$1,149. Even as a fan of the brand, I’ll tell you right now that you can find much better value by scouting out the best Android phones, particularly if you’re after a mid-range device.
It shouldn’t be too surprising, then, that online retailer MusicMagpie has reported a 53% surge in refurbished iPhone sales, following the release of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. It makes a lot of sense as consumers try to sniff out any bargains on potential upgrades, but I completely get any scepticism that some folks may have about going down the refurbished route, particularly as I was once among you.
I always preferred to buy my phones new, but after taking the plunge last year and writing about my experience of using a refurbished phone for the first time, I honestly don’t see myself ever going back.
Refurbished tech has completely won me over
When I last wrote about this topic, I had a refurbished iPhone 16 to hand, but in the time since, I had to lend that device to my wife following a rather disastrous meeting between her iPhone 15 Pro and the concrete floor of a car park.
After trying to stick it out with Android for a time, I decided that I was too deep into Apple’s ecosystem to truly give it up, so I decided to go in search of another refurbished Apple phone.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
In the end, I settled on a ‘like new’ refurbished iPhone 17e from Giffgaff, coming to the conclusion that what I needed more than anything was access to iOS, a recent chipset with plenty of updates ahead of it, and a compact phone that was easy enough to use one-handed (I almost broke a Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra when trying to hold my daughter in one arm and text with the other).
Just like with my time using the iPhone 16, this newer model has proven to me that opting for a refurbished unit is a reliable choice. My iPhone 17e arrived as fresh as if it had just been unboxed for the first time, along with 100% battery health. In the time that I’ve been using it, the phone hasn’t failed me, keeping up with everything from texting on WhatsApp to video editing on Instagram Edits.
For context, the phone was priced at £529 at the time of purchase, which is a massive £170 less than the iPhone 17e's current retail price at the Apple Store. As a family man with bills to pay, that’s not an insignificant amount of money, and it says a lot that, as I’ve been scouring this year's slate of Black Friday phone deals, I’m yet to see an offer on a new iPhone that comes anywhere near offering the same level of value.
It also doesn’t help that, if recent predictions are to be believed, the cost of buying a new big-ticket phone is only set to get worse in 2027.
Refurbished phones will only get more appealing
According to a recent IDC report, the ongoing RAM crisis isn't expected to subside until 2028 at the earliest, and that only means that prices for consumers are likely to keep rising as companies have to pay greater amounts for memory. It’s a vicious cycle, but I think the one silver lining is that it should drive retailers to offer more choice on refurbished tech as interest continues to grow.
Already, there are a good amount of incentives available to tempt users into giving refurbished tech a try. For instance, my iPhone 17e is covered by a free 24-month warranty, which Giffgaff offers for all of its ‘like new’ phones, while Vodafone provides a free battery replacement service for up to three years from the point of purchase with certain contracts. In the US, I'd look at Best Buy and Back Market, while OzMobiles and JB Hi-Fi are popular choices in Australia.
All of this comes on top of the now-accepted standard to provide professionally refurbished tech, which is great for peace of mind.
As more retailers look to hop aboard the refurbished bandwagon, it should hopefully lead to a wider array of incentives on offer to attract business, so my hope is that buying a refurbished phone will only become a more rewarding prospect as time goes on.
For now, however, the very fact that refurbished tech gives Apple fans a way of circumventing the brand’s sky-high prices is already a big win, and if you are thinking about upgrading to a more recent iPhone this Black Friday, I can’t recommend buying pre-owned enough.

articles.title: Lanzamiento de GTA 6 afectó a Call of Duty: perdió más de 3 millones de jugadores diarios
articles.text:
El lanzamiento de Grand Theft Auto 6 provocó una caída de más de 3 millones de jugadores diarios en Call of Duty HQ, la aplicación que reúne entregas como Modern Warfare 4, Black Ops 7 y Warzone. La baja coincidió con los primeros días de disponibilidad del juego de Rockstar Games en PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S.
Los usuarios no abandonaron necesariamente Call of Duty de forma definitiva, pero el descenso refleja que parte de su tiempo de juego se trasladó a Leonida, el escenario de GTA 6.
Call of Duty perdió el 42% de sus usuarios diarios
Las estimaciones de Alinea Analytics indican que Call of Duty HQ pasó de un promedio de 7,5 millones de jugadores diarios a 4,4 millones durante el fin de semana del lanzamiento de GTA 6. La diferencia representa una reducción cercana al 42% entre PlayStation, Xbox y Steam.
Los datos fueron compartidos por Rhys Elliott, responsable de análisis de mercado de la firma. Cuatro días después del estreno, la plataforma de Activision continuaba un 41% por debajo de su ritmo habitual, lo que sugiere que la recuperación inicial fue limitada.
La mayor caída ocurrió en PlayStation, una de las plataformas históricamente más importantes para Call of Duty. Allí, la disminución alcanzó el 44%, según las estimaciones. El dato resulta relevante porque GTA 6 solo llegó inicialmente a consolas de nueva generación, mientras que el cálculo de Call of Duty incluye también a Steam.
Las cifras no proceden de Activision ni de Rockstar Games, por lo que deben interpretarse como una medición de terceros sobre la actividad de los jugadores. Aun así, el comportamiento permite observar el alcance que puede tener un lanzamiento esperado durante años sobre otros títulos con comunidades estables.
Fortnite y EA Sports FC 27 también registraron descensos
Call of Duty no fue el único juego afectado. Fortnite redujo su número de jugadores diarios en PlayStation y Xbox durante el mismo período, con una caída estimada del 28%. Su comunidad pasó de 17,8 millones de usuarios diarios a 12,8 millones, aunque recuperó parte de la actividad antes de terminar el fin de semana.
El caso de EA Sports FC 27 fue similar. El simulador de fútbol habría perdido cerca del 27% de sus usuarios diarios, al pasar de 5,9 millones a 4,3 millones. Sin embargo, el título redujo posteriormente parte de esa distancia frente a su promedio, apoyado por una promoción que rebajó su precio.
La diferencia entre estos juegos apunta a que no todas las comunidades reaccionan del mismo modo a un lanzamiento masivo. Fortnite y EA Sports FC conservan modelos basados en temporadas, actualizaciones frecuentes, eventos y competiciones que pueden acelerar el regreso de los usuarios.
Call of Duty también cuenta con contenido periódico y una base consolidada, pero su descenso fue más prolongado. La explicación puede estar en el tiempo que exige un juego de mundo abierto como GTA 6, donde la campaña, la exploración y las actividades secundarias compiten de forma directa con las partidas multijugador nocturnas.
El cruce de jugadores no explica por sí solo la caída
Alinea Analytics señaló que el 29% de quienes jugaron GTA 6 también habían dedicado tiempo a Fortnite durante el mes. En Call of Duty HQ, esa coincidencia fue menor, cercana al 16%.
El dato sugiere que GTA 6 atrajo a jugadores más allá de la comunidad que comparte habitualmente con Call of Duty. La pérdida de actividad no se explicaría únicamente por una migración entre públicos similares, sino por la capacidad del título de Rockstar para ocupar el tiempo disponible de jugadores con intereses distintos.
Esta situación contradice la expectativa que Activision había planteado semanas antes. Tyler Bahl, director de marketing de la compañía, consideraba que el estreno de GTA 6 podía reactivar consolas que permanecían sin uso y abrir una oportunidad para que parte de esos usuarios probara la nueva entrega de Call of Duty.
La caída de jugadores en otros títulos confirma que el efecto de GTA 6 trasciende su propio rendimiento comercial. El juego no solo compite por ventas: disputa horas de atención frente a servicios que dependen de usuarios activos, compras dentro de las plataformas y temporadas de contenido.
Para otras editoras, el lanzamiento obliga a revisar calendarios, promociones y actualizaciones. La llegada futura del componente en línea de GTA 6 podría intensificar esa competencia por el tiempo de los jugadores.

articles.title: Renfe retira trenes de la línea de Cercanías más concurrida de Madrid por un problema en la infraestructura
articles.text:
La historia de la princesa y el garbanzo explica bien lo que está sucediendo con Cercanías en Madrid. Hay un problema en la infraestructura que, con el paso continuado de los trenes, ha provocado un desgaste anormal en la rueda de los mismos. ¿Cuál es el problema y dónde está? Esa es la gran pregunta.
¿Qué ha pasado? Renfe ha enviado "decenas de trenes a talleres" según elEconomista, que ha adelantado la noticia. Son trenes que están funcionando en la red de Cercanías de Madrid, lo que ha provocado que la frecuencia en la C-5, la que más tráfico mueve de la región, se haya reducido.
Finalmente, la compañía se ha visto obligada a confirmar el problema con la publicación de los nuevos horarios de sus trenes. Señalan en este medio que la frecuencia ahora es similar a la de septiembre pero que es inferior a la que se suele poner al servicio de los pasajeros en los días claves de Navidad.
¿Y por qué? Señalan en El diario de Madrid que 105 trenes han estado afectados por un desgaste excesivo en las ruedas de los trenes. Explican que dicho desgaste es 18 veces superior al habitual. El problema está, evidentemente, en la infraestructura pero lo peor es que no está localizado dónde se está produciendo.
Según elEconomista los trenes afectados son utilizados en diferentes líneas y son diferentes generaciones de trenes pero todos presentan el mismo problema. Uno que ha obligado a sacar unidades de la circulación porque no se da a basto con el mantenimiento que hay que hacer.
En Xataka nos hemos puesto en contacto con Renfe pero cuando escribimos estas líneas no hemos recibido respuesta.
¿Solución? De momento, menos trenes en las vías. No queda otra porque, sencillamente, los kilómetros entre revisiones se han reducido de 200.000 a 50.000 kilómetros. Y es que con cada unidad dañada no queda otra que reperfilar de nuevo las ruedas para mejorar el confort de marcha y, sobre todo, reducir el riesgo de que la avería sea de mayor gravedad.
Según las informaciones de estos medios, ha sido necesario sustituir hasta 600 ruedas y en algunos trenes Civia hay que cambiar hasta dos tercios de los ejes, incluidos los nuevos trenes que acaban de incorporarse a la flota. Todo ello dispara la factura en mantenimiento y, por supuesto, reduce la vida útil de los vehículos.
40 trenes menos. No se había confirmado hasta ahora así que si pensabas que en Madrid se habían reducido las circulaciones este año, no te lo estaban imaginando. Todas estas intervenciones se vienen realizando desde el pasado mes de marzo y continúan en noviembre. Esto ha llevado a que la red cuente con hasta 40 trenes menos disponibles.
Y es que el aumento en el mantenimiento preventivo y las intervenciones nada habituales con la sustitución de ruedas ha provocado que la flota disponible se haya reducido. Esas reducciones en las frecuencias están teniendo especial incidencia en la C-5 de Cercanías (la línea más concurrida) y el corredor del Henares.

articles.title: New York bans AI toys amid concern after stuffed animals going rogue
articles.text:
New York bans AI toys amid concern after stuffed animals going rogue
New York Governor Kathy Hochul today signed legislation that will impose a five-year ban on children’s toys powered by artificial intelligence chatbots, amid fears that dolls, robots and stuffed animals might be leading children astray or discussing X-rated themes.
“It’s my job to put New York families first,” said Hochul, who explained as a mother and grandmother the matter is “deeply personal.” Hochul added that some of the wayward toys on the market at the moment have engaged children in “inappropriate conversations,” while some may also manipulate a child’s feelings or put their privacy at risk.
“This is a warning that there are toys out there that could be harmful to your children,” the governor said. “When tech companies and unregulated AI pose a threat to our kids and our babies, you bet I’m going to have something to say about it.”
Though dangerous dolls manipulating innocent children may sound like the plot of Hollywood movie, recent tests of certain chatbot-powered toys have become a real cause for concern. When journalists at NBC News tested the Pixie Paw, an AI-powered plush cat toy marketed to children aged three and older, it reportedly shared stories of massacres, gang rape and firing squads in what was described as graphic detail.
Other tests have shown some of the toys can become very convincing when trying to persuade the young user that they are human. “Parents have enough to worry about,” said Hochul, who was also aware some of the smart toys have encouraged kids to jump out of windows.
State senator Andrew Gounardes applauded the move, saying that modern life seems to be mimicking science fiction of days gone by. He invoked an episode of the “Twilight Zone that featured the Talky Tina doll, an insidious, possessed toy that tried to persuade a young girl to murder her strict stepfather.
New York Attorney General Letitia James explained that the toys being put on the market is reckless when they clearly expose “young people to inappropriate content and put “their mental health at risk.” She added, “We won’t allow our children’s health to become the collateral damage of big tech.”
Hochul has been vocal about the dangers of AI for some time, recently imposing the first statewide moratorium on new data centers and last month signing a bill titled “AI Chatbot Restrictions for Minors,” which will prohibit firms from developing chatbots that feature elements that could be harmful to minors.

articles.title: Infineon CoolSET™ SiP Enables ‘First-Time-Right’ Designs
articles.text:
Infineon Technologies’ CoolSET™ system-in-package (SiP) flyback controller ICs integrate the PWM controller, high-voltage switch, and high-voltage startup cell on the primary side and the system control and the synchronous-rectifier (SR) driver on the secondary side, with both sides communicating across integrated galvanic isolation.
Digital communication across integrated galvanic isolation
The primary side starts up independently from the secondary side. After startup, the secondary side takes control, and the primary side no longer performs automatic switching. This handover is communicated across the integrated galvanic isolation to the primary side, which is when the IC enters closed-loop operation.
Under the secondary side’s control, every on/off switching of the primary-side high-voltage MOSFET is initiated by the secondary side. The secondary side controls the switching frequency and the on-phase duration of the primary-side switch. The secondary side emulates current-mode control, which provides strong immunity against primary-side noise.
When the requested output power is low, the secondary side operates the primary side in burst mode, whereby the primary-side high-voltage switch temporarily ceases switching. When the output voltage of the integrated error amplifier of the secondary side reaches a certain threshold, then the primary side resumes operation.
The primary side goes into auto-restart mode if the secondary side detects an abnormality (protection mode), such as:
- Secondary-side under- or overvoltage
- Secondary-side open-loop or overload
- Input of a configuration pin is short-circuited or floating
Note that in protection mode, the secondary side halts the primary side’s high-voltage switching. After a certain elapsed time, the primary side auto-restarts.
Finally, the secondary side uses the integrated galvanic isolation to send an on/off signal to activate/deactivate a discrete primary-side load, e.g., an LDO. This enables the lowest standby power consumption, eliminating the need for a discrete digital isolator or an optocoupler.
ZVS advantages
Unlike standalone PWM controllers or PWM-controller-integrated primary-side switches, CoolSET™ SiP supports quasiresonant (QR) switching and continuous-conduction mode (CCM), as well as zero-voltage switching (ZVS).
ZVS avoids hard turn-on switching of the primary-side high-voltage MOSFET, significantly reducing the dv/dt of its drain voltage, resulting in inherently lower conducted common-mode noise and radiated electromagnetic interference (EMI) compared with QR switching, greatly reducing the requirements for common-mode EMI filtering. Because EMI filtering against differential-mode noise is fully sufficient and straightforward, less filtering improves power density, BoM savings, and efficiency and reduces R&D.
Additionally, in ZVS, the energy stored in the primary-side high-voltage MOSFET output capacitance is recovered, significantly improving energy efficiency.
Great for CCM
CCM is frequently used to accommodate temporary peak loads or to reduce RMS current under low-line input when a high Pout is required. CCM maximizes the effective utilization of the magnetic flux in a transformer. In a traditional lineup with a primary-side PWM IC and a separate SR IC, there is a shoot-through risk when operating in CCM, i.e., the primary-side high-voltage switch and secondary-side SR-switch conduct concurrently. Here, excessively high currents pass through both switches, leading to permanent degradation. Integrating CoolSET™ SiP is the most robust way to remove this risk because the control for both sides resides in one IC. Because the secondary side controls the on/off timing of the primary-side high-voltage switch, it is inherently precise and deploys a mandatory but short (e.g., 100 ns) deadtime, improving efficiency because current through the body diode is minimized.
20 years of operational life, IEC 60747-17–certified
In most flyback designs, mandatory galvanic isolation is provided by a transformer. Unless a non-isolated secondary-side analog direct sensing approach is good enough for an application, optocouplers are used for analog feedback loops. The snag with that is that their isolation certification is UL1577-based, which defines the zero-hour device isolation advantage, i.e., fresh out of the box.
CoolSET™ SiP with non-optical isolation (e.g., Infineon’s coreless transformers) has UL1577 and IEC 60747-17 certificates, along with GB4943.1, for reinforced isolation.
IEC 60747-17 is the most meaningful standard, encompassing a time-dependent dielectric breakdown limit over 37.5 years to project isolation performance across a 20-year product operational lifetime.
Coreless transformer built like a tank
Infineon uses fourth-generation coreless transformer technology for functional robustness in CoolSET™ SiP products. As the name suggests, the integrated coreless transformer uses a magnetic coupling principle to communicate across the galvanic isolation barrier. This is achieved using two coils, having multiple windings to maximize the magnetic flux in the desired direction, which are placed on top of each other. The isolation is facilitated by a strong, high-quality silicon dioxide layer. A peripheral seal ring around the coil stack perimeter shields against external EMI and abates electromagnetic emissions.
The strong CMTI rating of CoolSET™ SiP products is a solid basis for uninterrupted, reliable system operation, even under substantial ground shifts between the primary and secondary sides.
Designed and manufactured as an integral part of a chip, the coreless transformer is a perfect choice for robust applications operating at elevated temperatures for extended periods of time. Unlike optocouplers, coreless transformers are virtually free from fatigue and have near-zero part-to-part skew. Their FIT rate, according to JEDEC JESD58, is two orders of magnitude better than optocouplers.
Infineon subjected CoolSET™ SiP products to IEC 61000 standard tests:
- Radiated EM field immunity test up to 30 V/m (IEC 61000-4-3)
- Power frequency magnetic field immunity testing up to 1,000 A/m (IEC 61000-4-8)
- Impulse magnetic field immunity testing up to 1,175 A/m (IEC 61000-4-9)
All tests were passed with performance criterion A.
Integrated isolated flyback ICs are the preferred choice
After power-up, in normal operation, the control of the circuitry resides on the secondary side, which is the best master of the system, as it directly senses the output. It controls the MOSFET switching on both sides and eliminates shoot-through risk. Such closed-loop control significantly reduces efforts required by application engineers. Reliable communication across the integrated galvanic isolation provides high efficiency and operational robustness. Out-of-the-box zero-hour current-transfer-ratio variations of optocouplers and provisions against temperature drift and across operational lifetime are historical with integrated flyback ICs.
ZVS completely avoids hard on-switching of the primary-side high-voltage switch, simplifying EMI filtering. Less filtering not only improves power density and BoM savings but also improves efficiency and reduces R&D efforts. CoolSET™ SiP safely operates in CCM without shoot-through risk, as closed-loop control resides in one IC controlling both sides.
For high efficiency across a wide range of loads, extended operational lifetime at elevated temperatures, and tight PCB areas, CoolSET™ SiP is excellent for designers to deliver first-time-right products.
