articles.title: Tidal eliminará cerca de 29 millones de canciones creadas con IA
articles.text:
Tidal eliminará cerca de 29 millones de canciones creadas íntegramente con inteligencia artificial a partir del 9 de diciembre de 2026. La plataforma de streaming confirmó que, además, rechazará entre 80.000 y 85.000 pistas diarias generadas por IA una vez entre en vigor la prohibición.
El anuncio lo realizó Robert Andersen, responsable de música de Tidal, a través de una publicación en X. Según sus datos, la música generada por IA representó el 43% de las canciones distribuidas a la plataforma durante los últimos 90 días, una cifra que llevó a la empresa a endurecer su política.
Por qué Tidal decidió prohibir la música de inteligencia artificial
La decisión de Tidal responde a un crecimiento que la plataforma considera insostenible: casi la mitad de todo el contenido que recibía en los últimos tres meses provenía de generadores de IA. Ante ese volumen, la empresa optó por pasar de las medidas parciales a una prohibición total.
El servicio de música en streaming había comenzado meses atrás a etiquetar y desmonetizar las canciones identificadas como generadas íntegramente por inteligencia artificial. Sin embargo, Andersen explicó que esa estrategia resultó insuficiente frente al ritmo de crecimiento del fenómeno.
El ejecutivo también aportó un dato que, según él, respalda la medida desde la perspectiva del oyente: el 96% de las canciones generadas por IA no recibe ninguna reproducción.
“Creemos que esto tendrá repercusión tanto para los artistas como para los oyentes, dado que el 96% de las canciones generadas por IA no reciben ninguna reproducción”, afirmó Andersen.
En qué consiste la prohibición de música de inteligencia artificial en Tidal se resume en una medida concreta: a partir del 9 de diciembre, la plataforma bloqueará el ingreso de canciones creadas exclusivamente con IA y borrará de su catálogo las que ya identificó bajo esa categoría, afectando a unos 29 millones de temas.
Cómo funcionará el bloqueo a distribuidores y canciones generadas por IA
Tidal no se limitará a retirar canciones ya publicadas. La plataforma también prohibirá a los distribuidores de música enviar pistas creadas con inteligencia artificial, lo que implica un filtro previo a la llegada de ese contenido al catálogo.
Para sostener ese control, la plataforma utilizará la herramienta de detección de IA Ircam Amplify junto con comprobaciones de metadatos, mecanismos pensados para rechazar las canciones generadas exclusivamente con esta tecnología antes de que lleguen a los oyentes.
La empresa fue explícita respecto a los límites de su política: no prohibirá las canciones creadas con la ayuda de herramientas de IA, siempre y cuando la inteligencia artificial no sea el único resultado del proceso creativo.
La distinción busca proteger a artistas que incorporan estas herramientas como parte de un proceso con intervención humana, sin alcanzar a la producción íntegramente automatizada.
En una publicación aparte en X, Tidal detalló el problema que busca combatir con esta política. “La música generada íntegramente por IA, con la intención de engañar a los oyentes e imitar a los artistas, es otro problema grave que no ha hecho más que aumentar: desvía las reproducciones y los derechos de autor de los artistas y confunde a los fans”, señaló la plataforma.
Qué otras plataformas de streaming combaten la música generada por IA
Tidal no es la única plataforma que endurece su postura frente a la música generada por inteligencia artificial. Bandcamp prohibió este tipo de contenido a principios de este año, una medida previa a la que ahora adopta Tidal.
Otras plataformas de streaming musical optaron por enfoques distintos, basados en etiquetado y ajustes algorítmicos en lugar de prohibiciones totales. Spotify anunció recientemente que eliminó 50 millones de canciones basura y spam de IA de las recomendaciones durante el último año.
Spotify también lanzó nuevas insignias de “persona de IA” para los artistas que usan una identidad de inteligencia artificial, una forma de transparencia dirigida a que los oyentes identifiquen el origen del contenido sin necesariamente eliminarlo del catálogo.
Por su parte, YouTube implementó etiquetas de música de IA, sumándose a una tendencia de la industria que combina distintas estrategias: desde el etiquetado y la desmonetización hasta la eliminación directa, como ahora aplicará Tidal a partir de diciembre.

articles.title: Como desligar o PS5 com segurança (com ou sem controle)
articles.text:
Como desligar o PS5 com segurança (com ou sem controle)
Desligar o PS5 com segurança evita a corrupção de saves e a reconstrução do banco de dados do sistema
Você pode desligar o PlayStation 5 de forma rápida pelo menu “Energia” utilizando o controle DualSense ou segurando o botão de energia diretamente no console. Independentemente da escolha, aguarde sempre a luz indicadora parar de piscar e apagar por completo antes de desconectar o cabo da tomada.
Seguir esse cuidado para desligar PS5 corretamente protege o SSD interno e garante que os processos em segundo plano sejam encerrados sem falhas. Cortes bruscos de energia podem corromper seus saves de jogos e até exigir a reconstrução do banco de dados do sistema.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog te mostra o passo a passo para desligar o PS5 com segurança.
Para desligar o PS5 pelo controle DualSense de forma segura, basta acessar o menu rápido do console em poucos segundos.
Dê um toque rápido no botão PS, aquele com o logotipo da marca localizado no centro do DualSense, para abrir o Centro de Controle do PS5 na parte inferior da tela.
Use os direcionais do controle para navegar até o ícone Energia, geralmente posicionado na extremidade direita do Centro de Controle, e confirme a seleção apertando o botão X.
Escolha a opção “Desligar PS5” para desligar o PlayStation 5 com segurança e aguarde até que a luz indicadora do console pare de piscar em branco antes de removê-lo da tomada.
Se o controle DualSense descarregou ou não está por perto, você pode desligar o PS5 corretamente diretamente pelo botão de energia do console. Então, faça os seguintes passos:
- Localize o botão de energia na parte frontal do PS5.
- Mantenha esse botão pressionado por cerca de três segundos até ouvir um bipe emitido pelo console.
- Solte o botão imediatamente após o bipe para não forçar um desligamento brusco.
- Aguarde a luz indicadora piscar em branco e apagar por completo antes de mover o console ou desconectá-lo da tomada.
Desligar o PS5 puxando o cabo da tomada com o console ligado corta a energia bruscamente, o que pode corromper arquivos salvos e danificar o armazenamento SSD interno. Na próxima vez que você ligar o aparelho, o sistema operacional precisará executar uma reconstrução do banco de dados para tentar reparar esses erros.
Para proteger o console, certifique-se sempre de que todos os processos em segundo plano tenham sido encerrados antes de desconectá-lo da rede elétrica. Observe a luz indicadora do gabinete e só retire o fio quando ela estiver completamente apagada, já que qualquer sinal luminoso indica a gravação de dados em andamento.
Sim, é possível desligar o PS5 pelo celular usando o app PS Remote Play, ferramenta que espelha a tela do console pela internet para controle à distância. Como o PlayStation App não traz um botão direto para essa tarefa, basta iniciar uma sessão de Uso Remoto, tocar no ícone do botão PS na interface virtual e selecionar “Desligar PS5” no menu Energia.
Para realizar a ação, o console precisa estar ligado ou em modo repouso com a conexão à internet e o acesso remoto previamente ativados nas configurações do sistema. Além disso, o celular deve estar logado na mesma conta PlayStation (PSN) e contar com uma rede Wi-Fi ou móvel estável para evitar falhas de conexão.
Sim, você desliga apenas o DualSense pressionando o botão PS por cerca de 10 a 12 segundos até que a barra de luz do controle apague por completo. Esse atalho encerra apenas o pareamento sem fio Bluetooth do acessório para economizar bateria, mantendo o PS5 ligado enquanto você assiste a filmes ou faz uma pausa.

articles.title: I’ve tested 7 gaming headsets while playing GTA 6 for 130 hours, from budget bangers to premium planars, and I'd recommend any one of them this Black Friday
articles.text:
I've now clocked up around 130 hours in Grand Theft Auto 6 and have been using a host of different gadgets since booting it up for the very first time for review last month.
One of the areas of gaming hardware I know most about is headsets, and I've been able to test a fair few while playing GTA 6. From premium planar sets to mid-range open-backers, to budget-friendly reliable wired headsets, I've really mixed it up with my Vice City audio experience.
And getting the most out of your sound and audio is something you'll want to consider with GTA 6: it's got some incredible audio design, sound effects, and use of music, which only pulls you further into the game if you've got some awesome gear to immerse you deeper.
This isn't an exhaustive list by any means, but a short list of the sets I've been able to test and why they might be good ones to look out for if you're after something to enhance your Vice City audio experience.
Audeze Maxwell 2 ANC and 'regular' Maxwell 2 — planar brilliance
My absolute favorite gaming headsets of the day for pure quality audio were always going to be one of my top picks for and best experiences in GTA 6.
The planar magnetic drivers of the Maxwell 2 and Maxwell2 ANC are a huge joy for listening to the world and soundscape of Leonida. The detail of the audio is extraordinary to begin with, but then being able to hear all of it so clearly through the Maxwell 2's drivers is truly excellent. And even when things get their most chaotic in car crashes and high-octane gunfights with gangs, you'll still be able to hear clearly.
The Maxwell 2 ANC then offers you the extra welcome functionality of just shutting off the outside world by enabling the noise cancellation — and it won't kill the bass, either.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Beyerdynamic MMX 130 wireless
If you're looking for a gaming headset that's in the 'slightly north of $100 / £100' price bracket, then the recently released Beyerdynamic MMX 130 Wireless is one of the easiest headsets to recommend. It's such a good headset, and at such a good price.
I have loved using this headset, and have probably used it the second most out of all the products listed here. It's an open-back beauty that channels all the audio brilliance and pedigree of Beyerdynamic to make for a fantastically expansive soundscape experience, which has been a joy.
It's simple to use and get going with, has no complicated parts, and is also fabulously comfortable, so you won't even remember you're wearing it in those long, long hours in Vice City.
SteelSeries Arctis Nova 1
If you really need to keep the budget down when thinking about a headset for GTA 6, then the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 1 is a belter of a headset that won't cost you much, and if you don't mind being tethered to your controller, it will offer you a cracking audio experience.
While it sits at the budget end of SteelSeries' headset range, it still shares a lot of the same pedigree, standards, and audio quality that the very top of the brand's line offers — see below for more on those.
At its core, it has the same 40-mm neodymium drivers as other more expensive headsets in the SteelSeries range, which offer excellent audio quality of all kinds, and while its build might not be quite as robust or premium-feeling or changeable through a companion app, it's comfortable to wear, has easy-to-handle controls, and is spectacular value for money — especially in sales periods when you can pick one up for a song.
Turtle Beach Stealth Pro 2 — Superb superhuman hearing
I knew the Turtle Beach Stealth Pro 2 headset would likely be a great fit for Leonida — we did give it a full five stars after all — but I have been really taken with this headset, particularly when it comes to gunfire, deep and rumbling noises, and, in particular, that Superhuman Hearing feature.
These are the kind of things that Turtle Beach headsets have always done well anyway: proper gaming audio that accentuates the big and bombastic noises such as gunfire, crashes, chaos, high-octane impacts, and more.
However, with a touch of that Superhuman Hearing button to engage the feature, the headset offers a whole new level of immersion; details become more detailed (somehow), everything becomes clearer, and as a result, the immersion is greater. A fabulous choice for GTA 6.
SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni
One of my favorite headset releases of the year: the Nova Pro Omni from SteelSeries is such a great Swiss Army Knife of a gaming headset and one that's perfect to deploy for GTA 6.
As well as offering that excellent default SteelSeries audio quality right out of the box, it's got a whole host of 2026-ifications that make it a world-beater of a multiplatform headset. It builds upon the Nova Pro Wireless beautifully with a host of comfort and design benefits such as plush earcups and a ratcheted volume wheel, excellent battery life for those long hours driving across Vice City, and brilliant, certified Hi-Res wireless audio.
I've found it a particularly excellent option for playing GTA 6 on my PS5 Pro as part of a PC-and-console setup — it's a single headset solution to a multiplatform setup and makes it perfect for playing and absorbing the game on one platform, while being able to enjoy media, look up guides, or devour albums of music from artists from the game all in the comfort of one seat.
SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite
But the only real problem I have with the above Nova Pro Omni is that the Nova Elite exists, and I could test that straight after.
Both are wonderful headsets that I'd encourage anyone to go for if they are considering; however, the Nova Elite really does just offer something extra on the audio quality front. It just sounds better. Those custom carbon fiber drivers and the brass ring surround do seem to offer a level of audio brilliance that's both of the SteelSeries style and quality, but simultaneously better than the other SteelSeries headsets.
So if you had narrowed it down to one or the other of SteelSeries' premium headsets, then it might just be the sheer audio quality and prowess of the Elite that wins you over — as it did with me in GTA 6, as everything just sounded sharper, clearer, and offered more depth and richness, be it sirens from afar, vocal tones from NPCs, or the chaotic barrages of music and gunfights at the same time.

articles.title: Husband of Jensen Huang’s mistress has much more significant Chinese intelligence connections than her, report claims — US officials warn he was asset with Ministry of State Security connections
articles.text:
Husband of Jensen Huang’s mistress has much more significant Chinese intelligence connections than her, report claims — US officials warn he was asset with Ministry of State Security connections
The former Megaspeed employee's husband has ties to the Chinese intelligence service, officials have warned.
Just a day after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO, U.S. intelligence officials met to deliver a briefing to Congress about one of his love interests and her alleged ties to China's Ministry of State Security, or MSS. Alice Huang has been accused of being a Chinese spy, and her affair with Jensen Huang saw the Nvidia founder resign. But even with Jensen Huang now back in the saddle at Nvidia, attention has turned to whether she posed, or poses, a security threat to the United States as a whole, and its place in the global AI food chain. A New York Times report details the meeting for staff members of the House and Senate intelligence committees and aides to the leaders of both chambers, including its bombshell news that Alice Huang's husband has a much more significant intelligence connection.
The intelligence officials told those in attendance that they still don't fully understand what role Alice Huang played in the saga, but that there is no evidence that she initiated the affair at the behest of Chinese authorities. That being said, they also refused to dispute that she passed intelligence back to the country's top intelligence agency while the affair was underway. Further, the officials told those at the meeting that Alice Huang's husband, Kang Wei, was a more significant figure with respect to any connection to the MSS. In fact, he had at times been an MSS asset with deeper contacts within the agency than his wife. It's been reported that Alice Huang was in contact with the Chinese spy agency from the spring of 2025 until the fall of 2026, while Kang Wei was also in contact with the same agency during that time.
Alice Huang was a Megaspeed employee when it was a customer of Nvidia. The data center company was buying Nvidia's AI chips and is now under a criminal investigation over claims that it was bypassing export controls in an effort to get those advanced chips into China. The company has since been placed on a U.S. blocklist.
Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia came after days of campaigning for his reinstatement, including by U.S. President Trump. Trump later pressured Nvidia to rehire him, going so far as to call into a board meeting to do so. Despite Trump's backing, Jensen Huang must still face Congressional and Senate committees to discuss Nvidia, export controls, and any national security threats brought about by his infidelity.

articles.title: Un oso pardo ha muerto de un disparo durante una batida de jabalíes en Picos de Europa. Ahora hay una investigación abierta
articles.text:
El viernes 20 de noviembre se rastreó la zona y no apareció ningún indicio de oso. Sin embargo, al día siguiente, en Posada de Valdeón, dentro del Parque Nacional de los Picos de Europa, un disparo mataba a un oso pardo durante una batida de jabalíes. Este es uno de los grandes refugios del oso pardo en la cordillera Cantábrica. Hablamos de una especie en peligro de extinción, abatida en un espacio donde, sobre el papel, ya no se caza.
Qué ha pasado. Según la nota de la Junta recogida por iLeón, la actuación estaba supervisada por un agente medioambiental y dos celadores, además de vecinos con la formación exigida. El cadáver fue llevado al Centro de Recuperación de Animales Silvestres de Valladolid para la necropsia. No han trascendido ni el sexo, ni la edad del ejemplar.
La Junta asegura que se aplicaron los protocolos y que el rastreo del viernes no halló (valga la redundancia) rastro alguno. La primera hipótesis, según Infobae, apunta a un error: ¿de prevención o de alguien poniendo la mira de su rifle, en pleno monte, sobre el cuerpo del animal? Todavía no se sabe: el Seprona investiga las circunstancias y del autor, un joven cazador de una localidad del municipio, no ha trascendido nombre, ni detención, denuncia o expediente público.
¿Defensa propia? El lunes 23 de noviembre, el consejero de Agricultura de Castilla y León, Joaquín Antonio Pino (Vox), atribuyó el disparo a "un acto en defensa propia". Según El País, es una tesis que ni la Junta ni las fuentes del sector forestal habían planteado hasta entonces. Hasta ese momento, Medio Ambiente solo había insistido en que la batida tenía todos los permisos y en que el rastreo del día anterior no halló indicios de oso. Medio Ambiente, que dirige María González Corral (PP), sigue remitiendo todo a la investigación del Seprona.
Cazar donde no se caza. La Ley de Parques Nacionales prohíbe la caza deportiva, y en Picos de Europa no se caza desde 2020. Pero permite controlar especies sobreabundantes con informes científicos. El jabalí entra en esta ecuación especialmente por los daños al hábitat y las enfermedades que transmite al ganado.
La parte leonesa del parque (23.580 de sus 66.030 hectáreas) se rige por un decreto de diciembre de 2025 que exige controles selectivos y los prohíbe en zonas de reserva. De hecho, que el control de jabalíes esté autorizado no significa que lo esté matar un oso. Por ese hueco se está colando todo el caso.
La reacción de WWF. Habla de “hecho de extrema gravedad” y exige una investigación exhaustiva. Sostiene que los mecanismos de autorización “han fallado”, pide suspender todas las batidas del parque, publicar protocolos, informes de actuación y necropsia, y critica el uso de cazadores locales y perros. Estudia personarse por la vía administrativa y la penal.
PACMA también ha cargado contra un hecho “gravísimo e inadmisible” y exige el cese de controles letales de fauna en espacios protegidos. La Fundación Franz Weber llevará el caso a la comisaria europea de Medio Ambiente, Jessika Roswall, y pide una investigación independiente. Fuentes del sector forestal leonés recelan de ese anuncio tardío y lo ven una "treta para librar de la multa" al cazador.
Qué dice el Código Penal. El artículo 334 castiga con prisión de seis meses a dos años (o multa de ocho a veinticuatro meses) a quien, contraviniendo las normas, mate especies protegidas, con inhabilitación para cazar de dos a cuatro años. Si están en peligro de extinción, la pena se impone en su mitad superior; si hay imprudencia grave, baja a entre tres meses y un año de prisión. Habrá que determinar cómo se produjo el disparo y si hubo imprudencia.
Ya van unos cuantos. En noviembre de 2020, en una cacería de jabalíes en la Montaña Palentina, un hombre mató a una osa de un tiro desde unos 40 metros. En febrero de 2024, el Juzgado de lo Penal de Palencia lo condenó a dos años de cárcel, cuatro de inhabilitación para cazar y 17.505,95 euros de responsabilidad civil a la Junta, la mitad de lo pedido por la Fiscalía y la Fundación Oso Pardo, porque la cacería debió suspenderse al saberse que había una osa con su cría. Tres años y medio entre el disparo y la sentencia.
Éxito frágil. El último censo genético, de 2023, contó 370 osos cantábricos: 250 en la subpoblación occidental y 120 en la oriental. El Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica presume un salto de menos de 70 a más de 400 ejemplares en menos de 30 años. Pero el área de cría apenas ha crecido en 45 años, según el estudio de la Estación Biológica de Doñana, y la especie sigue en peligro de extinción. Un oso muerto es uno de cada 370.
Los defensores del control tienen argumentos: sin él, el jabalí daña el parque y el ganado. Pero si un oso puede estar ahí aunque nadie lo vea y si ya hay precedentes con condena, ¿tiene sentido batir en pleno territorio del oso? Además, ya no se quedan en lo más profundo del monte: ya contamos cómo en Asturias hay pueblos donde se los encuentran en la puerta de casa. A más recuperación, más convivencia y menos margen de error.

articles.title: Shuttle lance un mini PC ultra-compact de 0,4 litre avec processeur Intel Wildcat Lake
articles.text:
Un temps pionnier sur le mini-PC, Shuttle veut revenir dans la course et profite pour cela de la génération Wildcat Lake d'Intel.
Shuttle est une marque emblématique du phénomène du mini-PC et si la firme est moins en vogue depuis déjà quelques années, elle cherche toujours à proposer des produits innovants. Semi-durci et conçu autour de la génération Wildcat Lake d'Intel, le NW10U est de ceux-là.
Shuttle mise sur Wildcat Lake
Juillet 2002. Voilà qui ne nous rajeunit pas. À l'époque déjà, je testais des composants pour Clubic et j'avais été l'un des premiers Européens à mettre la main sur le SS50, un PC pas tout à fait comme les autres.
Venue d'Asie, la vague des mini-PC commençait à peine à arriver en Europe et le shuttle SS50 était l'un des premiers modèles à être disponible sur le Vieux Continent. Des sacrifices, il fallait en faire – notamment au niveau de la carte graphique – mais l'idée était déjà de proposer des PC aussi complets que possible tout en réduisant fortement leur encombrement.
Vous vous en doutez, en près de 25 ans, de l'eau a coulé sous les ponts et, paradoxalement, l'une des marques pionnières en la matière a presque disparu des radars, en tout cas en Europe. Shuttle existe toujours, mais sa présence en France est bien moins notable et des marques de mini-PC comme Beelink, Geekom ou NiPoGi l'ont largement éclipsé.
Éclipsé certes, mais Shuttle n'a pas dit son dernier mot et la firme taïwanaise dispose encore d'une belle réputation, notamment dans son pays d'origine où elle cherche encore et toujours à innover là où les marques de mini-PC se copient très souvent les unes les autres.
Un mini-PC d'à peine 0,4 litre de volume
Le NW10U s'inscrit dans cette ambition d'apporter quelque chose de neuf au monde du mini-PC et, pour ce faire, il se repose sur la nouvelle architecture Wildcat Lake d'Intel.
Si vous connaissez cette gamme de puces, vous savez déjà que l'objectif n'est pas la quête de la puissance extrême, mais plutôt celle du compromis entre puissance effective et empreinte énergétique afin de limiter à la fois le bruit, la consommation et la chauffe. Signe qui ne trompe pas, le NW10U est d'ailleurs un produit que Shuttle présente comme « semi-durci ».
Derrière ce terme se cache un PC conçu pour fonctionner même dans des environnements relativement hostiles : Shuttle parle d'une machine capable de tourner 24 heures sur 24, 7 jours sur 7, et ce, avec une température ambiante comprise entre 0°C et 50°C. Mieux, le NW10U reste redoutablement compact, avec un volume de 0,4 litre (103 x 97 x 36,5 mm).
À l'intérieur de la bête, on retrouve au choix Intel Core 3 304, Core 5 320, Core 7 350 de la gamme Wildcat Lake, soit 5 ou 6 cœurs avec un TDP de 15 watts et un maximum de 64 Go de mémoire vive DDR5-6400. Il est prévu un maximum de deux SSD M.2 NVMe 2280 PCIe 4.0 avec option RAID 0/1 et un troisième M.2 au format 2230 est prévu pour un module sans fil optionnel.
Shuttle met en avant la riche connectique – compte tenu de la taille du PC – avec un port HDMI 2.1, deux USB-C compatibles DisplayPort 2.1 ainsi que deux USB-A 3.2 et deux USB-A 2.0. Un port Ethernet RJ45 à la norme 1 GbE vient compléter l'ensemble alors que Shuttle souligne la présence d'une fixation VESA compatible 75 x 75 mm et 100 x 100 mm. Bien vu.
Pour l'heure, nous ne savons pas si ce mini-PC ultra compact sera disponible en Europe, à fortiori en France. Il est toutefois question d'un prix de 1 259 dollars pour la version Core 3 304 avec 8 Go de RAM et un SSD de 512 Go, tandis que le modèle « haut de gamme » est facturé 3 034 dollars avec un Core 7 350, 32 Go de RAM et un SSD de 1 To. Tout cela, hors taxes : oui, ça pique quand même pas mal.
Source : Shuttle

articles.title: Nouveau smartphone : B&YOU associe 170 Go en 5G et Amazon Prime à petit prix
articles.text:
B&YOU : un forfait 5G avec Prime inclus à moins de 15 €/mois
Pour le Black Friday, B&YOU réduit le prix de son forfait 170 Go 5G avec Amazon Prime inclus. Une formule sans engagement à considérer après l'achat d'un nouveau smartphone.
B&YOU : 170 Go en 5G et Amazon Prime pour 14,99 €/mois
Un smartphone acheté pendant le Black Friday, c'est bien. Encore faut-il lui associer un forfait mobile adapté à ses usages. B&YOU profite de cette période commerciale pour mettre en avant son forfait 170 Go en 5G avec Amazon Prime inclus, proposé à 14,99 €/mois au lieu de 17,99 €/mois. Une réduction de 3 € par mois qui permet aussi de profiter de plusieurs services de la plateforme sans souscrire un abonnement Prime séparément.
Cette formule s'adresse notamment aux personnes qui utilisent régulièrement leur smartphone pour regarder des vidéos, écouter de la musique, naviguer sur Internet ou consulter leurs réseaux sociaux. Avec une enveloppe de 170 Go, les usages mobiles peuvent rester confortables, y compris en déplacement.
Le forfait comprend notamment :
- 170 Go de data en 5G utilisables en France métropolitaine.
- 60 Go depuis l'Europe et les DOM pour rester connecté pendant les déplacements.
- Appels, SMS et MMS illimités en France métropolitaine.
- Amazon Prime inclus, avec Prime Video, la livraison Premium et les offres réservées aux membres.
L'abonnement reste sans engagement. Il est donc possible de changer de formule ou de résilier sans attendre une échéance contractuelle. Un point intéressant pour accompagner l'achat d'un smartphone en promotion sans multiplier les contraintes sur la durée.
Un forfait avec Prime inclus, mais à quel prix sur la durée ?
L'intégration d'Amazon Prime constitue l'un des principaux arguments de cette offre. En plus du forfait mobile, l'abonnement donne accès au catalogue de films et de séries de Prime Video, à la livraison rapide sur des millions d'articles et à certaines promotions réservées aux membres. Pour les personnes qui utilisent déjà ces services, l'économie peut donc être intéressante.
B&YOU propose également une formule de 170 Go avec Deezer Premium inclus, elle aussi affichée avec une réduction de 3 €/mois pendant le Black Friday. Le choix dépendra surtout des habitudes : streaming vidéo et achats en ligne d'un côté, musique de l'autre.
Attention toutefois aux conditions de l'offre : les 14,99 €/mois correspondent au tarif promotionnel. Il faut également vérifier les modalités d'inclusion d'Amazon Prime et les destinations couvertes par les 60 Go utilisables à l'étranger (Europe et DOM).
Au final, ce forfait B&YOU constitue une option intéressante pour accompagner un smartphone acheté pendant le Black Friday. Avec 170 Go en 5G, les appels illimités et Prime inclus, il réunit une enveloppe data confortable et plusieurs services dans un abonnement sans engagement.

articles.title: SpaceX de Elon Musk recibe autorización para lanzar un millón de satélites y crear centros de datos en el espacio
articles.text:
La Comisión Federal de Comunicaciones de Estados Unidos (FCC) autorizó a SpaceX, la compañía aeroespacial de Elon Musk, a desplegar un millón de satélites para crear una constelación de centros de datos en el espacio.
La autorización permitirá a SpaceX poner en órbita hasta un millón de módulos informáticos de la constelación Starmind, destinados a procesar grandes cantidades de datos que luego se utilizarían en la Tierra.
Según la FCC, se trata de la primera autorización de este tipo en la historia de Estados Unidos.
La agencia estadounidense señaló que el proyecto busca responder a la creciente demanda de capacidad de procesamiento para inteligencia artificial. Los módulos orbitales utilizarían energía solar y operarían de acuerdo con las normas de la FCC sobre desechos espaciales.
Qué autoriza la FCC a SpaceX
La decisión habilita a SpaceX a establecer una red de centros de datos orbitales a gran escala. La compañía había solicitado el permiso a principios de 2026 para desplegar los módulos informáticos y procesar datos desde el espacio.
Además, la FCC autorizó el uso de enlaces de radiofrecuencia para respaldo, telemetría de emergencia, seguimiento y control de los satélites. También aprobó comunicaciones adicionales para reforzar la red óptica de la empresa.
De acuerdo con los términos del permiso, SpaceX deberá iniciar el despliegue antes de noviembre de 2033. La empresa tendrá que poner en órbita 100.000 satélites antes de noviembre de 2035 y completar el 50% del proyecto antes de noviembre de 2038.
Respuesta de Elon Musk ante la autorización de la FCC
El presidente de la FCC, Brendan Carr, sostuvo que el traslado de la capacidad de procesamiento fuera de la Tierra permitirá responder a las necesidades de infraestructura para la inteligencia artificial.
“Al trasladar la capacidad de procesamiento más allá de la Tierra, SpaceX y los numerosos competidores que desarrollan sus propios centros de datos orbitales están respondiendo a las exigencias de este momento histórico”, expresó.
Carr afirmó que los centros de datos son esenciales para sostener el liderazgo de Estados Unidos en inteligencia artificial y que las constelaciones orbitales podrían aprovechar la energía solar de forma casi constante.
Por su parte, Elon Musk respondió al anuncio de la FCC en X: “Muy agradecido. Esto será un gran activo para América y el mundo”.
La FCC indicó que continúa evaluando otras propuestas de centros de datos orbitales y que emitirá resoluciones sobre cada una de ellas conforme a sus procedimientos habituales.
Elon Musk visita a Jensen Huang en sede de Nvidia
Elon Musk estuvo en las oficinas centrales de Nvidia, en Santa Clara, California, para mantener una reunión con Jensen Huang, máximo responsable de la empresa de chips e inteligencia artificial.
El fundador de Tesla y SpaceX asistió junto a dos de sus hijos y replicó en X una imagen del encuentro que había publicado la cuenta Tesla Owners Silicon Valley. Por su parte, Ben Pouladian, fundador de BEP Research y accionista de Nvidia, difundió otras fotografías de los dos empresarios.
La reunión se realizó después de que Nvidia anunciara, el 23 de noviembre, el retorno de Huang como director ejecutivo.
El directivo había dejado el cargo el 12 de noviembre, en medio de cuestionamientos vinculados con su conducta personal y eventuales implicaciones para la seguridad nacional. Musk celebró su vuelta con un mensaje en X: “El error ha sido corregido”.
El directorio de Nvidia señaló que avaló la reincorporación después de conversar con Huang y recopilar información de altos funcionarios estadounidenses.
La compañía afirmó que no considera que su regreso represente un riesgo para la seguridad nacional, aunque continuará con la investigación interna sobre las circunstancias de su salida.
Durante una reunión con empleados, Huang admitió fallas, ofreció disculpas y remarcó que debe cumplir las reglas de la empresa. Está previsto que responda preguntas de legisladores de Estados Unidos en diciembre de 2026.

articles.title: Attacker used 1Password employee's GitHub account to copy customer records
articles.text:
Attacker used 1Password employee’s GitHub account to copy customer records
Identity security company 1Password today disclosed a security incident in which an attacker, working through an employee’s corporate GitHub account, copied account records belonging to a subset of its customers.
According to the company, the incident came to light on Nov. 19, when 1Password began investigating signs that the GitHub account had been compromised. Using the account, the attacker is said to have pushed malicious code to 1Password’s backend services, which then downloaded what the company describes as “administrative data pertaining to our customers.”
The records taken include names and email addresses, account and user identifiers, account creation and last sign-in times, public keys, Secure Remote Password protocol parameters and other non-secret account metadata. Rounding out the list are tokens found in certain emailed links for invitations, provisioning and account recovery.
Customer vaults, the items stored in them and the keys that protect them were not affected, according to 1Password. “At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker,” the company said in its disclosure. Account passwords and Secret Keys are not stored by the company. Also left untouched, the company says, were account recovery keys and the 1Password apps and browser extensions.
Beyond the customer records, the attacker is said to have copied source code from private repositories. Access was also gained to 1Password’s continuous integration and continuous delivery system, which contains infrastructure-related secrets needed for its product to work. According to 1Password, the source code contains no user secrets. Having triggered a rotation of all credentials that may have been exposed, the company claims there has been no impact to its services, availability or product security.
The tokens taken from emailed links cannot be used on their own to access an account, since completing an invitation or recovery also requires a sign-in through single sign-on or a six-digit code sent to the user’s registered email address. Users with provisioning invites or recovery requests pending at the time of the incident, said to be a small number, have been notified directly.
As a precaution, the emailed codes have now been lengthened from six numeric digits to 10 alphanumeric characters. 1Password says it has found no internal evidence of account takeovers using the exposed tokens. Other steps taken in response include disabling the affected GitHub account, revoking the stolen token, tightening internal controls and bringing in independent cybersecurity experts to validate its containment and remediation work.
Customers do not need to change anything in their 1Password accounts. The company is instead warning users to be cautious of phishing attempts, such as unexpected emails, texts or calls about invitations or account recovery requests they did not start. “1Password will never contact you to ask for your account password or Secret Key,” the company noted.
1Password, which claims to serve more than 200,000 businesses, did not say how many customers had records downloaded. How the employee’s GitHub account was compromised was also left unexplained.
This is not the first intrusion 1Password has disclosed. In October 2023, the company said that an attacker had accessed its Okta tenant using session data stolen in the breach of Okta Inc.’s customer support system. No user data was found to have been compromised in that case.
Today’s disclosure comes nearly four years after rival password manager LastPass US LP revealed that a hacker had copied encrypted customer password vaults, using information taken in an earlier breach of its development environment.
1Password says it will update its post if the investigation turns up anything that changes what it has disclosed so far.

articles.title: GameSir Introduces Nova Vision Controller with Built-In LCD Screen and Adjustable Tension Sticks
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
GameSir Introduces Nova Vision Controller with Built-In LCD Screen and Adjustable Tension Sticks
GameSir has just announced the Nova Vision, a versatile gaming controller designed to make customization more accessible through a built-in 0.96-inch LCD screen. Allowing players to adjust and view key settings directly on the controller, Nova Vision combines convenient on-screen controls with adjustable stick resistance, dual-mode triggers and support for Nintendo Switch, PC and mobile gaming.
Designed for players who want greater control over how their controller feels and responds, Nova Vision features GameSir Hall Effect sticks with adjustable tension from 30gf to 80gf, a polling rate of up to 1,000 Hz and a six-axis gyroscope for motion-based gameplay. Two additional back buttons, macro recording and customization through the GameSir App or GameSir Connect software provide further flexibility across supported platforms.At the heart of Nova Vision is a 0.96-inch LCD screen with a resolution of 160 × 80 pixels, bringing controller settings directly to the device. Rather than relying solely on external software to make adjustments, players can view and interact with settings on the built-in display, making it easier to personalize their setup and fine-tune their controls.For further customization, the GameSir App and GameSir Connect software provide access to additional settings and profiles, giving players more ways to adapt the controller to their preferred games and play styles.
Nova Vision features GameSir Hall Effect sticks designed to provide consistent control while helping to prevent stick drift. Their adjustable tension system ranges from 30 gf to 80 gf, allowing players to choose a lighter resistance for smoother movement or a firmer feel for more deliberate, precise inputs.The controller also features dual-mode triggers, combining Hall Effect analogue triggers for progressive input with Micro Switch trigger stops for quicker actuation. Players can switch between trigger modes to suit different genres, whether they prefer the finer control required for racing games or faster responses in action-packed shooters.
With a polling rate of up to 1,000 Hz, Nova Vision is designed to deliver responsive input, while its six-axis gyroscope supports motion controls for compatible games, including aiming and steering.
Two additional back buttons provide more options for assigning frequently used commands, while support for up to 12-step macro recording allows players to configure sequences of inputs through the GameSir App or GameSir Connect software.Dual asymmetric vibration motors deliver tactile feedback during gameplay, supported by an instant start-stop circuit designed to provide more immediate vibration responses. Laser-engraved textured grips add extra grip and comfort, helping players maintain control during longer sessions.
Designed primarily for Nintendo Switch and Switch 2, Nova Vision also supports PC and mobile gaming. Tri-mode connectivity provides Bluetooth, 2.4 GHz wireless and wired options, offering flexibility across supported devices.
The controller includes a 1,000 mAh battery and weighs 240 g, making it a practical option for both home gaming and portable setups. A charging station is available as an optional accessory, with the bundle configuration providing additional value for players looking for a more complete setup.
GameSir Nova Vision - Specifications
- Compatible platforms: Nintendo Switch, Switch 2, PC and mobile
- Connectivity: Bluetooth, 2.4 GHz wireless and wired
- Polling rate: Up to 1,000 Hz
- Display: 0.96-inch LCD screen, 160 × 80 resolution, with screen interaction
- Analogue sticks: GameSir Hall Effect sticks
- Adjustable stick tension: 30 gf - 80 gf
- Bumpers: Tactile Switch
- Triggers: Hall Effect analogue triggers with Micro Switch trigger stops
- Home/View/Menu buttons: Tactile Switch
- ABXY buttons: Membrane
- D-pad: Tactile Switch
- Back buttons: Two, with support for up to 12-step macro recording
- Gyroscope: Six-axis motion control
- Battery capacity: 1,000 mAh
- Turbo function: Supported via GameSir App / GameSir Connect
- Macro function: Supported via GameSir App / GameSir Connect
- Vibration: Dual asymmetric grip motors with instant start-stop circuit
- Grips: Laser-engraved textured grips
- Customization software: GameSir App / GameSir Connect
- Product dimensions: 155 × 104 × 57 mm (6.10 × 4.09 × 2.24 in)
- Net weight: 240 g (0.53 lb)
- Package dimensions: 180 × 154 × 86 mm (7.09 × 6.06 × 3.39 in)
- Gross package weight: 436 g (0.96 lb)
- Gross package weight (bundle): 615 g (1.36 lb)
The GameSir Nova Vision is available for $54.99 / £59.99 from the GameSir website, Amazon US and Amazon UK.
Source:
				GameSir

articles.title: iPhone 15 (256 GB) recebe o segundo maior desconto do ano na Black Week
articles.text:
iPhone 15 (256 GB) recebe o segundo maior desconto do ano na Black Week
iPhone 15 (256 GB) com tela OLED de 2.000 nits e câmera de 48 MP fica abaixo da metade do preço no Pix em oferta da Amazon, na semana da Black Friday 2026
O iPhone 15 de 256 GB está saindo por apenas R$ 3.999 no Pix na Amazon. O celular da Apple, com câmera wide de 48 MP e tela OLED de 2.000 nits, atinge o 2.º menor preço de 2026 na semana da Black Friday, com desconto de 51% sobre o original de R$ 8.099.
Esta oferta é interessante para quem procura um celular da maçã acessível e com mais câmeras que o 16e e 17e, mas está disposto a abrir mão do Apple Intelligence para isso.
O menor preço que já encontramos para o iPhone 15 256 GB foi R$ 3.499, na Black Friday de 2026 (Amazon). Fora de datas promocionais, esta oferta é o menor preço que já encontramos.
O iPhone 15 é o modelo mais acessível dos celulares da Apple no momento. Seu chip A16 Bionic e os 6 GB de RAM rodam apps pesados e games, mas não suportam a suíte Apple Intelligence. Os 256 GB de espaço interno são adequados para guardar fotos e vídeos.

articles.title: No GPS required: Ukrainian 11th-grader creates AI drone navigation system
articles.text:
No Starlink, no problem, part deux: Ukrainian student invents autopilot system for UAV that works without GPS, receives "The future of Ukraine" presidential award
Ukrainian teenager builds an AI-powered drone guidance system
- Ukrainian teenager develops drone autopilot capable of operating without GPS signals
- 11th-grade student Yaroslav Sheiko receives Ukraine's presidential award for drone innovations
- Artificial intelligence powers the student's GPS-independent drone navigation technology
A Ukrainian high school student has developed drone technology capable of guiding unmanned aircraft without depending on satellite navigation systems.
Yaroslav Sheiko, an 11th-grade pupil from Poltava, received the presidential distinction known as "The Future of Ukraine" for his engineering achievements.
His work includes an artificial intelligence-powered flight control system and optical-electronic stabilization technology designed for unmanned aerial vehicles.
Ukrainian student develops drone navigation technology without GPS
Sheiko's main innovation involves an autonomous guidance system that allows drones to reach designated destinations without relying on conventional satellite positioning signals.
The technology is designed to help unmanned aircraft maintain their intended flight paths when GPS and other global navigation services become unavailable.
According to information released by Poltava's municipal education department, the student has been developing engineering solutions for unmanned aerial vehicles.
His navigation system enables an aircraft to independently approach a location selected by its operator while flying relatively close to the ground.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
This capability addresses a major difficulty facing drone operators when electronic interference disrupts satellite navigation signals during flight.
GPS jamming and spoofing can interfere with conventional navigation equipment, potentially preventing aircraft from maintaining accurate positioning.
Sheiko's work also includes optical-electronic stabilization equipment incorporating artificial intelligence for improved drone control and navigation.
Such equipment can help maintain stable observations and support guidance when conventional satellite-based positioning becomes unreliable.
However, there is no information on the precise sensors, algorithms, or computational hardware powering his navigation system.
Details about its operational testing, navigation accuracy, maximum range, and performance under different environmental conditions have also not been disclosed.
Without further technical details, it remains difficult to determine how his invention compares with existing GPS-independent navigation systems.
Nevertheless, receiving national recognition while still attending secondary school is a major achievement for the young Ukrainian engineer.
Presidential award follows several international science competition victories
The "The Future of Ukraine" distinction adds another achievement to Sheiko's growing record of recognition in engineering and scientific competitions.
He has previously received presidential scholarships on two occasions, recognizing his performance and contributions to scientific research.
The student has also secured first place twice in nationwide competitions organized by Ukraine's Junior Academy of Sciences.
His entries competed within the aerospace and defense technology category, focusing on engineering developments relevant to unmanned systems.
International competitions have also featured his inventions, including the INOVA 2025 International Inventions Show, where he secured a gold medal.
He additionally received a silver medal in the 2025 Hackathon, adding another international achievement to his academic record.
His latest presidential award recognizes his contributions to drone engineering, particularly developments involving autonomous navigation and electronic stabilization.
Ukraine's continuing efforts to maintain drone operations despite electronic interference have also encouraged interest in alternative communication technologies.
The country has been exploring alternatives to Starlink for maintaining drone communications when satellite connectivity becomes unavailable during military operations.
It recently reportedly combined airborne relay systems with Israeli-Italian satellite communications technology to provide alternative links for unmanned aircraft.
While these systems maintain communication with operators, Sheiko's invention addresses another challenge by allowing drones to navigate without GPS signals.
Via Poltavawave (originally in Ukrainian)

Efosa has been writing about technology for over 7 years, initially driven by curiosity but now fueled by a strong passion for the field. He holds both a Master's and a PhD in sciences, which provided him with a solid foundation in analytical thinking.

articles.title: China's memory giants have a record year as Huawei ships HBM without a named source
articles.text:
The state of China's memory industry in 2026 — CXMT and YMTC are booming, but HBM remains a headache
A record year for Chinese memory, while Huawei ships its own HBM without a named source.
China’s homegrown memory comes largely from two companies, CXMT for DRAM and YMTC for 3D NAND, and both are booming. CXMT’s Oct. 30 quarterly report shows a nine-month net profit of ¥132.0 billion ($19.6 billion), against a ¥5.28 billion ($785 million) loss a year earlier, on revenue more than eight times as high, at ¥269.0 billion ($40.0 billion). YMTC’s numbers, just for Q1, are at ¥47.04 billion ($7.0 billion) in revenue and ¥33.38 billion ($5.0 billion) in profit attributable to shareholders, more than double 2025.
Both are expanding and adding fabs, and each is edging into the other’s products. No Chinese manufacturer can yet produce high-bandwidth memory (HBM) in volume, though. HBM is the stacked DRAM that AI accelerators depend on, and currently the U.S. bars Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron from selling it into China. CXMT’s prospectus lists no HBM project, though its HBM3E is reportedly in risk production, an early run before the process is fully qualified. Huawei designs its own HBM but doesn’t say who makes it.
Memory is a commodity, so the story is in the wafers. We cover the companies running memory fabs in China: CXMT, YMTC, a handful of smaller Chinese fabs, and Samsung and SK hynix, which run some of their biggest plants there. Huawei makes the cut for its HBM program, though it has no memory fab. Fabless designers, module makers, and NOR flash producers are left out, except XMC for its HBM line. Fab counts, products, and financials come from filings and company statements; capacities, planned fabs, and the HBM progress that remains the big question mark rest largely on anonymous reporting. Let's dive into the current state of the Chinese DRAM industry.
CXMT: three DRAM fabs running, three more on the way
CXMT, short for ChangXin Memory Technologies, is China’s biggest homegrown DRAM maker. It operates two 12-inch fabs in Hefei and one in Beijing, each able to produce around 100,000 wafers a month. It is also building fabs in Shanghai and Hefei and is in funding talks for a second Beijing fab, which together could take it past 600,000 wafers a month. The Shanghai fab is expected to have two to three times the capacity of the Hefei base, with tools going in during the second half of 2026 and volume in 2027.
CXMT is now the fourth-largest DRAM maker worldwide, with 9.5% of DRAM revenue in Q2, according to TrendForce. CXMT says LPDDR6 is in mass production for Xiaomi, and its president says the first 4F² product, a server DDR5 RDIMM, is due by year-end. This comes after record first-half revenue of ¥150.3 billion ($22.4 billion), net profit of ¥77.6 billion ($11.5 billion), an 84.84% gross margin on its main business, and a listing on Shanghai’s STAR Market on July 27. Third-quarter profit alone was ¥54.4 billion ($8.1 billion).
The primary products are DDR5 rated up to 8,000 MT/s with 24Gb dies, and LPDDR5X rated up to 10,667 MT/s. CXMT says its fifth-generation G5 platform reaches 11.95nm active-area half-pitch with quadruple patterning for 24Gb LPDDR5X, and gets at least 50% more dies out of each wafer than G4, counted as 8Gb dies. CXMT says a DRAM product on its sixth-generation platform has also completed engineering-sample validation. Jeongdong Choe, Senior Technology Fellow at TechInsights, told Tom’s Hardware Premium that the firm measured the smallest active half-pitch on CXMT’s G4 at 14.8nm and hasn’t analyzed G5 yet.
CXMT lists no GDDR or 3D NAND among its products and is limited to nodes made without extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography as it lacks the tooling. CXMT’s second Beijing fab, however, is planned to include a 3D NAND R&D line, which could shake things up. The growth picture for now is capacity and price, with the tests of scaling without EUV lying with the RDIMM and Shanghai fab.
YMTC: going all out on NAND, DRAM in testing
YMTC, short for Yangtze Memory Technologies Co., has two fabs of its own in Wuhan, which can produce about 200,000 wafers a month together. A third fab in the Xinzhou district, registered in September last year, is expected to produce about 50,000 wafers a month by 2027 and eventually 100,000 at full capacity. While YMTC is known for its NAND flash, roughly half of Fab 3’s output is earmarked for DRAM. The company also makes enterprise SSDs and UFS and eMMC parts, and sells consumer SSDs under its ZhiTai brand. YMTC filed its own STAR Market prospectus, to match CXMT’s, on Aug. 21.
NAND flash was, until recently, the star of the show for Chinese memory, and YMTC’s Xtacking technology is one reason why. Its fifth-generation Xtacking 4.0 die, used in 1Tb TLC and 2Tb QLC parts, has 294 gates, and Choe told us 267 of them are active word lines. Most of what YMTC ships, however, is still 160- and 232-layer NAND. Samsung licensed YMTC’s Xtacking bonding patents in February 2025, so the technology could be considered both proven and valuable.
Omdia data put YMTC at 38.5% of China’s NAND market in Q2, ahead of Samsung’s 33.5%. Globally, YMTC ranked third in NAND shipments in Q2, according to Counterpoint Research, and its share of NAND revenue rose from 9% to 14% between Q1 2025 and Q1 2026. YMTC’s stated long-term targets are about 20% of global NAND supply and about 500,000 wafers a month, DRAM included.
For DRAM, YMTC’s Fab 2 is running about 5,000 wafers a month of 16Gb LPDDR5, still in R&D and testing, with no plan for mass production. However, a 9,600 MT/s part on a vertical channel transistor (VCT) 4F² cell is slated for mass production at Fab 3 if it passes qualification. XMC, YMTC’s former foundry unit, left its control in July.
The smaller fabs: Jinhua’s DDR4 and SwaySure’s unfinished line
Two smaller fabs worthy of note are Fujian Jinhua and SwaySure. The former has a 12-inch fab in Jinjiang, which produces custom DDR4 on 25nm, at 40,000–50,000 wafers a month, with about 90% going to Huawei. DDR4 prices have surged this year, by as much as 50% in the first quarter alone, as the big suppliers wind DDR4 down in favor of server and HBM parts and enterprise buyers stock up.
SwaySure, a Shenzhen company founded in March 2022 with state-owned investment, is building a 28nm 12-inch DRAM line and is reportedly backed by Huawei. Analyst Jim Handy of Objective Analysis doubts the 28nm line could make HBM. Neither company responded to our requests for additional information.
| China’s memory fabs: what each makes, and what it doesn’t |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Company | Fab (location) | Makes | Notably doesn’t make | Status | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CXMT | Hefei Phase 1 and Phase 2 (Anhui); Beijing (Yizhuang) | DRAM | GDDR, 3D NAND, HBM in volume | Producing; about 100,000 wafers a month each | 
| CXMT | Shanghai DRAM fab | DRAM for servers, PCs, and cars, plus HBM lines | — | Under construction; volume in 2027 | 
| CXMT | Shanghai HBM packaging plant | HBM stacking and packaging | — | Under construction; due by the end of 2026 | 
| CXMT | New Hefei fab; second Beijing fab | DRAM; NAND R&D line planned for Beijing | — | Hefei under construction; Beijing in funding talks | 
| YMTC | Wuhan Fab 1 and Fab 2 (Hubei) | 3D NAND, TLC and QLC, on Xtacking | DRAM in volume, HBM | Producing; about 200,000 wafers a month combined | 
| YMTC | Wuhan Fab 3 | 3D NAND; DRAM planned (9,600 MT/s LPDDR5 on a VCT 4F² cell) | — | Equipping; starts late 2026 or 2027; about 50,000 wafers a month by 2027 | 
| YMTC | Two more fabs, sites not reported | 3D NAND and some DRAM | — | Planned; 100,000 wafers a month each | 
| XMC | Wuhan, two 12-inch fabs and a reported HBM line | Specialty foundry: NOR flash, MCUs, 3D integration | HBM (a 3,000-wafer-a-month line under construction since February 2024) | Operating; out of YMTC’s control since July 2026 | 
| Fujian Jinhua (JHICC) | Jinjiang (Fujian) | Custom DDR4 on 25nm | DDR5; HBM unproven | Producing; 40,000 to 50,000 wafers a month | 
| SwaySure | Shenzhen (Guangdong) | DRAM on a 28nm line, planned | — | Under construction | 
HBM: who’s chasing, and who isn’t
Not every AI chip needs HBM. Inference hardware can get by on LPDDR5X, as Axera’s AX8860P does in Sipeed’s MaixStation, or on DRAM bonded straight onto the processor, the approach PieceMakers is betting on. Training-class accelerators like Huawei’s Ascend series still need HBM, though, and since the U.S. banned the export of HBM as of Dec. 2, 2024, China can’t buy it from the big three memory makers.
Even those who can get HBM are seeing heat and yield issues with larger memory stacks, specifically 12-high. SK hynix said on its Q3 2026 earnings call that some customers’ spec changes show “demand is indeed overwhelming supply,” and that lowering the stack is “a strategy to increase the number of cubes that can be obtained for the same capacity.” This mirrors other indicators, including potential Nvidia Rubin Ultra decisions, and it suggests that HBM is in short enough supply that even easier-to-build stacks are in high demand.
CXMT has sampled HBM with Tongfu, and HBM3 built on its 16nm-class G4 node to Huawei. Its HBM3E has now gone to several domestic AI chip designers as samples, with limited production due by the end of 2026, and an expansion expected in 2027. Yields are only about 20% to 30%, though, against about 70% at SK hynix, and in testing the chips performed closer to SK hynix’s HBM3 than to its HBM3E. An HBM packaging plant in Shanghai worth at least ¥17.1 billion ($2.5 billion) is targeted for year-end, with capacity for about 30,000 units a month.
Tongfu reportedly sampled HBM2, but its own filings mention only DRAM and flash packaging. Huawei said last year that “we will offer two proprietary HBMs.” It launched the Atlas 350 card in March, built on the Ascend 950PR, which carries 112GB of HBM. XMC has had a 3,000-wafer-a-month HBM line under construction since early 2024, but no production has been confirmed. At this time, YMTC, Jinhua, and SwaySure don’t appear to make HBM, though reports say YMTC is developing the through-silicon via (TSV) stacking it would need, and Jinhua was named in a Huawei-led HBM group in 2024.
Huawei said in 2025 that the 950PR would use HiBL 1.0, its own “low-cost HBM”; TechInsights told us it hasn’t analyzed HiBL 1.0 yet. However, Huawei’s 2025 roadmap specced out the 950PR's 128GB of HBM at 1.6TB/s. Huawei said that its 950PR is “optimized for the prefill stage of inference,” which is compute-heavy with “lower demand for memory access bandwidth,” and that using HiBL 1.0 is “more cost-effective than HBM3E and HBM4E” for that workload. The higher-end HiZQ 2.0, for the 950DT, is due in Q4 and, by Huawei’s figures, brings 144GB at 4TB/s. In both cases, Huawei’s supplier remains in doubt, and the company did not respond to our requests for comment.
| Who is chasing HBM in China |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Company | HBM effort | Stage | 
|---|---|---|
| CXMT | HBM3 and HBM3E DRAM | HBM3 samples to Huawei; HBM3E sampling, with limited production by year-end at 20–30% yields | 
| CXMT | Shanghai HBM packaging plant | Under construction; due by the end of 2026 | 
| Huawei | HiBL 1.0, in the Ascend 950PR | Shipping since March 2026 in the Atlas 350 (112GB); maker not disclosed | 
| Huawei | HiZQ 2.0, in the Ascend 950DT (144GB at 4TB/s) | Due in Q4 2026; maker not disclosed | 
| XMC | HBM packaging line, 3,000 wafers a month | Under construction since February 2024; production not confirmed | 
| Tongfu Microelectronics | HBM packaging | HBM samples with CXMT and HBM2 samples reported; filings show only DRAM and flash packaging | 
| YMTC | None in production | TSV stacking in development | 
| Fujian Jinhua | Named in a Huawei-led HBM group in 2024 | Unproven | 
| SwaySure | None known | Doubtful on a 28nm line (analyst Jim Handy) | 
| Samsung, SK hynix, Micron | Can’t sell HBM into China | Barred by the U.S. rule of Dec. 2, 2024 | 
The foreign fabs, and the restrictive rules
Of the companies from outside China, Samsung and SK hynix both run large memory fabs on Chinese soil, and both are now upgrading their NAND lines there. Samsung’s Xi’an handles about 40% of the company’s NAND, including 236-layer, or V8, in volume, with X2 converting to 286-layer, or V9, this year, slated to reach 5,000 V9 wafers a month in December and 40,000 by December 2027. A Samsung spokesperson told Tom’s Hardware Premium that the company “has been transitioning its existing manufacturing operations in Xi’an to 9th-generation V-NAND in compliance with U.S. export regulations and in close communication with the U.S. government.”
SK hynix’s Wuxi produces 30–40% of its DRAM and has moved from 1z to 1a, with the EUV layers done in Korea. Dalian turns out about 100,000 wafers a month of 192-layer floating-gate NAND and is moving to 240 layers, the most SK hynix is authorized to make there.
SK hynix, which already sells NAND with up to 321 layers elsewhere, told us it needs a U.S. license every year and declined to give product details or capacities for individual fabs. The company said that it intends for its 321-layer flash to be “over 50% of domestic (Korean) capacity in the fourth quarter,” which puts the Dalian lag into relief.
SK hynix also has “Mod B,” a second fab at its Dalian site that was completed in 2023. The company has reportedly tied a new U.S. NAND fab to Washington, letting it ship more U.S. tools there: Dalian’s 2026 license capped its equipment, no 2027 license had been issued as of mid-October, and its U.S.-based Solidigm unit has applied for an export license to buy more tools for Mod B. SK hynix told Tom’s Hardware that “no capacity expansion is being sought for the Dalian Mod B” and has been installing equipment at its Dalian factory.
Solidigm is now reportedly in talks with the U.S. Commerce Department over a $45 billion chip plant in the U.S., but wants Washington’s approval to ship equipment to upgrade the Dalian plant first, arguing that the upgrade would help finance the new site. However, SK hynix denied an earlier report of such a deal and says no specific plans have been finalized.
As for its Chongqing packaging plant, SK hynix told us it is “exploring various strategic options to enhance our packaging competitiveness,” though nothing is final. Elsewhere in China, Samsung’s Suzhou plant handles assembly and testing, and Micron’s Xi’an site handles packaging and testing.
All of this plays out inside a U.S.-China fight over chips that AI has only sped up. CXMT isn’t currently on the Commerce Department’s Entity List, which bars U.S. suppliers from shipping to listed companies without a license; YMTC, Jinhua, and SwaySure are. Jinhua has been on the list since 2018; SwaySure joined in December 2024 over its Huawei links, and YMTC was added in December 2022.
CXMT is, however, on the Pentagon’s 1260H list of Chinese military companies, which it is suing over. It’s been on the list since January 2025 and stayed on with the June update. For Samsung and SK hynix, the validated end-user status that let both firms ship in U.S. tools was revoked as of Dec. 31, 2025. Annual licenses are now required, and the Commerce Department has said it doesn’t intend to license capacity expansions or technology upgrades. Meanwhile, both companies say upgrades are under way, which sits uneasily with that policy.
China, for its part, has been weighing broader technology export controls and has now proposed adding 40 technologies, reportedly including some memory-chip design technologies, to its Catalogue of Technologies Prohibited and Restricted from Export. The draft, Announcement 48 from China’s Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology, is open for comment until Nov. 15, and anyone exporting a listed technology must register first.
| Foreign-owned memory fabs in China |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Owner | Fab (location) | Makes | Share of owner’s output | Status | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Samsung | Xi’an X1 (Shaanxi) | 3D NAND: 236-layer V8; V6 ended | About 40% of Samsung’s NAND (both Xi’an fabs) | Producing | 
| Samsung | Xi’an X2 (Shaanxi) | 3D NAND, converting to 286-layer V9 | In the Xi’an figure | Converting to V9; 5,000 V9 wafers a month in December 2026, 40,000 by December 2027 | 
| SK hynix | Wuxi (Jiangsu) | DRAM, mostly 1a; EUV layers done in Korea | 30% to 40% of SK hynix’s DRAM | Producing | 
| SK hynix (Solidigm) | Dalian Fab 1 (Liaoning) | Floating-gate 3D NAND, 192-layer, moving to 240 | About 100,000 wafers a month; 30% to 40% of SK hynix’s NAND | Producing; upgrading, authorized up to 240 layers | 
| SK hynix (Solidigm) | Dalian Mod B (Liaoning) | 3D NAND, if equipped | Not stated | Built in 2023; SK hynix says no expansion is sought; no 2027 license yet | 
Currently, China’s homegrown memory hinges on two manufacturers that are, admittedly, booming at the moment, although the memory industry worldwide has seen a massive surge since spring 2025. SK hynix said that “our DRAM and HBM volume for the next three years through 2029 are effectively sold out” with supply failing to keep up with demand as “a constraint projected to continue through 2030.” Its average selling prices rose from Q2 by mid-20% for NAND and high-20% for DRAM.
There may be some signs of at least temporary cooling in China’s consumer channel, though, as China Flash Market reports that SSD prices fell across the board this week, with most spot NAND wafers trading more than 30% below suppliers’ official prices. It looks like supply will remain a hot topic and China’s production capabilities are front and center.
CXMT and Huawei both have HBM milestones due by year-end: CXMT’s limited HBM3E production and Shanghai packaging plant, and Huawei’s 950DT with HiZQ 2.0. YMTC’s Fab 3 is due in late 2026 or 2027, and CXMT’s HBM3E expansion is expected in 2027. That leaves little time to ramp within 2027, especially at CXMT’s current yields, so we’re skeptical of volume HBM from a Chinese fab, whether measured against domestic demand or global supply, before 2028. Samsung and SK hynix, meanwhile, still need U.S. licenses for next year to keep tooling their Chinese fabs.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: Huawei reconnu coupable aux États-Unis de vol de secrets commerciaux et de trafic avec l'Iran
articles.text:
Le géant chinois arrive au bout d'une procédure judiciaire de huit ans aux États-Unis. Et elle le reconnaît coupable de plusieurs méfaits.
Cela peut sembler dater, mais il faut se souvenir que les actions des États-Unis contre Huawei ont commencé en janvier 2019. À l'époque, une instruction judiciaire était lancée par le département de la Justice des États-Unis contre le géant des télécommunications chinois. Le procès ne s'était finalement ouvert qu'au mois de septembre 2026, et après trois mois, ainsi que l'audition de près de 60 témoins pour l'accusation, le verdict est enfin tombé !
Huawei reconnu coupable de 10 des 12 chefs d'accusation
Huawei était poursuivi pour 12 chefs d'accusation devant un tribunal de New York. Il a finalement été reconnu coupable pour 10 d'entre eux, avec le plus grave - celui d'association de malfaiteurs en vue de détournement de propriété intellectuel - finalement écarté.
Le géant chinois est ainsi dorénavant officiellement coupable aux yeux de la justice américaine de vols de secrets industriels. Parmi les entreprises ciblées (américaines et internationales) sont citées T-Mobile, Cisco Systems, Quintel, CNEX et Fujitsu.
L'entreprise reconnue comme un vrai danger pour la sécurité nationale américaine
Les autres chefs d'accusation portent notamment sur des faits de fraude électronique, de fraude bancaire ainsi que de contournement des sanctions américaines contre l'Iran. Huawei est ainsi coupable d'avoir trompé les banques sur ses activités avec l'Iran. « Huawei a menti aux banques au sujet de ses activités en Iran afin d'obtenir des milliards de dollars américains et d'accéder à des services de compensation en dollars américains » note le département de la Justice.
Le groupe chinois aurait travaillé avec les renseignements iraniens, aidé à la censure du web local, et fourni des caméras de surveillance pour surveiller les protestations. Ses activités étaient regroupées dans une filiale du nom de « Skycom », présentée par Huawei comme un simple partenaire commercial - ce qui lui permettait d'affirmer à Washington avoir cessé officiellement de travailler avec l'Iran depuis 2011.
« Peu de crimes sont aussi graves que la pratique, mise en œuvre depuis des décennies par Huawei, qui consiste à mettre en danger la sécurité nationale des États-Unis, à porter atteinte à l'intégrité du commerce américain et à entraver l'application des lois américaines » a résumé le procureur fédéral Joseph Nocella. Du côté de Huawei, on parle déjà de faire appel, alors que Pékin accuse Washington de manoeuvre inéquitable pour faire mal à un fleuron chinois.
Source : US department of Justice

articles.title: Moritz Schularick, economista alemán: "Deberíamos vender Volkswagen a los chinos mientras consigamos algo"
articles.text:
Sin medias tintas. Moritz Schularick, presidente del Instituto de Economía Mundial de Kiel (centro de investigación y asesoramiento económico con gran renombre en Alemania) apuesta por vender "cierta marca de Wolfsburgo" a China. Las declaraciones las ha pronunciado en la conferencia industrial del Ministerio Federal de Economía, la Asociación Federal de la Industria Alemana (BDI) e IG Metall en Berlín.
¿Qué ha pasado? Moritz Schularick ha hablado. Lo ha hecho en uno de los eventos económicos más importantes del año en Alemania. Y lo que ha dicho no es una cuestión menor. "Si vendiéramos cierto grupo de Wolfsburgo a los chinos mientras consigamos algo para ellos, no es una mala idea", ha sentenciado según recoge el diario alemán Handelsblatt.
Según este diario, Schularick ha apostado por deshacerse de la parte industrial de Volkswagen (ese "cierto grupo de Wolfsburgo") porque en su opinión el valor de la compañía no está exactamente en la producción de los coches. En su lugar, deberíamos apostar por el desarrollo de los vehículos.
¿Quién es? Moritz Schularick es uno de los economistas más influyentes en Europa de los últimos años. Desde 2023 preside uno de los centros de asesoramiento económico más importantes de Alemania pero, además, en 2025 fue nombrado asesor externo en materia de industria de defensa por parte del propio Gobierno germano.
Sus investigaciones se han basado en entender la economía a muy largo plazo, intentando encontrar los patrones que han desembocado en crisis financieras a lo largo de las décadas. Uno de esos patrones es, según Schularick el aumento del crédito privado, lo que le llevó a adelantar la crisis del 2008. Sin embargo, sus críticos se han mostrado contrarios a sus teorías más radicales como la de que Alemania podía cortar le flujo de gas ruso de inmediato tras la invasión de Ucrania.
"Secundario". Es lo que opina Schularick sobre quién debe producir los automóviles. Y es que, según el economista alemán, el valor añadido de la industria no está en quién produce esos coches, por eso no vería con mala idea vender Volkswagen a China. Lo importante es que "la creación de valor y la producción se queden aquí", asegura.
Esa idea es una fórmula clásica de entender la economía. La teoría de la Smiling Curve (Curva de la sonrisa) asegura que el verdadero valor del producto está en el desarrollo del mismo y el trabajo de distribución y marketing. Al contrario, la fase productiva es la que menor valor y dinero aporta. Simplificando, es el famoso Design in California, made in China de Apple.
Made in Europe. La otra gran apuesta de Schularick es la misma por la que llevan apostando algunos otros expertos de la industria del automóvil y que defienden en países como Francia: si China quiere vender en Europa, tendrá que asociarse. Bien fabricando en suelo europeo o bien llegando a acuerdos con los fabricantes europeos para crear valor.
Francia ha defendido esta posición para crear categorías como el eCar, un coche fabricado en Europa con materiales europeos que pueda venderse con fondos de la Unión Europea para hacerlos más asequibles. Dichos fondos sólo llegarían a las compañías que fabriquen en nuestro suelo creando tejido industrial. Es decir, no sería suficiente con ensamblar kits como hace Chery en Barcelona.
¿Quién debe aprender de quién? Cuando Schularick defiende que se deben poner algunas barreras a la venta de coches chinos porque ellos mismos obligaron a los fabricantes tradicionales a asociarse con marcas locales en su mercado está en lo cierto.
Pero la gran duda es quién debe aprender ahora de quién y quién tiene de verdad el conocimiento y el valor del desarrollo. BMW o Mercedes han demostrado con sus últimos productos que pueden hacer buenos coches eléctricos con sus propios conocimientos pero empresas como Renault están apostando por aprender de China. También Volkswagen se ha asociado con empresas chinas para traerse conocimientos a sus coches europeos. Leapmotor será la base de los coches baratos de Stellantis.
¿Tiene los fabricantes europeos una verdadera posición de fuerza?
