articles.title: Cómo activar en Android los ajustes que bloquean el celular si un ladrón te lo arrebata
articles.text:
Google explica en su página de ayuda oficial de Android cómo activar la Protección contra robo, un conjunto de ajustes que bloquea la pantalla del celular si alguien lo arrebata, si el dispositivo queda sin internet o si el código se ingresa mal varias veces. Se activan desde Configuración, en pocos toques.
Las funciones forman parte del menú Protección contra robo, que Google ubica dentro de su sección de seguridad. Algunos pasos solo funcionan en Android 10 o versiones posteriores, y otros exigen Android 15. Tampoco están disponibles en dispositivos Android Go, tabletas ni relojes, y el soporte puede variar según el modelo.
Para empezar, el teléfono debe tener un bloqueo de pantalla configurado. Después: abrir Configuración, tocar Google, luego Todos los servicios y, en el apartado “Personal y seguridad del dispositivo”, entrar en Protección contra robo. Desde ahí se enciende cada función por separado. Google aclara que algunas ya vienen activadas de fábrica y remite a la guía de cada fabricante. Si una opción aparece en gris, el aparato no la admite.
Tres bloqueos automáticos de la pantalla
El primero es el Bloqueo por detección de robo. Según Google, usa inteligencia artificial, los sensores de movimiento del teléfono, el Wi-Fi y el Bluetooth para detectar que alguien se lo quitó de la mano y huye corriendo, en bicicleta o en un vehículo. En ese caso, la pantalla se bloquea sola. La función no actúa con la pantalla ya bloqueada y tampoco se dispara si el teléfono tiene una conexión estable de Wi-Fi o Bluetooth, o si hubo varios bloqueos seguidos en poco tiempo.
El segundo es el Bloqueo sin conexión. Si un ladrón apaga el internet para impedir que el dueño localice el aparato con Find Hub —la herramienta de Google para ubicar dispositivos—, la pantalla se bloquea tras un breve período de uso sin conexión. El teléfono debe estar desbloqueado cuando pierde la conectividad, y la pantalla puede bloquearse dos veces cada 24 horas.
El tercero, el Bloqueo por autenticación fallida, cierra la pantalla cuando se ingresa mal el código varias veces seguidas. Junto con la protección de ajustes sensibles, viene activado por defecto cuando hay un bloqueo de pantalla configurado.
Bloqueo remoto y verificación de identidad
El Bloqueo remoto permite trabar la pantalla de un teléfono perdido solo con un número de teléfono verificado. Requiere bloqueo de pantalla, una tarjeta SIM activa, Find Hub encendido y conexión a internet. Si el aparato está sin conexión, se bloquea cuando vuelva a conectarse. También puede usarse dos veces cada 24 horas.
Para activarlo, el camino es el mismo menú: Protección contra robo, Bloqueo remoto y activar la opción. Si el número no está verificado, hay que tocar Verificar número o activar la verificación automática. Con el teléfono ya perdido, se ingresa a android.com/lock desde otro dispositivo, se escribe el número, se resuelve un reCAPTCHA y se solicita el bloqueo.
Google ofrece además una pregunta de seguridad opcional, que se define en el mismo apartado tras verificar la identidad con PIN o datos biométricos. Quien la configura debe responderla en android.com/lock para que el bloqueo se concrete; una respuesta incorrecta lo hace fallar. Para borrar o asegurar el aparato a distancia hay que iniciar sesión en Find Hub.
La Verificación de identidad es la capa más estricta y solo aparece en ciertos dispositivos. Fuera de los lugares de confianza que el usuario define —como casa o trabajo—, exige huella o rostro y no admite PIN, patrón ni contraseña. Se activa en el mismo menú, con una cuenta de Google, bloqueo de pantalla, datos biométricos y lugares de confianza configurados.
Con esa verificación activa, hacen falta datos biométricos para ver contraseñas y llaves de acceso guardadas en el Administrador de contraseñas de Google, cambiar el bloqueo de pantalla, restablecer el teléfono de fábrica, apagar Find Hub o desactivar la propia función. También para cambiar la contraseña de la cuenta de Google o sus factores de recuperación.
Otros pasos que recomienda Google
La página aconseja un PIN de seis o más dígitos, aun si se usa huella o rostro, y activar la copia de seguridad para poder restablecer un teléfono robado sin perder datos. Find Hub debe estar encendido antes del robo: se activa solo al añadir una cuenta de Google. Desde allí se puede ubicar, bloquear o borrar el aparato.
Google recomienda también anotar el número IMEI —el código único del teléfono—, porque la operadora puede usarlo para ubicarlo o suspender el servicio, y las autoridades pueden pedirlo al denunciar el robo. En Configuración se consulta, según el modelo. Las instrucciones corresponden a la página de ayuda de Android consultada el 25 de noviembre de 2026.

articles.title: AI infrastructure stocks continue their slide, but Anthropic closes higher
articles.text:
AI infrastructure stocks continue their slide, but Anthropic closes higher
Investors continued to offload artificial intelligence infrastructure stocks today, but Anthropic PBC recouped some of its losses from earlier this week.
The AI selloff reportedly began in August. It accelerated on Nov. 17, the day Nvidia Corp. CEO Jensen Huang resigned over his affair with a former executive of Megaspeed, a cloud provider under investigation over alleged export control violations. Huang returned to the helm of the chipmaker Monday.
Nvidia closed at $173.73 the day before Huang’s resignation. It dropped as low as $125 during the executive’s two-week hiatus and surged 30% on Monday, the day he returned. Nvidia lost some of its recent gains in today’s trading session: Its share price closed 3.8% lower.
Other AI chip stocks have also taken a hit. Broadcom Inc. closed a small fraction of a percent lower than yesterday, while Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Intel Corp. fell 1.6% and 0.6%, respectively.
The semiconductor stock that logged the biggest drop today is Ambarella Inc., a relatively low-profile maker of AI image analysis chips. Its accelerators are used by edge devices to process footage from their cameras. Ambarella dropped 19.8% today after closing 19% lower yesterday.
The stock’s decline was driven not so much by the broader AI selloff, but rather the weak earnings that Ambarella posted on Tuesday. The company missed expectations across the board. Ambarella said that some customers had canceled or delayed orders to mitigate the financial impact of soaring memory prices.
Micron Inc., one of the world’s top memory chip suppliers, saw its market capitalization drop more than 4.5% today. That’s despite CEO Sanjay Mehrotra’s recent disclosure that the company has already sold out 75% of its 2027 manufacturing capacity. According to the executive, the gap between memory demand and supply is only set to increase next year.
Companies downstream from chipmakers in the AI data center supply chain fared better. Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. ended the trading session 1.8% higher after dipping into the red earlier today, while Dell Technologies Inc. gained 0.64%.
In contrast, the major cloud providers weren’t left out of today’s selloff. Amazon.com Inc., the cloud market’s largest player, closed 3% lower. Microsoft Corp. and Google LLC dropped 1.25% and 2%, respectively. Oracle Corp., which trails the three companies in market share but has emerged as an important AI infrastructure provider, took the biggest hit: It’s down 5% from yesterday.
Anthropic ended the trading session with a 1% gain. The company thereby recouped some of yesterday’s losses, which pushed its stock below its $80 debut price. Anthropic went public last week through a record-setting offering that raised more than $93 billion.
Overall, the tech-heavy Nasdaq lost 0.6% while the S&P 500 slid 0.25%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.33%.

articles.title: Votre Chromecast avec Google TV s’offre une seconde jeunesse grâce à cette mise à jour
articles.text:
On pensait le Chromecast avec Google TV relégué aux oubliettes par le nouveau Google TV Streamer, mais Google ne semble pas encore avoir coupé le cordon. Onze mois après le dernier patch, le géant de Mountain View vient de déployer un nouveau firmware pour sa clé TV lancée il y a six ans déjà. Cette mise à jour vient prolonger la durée de l’appareil, toujours très populaire chez les amateurs de streaming.
Un correctif ciblé pour le streaming et la sécurité
La mise à jour déploie le patch de sécurité Android d’août 2026, remplaçant la version d’octobre 2025 installée l’an dernier. Google ne se contente pas de boucher les failles puisque la page officielle mentionne des améliorations sur la connectivité Wi-Fi, la stabilité du flux vidéo et le rendu de l’affichage. De nombreux bugs sont également balayés au passage, venant ainsi rendre la navigation plus fluide.
D’abord repéré sur le Chromecast avec Google TV (4K), le Chromecast avec Google TV (HD) reçoit aussi une mise à jour (voir ci-dessus). Si vous ne voulez pas attendre la notification de mise à jour, vous pouvez la lancer manuellement en vous rendant dans les paramètres du système, puis dans « À propos > Mise à jour du système ».
Le Chromecast avec Google TV toujours debout
Pour les plus bidouilleurs, ce correctif pourrait corriger la faille sabrina-unlock-v2 qui est utilisée par la communauté pour déverrouiller le bootloader et installer des systèmes alternatifs comme LineageOS. Cette vulnérabilité serait donc bloquée, même si Google n’a pas confirmé l’information officiellement. Les utilisateurs de ROMs personnalisées devront donc vérifier à deux fois avant de valider l’installation.
À lire : Le Chromecast avec Google TV gagne une des meilleures fonctionnalités de son successeur
Commercialisé en 2020 puis retiré du catalogue il y a deux ans, le Chromecast avec Google TV continue donc son chemin. Face à la hausse globale du prix des lecteurs multimédias, pouvoir conserver ce petit dongle reste donc une bonne affaire. Même si Google pousse désormais son nouveau TV Streamer, on ne refusera pas des mises à jour pour les anciens modèles.

articles.title: VPN familial : attention, tous vos appareils ne sont pas protégés de la même façon
articles.text:
Quel VPN choisir pour un foyer qui utilise Windows, Mac, Android et iPhone ?
Quel VPN pour Windows, Mac, Android et iPhone ? Comparez les fonctions par système, les connexions simultanées et le coût pour équiper votre foyer au mieux.
À la maison, le PC familial tourne sous Windows, un autre ordinateur est un Mac, les enfants utilisent Android et un parent possède un iPhone. Un seul abonnement VPN peut couvrir cet ensemble. Mais retrouver le même logo sur quatre écrans ne garantit pas les mêmes réglages. Les exclusions d’applications, les protections complémentaires et le nombre de connexions autorisées varient. Pour choisir un VPN Windows, Mac, Android et iPhone, il faut donc compter les appareils réellement connectés et identifier les fonctions indispensables sur chacun. Une offre illimitée résout le premier problème ; elle ne suffit pas à régler le second.
Compter les connexions du soir plutôt que les appareils du placard
Prenons un foyer de quatre personnes : deux PC Windows, un Mac, deux smartphones Android, deux iPhone et une tablette. Si les huit appareils utilisent le VPN en même temps, une limite de sept connexions impose de libérer une place. Avec dix, il reste deux connexions disponibles. Ajouter trois appareils actifs porte le besoin à onze et dépasse alors ce plafond. Ce scénario compare des capacités, sans prétendre reproduire les usages de toutes les familles.
NordVPN et Proton VPN Plus autorisent dix connexions simultanées. CyberGhost en accepte sept. ExpressVPN distingue Basique, Avancé et Pro, avec dix, douze et quatorze connexions. Surfshark Starter, One et One+ n’imposent pas de plafond numérique de connexions VPN simultanées, sous réserve des règles d’utilisation du service.
Le calcul porte sur les tunnels actifs, pas sur le nombre de membres du foyer. Un téléphone peut rester connecté au VPN pendant que son propriétaire travaille sur ordinateur. À l’inverse, installer une application sur une machine inutilisée ne suffit pas à compter une connexion supplémentaire. Chez CyberGhost, les appareils et places disponibles se gèrent également depuis le compte.
La compatibilité ne garantit pas les mêmes fonctions
Le split tunneling permet de laisser une application ou une destination hors du tunnel. C’est utile lorsqu’unservice de streaming refuse l’adresse IP du VPN ou lorsqu’un logiciel doit communiquer directement. Mais exclure une application entière, un domaine ou une adresse IP correspond à trois réglages différents. Une fonction présente sur iPhone peut ainsi être moins souple que son équivalent Windows.
| VPN | Windows | macOS | Android | iPhone | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NordVPN | Applications | Pas de split tunneling natif | Applications | Pas de split tunneling natif | 
| Proton VPN Plus | Applications et IP | Applications ; expérimental | Applications et IP | Pas de split tunneling natif | 
| CyberGhost | Exceptions de sites | Pas de split tunneling natif | Applications | Pas de split tunneling natif | 
| ExpressVPN | Applications et IP | Applications et IP sur app récente | Applications | Adresses IPv4 individuelles | 
| Surfshark | Applications et sites | Applications et sites ; hors Big Sur | Applications et sites | Sites uniquement | 
Ce tableau compare les possibilités d’exclusion du tunnel dans les applications, avec leurs principales restrictions. Les versions du système et de l’application restent déterminantes.
Une exclusion laisse la destination concernée hors du VPN et lui expose l’adresse IP habituelle. Elle ne supprime pas pour autant le chiffrement HTTPS du site. Il faut donc réserver ces exceptions aux besoins identifiés, puis vérifier le résultat sur chaque appareil.
Le kill switch répond à une autre question : que se passe-t-il si le tunnel tombe ? Il vise à empêcher la reprise du trafic protégé par une connexion directe. Son activation et ses interactions avec les exclusions doivent être vérifiées sur chaque appareil. Chez Proton, Android gère le VPN permanent et le blocage sans VPN dans les paramètres système.
Chez ExpressVPN sur iPhone, le split tunneling exige de quitter le mode de kill switch avancé pour le mode standard.
NordVPN convient aux foyers de dix connexions au maximum
NordVPN couvre notre foyer de huit appareils avec deux places de réserve. Son split tunneling sur Windows et Android permet de sortir une application du tunnel ; cette possibilité manque sur Mac et iPhone. Le service convient donc si les besoins d’exclusion concernent surtout les PC et téléphones Android. Si une application Mac récalcitrante constitue le problème principal, acheter une formule supérieure ne fera pas apparaître ce réglage.
Le supplément Premium mérite une lecture distincte. L’antivirus nouvelle génération concerne Windows et macOS ; les mobiles ne récupèrent pas l’analyse des fichiers de la version de bureau. Sur Mac, cette protection nécessite l’application distribuée directement par NordVPN plutôt que la version App Store. L’intérêt du pack dépend ainsi des ordinateurs à protéger, pas simplement du nombre de smartphones.
Proton VPN rapproche les fonctions mais conserve une réserve sur Mac
Proton VPN Plus associe dix connexions à NetShield et Secure Core sur les quatre systèmes. NetShield filtre des domaines liés aux publicités, traqueurs et malwares ; Secure Core ajoute un passage par un serveur intermédiaire. Ces fonctions offrent une continuité utile entre ordinateurs et mobiles, mais le filtrage DNS ne remplace pas une analyse antivirus des fichiers.
Le split tunneling fonctionne sur Windows et Android. Sur Mac, il reste expérimental, limité à certains protocoles et incompatible avec le fonctionnement attendu des applications WebKit, dont Safari. Sur iPhone, il est absent. Un foyer qui souhaite exclure précisément Safari sur Mac devrait donc privilégier une autre solution plutôt que considérer cette fonction comme acquise.
CyberGhost demande de vérifier le plafond avant le prix
Avec sept connexions, CyberGhost ne couvre pas les huit appareils de notre scénario lorsqu’ils sont tous actifs. Pour un foyer qui n’en connecte habituellement que cinq ou six, ce plafond peut rester suffisant. La différence entre un abonnement bien dimensionné et une contrainte quotidienne se joue ici à un seul appareil, même si les quatre systèmes disposent d’une application.
Sur Android, l’exclusion porte sur des applications. Sur Windows, les Smart Rules proposent notamment des exceptions pour des sites : lancer automatiquement le VPN à l’ouverture d’un logiciel n’équivaut pas à exclure ce logiciel du tunnel. Pour un foyer principalement Apple qui exige des exclusions fines, CyberGhost offre moins de souplesse. Son tarif initial ne doit donc être décisif qu’après validation de ces usages.
ExpressVPN fait varier la capacité avec le forfait
ExpressVPN Basique suffit à huit connexions ; Avancé devient pertinent à onze ou douze. Sur les applications récentes, Windows et Mac disposent du split tunneling, tandis que l’iPhone accepte des exclusions d’adresses IPv4 individuelles. Sur iOS, il est impossible de saisir directement une URL, un domaine ou une plage IP. Un grand service utilisant plusieurs adresses changeantes sera donc difficile à exclure proprement.
Ce détail fait basculer le choix : pour écarter facilement des sites sur iPhone, la saisie d’adresses IP peut demander trop d’entretien. Pour onze appareils actifs et des exclusions surtout sur ordinateur, Avancé répond en revanche à un besoin précis. Passer de Basique à Avancé ajoute deux connexions, sans rendre les exclusions iPhone identiques à celles d’un PC.
Surfshark supprime le plafond sans rendre les applications identiques
Surfshark absorbe les huit appareils du scénario, puis les trois supplémentaires, sans changement de forfait VPN. Bypasser exclut des applications ou des sites sur Windows, Android et les Mac compatibles. Big Sur reste exclu de cette fonction sur macOS. Sur iPhone, Bypasser se limite aux sites : il ne permet pas de sélectionner une application bancaire entière comme sur Android.
C’est une option convaincante pour un foyer très équipé, notamment si les exclusions sur iPhone concernent des sites. Starter et One partagent ici le même prix promotionnel, mais leurs renouvellements doivent être comparés séparément. L’antivirus de One fonctionne sur Windows, macOS et Android ; il ne transforme pas l’iPhone en appareil doté du même antivirus. L’illimité des connexions VPN ne vaut pas automatiquement pour les autres services.
Comparer le budget sur trente six mois
Pour huit connexions, le besoin impose d’abord une offre capable de les accueillir. Le tableau conserve les formules de base pour montrer aussi leurs limites. Les prix reprennent les montants affichés en France fin octobre 2026 : NordVPN, CyberGhost et ExpressVPN prévoient des taxes éventuelles ; Surfshark affiche ses prix hors taxes, si applicables. Aucune TVA calculée n’est ajoutée aux montants. Le total de commande reste à vérifier avant paiement.
| Offre | Prix mensuel et paiement initial | Durée initiale | Renouvellement | Pour couvrir 36 mois | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NordVPN Basique 10 connexions | 2,99 €/mois 80,73 € en une fois | 27 mois 24 + 3 offerts | 139,08 €/an | 219,81 € | 
| Proton VPN Plus 10 connexions | 2,49 €/mois 59,76 € en une fois | 24 mois | 83,88 €/an | 143,64 € | 
| CyberGhost 7 connexions | 1,99 €/mois 55,72 € en une fois | 28 mois 24 + 4 offerts | 55,72 €/an | 111,44 € 7 connexions seulement | 
| ExpressVPN Basique 10 connexions | 2,39 €/mois 66,92 € en une fois | 28 mois 24 + 4 offerts | 79,95 €/an | 146,87 € | 
| Surfshark Starter Illimitées | 2,49 €/mois 67,23 € en une fois | 27 mois 24 + 3 offerts | Montant contractuel à vérifier | 67,23 € + un renouvellement annuel | 
Calculs avec une utilisation continue et une reconduction au montant indiqué, sans nouvelle promotion. Les périodes annuelles sont payées intégralement : certains parcours laissent des mois disponibles après le trente-sixième mois. Pour Surfshark, le total à trente-six mois dépend du tarif annuel applicable au contrat, à relever avant paiement.
Chez ExpressVPN, Avancé demande 97,72 € pour vingt-huit mois, puis 109,95 € par an, soit 171,02 € pour couvrir trente-six mois. Le supplément atteint 50,80 € face à Basique sur cet horizon. Pour onze connexions actives, ces deux places supplémentaires répondent au besoin ; pour huit, elles restent inutilisées. Une IP dédiée constitue encore un autre achat : elle ne relève pas automatiquement le plafond et ne crée pas les fonctions absentes d’un système.
Choisir en fonction de l’appareil le plus contraignant
Pour huit appareils actifs, NordVPN et Proton VPN disposent de deux places de réserve ; CyberGhost oblige à réduire le nombre de tunnels. ExpressVPN Basique suffit aussi, mais son exclusion sur iPhone demande une gestion d’adresses IP. Surfshark facilite la croissance du parc et l’exclusion de sites sur iOS. Si exclure une application iPhone entière est indispensable, aucun réglage décrit ici ne répond à ce besoin comme sous Android.
Un routeur compatible peut regrouper les appareils du domicile derrière un seul tunnel : chez ExpressVPN, il compte pour une connexion. Mais cette organisation ne suit pas le smartphone en 4G ou en 5G et peut nécessiter un équipement supplémentaire. Le choix d’un VPN Windows, Mac, Android et iPhone doit donc partir des usages mobiles et des exceptions nécessaires, puis du budget VPN. C’est l’appareil le moins bien servi qui révèle les limites du forfait.

articles.title: Samsung and SK hynix to License YMTC's Xtacking Technology
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Samsung and SK hynix to License YMTC's Xtacking Technology
According to Nikkei Asia, South Korea's largest chipmakers are currently looking to license technology from China's YMTC. Specifically, SK hynix and Samsung are exploring ways to integrate YMTC's highly successful Xtacking silicon 3D NAND design. In the fourth iteration of Xtacking, YMTC can separate memory cell wafers from peripheral logic circuits and combine them using hybrid bonding wafer-to-wafer stacking. Hybrid bonding creates a permanent bond between two silicon chips using embedded metal bumps that are fused together to form a single chip. Multiple dies or entire silicon wafers can be connected by stacking the back ends of two chips together, and SK hynix and Samsung see this as a potential way to advance their 3D NAND production.
Since 2019, YMTC has been manufacturing using Xtacking technology, now on version 4.0. Samsung told Nikkei Asia that this bonding technology offers numerous advantages over the current approach to building many-layer NAND flash. SK hynix and Samsung are building NAND with hundreds of layers but are hitting single-wafer limitations. YMTC's technology has been refined and production-tested, making it easier for Samsung and SK hynix to switch to it. Additionally, YMTC has filed more than 4,000 patents related to 3D memory production, packaging, and more since 2018. For Samsung and SK hynix, it is much easier to license the technology from YMTC to avoid legal disputes instead of developing their own path.Even though Xtacking could be adopted by any memory maker at this point, the patent wall protects the technology, so if South Korean makers want to achieve something similar, they must carefully navigate the extensive data records in the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO). Hence, cross-licensing is much easier. Both companies declined to comment on Nikkei's request about this deal, but it seems to be holding for now. We don't know when we will first see Xtacking NAND from SK hynix and Samsung, but it could be just a year or two away.
Source:
				Nikkei Asia			
	
	
	
		
	
		
19 Comments on Samsung and SK hynix to License YMTC's Xtacking Technology
What is ironic? YMTC has developed & patented a tech Samsung & SK Hynix want to use, so they are doing the proper, legal thing and paying YMTC a license fee to use it. That is how things are supposed to work.
Oh idk the mass hysteria regarding the transfer of technology to Chinese companies perhaps
Politics.
YMTC allegedly used stolen IP (from Micron, if my memory serves me right) to develop their Xtacking tech, and for their alleged connections to Chinese military they were put into the US DOC's Entity List.
So yeah, having the "allied" Samsung and SK Hynix license tech from the YMTC you once fought is a bit ironic in my view. Just as much as Qualcomm licensing Huawei tech.
It's not hysteria if it's true. And it happened numerous times in the past decades in many-many industries.
Look no further than the story of Segway. It is owned today by the company infringed it's patents and mass-produced it's signature vehicles for cheaper, literally driving the creator to bekrupcy. Then they bought it up with all the patents they infringed upon...
I just think this whole farce needs to end. We need to work together, not against each other. This us vs. them thing is so tiresome. Imagine what we could do if it went away.
Wait until you find out almost all AI technology is based on Chinese whitepapers.
how exactly would that work?
there is a ton of R&D going on in each company, and that is a ton of $ being spent on it, so, you want all the companies to share R&D and each company pony up the $?and this is the problem going forward, if this is based on Micron's IP, then SK Hynix & Sammy should be paying Micron, not YMTC
It is pretty complicated though, engineers from Micron signed agreements, then they now work for YMTC, and they used some of Micron's IP (at least this is claimed), so... yes, this would be super ironic to pay YMTC for something that YMTC may not even own legally
Oh, so they also stole and subverted Microsoft's Embrace, Extend and Extinguish tactics? Or had the relevant patent already expired by then?
I think that spending tons of money for highly paid specialist ≠ tons of r&d work done. A person has the capacity to work and cannot exceed it. Just because he received really crazy amounts of money for his work, doesn't mean that this work is as quantitative as tons.
A single test run in silicon costs a bit of money and involves a load of very specialised professionals.
A base technology like x sczling will have taken quite a few runs to get to a point that it’s working and replicable at scale.
Microns licensing definetely costs leagues more and not even ready for production like YMTCs version.
I don't see a contradiction. If you try to misunderstand what I wrote, that's your right.
virus.hr/en/industry/micron-accuses-ymtc-of-stealing-3d-nand-technology
Kind of old business trick for centuries. That lawsuit can be useful for as self defense, also can be used for attacking competitors to waste their precious time and money no matter the results.

articles.title: ChatGPT ahora analiza la actividad física y salud en Android con esta función
articles.text:
OpenAI habilitó ChatGPT Health en la aplicación de ChatGPT para Android, con soporte para Health Connect, el servicio de Google que reúne datos de salud y actividad física del teléfono. La función llega de forma gradual y, por ahora, solo para usuarios elegibles de Estados Unidos mayores de 18 años.
Según OpenAI, Health está disponible para cuentas de ChatGPT Free, Go, Plus y Pro con sesión iniciada en ese país. Funciona en la web, en iOS, en Android y en la aplicación de escritorio.
Si no aparece en el menú lateral, la empresa recomienda actualizar la aplicación. La página oficial aclara que algunas cuentas todavía pueden no tenerla.
Los usuarios pueden hacer preguntas de salud sin conectar nada. Para obtener respuestas basadas en sus propios datos, pueden vincular Health Connect en Android o Apple Health en iPhone, además de historiales médicos de ciertos sistemas hospitalarios de Estados Unidos, One Medical y Function Health.
Cómo funciona ChatGPT Health en Android
El proceso empieza en la sección Health del menú lateral o en el menú Explorar. Allí el usuario elige Health Connect y marca las categorías de datos que autoriza, como sueño, actividad o entrenamientos. Puede agregar o quitar cuentas cuando quiera desde la pestaña de cuentas.
Con esa información, ChatGPT puede comparar resultados de análisis con estudios anteriores, resumir cambios desde la última consulta o explorar cómo se relacionan el sueño, la actividad y los entrenamientos con la rutina de la persona, según OpenAI.
Health Connect funciona como intermediario. Dataconomy precisó que quienes usan relojes Garmin o el anillo Oura deben comprobar que las aplicaciones de esos dispositivos compartan datos con Health Connect.
OpenAI advierte que ChatGPT solo ve lo que esas aplicaciones comparten y que algunas métricas propias, como una puntuación de sueño, pueden no aparecer o calcularse de otro modo.
OpenAI indica que ChatGPT no puede modificar los historiales que guarda un proveedor médico ni escribir información de vuelta en Apple Health o Health Connect.
Los cambios en condiciones actuales, medicamentos o antecedentes familiares solo afectan el perfil de Health dentro de ChatGPT.
La empresa describe el servicio como un apoyo y no un reemplazo de la atención médica, y señala que no está pensado para diagnosticar ni tratar. Para síntomas urgentes recomienda buscar ayuda profesional inmediata.
El medio agrega que las mediciones de los dispositivos de consumo pueden ser incompletas o inexactas.
Qué promete OpenAI en cuanto a privacidad
Según OpenAI, los datos sincronizados en Health, incluidos los de Health Connect, no se usan para entrenar sus modelos base ni para dirigir publicidad. La empresa afirma que los chats se cifran por defecto y que la información conectada en Health recibe protecciones adicionales.
Hay una salvedad en la misma página: el ajuste “Mejorar el modelo para todos” determina si las conversaciones que mencionan datos de Health, y el contenido derivado de ellos, pueden usarse para mejorar los modelos. Quien no lo desee debe desactivarlo en los controles de datos de la configuración.
Si la memoria de ChatGPT está activada, las conversaciones que usan Health pueden crear recuerdos para personalizar chats futuros, por ejemplo la meta de mejorar el sueño. OpenAI aclara que los recuerdos no se crean directamente a partir de los datos sincronizados, y ofrece proyectos con memoria propia o chats temporales para separarlos.
Al desconectar una cuenta, los datos sincronizados desde esa fuente se eliminan de los sistemas de OpenAI en un plazo de 30 días.
Lo que ya quedó incluido en las conversaciones se conserva hasta que el usuario borre esos chats.
La compañía precisa que Health no es apto para uso clínico ni ofrece un contrato de asociado comercial, el requisito de la ley estadounidense de privacidad médica (HIPAA) para proveedores y aseguradoras. Los padres pueden desactivar Health en las cuentas vinculadas de adolescentes, lo que elimina los datos sincronizados.
OpenAI no indicó fechas para otros países. La página de ayuda limita la disponibilidad a Estados Unidos y no menciona una ampliación.

articles.title: SSD prices spiked all year — I'd buy these 5 1TB Black Friday deals
articles.text:
SSD prices are soaring, so I picked 5 Black Friday NVMe deals actually worth buying from Samsung, Lexar, and Kingston
It's time to beat the component cost crisis
Finding a good deal on high-speed internal storage has become increasingly difficult amid the ongoing NAND and DRAM shortages. But with Black Friday here, I've found five 1TB SSDs from Samsung, Kingston, Lexar, and WD that buck the trend of rising prices.
Now, my personal favorite is the Samsung 990, currently $180 (was $230). With read speeds up to 7,150 and write speeds of 6,450 MB/s, it offers a solid balance of performance and power efficiency. For a faster drive, the Samsung 990 Pro is the better pick, but more expensive at $248 (was $320).
Alternatively, the Lexar NM790 is 50 cents cheaper than the Samsung, but was originally $250. It boasts read/write speeds of up to 7,400MB/s reads and 6,500MB/s writes. The WD_Black SN7100, currently $195 (was $210) at Newegg, delivers impressive sequential read speeds of up to 7,250MB/s and write speeds of up to 6,900MB/s. And the Kingston NV3 is cheaper than all of them at $140 (was $216), but it's also the slowest, reaching up to 6,000MB/s read and 4,000MB/s write speeds.
Today's best 1TB SSD deals
The 1TB Samsung 990 PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD delivers sequential read/write speeds of up to 7,150/6,450 MB/s, improved power efficiency, hardware encryption, TRIM support, and dedicated SSD management software tools.
Read moreRead less▼
A PCIe 4.0 x4 NVMe SSD in the M.2 2280 form factor with 1TB of storage and rated speeds up to 7,400MB/s read and 6,500MB/s write. It's rated for 1,000TB written and uses Host Memory Buffer 3.0 instead of onboard DRAM, which helps it use up to 40% less power than DRAM-equipped Gen 4 drives.
Read moreRead less▼
The 990 Pro is one of the fastest PCIe 4.0 SSDs around, with read/write speeds of up to 7,450/6,900 MB/s. But don't worry, there's no compromise on power consumption as the 990 Pro offers 50% better performance-per-Watt than the 980 PRO.
Read moreRead less▼
A PCIe 4.0 x4 NVMe SSD in the M.2 2280 size with 1TB of storage and rated speeds of up to 6,000MB/s reads and 4,000MB/s writes. It's a DRAM-less design built for low power use, and it comes with Acronis True Image software for cloning your old drive.
Read moreRead less▼
Western Digital's popular drive is faster than the Samsung 990 - but not quite matching either the 990 Pro or Lexar. Still, it's impressive enough, with read/write speeds up to 7,250MB/s and 6,900MB/s.
Read moreRead less▼
Why we recommend them
The Samsung 990 delivers sequential read and write speeds of up to 7,150MB/s and 6,450MB/s. That's fast enough to handle most tasks without needing to upgrade to a PCIe 5.0 platform. Random read and write speeds reach up to 700,000 and 1.1 million IOPS, respectively.
Our sister site, Tom's Hardware, called the Lexar NM790 an all-around excellent SSD with little to lament in its review. We tested the heatsink version in our Lexar NM790 with Heatsink review, giving it a Great Value award and praising its PS5 benchmark score, though we noticed very occasional stutters while playing.
In our five-star Samsung 990 Pro review, we called it "an absolutely stellar M.2 SSD for both professional users and gamers alike. With solid capacities at a fair price and the fastest read/write performance of any PCIe 4.0 SSD we’ve tested, this SSD should definitely be at the top of your list if you’re looking to upgrade or do a new PC build."
The Kingston NV3 is a solid, affordable SSD - in Tom's Hardware's review, they noted that Kingston can change the components inside the NV3 over time, so the drive you buy may not perform exactly like the review unit. That's common for budget drives, and the NV3 is still much faster than any SATA SSD or hard drive.
The WD_Black SN7100 is a popular pick, particularly for gaming, where its read/write speeds favor fast loading and saving. The review from our sister site PC Gamer highlighted its strong read performance and low operating temperatures and concluding that it was “perfect for any gaming PC or console.” Personally, I'm not convinced the extra speed is worth the extra cost here, when the Lexar and 990 Pro are beating it. But others may disagree.
Price context & historical value
All five SSDs are set a fair price for today's market, but far from where they used to be before the component price sent every cost skyrocketing. Even last year, 1TB drives were around the $100 mark - and I'm not sure when we'll see prices fall back to that again. Fingers crossed for 2027.
One thing to note about the Samsung 990. The 1TB model currently offers better value per terabyte than its 2TB sibling, so there's little financial incentive in buying the larger drive unless you need the extra capacity.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Samsung 990 if... you're upgrading an older SSD or building a PC and want fast PCIe 4.0 storage for games, applications, and creative projects.
✅ Buy the Lexar NM790 if... you want near-flagship PCIe 4.0 speed for less than Samsung or WD charge, or you want high endurance for the money.
✅ Buy the Samsung 990 Pro if... you want blazing-fast speeds for heavy file transfers, video editing, and game saves.
✅ Buy the Kingston NV3 1TB if... you need an affordable boot drive or game drive, you're upgrading an older PC or laptop from a hard drive or SATA SSD, or you want the included cloning software.
✅ Buy the WD Black SN7100 if… you want a fast PCIe 4.0 SSD for a PC or laptop upgrade, and prefer it over the moderately pricier Samsung 990.

articles.title: AI Makes Formal Verification Practical
articles.text:
LONDON, U.K. — Math AI foundation model startup Harmonic is expanding into formal verification for software and hardware, starting with C, Verilog, and Rust.
Formal verification is a well-known technique for proving code is correct, and when extended to hardware description languages such as Verilog, for proving hardware designs are correct and will function exactly as the specification demands. Though it’s well known, formal verification is used in a relatively limited way today, and only by specialists, Harmonic CEO Tudor Achim told EE Times.
There are two main techniques used for formal verification today. Most existing schemes use model checkers, which run the code many times over to explore all the possible states to try to find a state for which the code doesn’t behave as intended. Model checkers are powerful, but as the complexity of hardware increases, they are increasingly compute-intensive.
The other method, theorem proving, creates a logical proof that the implementation of the code is mathematically equivalent to its specification. Until now, this required humans to write proofs, and was very difficult for complex hardware.
“Historically, theorem proving has been horrible compared to model checkers,” Achim said. “Because to write a theorem proving proof, you need to write a lot of language, and to write a model checking proof you just need to solve some very specific algorithmic math problems.”
Computers have historically been good at solving specific problems, such as those in model checking, but unsuitable for tackling unstructured problems such as writing proofs. AI has changed everything, Achim said.
“With AI, computers are now unbelievably good at writing unstructured things,” he said. “So now theorem proving, which had no promise for 50 years, now has all the promise, because it’s very scalable, if you can write down the right proof.”
Trained for math
An AI model trained for math, such as Harmonic’s Aristotle, can be applied to solve this type of proof. Aristotle has been trained using reinforcement learning over a period of two years, recently achieving gold-medal equivalent performance at the International Mathematical Olympiad.
Hardware and software are not handled differently by Aristotle; C or Verilog code is compiled via Harmonic’s proprietary compilers into a math problem, which is given to Aristotle to solve. Harmonic’s IP is in both turning the problem into math and solving that math, Achim said.
“It’s easy to vibe code a compiler that turns [code] into a math problem, but it’s hard to do one that’s actually correct across all the code on GitHub or can handle 30-million-gate designs,” he said. “There’s a lot of infrastructure [required] to actually do the proofs with this technology. You also need some models that are fast and cheap at doing it, because to write a proof of some code you probably need 10 to 100× as much code in the proof script as is in the original code.”
The actual theorem proving isn’t difficult, Achim said; in fact, it’s very simple compared to the hardest math problems.
“All it’s doing is what a smart developer would do—they have a mental model of what are the inputs to my function, what does my function do to it, and what’s the output,” he said. “You can think of it as really elaborate bookkeeping of the program state—there’s a lot more stuff you’re writing down for bookkeeping than in the code itself.”
This “elaborate bookkeeping” might be used to, for example, prove that there is no set of inputs to the chip that would result in deadlock. A natural-language statement gets turned into a mathematical theorem (written in Lean, a programming language invented for math), and the AI solves that theorem. The idea is to effectively build a model of what happens when the chip runs and prove for all possible inputs that a certain condition can’t happen. If it fails, the AI can produce a counterexample—perhaps a waveform for a particular set of conditions that results in deadlock.
This technique can be used to find bugs very deep in the design. AI chip company Tensordyne, a Harmonic customer, used Aristotle to find bugs more than 100,000 cycles deep, multiple orders of magnitude beyond what model checkers could have found, according to Achim.
How big a design can Aristotle handle?
“We’re at probably a million FLOPS and 20 million to 30 million gates right now, so still not quite full CPU scale,” Achim said. “Empirically, we have scaled the size of designs we can handle by 10× every two and a half months, and we see that continuing, so I think by the middle or end of next year, we’d ideally be at full CPU scale.”
In practice, Aristotle typically runs on blocks of the design, and theorems that have been proven for individual blocks can be reused to prove things about other blocks that depend on them, Achim said. This technique can be used to verify arbitrarily large designs.
The size limitation for single runs is the size of the proof scripts, which are orders of magnitude bigger than the original code, and the artifacts these scripts generate, which are even larger. Eventually, the infrastructure just isn’t big enough.
“Ultimately it becomes a data management question and a parallelization question,” Achim said.
There are also human factors that limit the size of designs that can be verified in a single run.
“As you approach larger designs, you start to run into limitations of the clarity of the specification the designer made—there might be assumptions baked in that are not clear,” Achim said. “A formal analysis is the most detailed analysis of a chip, and it forces you to have all your assumptions out in the open. Traditionally, teams have not been forced to do that.”
With AI, the ability to prove theorems is today outstripping humans’ ability to write specifications, especially as designs get more complex, Achim said.
AI-driven workflows
Formal verification has been used at the end of a workflow to ensure the design is correct before tape-out, but with the dawn of AI-driven workflows, Aristotle could be used during the design process as the specifications evolve with the design, testing that all the properties still hold for every revision, Achim said.
“What we see across the board is that people are rethinking what their flow looks like,” he said. “The old flow was very human-centric; you had well-integrated tools across the board, but people now want to develop at the speed of agents, and I don’t know that people are as wedded to their workflows as one might have thought a year ago.”
Many customers are using agents to assist with designs and write code, but verifying hardware (and software) has been a stubborn holdout for automation so far, Achim said. Automating formal verification could therefore be another step toward removing humans from the chip design process entirely.
Achim expects that easier, scalable formal verification will change the economics of chip design too, since it should make large chip designs approachable even for small teams. “Historically, a lot of money in chip development has gone toward verification, 70% to 80% by some estimates,” he said. “Even if you’re spending that much, you’re still limited in what you can be sure is correct, so I think people stayed away from super complex and weird designs … but once you have formal verification and correctness, I think all bets are off.”

articles.title: Justiça dos EUA condena Huawei por roubo de segredos comerciais
articles.text:
Justiça dos EUA condena Huawei por roubo de segredos comerciais
Empresa e três subsidiárias também foram consideradas culpadas por fraude bancária, lavagem de dinheiro e violações de sanções contra o Irã.
A Huawei foi considerada culpada pela Justiça dos Estados Unidos por conspiração para roubar segredos comerciais de empresas do país. Além da espionagem, a empresa também foi condenada por fraude bancária, lavagem de dinheiro e violações de sanções contra o Irã.
Segundo o Departamento de Justiça dos EUA (DOJ), outras três subsidiárias da companhia também foram condenadas: Huawei Device, Futurewei Technologies e Huawei Device USA. Apesar disso, o júri absolveu a Huawei das acusações de conspiração para extorsão organizada e de conspiração para obstruir a Justiça.
Em nota, mencionada pela Associated Press, a Huawei comemorou a absolvição nestes pontos e contestou os demais vereditos. “Acreditamos que as acusações restantes do governo também não têm mérito jurídico ou factual”.
As acusações fazem parte de um processo iniciado em 2019, mesmo ano em que os Estados Unidos sancionaram a Huawei por suspeitas de espionagem para a China — o que impede a empresa de negociar com empresas do ocidente há anos. A sentença deve ser determinada em audiência marcada para 14 de setembro de 2027. Em nota, a companhia alega que pretende recorrer.
De acordo com o DOJ, a Huawei e suas subsidiárias participaram durante anos de um esquema para obter propriedade intelectual de concorrentes e parceiros comerciais nos Estados Unidos. O material incluía códigos-fonte, manuais técnicos, tecnologia de antenas e sistemas usados para testar smartphones.
Em um dos casos, funcionários da Huawei teriam fotografado e até enviado peças de um robô de testes para telas sensíveis ao toque, que simulam gestos humanos, usado pela operadora T-Mobile. Em outra situação, engenheiros da chinesa teriam copiado código-fonte usado nos roteadores da Cisco.
Funcionários e pesquisadores ligados à Huawei também teriam roubado informações e repassado ao país asiático em casos envolvendo a Fujitsu e o laboratório de semicondutores CNEX. A acusação ainda aponta que a Huawei recebeu informações confidenciais da fabricante de antenas Quintel, sob um acordo de não divulgação, e depois apresentou um pedido de patente que incorporava a tecnologia da empresa.
Segundo o DOJ, a empresa também foi considerada culpada em acusações relacionadas a violações das sanções dos Estados Unidos contra o Irã, fraude bancária e lavagem de dinheiro. A Huawei teria fornecido serviços de telecomunicações ao governo iraniano, incluindo infraestrutura de internet e redes móveis, e ajudado autoridades do país a monitorar e censurar o acesso à internet.
As operações no Irã eram conduzidas por uma companhia chamada Skycom, que, segundo a acusação, tratava-se de uma subsidiária da fabricante chinesa. A Huawei dizia publicamente que a companhia era apenas uma parceira comercial.
A Huawei também teria fornecido informações falsas a bancos, jornalistas e ao governo dos Estados Unidos sobre suas atividades no país e sobre o cumprimento das sanções americanas. Segundo os promotores, bancos processaram bilhões de dólares em operações relacionadas à Huawei sem saber a verdadeira extensão das atividades da empresa no Irã.

articles.title: Huawei convicted of money laundering, conspiracy to steal trade secrets, and fraud by US jury — FBI says Chinese tech giant built its success on deception and theft
articles.text:
Huawei convicted of money laundering, conspiracy to steal trade secrets, and fraud by US jury — FBI says Chinese tech giant built its success on deception and theft
The sentencing hearing will not happen until September 2027, though.
A jury has found Huawei guilty of bank fraud, wire fraud, money laundering conspiracy, conspiracy to steal trade secrets, and violations of the U.S. sanctions against Iran, among others. According to Bloomberg, the verdict was the result of a nearly three-month trial in which a foreign company has been prosecuted by the U.S. Department of Justice. This is a rare occurrence, resulting in a conviction of 10 out of 12 counts, with the Chinese company getting cleared of conspiracy to obstruct justice and racketeering conspiracy.
“Today’s verdict makes clear that fraud, sanctions evasion, and the theft of intellectual property are not business strategies, they are serious crimes,” James Barnacle, the Assistant Director in Charge of the FBI New York Field Office, which conducted the investigation on the tech firm, told the publication. “Huawei’s success was built on deception and theft, and the FBI will never hesitate to pursue those who profit by breaking the law.”
Huawei has long been in the crosshairs of the U.S., with the company getting banned from the country in 2018 alongside other Chinese telecommunications hardware manufacturers. It has even sued the U.S. government, claiming that the equipment ban against the company is unconstitutional. Nevertheless, Washington proceeded with the move and built a case against the company as early as 2019. This has been hit by multiple delays, though, owing to the COVID-19 Pandemic, as well as Huawei’s multiple attempts to halt the investigation even before the case went to trial. There was even an allegation that two Chinese intelligence officers offered $61,000 in Bitcoin to a U.S. law enforcement official to get insider information about the case.
It was also in 2018 that the daughter of Huawei founder and company CFO Meng Wanzhou was arrested in Canada on suspicion of the firm’s attempt to circumvent U.S. sanctions on Iran. Washington even attempted to have her extradited to the U.S., but she was able to return to China in 2019 after admitting to the company’s illegal business in Iran. Aside from that, the U.S. Department of Justice provided other examples of Huawei’s violations, including the theft of T-Mobile’s robotic touch screen testing robot, with a Huawei employee stealing a part of the device from T-Mobile’s controlled lab, the copying of Cisco router source code, another Huawei employee photographing proprietary Fujitsu equipment, and using confidential information gathered through an NDA from Quintel, a U.S. antenna manufacturer, which was subsequently included in Huawei’s patent application.
On the other hand, the company’s lead defense attorney, Brian Heberlig, focused on its acquittal on two of the charges. “It’s hard not to have profoundly mixed emotions from the verdict we just heard,” Heberlig told Bloomberg. The racketeering conspiracy “alleged that the company was corrupt from top to bottom, that it had a corporate culture and policy of cheating, stealing, and lying, and the jury found the company not guilty on that charge.”
Sentencing hearing for the company is set for September 2027, although it’s still unclear what penalties the U.S. government is seeking. The Chinese Foreign Ministry, on the other hand, said, “The Chinese government firmly opposes the U.S. suppression and containment of Chinese companies and firmly supports Chinese companies in safeguarding their legitimate rights and interests.”

articles.title: Profitez du Black Friday pour passer à l’éclairage connecté : le pack Philips Hue Entertainment perd 130€ chez Boulanger
articles.text:
Le pack Philips Hue Entertainment permet d’équiper un téléviseur d’un système d’éclairage synchronisé, et associe à cela une lampe à poser Hue Play. Durant le Black Friday de Boulanger, l’ensemble passe de 299,99 € à 169,99 €.
Si le système Ambilight de Philips vous attire, mais que vous n’avez pas envie d’acheter un téléviseur de cette marque pour autant, alors cette alternative peut vous intéresser. Il s’agit du pack Philips Hue Entertainment, actuellement disponible pour 169,99 € chez Boulanger. Ce dernier permet d’installer un système similaire à Ambilight sur un téléviseur de 65 pouces au maximum, de n’importe quelle marque. En complément, une lampe à poser Hue Play est fournie, pour prolonger l’ambiance lumineuse.
Le pack Philips Hue Entertainment est disponible à 169,99 € chez Boulanger, contre un prix de référence de 299,99 €.
Pourquoi choisir le pack Philips Hue Entertainment ?
- Pour accompagner vos films et vos jeux : les éclairages reproduisent les couleurs présentes à l’écran afin de créer une ambiance autour du téléviseur.
- Pour son fonctionnement astucieux : la caméra analyse directement l’image, y compris lorsque vous regardez une plateforme de streaming depuis votre TV.
- Pour personnaliser votre installation : l’application Hue permet d’ajuster les effets et l’intensité lumineuse selon vos préférences.
Des éclairages synchronisés avec l’image à l’écran
La caméra Play Screen Sync s’installe au sommet du téléviseur. Grâce à son objectif fisheye, elle scrute l’écran puis adapte les éclairages au contenu. Pour profiter de cette immersion, il faut prendre le temps d’installer le ruban lumineux LED Play gradient de 2,5 mètres à l’arrière de votre téléviseur. Pour ce qui est de la lampe Hue Play, vous pouvez l’installer où vous voulez, à condition de disposer d’une prise secteur pour la brancher.
Un ruban qui fonctionne sans pont Hue
L’avantage de l’association entre la caméra Hue Play Screen Sync et le ruban LED Play gradient, c’est qu’elle gère la synchronisation toute seule et offre un grand choix de personnalisation via l’application Philips Hue. Néanmoins, si le ruban peut être synchronisé seul sans pont, un Hue Bridge vendu séparément est nécessaire pour synchroniser également la lampe à poser du pack.
✅ Les points forts
- Synchronisation avec tous les programmes présents à l’écran.
- Ruban lumineux et lampe à poser réunis dans le pack.
- Aucun changement nécessaire dans les branchements HDMI.
❌ Les limites
- Hue Bridge nécessaire pour synchroniser plusieurs éclairages.
- Caméra visible et sensible aux reflets sur l’écran.
Boulanger propose ce pack Philips Hue à 169,99 €, une offre intéressante pour bien démarrer dans l’éclairage connecté.
Pour renforcer l’immersion de vos séances de gaming et de cinéma, ce pack Philips Hue Entertainment peut représenter un bon investissement. Si vous disposez déjà d’un pont Hue à votre domicile, vous aurez accès à davantage d’options, dont la synchronisation de la lampe à poser. Sans pont, seul le ruban pourra suivre l’image.
Prenez cependant en compte que le ruban LED Play gradient compris dans ce pack est destiné à un téléviseur de 65 pouces au maximum. Il peut être découpé pour ajuster sa longueur, en suivant scrupuleusement le mode d'emploi de Philips.

articles.title: "Ma confiance est fortement entamée" : le piratage de 1Password, géant des mots de passe, passe mal
articles.text:
1Password a été piraté : données volées, mots de passe en danger ? Ce qu'il faut faire
Un pirate s'est introduit dans les serveurs de 1Password, le coffre-fort numérique de millions de particuliers et de 200 000 entreprises. Noms, adresses e-mail, jetons de récupération : il est reparti avec de quoi monter des arnaques très crédibles. Les mots de passe, eux, sont restés à l'abri. Voici ce qui a fuité et comment vous protéger.
Le gestionnaire de mots de passe 1Password a révélé mercredi 25 novembre avoir été victime d'une cyberattaque. Tout est parti du compte GitHub professionnel d'un employé. Le pirate s'en est servi pour accéder au code source de l'entreprise canadienne, puis pour glisser dans ses serveurs internes un code malveillant qui a aspiré des données de clients. Il a aussi eu accès au système de déploiement de l'entreprise, dont tous les identifiants ont depuis été changés. L'enquête a débuté le 19 novembre.
La cible pèse lourd. 1Password revendique des millions de particuliers parmi ses clients et, selon son bilan publié en octobre, plus de 200 000 entreprises, dont 85 % du classement Forbes des 50 champions de l'IA. Votre employeur fait peut-être partie du lot.
Quelles données ont été volées chez 1Password ?
Le pirate a récupéré les noms et adresses e-mail d'une partie des clients, leurs identifiants de compte, ainsi que les dates de création et de dernière connexion. Il a aussi emporté des jetons contenus dans les liens d'invitation et de récupération de compte envoyés par e-mail. L'éditeur ne précise pas combien de comptes sont touchés.
We’re sharing an update about a recent security incident involving some of 1Password’s backend systems. 𝗡𝗼 𝗰𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿 𝘃𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘁 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗻𝘁, 𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗹𝘂𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝗲𝗰𝗿𝗲𝘁𝘀, 𝗽𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝘃𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘁 𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀, 𝗼𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗸𝗲𝘆𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁…
— 1Password (@1Password) November 25, 2026
Le scénario rappelle le piratage de LastPass, lui aussi suivi d'un vol de données clients. Les coffres, où sont rangés les mots de passe, n'ont en revanche pas été consultés. 1Password ne stocke ni le mot de passe principal de ses abonnés ni leur clé secrète, indispensables pour déchiffrer leur contenu.
Les jetons volés ne suffisent pas non plus à ouvrir un compte : il faut aussi le code envoyé à l'adresse mail du client, ou une connexion via le système d'authentification de son entreprise. Par précaution, ce code passe de six chiffres à dix caractères mêlant lettres et chiffres.
Faut-il s'inquiéter pour ses mots de passe ?
L'incident passe mal. "Ma confiance dans l'entreprise censée garantir le plus haut niveau de sécurité est fortement entamée", a réagi sur X Greg Osuri, fondateur de la plateforme de cloud Akash Network, dans un message vu plus de 135 000 fois.
1Password has been hacked.
Although they claim no customer vaults have been compromised, my trust in the company that's supposed to maintain the highest levels of security is heavily diminished.
More: https://t.co/JIUb1fR5nv
— Greg Osuri 🇺🇸 (@gregosuri) November 25, 2026
1Password assure pourtant que ses clients n'ont rien à faire. C'est sur ce chiffrement que repose la fiabilité des gestionnaires de mots de passe, et fuir vers un concurrent ne garantirait rien.
Le vrai risque se trouve dans votre boîte de réception et sur votre téléphone. Avec un nom, une adresse et une date de dernière connexion, un escroc peut rédiger un faux message de sécurité, par mail ou par SMS, voire appeler en se faisant passer pour 1Password. L'éditeur le rappelle : il ne demandera jamais votre mot de passe principal ni votre clé secrète. Au moindre doute, ouvrez l'application ou tapez vous-même l'adresse du site, sans cliquer sur aucun lien.
Même vigilance chez la concurrence : Dashlane a lui aussi dû corriger une faille qui pouvait exposer des identifiants.

articles.title: iiyama Launches ProLite XCB4994DQSU-B1 49-inch Curved Dual QHD Monitor
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
iiyama Launches ProLite XCB4994DQSU-B1 49-inch Curved Dual QHD Monitor
iiyama has introduced a new 49-inch curved monitor, the ProLite XCB4994DQSU-B1. This office-oriented monitor has a 32:9 aspect ratio and a native resolution of 5120 x 1440 pixels. It is basically the equivalent of two QHD (2560 x 1440) displays placed side by side, giving users an ultrawide workspace without a central bezel. The VA panel with a matte finish has a 1000R curvature and supports refresh rates of up to 120 Hz. It features a typical brightness of 400 nits, a static contrast ratio of 3,000:1, and a 2 ms gray-to-gray response time. It covers 100% of the sRGB color space and 80% of NTSC. The monitor also supports HDR10 and Adaptive Sync, with a variable refresh rate range of 48-120 Hz over DisplayPort and 48-60 Hz over HDMI. Other display features include flicker-free operation and a blue light reducer.
Connectivity includes two HDMI 2.0 inputs and two DisplayPort 1.2 inputs. The integrated USB hub provides two USB-A 3.2 Gen 1 ports and two USB-C ports. All support data transfer speeds of up to 5 Gbps. The USB-A ports provide up to 4.5 W of power, while the USB-C ports are rated for up to 7.5 W. A headphone jack and two built-in 5 W speakers are also included. The monitor comes with a height and tilt-adjustable stand, and 100 x 100 mm VESA mounting support. iiyama lists the ProLite XCB4994DQSU-B1 on its European website for €668, including VAT.

articles.title: AI infrastructure economics takeaways from Fully Connected
articles.text:
Three insights you may have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of the Fully Connected event
AI infrastructure economics are increasingly defined by the cost of producing intelligence rather than acquiring computing capacity.
As inference demand outpaces training growth, infrastructure providers and their customers must increase productive computing time without a corresponding rise in operating costs. The emergence of continuously learning agents and physical AI applications is further complicating that equation. For CoreWeave Inc., the changing workload mix is altering the economics of infrastructure delivery, according to theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante and John Furrier.
“What you’re seeing CoreWeave do strategically is they’re expanding out beyond compute,” Vellante said. “They’ve got networking; they’ve got storage. They’ve got this software layer, which is observability. They’ve got security in there. They’ve got this closed-loop system between evaluation, observation [and] runtime curating … that’s sort of how they’re saying their software layer is now intact.”
During the Fully Connected event, Vellante and Furrier spoke with CoreWeave executives, technology partners and customers about the technical and economic realities of running artificial intelligence at production scale. (* Disclosure below.)
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video analysis with Dave Vellante and John Furrier:
Here are three insights you may have missed from theCUBE’s exclusive coverage of this event:
Insight #1: AI infrastructure economics hinge on productive capacity.
The commercial value of inference depends on both token volume and delivery speed. Nvidia Corp.’s Groq 3 LPX inference accelerator, which works with its Vera Rubin platform, is attracting interest in financial technology and other sectors that require real-time processing, according to Ian Buck, vice president and general manager of hyperscale and HPC at Nvidia.
“Data centers have a natural cap, and that cap is actually their power,” he told theCUBE. “With every generation of GPU, we make sure that our tokens per watt is upwards of 10 times more efficient. In fact, we saw that with Blackwell — we got, in the end, a 30x improvement in tokens per watt.”
Memory management adds another dimension to AI infrastructure economics as agents engage in increasingly lengthy interactions. A single session involving 500,000 tokens can consume between 5% and 10% of a graphics processing unit’s memory. Retaining session context in persistent storage can reduce costly recalculations, according to Alon Horev, co-founder and chief technology officer of Vast Data Inc.
“You can move a session from one busy GPU to one less busy GPU and move KV cache either over the network or read it from Vast,” he told theCUBE. “Once you look at inference as a distributed problem where you have the opportunity to use GPU memory, CPU memory and Vast across a fleet of machines, you have more optionality and you have more optimized scheduling.”
For AI-native startups, specialized cloud providers offer an alternative to owning capital-intensive infrastructure. LlamaIndex Inc. processes millions of document pages daily for customers in finance, legal services and insurance. Inference accounts for about 75% of its workloads, with training accounting for the remainder, according to Jerry Liu, co-founder and chief executive officer of LlamaIndex.
“We serve a lot of different customers at extremely persistent and also spiky workloads,” he told theCUBE. “We really, really need to make sure that we have the right capacity to serve our customers without getting throttled.”
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video discussion with Ian Buck:
Insight #2: Reducing operational risk protects AI infrastructure investments.
Protecting AI infrastructure investments starts on the factory floor. Dell Technologies Inc. has developed modular rack designs to accommodate different power and cooling configurations. Its collaboration with CoreWeave includes integrating the cloud provider’s Racky management software into factory testing and improving liquid-cooling leak detection, according to Sarat Krishnan, director of PowerEdge AI architecture and systems development engineering at Dell.
“It becomes increasingly expensive to remediate and fix something as you go later on in the manufacturing process; [it] becomes extremely expensive if you have to replace something in the data center,” he told theCUBE. “What we have done over the last two years is shift our most complex diagnostics — the ones that are going to capture true hardware failures — further and further left.”
At Cognition AI Inc., continuous model improvement involves training across data centers in multiple countries. The company’s Devin software engineering agent now handles tasks ranging from code development to resolving production issues, according to Chen Goldberg (pictured, left), executive vice president of product and engineering at CoreWeave, and Silas Alberti (right), head of research and founding team at Cognition. To support these learning systems, CoreWeave introduced Forge, a platform that connects inference, evaluation and model refinement and incorporates Agent Lens to trace agent activity.
“If you run a big training run, you’re not just looking at the GPUs, but you also want uptime,” Alberti said during the event. “If just one replica goes down, the whole training run goes down. I think a very important metric is getting to this 99.99% reliability.”
For International Business Machines Corp., the power and cooling demands of newer hardware helped drive its decision to work with CoreWeave. The relationship has since expanded to include joint engineering around identity management and workload isolation through CoreWeave Sandboxes. IBM also benchmarks the performance impact of security controls to inform architectural decisions, according to Brian Belgodere, senior technical staff member at IBM.
“This is a supply chain problem, top to bottom,” Belgodere told theCUBE. “It’s not just the hardware: it’s the firmware, kernel levels, code, your data provenance. Then you get into the whole world of agents, your images. It is an absolute provenance problem.”
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video discussion with Brian Belgodere:
Insight #3: Physical AI puts infrastructure investments to the test.
For organizations deploying physical AI, implementation time is a key consideration in AI infrastructure economics. Aston Martin F1, whose race cars generate a million data points per second each, operates under strict budget constraints and development deadlines. CoreWeave’s forward-deployed engineering approach brings specialized expertise to those operations, according to Richard Ahlfeld, senior vice president of physical AI at CoreWeave, and Eric Ernst, commercial technology ambassador of AMR GP Ltd., trading as Aston Martin F1.
“We really need people that can be outside of the car development phase and come in with the fresh knowledge of what’s happening in this industry that is moving extremely quickly,” Ernst said during the event. “You can build as many processes as you want, call it agile, whatever you want. You cannot stop that process. You got to hit a deadline.”
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video discussion with Richard Ahlfeld and Eric Ernst:
Walden Robotics Inc. uses large-scale virtual simulation to prepare robots for physical deployment. Its robots have been working full production shifts alongside humans since May, performing tasks such as machine tending, parts kitting and subassembly, according to Adrien Gaidon, co-founder and chief strategy officer of Walden Robotics, and John Mancuso, vice president of field engineering at CoreWeave Inc.
“If you’re changing things and you have machines that cannot change and continuously learn in deployment, then you become a burden,” Gaidon told theCUBE. “We do machines that continuously learn from deployment and adapt so customers can change their mind and improve the process and give them the superpower to change even more and faster.”
Here’s theCUBE’s full video discussion with John Mancuso and Adrien Gaidon:
Other highlights from theCUBE’s coverage of the Fully Connected event include:
- Bartley Richardson, chief of AI at CrowdStrike Holdings Inc., and Jim Higgins, chief information security officer of CoreWeave, talk with theCUBE about machine-speed defense, infrastructure-level security and operational trust.
- Rob Bahr, senior engineer at BattleBots Inc., sits down with theCUBE to discuss AI simulation for robot combat design and the potential for AI-driven robot autonomy.
- Harsh Banwait, senior director of product at CoreWeave, and Hannah Coutand, director of product marketing, Vera CPU, at Nvidia, talk with theCUBE about CPU requirements, sandbox performance and infrastructure security.
To watch more of theCUBE’s coverage of the Fully Connected event, here’s our complete video playlist:

articles.title: Windows 11 distribue des pilotes Intel obsolètes et vulnérables via Windows update
articles.text:
Les outils de Microsoft ont visiblement un gros problème de communication. Le site allemand Deskmodder rapporte en effet que le système d’exploitation a distribué, par l’intermédiaire de Windows Update, un pilote obsolète et vulnérable déclenchant une alerte de sécurité de Microsoft Defender.
Un pilote vulnérable, mais légitime, distribué par Windows Update
C’est après avoir mis à jour un système Intel NUC de 11e génération que Deskmodder a vu s’afficher une alerte de sécurité émise par Microsoft Defender. Celle-ci a mis en lumière un problème provenant du paquet Intel Performance Driver Extension dans sa version 1.0.0.38. Ce module lié au service Intel NUC Software Studio Service et qui a pour objectif de fournir une surveillance matérielle de bas niveau, comporte une importante faille de sécurité. Une brèche qui touche plus particulièrement le composant WinRing0 de ce pilote et dont la vulnérabilité est connue depuis 2020.
Cette faille, identifiée sous la référence CVE-2020-14979 permet une élévation locale des privilèges. Cela signifie concrètement que des attaquants disposant déjà d’un accès à la machine pourraient exploiter ce pilote légitime pour mener des attaques de type Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver et ainsi contourner les protections du noyau de Windows.
Windows Update réinstalle automatiquement le pilote après suppression
Mais le plus gros problème avec ce pilote, c’est que bien qu’il soit clairement identifié comme étant vulnérable par Microsoft Defender, Windows Update continue de le distribuer. Et cela, même après l’avoir supprimé.
Le module de mise à jour de Windows ne communique pas avec l’antivirus natif et continue de le délivrer en boucle ce pilote vulnérable lors des recherches de mises à jour. Un problème de taille alors que Microsoft a dévoilé il y a quelques mois son Driver Quality Initiative, censée corriger toute seule les pilotes problématiques.

articles.title: Estos son los 3 juegos que PlayStation Plus regalará en diciembre de 2026
articles.text:
Sony anunció los tres juegos que los suscriptores de PlayStation Plus podrán sumar a su biblioteca en diciembre: Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 y Amnesia: The Bunker. Estarán disponibles desde el martes 1 de diciembre hasta el lunes 4 de enero, según el blog oficial de PlayStation.
La compañía los presentó como los juegos mensuales para todos los miembros del servicio. Quien los reclame dentro de ese plazo podrá jugarlos mientras mantenga la suscripción activa. Sony aclara que la oferta puede variar según la región y remite a la página de PlayStation.com para consultar el detalle de cada país.
El anuncio lo firmó Adam Michel, director sénior de servicios de juego de Sony Interactive Entertainment. Los títulos llegan con casi cinco semanas de margen: el período de reclamo se extiende más allá de las fiestas de fin de año.
Tres juegos de géneros muy distintos
Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4 estará en su edición para dos generaciones de consolas, PS5 y PS4. Reúne las versiones renovadas del tercer y el cuarto juego de la saga de skate, con más patinadores, parques nuevos, trucos adicionales y música.
Según Sony, los escenarios de ambas entregas fueron rehechos en resolución 4K, con objetivos simplificados y el formato clásico de dos minutos por carrera. También incluye los modos Create-A-Skater y Create-A-Park, que permiten diseñar patinadores y parques. Por primera vez, los jugadores pueden crear objetivos propios y compartirlos con amigos.
En PS5, el juego corre en 4K nativo a 60 cuadros por segundo en el modo Fidelity. Sony advierte que la salida en 4K requiere un televisor o monitor compatible.
Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 también llegará para PS5 y PS4. Es un juego de acción y rol basado en la serie de animación: el jugador crea su propio personaje, recorre Conton City y se alía con figuras conocidas de la franquicia para entrenar y enfrentar a distintos enemigos.
Tiene modos multijugador en línea. Los usuarios pueden pelear contra otros jugadores de todo el mundo o participar en las Raid Battles, combates cooperativos contra enemigos gigantes.
Amnesia: The Bunker es el único de los tres que figura solo para PS4. Es un juego de terror en primera persona de los creadores de Soma y de la saga Amnesia, ambientado en un búnker abandonado de la Primera Guerra Mundial.
Recursos escasos y un recordatorio de noviembre
El jugador encarna a Henri Clément, un soldado francés que queda solo con un revólver con una única bala, una linterna de dinamo ruidosa y pocos suministros que debe recolectar y fabricar. Según la descripción oficial, un peligro constante reacciona a cada movimiento y sonido, y cada partida es distinta por la aleatoriedad del juego.
Los juegos de diciembre reemplazan a los de noviembre, que todavía pueden reclamarse. Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered y Monster Train 2 estarán disponibles hasta el lunes 30 de noviembre, de acuerdo con el mismo blog.
Pasada esa fecha, quienes no los hayan agregado a su biblioteca no podrán hacerlo con el beneficio del servicio.
Juegos de Xbox Game Pass para diciembre
Por su parte, Xbox Game Pass, el servicio que compite con PlayStation Plus, ya suma seis juegos confirmados para diciembre de 2026, cinco de los cuales llegarán durante los primeros cuatro días del mes. La selección combina estrenos del día uno con el regreso de una franquicia de terror pensada para el multijugador, además de una aventura cooperativa ambientada en paisajes del norte de Suecia.
Ambos títulos estarán disponibles en Xbox Series, PC y mediante juego en la nube, aunque con una diferencia relevante: uno se incorpora directamente a los planes Ultimate y PC Game Pass, mientras que el otro también llegará a Premium. Todavía resta que Microsoft confirme el resto del calendario de diciembre, algo que se espera durante la primera semana del mes, sin fecha ni formato de anuncio definidos.

articles.title: Urban VPN under legal scrutiny over claims it harvested users' private AI prompts
articles.text:
Urban VPN under legal scrutiny over claims it harvested users' private AI prompts
Attorneys are investigating whether three Urban VPN browser extensions allegedly captured and shared California users' AI chats without consent in 2025
- Urban VPN is under legal scrutiny over alleged data privacy violations
- California Chrome, Edge users of one of its VPN extensions may qualify
- Over 8M users may have had their AI prompts harvested by Urban VPN
Users who relied on Urban VPN's free browser tools for privacy may have had their AI chatbot prompts quietly recorded and sold instead. Attorneys are now investigating those claims for a potential class action lawsuit.
As reported by Top Class Actions, lawyers are examining whether Urban VPN's extensions broke California privacy law by collecting and sharing AI chats — a potential violation first revealed by researchers in December last year.
No court has ruled on the allegations, and no settlement exists yet. As of November 2026, the law firm is reviewing claims from eligible users before taking further legal steps.
TechRadar has contacted Urban VPN for comment on the investigation and will update this story if the company responds.
The probe, however, highlights why users should turn to the best VPN services instead of unvetted browser add-ons.
