Who qualifies for the Urban VPN lawsuit investigation?
The inquiry targets California residents who installed Urban VPN Proxy, 1ClickVPN Proxy, or Urban Browser Guard on Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge.
Eligible users must have had one of those extensions installed between July 9, 2025, and December 15, 2025, and used an AI chatbot in the same browser during that window.
Affected platforms include ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity, DeepSeek, Grok, and Meta AI. As the Top Class Actions page states, "People who trusted Urban VPN to protect their online activity may instead have had their private AI chatbot conversations collected and sold without their knowledge."
Attorneys are assessing whether CIPA, which protects private communications from unauthorized recording or sharing, applies to these AI conversations. Readers outside California fall outside this specific inquiry, and submitting a form does not guarantee compensation.
NEW: Leave No Trace — A weekly newsletter on digital privacy and online surveillance.
Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
How the AI snooping allegations emerged
This investigation follows December 2025 findings from cybersecurity firm Koi Security. As reported by TechRadar at the time, researchers discovered that version 5.5.0 of Urban VPN Proxy, pushed silently via browser auto-updates on July 9, 2025, added code that grabbed every prompt sent to supported AI chatbots.
That script compressed chats in real time and sent them to analytics.urban-vpn.com and stats.urban-vpn.com, where the data was aggregated before allegedly being passed to data broker BiScience. It kept running even when the VPN was off, or its "AI Protection" toggle was disabled, affecting over 8 million Chrome and Edge users.
Long before this incident, our Urban VPN review warned readers to avoid the service. It uses a peer-to-peer network, lacks any independent audit, and admitted in its own policy to logging IP addresses, search results, and visited pages
Does switching VPNs actually keep AI chats private?
Removing a compromised extension stops future interception, though it cannot claw back prompts already collected. Choosing a paid, audited virtual private network (VPN) also avoids the trap of free apps that monetize user traffic.
Top10VPN testing covered by TechRadar Pro found that 88% of 100 popular free Android VPNs leaked data and 71% shared it with third parties.
"The free VPN market is flooded with poor-quality apps whose only justification for their existence is to generate advertising revenue for their developers," Top10VPN Head of Research Simon Migliano told TechRadar.
Even a trusted VPN has limits, though. It encrypts traffic between your device and the VPN server, meaning the AI provider itself can still log whatever you type into your chat window.

articles.title: Rusia acaba de convertir una tranquila isla volcánica de Corea del Sur en un simulacro de la Tercera Guerra Mundial
articles.text:
Una pequeña isla volcánica situada frente a la costa oriental de Corea del Sur se ha convertido en el escenario de un incidente militar sin precedentes. Lo ocurrido el martes ilustra hasta qué punto las tensiones entre Rusia y los aliados de Estados Unidos han trascendido las fronteras de Europa.
Tres minutos de angustia. A las 7:52 de la mañana del 24 de noviembre, los aproximadamente 8.700 habitantes de Ulleungdo, una isla situada a 120 kilómetros de la península coreana, recibieron una orden de las autoridades: debían buscar refugio en instalaciones subterráneas o edificios cercanos.
Las sirenas comenzaron a sonar y las cadenas de televisión interrumpieron su programación para emitir avisos. Un vecino relató cómo una persona mayor le había telefoneado para preguntarle si había estallado una guerra. Tres minutos después, las autoridades levantaron la alerta.
Los F-15 en el aire. Lo que había detrás de aquella movilización era la presencia de alrededor de cinco aeronaves militares rusas en las inmediaciones de la isla. Las fuerzas armadas surcoreanas habían detectado los aviones antes de que penetraran en su zona de identificación de defensa aérea y desplegaron varios cazas, entre ellos los F-15K Slam Eagle.
Las aeronaves rusas acabaron abandonando la zona tras permanecer en ella durante aproximadamente 20 minutos. Según fuentes militares surcoreanas, de no haber intervenido sus cazas, podría haberse producido una violación del espacio aéreo soberano.
A escasos segundos. Según la cadena surcoreana SBS, citada por The War Zone, dos bombarderos y dos cazas rusos llegaron a situarse a unos 500 metros del espacio aéreo soberano surcoreano, una distancia que no ha podido verificarse independientemente. Para entender la magnitud del incidente, un responsable militar surcoreano explicó que estas aeronaves suelen desplazarse a entre 600 y 700 km/h, cerca de 200 metros por segundo.
Moscú, por su parte, anunció que dos bombarderos estratégicos Tu-160 habían completado una misión programada de diez horas sobre aguas internacionales, escoltados por cazas Su-35S y Su-30SM. En las imágenes difundidas por Rusia también aparece un Su-57 de quinta generación, aunque se desconoce si participó en el acercamiento a la isla.
La delgada línea roja. Aquí conviene diferenciar dos conceptos. La KADIZ, la zona de identificación de defensa aérea de Corea del Sur, se extiende más allá de su espacio aéreo soberano y tiene como objetivo identificar aeronaves potencialmente peligrosas. Penetrar en ella sin previo aviso no constituye por sí mismo una violación del derecho internacional. Rusia, de hecho, no reconoce dicha zona.
Lo excepcional del martes fue que Seúl consideró inminente una vulneración de su espacio aéreo hasta el punto de activar, por primera vez ante aeronaves rusas, una alerta aérea preventiva para la población civil.
La paciencia de Seúl. El incidente no ha surgido de la nada. Entre 2020 y 2024, Corea del Sur registró alrededor de 60 entradas de aeronaves rusas sin previo aviso en su zona de identificación aérea. En junio de este año fueron cerca de diez aviones rusos y chinos los que penetraron en ella, y en agosto volvieron a movilizarse los cazas surcoreanos.
También existe un precedente mucho más grave: en 2019, una aeronave militar rusa penetró en el espacio aéreo soberano surcoreano y provocó disparos de advertencia. Este martes, el Ministerio de Defensa convocó al agregado militar ruso, Nikolai Marchenko, para trasladarle una protesta formal y exigir medidas que eviten nuevos incidentes.
De Ucrania al Pacífico. Como explica The Wall Street Journal, Corea del Sur no es el único aliado estadounidense en Asia que observa con preocupación el incremento de la actividad militar rusa. Japón también tuvo que movilizar sus cazas la semana pasada ante la aproximación de aeronaves rusas, coincidiendo con una inusual visita de bombarderos Tu-95MS a Vietnam.
A ello se suma la creciente cooperación militar de Moscú con Pekín y, especialmente, con Pyongyang, que ha suministrado armamento y soldados a Rusia para su guerra contra Ucrania.
El peligro de normalizar lo extraordinario. Para Rusia, estas patrullas permiten exhibir su capacidad militar en el Pacífico occidental. Para Japón y Corea del Sur, suponen mantener unos elevados niveles de vigilancia y disponibilidad operativa.
El problema es que cuanto más frecuentes sean estos encuentros, mayor será el riesgo de que un error de cálculo termine desencadenando una crisis. Hasta ahora, buena parte de estos incidentes se habían resuelto entre pilotos y controladores militares. El martes, por primera vez ante una aproximación de aeronaves rusas, miles de civiles surcoreanos recibieron la orden de buscar refugio.

articles.title: Só no app: Galaxy Z Fold 8 registra menor preço em oferta de Black Friday
articles.text:
Só no app: Galaxy Z Fold 8 registra menor preço em oferta de Black Friday
Galaxy Z Fold 8 de 256 GB com tela AMOLED, câmera de 50 MP e chip premium recebe ótimo desconto com cupom e pagamento via Pix no aplicativo da Amazon
O Galaxy Z Fold 8 (256 GB) está disponível por R$ 9.649,10 no Pix usando o cupom SSG250, exclusivo para o app da Amazon. O smartphone dobrável da Samsung com design de passaporte e telas AMOLED, lançado por R$ 12.599, alcançou o menor valor visto pelo Achados do TB desde a sua chegada ao mercado em agosto deste ano.
Esta oferta é o menor preço que já encontramos para o Galaxy Z Fold 8 5G 256 GB. Nas outras 3 ofertas publicadas desde outubro de 2026, o melhor foi R$ 10.299,10 (Amazon, 11/11/2026).
O Galaxy Z Fold 8 traz uma tela externa AMOLED Dinâmico 2X de 5,5 polegadas com proporção 10:16, apresentando o novo formato de passaporte da linha de dobráveis. Já o painel interno AMOLED de 7,6 polegadas oferece uma proporção 4:3, garantindo uma ampla área de trabalho com taxa de atualização de 120 Hz.
O telefone tem uma câmera dupla traseira com sensores de 50 MP que fazem fotos com Estabilização Óptica de Imagem (OIS) e vídeos em 4K. Ele ainda conta com uma câmera frontal de 10 MP para selfies e vídeos em 4K.
Com suporte ao Galaxy AI, o Galaxy Z Fold 8 adota o chip Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 combinado com 12 GB de RAM. No entanto, os 256 GB de armazenamento interno podem ser bastante limitados para quem deseja salvar várias fotos, vídeos, aplicativos e outros arquivos.
O smartphone dobrável da Samsung é equipado com uma bateria de silício-carbono de 4.800 mAh, oferecendo uma autonomia de até 26 horas de reprodução de vídeo. O modelo tem suporte para carregamento rápido com fio de 45 W e carregamento sem fio de 20 W (Qi2).
Para o dia a dia, o telefone conta com conexões 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0, Ultra Wideband (UWB) e NFC. Ele vem de fábrica com o Android 17 (One UI 9) e, segundo a marca, receberá ao menos 7 grandes atualizações do sistema operacional.
Trazendo dobradiças de titânio reforçadas, o Galaxy Z Fold 8 (R$ 9.649,10 no Pix usando o cupom SSG250 no app) é construído com corpo em Alumínio Advanced Armor e acabamento em vidro Gorilla Glass. Ele ainda possui certificado IP48 de resistência à poeira e à água, sobrevivendo a mergulhos acidentais de até 1,5 metro em água doce por 30 minutos.
A Black Friday 2026 acontece no dia 27 de novembro, mas diversas lojas estão antecipando promoções e cupons de descontos especiais. Então, siga o Achados do TB para receber as melhores ofertas de celulares, TVs, notebooks e outros eletrônicos!

articles.title: Pendant le Black Friday 2026, cette enceinte Bose notée 5/5 chute à 268,76 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : L'enceinte Bluetooth portable Bose Portable Home Speaker "5 étoiles" à 268,76 € (-21%)
Actuellement notée 5/5 par notre rédaction, l'enceinte Bluetooth portable Bose Portable Home Speaker délivre une sonorité très équilibrée avec une diffusion à 360°. Le Black Friday 2026 est l'occasion de se l'offrir moins cher : elle passe à 268,76 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 21 % et 70,48 € d'économie.
La Bose Portable Home Speaker tente le pari de l'hybridation entre enceinte sans fil transportable et modèle sédentaire pour le salon. La marque y intègre le Wi-Fi ainsi que les assistants Alexa et Google Assistant pour piloter la musique à la voix. Ce modèle avait pleinement convaincu notre laboratoire lors de ses tests acoustiques.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, la Portable Home Speaker descend à 268,76 € chez Amazon, soit environ 21 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (339,24 €). Cela représente une économie de 70,48 € sur cette référence audio.
Une acoustique précise et une diffusion à 360°
Le point fort de cette enceinte réside dans son architecture acoustique, capable de diffuser le son uniformément à 360°. Les timbres sont clairs, les médiums et les aigus restent précis tandis que les basses apportent de la profondeur sans masquer le reste du spectre sonore, comme détaillé dans notre test complet. Actuellement notée 5/5 par notre rédaction, elle assure une restitution musicale très équilibrée dans toute la pièce.
Cette qualité sonore s'accompagne d'une captation efficace pour les commandes vocales d'Alexa et de Google Assistant, intégrés directement dans l'appareil. Côté sans-fil, la liaison Bluetooth enregistre en revanche une latence mesurée de 316 ms, un décalage qui perturbera la synchronisation labiale sur les vidéos sans compensation logicielle.
Bose Portable Home Speaker
Points forts
- Sonorité très équilibrée.
- Graves profonds et énergiques.
- Médiums et aigus très précis, timbres clairs et définis.
- Émission à 360°.
- Qualité de fabrication.
- Commandes exhaustives.
- Bonne reconnaissance vocale.
Points faibles
- Le rendu sonore dépend très fortement de la surface sur laquelle l'enceinte est posée.
- Aucune connectique filaire.
- Peu de sources réseau nativement compatibles.
- Autonomie en veille un peu faible, socle de recharge vendu séparément.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
L'expérience sans-fil pensée pour la maison
L'enceinte fait le choix du tout-sans-fil et fait l'impasse sur la connectique filaire classique, en limitant ses protocoles réseau à Spotify Connect et AirPlay. Le rendu sonore dépend également beaucoup de la surface sur laquelle vous la déposez, mais cette caractéristique ne posera aucun souci si vous l'installez sur un meuble stable et massif. La recharge s'effectue par son port USB-C, le socle dédié restant vendu séparément.
Sur le plan de l'alimentation, notre laboratoire a relevé une autonomie de 12 heures, ce qui permet de déplacer l'appareil d'une pièce à l'autre tout au long de la journée sans chercher une prise secteur. La construction est soignée et l'ensemble des commandes physiques sur le dessus offre une navigation complète sans passer systématiquement par l'application mobile.
Sonos Play : l'autre option face au Bose Portable Home Speaker
La Sonos Play partage le même créneau de l'enceinte transportable taillée pour le salon, avec ses liaisons Wi-Fi et Bluetooth ainsi que ses assistants vocaux embarqués. Elle intègre le système de calibrage automatique TruePlay et propose une conception étanche absente du modèle de Bose, tout en conservant une excellente tenue en puissance.
L'enceinte Sonos Play est vendue 279,00 €, soit un tarif supérieur de 10,24 € à celui de la Bose Portable Home Speaker. Actuellement notée 5/5, la Bose Portable Home Speaker conserve l'avantage de la note maximale et d'un prix plus bas pour profiter d'un son diffusé à 360°.
Sonos Play
Points forts
- Restitution riche et équilibrée, sans excès.
- Graves imposants pour son format.
- Bonne tenue en puissance.
- Connectivité très étendue.
- Concentré de technologies (Alexa, multiroom, calibrage TruePlay, etc.)
- Construction soignée, transport aisé et étanchéité.
- Autonomie confortable, socle de charge inclus.
Points faibles
- Basses un peu ronronnantes.
- App non disponible hors connexion wifi.
- Sensibilité aux chocs.
- Latence Bluetooth élevée.
- Adaptateur mini-jack non inclus.

articles.title: Black Friday : le n°1 des antivirus Mac tombe à 65€ pour 2 ans aujourd'hui
articles.text:
Intego affiche 50 % de remise sur sa suite de sécurité pour Mac pour le Black Friday, calculée sur un tarif qui sera aussi celui du renouvellement. Intego ONE Complete, premier de notre comparatif des antivirus pour Mac avec 9,6/10, est facturé 65 € les deux premières années, soit 12,99 € sous son plus bas des 30 derniers jours, mais notre test lui reproche un moteur gourmand en mémoire.
Intego est un nom ancien de la sécurité sur Mac : l’éditeur a été fondé en 1997 et a lancé Intego ONE début avril 2026 pour remplacer Intego X9. La suite réunit dans une seule application l’antivirus, le pare-feu, le nettoyage SmartClean et, dans la formule Complete, le VPN de l’éditeur.
L’offre Intego ONE Complete à 65 € pour deux ans couvre un Mac et un iPhone, avec 50 % de remise affichée par rapport à 129,99 €. Elle s’adresse à celles et ceux qui veulent un antivirus, un pare-feu et un VPN sous une seule facture, sans empiler les abonnements.
Intego ONE Complete pour 1 Mac et 1 iPhone, c’est 65 € pour les deux premières années au lieu de 129,99 €, soit 2,71 € par mois, directement chez Intego.
Pourquoi choisir Intego ONE Complete ?
- Une détection validée par un laboratoire : en mars 2026, AV-TEST a relevé 100 % de détection sur 405 échantillons de malwares macOS, sans faux positif, avec 6/6 en protection, en performance et en utilisation.
- Un VPN dans la même application : notre test salue ses excellentes performances, son kill switch et ses 51 pays, un atout que les formules inférieures d’Intego n’incluent pas.
- Un tarif sous le plus bas récent : à 65 € pour deux ans, soit 2,71 € par mois, l’offre passe 12,99 € sous le plus bas des 30 derniers jours affiché par Intego, 77,99 €.
Protéger un Mac, un iPhone et votre connexion au quotidien
Au quotidien, l’antivirus surveille votre Mac en temps réel, tandis que le pare-feu affiche les applications qui se connectent à Internet et vous laisse bloquer celles de votre choix. Le VPN préserve la confidentialité de votre navigation, avec 51 pays au choix. SmartClean surveille le processeur, la mémoire et le stockage, et nettoie caches, journaux et fichiers de corbeille. Côté iPhone, la page de l’offre annonce une vérification de ses risques de sécurité.
Dans notre test d’Intego ONE, nous avons salué une interface claire et un VPN convaincant, mais relevé un moteur anti-malware qui occupe environ 1,3 Go de mémoire hors analyse. Sur notre MacBook M1 de 8 Go, un scan complet a duré 26 minutes, avec une latence d’environ une seconde dans les actions courantes. Cette suite convient donc mieux à un Mac récent ou bien doté en mémoire, et moins à un modèle modeste que vous utilisez pendant les analyses.
Intego face aux suites multi-appareils de Bitdefender et Norton
Intego ONE Complete mise sur un Mac et un iPhone, quand Bitdefender Total Security, deuxième de notre comparatif des meilleurs antivirus pour Mac, couvre 3 à 10 appareils et ajoute anti-phishing, anti-ransomware et contrôle parental, trois protections absentes d’Intego ONE. Norton 360, troisième, vise les familles avec 10 appareils. Intego reste pourtant en tête chez nous grâce à sa conception pour macOS et à son VPN. Si vous protégez un seul Mac, c’est l’argument qui compte ; si toute la famille doit être couverte, regardez ailleurs.
✅ Les points forts
- Premier de notre comparatif des antivirus pour Mac, noté 9,6/10
- Note maximale chez AV-TEST en mars 2026
- VPN avec kill switch inclus dans la formule Complete
- Un Mac et un iPhone couverts pour 65 € pendant deux ans
- Garantie satisfait ou remboursé de 30 jours
❌ Les limites
- Renouvellement automatique à 129,99 € tous les deux ans
- Moteur anti-malware lourd en mémoire, scan complet de 26 minutes sur notre Mac de test
- Ni anti-phishing, ni anti-ransomware, ni contrôle parental
- Pare-feu très directif au premier lancement
Si le renouvellement à 129,99 € ne vous freine pas, la garantie de 30 jours satisfait ou remboursé permet d’essayer Intego ONE Complete sur votre propre Mac.
La remise de 50 % se mesure par rapport à 129,99 €, un prix qui est aussi celui du renouvellement. Le gain réel se lit plutôt face au plus bas des 30 derniers jours : 12,99 € de moins, soit près de 17 %. Pour un Mac et un iPhone couverts deux ans, avec antivirus, pare-feu et VPN, la facture de 2,71 € par mois reste mesurée.
Cette offre s’adresse au propriétaire d’un Mac récent qui veut une suite pensée pour macOS, VPN compris, et qui accepte de repasser à 129,99 € au renouvellement. Elle convaincra moins si vous devez protéger plusieurs appareils ou toute une famille, car Bitdefender et Norton en couvrent davantage et ajoutent des protections absentes ici. Avant de payer, notez dans votre agenda la date du renouvellement : c’est à ce moment que le tarif change vraiment.

articles.title: US blacklists Megaspeed, but leaves potential loophole for lower-performance chips — company at center of Jensen Huang affair scandal added to entity list
articles.text:
US blacklists Megaspeed, but leaves potential loophole for lower-performance chips — company at center of Jensen Huang affair scandal added to entity list
But does it make any sense now?
The U.S. Department of Commerce has added Megaspeed and six affiliated entities to its Entity List due to concerns about diversion of advanced AI accelerators to China. However, unlike previous additions of companies suspected of similar activities, the department did not apply a special foreign direct product rule (FDPR) designation to Megaspeed, which raised questions about the effectiveness of the restrictions. While the omission potentially limits the scope of the sanctions, existing U.S. export controls should still restrict Megaspeed's access to advanced processors from AMD and Nvidia. Former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, allegedly a Chinese intelligence asset, is the woman at the heart of the Jensen Huang scandal, which saw Nvidia's CEO resign and then be reinstated as head of the company in recent days.
Chris McGuire, a fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations and a former Biden administration official who dealt with export controls at the National Security Council, noted that neither Megaspeed nor any of the six associated entities received a so-called Footnote 4 designation on the Entity List. According to McGuire, the Department of Commerce had previously applied the designation to Chinese companies blacklisted over concerns about their access to advanced AI processors.
McGuire claims that without the application of the Entity List-specific FDPR, the new restrictions will have essentially no effect on Megaspeed's ability to procure Nvidia's AI processors since, while they are developed in the U.S., the vast majority of them are produced by TSMC in Taiwan.
While McGuire acknowledged that new U.S. export controls that took effect on November 19 already require licenses for shipments of high-end AI accelerators to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil, with exemptions for U.S.-based companies and their subsidiaries (i.e., Google or Microsoft can get Rubin-based machines for their data centers in the said countries, but Megaspeed or other local players cannot), he questioned the rationale behind Megaspeed's addition to the Entity List without Footnote 4.
It is necessary to note that the new country-wide controls impose a license requirement, not an outright ban, whereas the addition of Megaspeed to the Entity List subjects license applications to a presumption of denial, which is a reason why the designation has practical effect even without Footnote 4. Meanwhile, McGuire suggested that the omission could be either a regulatory oversight or a deliberate decision to reduce the scope of restrictions.
Companies on the Entity List typically cannot procure products subject to the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR) without a license from the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS). Such license applications are reviewed with a presumption of denial, and this certainly concerns Megaspeed and entities linked to it. Footnote 4 substantially expands the scope of products subject to the EAR to include foreign-made goods that use American technology or are made using American technologies.
Meanwhile, advanced AI accelerators from AMD and Nvidia are already subject to a separate Advanced Computing FDPR (§734.9(h) of the EAR), which has worldwide geographical coverage irrespective of where the chips are made. In fact, BIS explicitly retained the worldwide scope of this provision in its November 19 amendments to the EAR. Therefore, Megaspeed's addition to the Entity List should effectively cut the company off from qualifying advanced AI accelerators even in the absence of Footnote 4.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
What the absence of Footnote 4 could mean, though, is that Megaspeed may retain access to certain foreign-made lower-performance AI GPUs, networking chips, and other data center hardware that falls outside the scope of the EAR. At this point, it remains unclear whether the Department of Commerce deliberately opted for a narrower set of restrictions.
Meanwhile, Malaysia's Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry announced on Tuesday that it would advise all data center operators in the country against the provision of infrastructure, space, or services to the seven blacklisted entities, a move that could affect Megaspeed's ability to operate its existing AI infrastructure in Malaysia, regardless of the scope of U.S. export restrictions.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Open-weight models are the hottest thing in AI. Are they right for you?
articles.text:
Open-weight models are the hottest thing in AI. Are they right for you?
For the first three years of the generative artificial intelligence boom, enterprise technology strategy relied on a simple rule: Select the premier frontier foundation model, route every prompt through its commercial application programming interface and pay the subscription premium for access to cutting-edge technology.
That monolithic approach is now collapsing under the weight of operational reality. Open-weight models, AI models whose trained parameters, or “weights,” are publicly available for others to download, run, customize and fine-tune, are the overnight sensation in an industry already moving at light speed.
These models don’t necessarily provide access to their training data, source code or training methods. They also carry a variety of license types that may restrict how they can be used commercially. But they offer choice, flexibility and cost advantages that the leading-edge “frontier” models such as OpenAI Group PBC’s ChatGPT and Anthropic PBC’s Claude don’t. For information technology organizations, they can be a respite from spiraling token costs.
Model overkill
The popularity of these models has soared as AI has matured and organizations have realized that not every use case demands the biggest and best solution. They come in various shapes and sizes, ranging from less than 1 billion to nearly 3 trillion parameters. Many are tuned for specific tasks, such as recognizing images or writing software. That gives organizations the flexibility to match the model to the job.
“Frontier intelligence is priced for the hardest problems, and most agent work isn’t hard,” said Dhruv Amin, co-founder of Anything, the business name of Create Inc. and developer of an AI-powered platform for building mobile and web applications. “Companies are chartering a jet to cross the street.”
“There are lots of tasks in customer self-service and employee self-service that need a smaller model,” said Dheeraj Pandey, chief executive officer of DevRev Inc., maker of a unified customer support, software development and engineering platform.
DevRev created an open, vendor-neutral benchmark to measure how reliably enterprise AI agents perform in realistic organizational environments. “We get almost the same accuracy and precision on enterprise tasks, whether you use the open-weight models or the frontier models,” he said.
The ascendancy of open-weight models has been breathtaking. Vercel Inc.’s monthly AI Gateway report found that their share of observed token traffic surged from 7% last December to 56% in August and that the models held eight of the 10 busiest spots on OpenRouter Inc.’s large language model ranking in August by token volume.
Three-year-old OpenRouter itself turned heads in August when it sold to Stripe Inc. for an eye-popping $7.5 billion. The firm’s technology connects developers and users with hundreds of AI models from dozens of providers through a single interface.
In September, Nvidia Corp. paid nearly $13 billion for Hugging Face Inc., which hosts more than 3 million models. “For most enterprises, the practical path to an open-weight model — evaluate, fine-tune, quantize, deploy — runs through that hub,” wrote Zeus Kerravala, principal analyst at ZK Research, referring to Hugging Face.
Cost concerns
Enterprises aren’t abandoning frontier models. Rather, they’re learning to fit the model to the problem. None of the experts SiliconANGLE contacted believes open-weight models are a threat to the big players.
“All players can win because the market is growing and the number of places where it makes sense to deploy AI increases,” Amin said.
Cost is currently the principal driver of open-weight adoption. As AI use has evolved from question-and-response generative models to sophisticated multistep agentic workflows, inference costs have soared. Gartner Inc. predicts inference costs per agentic workflow will increase more than fivefold through 2028.
“They are quickly starting to rival even payroll expenses,” Amin said.
By most accounts, frontier models still offer the greatest power and range of usage options. But the gap is closing. Mozilla’s September State of Open-Source AI report put the capability gap between leading open-weight models and proprietary frontier models at roughly four months, down from 18 months just two years ago.
“The differences in quality are starting to be outweighed by the differences in cost,” wrote Ioana Hreninciuc, co-founder of inference platform Runware Ltd. She noted that though proprietary models still lead on top-tier reasoning, “you probably don’t need a frontier model for 80% of what you do.”
Hidden expenses
The pivot to open weights isn’t a zero-sum proposition. Low token prices can mask integration overhead, tool failures and operational risk. “Tokenomics,” or measuring, attributing and managing the cost of tokens, has become an essential information technology discipline.
In a Hyper Labs Inc. survey conducted by The Harris Poll, 86% of AI leaders said managing token expenses is as critical as containing cloud costs. More than three-quarters said they are directing routine tasks to smaller models to protect budgets, while 89% have redesigned AI initiatives after getting token shock.
“The whole world is trying to solve for tokenomics,” said Armando Franco, senior director of cloud and platform modernization at IT services provider TEKsystems Inc.
Experts say open-weight models are well-suited for repetitive, routine workloads. “Basically, they work best when the task is clear and it’s easy enough to check if the work was done correctly,” said Louis Amira, CEO of Circuit & Chisel Inc., an AI infrastructure and agentic commerce startup.
Karen Panetta, an IEEE Fellow and dean of graduate education at Tufts University School of Engineering, said open models are flourishing as technology leaders learn to match the engine to the task.
“If a bicycle will get you there, don’t pick the expensive sports car,” she said. “You have to ask: What problem you are trying to solve?” She asserted that for applications that don’t require 99.9% precision, organizations can achieve massive savings with compact models.
They’re also an attractive option when protecting customer data is a priority, since sensitive information never needs to leave the organization. “Customer data never, never goes into a frontier,” Scott Wallace, senior global director of solutions architecture at Digital Realty Inc., said in an interview with the Financial Times.
Sovereignty, or the ability to control and govern digital assets in line with local laws, security needs, and strategic interests, is a growing issue for organizations. A Linux Foundation survey last year found that 79% of AI leaders — and 86% in the U.S. — rate sovereignty as a strategic priority.
“What began as a specialized concern for highly regulated industries is rapidly becoming a strategic consideration for nearly every enterprise,” Paul Nashawaty, a principal analyst at theCUBE Research, wrote in a recent analysis.
Some early adopters are demonstrating impressive returns.
- AT&T Corp. shifted 40% of its AI workloads to open models and plans to grow that share to 70%, according to The Information. By delegating tasks such as code summarization to cheaper engines and using a router to direct work to the most efficient model, the telecom giant cut AI operating costs by 56% with only a 2% decline in quality.
- Pinterest Inc. achieved over 90% cost savings on its AI operations by moving away from frontier models, said William Ready said on the company’s second fiscal quarter earnings call in August.
- Uber Technologies Inc., which unexpectedly burned through an entire year’s AI budget in the first four months of this year, has cut model requests by one-third and costs per session by over half since February, largely by shifting more workloads to open-weight models.
Advocates point to a shrinking capability gap, too, with some open-weight models nipping at the heels of the frontier alternatives. Beijing Moonshot AI Technology Co., Ltd.’s 2.8 trillion-parameter Kimi K3 model and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s 2.4 trillion-parameter Qwen3.8-Max nearly match closed models on coding benchmarks, according to Stanford University’s Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence Institute.
An agent built by Tenzai Inc. recently captured the top spot on HackerOne’s leaderboard using Z.ai Inc.’s GLM 5.2, generating 30% more findings per unit of computing power than a previous baseline using a proprietary model.
“What was the frontier 18 months ago is now well-mapped territory, and open-source models are closing the gap at a fraction of the cost” wrote Runware’s Hreninciuc.
Open weight ≠ open source
Though such metrics explain open models’ ascendancy, the decision to use them isn’t open-and-shut. Experts cite four common myths that can mitigate the cost efficiencies.
One is the mistaken belief that open-weight models conflate with traditional open-source software and its permissive licenses. “This is a misnomer among many enterprises,” said Dr. Dorotea Baljević, EMEA Lead for AI Advisory at technology research and advisory firm Information Services Group. “There is licensing for these models in most cases, particularly for commercial usage.”
Although some, such as Qwen3, Mistral 3, Gemma 4 and DeepSeek V4, are covered by standard Apache or MIT licenses, terms and conditions vary. For example, Liquid AI Inc.’s open-weight models are free for commercial use only to organizations with less than $10 million in annual revenue.
“Other licenses require attribution, restrict certain application categories, or impose acceptable use policies, none of which carry a direct fee but all of which create legal exposure if ignored,” noted Bumu Technologies Inc., which does business as Nanobase.
Baljević said two hidden liabilities are data distribution rights for public training datasets used upstream and the evaluation, stability and legal audit costs that shift directly to the enterprise. “When using open-weight models, you need to lean in on understanding data distribution rights, copyright, contractual restrictions and consent,” she said. “In most cases, this carries costs.”
Evaluating models for accuracy, stability and explainability also falls to the user. With thousands of open-weight models available, the costs of a bake-off between multiple candidates can add up.
Baljević suggests organizations consider whether the model will be used internally or externally, the organization’s tolerance for accuracy, strategic fit and switching costs as evaluation criteria. Performance on public benchmarks also doesn’t guarantee a model will work well with an organization’s data, workflows and language.
More than tokens
Finance leaders may look at the 80% to 90% cost advantage of open-weight tokens and assume operational expenditures will drop proportionally. But tokens are only one part of the cost equation and not necessarily even the biggest one.
Organizations that plan to deploy models on their own infrastructure must bear the costs of integration, API development, IT infrastructure and human labor required for auditing and verification. A fraction of a cent saved on an inference call can be wiped out by the cost of a human expert spending a half-hour re-entering flawed database transactions.
Lack of visibility into how the model is operating can also produce sticker shock. A retry loop, in which an agent tries repeatedly to complete a failed task, can go on for hours or even days. The Wall Street Journal recently reported on a case in which an AI-generated out-of-office message at a San Francisco-based software company went into a loop that ultimately burned $10,000 a day in token costs.
If a cheap open-weight model fails a multi-system query or generates invalid JSON, it triggers automated retries that can consume millions of secondary tokens. The human expertise required to repair the transaction manually can erase months of token savings.
“The core software engineering required to test and integrate new models into the software stack is often the biggest hurdle, since not all frontier models have the same capabilities, APIs and such,” said Alex Bakker, an ISG distinguished analyst. “The frontier labs tend to maintain more consistency in their upgrade paths.”
Self-hosting isn’t always cheaper
Using private graphics processing unit clusters eliminates external API fees, but self-hosting economics hinge on high, sustained utilization. Models that sit idle or at low usage levels consume power, create processing inefficiencies and incur costs if restarts are required.
Cast AI Group Inc. reported last spring that the average GPU utilization was 5% across thousands of clusters it monitored. Frontier models are usually a better option in that case. “Open models can be dramatically cheaper at high utilization, while frontier APIs remain cheaper for intermittent workloads because you aren’t paying for idle capacity,” said Arun Chandrasekaran, distinguished VP analyst at Gartner.
For intermittent workloads such as batch payroll processing or seasonal financial reporting, the organization pays 100% of capital expenses, power, cooling and depreciation while hardware idles.
“On-premises hosting wins when there is high, predictable 24/7 traffic where servers are constantly busy,” said Debojyoti Dutta, chief AI officer at Nutanix Inc. A hosted frontier model is a better choice “with spiky or lower traffic, where paying per token with zero setup cost is cheaper than renting idle hardware.”
Model-swapping fallacy
When AI agents fail, the default reaction is to switch to a newer model, but benchmark data shows that approach is usually a dead end.
Most evaluation tests give agents relatively simple tasks and judge them mainly on whether they get the right answer. But real business environments are much more complicated. Agents must gather information from different systems, connect it correctly, handle growing amounts of data, and work within security rules.
This interface complexity is what usually breaks AI agents. DevRev estimates that moving an agent from clean test tools to real-world corporate use causes an 18% to 19% drop in accuracy. Upgrading the model improves performance by less than 1%.
“Every time a new model comes out, you need to re-evaluate your benchmarks, your models and your fine-tuning processes,” said Steven Yang, senior director of product management at Tanium Inc. That means better data integration is a more effective strategy than buying new models.
When open-weight makes sense
Though the open-weight option is viable for any company, experts say the best use cases are those where control, accountability and performance are paramount. The following three factors are at least as important as cost.
Compliance: Regulated industries have been held back from adopting AI over data residency and confidentiality concerns. Deploying open weights within enterprise data centers or virtual private clouds reduces the need for external data egress, ensures zero training data retention and allows for total physical isolation. The models also allow inspection of internal mechanics such as log-probabilities, token confidence scores and loss landscapes.
Training datasets, model weights and inference prompts never cross borders or leave the organization’s physical perimeter. That makes it easier to comply with strict data localization laws such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act in the U.S. and the General Data Protection Regulation in Europe. Local auditing and observability also aid in compliance with regulatory frameworks like the EU AI Act, which requires detailed logging, risk assessments and explainability.
But deploying on private infrastructure isn’t a cure-all. “You still have to maintain an aggressive data security posture around your processes because even open-weight models sometimes will take action trying to accomplish their tasks that could potentially violate some type of compliance rule,” said TEKSystems’ Franco.
Transparency: Understanding how models arrive at an answer is critical in many scenarios, particularly those involving safety, law and finance. “Open-weight models expose the math behind their answers,” said Brian Weiss, chief technology officer at document processing platform maker Hyperscience, the business name of Hyper Labs Inc. “You can use that to hold the model accountable for accuracy.”
In contrast, frontier APIs often obscure the equations used to generate probabilities, which are critical to assessing accuracy. Asking a model how confident it is in its answer may yield a subjective response. Open weights allow confidence scores to be scored against ground-truth outcomes for better reliability.
“People can take these models inside their organization, do some post-training and fine-tuning and have a customized model where they know the costs, where it’s sitting and what data is being sent to it,” said David DeSanto, CEO of Anaconda Inc., maker of an AI development platform.
“The future is an orchestrated ensemble of bounded, transparent, governed, cost-effective models,” Weiss said. “If I find a better model for a particular task, I can swap it out because I have the framework to do that.”
Performance: As organizations move from the relatively simple generative AI question-and-response metaphor to sophisticated multi-agent frameworks, latency issues can compound exponentially. For example, a 500-millisecond API delay across 50 sequential reasoning steps creates 25 seconds of cumulative latency, which would render many applications useless.
Executing open-weight models directly alongside operational databases or within containerized edge pods minimizes routing hops and rate limits. Distillation, which trains smaller, specialized open models from frontier “teacher” models, is faster.
Hyperscience reported that distillation delivers up to 97% cost reduction and four times faster inference, while retaining over 95% of the original model’s performance on designated tasks. Small models are faster and considerably cheaper than frontier LLMs.
Are open-weight models for you?
Experts say constructing a business case for open-weight models requires understanding three major sources of hidden expense.
Complexity tax: Reasoning can break down when open-weight models interact with complex enterprise data at scale. The “Cartesian Shortcut” refers to a phenomenon in which AI models rely on workarounds learned during training rather than demonstrating a flexible understanding of the problem they’re trying to solve.
Google LLC researchers found that the models struggled with visual reasoning problems, such as solving mazes, when the data was presented in a circular rather than a grid layout. Leading models answered 69% to 83% of the square-grid problems correctly, but their accuracy fell to below 40% when the problems appeared in circular layouts.
Source: Google DeepMind
The corollary to a business scenario is a multihop join across multiple systems. Models may “cheat” by collapsing field-level relationships into hierarchical groupings, generating massive data fabrications.
Human oversight remains critical: “For validation and rework, humans in the loop need to be taken into account on top of all the tokens you’re paying for already,” said TekSystems’ Franco.
Poor data quality: Foundation models can’t fix bad data, a fact that’s holding back AI adoption across the board. The Hyperscience/Harris Poll study found that 86% of IT leaders said dirty internal data is actively crippling GenAI performance.
Feeding error-strewn or outdated information into probabilistic models creates “context pollution,” the accumulation of irrelevant, redundant, outdated or contradictory information. When agents execute multistep database joins, system workflows or automated tool calls based on flawed data or ambiguous schemas, cascading errors can occur.
Sauce Labs Inc. Chief Technology Officer Anoop Tripathi recommends creating validated “golden datasets” for fine-tuning and evaluation. He also cautions architects against misapplying probabilistic AI to structured business logic. In other words, use models only where they add value and apply conventional (and cheaper) data processing to everything else.
Continuous evaluation: Selecting the right model out of thousands of open-weight alternatives requires ongoing evaluation against internal workloads rather than public leaderboards. That demands expensive MLOps, site reliability engineering and platform engineering skills.
Because new models are constantly being introduced and revised, Circuit & Chisel’s Amira recommends building custom testing harnesses that can quickly evaluate candidate models against business-relevant tasks.
Rather than treating open-weight adoption as an all-or-nothing choice, enterprise architects should bucket organizational tasks into distinct operational tiers. Don’t feed every problem into a token-hungry trillion-parameter model if a smaller, specialized one will do the trick.
“Organizations don’t give a heavyweight reasoning model a lightweight sorting job,” said Nutanix’s Dutta. “They divide their business workloads into tiers based on cost, speed and hardware footprint.”
Lower-tier workloads such as search, embeddings and document classification work well with inexpensive, compact open-weight and small language models. Sophisticated tasks such as autonomous reasoning and restructuring large, deeply entangled legacy software systems are better suited to commercial alternatives.
ISG’s Bakker believes the need for constant evaluation is the biggest impediment to open-weight adoption. “The core software engineering required to test and integrate new models into the software stack will likely be the biggest hurdle, since not all frontier models have the same capabilities and APIs,” he said. “The frontier labs tend to maintain more consistency in their upgrade paths.”
Enterprise IT organizations must develop expertise in local model execution, containerized execution sandboxes and agent harness orchestration. Managing AI and agents safely “is, in the near future, going to be as important an indigenous knowledge as how to upgrade Windows,” said Gordon Allott, founder and CEO of private infrastructure provider nFOX Lab.
The shift toward open-weight models represents a permanent maturation of enterprise IT from experimentation to disciplined financial and architectural management. Success is no longer about raw model parameter size or benchmark ranking, but matching the model to the task. That’s a discipline that was barely on the roadmap a year ago.
At the start of the year, there was no way enterprises were going to touch open-weight models, Brad Maltz, head of AI factory solutions at Dell Technologies Inc., said in a November interview on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE’s streaming media platform. “People were pretty wrong about that. I think the open-weight movement is the future.”

articles.title: Strava met à jour son application Wear OS avec deux fonctionnalités très attendues
articles.text:
Sur Apple Watch, Strava permet de suivre ses itinéraires directement au poignet depuis janvier 2026. Les montres sous Wear OS, le système de Google qui équipe notamment les Galaxy Watch et les Pixel Watch, comblent cet écart.
    Pour aller plus loin
Quelles sont les meilleures montres connectées en novembre 2026 ?
            
Dans un e-mail envoyé à ses utilisateurs ce mercredi 25 novembre, Strava a annoncé l’arrivée des Live Segments et du suivi d’itinéraire, après une mise à jour publiée deux jours plus tôt sur le Google Play Store.
Les Live Segments intégrés aux montres Wear OS
Pour rappel, les segments Strava sont des portions de route ou de sentier sur lesquelles les sportifs comparent leurs temps. Avec les Live Segments, quand vous approchez d’un segment mis en favori, la montre vous prévient, puis affiche en direct si vous êtes en avance ou en retard sur votre record personnel.
Sur le papier, Strava promet dans son e-mail que vous connaîtrez votre avance ou votre retard « à la seconde près ». Dans les faits, sa page d’aide consacrée à Wear OS précise que seuls les abonnés voient cet écart chiffré. Les comptes gratuits savent uniquement s’ils sont devant ou derrière leur record, avec un arc de progression qui se remplit le long du segment.
Des itinéraires planifiés avant de sortir
Les itinéraires fonctionnent de la même façon : ceux créés dans l’application sur smartphone se synchronisent tout seuls avec la montre, mais l’enregistrement d’itinéraires est réservé aux abonnés. Quant aux alertes qui préviennent quand vous sortez du parcours, Strava les annonce seulement comme « bientôt disponibles », sans date précise.
L’application demande une montre sous Wear OS 3.0 ou plus récent, ce qui inclut les Galaxy Watch 4 et suivantes, les Pixel Watch et les OnePlus Watch.

articles.title: Fuite de données chez 1Password : faut-il changer vos mots de passe de toute urgence ?
articles.text:
1Password a été piraté. Dans une alerte publiée ce 25 novembre, le célèbre gestionnaire de mots de passe révèle avoir été victime d’une intrusion dans ses systèmes internes. L’intrusion a été détectée quelques jours plus tôt. Le 19 novembre, 1Password « a commencé à enquêter sur des indices selon lesquels un attaquant avait obtenu l’accès au compte GitHub professionnel d’un employé ».
Quelles données ont été volées à 1Password ?
Après avoir pris le contrôle du compte, le pirate en a profité « pour accéder au code source et pousser du code malveillant vers des services internes, explique 1Password. Ensuite, l’attaquant a « téléchargé des données administratives concernant nos clients » et « copié du code source de dépôts privés ». Dès que l’attaque a été enregistrée, l’entreprise a « révoqué le jeton volé », remplacé tous ses identifiants internes exposés et fait appel à des experts indépendants.
Parmi les données compromises dans l’incident, on trouve des noms et adresses e-mail, des identifiants de comptes, des dates de création et de dernière connexion. Par ailleurs, des « jetons », présents dans certains liens d’invitation et de récupération de compte, ont aussi été siphonnés. Ces jetons ne donnent pas accès au compte de la victime. Il faut aussi un code envoyé par e-mail, qui passe par précaution de six chiffres à dix caractères, rendant « pratiquement impossible » toute tentative de le deviner.
1Password assure n’avoir trouvé « aucune preuve interne de prise de contrôle de comptes ». L’entreprise ne précise pas combien de clients sont concernés. Pour rappel, 1Password revendique des millions d’utilisateurs et plus de 200 000 entreprises clientes.
Pourquoi vos mots de passe sont encore en sécurité
Le gestionnaire de mots de passe se veut rassurant. Selon la société, « à aucun moment le contenu des coffres des clients n’a été accessible à l’attaquant ». De facto, le pirate n’a pas pu s’emparer des mots de passe stockés par les utilisateurs. Pour résister aux tentatives de vol, 1Password chiffre vos mots de passe directement sur votre appareil. Pour les déchiffrer, il faut votre mot de passe principal et votre « clé secrète », un code de 34 caractères. Or, 1Password ne stocke ni l’un ni l’autre sur ses systèmes, justement pour éviter les attaques.
« Vos secrets sont chiffrés avec des clés que vous seul détenez, nous ne pouvons donc pas y accéder, et un attaquant qui s’introduit dans nos serveurs non plus », souligne l’entreprise.
Non, il ne faut pas changer vos mots de passe d’urgence
De facto, il n’est pas nécessaire de changer tous vos mots de passe. Les coffres, ainsi que les clés qui les protègent, n’ont pas été compromis. Les clients n’ont donc pas besoin de modifier les mots de passe ou les réglages de leur compte. La fuite de données n’est cependant pas sans conséquence.
En effet, une pluie d’attaques phishing risque de déferler sur les personnes concernées. Avec les noms et les adresses e-mail des clients, des pirates pourraient envoyer de faux messages très crédibles, taillés pour subtiliser vos coordonnées bancaires, vos mots de passe ou d’autres données. 1Password appelle à se méfier des « e-mails, SMS ou appels inattendus qui mentionnent 1Password, des invitations ou des tentatives de récupération de compte ». L’entreprise ajoute qu’elle ne « vous contactera jamais pour vous demander le mot de passe de votre compte ou votre clé secrète ».
C’est la première fois que 1Password subit une violation de données. En 2023, l’entreprise avait bien repéré une activité suspecte liée au piratage d’Okta, un prestataire de gestion des identités, mais aucune donnée client n’avait été compromise. L’an dernier, des pirates avaient aussi visé des utilisateurs avec un faux mail d’alerte, mais, là encore, aucune information n’avait réellement été subtilisée.

articles.title: Hackers breach CIA system in possible ARTEX cyberattack and leak unclassified data
articles.text:
Hackers breach CIA system in possible ARTEX cyberattack and leak unclassified data
Three US spy agencies were broken into
- Attackers breached unclassified intelligence-analysis systems used by multiple US intelligence agencies and exfiltrated collected data
- Officials said classified information was not compromised, and the affected systems primarily contained open-source intelligence material
- Investigators are examining possible China-linked involvement, with reports highlighting use of the AI-powered ARTEX reconnaissance platform
The US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, were recently breached by what appear to be Chinese hackers, who got away with some data, but fortunately it appears to be nothing classified.
The New York Times, citing multiple US officials and other people familiar with the matter, reported that threat actors broke into an open source intelligence analysis system - essentially a network that harvests public, unclassified material, and turns it into actionable intelligence - and took the data found there.
In other words, these are all information available to anyone, these agencies just scraped them and likely built a narrative around them.
ARTEX is the talk of the town
We don’t know what the nature of the stolen files is. We don’t know if those are names or emails, but the publication stressed that classified material was not jeopardized. We also don’t know exactly how the incident played out, but we do know some of the tools that were used, ARTEX being one of them.
ARTEX has been making headlines for several weeks now - recently as news broke of cybercriminals using the tool to break into the European Commission, and even forcing the organization to pull a few apps offline, namely Sysper, the Commission’s human resources platform that employees use to access payroll information, leave requests, and work hour logs, and MyPMO, a medical reimbursement system.
A few weeks before that, security researchers Censys reported finding more than a thousand of ARTEX instances readily available for anyone who knew where to look. Many were also running other known hacking tools alongside it.
ARTEX started out as a legitimate penetration testing tool, only to later be hijacked for malicious purposes, similar to what happened to Cobalt Strike, for example. The tool was released in the summer of 2025 by a developer called Autumn-27. This author, who appears to be Chinese, first built ScopeSentry, a tool security researchers described as a “widely used Chinese asset-discovery and vulnerability-scanning platform.”
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
They then added an AI agent layer on top of that tool, and thus ARTEX was born. In other words - it is an LLM-powered version of Scope Sentry that syncs assets found by the tool’s domains, subdomains, IPs, ports, and endpoints.
Who is the world's biggest cyber-bully?
ARTEX was released in late July 2026 and quickly gained popularity. On October 7, security researchers CrowdStrike reported seeing it used in malicious attacks and a day later, the developer distanced themselves from the illicit activity and stressed the tool was built for testing within authorized asset scopes. They then turned it into a closed-source tool with no further releases.
However, despite the repository being taken down, Censys claims archived copies, translations, and different rebrands are still circulating.
At the time of publication, no one claimed responsibility for the attack on the CIA and other spy agencies. NYT says initial signs, including the use of ARTEX, suggests that China may be behind it. For this information it cited two of the people who are familiar with the breach.
For years, security researchers and law enforcement agencies have been pointing the finger at China, warning about malicious activities such as cyber-espionage or data theft, aimed at western enterprises and governments. In fact, this is one of the reasons why US President Donald Trump barred American companies from doing business with many Chinese tech firms such as Huawei or ZTE.
China, on the other hand, vehemently denies all such claims, describing them as baseless allegations, and instead saying it’s the US government that’s acting as the world’s biggest cyber-bully.

articles.title: Un dron de Amazon chocó contra un garaje durante una entrega en Michigan y la FAA abrió una investigación
articles.text:
La Administración Federal de Aviación de Estados Unidos (FAA) abrió una investigación después de que un dron de Amazon chocó contra un garaje durante una entrega en Huntington Woods, Michigan.
El aparato, que acababa de dejar una botella de champú en el patio de un cliente, golpeó un cable de fibra óptica al despegar, perdió una hélice y terminó atrapado entre líneas eléctricas. No hubo heridos.
El incidente ocurrió el viernes 20 de noviembre, cerca de las 16:30, hora local, en este suburbio de Detroit. El informe preliminar de la autoridad aeronáutica señala que la aeronave no tripulada impactó un cable de fibra, una vivienda con garaje y quedó enredada en el tendido eléctrico durante el despegue.
Ahora, la agencia deberá determinar ahora las causas del hecho y si corresponde adoptar medidas regulatorias.
El MK30 entregó el paquete y perdió una hélice al iniciar el ascenso
El vehículo de Prime Air, el servicio de entregas aéreas de Amazon, dejó el pedido en el patio trasero de la vivienda de Jim Brennan. Según el testimonio del residente recogido por CNBC, el dron rozó un cable de fibra óptica cuando retomaba altura y una de sus hélices resultó dañada.
Brennan había recibido una notificación que indicaba que el envío llegaría por aire y salió a observar el recorrido. En el video que registró, el aparato se balancea y se desplaza sin estabilidad antes de caer sobre el garaje de una propiedad vecina. El paquete, una botella de champú encargada por su esposa, sí había sido entregado.
El dueño del garaje, Logan Coomes, dijo a la cadena local WXYZ que el impacto desplazó algunas tejas y dejó una parte del techo expuesta. El dron quedó inmovilizado entre la estructura y los cables de electricidad, una situación que obligó a intervenir a técnicos de la empresa eléctrica.
La FAA analiza el accidente y la NTSB reúne información
La FAA confirmó que investiga el accidente. Su informe preliminar no atribuye todavía el suceso a una causa concreta ni informa el estado final de la aeronave.
La revisión federal busca establecer cómo se produjo el contacto con la infraestructura residencial y si la operación cumplió con las condiciones aplicables al vuelo.
La Junta Nacional de Seguridad en el Transporte (NTSB, por sus siglas en inglés) conoce el caso y recopila datos, pero aún no decidió si abrirá una pesquisa propia.
Amazon indicó que retiró el dispositivo y que se puso en contacto con los residentes afectados. Jack Stelzner, portavoz de la compañía, afirmó que la seguridad es la prioridad de la empresa y que cada entrega que no se desarrolla según lo previsto es objeto de análisis.
Para retirar el equipo, la distribuidora DTE Energy interrumpió temporalmente una línea de acometida. Un equipo de Amazon llegó poco después del impacto, aunque la recuperación del dron demandó cerca de tres horas, según los reportes locales.
La compañía ofreció colaborar con las reparaciones del techo y entregó tarjetas de regalo de USD 100 a Brennan y a algunos vecinos afectados.
El accidente ocurre durante la expansión de las entregas aéreas de Amazon
El modelo involucrado es el MK30, una aeronave de reparto capaz de transportar pedidos de hasta 2,3 kilogramos. Amazon sostiene que el sistema utiliza cámaras, sensores y mecanismos de navegación redundantes para detectar obstáculos y realizar los vuelos autónomos.
El caso se produjo mientras la empresa busca que Prime Air opere en casi 500 ciudades y localidades de Estados Unidos antes de que concluya 2026.
Amazon afirma que el servicio efectúa cerca de 6.000 entregas diarias y que acumuló cientos de miles de paquetes distribuidos este año. Esos objetivos de expansión y los antecedentes del programa fueron informados por Arstechnica.
La operación de los drones de reparto cuenta con certificación Parte 135 de la FAA, pero el programa ha afrontado retrasos regulatorios, dificultades técnicas y cuestionamientos de comunidades cercanas a sus zonas de prueba.
En octubre de 2025, dos unidades MK30 chocaron contra una grúa de construcción en Arizona y los vuelos se suspendieron de forma temporal; un mes más tarde, otro dron derribó un cable de internet en Waco, Texas. Las investigaciones sobre esos episodios también quedaron en manos de autoridades federales.

articles.title: Black Week: IPhone 17 Pro Max (512 GB) tem a melhor oferta que já vimos
articles.text:
Black Week: IPhone 17 Pro Max (512 GB) tem a melhor oferta que já vimos
iPhone 17 Pro Max (512 GB) com chip A19 Pro e suporte local ao Apple Intelligence sai 32% mais em conta na semana da Black Friday 2026, com desconto no Pix na Amazon
O iPhone 17 Pro Max de 512 GB está saindo por R$ 9.499 no Pix na Amazon. O celular premium da Apple, equipado com câmeras de 48 MP e tela OLED de 120 Hz, alcança o menor preço publicado pelo Achados, com desconto de 32% sobre o original de R$ 13.999.
Embora continue caro, o gadget alcança na Black Friday 2026 um preço menor que o do iPhone 17 Pro de 512 GB, e fica bem abaixo da média recente.
Esta oferta é o menor preço que já encontramos para o iPhone 17 Pro Max 512 GB. Nas outras 7 ofertas publicadas desde janeiro de 2026, o melhor foi R$ 9.796,76 (Mercado Livre, 1/10/2026).
Um dos melhores celulares da Apple, o iPhone 17 Pro Max possui uma tela Super Retina XDR OLED de 6,9″ com ProMotion de 120 Hz e brilho de até 3.000 nits. Tal combinação a permite reproduzir imagens com cores fiéis, alta fluidez e visibilidade garantida.
Seu chip A19 Pro e os 12 GB de RAM suportam apps pesados em multitarefa, games exigentes e soluções do Apple Intelligence localmente. Os 512 GB de espaço interno dão e sobram para guardar vídeos e fotos.
O kit de câmeras inclui wide com OIS e ultrawide com ângulo de 120º, que captam belas cenas ao ar livre, e telefoto com zoom óptico de 3x para aproximações, todas de 48 MP. A frontal de 18 MP tira ótimas selfies no modo Paisagem, mesmo segurando o celular em pé.
O corpo de alumínio do iPhone 17 Pro Max é revestido de ambos os lados pelo vidro Ceramic Shield, resistente contra pancadas e quedas. A certificação IP68 confere proteção em cenários como poeira intensa e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 4.832 mAh resiste a até 37 horas de reprodução de vídeo, segundo a fabricante. O suporte a MagSafe e carregamento rápido de 40 W via USB-C permitem receber uma carga de 50% com um carregador de 40 W (vendido separadamente).
O iPhone 17 Pro Max de 512 GB (R$ 9.499 no Pix) foi atualizado para o iOS 27 e deve receber pelo menos mais cinco updates do sistema operacional. O celular da Apple possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0, NFC e suporta eSIM.
A Black Friday 2026 chega nesta sexta-feira (27), mas você já pode desde já aproveitar diversas ofertas de gadgets com cupons e condições especiais, que lojas como a Amazon oferecem por todo o mês de novembro.
Acompanhe o Achados no Telegram ou WhatsApp e aproveite todas as promoções.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Seoul Semiconductor Enables Beyond-OLED Picture Quality with LCD
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Seoul Semiconductor Enables Beyond-OLED Picture Quality with LCD
Seoul Semiconductor Co., Ltd., a global opto-semiconductor company, today announced that its 'WICOP Pixel'—the world's first package-free technology, developed by its subsidiary Seoul Viosys—arranges RGB chips at an ultra-fine pitch of several tens of micrometers (µm) to render tens of thousands of colors. Replacing conventional white-light LCD backlights, the technology achieves 100% of DCI-P3 color gamut, the international film industry standard for reproducing natural colors, while delivering more than three times the brightness of OLED displays. The company has entered full-scale mass production and begun expanding supply to global TV manufacturers.
Seoul Semiconductor's display-related revenue in the third quarter rose nearly 20% year-over-year. To meet capacity needs across the global market, the company plans to convert its existing white backlight light-source capacity to WICOP Pixel production rather than make large new investments, while expanding both revenue and profit through a global patent licensing program. In this way, it will support stable production for its customers while generating royalty income, which it plans to invest in expanded research and development in future fields such as biotechnology, 3D printing, AR and AI data communications.The core of the 'WICOP Pixel' RGB backlight technology is that, while using a standard LCD panel, it reproduces natural colors and scenes more faithfully than OLED and heightens immersion even in bright settings such as living rooms and public spaces. This strengthens its appeal for home-theater TVs and raises product value and profitability for TV manufacturers. In addition, it reduces dependence on expensive LCD panels, and to cut costs further, the company is also researching technology to eliminate the color filter, which accounts for about 20% of LCD panel material costs.
The technology also covers 100% of the DCI-P3 color gamut, the international standard for digital cinema, enabling richer, more vivid color than OLED. Its peak brightness of up to 3,000 nits is more than three times that of OLED, delivering sharp images and strong immersion even in bright indoor and outdoor environments. Experts expect this to further strengthen TV's role as home theaters and to deliver clear images even in bright public spaces. It also offers more than twice the lifespan of OLED.
According to a market research firm Omdia, the shift to RGB backlights—the category that WICOP Pixel technology addresses—is accelerating. Global RGB TV shipments, led by the large-screen premium segment, are expected to reach about 7 million units by 2030, representing more than 10% of global TV market revenue. As the current white-backlight market of about USD 3 billion shifts to RGB, the market is expected to more than double in size with the adoption of Advanced Packaging technology.
- DCI-P3 (Digital Cinema Initiatives - P3): An international color gamut standard used in the digital cinema industry that defines the range of colors a display can reproduce. 100% DCI-P3 coverage means a display can reproduce the standard's entire color gamut.
- BT.2020: An international standard for ultra-high-definition video established by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU).
- WICOP Pixel: Seoul Viosys' WICOP is the world's first opto-semiconductor technology that achieves a robust chip structure without a separate package, allowing it to be used like an ordinary electronic component. The WICOP technology previously applied to blue opto-semiconductors has been extended to all wavelengths, including green, red and UV. WICOP Pixel integrates multiple wavelengths, such as red, green and blue, into a single pixel unit. Each color is controlled independently and combined precisely, reproducing tens of thousands of natural colors efficiently and vividly.
Source:
				Seoul Semiconductor
