articles.title: Google's AI Mode can now read your Wallet and Drive if you let it
articles.text:
Editor's take: Google recently announced a tighter integration between its AI-powered Search service and other apps from the company. The idea is that users will enjoy a better, more personalized experience if they opt to surrender some of their most personal data to the advertising giant.
Google is bringing its Personal Intelligence feature to even more apps and services. The feature, which was introduced in Google Search's AI Mode earlier this year, can pull personal data from multiple apps to further customize the chatbot-like search experience. The Mountain View corporation is now expanding this integration, starting with the option to connect Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, with Drive to follow in the coming weeks.
Robby Stein, Google's VP for Search, explained that a more connected Search should provide users with unique insights into their digital life. After connecting Wallet to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, users can track their financial "milestones" or get useful advice on ways to improve their spending.
Other options include maximizing credit card benefits based on the cards saved in Wallet. Google highlights that AI Mode can read financial data from a user's accounts, but cannot move, manage, or invest money on their behalf. Once Drive support arrives, Personal Intelligence in AI Mode will scan PDFs, documents, and other files in the user's cloud storage stash to contextualize answers, suggest ideas, and more.
Finally, in the coming weeks, there will be yet another option for sharing "context" across Gemini and AI Mode in Search. Users will be able to start chatting in the Gemini app and then continue the chatbot interaction in Search's AI Mode – or vice versa. Users could already connect their Search history to Personal Intelligence in the Gemini app, but they will now be able to go the other way around by connecting Gemini to AI Mode.
Google explains that these new contextualization features are strictly opt-in, which means they must be manually enabled before the company's AI models start ransacking users' data. Furthermore, the deeper integration can be disabled at a later date. Google also says AI Overviews and AI Mode will deliver more personalized and relevant responses based on the user's recent search context.
Google is clearly trying to turn its traditional search service into a personal, all-knowing digital assistant that users won't be able to do without in the future.
The advertising corporation is apparently willing to give up its web search golden goose to push AI Mode onto more users, even though the search chatbot is still earning less money than traditional search, as Google acknowledged on its latest earnings call.

articles.title: Microsoft decreta "Código Vermelho" após apagão no Outlook
articles.text:
Microsoft decreta “Código Vermelho” após apagão no Outlook
Documentos internos revelam que Microsoft criou a estratégia "Code Red" para evitar novos apagões graves como o que afetou o Outlook em 12 de novembro.
O “apagão” no Outlook e serviços relacionados que aconteceu em 12 de novembro continua mobilizando a Microsoft. Como parte de um plano que visa evitar que um problema tão ou mais sério ocorra novamente, a companhia decretou uma estratégia de reação sob o codinome “Code Red” (“Código Vermelho”).
É o que revela a Reuters, que afirma ter tido acesso a memorandos internos da companhia sobre o assunto. Uma denominação tão pomposa nos faz pensar em um estado de alerta temporário ou em uma ferramenta de segurança ativada às pressas. Mas não é o caso. Na verdade, a iniciativa estabelece a execução de cinco frentes de trabalho principais para prevenir incidentes tão graves como o do último dia 12. São elas:
- melhorar o gerenciamento de carga: os sistemas da Microsoft devem suspender ou limitar a execução de cargas de trabalho com menos prioridade para reduzir o risco de sobrecargas;
- organização geográfica do tráfego: a companhia pretende otimizar o tráfego de dados entre diferentes regiões de modo que, se uma estiver com problemas, as outras não sejam afetadas;
- recuperação mais rápida: os mecanismos de recuperação devem ser mais eficientes para que serviços instáveis ou interrompidos voltem a funcionar o quanto antes;
- apoio com inteligência artificial: a Microsoft considera recorrer a agentes de IA para ajudar suas equipes a identificar e solucionar incidentes rapidamente;
- monitoramento mais rigoroso: Jason Henderson, presidente da divisão M365 Core, fará reuniões diárias com os supervisores do grupo de engenharia responsável pelos serviços do Microsoft 365, presumivelmente para evitar um “relaxamento” dos cuidados.
O terceiro aspecto da lista, provavelmente, é o mais importante. O “apagão” da Microsoft só foi solucionado em 13 de novembro, o dia seguinte, o que trouxe transtornos para milhares de usuários e organizações ao redor do mundo.
Nesse sentido, a Microsoft estabeleceu o objetivo de solucionar incidentes de alcance global em até uma hora. A companhia também pretende acelerar a distribuição mundial de correções urgentes, especialmente quando relacionadas a problemas críticos. Mas o próprio Jason Henderson reconhece que não será fácil, o que, talvez, explique o estabelecimento do tal Código Vermelho:
Em um incidente recente separado, uma correção urgente em produção levou de cinco a seis dias para atingir a cobertura mundial. Para nossos problemas de segurança mais urgentes, precisamos ir da detecção à implantação segura em todo o mundo em uma hora. Desnecessário dizer que ainda não chegamos lá.
Jason Henderson, presidente da divisão M365 Core
Vale relembrar que a companhia atribuiu a causa do problema recente a uma atualização de software nos gateways de rede do Microsoft 365, que são servidores responsáveis por receber e distribuir as conexões dos usuários entre os serviços da empresa. Não houve ataque hacker ou ação de malwares, portanto.

articles.title: Backblaze explains why it’s sharing customer information with advertisers
articles.text:
Some customers have raised concerns about Backblaze’s privacy policy taking effect next month, which says the backup and cloud storage company may sell certain personal information to advertisers.
Backblaze’s current privacy policy says that in addition to the personal information that users may provide, such as their email address when creating an account, it may also “automatically” collect information, such as “your software, the operating system you use when accessing our service, your Internet Protocol address, and the date and time of each request you make to Backblaze.”
The current policy adds: “Under no circumstances do we rent, trade, or share your address or e-mail address with any other company for their marketing purposes without your consent.” It also makes no mention of advertisers.
On December 1, a new privacy policy takes effect. It includes a table listing the types of “general personal information” that Backblaze says it has been collecting and sharing with third parties, including “advertising and marketing partners” since December 1, 2025, This information includes identifiers (such as “name, address, Internet Protocol address, [and] email address”); commercial information (such as “records of personal property, products or services purchased, obtained, or considered, or other purchasing or consuming histories or tendencies”; geolocation data that “can be used to determine a device’s physical location”; and “sensory or surveillance data” (which includes “call recordings or other audio, electronic, or visual monitoring or surveillance”).
This has concerned some users, but a Backblaze spokesperson told Ars Technica that “Backblaze does not sell or share sensory or surveillance data, such as call recordings, for targeted advertising, and we do not disclose it to advertising or marketing partners.” They added:

articles.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan to put AI data centers in space
articles.text:
SpaceX was given conditional approval by the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday to deploy and operate a constellation of up to 1 million satellites for its orbital data center business, a regulatory victory for Elon Musk and his bid to move AI data centers into space.
The FCC authorization was granted despite objections from Amazon, Viasat, and the American Astronomical Society, which flagged concerns over orbital debris and congestion, radiofrequency interference, and environmental consequences. Amazon, which is building a competitor to SpaceX’s Starlink service, argued in its petition that the application lacked basic details and described it as a “lofty ambition rather than a real plan.” Despite that lack of detail, Amazon also said the proposal “risks real harm.”
The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority.
FCC Chair Brendan Carr said in a statement that the action “opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.”
Musk thanked Carr in a post on X, writing “Much appreciate. This will be a great asset to America and the world.”
This initial regulatory approval doesn’t mean orbital data centers are imminent.
SpaceX faces a number of technical and economic challenges, including how to dramatically reduce the cost of manufacturing and launching satellites, cool processors in space, and even how to secure financing for chips that are destined for orbit.
The company must also clear other regulatory hurdles. The FCC has not yet approved SpaceX’s plans to handle orbital debris for satellites that would operate above 600 kilometers, for instance. SpaceX requested a waiver of existing FCC rules, which requires satellites ending missions below 2,000 kilometers reenter Earth’s atmosphere within five years of completing those missions. The company is interested in moving some of these retired satellites into other orbits around Earth or even around the sun, according to the FCC authorization document.
SpaceX has said it plans to deploy the satellites, known as Starmind, at altitudes ranging from 500 to 1,002 kilometers. The FCC’s approval gives SpaceX the authority to use radiofrequency communications to maintain contact with and control its orbital data centers from Earth if their primary communications systems fail. The Starmind satellites would primarily communicate using lasers to connect with other satellites, including SpaceX’s Starlink.
The FCC has given SpaceX time to sort out these issues. Under the approval, SpaceX has seven years to get its first operational satellite into orbit and 14 years to deploy the entire constellation.

articles.title: Claude Ship: Anthropic automatisiert Code-Reviews für mehr Produktivität
articles.text:
Claude Ship: Wie Anthropic den Code-Review-Engpass löst und Produktivität steigert
Anthropic hat Claude Ship vorgestellt. Das Tool für Entwickler:innen prüft Codeänderungen automatisch, behebt Probleme und gibt Änderungen gemäß den Regeln eines Teams frei. Die Neuerung soll ein bestehendes Problem lösen: Zwar erstellen KI-Agenten Code sehr viel schneller als Menschen – wegen der anschließenden Prüfungen und Korrekturen beschleunigte sich der gesamte Prozess bisher aber nur bedingt.
Zeitfresser im Code Review Prozess reduzieren
KI-Tools können zwar die Produktivität beim Programmieren steigern, die Gewinne schlagen sich aber oft weder im Ergebnis noch im Arbeitsaufwand nieder. Das hat eine Harvard-Studie ergeben. Der Grund: Entwickler:innen müssen mehr Zeit in die manuelle Prüfung von KI-generiertem Code investieren. Die Forscher:innen werteten über 300 Millionen Arbeitsergebnisse der Engineering-Analytics-Plattform Jellyfish aus. Dadurch wollten sie herausfinden, wie sich KI konkret auf die Arbeit von Entwickler:innen auswirkt.
Laut den Studienautor:innen entstanden durch Coding-Tools und KI-Agenten zwar messbar mehr Codezeilen – auf den Output hatte das allerdings kaum einen Einfluss. „Wir sehen Anzeichen für einen Engpass im Überprüfungsprozess des Codes”, heißt es in den Ergebnissen der Harvard-Studie. Durch den Einsatz von KI stieg die durchschnittliche Zeit für die Überprüfung eines Pull-Requests deutlich, ebenso wie der Anteil der Pull-Requests, bei denen Änderungen nötig waren. Die Aufgaben der Entwickler:innen würden sich deshalb zunehmend hin zur Überprüfung verlagern.
KI-Agenten für die automatisierte Pull-Request-Freigabe
Mit Claude Ship will Anthropic jetzt eine Lösung bieten und erweitert die Entscheidungsbefugnisse der eigenen KI. Entwickler:innen können künftig nicht nur die Prüfung und Korrektur von Codeänderungen, sondern auch deren Freigabe nach individuell definierten Richtlinien an Claude delegieren. Für Claude Ship kombiniert Anthropic das seit Oktober 2026 regulär verfügbare Code Review mit zwei neuen KI-Agenten: PR Steward und Claude Approvals, die zunächst in der Beta-Version verfügbar sind. Gemeinsam übernehmen sie die Bearbeitung von Pull Requests, mit denen Entwickler:innen Änderungen an einer bestehenden Code-Basis vorschlagen. Code Review identifiziert mögliche Fehler, PR Steward nimmt notwendige Korrekturen vor und Claude Approvals entscheidet anhand der hinterlegten Richtlinien, ob die Änderungen freigegeben werden dürfen.
Mithilfe von Code Review ermöglichte Anthropic es Entwickler:innen, Codeänderungen im Kontext der gesamten Code-Basis automatisiert auf Fehler zu prüfen. So müssen sie weniger Zeit in manuelle Prüfungen investieren und können sich stärker auf neue Funktionen konzentrieren. Über die drei Review-Stufen Quick, Standard und Deep lässt sich bestimmen, wie gründlich Claude dabei vorgeht. Welches Potenzial in KI-gestützten Reviews steckt, zeigt Anthropic anhand eigener Erfahrungen mit dem Tool. Im eigenen Coding-Team, das die Funktion als eine von mehreren Prüfinstanzen nutzt, habe sich die Zahl der zusammengeführten Pull Requests zwischen Juni und September mehr als verdoppelt. Zugleich sank der Anteil der rückgängig gemachten Änderungen um über 40 Prozent.
Verfügbarkeit von Claude Ship für Enterprise Teams und GitHub Workflows
Damit die Eingriffe der KI nachvollziehbar bleiben, dokumentiert PR Steward nach jeder Aktualisierung, welche Änderungen er vorgenommen hat und wie sich diese bei Bedarf rückgängig machen lassen. Der Agent darf den Code zwar ändern, diesen aber nicht eigenständig freigeben. An dieser Stelle kommt Claude Approvals ins Spiel. Welche Entscheidungen Entwickler:innen der KI überlassen, legen sie in einer Richtliniendatei im jeweiligen Repository fest. Nutzer:innen mit Team- oder Enterprise-Abonnement, die ihren Code auf GitHub verwalten, können ab sofort auf Claude Ship zugreifen. Berechtigten Enterprise-Kund:innen gewährt Anthropic ein Guthaben von mindestens 10.000 US-Dollar.
;)) Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: Iliad Partners announces the final close of its $33.4 million VC fund
articles.text:
Iliad Partners announces the final close of its $33.4 million VC fund
- UAE-based venture capital firm Iliad Partners has announced the final close of its debut fund, Iliad Partners Tech Ventures Fund I LP, at $33.4 million, with new commitments from the Hellenic Development Bank of Investments (HDBI), Greece's sovereign fund of funds, and Alpha Bank.
- The fund's limited partners (LPs) include Saudi Arabia's Jada Fund of Funds, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Public Investment Fund (PIF), HDBI, Greece's four largest systemic banks, Alpha Bank, Eurobank, National Bank of Greece and Piraeus Bank, alongside family groups and family offices across the GCC and Europe.
- Founded by Christos Mastoras, Iliad Partners invests in early-stage B2B software and AI startups across sectors including enterprise technology, fintech, logistics and proptech, with a primary focus on Saudi Arabia and the UAE, alongside selective investments in European startups, particularly in Greece.
- The fund's current portfolio includes OTO, Penny, Qashio, Comfi and Balio. Iliad Partners plans to continue deploying capital over the next three years while supporting portfolio companies' access to financing, corporate partnerships and cross-border expansion between the GCC and Europe.
Press release:
Iliad Partners, an early-stage venture capital firm based in the UAE, has announced the final close of its $33.4 million Fund, Iliad Partners Tech Ventures Fund I LP. New major institutional investors, including the Hellenic Development Bank of Investments (HDBI), Greece's $2.5 billion sovereign fund of funds, and Alpha Bank, one of Greece's leading systemic banks, have joined the final closing of the Fund.
The new investors further strengthen the Fund’s institutional LP base, which now includes two sovereign investors, HDBI and Jada Fund of Funds, a wholly owned subsidiary of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), all four of Greece’s largest systemic banks, Alpha Bank, Eurobank, National Bank of Greece and Piraeus Bank, as well as prominent family groups and family offices from Saudi Arabia and across the GCC and Europe.
The Iliad Fund backs early-stage B2B software and AI companies driving digital transformation across sectors including enterprise, fintech, logistics and proptech. It focuses primarily on opportunities in the core GCC markets of Saudi Arabia and the UAE, while selectively investing in European startups, particularly from Greece. Through its extensive networks and strategic partnerships, Iliad Partners supports GCC startups expanding into European markets and European startups entering the GCC, reinforcing its role as a two-way venture bridge between the regions. The Fund’s current portfolio includes OTO, Penny, Qashio, Comfi, and Balio, with additional investments underway as the Fund continues deploying capital over the next three years.
Christos Mastoras, Founder & Managing Partner of Iliad Partners, said “The GCC has emerged as one of the most dynamic markets for technology and innovation, offering significant opportunities for ambitious companies to scale. At the same time, Europe brings a deep pool of talent, technological expertise, and established industries. We see tremendous potential in building bridges between these complementary ecosystems, unlocking new opportunities for entrepreneurs and businesses across both regions. With the successful closing of our first fund, we are entering an exciting new chapter, focused on translating this vision into tangible opportunities for the founders we back and supporting them in building enduring, globally competitive businesses.”
Dr. Haris Lambropoulos, the President of HDBI, and Ms. Antigoni Lymperopoulou, the CEO of HDBI, said “HDBI's participation in Iliad Partners reflects our conviction that Greece's innovation ecosystem will grow faster when it is connected to the capital, networks and dynamic markets like the GCC. Iliad Partners, with its long presence in the region, is well placed to act as a bridge between the Middle East and Europe. We are pleased to support the fund's final closing – alongside our Saudi sovereign peer, Jada, and other investors. We look forward to seeing the Fund’s investments strengthening Greek companies, creating skilled jobs and opening new paths to international growth. With $2.5 billion under management across 47 funds to date, HDBI will keep on financing innovation and investing in growth, partnering with managers who bring value to Greece.”
Lazaros Papagaryfallou, Deputy CEO of Alpha Bank, said “At Alpha Bank, innovation is a strategic priority and a catalyst for sustainable growth. As economic and investment ties between Greece and the Middle East continue to strengthen, we see growing opportunities for our clients and the wider business community. Our investment in Iliad Partners reflects this conviction, providing access to a differentiated, high-growth technology venture capital strategy in the Middle East, while connecting us more closely with emerging technologies, entrepreneurial talent and dynamic innovation ecosystems. At the same time, the investment contributes to the broader effort to foster commercial and cross-border business opportunities in the broader region, further reinforcing Greece's role as a natural gateway between Europe and the Middle East.”
Through its institutional LP partnerships, Iliad Partners will continue executing the Fund’s investment strategy, to provide portfolio companies with access to additional equity and debt financing opportunities, new pools of later-stage capital, large corporate clients, and support for market entry and geographic expansion across the GCC and Europe.

articles.title: Finnable raises Rs 405 crore in Series C to expand multi-product lending
articles.text:
Finnable raises Rs 405 Cr in Series C to expand multi-product lending
The Bengaluru-based lender has crossed Rs 4,600 crore in assets under management and says it made Rs 51 crore in profit after tax in the first half of FY27.
Fintech company Finnable has raised Rs 405 crore in a Series C round. The new investors are Bharat Value Fund, part of the Pantomath Group, along with Pratithi Investments and NKSquared. Pratithi is the investment vehicle of Infosys co-founder Kris Gopalakrishnan's family, and NKSquared is the firm of Zerodha co-founders Nithin and Nikhil Kamath.
Existing backers Z47, TVS Capital and Claypond Capital continue in the company. TVS Capital and Claypond Capital put in more money in this round. The Rs 405 crore figure carries an asterisk in the company's release. A disclaimer says final allotments and regulatory filings are still being completed and the figure is subject to final subscription numbers.
Profit ahead of last year's full-year total
Finnable said its assets under management crossed Rs 4,600 crore in October 2026. It reported a profit after tax of Rs 51 crore for April to September 2026, which already exceeds the Rs 46 crore it earned in the whole of FY26.
On asset quality, the company said its latest PAR 90 at six months on books stands at 0.24%. This measures loans overdue by more than 90 days among those that have been on the books for six months. Finnable pairs digital loan journeys and technology-led credit assessment with in-house collections.
Three lending lines
Finnable runs three businesses. Its personal loans target salaried professionals, mainly in metros and Tier I cities. Its loan against property (LAP) business offers secured credit to small business owners in Tier II and Tier IV markets. Its consumer finance arm provides instant checkout credit on leading e-commerce platforms, giving it access to younger, digitally active customers.
The company said it combines on-book lending with co-lending partnerships, which co-founder Amit Arora described as a capital-efficient model built to hold up across credit cycles.
Where the money will go
The funds will go towards taking the LAP business into new geographies, scaling consumer finance partnerships and strengthening technology. Finnable also plans to keep investing in AI across underwriting, fraud detection, collections and customer service.
Over the past year the company has also reinforced its board. It has appointed Shrimohan Yadav, a former chief general manager at the Reserve Bank of India, and Sreeram R. Iyer, a former global COO of the corporate and institutional business at ANZ Banking Group. The most recent addition is Sekhar Garisa, managing director at Claypond Capital.

articles.title: 3DMark Basic Edition
articles.text:
3DMark is not just for Windows either. With 3DMark you can compare your scores with Android and iOS devices, too. It's the most powerful and flexible 3DMark we've ever created.
Can I use 3DMark Basic Edition to benchmark my CPU and GPU?
Yes. Although 3DMark Basic Edition is primarily designed for GPU benchmarking, many tests also utilize the CPU to simulate real-world gaming and content creation scenarios. The benchmark provides detailed charts of CPU and GPU temperatures, clock speeds, power consumption, and frame rates throughout the test. A more complete (paid) version of 3DMark can test your CPU more thoroughly along with other tests like ray tracing and even storage.
Which 3DMark benchmark should I use?
3DMark Basic Edition currently includes several benchmarks suited to different hardware and use cases:
- Time Spy – For gaming PCs with DirectX 12 support.
- Fire Strike – For older or mid-range gaming PCs using DirectX 11.
- Night Raid – For laptops, tablets, and integrated graphics.
- Speed Way – For high-end PCs and graphics cards with DirectX 12 Ultimate, including ray tracing support.
When you launch the app, 3DMark scans your hardware and recommends the most suitable benchmark, but you're free to run any test manually.
How long does it take to run a 3DMark benchmark?
Most 3DMark benchmarks take between 5 and 15 minutes to complete, depending on the complexity of the test and the speed of your hardware.
Can running a benchmark damage my CPU or GPU?
No. 3DMark benchmarks are designed to test performance safely within the thermal and power limits set by your hardware's manufacturer. As long as your system is properly cooled and configured, running benchmarks will not cause damage. You can also adjust settings like resolution and workload to suit your cooling and power capabilities.
Is 3DMark Basic Edition free?
Yes, 3DMark Basic Edition is free for personal use. Paid versions offer additional benchmarks, stress testing, and advanced features such as custom settings and automated result comparisons. You can learn more about the available versions here.
Features
- The world's most popular benchmark.
- Includes three stunning tests for DirectX 9, DirectX 10 and DirectX 11 hardware.
- Test everything from tablets to gaming PCs.
- Includes Ice Storm, Cloud Gate and Fire Strike.
- Compare scores across Windows, Android and iOS.
- Easy to use, no technical know-how needed.
- Free online account to manage your results.
What's New
3DMark for Mobile 2.7.5123 Release Notes:
Announcing CPU Rumble - our new custom gaming CPU benchmark
Test iOS and Android CPU gaming performance
We're very excited to announce CPU Rumble – the first of two new CPU benchmarks we're creating to make understanding how your CPU affects gaming performance easy.
3DMark CPU Rumble's visual design is a throwback to classic games from even beyond the first 3DMark benchmark. It has minimal graphical effects to reduce the impact of GPU performance on benchmark results but still shows off an exciting benchmark scene where you can see the real-time work being done by your CPU in a game-like environment.
How have we designed 3DMark CPU Rumble?
In many currently available CPU benchmarks, your result mainly reflects the performance when either a single thread is used, or when the CPU is working at its maximum thread count. This can be useful for understanding the raw maximum performance of a CPU ideal scenarios – but modern games rarely, if ever, use a CPU in this way.
In most cases, your game of choice will use somewhere between 2 and 8 CPU threads, with one thread acting as a "main" thread that handles the most critical tasks for keeping the game running, with the other "worker" threads handling tasks such as audio, NPC AI, or assets. This is how you can sometimes experience game audio issues if your CPU is struggling, without the entire game crashing.
In the case of mobile games, their implementations make this approach even more obvious, as mobile CPUs have a variety of different core types that balance performance and energy efficiency.
CPU Rumble is designed to test the performance of a CPU in a scenario that closely mimics a game, while minimizing the non-deterministic component of them – something crucial to the development of a reliable benchmark. We've achieved this balance by using the same APIs and libraries popular among game developers.
3DMark Windows 2.32.8897 Release Notes:
Fixed
- Fixed an issue during 3DMark installation where legacy DirectX redistributables would not be installed, causing Fire Strike tests to fail if the components were not already present on the system.
Steam Version only
- Fixed an issue where opening a webpage link through the 3DMark application would prevent the Steam client from properly detecting when 3DMark was closed later.
3DMark Windows 2.32.8853 Release Notes:
- Improved the result validation for all 3DMark benchmarks.
3DMark Windows 2.32.8826 Release Notes:
Fixed
- Fixed the missing 'Save result' button that was incorrectly not shown in some situations.
Known Issues - Professional Edition:
- Windows on Arm result export (XML, PDF) currently isn't working. This will be fixed in a future update. Workaround is to do the exporting from a saved result file on a x86-based Windows machine
3DMark Windows 2.32.8426 Release Notes:
New
- Added the 3DMark Solar Bay Extreme Benchmark
- Added the 3DMark Solar Bay Extreme Stress Test
Fixed

3DMark Windows 2.31.8385 Release Notes:
This is a minor update. Benchmark scores are not affected.
New
- Added support for up to 8k and ultra-wide resolutions in custom mode for the Steel Nomad, Steel Nomad Light and Speed Way Benchmarks.

- Fixed an issue where the DLSS 4 feature test was missing its Traditional Chinese localization.
- Fixed an issue with the DLSS support detection that could cause systems with supported NVIDIA GPUs to claim that DLSS was not supported.

3DMark Windows 2.30.8348 Release Notes:

Speed Way v1.1.1.2

3DMark 2.29.8256 release notes
- Android version updated to 2.4.4934
This update supports the addition of XeSS 1.1,1.2 and 1.3.1 to the Intel XeSS feature test. Other benchmark scores are not affected.
New
- Added support for XeSS 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3.1 to the Intel XeSS feature test.

3DMark Windows 2.29.8282

3DMark Windows 2.29.8278
New

Fixed

Previous releases notes
3DMark Steel Nomad is out now
Today, we're thrilled to launch 3DMark Steel Nomad and 3DMark Steel Nomad Light. This update includes two new non-raytraced cross-platform benchmarks – Free for all 3DMark users.
Time to Move on
Since Time Spy launched in 2016, there's been a truly gigantic number of submitted results: Almost 48 million.
Over time, the average Time Spy score has approximately quadrupled. This, alongside game and hardware technology developments over the last eight years, meant that Time Spy was starting to show its age, and a new non-ray-traced benchmark was needed.
We're not fully retiring Time Spy just yet, but we suggest you use our latest benchmarks to get the best benchmarking experience on modern hardware.
Steel Nomad strides into town
Steel Nomad is a non-raytraced, cross-platform GPU benchmark that uses graphics technologies just like your favorite new game titles.
Running at a native 4k resolution, it improves upon Time Spy with more modern implementations of graphics technologies and is roughly three times heavier for your PC than Time Spy, and almost seven times heavier than Fire Strike. You can see this is not reflected in the data from a high-end GPU from 2024, as CPU bottlenecking is negatively impacting frame times in Fire Strike and Time Spy.
Steel Nomad launches today on Windows and Windows-on-Arm using the DirectX 12 and Vulkan APIs, Android using Vulkan, and iOS using Metal. As a cross-platform benchmark, we'll be releasing support for new APIs and platforms throughout the year. Also, due to popular demand, we've brought back sound for this benchmark.
Stay tuned for information on macOS soon! As for Linux gamers, unfortunately you'll have to wait a bit longer, but we are still committed to releasing 3DMark Steel Nomad for you as well.
"This town is big enough for the both of us"
PC gaming is more accessible, portable and flexible than ever. Desktop rigs are pushing more frames than ever, laptops are capable of comfortably playing top-end games, phones and tablets have the power to deliver full gaming experiences, and we've seen the rise of portable handheld gaming PCs in recent years.
With so many hardware configurations, Steel Nomad arrives alongside Steel Nomad Light, letting gamers, reviewers, and enterprises test all their gaming hardware in a non-ray-traced gaming workload.
With the addition of these two benchmarks, the 3DMark application provides a complete set of benchmarks for testing modern gaming hardware in both raytraced and non-raytraced gaming situations.
|  | Very Heavy | Heavy | Medium | Light | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ray-tracing | Speed Way (Windows only) | Port Royal (Windows only) | Solar Bay (cross-platform) |  | 
| Non-ray-tracing | Steel Nomad (cross-platform) |  | Steel Nomad Light (cross-platform) | Wild Life Extreme (cross-platform) | 
Explore the Frontier
In Explorer mode, you'll be able to explore the benchmark scene and toggle or change graphics settings. Hidden in the world are several secret locations for you to find and many Easter eggs referencing the last 25 years of 3DMark Benchmarks. We recommend enabling sound for the full experience. Explorer mode for Steel Nomad and Steel Nomad Light is available for everyone who has purchased 3DMark.
Updates to 3DMark Editions
For those of you trying out 3DMark with the 3DMark Demo before you buy, the 3DMark Steel Nomad and 3DMark Steel Nomad Light benchmarks will also be available for you to run. As with all other benchmarks in the 3DMark Demo, you won't be able to access custom benchmark settings, HDR, or modes such as Explorer and VS. Mode.
With the release of Steel Nomad, we're also updating the naming of 3DMark editions to align better with their intended users. This does not affect any features in these editions.
| Old Name | New Name | 
|---|---|
| 3DMark Basic Edition | 3DMark Demo | 
| 3DMark Advanced Edition | 3DMark | 
| 3DMark Professional Edition | 3DMark for Enterprise | 
Previous Release Notes:
This update supports the launch of the 3DMark Solar Bay. Other benchmark scores are not affected.
New
- Added 3DMark Solar Bay, a cross-platform ray tracing benchmark.
Fixed
- Fixed an issue where some 3DMark tests would fail if 3DMark was installed in a directory mounted to an NTFS volume.
- We're excited to announce the launch of 3DMark Solar Bay, a new cross-platform benchmark for testing ray traced graphics performance on Windows PCs and high-end Android devices. This benchmark measures games-related graphics performance by rendering a demanding, ray-traced scene in real time.
Solar Bay is available now for Android on the Google Play Store and for Windows on Steam, Epic Games or directly from UL Solutions.
Compare ray tracing performance across platforms
Ray tracing is the showcase technology for Solar Bay, simulating real-time reflections. Compared to traditional rasterization, ray-traced scenes produce far more realistic lighting. While dedicated desktop and laptop graphics processing units (GPUs) have supported ray tracing for several years, it's only recently that integrated GPUs and Android devices have been capable of running real-time ray-traced games at frame rates acceptable to gamers.
Built using the Vulkan 1.1 API, Solar Bay offers two new tests for ray tracing- capable hardware: a quick-to-run benchmark measuring immediate performance and a stress test that measures how device performance changes over extended periods of heavy load.
Solar Bay's ray-traced workload increases over three stages, with each section increasing linearly by 100%. Solar Bay complements our heavier ray tracing benchmarks, Port Royal and Speed Way, on PC. With Solar Bay, 3DMark has a great range of ray tracing workloads, making it an excellent way to measure how your Windows or Android device's ray tracing performance scales.
Solar Bay benchmark
Run the 3DMark Solar Bay benchmark to measure a device''s ability to provide instant performance for a short period of time. This test mirrors mobile games in which the gameplay loop is a series of short bursts of activity.
Solar Bay produces four scores on completion: an overall score and three sub-scores for each ray tracing section. These scores reflect your device''s frame rate in Solar Bay; the higher the frame rate, the better the score.
Solar Bay stress test
The Solar Bay stress test is a longer test that shows how a device will perform over extended periods of ray-traced gaming. It mirrors a longer session of ray-traced gaming.
This test runs the Solar Bay workload in a loop for 20 minutes, producing a chart showing how performance varies over the test. An ideal outcome is a steady set of results showing that performance is not throttled.
Detailed results page
The 3DMark app lets you immediately compare your device's result with scores from the same model or other popular devices. With its unique charts, lists and rankings, 3DMark gives you unrivaled insights into the performance of Android devices.
New
- Added the AMD FSR feature test.
Fixed
- Fixed an issue in the Mesh Shader feature test, where a division by zero error was possible in a culling shader.
- Fixed an issue where Speed Way and the Speed Way stress test would fail if the user's Documents or Picture folders are missing.
Previous release notes
This is a minor update. Benchmark scores are not affected.
Fixed
- Fixed an issue with Night Raid colorspace when rendering on one GPU and outputting to another. This issue was purely cosmetic and had no effect on performance or results in the previous 3DMark version.
Previous release notes:
Fixed
- Fixed a rare issue that prevented 3DMark from starting on some systems.
Improved
- Autosaved result files in your Documents/3DMark/ folder now include the test name and the overall score in the filename.
Fixed
- Fixed an issue with video memory allocation in Wild Life Extreme that could cause the test to fail on some systems with an AMD APU.
- Fixed an issue that prevented Time Spy and Time Spy Extreme custom runs from looping multiple tests, for example, looping both Graphics Test 1 and Graphics Test 2 in a custom run.
Fixed
- Fixed a UI issue with the score context labels on the benchmark result screen.
- Fixed a UI issue with the CPU Profile result screen showing incorrect core and thread counts for some CPU models.
3DMark Sky Diver
3DMark Sky Diver is a DirectX 11 benchmark for PCs with integrated graphics. Released in 2014, it is now too lightweight for modern PCs. UL recommends using 3DMark Night Raid (DirectX 12) and 3DMark Wild Life (Vulkan) to benchmark laptops, notebooks and other systems with integrated graphics.
3DMark API Overhead feature test
The 3DMark API Overhead feature test was released in 2015 to coincide with the launch of Windows 10 and DirectX 12. The test compares the draw call performance of graphics APIs. At launch, this was the most significant difference between older APIs and new, low-level APIs like DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Today, developers are more likely to choose a graphics API based on feature support and compatibility. Draw call performance is no longer the deciding factor. UL has no plans to update or replace this test.
Improved
- Updated SystemInfo to v5.34 to improve compatibility with latest hardware.
Fixed
- Minor fixes for the 3DMark benchmark results screen.
Previous Release Notes:
This is a major update that adds new features to the benchmark results screen. Game performance estimates are only available in 3DMark Advanced Edition and 3DMark Professional Edition.
- This update adds a new design for the benchmark results screen to help PC gamers better understand their 3DMark scores.
- With the new features we've added, it's easy to see how your 3DMark score compares with results from other systems with the same components.
3DMark has a new result screen to help PC gamers make sense of their scores.
Learn more about your PC's performance
- 3DMark now shows you how your benchmark score compares with results from other systems with the same components. This makes it easy to see if your PC is performing correctly.
3DMark shows how your score compares with other results from the same hardware.
- This new chart shows the range of scores submitted by other 3DMark users with the same combination of CPU and GPU.
- The peaks in the chart show the most common scores. The green line shows your score. The blue, dotted line shows the average score for your combination of components.
- If your score is close to the average, it means your PC is working as it should. A score well below the average could indicate a hardware or configuration problem. The best score gives you an idea of the overclocking potential of your setup.
- The new benchmark result screen and score comparison feature are available in all 3DMark editions, including 3DMark Basic Edition.
Discover real-world game performance

3DMark estimates game performance from your benchmark score.

articles.title: Take-Two frena Leonida, un proyecto que pretendía llevar 'GTA VI' a Windows a partir de una versión filtrada de Xbox
articles.text:
Para quienes juegan en PC, el lanzamiento de un nuevo 'Grand Theft Auto' tiene un significado algo distinto. Lo vimos con 'GTA V', que debutó en consolas en septiembre de 2013, pero no llegó a los ordenadores hasta abril de 2015. Con 'GTA VI' volvemos a encontrarnos ante una situación parecida: el juego ya está disponible en PS5 y Xbox Series X|S, mientras que su llegada a Windows sigue sin fecha oficial. En esta ocasión, parte de la comunidad ha decidido explorar sus propias vías para acortar la espera.
Una de las iniciativas más destacadas se llamaba Leonida, un proyecto que pretendía utilizar una versión filtrada de 'GTA VI' para Xbox como punto de partida para conseguir que el videojuego funcionase de forma nativa en Windows. Su recorrido, sin embargo, se ha visto interrumpido por Take-Two Interactive, la compañía matriz de Rockstar Games. Según consta en una notificación publicada por GitHub el 24 de noviembre, la empresa ha presentado una solicitud de retirada de contenidos al amparo de la Ley de Derechos de Autor de la Era Digital (DMCA) de Estados Unidos.
Para entender cómo hemos llegado hasta aquí, basta con remontarnos a la semana pasada. El videojuego salió a la venta el 19 de noviembre y, según la notificación de Take-Two, apenas un día después comenzaron a distribuirse públicamente archivos sustraídos de la versión para Xbox Series. El repositorio de Leonida se creó el día 21, cuando todavía faltaba el ejecutable principal del juego. Según PC Gamer y Tom's Hardware, el 23 de noviembre un usuario conocido como Cyberleek difundió ese archivo, lo que dio un nuevo impulso a los trabajos de ingeniería inversa.
Una filtración y una carrera por llevar 'GTA VI' a PC
Detrás de Leonida estaba NotRexed, un desarrollador que afirma tener 15 años. Su propuesta no consistía en emular una consola, sino en recurrir a la recompilación para generar código ejecutable de forma nativa en un ordenador. Aunque las Xbox Series X|S comparten la arquitectura de procesador x86-64 con muchos PC, eso no resuelve todas las diferencias entre ambos entornos. También hay que abordar cuestiones relacionadas con las interfaces de programación gráfica, las llamadas al sistema y otros servicios de los que depende el videojuego.
Conseguir que el juego arranque es solo una parte del camino. PC Gamer recoge que, durante una retransmisión, el equipo aparentemente consiguió mostrar la pantalla de presentación del título en un ordenador, antes de que el programa se cerrase de forma inesperada. La distancia entre ese resultado y una versión plenamente jugable sigue siendo considerable: el código debe funcionar correctamente y ofrecer un rendimiento adecuado durante la partida. El medio también señala que miembros de la comunidad están recurriendo a herramientas de inteligencia artificial como Claude para agilizar tareas de programación.
Take-Two sostiene que el repositorio reproducía elementos protegidos del videojuego, constituía una obra derivada y vulneraba las condiciones de la licencia de Rockstar. Leonida pedía a los usuarios que aportasen sus propios archivos, algo que la compañía considera engañoso porque la iniciativa estaba específicamente orientada a la versión filtrada de Xbox. Según precisa GitHub, la plataforma ha tramitado la solicitud de retirada contra toda una red de 3.007 repositorios. Conviene señalar que este procedimiento no equivale a una sentencia judicial sobre la legalidad del proyecto.
NotRexed anunció su retirada tras el cierre del servidor de Discord de Leonida, aunque explicó que este solo había sido uno de los motivos de su decisión. En declaraciones recogidas por PC Gamer, también mencionó sus responsabilidades escolares y deportivas, así como la presión de la comunidad. A fecha del 24 de noviembre, según The Verge, VIctory figuraba entre las iniciativas de recompilación que seguían adelante, mientras que otros aficionados exploraban el uso de XCL, una capa de compatibilidad que busca proporcionar en Windows las interfaces necesarias para ejecutar videojuegos de Xbox Series X.
La incógnita ahora es cuánto tiempo tendrán que esperar los jugadores de PC. GamesBeat, que cita a cuatro fuentes de la industria familiarizadas con los planes de Rockstar, sitúa el posible lanzamiento de la adaptación oficial en el primer trimestre de 2027, aunque el estudio todavía no lo ha anunciado. Si esa previsión se cumple, podría darse una situación particular: que quienes llevan días intentando superar por su cuenta las barreras técnicas reciban una versión oficial antes de conseguir que sus propias adaptaciones sean plenamente funcionales.

articles.title: L'aspirateur balai Bissell PowerClean tombe à 149,98 € pendant le Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : L'aspirateur balai Bissell PowerClean FurGuard à 149,98 € (-19%)
À l'occasion du Black Friday, l'aspirateur balai Bissell PowerClean FurGuard passe à 149,98 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 19 % et 29,67 € d'économie. Efficace pour nettoyer tous les types de sols avec sa filtration multicyclonique, cet appareil affiche une note actuelle de 3,5/5 par notre rédaction.
Le Bissell PowerClean FurGuard vise avant tout le ramassage des poils d'animaux et des saletés du quotidien avec un format stick épuré. Ce modèle sans fioritures va droit au but pour aspirer tous les types de sols, et son passage dans notre labo a montré qu'il remplit cette mission de base sans faiblir.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le PowerClean FurGuard descend à 149,98 € chez Amazon, soit environ 19 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (179,65 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 29,67 €.
Une filtration cyclonique efficace et des détails pratiques
Cet aspirateur balai se concentre sur l'essentiel : retenir la poussière dans son collecteur de 0,4 l. Le système de filtres associe technologie cyclonique, mousse et HEPA pour bien confiner les détritus et assainir l'air rejeté, comme le détaille notre test complet. Bissell a également pensé à l'ergonomie en intégrant une position de station debout ainsi qu'une commande déportée pour détacher la tête d'aspiration sans se pencher.
Bissell PowerClean FurGuard
Points forts
- Filtration multicyclonique efficace.
- Quelques astuces bienvenues (libération de la tête déportée, station debout…).
- Batterie amovible.
Points faibles
- Fonctionnalités réduites au strict minimum.
- Vidange du collecteur fastidieuse.
- Des cheveux dans la brosse malgré les peignes.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Un équipement basique et un entretien qui demande du temps
Pour atteindre ce tarif, l'appareil rogne sur le confort d'utilisation au quotidien. La vidange du bac impose de retirer tout le collecteur du bloc principal, une manipulation peu pratique face aux mécanismes rapides des références plus onéreuses. De plus, la brosse motorisée retient tout de même certains cheveux malgré ses peignes intégrés, ce qui demandera de la nettoyer manuellement de temps à autre. Ce modèle s'adresse donc avant tout à ceux qui recherchent un appareil d'appoint sans options superflues, d'autant que sa batterie reste entièrement amovible.
Hoover HF3 Dynamic Clean : l'autre option face au Bissell PowerClean FurGuard
Le Hoover HF3 Dynamic Clean se positionne lui aussi sur le créneau des aspirateurs sticks très simples. Vendu à 127,99 €, il est 21,99 € moins cher que le PowerClean FurGuard à son prix du jour. Le HF3 met en avant un entretien plus aisé au quotidien et un stationnement rapide, mais ses performances s'avèrent plus limitées sur moquette fine.
Le Bissell PowerClean FurGuard, actuellement noté 3,5/5, offre une filtration plus rigoureuse sur tous les sols que le Hoover HF3 Dynamic Clean, noté 3/5, qui garde pour lui un tarif inférieur.
Hoover HF3 Dynamic Clean
Points forts
- Indicateur d'autonomie précis.
- Facile à entretenir.
- Système QuickPark pertinent.
Points faibles
- Peu à l'aise sur la moquette fine.
- Aucun système contre les poils et les cheveux longs
- Bruyant.

articles.title: Plus besoin de coder : Claude crée vos propres applications pour Windows et Mac
articles.text:
Les artefacts, ces petites applications que Claude fabrique quand on les lui décrit dans la conversation, vivaient jusqu’ici dans le chatbot ou dans un onglet de navigateur. Depuis le 24 novembre, une option « Installer en tant qu’application » les transforme en logiciels de bureau, avec leur icône et leur fenêtre, sur Mac comme sur Windows. La bêta est ouverte à toutes les offres, et personne ne contrôle ce qui s’y installe : Anthropic prévient elle-même qu’elle ne passe pas ces applications en revue.
De la conversation à la barre des tâches
Le circuit tient en trois gestes : décrire l’outil voulu à Claude, le tester dans la discussion, puis passer par le menu de partage pour l’installer. Aucun empaquetage, aucune signature de code, pas de clé d’API : tout transite par le compte Claude. Les requêtes de l’application sont décomptées des limites de votre abonnement, qu’un outil bavard peut donc entamer comme n’importe quelle conversation. Il faut d’ailleurs être connecté pour ouvrir l’une de ces apps, le hors-ligne n’est pas au programme.
Lire aussi : Après Photoshop, il recrée Microsoft Word et Excel en version gratuite grâce à l’IA
Une fois installée, l’application se comporte en citoyenne du système : icône dédiée, fenêtre indépendante, notifications, et même un emplacement dans la barre des menus ou la zone de notification. Elle peut appeler Claude et vos connecteurs, se partager autour de vous, et se met à jour toute seule dès que l’artefact d’origine est modifié, chaque retouche se propageant à tous ceux qui l’ont installée. Les documents, diaporamas et feuilles de calcul maison restent à quai, tout comme les organisations soumises aux règles de santé américaines et les déploiements hybrides.
Sur l’offre Team, la fonction est allumée par défaut, accès complet exclu ; sur Enterprise, elle attend qu’un propriétaire du compte l’active. Des applications de bureau Claude existent depuis le 31 octobre 2024, mais elles logeaient le chatbot lui-même : vos créations n’en étaient jamais sorties.
Trois paliers de permissions, zéro contrôle à l’entrée
Par défaut, le bac à sable est strict : « une application installée ne peut faire que ce qu’elle ferait dans un navigateur ». Un deuxième palier l’autorise à demander des fonctions courantes, que Claude encadre de près. Le troisième, baptisé accès complet, permet de lancer des programmes et de lire, modifier ou supprimer des fichiers sans redemander à chaque fois.
Ce dernier palier est réservé aux applications que vous avez créées vous-même ou, sur les offres professionnelles, à celles nées dans votre organisation. Impossible, donc, d’accorder les pleins pouvoirs à l’app partagée par un inconnu. La prudence s’arrête là : Anthropic ne vérifie aucune application avant son installation et renvoie la responsabilité à l’utilisateur, invité à réserver l’accès complet aux outils de confiance.
Les permissions sont redemandées après chaque mise à jour, y compris les vôtres. Une exception de taille subsiste : si une partie de l’application est chargée depuis un site extérieur, cette partie-là peut changer sans déclencher la moindre demande. Le cas est fréquent pour des programmes nés dans le navigateur.

articles.title: En imágenes el encuentro entre Elon Musk y Jensen Huang de regreso a Nvidia
articles.text:
Elon Musk visitó la sede de Nvidia en Santa Clara, California, donde se reunió con Jensen Huang, director ejecutivo de la compañía especializada en chips e inteligencia artificial. El encuentro llamó la atención porque el empresario de Tesla y SpaceX llegó acompañado de dos de sus hijos y compartió públicamente la fotografía del momento en su cuenta de X.
La imagen fue difundida inicialmente el miércoles por la cuenta Tesla Owners Silicon Valley, que publicó una fotografía de Musk y Huang junto a trabajadores de Nvidia. El empresario no solo apareció en la publicación, sino que también repoteó el mensaje en su perfil de X, amplificando la difusión del encuentro.
La reunión se produjo en un momento particular para Huang, quien recientemente regresó a la dirección ejecutiva de Nvidia después de una breve salida del cargo que generó incertidumbre sobre el liderazgo de la compañía. Musk había expresado públicamente su respaldo a esa decisión y el lunes escribió en X: “El error ha sido corregido”.
La visita añade un componente personal a ese apoyo. Además de la fotografía compartida por Tesla Owners Silicon Valley, Ben Pouladian, fundador de BEP Research y accionista de Nvidia, publicó otras imágenes de ambos empresarios juntos, incluidas algunas de encuentros anteriores.
El respaldo de Musk a Jensen Huang tras su regreso a Nvidia
La visita se produjo apenas dos días después de que Nvidia anunciara oficialmente la reincorporación de Huang como presidente y director ejecutivo. El empresario había renunciado el 12 de noviembre de 2026, mientras la compañía atravesaba una crisis relacionada con cuestionamientos sobre su conducta personal y posibles implicaciones para la seguridad nacional.
Durante ese periodo, Musk se convirtió en uno de los empresarios tecnológicos que defendieron públicamente su regreso. El fundador de Tesla y SpaceX incluso respaldó una petición que reclamaba que Huang volviera a dirigir la compañía. Cuando Nvidia confirmó la decisión de su junta directiva, el lunes 23 de noviembre, Musk no dudó en celebrar la noticia.
La junta de Nvidia explicó que tomó la decisión después de mantener conversaciones con Huang y recibir información de altos funcionarios del Gobierno estadounidense. Según el comunicado oficial, el directorio consideró que su reincorporación no representaba un riesgo para la seguridad nacional. No obstante, la empresa confirmó que continuará una investigación interna sobre los acontecimientos que llevaron a su salida.
Jensen Huang pidió disculpas a los empleados y reconoció que está en terapia
El regreso del directivo también estuvo acompañado de explicaciones ante los trabajadores. Durante una reunión interna celebrada el martes 24 de noviembre, Huang reconoció que había cometido errores y pidió disculpas por incumplir partes del código de conducta de Nvidia.
Según informó Reuters, el ejecutivo admitió que sus acciones habían afectado a su familia y a los empleados de la compañía. También señaló que asiste diariamente a sesiones de terapia de 90 minutos.
Huang calificó como inaceptable haber incumplido las normas internas, especialmente porque había participado en la elaboración de algunas de ellas. Además, rechazó que su regreso significara estar por encima de las reglas de la empresa.
La situación mantiene a Nvidia bajo atención pública y política. El directivo deberá responder preguntas de legisladores estadounidenses en diciembre, en medio de investigaciones relacionadas con su conducta, la seguridad nacional y las actividades de la compañía frente a las tensiones tecnológicas entre Estados Unidos y China.
Por ahora, la fotografía de Musk junto a Huang y los dos hijos del empresario se convirtió en una nueva muestra pública de respaldo al directivo. El hecho de que Musk también haya reposteado la publicación original refuerza el mensaje de apoyo que había expresado desde que se conoció la salida temporal del máximo responsable de Nvidia.

articles.title: Margaret Atwood calls on feds to block telecom tower on Ontario island
articles.text:
Margaret Atwood is urging the federal government to prohibit the construction of a telecom tower on Ontario’s Pelee Island.
The famed Canadian author of The Handmaid’s Tale is part of the Pelee Island Bird Observatory (PIBO), which argues that the proposed 600-foot tower will threaten bird safety. According to PIBO, Pelee Island “sits on a major bird migration route and within areas where critical habitat is mapped for seven species at risk.”
The group has been asking Canadians to sign a petition calling for the government to block the tower and conduct a full environmental assessment of the project. It also held a media briefing earlier today in which it noted that more than 200,000 birds in Canada are killed by communication towers annually.
DRW, the company behind the tower, told Global News that it’s using “best-in-class” technology to protect wildlife. The tower would be used for a U.S.-based company to trade data between Chicago and New Jersey. PIBO, for its part, says it has received thousands of letters of support for its pleas.
“Pelee Island is one of the stupidist [sic] places on the planet to put such a stock-trading tower,” wrote Atwood on her Substack. “It’s not a wifi tower, it would bring no communications benefits to the Island, and it would seriously tarnish the image of Pelee as a nature and birding oasis. If you wanted to kill a lot of birds with a huge, deadly tower—a LOT of birds — you couldn’t have planned it better.”
Source: PIBO Via: Global News

articles.title: AMD Wants to Ray Trace Large, Dynamic Worlds with Reusable Parts
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
AMD Wants to Ray Trace Large, Dynamic Worlds with Reusable Parts
To scale large, open, dynamic worlds with ray tracing, AMD is developing a new approach to simplify the process. By extending traditional techniques, AMD introduces Ray Tracing Multi-Level Acceleration Structures (RT-MLAS). This technology adds additional levels of reusable acceleration structures within ray-traced objects, reducing both memory consumption and the time required to build and update them. Traditional ray tracing pipelines rely on two levels of acceleration structures: Bottom-Level Acceleration Structures (BLAS), which contain geometry, and a Top-Level Acceleration Structure (TLAS), which organizes instances of that geometry. However, large open worlds can have an enormous number of objects, making the TLAS increasingly expensive to rebuild as objects move or change their level of detail (LOD).
RT-MLAS addresses this challenge by introducing Mid-Level Acceleration Structures (MDLAS), allowing developers to organize objects into additional reusable hierarchies. AMD's implementation supports up to two additional levels, enabling repeated scene components to share acceleration structures rather than being individually duplicated or registered in an increasingly large TLAS. For example, an entire building can be represented by an MDLAS containing reusable walls, windows, doors, and roof components. This approach is particularly useful for open-world environments, where developers can organize different areas into independently manageable structures and rebuild only the sections that need updating. AMD's research also shows how the technology can benefit heavily animated environments, such as forests with tens of thousands of independently animated plants.In its Graphics Programming Conference 2026 presentation, AMD showcased more than 40,000 independently animated plants with ray-traced primary and shadow rays running at over 60 FPS at 1080p on a Radeon RX 9070 XT. By combining tetrahedral-cage animation with MLAS, the demonstration reduced the overhead of managing acceleration structures, allowing it to become traversal-limited instead of build-limited. This advancement could help developers implement real-time ray tracing in expansive environments containing thousands of independently moving objects. Finally, AMD notes that the technology is available on RDNA 4 GPUs through the Vulkan API, and developers can use Radeon RX 9000 series or Radeon AI PRO R9000 series.

articles.title: PS5 modder rips out logic board to turn his console into liquid-cooled Phanteks PC — custom PlayStation 5 Pro build took 120 hours, has its own PSU, AIO, and 3D-printed parts
articles.text:
PS5 modder rips out logic board to turn his console into liquid-cooled Phanteks PC — custom PlayStation 5 Pro build took 120 hours, has its own PSU, AIO, and 3D-printed parts
If you're going to spiff up your PS5 Pro's cooling, do it right
The PlayStation 5 cooling system isn't an ideal design. Users report that it can run pretty loud with heavy loads and that it has a tendency to overheat easily because of dust buildup. The recent release of GTA VI revealed that many gamers needed to give their consoles a dusting or TIM replacement. But a Swiss YouTube tech enthusiast by the name of Nico wanted a more permanent fix for the issue, so he engineered an entirely custom PS5 build with a watchmaker's precision.
The final build uses a Phanteks XT V3 case, a small NZXT power supply, a Lian-Li Hydroshift II 360-mm CLC, and a pleasantly excessive number of fans. Oh, right, and there's a PlayStation 5 Pro at the center of it all. Nico shared the details of this wild custom build with Tom's Hardware.
The PS5 doesn't have a conventional ATX power adapter, but it only needs 12V power to run. As a solution, Nico split two PCIe power connectors into their respective positive and negative leads, then soldered them in parallel to a 4.5 mm cable and lug to wire directly to the console's motherboard. He wired the case's power switch to bridge the PS_ON and ATX pins, mirroring the paper-clip trick that us PC builders use. The PS5 itself then can be turned on normally via the controller.
Nico's first revision of this project used a custom loop with a pump he wired to the PS5's PWM fan control. That made the pump run too fast, though, and for our precision-minded friend, this wouldn't do.
To improve on his design, he looked far and wide and found the Lian-Li Hydroshift II 360mm LCD-C. This cooler only requires the power supply to be on to operate, and Nico particularly likes its integrated knob control, which changes the displayed information when it's turned left and adjusts the RGB LED lighting when it's turned right.
The fan sets Nico used came from Jonsbo, one of which is standard flow and one reverse, the latter of which is presumably for intake purposes. These are managed by a no-name controller off AliExpress with a remote, wired to one of the PSU's SATA power ports. He also wired the case USB-C port directly to the console's board as well.
The most significant time investment for Nico, though, were the custom 3D-printed parts he devised, namely the I/O shield, motherboard support, and cold-plate bracket. He didn't have prior CAD experience, so he reports that the entire process across his first iteration and revised builds took 80 to 120 hours to fully figure out. He expects that an experienced person would need 20-30 hours total for the mod.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
As for the cost, well, Nico says it's not much of a value. He notes that he essentially did the build twice, and estimates his costs across both builds at 800-1000 CHF, or $960 to $1200, including the value of failed 3D prints. Using his parts list and 3D printer files, though, we guesstimate that the price tag would stand at about $375 for the perfected attempt.
You can check out all the build guides for this mod on Nico's dedicated Youtube channel, though he doesn't appear to have uploaded the latest revision yet. In any event, we applaud Nico's clean build.
Download the Tom's Hardware app for up-to-the-minute updates on iOS and Android. Also follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

articles.title: UAE's Sooner raises $20 million to expand home financing solutions
articles.text:
UAE's Sooner raises $20 million to expand home financing solutions
- UAE-based fintech startup Sooner has secured $20 million in seed funding, comprising $5 million in equity led by Nuwa Capital, with participation from 500 Global, Annex Investments, Plus VC, Serkal Group, Axeed Group, 21Ventures, Iliad Partners and angel investors, alongside a $15 million Shariah-compliant debt facility from Amwal Capital Partners.
- Founded in 2026 by Mohammed Aziz, Gabriel García Leyva and Vlad Cherevkov, Sooner operates a down payment support platform licensed by the Dubai Land Department, enabling first-time homebuyers to pay 10% instead of 20% upfront on eligible properties, with the remaining down payment spread over 60 equal Shariah-compliant monthly instalments.
- The funding will give Sooner the capacity to support AED 1 billion ($272 million) in home purchases in 2027. The company also plans to launch a Home Equity Line of Credit (HELOC) product next year, enabling existing homeowners to access financing against their property equity, alongside plans for regional and international expansion.
Press release:
Sooner, the UAE's first down payment support platform, has announced a $20 million seed round. First-time homebuyers in Dubai usually have to pay a 20% down payment plus 7 to 10% in closing fees in cash upfront. This changes with Sooner, which is licensed by the Dubai Land Department, with buyers having to put down 10% instead of 20% with the rest paid monthly over five years.
The round comprises $5 million in equity led by Nuwa Capital, with participation from 500 Global, Annex Investments, Plus VC, Serkal Group, Axeed Group, 21Ventures, Iliad Partners and angel investors, including operators from AWS, Lean Technologies and Sarwa, and a $15 million Shariah-compliant debt facility from Amwal Capital Partners, which gives Sooner the capacity to support $272 million of home purchases in 2027.
Most first-time homebuyers can afford the monthly mortgage payments but are held back by the availability of immediate cash. The down payment plus closing fees come to 27 to 30% of the price, about $230,000 (AED 850K) on an $800,000 (AED 3M) home, against roughly 6 to 10% in the United States and the United Kingdom.
Sooner's mission starts with helping renters become homeowners about two years sooner. Homebuyers pick from Sooner-compatible homes, where they pay 10% instead of 20% upfront and the remainder in 60 equal Shariah-compliant monthly instalments, while getting access to first-time homebuyer mortgages from all leading UAE banks with the lowest mortgage rate guarantee.
Sooner's founders come from leading fintech and proptech startups. Mohammed Aziz (CEO) exited his payments company Pluto to Tamara and was the first UAE-based founder to be backed by Y Combinator. Gabriel García Leyva launched rent now pay later at Keyper, and Vlad Cherevkov previously led products at Revolut and Deel.
"We built the product we wished we had," said Mohammed Aziz, CEO and co-founder of Sooner. "I went through this by buying our first family home, saving towards the down payment while also paying rent. My co-founder Gabriel and his wife went through the same as they bought the unit they rented. Every year a first-time buyer spends saving for a down payment, which is a year of rent paid towards someone else's mortgage. We are solving that problem and making sure that people in the UAE can realise their dream of home ownership sooner."
Since its launch in July 2026, Sooner has received about 9,000 applications, representing $4.5 billion in buying demand, and has already supported around $10 million of home purchases.
That mission evolves beyond the first home into helping the same customers build wealth through real estate. In 2027 Sooner will launch the UAE’s first Home Equity Line of Credit (HELOC) product, allowing existing homeowners to unlock value from their current properties to easily secure financing for a new home. This is modelled on America's largest HELOC platforms: publicly listed Figure and Aven, a $2.2 billion unicorn backed by Khosla Ventures, Founders Fund and General Catalyst.
"The UAE market has been historically undercredited and investor-focused. It’s now ripe for a shift to end-user homeowners," said Gabriel García Leyva, co-founder of Sooner. "We reduce the barrier to access and leverage technology to deliver instant mortgage and Sooner down payment pre-approvals, as well as enabling a buyer-focused home discovery and closing experience that helps our customers get keys in hand in as little as 2 weeks."
The timing follows a shift towards end-user buying in Dubai. Residential mortgage lending hit a record $5.9 billion in the third quarter of 2026 (Cavendish Maxwell), and Dubai's Real Estate Sector Strategy 2033 targets a home-ownership rate of 33%.
"Down payment support and home equity release are standard in developed housing markets and still largely missing in the Gulf," said Arnav Danthi, partner at Nuwa Capital. "Sooner is building that for UAE homebuyers, and Mohammed, Gabriel and Vlad are one of the strongest early-stage fintech teams we've seen in the region."
"The Dubai property story is shifting from investor speculation to resident ownership," said Sharif Eid, Head of Fixed Income at Amwal Capital Partners. "Sooner is at the heart of this shift and is built on two simple observations: the down payment is the biggest barrier to ownership, yet it measures savings, not affordability; and people who own their home are people who stay. Sooner paired those insights with the right structure and technology, and that is why we backed them."
The UAE alone is a $4.1 billion revenue opportunity for Sooner's products, and the platform plans to expand to structurally similar markets, regionally and internationally.
Salaried homebuyers can get verified in about two minutes at www.joinsooner.com to get access to the platform.

articles.title: ARTEX a encore frappé : l’IA est soupçonnée d’avoir piraté un réseau de la CIA
articles.text:
Aux origines, ARTEX n’a rien d’une arme ou d’un outil de piratage. Développé par un ingénieur chinois connu sous le pseudonyme Autumn-27, il a été conçu comme un outil de « test d’intrusion ». En clair, ARTEX devait aider les experts en cybersécurité à débusquer les failles avant les pirates. Publié en libre accès sur Github, le logiciel a été promptement détourné par des cybercriminels. Branché sur des modèles d’IA chinois, comme DeepSeek, ARTEX peut orchestrer des attaques en toute autonomie, sans la moindre intervention initiale.
Des pirates s’en sont donc servis pour dérober les données personnelles d’environ 67 000 personnes en s’attaquant à des banques sud-coréennes. Les attaques se sont multipliées jusqu’à ce que le FBI publie une alerte officielle, assurant qu’« ARTEX réduit considérablement le temps nécessaire pour enchaîner les techniques d’attaque, certaines intrusions passant du ciblage initial à un accès privilégié en moins de trois heures ».
Dos au mur, le développeur Autumn-27 n’a pas tardé à retirer ARTEX de GitHub, mais des copies circulent toujours. En dépit de son retrait, ARTEX s’est retrouvé impliqué dans la cyberattaque contre la Commission européenne, qui a obligé l’institution à couper une partie de ses systèmes pendant dix jours. En interne, la Commission soupçonne des pirates soutenus par la Chine.
Le nouveau coup d’éclat d’ARTEX
Quelques jours après la cyberattaque contre la Commission européenne, ARTEX a refait parler de lui. Le 24 novembre, le New York Times a révélé qu’un réseau partagé par plusieurs agences fédérales a été compromis. Le réseau était utilisé par la CIA et le bureau du directeur du renseignement national (ODNI), qui supervise les agences de renseignement américaines, et la NGA, chargée du renseignement par image satellite, pour mener des opérations de renseignement. Selon les personnes proches de l’enquête, interrogées par le média, les pirates se seraient servis d’ARTEX pour compromettre le réseau.
Le réseau piraté a été conçu pour analyser des informations issues de « sources ouvertes », comme des publications sur les réseaux sociaux, des vidéos, des données commerciales ou des images satellites. Les autorités fédérales se veulent rassurantes et assurent que le problème a été résolu. Par ailleurs, l’ODNI (Office of the Director of National Intelligence) est le bureau du directeur du renseignement national, assure qu’il « n’y a eu aucune perturbation des capacités essentielles ni des systèmes classifiés ». De son côté, la CIA a refusé de commenter. Les données qui ont été exposées ne sont pas classifiées. Il s’agit de données publiques, mais qui peuvent néanmoins être exploitées à des fins malveillantes.
À lire aussi : « Code rouge » – après la panne historique d’Outlook, Microsoft déclenche l’alerte maximale
« Un saut technologique »
Selon les deux sources du New York Times, plusieurs indices, dont l’utilisation d’ARTEX, suggèrent que la Chine pourrait être impliquée dans la cyberattaque. L’outil est en effet massivement exploité par des gangs mandatés par Pékin. Ce piratage s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une série noire d’incidents pour les États-Unis. Quelques jours avant l’incident à la CIA, la base de données criminelles du FBI a été piratée. Interrogé par ABC News suite au hack du FBI, Jay Clayton, directeur du renseignement national, pointe du doigt l’augmentation des incidents de sécurité aux États-Unis, à cause de l’essor de l’intelligence artificielle.
« En 2020, environ 750 000 cyberincidents ont été signalés au FBI. On en est maintenant à plus d’un million », explique Jay Clayton, soulignant que le monde fait « face à un saut technologique, avec une superintelligence et une puissance de calcul qui progressent de façon exponentielle ».

articles.title: Green Aero raises $14M as India pushes for indigenous jet propulsion
articles.text:
Green Aero raises $14M as India pushes for indigenous jet propulsion
Over the next 12 to 18 months, Green Aero plans to expand engine-testing facilities, hire engineers, and advance the flight qualification of transonic and supersonic drones.
Green Aero, an aerospace and defence startup developing jet engines, military drones and autonomous aircraft, has raised $14 million in a Series A round led by Crane Ventures, an investor focused on artificial intelligence and deeptech.
Other participants were 3one4 Capital, an early-stage venture capital firm, and Antler Elevate, Antler’s growth fund, alongside returning backers pi Ventures, a deeptech investor; Antler India; and Rebalance, an accelerator and angel community.
Over the next 12 to 18 months, Green Aero plans to expand engine-testing facilities, hire engineers, and advance the flight qualification of transonic and supersonic drones. Transonic flight occurs around the speed of sound, while supersonic flight is faster.
The startup also aims to commercialise existing engines, citing early interest from overseas buyers, and bring its drone and combat-aircraft platforms to market. Founder Prithwish Kundu said the funding would accelerate technology development across jet engines, military drones, and collaborative combat aircraft.
Founded in November 2023, Green Aero develops propulsion systems, aircraft electronics, flight-control systems, and airframes in-house. Its 50-member team works from an 87,000 sq ft facility in Bengaluru, which houses research, assembly and testing. Founder Kundu had previously worked at Argonne National Laboratory in the US.
The startup has also developed the Blue Dragon, an aero-engine core built from scratch in India, and completed more than 100 hot-fire tests of its small jet engines. Building on this propulsion work, it is now developing larger-thrust engines alongside autonomous flight-control systems, onboard computing and navigation capabilities designed to operate without satellite signals.
Green Aero's work has received support from Larsen & Toubro, Boeing’s BUILD programme, and SIDBI’s Green-Tech Accelerator.
The startup's technologies are intended to support collaborative combat aircraft, uncrewed military planes designed to operate alongside conventional fighter jets. Air forces are exploring such systems to combine crewed aircraft with autonomous or remotely supervised platforms.
Shubham Sandeep, Partner at pi Ventures, described sovereign propulsion as “a decade-defining opportunity”.
The fundraise comes amid uneven investment in India’s defence-tech sector.
Hyderabad-based Constelli raised $20 million in February 2026 for electronic-warfare and communications systems, while Raphe mPhibr secured $100 million in 2025 to expand its unmanned aircraft business. Tracxn data shows that defence-tech companies raised $73 million through October 2026, compared with $304 million across 61 deals in 2025.
Government support includes iDEX, which had engaged 676 startups, MSMEs and innovators and signed 551 development contracts by March 2026, and ADITI, a companion scheme with a Rs 750 crore outlay. There is also a proposed investment of Rs 5,000 crore programme for an indigenous high-thrust aero-engine.
Edited by Swetha Kannan
