articles.title: Signal now blocks screenshots by default to keep AI agents from reading your chats
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Signal has begun blocking screenshots by default in its messaging app. The change is aimed at AI agents that can read a phone's screen and capture sensitive information in the process. Signal argues that agents built into the operating system can bypass the end-to-end encryption that is the app's main selling point.
The company's concern is where these agents operate. Signal says Google, Apple, and Microsoft are integrating autonomous agents "deep" into their device operating systems. An agent with that level of access does not need to break an app's encryption because it can see messages, pictures, and emails after the app decrypts them for display. Any safeguards built into an individual app can therefore be bypassed.
Udbhav Tiwari, Signal's head of strategy and global affairs, put the stakes in strong terms. "The ability for billions of devices to permanently spy on their users makes the Edward Snowden revelations look like a joke," he told Politico, referring to the 2013 disclosures about mass US government surveillance.
He also raised a potential legal avenue for surveillance. Governments seeking access to private information could ask technology companies for data collected by their agents. That would eliminate the need to break encryption or install malware on a target's phone.
Apple, Google, and Microsoft declined to comment on Signal's claims. Signal wants operating system makers to give apps a way to opt out of AI data access and processing. Blocking screenshots is a temporary measure until such tools become available.
Privacy groups share the unease. Gus Hosein, executive director of Privacy International, pointed to what a phone holds. "Probably the most sensitive device in your entire life is your phone. If it gets nicked, the person stealing your phone is not going to have access to your whole life. We're undoing all those safeguards by inviting AI agents onto these devices," he said.
Itxaso Domínguez de Olazábal, a policy adviser at the European digital rights group EDRi, called for "serious limits" on what agents can access. She described a future in which "the companies controlling our operating systems can effectively decide how much privacy we are allowed to have, even when we deliberately choose services designed to protect it."
Operating-system-level agents have already launched in many countries. Their rollout has been slower in the European Union, where Apple has cited the bloc's digital competition rules as a key obstacle to introducing its newest AI assistant features. Meta is also advancing its own agent, Muse, which has launched in the United Kingdom.
The UK's Information Commissioner's Office warned last month that AI agent products "may amplify and accelerate risks" to consumers. It said this week that Meta committed to a "voluntary monitoring and reporting scheme" so regulators can keep watching the product. The office is also preparing new guidance on how privacy law applies to AI agents. Meta says Muse is "private, safe and secure by design" and that it has "engaged constructively" with regulators.
Beyond the most serious privacy risks, there are also concerns about what happens to data once an agent gains access to it. Critics worry that the information could be repurposed for AI training or targeted advertising.
Regulators are focusing on one particularly difficult aspect of this problem: data belonging to people who have never interacted with the agent. Third-party data includes messages and holiday pictures sent to a friend who has quietly allowed an AI agent to access their conversations. The sender may have no idea their information is being collected.
Ireland's Data Protection Commission, which oversees privacy matters involving Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and other major technology companies, has begun taking action. In the past month, it stepped in to stop X, owned by Elon Musk, from using third-party data collected by its Grok chatbot to train AI models.
Irish Data Protection Commissioner Niamh Sweeney said last week that it is "much more challenging" to inform third parties that their data is being processed or give them an opportunity to opt out when they have "no idea" their information could also be collected. Her point highlights a weakness in consent-based privacy protections: Users can choose a private messaging app and still have their information exposed through the device of the person on the other end of the conversation.

articles.title: Cómo eliminar los mensajes programados en WhatsApp, paso a paso
articles.text:
WhatsApp incorporó los mensajes programados, una herramienta que permite redactar un texto, una foto o un video en cualquier momento y programar su envío con entre 10 minutos y 14 días de anticipación, tanto en conversaciones individuales como en grupos.
El despliegue global comenzó este 25 de noviembre. La distribución es gradual y la disponibilidad puede variar según la cuenta, el dispositivo y la versión instalada de la aplicación. La función llegó tras un período de pruebas en las versiones de desarrollo de Android e iOS: las primeras se realizaron el 12 de octubre en Android y se extendieron el 22 de octubre a iPhone.
Cómo programar un mensaje dentro de WhatsApp
El proceso comienza en la conversación individual o grupal elegida. Una vez redactado el texto o seleccionado el archivo que se quiere enviar, el usuario debe mantener presionado el botón de enviar en lugar de tocarlo una sola vez.
La aplicación muestra entonces la opción para elegir la fecha y la hora de entrega. El plazo disponible va desde 10 minutos hasta un máximo de 14 días de anticipación. Tras confirmar el horario, el mensaje queda en espera dentro de la plataforma y se enviará de forma automática en el momento definido.
La programación no se limita a textos. La función también admite fotos y videos, de modo que es posible preparar desde una felicitación con imagen hasta un aviso audiovisual para familiares, compañeros o integrantes de un grupo. Para quien recibe el mensaje, el contenido llegará como cualquier otro: sin marcas que indiquen que fue preparado con anticipación y sin ninguna acción adicional de su parte.
WhatsApp aclaró además que el envío se realizará aunque el teléfono del remitente esté apagado, sin conexión o sin batería en el momento acordado. La empresa confirmó también que estos mensajes conservarán el cifrado de extremo a extremo, el sistema de protección que aplica a todas las comunicaciones personales dentro de la plataforma.
Dónde se consultan o borran los mensajes que aún no salieron
Quienes utilicen la herramienta tendrán acceso a una sección dentro de la aplicación donde podrán ver todos los mensajes pendientes. Para llegar a ella, basta con ingresar a la conversación correspondiente y tocar el aviso que indica que hay un mensaje programado. Esa acción lleva directamente a la pantalla de mensajes programados, donde se figuran todos los envíos que todavía no se concretaron.
Desde allí es posible revisar el contenido y la fecha asignada a cada uno. Esa posibilidad resulta útil cuando las circunstancias cambian después de haber programado un mensaje: una reunión que se cancela, un saludo que ya no es pertinente o información que dejó de ser válida pueden retirarse antes de que lleguen al destinatario.
Cómo eliminar los mensajes programados en WhatsApp
- Abrir el chat donde aparece el aviso “Programaste un mensaje”.
- Tocar ese aviso para ingresar a la pantalla de mensajes programados.
- Buscar el mensaje cuyo envío se desea cancelar.
- Tocar el mensaje para seleccionarlo.
- Presionar el ícono del tacho de basura.
- Confirmar la eliminación, si la aplicación lo solicita.
- Verificar que el mensaje haya desaparecido de la lista: ya no se enviará a esa conversación.
La cancelación solo es posible antes del momento fijado para el envío. Si el horario ya se cumplió, el mensaje habrá salido de forma automática y no podrá recuperarse desde esa pantalla. Por eso, cualquier cambio de opinión debe hacerse con tiempo suficiente antes del horario elegido.
La posibilidad de revisar y cancelar los mensajes pendientes funciona, en la práctica, como una red de seguridad: permite corregir errores, retirar información desactualizada o simplemente reconsiderar un envío antes de que el destinatario reciba algo.
Con un límite de hasta dos semanas de anticipación, la función suma a WhatsApp una herramienta de planificación que, hasta ahora, no existía dentro de la propia aplicación.

articles.title: Nova York bane brinquedos com chatbots de IA
articles.text:
Nova York bane brinquedos com chatbots de IA
Lei começa a valer em fevereiro de 2027 e busca proteger crianças de conversas inadequadas. Califórnia já adotou restrição semelhante.
Resumo IA
- Proibição alcança fabricação, distribuição e venda de brinquedos com chatbots de companhia.
- Infrações poderão gerar multas de até US$ 15 mil por dia (cerca de R$ 90 mil.
- Medidas estaduais ampliam a pressão sobre a segurança desses produtos.
O estado de Nova York proibirá por cinco anos a fabricação, distribuição e venda de brinquedos infantis com chatbots de companhia baseados em inteligência artificial. A governadora Kathy Hochul sancionou a lei nesta terça-feira (24/11), citando riscos de conversas inadequadas, manipulação emocional e coleta de dados das crianças.
A restrição começa a valer em 22 de fevereiro de 2027, 90 dias após a assinatura. Portanto, esses produtos ainda poderão ser vendidos livremente durante as compras de fim de ano.
Quais brinquedos serão proibidos?
A lei mira brinquedos destinados a crianças de até 12 anos que tenham um companheiro de IA integrado. Entram nessa categoria bonecos, robôs e bichos de pelúcia capazes de manter conversas personalizadas. O alvo são sistemas que simulam relações com o usuário, incluindo memória de interações e diálogos pessoais.
O texto proíbe também trocar ou manter esses produtos à venda. A fiscalização caberá à Procuradoria-Geral do estado americano, que poderá buscar multas de até US$ 15 mil por dia e por infração (quase R$ 90 mil em conversão direta). A suspensão termina cinco anos após a entrada em vigor.
No anúncio, o governo citou testes em que brinquedos discutiram temas sexualmente explícitos, indicaram onde encontrar fósforos e demonstraram tristeza quando a criança encerrava a conversa. Segundo o comunicado, alguns produtos ofereciam poucos controles parentais e podiam gravar voz ou escanear rostos.
Em testes, a organização de defesa do consumidor PIRG (Public Interest Research Groups) identificou falhas nos filtros de segurança desses brinquedos.
Restrições avançam em outros estados
A Califórnia também sancionou uma medida parecida em setembro, mostrando que o movimento já ultrapassou Nova York. No estado, a duração da suspensão será de quatro anos e também mira chatbots de companhia. As medidas ampliam a pressão sobre os fabricantes diante dos riscos relacionados ao conteúdo das conversas, à privacidade e aos vínculos emocionais com crianças.
No Brasil, o Ministério da Justiça já apontou riscos em 13 plataformas de companheiros de IA, incluindo conteúdo sexualizado e coleta de informações pessoais. A análise foi encaminhada à ANPD e à Senacon. O levantamento trata de serviços digitais e ainda não representa uma proibição de brinquedos com IA no mercado nacional.

articles.title: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
articles.text:
OpenAI has started rolling out a unified Chat and Work experience in ChatGPT to a few of its users, amid criticism from some subscribers that the merger could restrict their usage.
The ChatGPT maker began introducing the update to a small group of Pro subscribers, product lead Thibault “Tibo” Sottiaux said in a post on X on Tuesday. The rollout follows OpenAI’s earlier announcement of the merger in an email to users. An OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch that while most users are not expected to face more frequent usage resets, a small fraction of its heaviest users may hit their limits sooner.
That’s among the concerns raised by some ChatGPT subscribers on social media and OpenAI’s community forum recently. The users fear that merging the usage limits for Chat and Work could leave them with less access to advanced reasoning models than they currently have, even as they continue paying the same subscription fees.
Under the new system, Chat and Work will share a single usage meter across ChatGPT, the OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch. Conversations using the Instant model will, however, remain unlimited and will not count toward the shared allowance. Users can also continue using Instant after exhausting their usage limits. The spokesperson added that OpenAI would continue working to improve efficiency so subscribers could get more out of their plans.
While the rollout has started for a small group of users, OpenAI plans to bring shared usage limits more broadly in December, per its support page.
Similar to OpenAI, rival Anthropic also moved to bring its conversational chat service Claude and work-focused Cowork under one interface in September.
The changes come as AI companies face mounting infrastructure costs and growing demand for increasingly capable models, putting pressure on their computing resources. Bringing conversational and work-related tools into a single interface could also make AI chatbots simpler to use, allowing users to move between chats and more complex tasks without switching tabs.

articles.title: The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites
articles.text:
In an extraordinary decision, the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy a constellation of up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital data centers.
If fully deployed, this constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold.
“The United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement on Wednesday. “This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.”
The decision, announced a day before the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States, represents a major regulatory victory for SpaceX and its founder, Elon Musk, who has allied himself with the Trump administration.
A long deployment runway
This announcement clears a major hurdle to deploying data centers in space, although it does not establish that orbital data centers are technically or economically viable. Nevertheless, the FCC authorization appears designed to give the company wide latitude as it works through these remaining issues.
For example, SpaceX has seven years to deploy a single operational Starmind satellite under the order. SpaceX has until November 2035 to deploy 100,000 operational satellites, and November 2040 for the full constellation. SpaceX, therefore, has a 14-year regulatory runway to deploy the most ambitious industrial project ever approved for spaceflight.
The authorization includes some conditional aspects. SpaceX has proposed operating in six orbits, ranging from 550 km to about 1,000 km. The company sought a waiver from FCC rules to allow satellites above 600 km to be disposed of into “Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” That is, instead of burning them up in Earth’s atmosphere, SpaceX wants the flexibility to move retired satellites into other orbits around Earth, or potentially into orbit around the Sun.

articles.title: Toronto considering a $2/mo 911 fee amid financial constraints
articles.text:
The City of Toronto is looking for ways to put a little bit more cash in its pocket amid a series of “current and longer-term financial pressures.”
According to a report from the City of Toronto, staff are floating the possibility of adding a monthly Next Generation 911 fee to Toronto cellphone bills, alongside revisiting a commercial parking levy and increasing the city’s Municipal Accommodation Tax.
If approved, the city manager would be authorized to “formally engage telecommunications carriers to negotiate and execute agreements for the collection and remittance” of the fee.
According to the report, the money from the fees would be used to fund investments in emergency services and could bring in up to $65 million in total revenue in both 2027 and 2028.
The report also noted that “following implementation, it’s expected this revenue would be relatively stable with minor year-over-year revenue fluctuations based on annual changes to mobile phone usage.”
“The NG911 fee is not designed to generate revenue for new initiatives. Funding received through an NG911 monthly fee will support existing operating and/or capital investments in next-generation emergency services (offsetting operating, technology, and training costs).”
To add some context, NG911 was first introduced to Canada in 2017, although it was slowly added across different areas before being added in Toronto in 2024. NG911 uses technology to reduce the number of calls to the call centre by automatically calling back 911 hang-ups. In fact, Toronto Police told CP24 that 27 per cent of the 911 call volume was due to “misdialed or pocket calls.”
911 fees aren’t new in Canada, though this would be a first for Ontario. Currently, seven provinces charge 911 fees, with Prince Edward Island charging only $0.70/mo and the Northwest Territories charging $3/mo. Toronto’s $2/mo fee would be $0.22 cheaper than Saskatchewan’s current 911 fee.
If the new fee is approved, you could start seeing it on your cellphone bill starting in October, 2027.
Source: City of Toronto via CP24

articles.title: Kioxia to Showcase XL-FLASH Generation 3 Technology, the Next-Generation Low-Latency, High-Performance Flash Memory for AI
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Kioxia to Showcase XL-FLASH Generation 3 Technology, the Next-Generation Low-Latency, High-Performance Flash Memory for AI
Kioxia Corporation, a world leader in memory solutions, today announced that it will showcase a prototype of its XL-FLASH generation 3 technology, the next generation of its low-latency, high-performance flash memory for AI applications, at KIOXIA Forum in Tokyo on November 26, 2026.
XL-FLASH features significantly lower read latency and higher write endurance than typical NAND flash memory and is being developed for use as a new memory tier that bridges the gap in performance, capacity and cost between storage and DRAM.XL-FLASH generation 3 flash memory leverages CMOS directly Bonded to Array (CBA) technology, a key feature of Kioxia's BiCS FLASH 3D flash memory, to deliver approximately 70% higher bit density than XL-FLASH generation 2 flash memory while maintaining high performance. It also achieves an average read latency of 3 microseconds—less than one-tenth of BiCS FLASH generation 8 TLC products. In addition, power efficiency for reads in 512-byte units has been improved by approximately 135% compared to XL-FLASH generation 2 flash memory. Samples for functional evaluation are scheduled to ship to select customers in March 2027.
The growth of data-intensive applications, including generative AI, has driven a rapid increase in demand for high-capacity memory in computing systems. However, keeping most data in DRAM presents challenges in terms of capacity, cost and power consumption. By leveraging the read latency and power efficiency of XL-FLASH, new system architectures can store data appropriately based on access frequency and performance requirements, complementing DRAM or replacing a portion of it with flash memory. This approach will expand memory capacity and reduce system total cost of ownership (TCO) in AI servers, data centers and other applications.
Kioxia will continue to leverage the speed, power efficiency and endurance of XL-FLASH while pursuing its use across a range of applications, including Super High IOPS SSDs and Compute Express Link (CXL)-enabled memory expansion modules. Through these efforts, Kioxia aims to create a new memory tier that bridges the gap between DRAM and conventional storage.

articles.title: É difícil imaginar que humanidade manterá o controle, diz Meta sobre IA
articles.text:
É difícil imaginar que humanidade manterá o controle, diz Meta sobre IA
Em post, diretor de inteligência artificial da big tech destaca a chegada iminente da chamada superinteligência.
Uma inteligência artificial mil vezes mais capaz que nós humanos dificilmente ficará sob nosso controle. É o que afirma Alexandr Wang, diretor de inteligência da Meta, em uma publicação no X. O executivo destacou a chegada iminente da chamada superinteligência, próxima fase da IA que tem gerado muitas preocupações entre desenvolvedores e líderes do setor.
Segundo Wang, além da inteligência muito maior, essa nova etapa também traria o chamado aprimoramento recursivo, ou seja, a possibilidade de realizar melhorias por conta própria, sem supervisão humana.
No post, o diretor diz ainda não concordar com uma “entrega” da sociedade à IA, mas que acredita no desenvolvimento da tecnologia pensando em um “futuro positivo” para a humanidade. Além disso, ele aponta que as ações relacionadas às IAs no próximo ano teriam “grande consequência no mundo em que vamos viver”.
Em sua publicação no X, Wang fala sobre a resolução da Hipótese de Riemann, um dos problemas matemáticos mais famosos do mundo. Em 20 de novembro, um matemático da Anthropic, Levent Alpöge, anunciou que havia resolvido a questão de 160 anos atrás utilizando o Claude, IA da companhia.
Segundo Wang, a descoberta da bomba atômica seria um mero “dever de casa” perto da resolução da hipótese de Riemann.
Ele afirma ainda que os questionamentos feitos por profissionais ao uso da inteligência artifcial no processo apontam para uma resistência da sociedade às futuras automações envolvendo desenvolvimento científico e tecnológico – algo que ele classifica como inevitável.
Após defender a ideia de que a chegada da superinteligência é iminente, o executivo da Meta falou que há um “pensamento preguiçoso” na indústria de IA.
Wang diz que o desenvolvimento com segurança não é suficiente para evitar problemas no futuro, sendo necessário também investir na construção de uma tecnologia que “entregue um futuro positivos para a humanidade”. Mas, para isso, seria necessário mudar a lógica de desenvolvimento atual.
Recentemente, outro líder de IA falou sobre a necessidade de “aceitar algumas coisas ruins” no desenvolvimento da IA, além da importância de “não se entregar” à tecnologia, o que levaria à perda de controle da situação.
Outros nomes do setor também têm se posicionado de maneira mais alarmista, como o próprio Dario Amodei, da Anthropic, que defendeu a diminuição no ritmo de desenvolvimento da tecnologia dias após um ex-funcionário falar publicamente sobre os riscos da superinteligência para a humanidade.

articles.title: Ladybird browser’s first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable
articles.text:
Note: At the time of writing, I was unaware of criticism directed at Ladybird creator Andreas Kling’s public statements. Readers interested in this background can find further context in accounts by Kelson Vibber and Drew DeVault.
After four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux. Previously, curious users had to compile the browser themselves from its source. Now it’s an installable package with automatic updating.
Ladybird is most notable for what it isn’t: another browser fork. Where Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera all run on Google’s Blink engine, and Firefox depends on Gecko, Ladybird’s rendering engine and its LibJS JavaScript engine were written from scratch. “The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork,” project lead Andreas Kling wrote in Monday’s announcement. “The browser around it is modest, but functional.”
A fourth engine
Nearly the entire modern web currently runs on three browser engines. There’s WebKit (Safari), Gecko (Firefox), and the biggest of them all, Blink (Chromium). Those limited options mean that web developers often end up optimizing sites for Chromium specifically, since that’s where the majority of traffic is, and as a result, the whole web platform tends to follow suit toward whatever the dominant engine supports.
An independent implementation of web standards has value not just by providing additional competition in the market, but because it can’t help but reveal places where sites depend on Chromium behaviors rather than published specifications. The fact that Ladybird exists isn’t likely to shift the market tides any time soon, but every new browser engine increases the number of implementations that standards can be tested against, which can surface Chromium-specific assumptions and push the ecosystem toward the spec.
Some background
The Ladybird project was borne out of Kling’s SerenityOS project, an attempt to develop a new independent OS from scratch, before splitting off as a separate project. Kling formed the Ladybird Browser Initiative, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit funded by sponsorships and donations. The project’s site highlights that there are no sponsored search engine deals supporting the project like many other popular browsers, and sponsoring entities have no say in the project roadmap.

articles.title: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia's code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it
articles.text:
When Jensen Huang gave his first all-hands address since returning as CEO, there was an odd emphasis on Nvidia’s code of conduct. He admitted to violating the code, then emphasized that no one was exempt from it. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” Huang said, according to Wired. “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” still matter. In other words, the code applies to everyone, but breaking it doesn’t automatically cost anyone their job, including, apparently, the CEO.
It’s an awkward stance for a company whose CEO has admitted to breaking its rules. A central part of modern human resources, a code of conduct can seem like a quasi-legal rulebook that lays out unacceptable behavior. But experts say most codes are better understood as a reflection of corporate culture. When an infraction goes unpunished, the main risk isn’t legal but cultural — that employees will feel embarrassed or even angry about the company they work for. That’s the risk Huang now faces at Nvidia.
Matt Plass, chief market strategy officer at LRN, an ethics and compliance training outfit, recently surveyed more than 2,000 workers across different industries for a study on workplace codes of conduct. As Plass sees it, the biggest risk is that employees will become ashamed of their workplace.
“People coming into the workforce now, ethics is incredibly important to them,” he told TechCrunch. “They’re really mindful of the ethical standards of their company. They’re really embarrassed and angry when senior leadership lets them down.”
The consequences of violating the rules aren’t always tangible, but they’re definitely real. Plass gave one example of a company that banned corporate travel to cut costs — only to have its CEO turn up in a VIP box at the Olympics.
“For over a decade afterwards, ‘the Olympics’ was used within that company as an example of the worst thing an employee could do. People would say, ‘Yeah, I shouldn’t have done that, but it’s not like I went to the Olympics.’”
Plass says companies that remove an executive typically do so after an investigation, then try to win back employees. “In most organizations they make a change at the top based on what’s happened,” he said, “and then they will have a hearts-and-minds initiative, to go out to their employee base and their customers and their investors and everybody else, and say, we get it. We’re sorry. We’ve changed. That’s essentially what they do.”
Of course, that playbook is harder to follow at a company like Nvidia, where Huang left without a clear succession plan, and there are serious doubts about whether the company could continue to thrive without him. In cases like that, Plass acknowledges there’s no easy answer.
“I would draw a distinction there between the kind of companies where the CEO is a kind of godhead figure … where the person and the company are almost impossible to separate,” he said. “There it’s much, much harder to deal with.”
In that context, Huang’s stutter-step over the code of conduct is easier to understand. Judging by the employee campaign for his reinstatement, Huang’s return hasn’t created a morale problem so far. But as the coming months put more pressure on Huang and his colleagues, sidestepping the code could end up costing Nvidia something harder to measure — its employees’ pride in the company.

articles.title: Black Friday: So baust du dir mit ChatGPT einen Preisalarm
articles.text:
Black Friday: So baust du mit ChatGPT einen Preisalarm
Am Black Friday locken viele Rabatte: Statt in dutzenden Tabs Preise zu vergleichen, kannst du die Suche an KI abgeben. Prompt Engineer Susanne Renate Schneider hat das für den Podcast t3n MeisterPrompter getestet. Sie teilt, wo der kurze Prompt funktioniert und warum es gut ist, dass Shopping nicht automatisch funktioniert.
Prompt erstellt automatisch eine Aufgabe
Mit einem einfachen Prompt erstellte sie eine Aufgabe in ChatGPT: „Ich will mir [Produkt nennen] kaufen. Ist das gerade irgendwo günstiger? Sag mir Bescheid, wenn der Preis fällt.“ Der Zusatz am Ende gibt den Impuls für eine automatisch eingeplante Aufgabe.
Dabei prüft die KI im Hintergrund in festen Abständen, ob der Preis fällt. Aus dem kurzen Prompt schreibt ChatGPT eine lange Aufgabenbeschreibung. Darin steht unter anderem, keine Angebote bei zweifelhaften Händlern auszuspielen. Wichtig ist, diese automatisch generierten Anweisungen direkt zu prüfen, denn sie können fehlerhaft sein.
Für ChatGPT war der Händler zu unseriös
Gleichzeitig war der erste Test kurz ernüchternd: Renate recherchierte selbst im Netz und fand ein günstigeres Angebot. Das teilte sie auch im KI-Chat mit. Die Reaktion von ChatGPT: Das Angebot wurde gesehen, die Händlerbewertungen seien jedoch zu schlecht. Renate prüfte das selbst nach, demnach hatte die KI Recht.
Dennoch rät sie davon ab, sich vollständig auf diese automatische Suche zu verlassen. Es ist nicht auszuschließen, dass beispielsweise Fake-Shops trotz entsprechendem Hinweis in der Übersicht landen. Und für Nutzende ist unklar, wie die KI zu ihrer Wertung kommt.
Als automatisierte Hilfe zur Übersichtserstellung nutzt Renate die Funktion weiterhin. Aber was bedeutet diese Automatisierung eigentlich für die Zukunft des Shoppings? Einen Ausblick und den vollständigen Prompt gibt es in der verlinkten Episode.
Hier hörst du t3n MeisterPrompter – auf allen Plattformen
Den Podcast hörst du über die Podcast-Plattform deiner Wahl. Gib dafür in der Suche „t3n MeisterPrompter“ ein. Alternativ findest du direkte Verlinkungen hier:
Du hast einen Vorschlag für ein Episoden-Thema? Schreib uns unter meisterprompter@t3n.de. Renate erreichst du außerdem über Instagram und Tiktok unter @renate.gpt oder du meldest dich auf Instagram oder Tiktok unter @t3n_magazin.

articles.title: XEBO.ai bags 10.5M funding from Emirates Growth Fund
articles.text:
XEBO.ai bags $10.5M funding from Emirates Growth Fund
The capital injection will primarily enhance XEBO voice-of-customer portfolio, expanding capability into call analytics and digital experience monitoring. A key portion of the funding will advance agentic AI.
Dubai-headquartered technology firm XEBO.ai has raised $10.5 million in Series A funding from the Emirates Growth Fund, marking the sovereign investor as its first institutional partner.
Founded in 2017 by Yash Sultania and Anand Nigam, XEBO is an AI-native experience management platform that converts customer and employee feedback into decision-ready insights. Experience management platforms help organisations capture feedback across surveys, social listening and customer journey mapping to guide strategic operational decisions.
The capital injection will primarily enhance XEBO voice-of-customer portfolio, expanding capability into call analytics and digital experience monitoring. A key portion of the funding will advance agentic AI.
Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Yash Sultania explained that the investment enables the team to “deepen our VoC portfolio, with agentic AI at its core, and take it to customers around the world faster”.
Beyond software development, the firm plans to expand its commercial operations across the Gulf Cooperation Council region, establish a presence in the United States, and recruit senior operational leaders.
The company also intends to leverage technology integrations with partner channels such as Microsoft to widen enterprise reach. Co-founder Anand Nigam noted that the backing allows the firm to “drive technology innovation, strengthen our presence in existing markets and expand into new geographies as we scale globally”.
The experience management sector has historically been dominated by legacy global platforms, but XEBO has built traction with over 350 enterprise clients across banking, aviation, telecommunications and healthcare. Operating from offices in the United States, the UAE, India and Saudi Arabia, the company has received industry recognition from analyst firms Gartner, IDC and Forrester.
Anshul Garg, Investment Director at Emirates Growth Fund, highlighted that XEBO managed to “build an innovative product that addresses a real market need” while demonstrating relevance alongside established global players.
The Emirates Growth Fund represents the flagship growth equity investor of the United Arab Emirates. Launched by Dr Sultan Al Jaber at Make it in the Emirates 2025 and backed by Emirates Development Bank, it stands as the only UAE sovereign fund focused exclusively on growth-stage enterprises through strategic minority equity investments.
Matthew Singh, Chief Investment Officer at Emirates Growth Fund, noted that the firm “has proven itself with leading enterprises in demanding markets” and remains “well placed to scale internationally”.

articles.title: 7 places, 400 km d’autonomie et un prix cassé : le futur Dacia Jogger électrique va frapper un grand coup
articles.text:
En presque 20 ans de carrière, la Dacia Sandero s’apprête à vivre une révolution avec plus de design, plus de technologie, plus de confort et une inédite motorisation 100 % électrique. Ça, c’est déjà dans les cartons. Mais qui dit nouvelle Sandero dit nouveau Jogger, pas vrai ? Si l’information n’a pas encore été confirmée, il est quasiment certain que le 7 places suivra le même chemin que la citadine dont il dérive étroitement.
Il faudra donc parier sur une version électrique permise par la plateforme CMF-B. Cette hypothèse donne alors de beaux indices sur la partie technique puisque cette base est également utilisée par la Renault 5. Il est ainsi admis que la citadine française accueille une batterie de 40 ou 52 kWh, cette dernière offrant jusqu’à 430 km d’autonomie. Il est donc très probable que le futur Jogger électrique reprenne ce dernier pack.
La grande batterie de la Renault 5 pour atteindre 400 km d’autonomie
L’accumulateur de 40 kWh permettrait de contenir les prix, certes, mais son rayon d’action trop limité n’aurait pas grand sens sur un véhicule aussi familial que le Jogger. Tous les espoirs reposent donc sur la batterie de 52 kWh, qui pourrait permettre au véhicule d’atteindre les 400 km d’autonomie. La charge rapide arriverait en série en pointant à 100 kW en pic, comme sur la R5. Que du blabla, dites-vous ?
Dans un entretien accordé à Auto Express, Katrin Adt, la PDG de Dacia, affirme qu’un nouveau Jogger est plus qu’une éventualité : « nous l’envisageons toujours du point de vue des besoins de nos clients, et nous constatons que nous proposons une offre très spécifique, avec une clientèle fidèle. Il occupe donc une place bien particulière, et nous réfléchissons constamment à la manière de le pérenniser ».
De l’hybride, un nouveau visage inspiré du Striker et un tarif autour de 28 000 €
Bien sûr, il est certain que le futur Jogger ne sera pas uniquement proposé en version électrique. Les déclinaisons essence et hybride subsisteront pour assurer le cœur des ventes. Pas de diesel, en revanche. Mais ce n’est pas censé être une surprise. D’ailleurs, ce n’est pas la seule chose qui sera prévisible. Le style devrait ainsi reprendre les grandes lignes du Striker, avec un visage inédit.
Les feux horizontaux du Jogger actuel laisseront ainsi place à des optiques en forme d’équerre alors que l’ensemble devrait se caractériser par un dessin plus moderne et fluide. Même histoire à bord, où la présentation évoluera par petites touches pour améliorer sa qualité globale. Le but est, là encore, de ne pas faire exploser les prix. Une entrée de gamme aux alentours des 28 000 € pour la version électrique serait raisonnable.

articles.title: Vers un événement Intel fin février : la présentation officielle de Nova Lake ?
articles.text:
Que de mystère autour de la prochaine génération de processeurs signée Intel : le lancement pourrait finalement arriver en mars prochain.
Intel joue gros. Le lancement de son architecture Nova Lake sera l'occasion de se tester sur le marché du processeur grand public pour un groupe américain qui subit de plein fouet le recul du marché du PC domestique et la concurrence de son meilleur ennemi, AMD.
Un événement presse fin février ?
À Clubic, nous parlons des puces Nova Lake depuis maintenant plusieurs mois et, pour être tout à fait honnête, les premières informations remontent même à plusieurs années. Mais, on commence enfin à avoir du très concret.
En effet, alors que certaines rumeurs évoquaient une possible présentation par Intel lors du CES 2027 qui se tiendra début janvier à Las Vegas, tout porte à croire que l'entreprise présidée par Lip-Bu Tan se dirige vers un lancement commercial un peu plus tardif. Cela dit, l'un ne contredit pas forcément l'autre, le site VideoCardz précise justement les choses.
À en croire notre confrère, plusieurs médias auraient été contactés par Intel afin de vérifier qu'ils soient bien disponibles pour un événement autour de sa prochaine génération de processeurs desktop. VideoCardz souligne qu'il s'agit d'un événement d'une durée de quatre jours, organisé à Berlin, et que cela se passerait au cours de la dernière semaine de février.
Un événement allemand qui n'empêcherait pas la tenue d'une présentation officielle lors du CES de Las Vegas six semaines plus tôt, au contraire. Intel aurait alors dans l'idée de, d'abord, présenter la nouvelle génération de puces, en grande pompe, dans le Nevada.
Une présentation en deux temps pour Nova Lake
Dans un second temps, Intel réunirait la presse internationale à Berlin pour un événement plus technique, comme le groupe américain a déjà pu le faire par le passé afin de décortiquer la nouvelle architecture.
Cet événement serait aussi bien plus proche du lancement officiel et, donc, de la commercialisation des puces Nova Lake, laquelle pourrait intervenir au cours du mois de mars. VideoCardz souligne qu'un tel calendrier coïnciderait avec les informations reçues dès le mois de juillet : il était alors question d'un lancement en plusieurs étapes pour cette nouvelle génération.
Le premier processeur Nova Lake prévu serait donc le modèle 28 cœurs qui pourrait débouler dans la foulée de cet événement allemand. D'autres modèles seraient ensuite prévus par Intel, tout au long de l'année 2027. Le navire amiral de cette nouvelle génération Nova Lake, le surpuissant modèle 52 cœurs, ne débarquerait pour sa part pas avant le mois de septembre.
Gardez bien à l'esprit que ces différents éléments de calendrier n'ont jamais été confirmés de quelque manière que ce soit par Intel. Toutefois, nos confrères n'ont pas l'habitude de relayer ce genre d'informations sans de solides éléments. Tout porte à croire que deux rendez-vous sont donc pris avec Intel : début janvier et fin février.
Source : VideoCardz

articles.title: Siempre nos han dicho que parar 15 minutos a hacer ejercicio mejora el estudio. La ciencia dice que no es tan sencillo
articles.text:
Cuando nos ponemos a estudiar delante de un tocho de apuntes, es fácil que al rato la concentración comience a flaquear. En este caso, levantarse de la silla para hacer 15 minutos de ejercicio moderado es algo que siempre nos han dicho que puede despejarnos y mejorar el rendimiento académico. El problema es que no es tan fácil.
La base. Uno de los pilares habituales para defender los descansos activos viene de un ensayo publicado en 2014. En este un grupo de investigadores evaluó a 123 niños de entre 10 y 11 años de cuatro colegios de primaria tras hacer una hora de deberes. De este modo, cada estudiante pasó por cuatro escenarios distintos: seguir sin pausa, hacer un descanso pasivo, realizar 15 minutos de actividad física moderada o hacer 15 minutos de ejercicio vigoroso.
El resultado determinó que la mejora cognitiva más marcada se daba en el grupo de niños que habían hecho una actividad moderada. Por contra, el ejercicio vigoroso arrojó resultados similares a los que se vieron en hacer un simple descanso pasivo, seguramente por la fatiga que genera.
Tiene sentido. Para explicar cómo el movimiento puede ayudar a fijar todo lo que se ha estudiado, se suele recurrir a un estudio de 2021 donde se analizó todo lo que ocurría en el cerebro cuando se estaba haciendo bicicleta estática. Aquí los investigadores observaron que tanto el ejercicio moderado como el intenso elevaban los niveles de BDNF del cerebro y de anandamida, un endocannabinoide implicado en la plasticidad sináptica.
Tres meses después, los participantes recordaban mejor las asociaciones aprendidas tras la sesión de ejercicio moderado que tras el reposo, un efecto acompañado de cambios en los patrones de activación del hipocampo detectados mediante resonancia magnética funcional.
El deporte influye. Otro argumento habitual señala que los deportes de equipo aportan un extra cognitivo frente a actividades individuales como correr o nadar. Y esto es algo que también se ha estudiado, determinando que los deportes en lo que el entorno cambia constantemente, como el fútbol, favorecen en mayor medida el control inhibitorio y la flexibilidad cognitiva.
El rendimiento académico. Hasta aquí sabemos que el deporte puede mejorar nuestro cerebro y las conexiones que va realizando, pero cuando comprobamos si de verdad tiene un impacto en cómo rendimos en el estudio, la verdad es que hay varios matices. Estos los aporta una revisión paraguas donde se comparó el impacto de la actividad física puntual a la hecha durante vairos meses.
El resultado nos mostró que, mientras la actividad física regular y sostenida en el tiempo tiene un efecto positivo moderado en los logros académicos, el ejercicio puntual no mostró esta misma mejora de rendimiento. Esto nos hace que ver que parar de estudiar 15 minutos para hacer ejercicio no aporta beneficios al estudio, sino que es importante mantener una rutina si de verdad queremos ver sus efectos.

articles.title: Ce téléviseur OLED LG noté 5/5 passe sous les 2 000 € à l'occasion du Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Top produit : Le téléviseur LG 77C6 à 1 999,00 €
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le téléviseur LG 77C6 passe à 1 999,00 € chez Fnac.com, Boulanger.com et Darty.com, soit une baisse d'environ 2 % et 40,00 € d'économie. Doté d'un contraste parfait et de quatre ports HDMI 2.1 très efficaces en jeu vidéo, ce modèle affiche une note actuelle de 5/5 dans nos tests.
LG décline son téléviseur OLED 77C6 dans un format géant de 77 pouces pensé pour le cinéma à domicile et le jeu vidéo exigeant. Contrairement aux versions de 55 et 65 pouces, cette référence intègre la technologie de dalle Tandem OLED issue des séries supérieures de la marque. Ce grand écran a pleinement convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage sur le banc d'essai.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, ce modèle descend à 1 999,00 € chez Fnac.com, Boulanger.com et Darty.com, soit environ 2 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (2 039,00 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 40,00 € sur cette diagonale de 196 cm.
Une dalle OLED très lumineuse pour magnifier les contenus HDR
Le téléviseur LG 77C6 se distingue avant tout par son intensité lumineuse en HDR, un secteur où les dalles OLED traditionnelles montrent souvent leurs limites en pleine journée. Notre laboratoire a mesuré un pic de luminosité maximale de 2 105 cd/m², une valeur qui permet de faire éclater les hautes lumières dans les films récents tout en conservant le contraste infini et les noirs parfaits propres à l'OLED. Vous pouvez retrouver toutes nos mesures détaillées dans notre test complet.
Cette performance visuelle est complétée par une gestion exemplaire de la couleur en haute dynamique, avec un Delta E mesuré à 1,8 garantissant une fidélité chromatique parfaite pour l'œil humain. L'appareil est également adapté aux consoles de salon et aux ordinateurs grâce à une fréquence de rafraîchissement atteignant 165 Hz.
LG 77C6
Points forts
- Contraste parfait de l’Oled.
- Pic lumineux HDR en très nette hausse.
- Couverture Rec.2020 au niveau du G6.
- Très bonnes performances en jeu vidéo.
- Quatre ports HDMI 2.1.
- Faible consommation.
- Bon système audio.
Points faibles
- Reflets encore visibles face aux haut de gamme.
- Spatialisation audio limitée.
- Télécommande non rétroéclairée.
- Compte LG désormais obligatoire.
Une connectique complète taillée pour les joueurs malgré quelques reflets
Pour le jeu vidéo, l'écran assure une excellente fluidité grâce à ses quatre ports HDMI 2.1 qui acceptent les flux 4K à cadence élevée sans aucune restriction de bande passante. Notre banc d'essai a relevé un retard à l'affichage contenu à 9,3 ms, ce qui évite tout décalage perceptible entre la manette et l'action à l'écran. La consommation électrique reste également maîtrisée avec une valeur de 41,7 W/m² mesurée en fonctionnement standard.
Le traitement antireflet montre en revanche ses limites avec un taux de réflectance mesuré à 26 %, ce qui laissera des reflets visibles si vous installez le téléviseur face à une fenêtre en pleine journée. La télécommande n'est pas non plus rétroéclairée et la spatialisation du système audio intégré demeure limitée dans les grands volumes. Ces concessions ne poseront toutefois aucun souci aux spectateurs qui regardent leurs films dans l'obscurité avec un ensemble d'enceintes dédié.
Philips 77OLED811 : l'autre option face au LG 77C6
Le Philips 77OLED811 partage avec l'écran de LG une diagonale de 77 pouces, une fréquence de dalle grimpant à 165 Hz et quatre entrées HDMI 2.1 pensées pour le jeu. Il se différencie principalement par son système d'éclairage d'ambiance Ambilight qui projette les couleurs de l'image sur le mur arrière, mais il utilise l'interface Titan OS dont l'ergonomie générale est moins aboutie que celle de WebOS chez LG. Actuellement noté 5/5, le téléviseur de Philips s'affiche à un tarif inférieur de 105,20 € par rapport au prix remisé du modèle LG.
Le Philips 77OLED811 offre une alternative financièrement plus accessible avec le confort visuel de l'Ambilight, mais le LG 77C6 conserve l'avantage d'une dalle Tandem OLED plus lumineuse pour justifier cet écart de prix.
Philips 77OLED811
Points forts
- Excellente colorimétrie SDR et HDR
- Calibration globale.
- Contraste parfait et noirs profonds de l’Oled.
- Pic lumineux en nette hausse par rapport à l'OLED810.
- Quatre ports HDMI 2.1 et dalle 165 Hz.
- Pied orientable.
- Ambilight toujours sympathique.
Points faibles
- Titan OS encore loin d'être abouti.
- Reflets bien présents.
- Basses qui font grésiller le châssis.
- Consommation assez élevée.

articles.title: DuckDuckGo Browser
articles.text:
Seamlessly take control of your personal information, no matter where the Internet takes you. DuckDuckGo for Windows comes with these best-in-class privacy protections switched on by default, leading to a better everyday user experience.
By blocking trackers before they load, for example, our desktop browsers use about 60% less data than Chrome. Switching is easy, too; you can import passwords and bookmarks from another browser or password manager in just a few clicks.
How does DuckDuckGo Browser protect user privacy?
The browser blocks many third-party trackers and upgrades connections to HTTPS when available, without requiring additional extensions. It also restricts third-party cookies by default and allows users to control site-specific permissions, such as location or camera access, on an individual site basis.
How does DuckDuckGo Browser differ from private or incognito modes in other browsers?
Rather than acting as a temporary mode, the DuckDuckGo Browser applies privacy protections consistently across all browsing sessions by default.
How does Duck Player work with YouTube videos?
Duck Player allows YouTube videos to be viewed in a privacy-focused player that reduces tracking and limits personalized ads. It plays videos without requiring users to be signed into a Google account and minimizes data sharing while watching content.
Does DuckDuckGo Browser store or synchronize browsing data?
The browser does not build user profiles or track browsing behavior by default, and provides a single action to clear tabs, data, and history. Data synchronization across devices is limited compared to some mainstream browsers, reflecting a design choice focused on privacy and reduced data collection.
Can it be used as a primary daily browser?
Yes. DuckDuckGo Browser supports modern web standards and common browsing tasks, including tabs, bookmarks, and password management, making it suitable for everyday use.
Is DuckDuckGo Browser based on Chromium?
On desktop platforms, DuckDuckGo Browser uses system web engines-such as Chromium on Windows-while applying its own interface and privacy controls on top. On mobile devices, it relies on the underlying platform's web engine, using Blink/Chromium on Android and WebKit on iOS, in line with operating system requirements.
Features
Enjoy a better browsing experience on Windows thanks to the DuckDuckGo browser's unique built-in privacy protections:
- Duck Player, a YouTube player that lets you watch YouTube videos without privacy-invading ads and keeps video views from impacting your recommendations.‌‌
- Tracker blocking that goes above and beyond what's available from Chrome and other browsers. Our 3rd-party Tracker Loading Protection, for example, blocks the hidden trackers from companies like Google and Facebook lurking on other websites before they get a chance to load. ‌‌‌‌
- Smarter Encryption to ensure that more of the websites you visit and the links you click are encrypted, relative to other browsers.
- Cookie Pop-up Management, a tool that automatically selects the most private options available and hides cookie consent pop-ups. ‌‌‌‌
- The Fire Button, which burns recent browsing data in one click. (There's also a handy "Fireproof" option for any sites you want to stay logged into.) ‌‌‌‌
- Email Protection, which can hide your email address with unique @duck.com addresses when signing up for things online.
- Making the switch is easy; new users can import bookmarks and passwords from other browsers and password managers.
DuckDuckGo Browser for Android
- Tap Fire Button, Burn Data - clear all your tabs and browsing data with one tap.
- Escape Online Tracking - automatically block hidden third-party trackers we can find lurking on websites you visit, which stops the companies behind those trackers from collecting and selling your data.
- Search Privately - our private search engine comes built-in so you can search the Internet without being tracked.
- Enforce Encryption - force sites to use an encrypted (HTTPS) connection where available, protecting your data from prying eyes, like from unwanted snoopers and Internet service providers.
- Decode Privacy - each site you visit gets a Privacy Grade (A-F) so you can see how protected you are at a glance, and you can even dig into the details to see who we caught trying to track you.
- Signal Your Privacy Preference with GPC - built into the browser, Global Privacy Control (GPC) intends to help you express your legal opt-out rights automatically. This will tell websites not to sell or share your personal information under future legal frameworks (e.g., CCPA, GDPR) in various states or countries.
What's New
- DuckDuckGo Browser 0.181.4.0 for Windows
- Android version updated to 5.305.0
- DuckDuckGo Browser 1.217.0 for macOS
 
  - We fixed an issue where clicking a link would open in new window instead of a new tab on macOS Sonoma.
  - We fixed an issue where Duck Player was not loading videos on macOS Big Sur.
Watch YouTube Without Ads on the DuckDuckGo Browser
- DuckDuckGo now blocks most video ads! Use our free browser to get the full YouTube experience, minus the ads.
- YouTube Ad Blocking joins our powerful lineup of browsing protections that manage cookie pop-ups, protect you from invasive tracker-based web ads, and more.
- YouTube Ad Blocking is already on by default for most iPhone, Windows, and Mac users! It will be auto-enabled for Android soon, but users can opt in via browser Settings in the meantime.
Interruption-free YouTube with DuckDuckGo
Tired of ads interrupting your videos? Us, too. The DuckDuckGo browser now blocks most video ads, including on YouTube! This new feature blocks ads that run before and during your videos, letting you watch YouTube without the interruptions.
If you've been here a while, you already know that the DuckDuckGo browser also protects you from invasive ads and annoying pop-ups on multiple fronts. We block tracker-powered web ads before they can load. We have Global Privacy Control enabled by default, expressing your opt-out rights by telling websites not to sell or share your personal information. We can even manage cookie pop-ups behind the scenes, so you don't have to deal with the distraction.
How do I access YouTube Ad Blocking?
YouTube Ad Blocking is on by default for iOS, Windows, and Mac. So, there's no need to adjust your settings, if your app is up to date; just open the browser and start enjoying ad-free videos! The feature will be on by default for Android soon, but in the meantime, turn it on in your browser's Settings > Ad Blocking. If you don't see YouTube Ad Blocking on your device, try updating your app.
On all devices, you can disable or re-enable YouTube Ad Blocking any time from your browser's Settings > Ad Blocking. You can also turn it on and off while you're watching a video. On desktop, click the video icon next to the green shield in your address bar. On mobile, tap ☰ > Disable YouTube Ad Blocking.
When you disable ad blocking mid-video, the browser will prompt you to send an error report, alerting us to any problems. This is completely optional, anonymous, and helps us make our product better...so we appreciate it!
Please note: if you're on a mobile device, links to YouTube videos may open in the YouTube app by default. To enjoy DuckDuckGo's YouTube Ad Blocking, you need to open the YouTube website in the DuckDuckGo browser. It won't work in the YouTube app.
Manage your YouTube Ad Blocking and Duck Player preferences from browser Settings.
Is YouTube Ad Blocking different from Duck Player?
Yes, they're different – but complementary!
Duck Player is the browser's built-in video player that lets you watch YouTube videos in a distraction-free theater mode. It also protects you from tracking cookies and personalized ads by enforcing YouTube's strictest privacy settings for embedded video. This means what you watch in Duck Player won't influence your YouTube recommendations. (It also won't save your place in playlists.) Opt in to Duck Player and adjust your preferences from your browser Settings > Ad Blocking.
YouTube Ad Blocking blocks video ads on the YouTube website, so you can watch without interruption. It's the regular YouTube experience, just without ads. So you're free to take advantage of YouTube features like remembering your viewing history and saving your spot in playlists.
You don't have to pick just one: you can have YouTube Ad Blocking and Duck Player enabled at the same time.
How does YouTube Ad Blocking work?
To detect and block YouTube ads, we use community-driven filter lists sourced from uBlock Origin. These lists are maintained by an active open-source community and are regularly updated to keep up with changes to how ads are served. We may also apply our own rules to improve compatibility and reduce breakage. As with most ad blockers, using our ad blocker can lead to some additional buffering times. But once your video loads, you won't be interrupted with ads.
Previous Release Notes:
DuckDuckGo Browser – now available for Windows
Windows users, this one's for you! Starting today, our desktop browser for Windows is officially in public beta – no invite codes, no waiting list, just a fast, lightweight browser that makes the Internet less creepy and less cluttered. DuckDuckGo for Windows is already equipped with nearly all the privacy protections and everyday features that users know and trust from our iOS, Mac, and Android browsers – and it's getting closer to parity with those browsers every day.
Relative to Mac users, Windows users work across a wider variety of hardware and software configurations. During our brief closed beta period, we've been gathering testers' feedback and making improvements to meet as many of those needs as possible, but we haven't tested every configuration yet, so if you do see any issues, please send feedback!
Extensions and the Windows browser
The browser doesn't have extension support yet, but we plan to add it in the future. In the meantime, we've built the browser to include features that meet the same needs as the most popular extensions: ad-blocking and secure password management.
Secure password management: Our browser includes our own secure and easy-to-use password manager that can automatically remember and fill in login credentials. DuckDuckGo for Windows can now also suggest secure passwords for new logins. This will get even more convenient soon when we roll out private syncing across devices, so you'll be able to sync your bookmarks and saved passwords between different devices, whether you're using a DuckDuckGo browser on Windows, iOS, Android, or Mac. ‌‌‌‌
Ad blocking: DuckDuckGo for Windows is equipped with our privacy-protecting alternative to ad blockers: the browser blocks invasive trackers before they load, effectively eliminating ads that rely on that creepy tracking. (Because so many ads work that way, you'll see way fewer ads – if any at all.) We also remove the whitespace left behind by those ads for a clean, distraction-free look without the need for an outside ad blocker.‌‌‌‌ ‌‌‌‌
Duck Player, our browser's more-private way to watch YouTube: This built-in video player protects you from tracking cookies and personalized ads with a distraction-free interface that incorporates YouTube's strictest privacy settings for embedded video. (In our testing, by blocking the trackers behind personalized ads, Duck Player prevented ads from loading on most videos altogether.) YouTube still logs video views, so it's not completely anonymous, but none of the videos you watch in Duck Player contribute to your personalized recommendations or your YouTube advertising profile. You can leave the feature always-on, or opt in on individual videos.

articles.title: Nintendo ya permite regalar juegos digitales en Switch y Switch 2, pero solo dentro del grupo familiar
articles.text:
Nintendo permite desde mediados de noviembre regalar juegos digitales a otros miembros del grupo familiar en la Switch y la Switch 2, según informó la compañía en su sitio oficial. La función llega a la tienda eShop antes de las fiestas y entrega el obsequio al instante.
Con la novedad, el comprador puede enviar juegos elegibles, contenido descargable adicional y paquetes de mejora que adquiera en la eShop desde su propia consola. Hasta ahora, un jugador que quería regalar un título digital a otro tenía que resolverlo por fuera de esa tienda.
Nintendo explicó que cualquier persona con una cuenta Nintendo puede crear un grupo familiar y sumar hasta ocho miembros en total. El nombre es engañoso: según el medio VICE, el grupo no se limita a parientes, y basta con invitar a cuentas existentes o crear una cuenta infantil.
Cómo se envía y cómo se recibe un juego
El proceso se hace dentro de la eShop. Primero hay que buscar el juego, y en su página marcar la casilla “Give as a Gift” (“Regalar”), y avanzar con la compra. Después se elige al destinatario entre los integrantes del grupo y se indica a cuál de sus consolas vinculadas llegará.
Antes de pagar, el comprador escoge el color del papel de regalo virtual y otras opciones. VICE menciona rojo, púrpura y dos tonos de azul. Luego se completa el pago como cualquier otra compra en la tienda.
Nintendo advirtió que el regalo se envía de inmediato, por lo que conviene revisar la selección antes de confirmar. El destinatario lo ve en el menú principal de su consola, donde puede elegirlo, aceptarlo y jugarlo en el acto.
Los límites que fijó la compañía
La empresa precisó tres restricciones. Algunos productos pueden no ser elegibles para regalo digital. Las cuentas supervisadas, que son las de menores administradas por un adulto, no pueden enviar regalos. Y el número de compras para regalar permitidas en un período dado es limitado.
Nintendo no detalló en su anuncio qué títulos quedan excluidos ni cuál es el tope de compras. Tampoco indicó el período en que se aplica ese límite, un dato que el comprador solo conocerá al intentar el envío.
Para recibir la función hace falta tener la consola actualizada. Según la nota de la compañía, la herramienta está disponible en sistemas con la versión 23.5.0 o posterior, lanzada el 9 de noviembre de 2026. La actualización debería descargarse sola si la consola tiene conexión a internet, y también puede iniciarse a mano desde los ajustes del sistema.
En su mensaje, Nintendo presentó la función como una forma de celebrar una ocasión especial con los hijos. La compañía indicó que quien necesite ayuda para armar un grupo familiar puede consultar su página de asistencia oficial.
La fecha de llegada tiene una diferencia entre fuentes. La publicación de Nintendo lleva fecha del 9 de noviembre y ubica la incorporación a la eShop el 16 de noviembre, mientras que VICE, en una nota del 25 de noviembre, habla de un anuncio del 17. Ambas coinciden en que la función ya está activa.
Nintendo eliminará el inicio de sesión con Google y Apple desde 2027
Nintendo dejará de permitir la vinculación de cuentas de Google y Apple con las Cuentas Nintendo a partir del 26 de enero de 2027. Desde ese día no se podrán enlazar esos servicios ni usarlos para crear cuentas o iniciar sesión.
El cambio afectará a Nintendo Switch 2, Switch, Switch Lite y Switch – OLED Model, y también eliminará la misión de puntos platino de My Nintendo por vincular Google.
Quienes ya tengan sesión activa podrían no necesitar reingresar datos. Si se solicita, deberán usar correo y contraseña de su Cuenta Nintendo, o una clave de acceso mediante huella o reconocimiento facial, método que la compañía recomienda para mayor seguridad.

articles.title: The canceled Tesla Cybertruck is the fastest-selling used truck in America
articles.text:
Tesla Cybertruck sales never reached the lofty heights CEO Elon Musk predicted when it launched. But the futuristic, steel-clad EV is finding new life in the used car market, according to analysis of sales figures by iSeeCars.com.
The automotive search engine and research platform analyzed more than 1.1 million sales of one- to five-year-old used vehicles in October 2026 and measured the average days on market by drivetrain, vehicle type, and individual model. The upshot: The Tesla Cybertruck was the fastest-selling used truck, averaging just 39.1 days on the market compared with 65.5 days for trucks overall. Used Cybertrucks sold faster than any other truck, including the Ford Maverick Hybrid, which held the No. 2 spot, and the Rivian R1T, in third place.
According to iSeeCars.com, the Cybertruck’s sales performance lines up with a broader pattern in the used vehicle market: Used battery electric vehicles are hot sellers right now, with 16 of the 25 fastest-selling used cars fully electric. EVs are even edging out hybrids in terms of average days on market. EVs average 45.6 days on market compared to 54.5 days for hybrids and 61 days for gasoline-powered vehicles. Not every EV is selling well, however. For instance, iSeeCars.com found that the Cadillac Escalade IQ was the slowest-selling vehicle in the study, averaging 134.3 days on the market, more than twice the overall industry average.
Karl Brauer, executive analyst at iSeeCars.com, told TechCrunch that high gasoline prices have changed consumer-buying habits, prompting more people to opt for an EV or hybrid over an internal combustion engine vehicle. If high prices persist, as they have since March, that trend could continue.
Keep in mind that these were October sales, the month before Musk announced Tesla would stop making the Cybertruck in 2027. Fuel prices and the relative rarity of Cybertrucks in the used car market were driving demand even before the cancellation announcement, Brauer said.
“The Cybertruck has only been out for a few years, so you have a lot of used ones coming off lease and entering the used car market for the first time,” he said, adding that used Cybertrucks are cheap relative to their MSRP.
The impending cancellation will likely fuel used Cybertruck sales, although the pace may ebb and flow over the next year.
“The canceling of the new Cybertruck is making people kind of aware — it’s like, oh wow, these things aren’t going to be coming anymore,” Brauer said. “Whatever demand is for them, supply will not be continuing to grow.”
Brauer said that once production of the Cybertruck ends — which is expected in summer 2027 — sales of used versions may pop once again.
“When the last one is being produced, that’ll probably reignite things again, and for a few months after that,” he said.

articles.title: Chefe do Instagram reafirma que app não “escuta” o que você diz
articles.text:
Chefe do Instagram reafirma que app não “escuta” o que você diz
Adam Mosseri fala mais uma vez sobre o tema e garante que aplicativo não usa microfone do celular para direcionar anúncios aos usuários.
O chefe do instagram, Adam Mosseri, falou mais uma vez sobre uma suspeita antiga de usuários do Instagram: o app da Meta usaria o microfone do celular para ouvir o que está sendo falado e direcionar anúncios. O executivo voltou a se pronunciar sobre o assunto nesta terça-feira (24/11) na própria rede social, repetindo o discurso que trouxe em outubro de 2025.
Basicamente, ele nega qualquer tipo de “escuta” pelo app no smartphone. Os argumentos utilizados são os mesmos do ano passado. Segundo ele, essa seria uma grande violação de privacidade por parte do app. Além disso, a bateria acabaria rapidamente, da mesma forma que uma luz vermelha acenderia indicando uma gravação em curso. Dessa vez, em vez de “talvez você veja algo logo depois de falar”, Mosseri reconhece que isso acontece, mas explica que isso é mais psicológico do que tech.
Ou seja: o fato de você identificar anúncios logo depois de falar teria a ver com a sua atenção ao que está na tela, e não ao conteúdo em si. A Meta sempre negou essa teoria, sugerindo que já tem tantas informações sobre os usuários que não faria sentido coletar dados a partir de gravações do tipo.
Em outubro de 2025, um vídeo bem parecido foi publicado pelo executivo. Os argumentos também são idênticos, assim como a “culpada” pelo tema ser levado a público: sua esposa, com quem Mosseri teria discussões anuais sobre. No primeiro vídeo, a legenda chama de Myth Busting, ou uma caça ao mito, em português. Dessa vez ele foi mais sucinto, mas ainda trouxe o mesmo conteúdo.
De acordo com Mosseri, são três os principais motivos para você ter a sensação de que um anúncio apareceu logo após ter falado sobre um assunto:
- Você pode ter visto esse anúncio algumas vezes antes, o que teria levado a falar sobre o tema (antes de vê-lo novamente).
- Depois de ter falado sobre, o assunto fica na sua cabeça. Ao ver o anúncio novamente, fica com a sensação de ter sido direcionado.
- Você pode ter comentado o assunto com algum amigo próximo, cujos dados são, de fato, analisados pelo instagram. Com isso, o anúncio também poderia ser interessante para você, aparecendo na sua conta.
Por esses motivos, o chefe do Instagram reconhece a situação: você comenda sobre um assunto e, logo depois, o anúncio aparece. Mas ele reforça que isso não teria absolutamente nada a ver com gravações de áudio ou vídeo.
Dessa vez, além de argumentar contra a teoria do microfone, Mosseri afirma ter noção de que não vai convencer todos os usuários de que o Instagram não grava suas conversas. Ao reconhecer que a sugestão de produtos e serviços passa, sim, essa sensação, o executivo destaca o uso de outras formas de captação de informações dos usuários.
A própria Meta fala sobre o tema desde 2016, garantindo que não há necessidade de coletar dados dessa maneira. Em um artigo sobre a teoria ainda no Facebook, a empresa destacou que o uso do microfone é exclusivo de áreas em que há algum tipo de permissão por parte do usuário, como gravações de vídeo, por exemplo.

articles.title: Even Doug Ford admits that Ontario gambling ads are ‘out of control’
articles.text:
Ontario Premier Doug Ford has acknowledged that there are too many online gambling ads that run in the province.
Speaking to media on Tuesday en route to his party’s weekly caucus meeting, Ford said that “Every time you pop on the TV, it’s just ads, ads ads” for online gambling, which, he admits, is “not good on the people.” He added that “it’s out of control,” noting that he’s asked cabinet officials for a report on the impacts of all of these ads.
These comments come amid numerous studies showing the rise in gambling-related issues among Canadians. For instance, research released last month by the Alberta Gambling Research Institute (AGRI) found that nearly 130,000 Ontarians now show signs of gambling problems, triple the number in 2018.
And earlier this year, the Canadian Medical Association Journal reported that the number of young men contacting Ontario’s mental health hotline for gambling problems has increased by more than 300 per cent in the last decade.
AGRI told CBC News that these numbers are significant because they demonstrate a continued rise ever since Ontario, under Ford’s leadership, opened the door to private casinos in 2022. It added that while these increases have been seen across Canada, they’re most prevalent in Ontario.
Meanwhile, Ontario iGaming, the organization that regulates the province’s gambling market, is run by the Government of Ontario and even shelved a study that would have tracked data on gambling addiction, according to a Toronto Star investigation. Therefore, Ford’s comments about these gambling ads getting out of control are a little disingenuous, considering it was his government that allowed it to get to this level.
Image credit: Netflix

articles.title: Etsy clarifies AI terms after seller backlash
articles.text:
After backlash from sellers frustrated by Etsy’s new AI policies, which appeared to allow the company to train AI on user artwork, Etsy has now clarified its stance.
In a note published on Monday, CEO Kruti Patel Goyal discussed recent tweaks to the company’s terms of service and admitted that her team “should’ve given you more context on what the updates meant for your creative content.”
“Our recent terms update was meant to reflect the evolving technologies we’re using to build better tools and experiences for sellers and the Etsy community,” Goyal wrote this week. “It was not meant to enable us to train AI models for the purpose of creating copycats of your items. We do not and will not do that.”
Aaron Meshon, a longtime professional illustrator and Etsy seller, told Ars that even though the company had dialed back its AI language somewhat, the changes were mere “sugar coating.”
He said he still plans on shutting down his 15-year-old Etsy store on December 1.
“I would say I’m losing 20 percent of my yearly income,” he said. “It’s a few mortgage payments.”
He noted that Etsy’s announcement also seems to be rather tone-deaf, given that many retailers make a substantial portion of their annual revenue in the run-up to the end-of-year holiday season.

articles.title: Intel Core Ultra 4000 "Nova Lake-S" Preliminary Specs Leaked
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Intel Core Ultra 4000 "Nova Lake-S" Preliminary Specs Leaked
More information has surfaced about Intel's upcoming "Nova Lake-S" desktop CPU lineup. According to an Intel document obtained by Videocardz, the Core Ultra 4000 series lineup will be led by the Ultra 9 4970K BFC, with 28 cores and 144 MB of L3 cache, along with a 5.5 GHz boost clock. The document lists specs for seven Nova Lake-S desktop chips. Videocardz notes that these are C1-stepping qualification samples, so there may be some changes between these specs and the retail models, particularly the final clock speeds. We don't often see changes between qualification samples and retail processors so close to launch, but it's something to remember regardless. 
Looking at the table, the Core Ultra 9 4950K slots in just under the flagship 28-core 4970K BFC. The 4950K also has 28 cores in an 8P+16E+4LPE configuration, but it drops the BFC suffix and doesn't carry the additional L3 cache, topping out at 36 MB. The boost clock drops from 5.5 GHz on the 4970K to 5.4 GHz on the 4950K. This settles the confusion around the 4950K's core count, since the October lineup leak showed it without any LPE cores. There's also the 22-core Ultra 9 4900 BFC, an interesting non-K SKU that has fewer cores than the Ultra 7 models. This model only has a 65 W TDP, while all other leaked variants show a 125 W base power rating.After that, we get the Core Ultra 7 4870K BFC and 4850K, both of which have 24 cores (8P+12E+4LPE) and a 5.2 GHz boost, but are again split by the difference in L3 cache. Moving down the stack, the Core Ultra 5 4650K and 4650KF get 22 cores (6P+12E+4LPE), 30 MB of L3 cache, and a 5.1 GHz boost clock. Of course, the KF variant does not have an iGPU. Curiously, the 125 W 6P+12E+4LPE bLLC chip is missing from this stack, which lines up with leaker Jaykihn's claim that it was moved to Razor Lake. All Nova Lake-S CPUs support DDR5-8000 memory, up from DDR5-6400 on Arrow Lake-S. Per Videocardz, Intel is planning a next-generation desktop event in Berlin between February 22 and 25, which is now expected to be the launch event for Nova Lake-S.

articles.title: Jensen Huang denies special government treatment at first Nvidia all-hands since return — "there are rumors on the internet that apparently I’m a tech bro, and therefore I’m back"
articles.text:
Jensen Huang denies special government treatment at first Nvidia all-hands since return — "there are rumors on the internet that apparently I’m a tech bro, and therefore I’m back"
"That is completely untrue."
Jensen Huang, Nvidia's reinstated CEO, has officially started his apology tour at the Nvidia offices. The firm had its first all-hands meeting since Huang's second coming, and he reportedly had some interesting things to say both about the situation surrounding his departure and the path forward now that he's back.
For those out of the loop, Huang had quit as CEO of Nvidia a couple of weeks ago due to multiple extramarital romantic relationships. The most troublesome of those is with Alice Huang, both a suspected Chinese honeypot and an executive of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which stands accused of siphoning billions' worth of export-controlled Nvidia GPUs to China.
On the all-hands event, Huang started off contrite, saying it was "the hardest company meeting [he's] ever done," and that he's been having daily therapy for at least an hour and a half. He added that Nvidia's code of conduct, mostly written by himself, is still expected to hold up. However, the New York Times remarks that the meeting "began somber before transforming into a defiant airing of grievances."
Perhaps illustrating that point, Jensen reportedly said clearly that he was not the recipient of preferential treatment from either Silicon Valley or the government itself. Some may take umbrage with that statement, given that the White House itself confirmed that President Trump called Nvidia's board himself, asking for Jensen's return, citing concerns with the stock market.
Huang also addressed his active-aggressive management style by reportedly denying he was an abusive boss — yet acknowledging he goes too far on occasion, plus that he needed to keep a high degree of dedication without hurting people.
One interesting tidbit from the meeting was that he's being subjected to a monthly 360º performance review — wherein management collects anonymous feedback from multiple people who work with the reviewee, not just their direct reports. This is an Nvidia first.
The company's board investigation about whether Huang was the target of foreign intelligence continues, though a cynical person may wonder the incentive that the company now has to complete or publish the results of said work.
