articles.title: ‘We are the most apolitical company,’ Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff — as Trump says pardoning the CEO is ‘always an option’
articles.text:
‘We are the most apolitical company,’ Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff — as Trump says pardoning the CEO is ‘always an option’
Did we see this coming?
- Reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang addressed employees at an all-hands on Monday
- He talked about the company's code of conduct, which despite his own actions he insists remains in place and enforceable
- President Trump said a Huang pardon is possible, though likely unnecessary
Jensen Huang has had a lot of explaining to do as he settles back into his former role as President and CEO of Nvidia, one of the world's most important tech companies — and some of his explanations are a little confusing.
According to reports from The New York Times and Wired, Huang spoke to his employees at an all-hands meeting on Monday, during which he assured them that he is not "above the law" or the company's code of conduct, which he helped write — not surprising, when you consider that he cofounded the graphics and chip company more than three decades ago.
In the oddest sort of self-own, Huang also insisted that, despite his "cool jacket", and his return to the company amidst a general lack of clarity about what actually happened — an admitted series of infidelities, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, and ongoing investigations into whether or not Huang allowed advanced Nvidia AI chips to funnel to China, and what he knew and when — Huang is not "a tech bro".
In fact, Huang had a message for Nvidia employees: "If one of you were to violate a code of conduct, what does that mean? If you were ever to violate a code of conduct, it is not appropriate. I just wanted you to know, it is not right, it's not appropriate, it won’t be tolerated."
Code followers
It's a shame there isn't video of this meeting, because one can only imagine the confusion, given that Huang himself appears to have broken the company's code with a series of relationships with direct reports. He quickly clarified that anyone who breaks the code won't immediately be shown the door, but that the company will follow due process, with management teams considering "Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments."
All of this appears to be a reference to an apparent lack of due process in Huang's case. While reports of his alleged infidelity and a potential relationship with a spy started surfacing in September, Huang was suddenly out — he resigned not quite two weeks ago — as soon as additional alleged infidelities with coworkers were revealed.
Huang also touched on his relationship with US President Donald Trump, who has proudly touted his role in bringing back Huang, telling reporters that he called the Nvidia board and urged them to reinstate him.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
"Don’t think for a second that politics ever plays a role in this company, not even a little bit," Huang told the meeting. "We are the most apolitical company."
Calling "rumors" that he was returned because "highest levels of our government wanted me back" untrue, Huang insisted that he was brought back by a board that was performing their "duty as they should have.”
Please pardon this question
Trump, though, is apparently not done meddling in this ongoing affair.
Huang is scheduled to testify before the US House and Senate next month, and will likely be pressed on whether he knew about Alice Huang's (no relation) possible links to Chinese intelligence, and if their alleged personal relationship had any bearing on Nvidia's chip sales to China. Lawmakers will also be looking to learn if that relationship in any way enabled the alleged illegal shipment of high-powered Nvidia AI chips to China.
When asked by The New York Post if Huang might need to plead the Fifth Amendment (which permits individuals to refuse to answer questions that could potentially incriminate them in criminal proceedings) during his testimony, Trump said no, and added "I want him to just tell the truth."
If the Senate and House committees conclude that there has been wrongdoing, and things escalate, Trump may still have Huang's back. The New York Post asked about a potential pardon, and Trump did not dismiss the notion, telling the newspaper, "It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary.”
The use of the word "necessary" is interesting, since it implies that if things do go in a prosecutorial direction, Trump may believe he has to pardon Huang.
The comments took me back almost two weeks, to when we were all trying to figure out what crimes, if any, Huang had committed, and I realized that Trump could easily short-circuit any investigation, posting on X:
Jensen Huang's reinstatement, without any of the answers we hoped to see, either before he resigned or in the interim, means that, in a way, he already has some of the protection he needs.
It's unlikely that Nvidia's board would remove him a second time, even if Congress does ultimately assess that wrongdoing has ocurred. In that case, Trump could pardon Huang, all would be forgiven, and it would be business as usual for one of the world's biggest and most valuable tech companies.
He might even start wearing the leather jacket again.

articles.title: Neue Regeln für ChatGPT: Wer künftig schneller an sein Nutzungslimit stoßen könnte
articles.text:
ChatGPT: Wer künftig schneller an sein Nutzungslimit stoßen könnte
Bislang waren der Chat und OpenAIs Work-Angebot zwei separate Elemente in der ChatGPT-App für den Desktop. Das will das Unternehmen jetzt sukzessive ändern. Beide Teile sollen in einer gemeinsamen Oberfläche zusammenfließen. Ausprobieren darf das vorerst nur eine kleine Gruppe von Pro-Nutzer:innen, wie Product Lead Thibault Sottiaux auf X mitteilt. Demnach wolle man zunächst Feedback von dieser kleinen Gruppe einholen, bevor man die Zusammenlegung breiter verfügbar macht.
OpenAI kombiniert Nutzungslimits
Bei der Kombination aus Chat- und Work-Oberfläche allein wird es aber nicht bleiben. Laut Techcrunch wird OpenAI zudem die Nutzungslimits für beide Elemente sowie für Codex für Abonnent:innen der Plus-, Pro und Business-Pläne kombinieren. Das geht auf einen Sprecher des Unternehmens zurück. Nutzer:innen in den sozialen Medien befürchten schon jetzt, dass sie dadurch ihr Nutzungslimit deutlich schneller erreichen werden und ChatGPT nicht mehr in gewohnter Form nutzen können. Außerdem zahlen sie trotz Zusammenlegung weiterhin dieselben Preise.
Der namentlich nicht genannte Sprecher versucht, gegenüber Techcrunch zu beschwichtigen. So sollen die allermeisten Nutzer:innen von der Neuregelung nichts spüren. Lediglich einige wenige Heavy-User könnten ihr Limit künftig schneller als gewohnt erreichen.
Ausgeschlossen von dem Nutzungslimit ist der sogenannte Instant-Chat, also die Einstellung für alltägliche Fragen und schnelle Antworten. Sie lässt sich weiter nutzen, auch nachdem das Nutzungslimit für Work oder größere Modelle für komplexe Anfragen aufgebraucht ist. OpenAI wolle zudem an der Effizienz von ChatGPT arbeiten, sodass zahlende Kund:innen mehr aus ihrem Abo herausholen könnten.
Unbekannt bleibt zunächst, wann genau das Unternehmen die kombinierte Oberfläche für weitere Kund:innen zugänglich machen will. Die gemeinsamen Nutzungslimits sollen aber ab Dezember für alle Kund:innen gelten.

articles.title: Accuracy and Resolution for Magnetic Angle Sensors
articles.text:
Introduction
Magnetic position sensors, especially magnetic angle sensors, are the fundamental building blocks of countless motion-control applications that necessitate precision positioning. These sensors are pivotal in a wide range of industries, from automotive and robotics to consumer electronics and medical devices, underscoring their universal appeal and importance (see Figure 1).
However, to realize their full potential and utility, one must delve into two crucial parameters that govern their performance: accuracy and resolution. Although these terms are often used interchangeably, they represent distinct — albeit related — concepts in any measuring system. This comprehensive article aims to shed light on these parameters, explain how they impact the performance of magnetic position sensors, and provide guidance on optimizing these factors.
Understanding Accuracy and Resolution
Within the context of measurement and instrumentation, accuracy refers to the closeness of a measured value to the actual or true value of the quantity being measured. For magnetic position sensors, accuracy is the measure of how precisely the sensor’s angle measurement reports the actual angle. Accuracy is a way of understanding how closely the sensor’s read position corresponds to the actual position, with a high accuracy sensor producing readings that are very close to the true position.
On the other hand, resolution signifies the smallest change in the measured quantity that a sensor can detect. For magnetic position sensors, resolution is the minimum angle change that the sensor can ascertain. Resolution is essentially a measure of the sensor’s sensitivity to minute changes in the position. A high-resolution sensor can detect even the smallest changes in position, providing a detailed, granular measurement.
One critical distinction is that a high resolution does not inherently imply high accuracy. A sensor might be highly sensitive to minute changes, meaning it has a high resolution, but it could still be inaccurate if its measurements consistently veer away from the true value. Conversely, a sensor can be highly accurate and consistently provide measurements close to the true position, but it may have low resolution, which means it is unable to catch small changes in position.
This paradox underpins the complexity of designing and implementing magnetic position sensors. Engineers must strike a balance between resolution and accuracy to achieve optimal performance, depending on the specific needs of the application at hand.
Maximizing Sensor Performance: the Tradeoffs
To maximize the performance of a magnetic position sensor system, it is critical for engineers to understand how to quantify accuracy and resolution. More importantly, they must comprehend what system parameters can be tweaked to enhance accuracy or resolution, and they must understand how manufacturers represent these parameters in their datasheets.
Unfortunately, every improvement or enhancement comes at a cost, and the same applies to increasing resolution and accuracy. Striking the right balance between these two parameters requires careful consideration of various tradeoffs.
To enhance resolution, it is important to minimize noise. A window averaging output filter can be used to decrease noise, thus improving resolution. This filter works by smoothing out the random fluctuations in the sensor’s readings, helping to deliver more consistent and accurate results.
However, while an averaging filter increases resolution, it lowers the dynamic bandwidth, which means that the system’s reactions to accelerations will be delayed proportionally to the bandwidth reduction. If the filter window is set too wide, it can lead to a poor step response and instability in a servo control loop, negatively impacting the system’s performance. A basic rule of thumb for Hall-based magnetic angle sensors is that to achieve an extra half bit of resolution, the dynamic bandwidth will be halved.
On the other hand, increasing accuracy (or reducing integral nonlinearity (INL)) can be achieved through calibration. Calibrating the sensor output after it has been installed in its application can help counteract the effects of mechanical tolerance stack-ups and magnet imperfections, leaving only temperature drift as the primary INL contributor. The tradeoff here, however, is cost. Calibration requires time, resources, and specialized knowledge, which translates into increased production costs. For this reason, calibration might not be a feasible option for all applications, especially those where cost is a significant concern.
In situations where high resolution and high bandwidth are required, or where an extremely low INL is critical (below 0.1°, for example), specific solutions like the MA600A can offer an excellent balance between performance and cost (see Figure 2). The MA600A provides a higher bandwidth and resolution than Hall-based solutions, and it is significantly less expensive than the next best alternative, an optical encoder. Because the MA600A is tunneling magneto-resistance (TMR) based, its noise is significantly lower than a Hall-based solution; in addition, the MA600A’s noise profile is not Gaussian, unlike traditional Hall-sensors. These factors greatly reduce the bandwidth tradeoff in TMR.
Accuracy and Resolution Quantified
Manufacturer datasheets provide detailed information on not just the sensor’s accuracy and resolution specifications, but also other critical parameters, such as the operating temperature range, supply voltage, quiescent current, and magnetic field strength range. Not all datasheets are created equal, however, and one must be careful when comparing specifications.
For example, some manufacturers specify resolution based on a 1σ noise range, meaning that the minimum angle change can be detected only 68% of the time. Meanwhile, MPS specifies resolution as a ±3σ noise level (see Figure 3). This guarantees that the resolved difference between two angles will be correct 99.7% of the time. Not all manufacturers are so conservative, and it is easy to make the resolution look higher by ignoring the 3σ requirement.
Accuracy (or INL), on the other hand, is relatively straightforward and there is a less leeway to disguise the actual sensor performance. One thing to consider is the temperature range across which the specification is listed. As mentioned previously, calibration can reduce the INL created by mechanical or magnetic tolerances, but it is much more difficult to calibrate against temperature drift.
Conclusion
Choosing the right magnetic position sensor for a given application involves understanding the intricate tradeoffs between accuracy, resolution, and other system parameters. It also requires an understanding of how these parameters can be optimized to deliver the best possible performance.
By understanding the key concepts of accuracy and resolution and how they apply to magnetic position sensors such as the MA600A, engineers can make informed decisions when selecting sensors for their systems. This knowledge helps in optimizing performance, keeping costs under control, and ensuring the successful execution of their designs.
In the ever-evolving world of technology, where precision and accuracy are paramount, understanding the nuances of magnetic position sensors is invaluable. Armed with this knowledge, engineers are better equipped to navigate the complexities of the digital world and harness the full potential of magnetic position sensors in a wide range of applications

articles.title: Uber appoints former Zomato CEO Rakesh Ranjan as President for India, South Asia
articles.text:
Uber appoints former Zomato CEO Rakesh Ranjan as President for India, South Asia
Ranjan, who spent eight years at Zomato, will take charge of Uber’s India and South Asia operations from January 4, 2027.
Uber has appointed former Zomato food delivery CEO Rakesh Ranjan as President for India and South Asia, effective January 4, 2027, as the mobility platform looks to strengthen its presence in one of its largest global markets.
Ranjan will report to Dom Taylor, Uber’s Regional General Manager for Asia Pacific. He joins Uber from Allen Online, where he currently serves as CEO.
Ranjan joined Zomato in 2017 and spent eight years at the company. During his tenure, he led its food ordering and delivery business as CEO, having previously held leadership roles across Zomato Gold and sales.
“Uber has built a business that matters to how people move and earn across India and South Asia. The opportunity ahead is significant, and it starts with the everyday experience: dependable rides, value across different journeys and better earning opportunities for drivers. I’m excited to join the talented team and build on a great foundation,” said Ranjan in a statement.
Announcing the appointment, Taylor said: “After a search spanning more than three months, we’re delighted to welcome Rakesh to Uber. We set a high bar for this role, and his experience running large consumer businesses in India, combined with his ambition for what comes next, stood out."
"India and South Asia matter enormously to Uber’s future. Rakesh joins a business with real scale and enduring strength and he brings valuable experience to lead the next chapter of growth and innovation for our business in the region,” Taylor added.
India is Uber’s third-largest market globally by trips, after the US and Brazil, and its second-largest by the number of earners. The company operates in more than 225 cities across the country, offering multiple mobility options, including bikes, autos, cars and metro services. More than two million monthly active drivers earn through its platform.
India is also home to Uber’s largest technology centres outside the US, located in Bengaluru and Hyderabad. The company entered the Indian market in 2013 and has since expanded its presence across mobility categories.
Edited by Megha Reddy

articles.title: Ainoa, una camionera en España: "La ruta cambia cada día. Si voy a Madrid, calculo las horas que puedo hacer del tirón para saber dónde parar"
articles.text:
Ainoa Blasco es una camionera de 30 años que comparte el día a día de su profesión en sus redes sociales. Y en una entrevista con La Vanguardia sobre los retos de su oficio, también contó que la ruta que le toca hacer cambia cada día, algo que la obliga a calcular cuántas horas puede conducir del tirón para saber dónde va a parar.
Una ruta que se decide a última hora. Una de las cosas que más pesan en su día a día es la falta de rutina, porque aunque normalmente duerme en casa, no sabe con mucha antelación qué recorrido le tocará al día siguiente. Por eso tiene que planificar cada viaje y, a la vez, estar dispuesta a cambiar esos planes sobre la marcha. “Hasta última hora del día no sabes lo que vas a hacer al día siguiente. Te puede salir alguna ruta de dormir fuera, que a veces agradezco, porque vas cambiando y es muy diferente la rutina de los viajes si son más cortos o más largos”, explicaba en la entrevista.
Parar bastante antes de Madrid. Cuando le toca ir a la capital, por ejemplo, calcula cuántas horas puede conducir seguidas y las reparte de manera que el viaje se pueda hacer con seguridad, aunque eso suponga no llegar ese día a su destino. Si sale desde Valencia y necesita dormir por el camino, prefiere detenerse bastante antes de llegar. El motivo es la seguridad, ya que, según cuenta, en algunas zonas es más probable que intenten abrir el camión: “Si llegas a Madrid, es más fácil que te intenten abrir el camión, ya no la cabina, sino también el remolque. Y al final, eres el responsable de la carga que llevas. Es tu responsabilidad”.
Los consejos de los veteranos. Eso sí, asegura que hasta ahora nunca ha sufrido un intento de robo, algo que atribuye en parte a lo que le han ido enseñando su padre, su hermano y otros compañeros con más experiencia en la carretera. Y es que para ella es fundamental hacer caso a quienes llevan años en el oficio, porque gracias a lo que le cuentan puede ver venir las situaciones peligrosas antes de encontrárselas en ruta.
Atascos y cuestas. Pero el cálculo inicial no siempre aguanta hasta el final de la jornada, porque un atasco, una retención o cualquier otro imprevisto pueden obligarla a buscar otra zona donde detenerse, de modo que conocer bien la carretera cuenta mucho. También influye lo que lleva detrás: cuando va con mucho peso, procura escoger carreteras más largas si con ello puede evitar pendientes pronunciadas, porque las cuestas exigen un mayor esfuerzo al camión. Vamos, que prefiere sumar kilómetros antes que castigar al vehículo en cada subida.
Camionera de familia. Ainoa no llegó al transporte desde fuera, ya que su padre y su hermano son chóferes y en su casa siempre se había hablado de camiones y de carretera. Fue con la pandemia cuando decidió seguir esa tradición y sacarse el carnet C para conducir camiones, y la entrada en el sector también llegó de la mano de su familia. Su hermano habló con su jefe y la respuesta fue directa: “Que no busque trabajo, que se viene con nosotros”.
Reconoce que el trabajo es duro, por las horas y por la responsabilidad que recae sobre quien conduce, pero también destaca lo que le ha aportado a nivel personal, sobre todo en autonomía y en capacidad para resolver problemas por su cuenta. “A nivel personal te espabila mucho porque te pones en situaciones en las que vas a estar sola y vas a tener que buscarte la vida para poder salir de ello. Te hace muy autosuficiente”, resume.

articles.title: How often should you do maintenance on a Mac?
articles.text:
Every Mac user knows that the operating system runs very well, and it can give you impressive performance for quite some time. But this is a machine and eventually there can be some problems which arise. Hence the reason why it makes sense to perform some maintenance. Now the question is, how often do you need to perform that maintenance? Here’s what you need to consider.
Does Mac OS maintain itself?
Yes, it does a lot of things in the background, on its own. The idea here is that it automates many tasks like clearing out expired temporary files, rebuilding internal databases or rotating system logs. All of that is made automatically in the background, which makes it incredibly rewarding and exciting as well, something to take into account.
Another thing that Mac OS does is it performs SSD Optimization. It trims the device in order to keep any file fragments close to one another. Doing so improves the overall speed of the device, and it leads to a way better and more consistent experience. Silicon Macs also have better RAM management and a system called unified memory. That’s excellent, and it truly helps enhance the experience in better ways than you might expect.
Things to do on a weekly basis
- A good idea is to wipe down the screen, keyboard and trackpad. It’s very easy for these to get dirty, so cleaning everything up is a very good idea.
- Some people leave their Mac open, and that can lead to all kinds of problems. The best approach is to try and restart your Mac often, as it will help reset processes and just improve performance as a whole.
- Do a better triage on your desktop and downloads folder. Basically, the idea is to try and better optimize your desktop’s files and not leave unused stuff. Removing things is easier, and it can eliminate many of the possible issues that sometimes arise.
Monthly maintenance tasks
- Use a cleanup tool like CleanMyMac. That can help optimize your Mac, perform maintenance and ensure everything runs smoothly. It’s something that, thanks to the app, you can do automatically. In doing so, you streamline the process, and it can help convey a much better overall result. It’s excellent and totally worth considering, especially in this situation.
- Try to leave at least 15% of your drive capacity free. That’s used by the operating system to ensure everything runs smoothly. Otherwise, you can end up with problems, and it’s certainly one of those things you want to avoid.
- Empty the trash, if you didn’t do so for quite some time. It allows you to recoup a lot of space, and it’s well-worth the effort.

- Another thing you can do is to audit login items and background extensions. Those things start with your Mac every time you login, and they consume system resources. Only allow stuff that you need to start off with your Mac, as it can help quite a lot.
- It’s also a good idea to clean up ports and cooling vents once every 1-2 months as well. Clean hardware will help make the experience smoother, and that’s exactly what you need to pursue.
Other maintenance tasks
2 times a year, you can go into heavier maintenance. It’s imperative to try and do that at least 1-2 times a year, because it helps you streamline the SSD storage and it will make things easier.
Annually, you can also assess the battery health and charging habits for your device, evaluate the internal dust, conduct a privacy and security checkup, and just ensure everything is running smoothly. It’s important to make sure that these maintenance tasks are performed often, so you don’t need to worry about anything here, and that’s what will help the most.
Conclusion
We recommend taking your time when it comes to performing maintenance on a Mac. And that’s the thing, the primary focus is on ensuring it all works correctly, and that it gives you the ROI that you are looking for. Ensuring that you optimize your approach and that you always perform some maintenance tasks will help you more than expected. articles.title: Pendant le Black Friday 2026, le multicuiseur Ninja Foodi OL550EU tombe à 194,35 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le multicuiseur Ninja Foodi OL550EU SmartLid à 194,35 € (-26%)
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le multicuiseur Ninja Foodi OL550EU SmartLid passe à 194,35 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 26 % et 68,61 € d'économie. Pratique avec sa cuisson sous pression et à l'air chaud sans changer de couvercle, l'appareil affiche une note actuelle de 3,5/5 par notre rédaction.
Le Ninja Foodi OL550EU SmartLid réunit la cuisson sous pression et la friture sans huile au sein d'un seul appareil grâce à son couvercle unique. Ce multicuiseur vise ceux qui cherchent à diversifier leurs préparations culinaires avec 11 programmes automatiques. Lors de son passage dans notre labo, il avait convaincu par sa maîtrise des cuissons.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, son tarif descend à 194,35 € chez Amazon, soit environ 26 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours. Cela représente une économie de 68,61 €.
Onze programmes et une chauffe homogène sans changer de couvercle
Ce multicuiseur simplifie la préparation des repas en évitant les manipulations habituelles : son système à couvercle unique permet d'alterner directement entre la cuisson vapeur, le mijotage et le croustillant. Comme nous l'avons constaté dans notre test complet, l'appareil délivre une chauffe stable et homogène sur tous ses modes. Sa cuve offre une capacité de 6000 ml et s'accompagne d'une grille réversible, ce qui autorise la cuisson sur deux niveaux distincts pour préparer simultanément une viande et ses légumes.
Ninja Foodi OL550EU SmartLid
Points forts
- Cuisson à l'air chaud et sous pression dans le même appareil.
- Plus besoin de changer de couvercle.
- Grande capacité et une grille pour cuire sur deux niveaux.
- Chauffe stable et homogène.
Points faibles
- Friture moins rapide et pratique qu'avec une friteuse.
- Livret de recettes assez mince et toujours pas d'app pour en trouver d'autres.
- Panneau de commandes en anglais.
- Bruyant en modes Air Fry et Grill.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une utilisation qui demande un temps d'adaptation
Ce modèle présente toutefois quelques contraintes d'usage à connaître avant de cuisiner. L'appareil devient bruyant dès que la ventilation s'active sur les fonctions de grillade et de friture sans huile, un mode d'ailleurs moins rapide qu'une friteuse dédiée. L'interface affiche l'ensemble de ses commandes en anglais, tandis que l'absence d'application mobile et le livret de recettes restreint imposent d'adapter soi-même ses temps de cuisson. Ces détails conviendront avant tout aux cuisiniers autonomes qui n'ont pas besoin d'un guidage pas à pas.
Ninja OP100EU : l'autre option face au Ninja Foodi OL550EU SmartLid
Le Ninja OP100EU mise sur un gabarit plus compact tout en conservant le principe de la cuisson sous pression combinée à l'air pulsé. Il se limite à 6 modes de cuisson et impose des manipulations supplémentaires avec ses couvercles interchangeables, là où l'OL550EU intègre tout sous une même charnière et propose 11 programmes pour cuire de plus grands volumes.
Le Ninja OP100EU coûte 33,55 € de moins que le Ninja Foodi OL550EU SmartLid, mais ce dernier offre une cuve plus vaste de 6000 ml et un confort d'usage supérieur pour les repas familiaux.
Ninja OP100EU
Points forts
- Large cuve.
- Commandes directes.
- 6 modes de cuisson, dont pression et air pulsé.
- Bonnes performances de cuisson.
Points faibles
- Beaucoup de termes en anglais.
- Pas de recettes intégrées.
- Pas de poignée sur la cuve.
- Encombrement.

articles.title: Petite révolution sur Gemini : vous pouvez enfin protéger vos données tout en conservant votre historique
articles.text:
Jusqu’à présent, les utilisateurs de Gemini ne pouvaient pas conserver leur historique de conversations avec l’assistant IA sans accepter, de facto, que leurs informations partagées servent à entraîner le modèle. D’une part, cela pose un problème de confidentialité. D’autre part, la désactivation de l’historique de conversations rend le modèle d’IA bien moins intéressant. Les utilisateurs se trouvaient donc face à un dilemme. Mais bonne nouvelle, Google leur permet dorénavant de gérer ces deux paramètres indépendamment.
Un premier paramètre pour gérer la sauvegarde de l’historique de conversations
Les utilisateurs de Gemini peuvent désormais conserver leur historique de conversations, tout en contrôlant indépendamment l’entraînement du modèle d’IA générative. Comme nous pouvons le voir ci-dessous, il existe deux paramètres distincts. Le premier permet tout simplement d’activer ou de désactiver l’historique de conversations avec Gemini (il est activé par défaut). Google précise que « les conversations futures seront conservées pendant environ deux mois et utilisées pour vous répondre, traiter vos commentaires et protéger Google, ses utilisateurs et le public, avec l’aide d’examinateurs humains ».
Un second paramètre pour gérer l’entraînement du modèle d’IA
Le second paramètre permet quant à lui de gérer les autorisations accordées à Google pour entraîner son modèle d’IA. L’entraînement de Gemini sur les conversations, y compris le texte et les pièces jointes, est activé par défaut. L’entraînement de Gemini sur les enregistrements audio, les vidéos et les partages d’écran Gemini Live reste quant à lui désactivé par défaut.
Google précise que si la case « Contenu des discussions » est désactivée « vos futures conversations ne seront pas utilisées pour entraîner des modèles d’IA génératifs, sauf si vous fournissez des commentaires ». À noter que si vous désactivez la sauvegarde de l’historique de conversations, les deux autres paramètres seront automatiquement désactivés. Pour accéder à ces paramètres, vous pouvez suivre ce lien ou vous rendre dans les paramètres de Gemini et cliquer sur « Activité dans les applications Gemini ». Ces nouveaux paramètres sont en cours de déploiement. De notre côté, ils sont d’ores et déjà disponibles.

articles.title: Jobsuche in der IT: Mit diesen Profilen positionierst du dich am besten im KI-Zeitalter
articles.text:
Jobsuche in der IT: Mit diesen Profilen positionierst du dich am besten im KI-Zeitalter
Plötzlich war Schluss: Die E-Commerce-Agentur, bei der Peter Prochaska 2024 arbeitete, entließ die Hälfte ihrer Belegschaft – unter anderem auch ihn, den IT-Spezialisten. „Das kam sehr überraschend für mich“, sagt der 53-Jährige heute. Ebenso überraschend war für ihn, wie lange die Jobsuche im Anschluss dauerte. Sieben Monate war Prochaska damit beschäftigt, mehr als 300 Bewerbungen schickte er nach eigener Aussage los. Er bewarb sich querbeet als Entwickler, Datenschutzkoordinator oder Projektleiter. Nur zu zwei Vorstellungsgesprächen wurde er eingeladen.
Mittlerweile ist er in einem neuen Job glücklich geworden: Er arbeitet als Projektleiter bei einem bayerischen Dienstleister für Open-Source-Lösungen. Doch viele arbeitssuchende ITler machen gerade ähnliche Erfahrungen wie Prochaska: Die Jobsuche dauert lang, es gibt weniger Stellen als vor einigen Jahren und sie werden mit weniger Gehalt ausgeschrieben. Die Zahl der Arbeitslosen, die einen Job in der Informations- und Kommunikationstechnik anstreben, sei gegenüber dem Vorjahr um 27 Prozent gestiegen, teilte die Arbeitsagentur im Sommer mit. Laut Branchenverband Bitkom ist zwar weiterhin ein Fachkräftemangel zu verzeichnen, die Zahl der unbesetzten Stellen habe sich gegenüber 2023 aber fast halbiert. Während vor drei Jahren noch 149.000 Fachkräfte fehlten, seien es aktuell nur noch 79.000.

articles.title: New ReShade add-on brings ray-traced reflections to Red Dead Redemption 2 and potentially other DX12 games
articles.text:
In context: Thanks to Doom: The Dark Ages and other recent releases, ray tracing is becoming increasingly commonplace – and even mandatory – in modern games. Meanwhile, third-party developers continue to explore ways to optimize classic games and bring modern lighting effects to older titles.
A developer named Skynizz recently unveiled the Universal Ray Tracing Injector (URTI), an add-on for ReShade designed to further improve graphics realism in PC games. URTI adds another layer of visual fidelity to the popular post-processing injector, bringing real-time ray-traced reflections to DirectX 12 games that were not originally designed to support the effect.
Skynizz explained that URTI can "capture" 3D geometry in DX12 games by replaying every draw call through the stream output. At the end of the rendering pipeline, the game should display its original geometry, including any transformations, with realistic reflections on water, puddles, glass, and other simulated surfaces.
URTI performs its work using Microsoft's official ray tracing API for DirectX 12 games, DXR 1.1. Ray-traced reflections are hardware accelerated, but URTI does not need to modify the game's original assets or shaders. Although it could theoretically support more DXR-based games, URTI is currently focused exclusively on Red Dead Redemption 2.
After ReShade's injector is activated, URTI can add new lighting effects to Rockstar's Western adventure, including reflections on wet streets, windows, and polished floors. Skynizz warns that URTI injects itself into the game's rendering process, meaning it should only be used in single-player sessions and "never" online to avoid potential bans.
Developers have been trying to bring "proper" ray-tracing effects to ReShade and RDR2 for years, but URTI could offer something new. According to Skynizz, no other tool, as far as they know, can trace "real rays" through a game's live geometry without first knowing its data formats.
URTI can read a game's geometry buffer, determine which pixels should reflect, and project the resulting lighting effects based on the camera's position in every frame.
URTI could theoretically support many more games beyond RDR2, although each title might require a small configuration profile for now. The ReShade add-on also requires a GPU compatible with DXR 1.1, such as an Nvidia GeForce RTX 20-series card, an AMD Radeon RX 6000-series card, or a newer model.
Skynizz developed URTI after working on Knowledge Radiance Cache, a research prototype focused on path-traced global illumination.

articles.title: Cómo obtener Vintage Vice City Pack y cuánto vale
articles.text:
El Vintage Vice City Pack de GTA 6 ya puede comprarse por separado para quienes no lo obtuvieron como incentivo de reserva. El contenido adicional recupera elementos inspirados en la estética de Vice City y añade un vehículo clásico, un garaje, prendas, peinados y un diseño de arma para los protagonistas Lucía y Jason.
La disponibilidad permite acceder después del lanzamiento a extras que inicialmente estaban vinculados a la compra anticipada de Grand Theft Auto VI. El contenido no modifica la historia principal, pero amplía las opciones de personalización y ofrece un guiño directo a Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, la entrega de 2002 ambientada en una versión ficticia de Miami durante los años ochenta.
El precio del Vintage Vice City Pack en dólares, euros y América Latina
El complemento tiene un precio de USD 4,99 en la tienda digital de PlayStation de Estados Unidos. En territorios que utilizan el euro, su valor es de 4,99 euros.
Los precios pueden variar según la tienda, los impuestos locales y la plataforma. En las tiendas digitales de Xbox, el contenido aparece con estos valores de referencia:
- Colombia: COP$15.999
- México: MXN$89
- Argentina: USD 4,99 en la PlayStation Store argentina
- Estados Unidos: USD 4,99
- Europa: 4,99 euros
En Argentina, el gasto final puede ser superior por los impuestos que se apliquen a consumos digitales en moneda extranjera. Por ese motivo, el valor de USD 4,99 funciona como precio base y el monto en pesos argentinos dependerá de la cotización utilizada por el medio de pago y de los recargos vigentes.
El pack requiere tener una copia de Grand Theft Auto VI. No funciona como un juego independiente y tampoco concede acceso a la campaña si el usuario no compró previamente el título base.
Cómo comprar el contenido adicional de GTA 6
El proceso para obtener el Vintage Vice City Pack se realiza desde las tiendas digitales de PlayStation o Xbox. Antes de confirmar el pago, conviene comprobar que la cuenta corresponda a la misma región en la que se adquirió el juego.
Los pasos son los siguientes:
- Ingresar en la PlayStation Store desde una consola PS5, la aplicación móvil o la web oficial.
- Buscar “Grand Theft Auto VI: Vintage Vice City Pack”.
- Verificar el precio, la plataforma y la cuenta utilizada.
- Seleccionar la opción de compra.
- Descargar el complemento o comprobar que se instale junto al juego.
- Iniciar GTA 6 y avanzar en la campaña para habilitar los artículos.
En Xbox, el procedimiento es parecido. El usuario debe abrir Microsoft Store desde Xbox Series X|S o desde la web, buscar el nombre completo del paquete y confirmar la compra. El contenido quedará asociado a la cuenta de Microsoft vinculada con la consola.
Qué incluye el paquete Vintage Vice City
El contenido adicional incorpora un Vapid Stanier de 1955, un sedán de estilo clásico que puede guardarse en el garaje Shore Court, cerca de Ocean Beach. El espacio también incluye un depósito de armas y una zona para almacenar mercancía robada antes de venderla dentro del juego.
El pack añade ropa y peinados para los dos protagonistas. Jason recibe un traje de lino en tonos pastel y un corte de cabello asociado a la moda de los años ochenta. Lucía obtiene un minivestido rojo de lentejuelas y un peinado de rizos inspirado en esa década.
También incorpora un patrón tropical para armas, basado en la camisa de palmeras que se asocia con Tommy Vercetti, protagonista de GTA: Vice City. Los objetos no estarán disponibles desde el primer minuto, ya que se desbloquearán según el avance del jugador en la historia de Lucía y Jason.
El paquete recupera referencias de la Vice City original
La llegada del Vintage Vice City Pack enlaza el nuevo juego con el universo que Rockstar presentó en 2002. En aquella entrega, Tommy Vercetti salía de prisión y llegaba a una ciudad dominada por el crimen, los negocios ilegales, la música pop y la arquitectura art déco.
GTA 6 traslada esa identidad a la Vice City contemporánea de Leonida. El paquete utiliza vehículos, ropa, colores y accesorios para recuperar parte de ese imaginario sin cambiar la trama central. Para quienes compraron el juego después de la reserva, representa una forma de añadir esos elementos a su partida mediante un pago adicional.

articles.title: Cuts to Chinese CSP Demand Expecting to Slow Memory Industry Revenue Growth in 2027
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Cuts to Chinese CSP Demand Expecting to Slow Memory Industry Revenue Growth in 2027
TrendForce's latest memory industry research indicates that Chinese Cloud Service Providers (CSPs) have reduced their 2027 memory orders, putting downward pressure on the industry's price outlook. The NAND Flash market is expected to enter a downward pricing cycle as supply continues to expand, prompting TrendForce to lower its 2027 NAND Flash revenue forecast to approximately US$419.3 billion.
Meanwhile, although the DRAM market is expected to remain undersupplied, quarterly price increases are projected to moderate. This has led TrendForce to revise its 2027 DRAM revenue forecast downward to $1.15 trillion.In the NAND Flash market, Chinese CSPs began scaling back their enterprise SSD procurement plans for 2027 in mid-4Q26 amid concerns over GPU supply shortages. These reductions have exceeded the additional orders placed by North American CSPs.
For consumer electronics products such as PCs and smartphones, low-cost memory inventories have been depleted, and device prices face upward pressure in 2027. Brands are expected to reduce NAND Flash capacity specifications across their product portfolios to keep bill-of-materials (BOM) costs under control. Together, these factors will weigh on NAND Flash bit demand growth in 2027.
On the supply side, however, some manufacturers will continue expanding production capacity, while process technology migrations at other suppliers will further increase bit output. As a result, NAND Flash supply is expected to grow significantly in 2027, reinforcing an oversupplied market and pushing overall contract prices lower. TrendForce has therefore revised its 2027 NAND Flash industry revenue forecast downward to $419.3 billion, representing 29% YoY growth.
In the DRAM market, some Chinese CSPs began reducing their 2027 server DRAM bit demand outside long-term agreements (LTAs) in early 4Q26. However, North American CSPs quickly absorbed the resulting supply availability, keeping overall DRAM bit demand on a strong growth trajectory for the year.
DRAM bit supply is expected to continue growing year-over-year as major manufacturers expand wafer capacity and migrate to more advanced process technologies.
TrendForce expects DRAM supply to remain tight throughout 2027, although quarterly contract price increases are projected to narrow progressively, potentially leveling off in the second half of the year. As a result, TrendForce has lowered its full-year DRAM revenue forecast to $1.15 trillion, representing 69% YoY growth.

articles.title: Ars Live recap: Don’t expect military attacks on data centers to stop
articles.text:
Amazon data centers came under military attack for the first time ever in the Middle East this year, and Russia and Ukraine exchanged an unprecedented flurry of drone strikes on each other’s data centers. To examine what such attacks on data centers mean for the future of cloud services that all modern societies depend upon, Ars hosted a live discussion.
In a conversation with Ars Technica Tech Reporter Jeremy Hsu, Joseph Jarnecki at the Royal United Services Institute first talked about why public cloud data centers have increasingly become military targets during the 2026 Iran war and the ongoing full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine:
We see an increasing acknowledgement and fact of dual use in particularly the public cloud, but also just across the board in private cloud data centers as well. The dual use that I refer to is the utilization of compute functions within these data centers—within cloud services—by militaries, for example, to run battlefield management systems, to do their HR, to do their resource management. Once a military uses a piece of civilian infrastructure, at least under international law or in terms of the principles of targeting that are taken forward by militaries, it can sometimes become a military object and is therefore of interest to an adversary, and there’s an incentive to target it.
Jarnecki also highlighted the fact that relatively cheap kamikaze drones can inflict disproportionate economic costs and create widespread cloud disruptions when striking data centers:
The second reason that we’ve seen targeting particularly in Russia’s largest data centers or some of Russia’s largest public cloud data centers like Yandex, as well as American hyperscalers that are based in the Gulf, is to impose economic cost in a way that would be disadvantageous for an adversary and would otherwise be quite difficult to impose in other ways. So it’s relatively low cost of munition to high cost of disruption. If you think about the amount of investment that’s been put forward by AWS and other companies in the Gulf to build out these data center installations relative to the cost of the amount of Shahed drones that are manufactured, produced, and utilized by Iran to target these data centers, I would put it very, very conservatively at 100X or even more. The cost ratio is really very lucrative for the adversary, and it provides the opportunity to really degrade the economic outcomes of who you are targeting.
Much of the discussion also focused on cloud resilience lessons for both governments and hyperscalers, with the latter including large cloud and data center operators such as Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Meta. articles.title: Canadians can now shop Freedom Mobile at Visions Electronics
articles.text:
Freedom Mobile is teaming up with Canadian retailer Visions Electronics on a new retail partnership that will see Freedom made available at more stores across several provinces.
According to details the companies shared with MobileSyrup, Freedom Mobile products and services will be available at 37 Visions locations across B.C., Alberta, Manitoba, and Ontario.
The companies said the partnership “reflects a shared commitment to helping Canadians stay connected through accessible technology solutions and exceptional customer experiences.”
Overall, this is a great move that should help get Freedom in front of more potential customers, especially as it comes just ahead of Black Friday.
Not everyone is comfortable with or capable of shopping online, especially with the growing prevalence of fraud and scams. Expanding the number of physical locations through partnerships like this is a big win for customers.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’
articles.text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is pushing back against claims that Anthropic believes we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems. In a long X post on Wednesday, Amodei called the suggestion “absurd.”
“We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security,” he wrote. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea…No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different.”
The statement comes after a growing chorus from Anthropic rivals suggesting that human agency could be at risk if AI is developed irresponsibly. Earlier this month, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he wanted to ensure people continue to have “agency over the future.”
Meta’s chief AI officer Alexandr Wang also wrote in an essay on X that we “should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI.”
“It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement,” Wang wrote. “Now that we are at a point where the scientific and technical problems on capability progress are likely solved, we must not only make progress in the extremely urgent areas of safety, alignment, and security, but we have to start thinking through how we progress thoughtfully.”
But in published essays, Amodei claims he has repeatedly advocated for democratic oversight of AI, saying the technology should strengthen democratic institutions and that humans should retain ultimate decision-making power.
Amodei noted that there’s a difference between surrendering human free will broadly and the idea that “as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing specific tasks in a more automated way.” As examples, he gave AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing end-to-end software.
Amodei suggested drawing a line at recursive self-improvement (RSI), or AI that can improve itself without human assistance. Many safety experts see RSI as inevitably leading to a loss of human control, a point Amodei implicitly acknowledged, writing, “we may want limits on this process.”
Still, Anthropic is laying the groundwork for RSI by incorporating AI into an increasing share of its own research and development. The company said in June that Claude authored more than 80% of the code merged into Anthropic’s codebase. An independent assessment published this month by AI safety research nonprofit METR found that Anthropic’s models are improving at about twice their historical rate, primarily driven by AI-assisted research.
In its own IPO filings, Anthropic describes how each successive generation of Claude accelerates the development of the next, a process it refers to as “closing the loop.”
“As we said publicly in early November, we don’t expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously, without meaningful human supervision or understanding,” Amodei wrote.
The problem with “meaningful human supervision or understanding” is that AI is already advancing faster than engineers and safety experts can fully audit it, leaving them increasingly reliant on other AI systems to act as judge and jury. The issue compounds when AI models engage in deceptive behavior, particularly when they recognize they’re being evaluated, making them harder to trust and control.
Still, Anthropic is by no means the only company that is pursuing RSI or building AI systems to automate more and more human tasks. This week, OpenAI claimed to have solved one of the biggest open problems in computer science — the exact speed limit of matrix multiplication, which is the mathematical engine behind modern computing, including deep learning and physics simulations.
In his post, Amodei accused competitors of engaging in a “vibes-based commercial and political positioning,” disingenuously throwing around phrases like “human control and agency” or “AI should just be a tool” without approaching the AI race any differently.
“Certainly the products that they offer don’t differ materially in their orientation towards automation of tasks; every company seems to be releasing models more and more capable of task automation,” Amodei wrote. “Every company claims to understand there are risks and downsides of such automation and to offer safeguards.”

articles.title: 'You do increase the risk of something going wrong': Microsoft President Brad Smith says we should be prepared for mass outages to become the new normal
articles.text:
'You do increase the risk of something going wrong': Microsoft President Brad Smith says we should be prepared for mass outages to become the new normal
Tech outages could become the new norm, Microsoft President warns
- Microsoft President Brad Smith warns businesses and consumers to prepare for ongoing outages
- AI keeps identifying previously-undiscovered vulnerabilities – and attackers are loving that
- Microsoft's own Patch Tuesday went from fixing 200 bugs in June to 1,200 bugs in November 2026
Microsoft's President and Vice Chair, Brad Smith, has warned that we should prepare for further tech outages over the coming months and years as organizations tackle major infrastructure and security upgrades to protect themselves against an onslaught of threats in the AI era.
Speaking with CBS News (via Newsweek), Smith referenced the recent wave of outages and disruptions, suggesting that similar events are unlikely to be resolved any time soon.
"I think we have to be prepared, frankly, for the coming months because this isn't the type of thing that just gets done in a couple of weeks," he said.
More tech outages to come?
Smith blamed the recent rise in incidents on the "AI ripple effects" – AI can be credited with accelerating the discovery of existing vulnerabilities we didn't know about, but unfortunately, threat actors are also leveraging AI to identify these vulnerabilities at rapid pace.
Companies are also using AI to ship new and updated software faster than before, which could be enabling new bugs to slip through the net, intensifying issues.
Microsoft's own November 2026 Patch Tuesday addressed a record 1,200+ bugs (via Infosecurity Magazine), around twice as many as its July Patch Tuesday and a 6x increase compared with its June Patch Tuesday.
A recent Outlook outage springs to mind, though Smith ruled out a cyberattack in this instance, blaming it on an earlier software change, a later software update and changes in network traffic.

Even so, the Outlook incident underscores the precariously interconnected nature of today's digital world, and the widespread impacts one service disruption could have.
"For critical infrastructure, the objective must be to keep essential services functioning even when a component is compromised or unavailable," US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent added.

articles.title: New CPU benchmark tool promises 40 years of compatibility, with support as far back as i386, Windows 95 — CrystalMark CPUix tested on NEC PC-98 21Bs, Pentium 100, and more
articles.text:
New CPU benchmark tool promises 40 years of compatibility, with support as far back as i386, Windows 95 — CrystalMark CPUix tested on NEC PC-98 21Bs, Pentium 100, and more
Want to directly compare your Duron 900, Pentium G3258, and Core i9-9990XE CPUs? CPUiX is scheduled for release on March 31, 2027.
There's a new CPU benchmark on the way designed to handle and contextualize 40 years of personal computer chip development. The upcoming CrystalMark CPUix "evaluates performance from i386 through the latest processors using a single standard across past and future CPU generations," says developer Noriyuki Miyazaki [machine translation]. In terms of hardware/software compatibility, the benchmarking tool will evaluate processors as old as the i386 running on OSes as out of date as Windows 95 and NT 3.51.
Miyazaki says that the upcoming CPUix app will support 16-color environments, which might help folks at the more ancient and creaky end of the PC retro hardware spectrum. Even this limited color UI will have a base maroon theme, as used in the announcement graphic.
The developer is also welcoming feature requests on social media. Don't ask for support for OSes earlier than Windows 95, though, as it has already been stated by Miyazaki that stretching compatibility to Windows 3.1 "is a bit much."
To aid in the development of CPUix, Miyazaki has recently acquired an NEC PC-98 21Bs. This lovely beige desktop arrived on the developer's desk on Sunday, but it has already been used to implement and verify CPUix's functionality on processors without an FPU. Other older systems have been purchased, including a Pentium 100, to ensure wide compatibility. More systems, old and new, are also going to be acquired for testing.
We don't have a lot of information on the inner workings of CPUix as yet. Aspects of the benchmark's test workloads, score weighting, and so on aren't shared on the official pages or social media postings we found. As CPUix comes from the developer of CrystalDiskMark, it looks like it could be a more ambitious version of the CrystalMark Retro 2.0.0 release, which we reported on last year. That also supported systems back to Windows 95/NT 3.51, and CPUs from the i386 era.
CPUix is still in development, and its release date is currently penciled in for March 31, 2027. It seems to have been revealed early, as Miyazaki celebrates the 28th anniversary of Crystal Dew World.
