articles.title: These four portable monitors are on sale: Get a second screen for your PC or console for as little as $54
articles.text:
These four portable monitors are on sale: Get a second screen for your PC or console for as little as $54
Get a portable screen for travel, or second (or third) screen for your desk for less.
If you ever travel with your laptop, want to game on a console in places where you don't have access to a TV, or just want a second (or third) screen for your desk, a portable monitor is a must-have. And with many screens at all-time lows, veering into impulse-buy territory, there's never been a better time to pick one up. 
But how do you know what to buy when there are dozens of brands (especially on the low end) that you've probably never heard of (I haven't, and I've covered tech for 20 years)? Below are a few quick portable monitor shopping tips, followed by four of our favorite current deals.
- LCD, IPS, or OLED? OLED is the best in terms of color saturation and deep blacks, but it costs much more. IPS has better viewing angles than lesser screen technologies, and is becoming the standard even on budget screens. So you should stick to IPS or OLED at this point.
- Get a monitor with a kickstand. Most portable monitors still have floppy folding covers that double as stands. I've had a screen with one for years and it's awful. A rigid kickstand that's attached to the back and swings out will make you want to use your monitor more often and in more places. All of our deal picks below have kickstands.
- Pay attention to brightness. This spec is often buried on product pages, but it matters a lot, especially if you use the monitor in bright spaces. If using it with your laptop, try and get something that is close to the brightness of that screen. You don't want a washed-out second display.
- Get a cover or sleeve. Since these screens have a kickstand, they likely don't come with a protective cover. But you'll certainly one something to at least protect the screen while traveling. So budget in some extra money to protect your second-screen investment.
Productivity budget pick: Veout VE-1 16-inch portable monitor
This 16-inch IPS portable monitor sports a 1920 x 1200 resolution, a built-in kickstand, is just 0.3 inches thick and weighs 1.58 pounds. You'll want to get a case for it, but this is a great screen for productivity on the go.
Read moreRead less▼
The VE-1 isn't quite the cheapest portable screen we've seen, but I'd argue it's the biggest bargain. It's a little larger than most, thanks to its 16:10 display, which also gives it more pixels for getting work done. It's also rated to 300 nits of brightness and is slim and light for travel. It comes in different colors if you're willing to pay a few dollars more. I like this deal so much that I bought one to replace my aging portable monitor from 2018.
Better for games and movies: Arzopa A1 15.6-inch portable monitor
This 1080p portable monitor supports refresh rates up to 144 Hz, is rated to 106% of the sRGB color space, and has a built-in kickstand, a big upgrade over screens with floppy foldble cover stands.
Read moreRead less▼
This FHD, higher-refresh model is better for movie watching and games, as it's 16:9 and the screen is more colorful and responsive. It's rated to 300 nits of brightness and sports two USB-C ports and a Mini HDMI.
Affordable dual-screen dream
This dual-screen 14-inch setup pairs two 1920 x 1200 14-inch IPS panels in a clamshell design with a kickstand. It weighs 2.6 pounds and is rated to 350 nits of brightness.
Read moreRead less▼
What's better than a portable monitor? How about two in a fold-up package that you can connect to your laptop with a USB-C cable (or HDMI) and prop up with a built-in kickstand? There are cheaper dual-screen portable screens available. But most are from no-name brands and/or cost nearly as much as this one from Asus. And this Asus model has a higher brightness rating than most dual-screen alternatives.
The high-res, battery-packing OLED touchscreen champ: Innocn PU15-Pre
This 15.6-inch OLED touch monitor is rated for 400 nits of brightness and sports a pixel-dense 4K resolution as well as packing its own battery that's rfored to four hours of use. While it sadly lacks a kickstand, it does come with a protective case that also functions as a stand.
Read moreRead less▼
Yes, the Innocn PU15-Pre is more expensive than some other deals here. But it's also a 4K OLED panel, with deep blacks, vibrant colors, and a 282 PPI pixel density that's probably better than your laptop screen. It also has a rated 400 nits of brightness that puts it ahead of most portable monitor competition. On top of that, it brings its own battery, so you won't be quickly running down your laptop's cells to keep it going.
If you're a photo or video editor on the go or you just want a pixel-dense screen that will look good next to your laptop's OLED display, this is one of the best premium options we've seen so far during this deals season. The main downside seems to be that this model lacks a kickstand, so you'll have to use the included wrap-around sleeve as a stand, and those tend to be fiddly or flimsy (and sometimes both).

articles.title: La forma más inesperada de usar Windows XP en 2026 está dentro de Linux
articles.text:
Windows XP fue una de las versiones más emblemáticas del sistema operativo de Microsoft. A más de dos décadas de su lanzamiento, la nostalgia sigue muy viva y alguien ya la llevó al siguiente nivel. Un desarrollador consiguió ejecutar el escritorio de Windows XP como entorno gráfico de Linux a través de una versión modificada de Wine.
Conocido como win4wine, este proyecto de código abierto utiliza el archivo explorer.exe de Windows XP para extraer elementos como la barra de tareas, el menú Inicio o las ventanas del explorador de archivos. A diferencia de los temas visuales que imitan la apariencia del sistema operativo de antaño, aquí encontramos los componentes originales. El resultado es una experiencia que reproduce el comportamiento de Windows XP, tal y como lo recordábamos.
De acuerdo con el repositorio de GitHub, win4wine permite que las aplicaciones de Linux puedan mostrarse con marcos de ventana al estilo XP. Estas también se ubican en la barra de tareas del sistema y funcionan con atajos de teclado clásicos, como Alt+Tab. Otra ventaja es que los programas que instales en Linux se pueden añadir al menú Inicio para ofrecer una experiencia unificada.
Para conseguir todo esto, su creador echó mano de Wine 11.0, el cual se ha modificado con más de 150 parches para ejecutar los archivos originales de Windows XP extraídos de una imagen ISO oficial. El proyecto también incluye un gestor de ventanas que integra las aplicaciones nativas de Linux con el shell de Windows XP, así como herramientas para gestionar la bandeja del sistema, el teclado y otros elementos del entorno gráfico.
Win4Wine convierte tu Linux en un Windows XP funcional
En términos de compatibilidad, win4wine ejecuta la interfaz Luna e integra los íconos de red, batería y volumen, que son completamente funcionales. También existe soporte para aplicaciones Win32 (32 y 64 bits) a través de Wine y una pantalla de bienvenida inspirada en la que aparecía al iniciar sesión en Windows XP.
Si te interesa convertir tu Linux en una copia de Windows XP, existen algunas consideraciones. La más importante es que win4wine es un experimento y no se recomienda como un reemplazo del entorno de escritorio moderno.
Para instalar win4wine, el camino óptimo es contar con una imagen ISO de Windows XP Professional SP3 de 32 bits. El repositorio de GitHub no ofrece acceso a los archivos de Microsoft, por lo que tendrás que descargarlos desde Internet Archive. Una vez que la tienes, solo tienes que instalar Debian 13, clonar el repositorio y ejecutar el script de configuración.
git clone https://github.com/mikuta0407/win4wine.git ~/win4wine
cd ~/win4wine
scripts/[setup.sh](http://setup.sh) --media /ruta/a/WindowsXPSP3.iso --greeter
Tras reiniciar el sistema, el entorno puede iniciarse directamente desde la pantalla de bienvenida inspirada en Windows XP.
Una versión basada en Windows 7 también está en desarrollo
El desarrollador de win4wine ha llevado a cabo todas las pruebas en instalaciones nuevas de Debian 13, por lo que recomienda que utilices máquinas virtuales o un ordenador viejo como equipo de prueba antes de experimentar con él. Por último, las únicas versiones de Windows XP confirmadas son las SP3 en idioma inglés y japonés. Es probable que también funcione con el ISO en español usando la misma configuración.
Aquellos que no cuenten con una ISO de Windows XP podrán probar el proyecto usando el shell de ReactOS, el cual se descarga automáticamente desde las versiones oficiales de ese sistema operativo de código abierto. También existe una implementación basada en el shell de Windows 7, aunque todavía se encuentra en una fase preliminar de desarrollo y no ofrece todas las bondades de la variante con XP.

articles.title: RTO Grow vs the patchwork: why Australian RTOs are moving to one LMS learning management system
articles.text:
RTO Grow is the learning management system Australian RTOs are moving to when they’re done juggling software. It runs the whole RTO in one place: booking, enrolment, learning, marking, compliance and the certificate at the end.
Most RTOs didn’t plan to end up with four systems. It happened one problem at a time. An LMS for the learning. A student management system for enrolments and reporting. A spreadsheet for trainer credentials. A CRM for leads. Then someone in the office spends every week copying data from one to the next.
RTO Grow puts all of it in one system, so nothing gets copied and nothing goes missing.
Where the patchwork breaks
- Resubmissions get lost. When the LMS and SMS are only linked one way, a resubmitted assessment or a corrected result doesn’t flow back. Someone fixes it by hand, or nobody notices until audit.
- Enrolment forms collect the wrong data. A booking tool bolted onto an SMS means two forms, two sets of rules, and gaps in the student record.
- Compliance relies on memory. Pre-training reviews, LLND, LLN support plans and trainer credentials get chased manually across different tools.
- Trainers waste time. They log into one system to mark, another to check a student’s history, and email the office for everything else.
How RTO Grow does it in one system
- One record per student. The LMS, student management and quality management share the same record, so every result, resubmission and email shows everywhere straight away.
- Enrolment to certificate, connected. Learners book, pay, enrol, complete their pre-training review, study, submit and receive their certificate without leaving RTO Grow.
- Compliance that runs itself. Pre-training reviews and LLND go out automatically after every application, LLN support plans are created when needed, and trainer credentials are checked against units before rostering.
- Content built in. The AI content builder creates learner guides, assessments, slides and gamified courses in minutes, inside the same system the learners use.
- Marketing and leads in the same place. Lead pipelines, email templates and automations come built in, so there’s no separate CRM to pay for.
- Portals for everyone. Admin, trainer, student, employer and third party portals, all from one login.
- Australian built and hosted. Data stays in Sydney, support requests are handled the same day, and RTO Grow is AVETMISS™ 8.0 Ready and built for the Standards for RTOs 2025.
- Easy for everyone. Older and non-technical staff pick it up quickly, with one clear next step on every screen.
Side-by-side
| What your RTO needs | The patchwork | RTO Grow | 
| Online learning and assessment | One system | Built in | 
| Enrolments, USI and government reporting | A second system | Built in | 
| Pre-training review and LLND | Chased by hand | Sent automatically | 
| Trainer credential checks | A spreadsheet | Checked before rostering | 
| Learner guides and assessments | Bought or written elsewhere | AI content builder built in | 
| Leads and marketing emails | A separate CRM | Built in | 
| One record per student | Spread across tools | Yes | 
| Pricing | Several subscriptions | One flat price, no per-enrolment or per-staff fees, no exit fee | 
What the patchwork costs your RTO
Every extra system comes with its own subscription, its own login and its own training. New staff learn three or four tools before they’re useful. Trainers keep a password for each one. Someone in the office becomes the person who knows how the data moves between them, and when they’re on leave, it stops moving.
The bigger cost is time. Every enrolment typed into a second system, every result copied across by hand and every report rebuilt from exports is time taken away from learners. Every copy is also a chance for a typo, a missed field or an out-of-date record. When a funding report is due, someone spends days pulling exports from each system and matching them up.
Trainers feel it too. When a result is entered in one place and checked in another, they end up answering the same questions from the office again and again, instead of spending that time with learners. New trainers take longer to settle in because there is more to learn before they can do their actual job.
With RTO Grow there’s one subscription, one login and one place to train your team. Pricing is flat, so adding students or staff doesn’t add fees, and your data can be exported as CSV or ZIP files whenever you like, with no exit fee.
Why one system is easier to keep compliant
When your data lives in four places, compliance depends on people remembering to copy things across. Someone forgets, and the gap sits there until audit.
In one system, the record keeping happens as the work happens. Enrolment forms file themselves against the student. Pre-training reviews and LLND results are saved to the same record. Evidence is filed as learners submit it. Trainer credentials are checked before anyone is rostered, and LLN support plans are created the moment LLND shows a learner needs extra help.
The human eye stays where it belongs: reviewing work, marking, and making the final competency decision. Everything else is handled by the system, which helps you maintain audit-ready evidence without the end-of-quarter scramble.
And when someone asks for a student’s full history, it’s one screen. Pre-training review, enrolment form, payments, logins, emails and results, all together. It is ready the moment an auditor or a student asks for it.
Questions to ask in your next demo
- Show me a resubmission from start to finish. In RTO Grow it goes straight back to the trainer and updates the student record everywhere.
- How does a learner get from your website to enrolled and learning? In RTO Grow it’s one journey in one system.
- What happens after someone applies? RTO Grow sends the pre-training review and LLND automatically.
- Where is our data hosted? RTO Grow keeps it in Sydney.
- How long does it take a new trainer to learn it? RTO Grow is built so anyone can follow it, including staff who don’t love technology.
If your team is copying data between systems every week, it’s time to see an LMS learning management system that delivers, tracks and reports from one set of data. RTO Grow runs a free weekly live demo and a free 7-day trial, so you can watch it run your RTO before you commit.

articles.title: Quatre hommes jugés à Nancy pour de faux placements crypto
articles.text:
Une centaine de victimes, en majorité des particuliers démarchés par téléphone, auraient perdu environ quatre millions d'euros dans de faux placements en cryptomonnaies et en diamants. Mardi, à Nancy, le parquet a demandé jusqu'à douze ans de prison contre les quatre hommes jugés dans cette affaire.
En 2014, la cour d'appel de Paris a condamné Fabrice Sakoun à sept ans de prison pour une escroquerie à la taxe carbone, une affaire où la justice voyait en lui le « cerveau ». Ce Franco-Israélien de 53 ans vit aujourd'hui en Israël, et l'accusation le soupçonne d'avoir commandé une nouvelle arnaque, menée en France et en Belgique entre 2017 et 2018. Le procureur Vincent Legaut a requis contre lui douze ans de prison et 750 000 euros d'amende devant la Juridiction interrégionale spécialisée (Jirs) de Nancy, un pôle de magistrats chargé de la criminalité organisée. Les quatre prévenus sont présumés innocents, et le tribunal rendra son jugement le 9 décembre. Pour entrer dans l'arnaque, les victimes versaient d'abord 500 euros.
Les escrocs réclamaient toujours plus d'argent avant de couper le contact
Au téléphone, un prétendu conseiller promettait de gros rendements, puis il orientait la victime vers de faux sites d'investissement en cryptomonnaies ou en diamants. Après la première mise de 500 euros, il organisait chaque semaine des séances de trading avec elle, pendant plusieurs mois. Et les victimes continuaient à investir. L'une d'elles a perdu 150 000 euros, « les économies de toute une vie », d'après son avocat, Me Philippe Guillemard.
Mais quand les victimes demandaient à récupérer leurs gains, alors que leur contrat le prévoyait, leur conseiller disparaissait, avec sa ligne téléphonique et son adresse e-mail. Certaines ont ensuite reçu des courriels qui leur réclamaient de fausses amendes, et plusieurs les ont payées. Selon un sondage BVA réalisé en 2024 pour l'AMF, deux victimes probables d'une arnaque à l'investissement sur trois ont été recontactées par des escrocs après coup, et ceux-ci proposaient de récupérer leur argent.
Si un inconnu vous appelle pour vous proposer un placement, vous pouvez chercher son site sur les listes noires de l'Autorité des marchés financiers. Un vendeur de placements en diamants doit en outre faire enregistrer son offre auprès de l'AMF. Après une arnaque, vous devez porter plainte au commissariat ou à la gendarmerie, et l'AMF met en garde contre les faux avocats prêts à vous rendre votre argent contre des honoraires.
Le parquet soupçonne un octogénaire d'avoir organisé le blanchiment
Les enquêteurs ont suivi l'argent des victimes jusqu'à des comptes bancaires en Espagne, en Pologne, en République tchèque et à Hong Kong. Selon l'accusation, William Z., 80 ans, a créé plus d'une dizaine de sociétés un peu partout en Europe, et il a ouvert leurs comptes. Excusé pour raisons de santé, il ne conteste pas les faits, selon son avocat, Me Mattéo Cerimele. Le procureur a requis six ans de prison et 300 000 euros d'amende contre lui, un montant « totalement disproportionné », a protesté l'avocat, car son client touche moins de 1 000 euros de retraite.
Samuel F., 53 ans, seul prévenu à l'audience lundi, affirme avoir été « berné » par un homme rencontré en Israël. Pour le parquet, il a joué un rôle périphérique, mais il a participé en quelques mois à des mouvements de fonds de 1,8 million d'euros. Le procureur a requis deux ans de prison avec mandat de dépôt, c'est-à-dire une incarcération immédiate, et 10 000 euros d'amende pour blanchiment. Son avocat, Me Michel Harroch, a plaidé la relaxe pour association de malfaiteurs, en présentant son client en « gérant de paille », qui a prêté son nom et sa carte d'identité contre de l'argent.
Fabrice Sakoun a refusé de répondre aux enquêteurs français lors de son audition en Israël. La France le recherche avec un mandat d'arrêt, et une demande d'extradition est en cours. Hicham E., 41 ans, en fuite depuis 2021 et soupçonné d'avoir servi d'exécutant, principalement depuis le Maroc, fait lui aussi l'objet d'un mandat d'arrêt, et le parquet a requis trois ans de prison contre lui. Les quatre hommes doivent en outre répondre d'une tentative d'escroquerie de plus de deux millions d'euros contre la Métropole de Nice.
Leurs victimes veulent « essayer de récupérer ce qu'elles ont perdu », explique Me Arnaud Delomel, l'avocat de onze d'entre elles et de l'Association de défense des consommateurs. Mais si le tribunal condamne les prévenus à verser de lourdes amendes à l'État, elles pourraient avoir plus de mal à se faire rembourser, regrette-t-il.

articles.title: Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down; Lakshmi Venu moves court over family dispute
articles.text:
Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down; Lakshmi Venu moves court over family dispute
Under Krishnamurthy’s leadership, Flipkart grew more than fivefold and strengthened its position in India’s ecommerce market. The company is now preparing for a leadership transition.
Dear Reader,
Kalyan Krishnamurthy is stepping down as Flipkart CEO after more than 11 years with the company. More on who will lead Flipkart in the interim below.
India’s spacetech ambitions are getting a boost, with Karnataka approving Bengaluru-based Pixxel’s Rs 350 crore proposal to set up a satellite manufacturing facility in the state. The investment further strengthens Bengaluru’s position as a hub for aerospace and advanced manufacturing.
Meanwhile, AI infrastructure is attracting fresh capital, from data centres to startups that could test their products on live projects. Engineering consultancy Rodic Consultants has proposed a Rs 200 crore fund to back startups developing AI and other technologies for infrastructure, with selected companies getting access to live projects.
Nexent Capital has also launched a $1 billion fund to invest in AI data centres, quantum-ready infrastructure and advanced energy across India and North America, with a $20 million anchor commitment from the Tyagi family office.
Early-stage funding is broadening too. US-based VU Venture Partners has launched an accelerator and investment platform in India targeting cheques of $100,000 to $1 million, while Bengaluru-based Aeravti Ventures is targeting Rs 300 crore for its second fund to back 9 to 10 startups across food security, healthcare infrastructure and physical security.
Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs and Societe Generale have acquired a combined stake in eyewear retailer Lenskart for Rs 920.58 crore through block deals, signalling continued investor interest in the company.

articles.title: 1Password customer data stolen after employee GitHub account breach
articles.text:
1Password has disclosed a data breach after an employee's corporate GitHub account was hacked and used to deploy malicious code to the company's backend services to steal customer data.
The company says customer password vaults and the encryption keys protecting them were not compromised in the attack.
In a security incident disclosure published today, 1Password says it began investigating the breach on November 19 after detecting indications that an employee's GitHub account had been compromised.
The attacker used the account to access private source code repositories and inject malicious code into backend services that downloaded customer account records.
The stolen data includes:
- Customer names and email addresses
- Account and user IDs
- Account creation and last sign-in timestamps
- Public cryptographic keys
- Secure Remote Password (SRP) protocol parameters
- Invitation, provisioning, and account recovery tokens
- Other internal account metadata
The attacker also stole internal company source code and accessed its continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) environment, potentially exposing internal infrastructure credentials.
Among the stolen customer data were tokens embedded in links that 1Password emailed to users to accept account provisioning invitations or recover their accounts.
However, 1Password says these tokens cannot be used on their own to access customer accounts, as completing the invitation or recovery process requires either single sign-on (SSO) authentication or a six-digit verification code sent to the user's registered email address.
The company says only a small number of users were affected and have been individually notified.
As a precaution against brute-force attacks, 1Password has strengthened these verification codes from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric characters.
The company says it has now disabled the compromised GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, restored clean versions of affected services, and rotated or revoked potentially exposed infrastructure credentials.
1Password has also hired independent cybersecurity experts to validate its remediation efforts and says it has found no internal evidence of customer account takeovers.
The company is not requiring customers to change their account passwords or Secret Keys but warns them to watch for unexpected invitations, account recovery requests, and other potential phishing attempts.
While customer vaults were not compromised in the attack, the stolen data is valuable to threat actors as it provides a list of known 1Password users who could be targeted in phishing campaigns.
Threat actors could send emails impersonating 1Password, using the breach as a lure to trick customers into disclosing their account passwords, Secret Keys, or recovery verification codes.
Customers should be particularly wary of emails claiming they need to secure their accounts in response to the breach, reset their passwords, or verify their account information.
Rather than clicking on links in these emails, customers should access their accounts directly through the 1Password website or app and never share their passwords, Secret Keys, or verification codes with anyone.
BleepingComputer contacted 1Password with questions about the attack but has not yet received a response.

articles.title: Clint Eastwood (96 años) hablaba así de Estados Unidos: “No hay muchas formas de arte estadounidenses que sean originales”
articles.text:
Clint Eastwood se hizo famoso en todo el mundo como pistolero en las películas de Sergio Leone. Cuando hablaba de este género, lo hacía desde su propio punto de vista, ya que también era director. “No hay muchas formas de arte estadounidenses que sean originales”, aseguraba en un pasaje de una recopilación de sus entrevistas (publicadas entre 1968 y 1995).
“Me siento muy cercano al wéstern”. Para Eastwood, la mayor parte de las formas de arte americanas son derivadas de las tradiciones europeas. Pero hay algunas excepciones, como el cine del Oeste, el jazz o el blues. En 1987, durante el rodaje de Bird (su biopic sobre Charlie Parker), también mencionó el jazz y el wéstern como las dos aportaciones originales americanas.
Para Eastwood, el wéstern formaba parte del patrimonio cultural de Estados Unidos. El género llevó al cine las historias de frontera. Contribuyó a crear la imagen popular del Viejo Oeste.
Eastwood también dirigió y protagonizó sus propios wésterns en numerosas ocasiones. Es el caso de Infierno de cobardes (1973) o El fuera de la ley (1976). Regresó al Oeste en El jinete pálido (1985), una de sus películas favoritas, o en Sin perdón (1992, por la que recibió el Óscar a la mejor dirección en 1993). Décadas más tarde utilizó algunos elementos de este género en Cry Macho (2021).
Quienes quieran volver a ellas pueden buscar por plataforma. En la trilogía que le dio fama como el Hombre sin Nombre, trabajó tres veces bajo las órdenes de Leone. Primero en Por un puñado de dólares (1964), después en La muerte tenía un precio (1965) y luego en El bueno, el feo y el malo (1966).

articles.title: Lumineux en 4K, ce vidéoprojecteur Dangbei perd 120 € à l'occasion du Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le vidéoprojecteur Dangbei Mars Pro 2 (DBOX02) Avec pied réglable à 1 290,00 €
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le Dangbei Mars Pro 2 (DBOX02) passe à 1 290,00 € chez Son-Video.com, soit une baisse d'environ 9 % et 120,00 € d'économie. Fort d'une image 4K lumineuse complétée par l'interface Google TV avec Netflix natif, ce modèle affiche une note actuelle de 4,5/5 dans nos tests.
Le Dangbei Mars Pro 2 (DBOX02) est un vidéoprojecteur laser tout-en-un pensé pour installer une séance de cinéma chez soi avec un minimum d'appareils externes. Il réunit une définition 4K, un système sonore complet et l'interface Google TV avec Netflix intégré pour lancer directement ses contenus. Ce modèle avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de ses essais.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, ce projecteur descend à 1 290,00 € chez Son-Video.com, soit environ 9 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (1 410,00 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 120,00 €.
Une image 4K lumineuse et un fonctionnement discret
Le Dangbei Mars Pro 2 projette une image nette grâce à sa définition 4K de 3840 x 2160 pixels, qui permet d'afficher les détails les plus fins sur une très grande surface sans perte de piqué. Notre banc d'essai a relevé une luminosité maximale de 192 cd/m², une valeur solide qui autorise des projections confortables sans plonger la pièce dans une obscurité totale. Pour découvrir l'ensemble de nos mesures, vous pouvez consulter notre test complet. Le constructeur a également soigné le confort d'écoute : le niveau sonore mesuré se limite à 36 dB(A), ce qui rend la ventilation discrète pendant la lecture des vidéos.
Dangbei Mars Pro 2 (DBOX02)
Points forts
- Qualité d’image 4K.
- Luminosité très élevée.
- Nombreux réglages disponibles.
- Compensation de mouvement très efficace.
- Interface Google TV avec Netflix.
- Connectique complète.
- Silencieux.
Points faibles
- Contraste limité.
- Retient les traces de doigts.
- Pied optionnel.
- Télécommande basique et non rétroéclairée.
- Pas vraiment dédié au gaming compétitif.
Une utilisation quotidienne simple malgré un contraste en retrait
L'interface Google TV embarquée donne un accès direct aux principales applications de streaming avec une navigation fluide, sans ajouter de boîtier supplémentaire. Ce modèle, actuellement noté 4,5/5 par notre rédaction, accuse en revanche un taux de contraste mesuré à 818 :1. Ce chiffre limite la profondeur des noirs dans les scènes très sombres, ce qui gênera les amateurs de cinéma exigeants mais reste secondaire pour regarder des séries ou du sport en pleine journée. Sa latence mesurée à 31 ms convient aux sessions de jeu occasionnelles, sans convenir aux joueurs compétitifs à la recherche d'une réactivité immédiate.
XGIMI Horizon 20 : l'autre option face au Dangbei Mars Pro 2
Le XGIMI Horizon 20 adopte un positionnement proche avec son image 4K et son système Google TV, mais il mise davantage sur l'ergonomie physique. Il intègre notamment un pied sur balancelle, un zoom optique et un lens shift pour ajuster l'image sans déplacer le boîtier, alors que le Dangbei Mars Pro 2 demande un pied optionnel pour faciliter son orientation.
Les deux appareils s'affichent au même tarif, avec un écart de prix de 0,00 €. Le XGIMI Horizon 20, actuellement noté 5/5 par notre rédaction, propose une installation plus simple grâce à son pied intégré, mais le Dangbei Mars Pro 2 conserve une luminosité très élevée pour les pièces moins sombres.
XGIMI Horizon 20
Points forts
- Design soigné.
- Pic lumineux élevé.
- Image 4K détaillée.
- Zoom optique et lens shift.
- Pied intégré sur balancelle.
- Correction du trapèze et mise au point automatiques efficaces.
- Google TV complet et fluide.
- Compatibilité HDR10+ et Dolby Vision.
- Input lag particulièrement faible.
- Télécommande rétroéclairée.
- Ventilation très silencieuse.
Points faibles
- Colorimétrie perfectible.
- Contraste encore limité.
- Audio correct, mais qui manque de coffre.

articles.title: Varios usuarios han mostrado en directo cómo 'GTA VI' fríe sus consolas. De momento no es como para perder la calma
articles.text:
Llevo casi una semana jugando bastante a 'GTA VI' en una PS5 de 2020 sin ningún tipo de problema. No suena más de la cuenta ni me ha dado ningún error raro. Sin embargo, no todos pueden decir lo mismo, ya que por redes están circulando vídeos sobre consolas que dejan de funcionar con fallos visuales típicos de una GPU o VRAM que deja de funcionar como debe.
Esto ya ha encendido las alarmas, claro, y aunque no hay comunicados oficiales, las redes ya están dictando sentencia.
En corto. Tom Warren, periodista de The Verge, es uno de los que se ha hecho eco del problema citando un vídeo en el que a una streamer se le 'fríe' la consola en pleno directo. Empiezan a aparecer artefactos en la pantalla, que se congela y lleva al apagado de la consola.
En su caso, una PS5 que, como mostró poco después, había limpiado para no tener polvo acumulado en la zona del ventilador. También afirma tenerla en un espacio bien ventilado y, claro, se empezó a decir que 'GTA VI' está derritiendo la PS5.
No sólo PS5. Uno de los primeros culpables al que apuntaron algunos fue al sistema de disipación de calor de la consola de Sony. Los japoneses, al contrario que Microsoft, utilizaron metal líquido para conducir el calor de la APU al disipador y, con el tiempo, puede presentar fugas. Se ha dicho que, sobre todo, si está en vertical la consola es más susceptible debido a una degradación en las máquinas más antiguas del encapsulado de la APU. Pero, al margen de esto, los fallos no son sólo cosa de PS5.
En Reddit hay un hilo bastante generoso en el que hay usuarios que también están reportando fallos de sus Series X y Series S. Algunos responden a bugs del juego, pero otros muestran vídeos e imágenes que se corresponden con esos fallos de GPU/VRAM. Un taller llamado Solder Surgeon aseguró en un comunicado propio del 22 de noviembre que reparó 38 consolas (PS5 y Xbox Series X) durante las 72 horas posteriores al lanzamiento, atribuyendo los problemas al metal líquido en el caso de PS5, a daños en la alimentación eléctrica y a puertos HDMI mal soldados.
Exigente. Es innegable que 'GTA VI' es un juego tremendamente exigente. Es de lo más impresionante que he visto en cualquier plataforma y no es algo al aire: la propia Digital Foundry ha afirmado que nunca se ha hecho algo así en tiempo real. Es lógico que lleve las consolas al límite, pero en el caso de PS5, y como leemos en Notebookcheck, el técnico modyfikatorcasper midió 220 W con el juego encendido, pero sin hacer nada. Durante una prueba de carga máxima, el medidor registró 274,2 W.
Como apuntan, Sony diseñó el hardware para funcionar a 340-350 W como máximo y los juegos normalmente consumen entre 180 y 220 W, por lo que 'GTA VI' es, definitivamente, más glotón, pero no lleva al límite la energía de la máquina.
El matiz. Lo que sí puede pasar, y es algo que apunta el propio técnico, es que ese mayor consumo de energía y, por tanto, mayores temperaturas internas, hagan que el material entre la APU y el disipador pueda ser más maleable. En las consolas más nuevas o en la PS5 Pro se introdujeron cambios para mitigar esas fugas del metal líquido durante los vaivenes de la temperatura, pero podría afectar a las consolas más antiguas.
Cuidados. El asunto de la PS5 en vertical tiene sentido porque el metal líquido se puede ir deformando hasta no llegar a cubrir de forma homogénea la superficie de la APU, lo que hace que pierda propiedades de disipación. Hay recomendaciones básicas como una limpieza interior regular (da "miedo" desmontar un cacharro, pero no es tan difícil y hay mil tutoriales) y, sobre todo, no tenerla encajonada para que pueda 'respirar', pero esos cuidados son muy generales y llega un momento en el que pierden efectividad.
Las consolas se rompen por diferentes motivos, pero en el caso de la disipación, lo más efectivo es hacer un cambio de metal líquido o de pasta térmica. También puedes hacerlo en casa, aunque si nunca te has puesto, es algo más delicado que simplemente abrir para aspirar el polvo. Estos materiales se degradan, pierden efectividad y pueden causar esos fallos que estamos viendo, por lo que una visita a un técnico de confianza no está de más.
¿Anecdótico? De la forma que sea, aquí me gustaría tocar madera porque mi PS5 lleva en vertical seis años sin ningún problema y, además, poner un poco los pies en el suelo. Antes del primer día, 'GTA VI' vendió más de 30 millones de unidades, por lo que hay mucha, muchísima gente que está jugando al título de Rockstar y no a todos les están dando fallos.
Lo más fácil es que el juego, al exigir ese punto de más respecto a otros, está sacando a relucir algún fallo que la propia máquina ya podía tener, con la mala suerte de 'freírla'. Si la cosa se pone más seria y es la que empieza a hacer que una oleada de máquinas empiecen a fallar, hablaremos de ello, pero de momento, simplemente, parece muy mala suerte para un pequeño porcentaje de todos los jugadores que se han hecho con el título.

articles.title: Ryanair, easyJet, British Airways : 140 avions ont perdu le GPS en plein vol au-dessus de la mer du Nord
articles.text:
L’incident a duré une vingtaine de minutes, mais il a touché un nombre inhabituel d’appareils. Le 9 novembre, quelque 140 vols ont perdu leur signal GPS au-dessus du nord de l’Europe et de la mer du Nord, selon une analyse du spécialiste du renseignement aéronautique Hexbird, révélée par le quotidien britannique The i Paper. Parmi eux figuraient des avions partis d’Édimbourg, de Manchester et de Londres Heathrow, dont un Ryanair à destination de Rome, un easyJet vers Hurghada, en Égypte, et un British Airways vers Stockholm. Une quarantaine d’appareils se trouvaient dans l’espace aérien britannique ou à proximité, et sept vols ayant signalé la perte du GPS ont été guidés vers l’aéroport d’Amsterdam-Schiphol, selon le contrôle aérien néerlandais.
Une analyse de la plateforme Hexbird a fait remonter la source probable du brouillage à un unique émetteur radio situé en mer du Nord, à environ 300 kilomètres des côtes anglaises. Au même moment, trois cargos russes dont les propriétaires sont visés par des sanctions britanniques, américaines et européennes, le Lady R, le Lady D et le Maia-1, traversaient la zone sous l’escorte d’un navire de guerre russe, eux-mêmes suivis par un bâtiment français et un navire néerlandais.
Un navire militaire « presque certainement » à l’origine
Hexbird reste prudent et précise que son analyse « n’identifie pas le convoi comme la source, mais ne l’exclut pas non plus ». Ancien officier du renseignement naval, James Droxford est plus affirmatif. Selon lui, le navire de guerre russe est « presque certainement à l’origine du brouillage GPS, et non les navires marchands », peut-être pour décourager la surveillance de l’Otan.
Directeur général du Royal Institute of Navigation, Ramsey Faragher estime lui aussi que la puissance du brouillage, sur une zone très étendue, désigne plutôt une plateforme militaire dédiée. Si la piste russe se confirmait, ce serait « une intensification des perturbations que nous avons observées jusqu’à présent », juge Thomas Withington, spécialiste de la guerre électronique. « C’est la première fois, à ma connaissance, que l’on observe quelque chose d’aussi loin à l’ouest », ajoute-t-il.
Tous les acteurs ne partagent pas le même constat. Le contrôleur aérien britannique Nats assure n’avoir reçu aucun signalement de pilote faisant état d’un brouillage GPS ce jour-là, tandis que le gouvernement britannique refuse de commenter. La compagnie KLM a en revanche signalé l’incident aux autorités, qualifiant le brouillage et le leurrage de « phénomène international croissant ».
Pourquoi les avions n’ont pas été en danger
Le brouillage consiste à émettre de puissants signaux radio pour noyer ceux des satellites, très faibles une fois arrivés sur Terre. Le récepteur GPS ne parvient alors plus à calculer sa position ni l’heure exacte. Il ne faut pas le confondre avec le leurrage, ou spoofing, qui envoie de fausses positions au récepteur. Les avions de ligne ne dépendent toutefois pas du seul GPS et disposent de systèmes de navigation de secours tandis que les pilotes sont formés à voler sans signal satellite. Selon The i Paper, l’incident n’a d’ailleurs eu aucun impact opérationnel.
Les experts redoutent surtout un enchaînement de pannes. Un brouillage de cette ampleur coïncidant avec une défaillance du contrôle aérien serait un « scénario apocalyptique », estime Eric Schouten, ancien officier du renseignement néerlandais et dirigeant de la société de sûreté aérienne Dyami. Le risque dépasse aussi l’aviation, car de nombreux services s’appuient sur l’heure fournie par les satellites. « Le Royaume-Uni a eu de la chance que cela se produise aussi loin des côtes, car nous n’aurions pas voulu qu’un tel niveau de brouillage GPS inonde des choses comme nos réseaux de téléphonie mobile et nos stations de radio numérique DAB », souligne Ramsey Faragher.
Ces perturbations ont toutefois tendance à se multiplier depuis plusieurs années près des frontières russes, notamment autour de l’enclave de Kaliningrad. Elles ont d’ailleurs déjà affecté des personnalités, comme la présidente de la Commission européenne Ursula von der Leyen. En 2025, son avion avait été perturbé par un brouillage attribué à la Russie lors d’un déplacement en Bulgarie. Moscou présente de son côté ses brouilleurs comme une protection contre les attaques de drones ukrainiens. L’incident du 9 novembre se distingue par sa position, bien plus à l’ouest qu’à l’accoutumée.

articles.title: Mock Service Worker Releases v3.0 with ESM-Only Build, Socket-Based Interception and GraphQL Subs
articles.text:
Mock Service Worker, the API mocking library maintained by Artem Zakharchenko, has released version 3.0, nearly three years after the Fetch-based v2.0 rewrite. The release ships as ESM-only, completes the library's GraphQL story with subscription support, and introduces a socket-based interception algorithm in Node.js that Zakharchenko describes as going as deep into the runtime as JavaScript will allow without recompiling Node.
The headline breaking change is that MSW is now distributed natively as ECMAScript Modules only, with support for Node.js v18 and v20 dropped in favour of v22, v24, and v26. TypeScript 5.9 is now the minimum supported version. Several transitive dependencies have been removed, including graphql (now a proper optional peer), path-to-regexp, picocolors, and statuses. The result is a library tarball that drops from 416KB to 234KB, with type definitions shrinking by half, from 190KB to 90KB.
Alongside ESM, v3.0 introduces granular entrypoints that replace the single msw import with designated paths for each protocol:
import { http } from 'msw/http'
import { graphql } from 'msw/graphql'
import { sse } from 'msw/sse'
import { ws } from 'msw/ws'
GraphQL subscription support, a long-standing community request on the project's tracker, lands in this release. Building on the WebSocket interception shipped previously, subscription handlers can now be defined against a graphql.link() and publish events on demand, closing the gap between MSW's HTTP, WebSocket, and GraphQL coverage.
An experimental defineNetwork API is introduced as the eventual replacement for setupServer and setupWorker. The new primitive splits interception into sources (where traffic comes from) and handlers (how it is answered), allowing teams to replay HAR files, combine custom interceptors, or hand control of request timing to a test runner. The first ecosystem package to expose it directly is @msw/cloudflare, which wraps the API for Workers environments.
The most technically significant change sits in the underlying Interceptors library. Zakharchenko writes that after seven attempts at the problem, the team has moved network interception in Node.js down to the TCP and TLS wraps, the JavaScript bindings for Node's C-level network code. Moving any lower, he notes, would require recompiling Node.js itself. The new architecture supports arbitrary socket-based protocols, with SMTP cited as an early example. Nock already relies on the Interceptors library for its Node.js support.
A GitHub discussion reports failing tests after upgrading, traced to MSW now intercepting the browser-issued OPTIONS preflight requests that previous versions quietly ignored. Separately, a developer in discussion #2771 challenged the earlier decision to deprioritise Jest and JSDOM, arguing that a runner with 46 million weekly downloads warrants a formal breaking-change note rather than a quiet docs change.
In the Node-only space, MSW continues to compete with Nock, fetch-mock, and undici's built-in MockAgent, though as a recent comparison notes, none of those cover both browser and server with a single handler definition.
Teams on v2 should consult the official 2.x to 3.x migration guide before upgrading. Full release notes are available on GitHub.
Mock Service Worker is an open-source, MIT-licensed JavaScript library for mocking network traffic using Service Workers in the browser and runtime-level interception in Node.js. It is used widely for frontend and full-stack testing, and now covers HTTP, WebSocket, Server-Sent Events, and GraphQL including subscriptions.

articles.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets, but cleared of racketeering
articles.text:
The big picture: Washington has spent the better part of a decade calling Huawei a threat, though mostly via bans and blacklists rather than in a courtroom. On Tuesday, a jury finally got its say, and the result was split. Jurors in Brooklyn found the company guilty of conspiring to steal trade secrets from American rivals. But they acquitted Huawei of the racketeering charge that was supposed to tie the whole case together.
Huawei was convicted on 10 of the 12 counts it faced after a trial that ran about 11 weeks. Along with the trade secret conspiracy, those counts included bank fraud, wire fraud, money laundering, and sanctions violations linked to its business in Iran. The jury acquitted it of racketeering conspiracy and of conspiring to obstruct justice.
Losing the racketeering charge stings for prosecutors, since it was the one they used to paint Huawei as a criminal enterprise that lied and stole its way to the top over two decades. Huawei's lawyer, Brian Heberlig, called the acquittal a "profound rejection" of that story. The company itself says the remaining charges are just as baseless and that it will take "all necessary legal actions."
Still, some of what the jurors heard was surprisingly low-tech. Prosecutors said a Huawei worker once carried a robotic arm out of a competitor's lab so it could be photographed and measured. Someone else allegedly snapped pictures of a rival's networking hardware at a trade show in Chicago. The companies named in court records include Cisco, Motorola Solutions, T-Mobile, and Fujitsu.
Jurors also heard from a former Huawei trainer named Heather Campbell. According to The Bureau, she described a document from headquarters that offered staff rewards for gathering competitors' information. The most confidential finds were meant to be encrypted and sent to China. She ended up taking the document to the FBI.
For its part, Huawei argued that the government stitched a handful of employees' misdeeds into a grand conspiracy at a company with more than 200,000 workers. It also pointed out that the five trade secret disputes cited at trial were civil cases settled over the past 20 years.
What the verdict changes in practice is less clear. After all, Huawei is already barred from selling its gear to US carriers and has sat on a US trade blacklist since 2019, so there isn't much left for Washington to cut off. Meanwhile, the company still does business in more than 170 countries and has made significant advances in developing its own chips.

articles.title: What is a thought made of? Why human consciousness may be beyond AI’s reach
articles.text:
What is a thought made of? Why human consciousness may be beyond AI’s reach
- Date:
  November 25, 2026
- Source:
  The Hebrew University of Jerusalem
- Summary:
  A new theory suggests that the brain may chemically encode and retrieve memories rather than relying solely on electrical signals. Researchers propose that interactions between brain cells and their molecular surroundings could help explain the intimate connection between memory, emotion, and thought. Their findings challenge the assumption that increasingly powerful computers could eventually develop human-like consciousness.
- Share:
The fundamental difference between human intelligence and artificial intelligence may have less to do with computing power than with the chemistry of memory. Researchers propose that the brain not only communicates through electrical signals but may also "write" and "read" memories through chemical interactions involving neurons, astrocytes, and the molecules surrounding them. By linking memory to emotion and thought, the theory raises an increasingly relevant question: Can computational power alone give rise to the kind of consciousness experienced by living organisms?
Hearing a familiar song can transport someone back decades. A distinctive scent can bring a forgotten person or place to mind, while recalling a terrifying experience can trigger both emotional and physical reactions within moments.
Like the human brain, computers can store and retrieve information. However, the mechanisms underlying biological memory may be fundamentally different.
A new review by Dr. Gerard Marx of MX Biotech Ltd. and Professor Chaim Gilon of the Department of Chemistry at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem explores the physical and chemical mechanisms that could link memory, emotion, and thought.
In their paper, "Consciousness, Memory and Intelligence: A Mechanistic Perspective," the researchers suggest that understanding memory requires more than studying neurons and their electrical activity. They argue that other brain cells, particularly astrocytes, and the intricate molecular environment surrounding them may also play essential roles.
Building on their previous research into the molecular foundations of memory, Marx and Gilon examine whether the processes responsible for storing and retrieving experiences could also shed light on the origins of intelligence, thought, and consciousness.
The Brain's Hidden Chemical Code for Memory
Central to the researchers' proposal is a model known as the Tripartite Mechanism of Memory.
According to this theory, memories emerge from interactions between three major components: brain cells, especially astrocytes working alongside neurons; the molecular substances surrounding those cells; and various chemicals, including metal ions, neurotransmitters, and gliotransmitters.
Rather than relying exclusively on electrical communication between neurons, the brain may use chemical processes to encode and retrieve information.
Astrocytes, which are abundant throughout the brain and maintain close interactions with neurons, are particularly important to this proposed mechanism. Marx and Gilon suggest that groups of astrocytes help process cognitive information through their interactions with neurons and the extracellular environment, the space and molecular material surrounding brain cells.
The new paper expands this hypothesis to explore the nature of thought itself. If the brain can physically encode an experience as a memory, the process of recovering that information, recognizing it, and interpreting its significance might contribute to the formation of thoughts.
Why Memories Carry Emotional Meaning
One of the central arguments of the researchers' theory is that biological memories contain more than stored information. They are also closely connected to emotional experiences.
A scent associated with childhood may spark feelings of happiness. Hearing a familiar voice can provide reassurance, while remembering a frightening event may produce an immediate physical response.
Marx and Gilon contend that a physical model of memory must account for these emotional associations. Their proposed mechanism incorporates neurotransmitters and other chemical messengers that may help encode cognitive information alongside its emotional significance.
This potential biochemical connection between memory and emotion provides a starting point for investigating larger questions about how the brain generates thought, intelligence, and conscious experiences.
What Human Consciousness May Have That AI Lacks
The rapid development of artificial intelligence makes these ideas particularly relevant.
Although computers and brains can both retain and access information, the physical mechanisms behind these abilities may differ considerably. Computer memory is ultimately encoded in electronic hardware. Biological memory, the researchers propose, may instead depend on the intricate cellular and chemical machinery of living brain tissue.
This distinction becomes increasingly significant as AI systems grow more capable of performing tasks traditionally associated with human reasoning and intelligence.
Marx and Gilon challenge the assumption that simply increasing computational power and complexity will eventually produce consciousness comparable to that of a living brain. They argue that electronic systems lack the biological structures and emotional mechanisms found in living organisms.
The researchers are not suggesting that AI cannot develop increasingly advanced intellectual capabilities. Instead, they question whether demonstrating intelligent behavior is equivalent to possessing the biological mechanisms responsible for memory, emotion, and conscious experience.
How Memory May Give Rise to Thought
Marx and Gilon emphasize that their theory does not solve the enduring mystery of consciousness. They explicitly acknowledge that the nature of conscious life remains poorly understood.
However, their proposed biochemical framework offers a different way to investigate the physical processes that may underlie mental activity. By examining interactions between brain cells and their chemical environment, the Tripartite Mechanism of Memory could provide researchers with another avenue for exploring how the mind works.
While their earlier research focused on how memories might be physically encoded within the brain, their latest work addresses a much broader problem.
Understanding how living brain tissue transforms experience into memory could eventually help explain how memories become thoughts, how conscious experiences arise, and what fundamentally distinguishes biological intelligence from artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Canadian C-band 5G is nearly twice as fast as other 5G: analysis
articles.text:
Canada’s 5G performance on C-band spectrum is improving and closing in on peer countries, according to new analysis from Opensignal showing how Canada’s 5G compares to other members of the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).
To add some context, C-band is another name for midrange 5G spectrum that typically sits around 3.7 to 4.2GHz (about 3,700 to 4,200MHz) and acts as the middle option for 5G connections. It offers more capacity and higher speeds than low-band 5G, and better range than high-band 5G, also known as mmWave.
The report noted that 5G C-band usage has nearly doubled in Canada over the last three years. Opensignal noted that there was a bit of a slow start, and it is now closer to the median across its OECD peers, at 52 per cent of 5G readings now using C-band. Alongside that, 32 per cent of of 5G readings are still on the AWS spectrum that previously made up a lot of Canadian 5G readings in 2023.
Adding to this, the OECD median for 5G C-band readings has fallen from 70 per cent to 58 per cent, with countries like Austria, Finland, and Sweden shifting to lower-band spectrum for better range and indoor coverage.
Secondly, all three major Canadian operators are seeing faster 5G speeds on C-band. Users on the C-band 5G get 2.0-2.8 times faster speeds than users not on C-band 5G. Interestingly, Rogers customers saw the biggest improvement, with its C-band users getting speeds up to 2.8 times faster than non-C-band users. However, between operators, C-band speed results differ by less than 8 Mbps, ranging from 245 Mbps to 237 Mbps.
The same results are not seen for 5G Consistent Quality, which measures how often a 5G connection is good enough to use common apps. There was either no significant change or quality increased by a mere 1.3 to 1.6 per cent across tests. Rogers was the lowest, sitting at 81.2 per cent of tests. Telus jumped up to 91 per cent, and Bell was the highest at 92.1 per cent.
Interestingly, Opensignal notes that both Canada’s 5G Download Speed and its 5G Availability remain below the OECD median, with the U.K., Japan, Italy, and Germany below it. Above the median are France, the U.S., and South Korea; the latter has almost all connections using C-band, and each operator has 100MHz of contiguous spectrum. For Canadian operators, it varies depending on the carrier, and the region, with the average being between 60 to 100 MHz.

articles.title: Lead azide detonation sends clouds over Iowa as questions of health risks swirl
articles.text:
In a powerful explosion that launched gray-white clouds over southeastern Iowa, the Army detonated 68 barrels containing 9,700 pounds (4.4 tons) of degraded lead azide on Wednesday at about 9 am CT, preventing a spontaneous unmitigated explosion of the crystallized, highly unstable compound.
The detonation occurred at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa, a town of fewer than 400 people. Residents within a 5-mile area of the facility were advised to evacuate, while people farther out were told to shelter in place, close windows and doors tightly, turn off fans, and set indoor air systems to recirculate.
Local Iowa outlet KWQC caught the plume from the two earth-covered containers, which were detonated simultaneously. A KWQZ journalist, at a reportedly safe distance from the blast, said on the live broadcast that he could see and then feel the shockwave roll through the crop field in which he was standing. He put a mask on for the rest of the broadcast.
Lead is a neurotoxin that does not break down in the environment and poses significant health risks, particularly to young children and pregnant people.
In the hours leading to the detonation, the Army released maps showing modeled drift and distribution of the plume. They indicated that airborne lead would travel around 100 miles to the southwest of the facility, while dust deposition would cover around 200 square miles in that direction. Researchers and government workers have already collected air and soil samples from the area, which will act as baseline readings for lead levels in the aftermath and fallout of the detonation.

articles.title: System76 Launches Pop!_OS 26.04 With Major UI and Usability Improvements
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
System76 Launches Pop!_OS 26.04 With Major UI and Usability Improvements
Pop!_OS, the Linux distribution shipped by default with System76's PCs, like the recently released Thelio Prime desktop, has officially been updated to version 26.04 LTS from 24.06. The new update to Pop!_OS has brought with it a host of updates, most of which are aimed at making the distribution and its Cosmic desktop significantly more feature-complete and competitive with the likes of GNOME. The update to 26.04 is largely considered to be a big step for both Pop!_OS and Cosmic, because the Cosmic desktop has been playing catch-up, but it has some highly sought-after power-user design concepts, like the configurable, user-friendly, auto-tiling window management. 
The distribution itself is now on kernel version 7.2.15, although kernel versions aren't tied to a specific version of Pop!_OS, due to its update cycle. The major usability improvements come from changes to the desktop, which, in 26.04, include: new Cosmic Image Viewer and System Monitor apps; new Constellations themes with bundled wallpapers, icons, colors, and fonts; built-in drawing tablet support; an on-screen keyboard with touch and gamepad support; support for automatic system and app updates; remote desktop support; configurable workspace wrapping; variable refresh rate support; improved gaming, especially with Steam Big Picture; improvements to touchscreen support; and individual app volume control.There are also several other accessibility improvements, including shake to find cursor; cursor size options; cursor scaling; and improvements to screen magnifications. Users can also now also define what happens when they start typing in the overview. The built-in Cosmic apps have also been updated to be significantly more customizable and feature-rich, and Pop!_OS also now supports automatic GPU selection for gaming scenarios. 
At release, Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS is running kernel version 7.2.15, Mesa 26.2.3, Wayland 1.26, and the NVIDIA driver 595.104.02, all of which are reasonably up-to-date components, so even newer hardware should have no significant compatibility issues. The full update notes are available here.
Sources:

articles.title: GTA 6 vice president of music says ‘it was the ideal opportunity to work with Justice,’ who helped bridge the classic Vice City ’80s style ‘with contemporary electronic production to create the perfect backdrop for Jason and Lucia’s story in the game’
articles.text:
GTA 6 vice president of music says working with Justice was ‘the ideal opportunity’ and helped ‘bridge’ the classic Vice City ’80s aesthetic ‘with contemporary electronic production to create the perfect backdrop for Jason and Lucia’s story in the game’
- Grand Theft Auto 6 Vice President of Music Ivan Pavlovich confirms the "inspiration" for the game's music comes from GTA Vice City
- Rockstar Games wanted to emulate the '80s aesthetic of Vice City for GTA 6
- Pavlovich says working with electronic duo Justice "was the ideal opportunity" as they "bridge the classic VC ‘80s aesthetic with contemporary electronic production" for the story
Rockstar Games has revealed the musical influences for Grand Theft Auto 6 and why it chose electronic duo Justice to score the official soundtrack.
In a series of Rockstar developer quotes sent to TechRadar Gaming, Vice President of Music Ivan Pavlovich confirmed that the "inspiration" for GTA 6's music comes from GTA Vice City, "which was firmly cemented in ‘80s Miami, and bringing that to the vast environments of modern-day Florida."
Pavlovich said locations, including downtown Vice City, Key Lento, and the Grassrivers region in the game, "allowed us a lot of room to explore what the various sounds from all around Leonida could be."
"That means pulling sounds from the quintessential Latin vibes to Miami’s rap legacy and its club scene to the more backcountry areas that require blues and country to support the soundscape, and everything in between," the developer added.
This was one of the main reasons Rockstar chose Justice to score the game's main soundtrack, as the duo has the talent to combine GTA Vice City's nostalgic style with modern musical elements that complement the game's world.
"For the score, it was the ideal opportunity to work with Justice, who bridge the classic VC ‘80s aesthetic with contemporary electronic production to create the perfect backdrop for Jason and Lucia’s story in the game," Pavlovich said.
Rockstar has also shared how it hopes players will let the game play out naturally rather than focusing on completing a checklist of tasks and "completely rewrote the vehicle simulation" for "believability" and immersion.

articles.title: Polarwirbel im Stillstand: Was bedeutet das für unseren Winter?
articles.text:
Polarwirbel im Stillstand: Was das für unseren Winter bedeutet
Vom „frühen Wintereinbruch“ über den „Eiswinter“ bis hin zur „Eis-Peitsche“: Der stratosphärische Polarwirbel sorgte für aufgeregte Medienberichte und Prognosen über den Winter in Europa. Denn hoch über dem Nordpol, in rund 30 Kilometern Höhe, ist in den vergangenen Tagen etwas bisher Beispielloses passiert. Der Polarwirbel kam kurze Zeit zum Erliegen.
Wo um diese Jahreszeit eigentlich Stürme mit zunehmender Geschwindigkeit gen Osten brausen sollten, wehte nur ein schwaches Lüftchen mit etwa zwei Metern pro Sekunde – und das auch noch in Gegenrichtung. Im langjährigen Mittel lag die Geschwindigkeit des Westwindbandes Ende Oktober, Anfang November bei etwa 29 Metern pro Sekunde, der bisherige Tiefstwert lag bei etwa 11 Metern pro Sekunde.

articles.title: DOJ accuses former cyber executive of defrauding ransomware victims by secretly paying hackers
articles.text:
The U.S. Department of Justice has indicted a former executive of a ransomware recovery firm after he allegedly defrauded victims of cyberattacks by claiming the company could get their encrypted files back.
According to federal prosecutors, Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, 52, was the chief technology officer at RansomwareHelp, which purported to offer data recovery services to victims of ransomware. The company’s website, which currently reads as “under maintenance,” claimed it could decrypt hacked data by using its proprietary technology, according to an archived copy of the site from earlier this year. RansomwareHelp touted a success rate of “over 99%.”
But the company allegedly had no technical ability to unscramble data and instead “negotiated with and paid a ransom to the ransomware actors to decrypt the victim data,” while charging the ransomware victim more and keeping the difference,” per the Justice Department’s statement.
Palacio Escobar then allegedly used the funds to buy several properties in Florida.
The DOJ said the FBI carried out an undercover operation in June, in part posing as a company that claimed it had been hit by ransomware. The company claimed to the undercover agents that it never negotiated with hackers or paid a ransom. But then Palacio Escobar paid the apparent hackers some $6,000 in cryptocurrency, without the knowledge that FBI agents were also posing as the ransomware hackers.
404 Media first reported the indictment last week against Palacio Escobar. He faces three charges of wire fraud, and could receive 20 years in prison on each count.
Palacio Escobar is the latest, albeit rare, example of cybersecurity professionals going rogue. Earlier this year, two ransomware negotiators working for cybersecurity companies were jailed on hacking and extortion charges, after being caught moonlighting with the ransomware gangs that they were ostensibly investigating. A third ransomware negotiator was also convicted of helping hackers deploy ransomware against several companies.
Last month, independent cybersecurity journalist Brian Krebs reported that FBI agents arrested a Canadian cybersecurity executive in Philadelphia on allegations that he was involved with the theft of FBI personnel records by the hacking and extortion gang ShinyHunters. The hacking group told TechCrunch that they took credit for the theft of FBI data in September, which they said they would not publicly release, a departure from its earlier extortion-based cyberattacks.
The federal charges against the Canadian cybersecurity executive relate to conspiracy to commit extortion, though much of the court docket — and his alleged links to the hacking group — remains under seal.

articles.title: 1Password sufre un hackeo. Qué ha pasado y cómo te afecta
articles.text:
1Password, uno de los gestores de contraseñas más seguros y usados del mundo, ha sufrido un hackeo. La compañía confirmó que días atrás sufrió el acceso sin autorización a sus servidores y el robo de algunos datos de los usuarios. Pese a lo malo del incidente, la buena noticia es que las bóvedas y las contraseñas guardadas no se han visto impactadas.
De acuerdo con 1Password, el actor malicioso detrás del ataque pudo copiar parte de la información perteneciente a un grupo reducido de usuarios. De momento, la empresa no ha revelado un número preciso de clientes impactados por esta situación. Lo que sí ha mencionado es que en ninguno de los casos se ha vulnerado las contraseñas o claves secretas almacenadas en el servicio.
Así las cosas, 1Password está llevando calma a quienes utilizan su plataforma para gestionar las contraseñas de sus servicios en línea. Desde la firma aseguran que no es necesario realizar cambios en las cuentas de usuarios, ni nada por el estilo. Además, tanto las apps como los sistemas de la plataforma no han dejado de funcionar en ningún momento.
Cómo se produjo el hackeo a 1Password y qué datos robaron
Según reveló 1Password, el hackeo se produjo luego de que un atacante obtuvo acceso al GitHub de la compañía tras robar las credenciales de uno de los empleados. Esto permitió acceder introducir código malicioso en los sistemas de la plataforma y exfiltrar lo que se ha catalogado como "datos administrativos" vinculados con los clientes.
Entre la información robada aparecen los nombres y las direcciones de correo electrónico de algunos usuarios, como también sus nombres de usuarios, las fechas de creación de sus cuentas y de su inicio de sesión más reciente. También se extrajeron llaves públicas, otros identificadores internos "no secretos" y tokens usados en los enlaces que se envían por e-mail para invitar a nuevos clientes o recuperar una cuenta.
Desde 1Password sostienen que las bóvedas de cada usuario, al igual que toda la información almacenada en estas, no se han visto afectadas. Tampoco hubo acceso a las claves de recuperación de cuentas y el ciberataque no impactó sobre las apps para móviles o las extensiones para navegadores.
Esto debería ser suficiente para llevar tranquilidad a los clientes de 1Password que todas sus claves y contraseñas están seguras. Sin embargo, desde la compañía advierten que los datos robados sí pueden usarse para campañas de estafas y/o suplantación de identidad. Es por ello que se recomienda prestar especial atención a correos electrónicos y otras comunicaciones que puedan causar sospechas. Desde 1Password recuerdan que sus servidores no almacenan la contraseña de tu cuenta ni tu clave secreta.

articles.title: Il fait tourner le vrai bureau de Windows XP sur Linux : la démo qui fascine les internautes
articles.text:
Décidément, l’imagination des développeurs n’a pas de limites : un projet open source, win4wine, est parvenu à remplacer l’interface de Debian 13… par celle du vénérable Windows XP.
Windows XP a beau avoir plus de 25 ans, il n’est toujours pas prêt à prendre sa retraite. Il y a un peu plus d’un mois, on apprenait que Windows 11 s’était inspiré du système pour sa barre de tâches. Un peu plus tôt cette année, un utilisateur de Reddit avait réussi à marier la célèbre colline verte de Windows XP à l’esthétique de Windows 11 pour un résultat tout simplement impressionnant. Cette fois, la nostalgie gagne aussi les amateurs d’open source.
Un développeur ressuscite explorer.exe sur Linux
Les thèmes façon Windows existent depuis bien longtemps sous Linux. Mais le développeur japonais mikuta0407 a eu une idée encore plus originale : il est parvenu à exécuter l’explorateur de fichiers de Windows XP directement dans Debian.
Comment a-t-il réussi ce tour de force ? En modifiant la version 11.0 de Wine, un logiciel Linux qui permet de faire tourner des applications Windows : 151 correctifs ont été, en tout, nécessaires. Le résultat, qui a été publié sur GitHub sous le nom de win4wine, est bluffant : on retrouve la barre des tâches du système d’antan, mais aussi son menu Démarrer et ses fenêtres.
Même les logiciels Linux se fondent dans le décor : leurs fenêtres héritent du look propre à XP, leurs icônes côtoient celles de Windows et les boutons d'agrandissement ou de réduction se comportent comme en l’an de grâce 2001. Les programmes Windows 32 et 64 bits sont également de la partie et un contributeur a même ajouté Internet Explorer 6, Windows Media Player 9 ainsi que les sons natifs du système.
Un projet expérimental qui a ses limites
On vous voit déjà venir : vous rêvez vous aussi de retrouver la fameuse colline verte sur votre écran. Sachez que la tâche est loin d’être simple et que le développeur conseille de procéder avec prudence : « (l') installation sur un système déjà en service (équipé d’un autre environnement de bureau ou d'un autre gestionnaire d’affichage, par exemple) n’a pas été testée. Il est recommandé d’utiliser une machine virtuelle ou un ordinateur de secours » peut-on notamment lire dans le fichier README.
- Système d'exploitation libre et gratuit.
- Distribution en permanente évolution.
- Convient à tous les usages.
Il vous faudra aussi une version toute neuve de Debian 13, environ 90 minutes de compilation et votre propre ISO de Windows XP Professionnel SP3 pour arriver à vos fins. À noter : seules les versions anglaises et japonaises de Windows XP ont été testées. Il n’est pas garanti qu’un XP en français puisse fonctionner.
Un autre point important : côté légal, le dépôt ne contient aucun fichier appartenant à Microsoft et ses scripts n’en téléchargent aucun. On peut notamment lire la recommandation suivante : « respectez les conditions de licence de Microsoft concernant le fichier ISO et les fichiers qui en sont extraits. »
À bon entendeur…

articles.title: Un compte GitHub a suffi : le gestionnaire de mots de passe 1Password s’est fait pirater, voici ce que vous devez savoir
articles.text:
C’est à travers le compte GitHub professionnel d’un de ses employés que 1Password a été piraté.
Le 19 novembre 2026, les équipes de l’entreprise ont repéré des signes montrant que ce compte était utilisé par quelqu’un d’autre. L’intrus s’en était servi pour copier du code source, accéder à la chaîne de déploiement et envoyer vers les serveurs de 1Password un code malveillant qui lui a permis de récupérer des informations sur certains clients.
Six jours plus tard, l’entreprise a détaillé l’incident dans un article de blog, en insistant sur un point : « les coffres des clients n’ont pas été affectés ».
Quelles données ont été volées
Selon l’entreprise, les fiches copiées contiennent les noms et adresses mail de connexion, les identifiants de compte, les dates de création et de dernière connexion, ainsi que des métadonnées techniques que 1Password juge sans danger.
Certaines de ces fiches contiennent également des jetons présents dans les liens envoyés par mail lors d’une invitation ou d’une récupération de compte. Le communiqué précise que seul un petit nombre d’utilisateurs avaient une telle procédure en cours, et que ceux-ci ont été prévenus individuellement.
Ces jetons ne permettent pas à eux seuls de prendre le contrôle d’un compte, puisqu’il faut aussi une connexion SSO ou un code envoyé par mail. Par précaution, l’entreprise a remplacé ce code à six chiffres par dix caractères alphanumériques.
Pourquoi les mots de passe restent protégés
Ni le contenu des coffres, ni les clés qui les chiffrent, ni le mot de passe principal ou la Secret Key des utilisateurs n’ont été touchés. Cette affaire remet pourtant en cause la gestion interne d’un éditeur dont tout le modèle repose sur la confiance, puisqu’un seul compte d’employé a suffi pour introduire du code malveillant en production.
1Password dit avoir depuis désactivé ce compte, changé les identifiants exposés, renforcé ses contrôles et fait appel à des experts indépendants. Selon l’entreprise, les clients n’ont rien à modifier dans leur compte.
Le risque est très certainement ailleurs, car l’attaquant sait désormais qui utilise 1Password, ce qui lui permet d’envoyer des messages crédibles au nom de l’entreprise. Il faut donc se méfier de tout mail, SMS ou appel inattendu évoquant une invitation ou une récupération de compte, et ne saisir son mot de passe ou sa Secret Key que dans l’application ou sur le site officiel.
