articles.title: SA’s Community Wolf raises seed funding round led by Terra Industries
articles.text:
South African public safety tech startup Community Wolf has opened its seed round with a strategic investment from Terra Industries, which takes the strategic lead.
Founded in 2024 by Nick Mills and Michael Houghton, Community Wolf started with a WhatsApp number that lets anyone report crime and suspicious activity for free, anonymously and in their first language.
Its AI models structure the images, video and pin drops users submit, then alert people nearby and local responders. The startup – recently a winner at the South African Startup Awards – has since added emergency assistance, family safety, community communication and operational software for security operators. It has more than 700,000 users and has recorded over 180,000 incidents.
Terra Industries, also founded in 2024, builds autonomous security systems to protect critical infrastructure such as mines, power plants and pipelines across Africa and the Global South. Its air, land and maritime systems run on ArtemisOS, its software platform for large-scale security operations. Disrupt Africa reported in August the company had raised an additional US$18 million in strategic funding to close its own seed round at US$52 million.
The investment in CommunityWolf, the amount of which is undisclosed, marks Terra’s entry into public safety, with Terra CEO Nathan Nwachuku joining Community Wolf’s board. Community Wolf will use the funding to expand into communities around critical and urban infrastructure, while the two companies will also look at linking Community Wolf’s products to Terra’s software, so verified incidents reach Terra’s command centres alongside drone and sensor data.
“The people living around critical assets like mines are the first to feel an attack, and they are often the first to see it coming,” said Nwachuku. “We believe communal security will also be pivotal in how we protect lives and secure infrastructure.”
“Community Wolf gives residents a way to report and security operators an integrated platform to manage their communication and response,” said Mills. “Alongside Terra’s autonomous ground and aerial systems, we can keep millions more people safe across the continent.”

articles.title: India, Australia deepen education ties with focus on skills and edtech
articles.text:
India, Australia deepen education ties with focus on skills and edtech
India and Australia are deepening education ties through partnerships in edtech, vocational training and higher education, with a growing emphasis on workforce development and future skills.
Australia is expanding its education relationship with India into joint training, digital learning and workforce development, as a 21-member Australian delegation visits New Delhi and Bengaluru from November 23 to 27.
Led by the Australian Trade and Investment Commission (Austrade), and supported by Investment NSW and Trade & Investment Queensland, the group is attending DIDAC India 2026 at Bengaluru’s Bangalore International Exhibition Centre from November 25 to 27.
It includes universities, vocational providers and edtech firms working across schools, employability and workforce development.
Vik Singh, Austrade’s Trade and Investment Commissioner, said the delegation would connect education more closely with economic needs.
“Through this delegation, we are placing skills development and EdTech at the centre of our collaboration, connecting institutions, industry, governments and learners to build the skills needed for future economic growth. This is about building meaningful partnerships that bring education, technology and workforce needs closer together,” Singh noted.
Eight Australian universities are operating or preparing to establish a presence in India. Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade lists five Australian university branch campuses opened since 2024, in Gujarat’s GIFT City, Bengaluru, Mumbai and Greater Noida.
Education is Australia’s largest service export to India, valued at A$9.4 billion in 2025, when more than 140,000 Indian students were studying in Australia.
India’s National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 prioritises access, equity, quality and internationalisation in higher education. University Grants Commission rules introduced in 2023 opened the way for eligible foreign universities to establish campuses.
In December 2025, the bilateral Education and Skills Council backed online and blended learning, dual qualifications and employer-aligned courses, while citing the RMIT-BITS Pilani partnership and Monash University’s teacher-training initiative in Uttar Pradesh.
In July 2026, India’s National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) and Australia’s Australian Skills Quality Authority (ASQA) signed a letter of intent on vocational-training quality assurance, with qualification benchmarking and possible recognition among areas for further exploration.
The four-year Australia-India Future Skills Initiative supports partnerships for short courses and micro-credentials, short units that certify specific skills, in digital technology, energy, healthcare and infrastructure.

articles.title: Italy and Switzerland warn of autonomous AI-driven cyberattacks
articles.text:
Swiss and Italian cybersecurity agencies are warning about automated cyberattacks powered by AI agents targeting organizations in the critical infrastructure sector.
The two agencies listed four AI-powered penetration testing and red-teaming frameworks that have been involved in recent breaches and hacking incidents: ARTEX AI, CyberStrikeAI, DeepSeek Harness - Red Team, and PentAGI.
Both agencies have urged organizations to reduce the number of systems exposed on the internet, prioritize patching, and monitor for unusual activity.
Large-scale attacks in Italy
CSIRT Italia says it detected large-scale malicious campaigns that used autonomous AI agents to identify and exploit vulnerabilities and misconfigurations on exposed endpoints.
In some cases, the agency observed multiple AI agents working in parallel to compromise a large number of systems within a few hours.
In one instance involving a DeepSeek Harness setup, a coordinator assigned tasks to five AI agents that undertook a broad spectrum of operational stages, from information gathering to exploitation and persistence.
The agents chained vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and compromised credentials, leveraging exposed systems as a foothold to reach internal networks.
“During the observed campaigns, autonomous agents demonstrated the ability to carry out complex, sustained activity to detect misconfigurations, link even low-impact vulnerabilities into complex attack chains, and dynamically adapt their operating modules,” CSIRT Italia says.
“They went as far as writing malicious code in real time to evade endpoint defenses and carry out actions deeper within the infrastructure.”
The Italian cybersecurity agency advises administrators to prioritize patching internet-facing systems, focus on addressing flaws known to be actively exploited in the wild, and disable remote management interfaces if not needed.
The agency also recommends monitoring control plane operations, authentication sources, traffic to internal networks, and outbound server traffic to detect suspicious activity.
First AI breaches in Switzerland
Switzerland’s National Cyber Security Center (NCSC) warned of similar campaigns targeting organizations in the country, confirming the first cases of successful AI-assisted cyberattacks.
“In recent days, the NCSC has received its first reports of cyberattacks against organisations in Switzerland in which the attack was carried out with the assistance of an AI agent,” the Swiss NCSC said.
“Various organisations and operators of critical infrastructure across at least two sectors have been affected by these cyberattacks.”
“In all cyberattacks known to the NCSC, the use of AI agents led to the successful compromise of the victim’s IT systems.”
The agency described rapid attacks in which agents exploited weak passwords and known vulnerabilities in exposed endpoints, using frameworks to verify weaknesses and independently decide what to do next.
NCSC says that the number of AI agents publicly (and often freely) available to cybercriminals has nearly doubled since October, resulting in these massive waves against Swiss organizations, including critical infrastructure operators.
The agency recommends that administrators of internet-facing systems patch critical vulnerabilities within 24 hours of release, add multi-factor authentication (MFA) or passkey protection, and enforce least-privilege principles.

articles.title: Top 10 Cross-Platform Mobile App Development Companies in the USA 2027
articles.text:
Each product development team working to ship its application for iOS and Android faces the same decision at an early stage – either develop two native apps with two separate teams or write once and deploy to both.
The latter is the reason behind the rise of cross-platform development as the de facto standard for most consumer and B2B applications developed in the US.
You have a single code base, unified development process, and one small team responsible for that. The point when you choose to hire React Native developers or migrate to Flutter marks the beginning of another challenge – to find a partner who will not sacrifice quality on one platform in favor of the other.
React Native is the right choice for companies that have experience writing in JavaScript and React and also want to access a vast array of library support. Flutter is a bit better if you want better control over your render and you would like a consistent interface across different devices. React Native and Flutter both compile into native mobile applications, but their main difference is that Flutter requires a lot less engineering muscle than React Native.
It requires more than a number of stars to select the right one. The candidate agency should refer to live applications on both app stores and not to prototypes, as well as to provide detailed information on how it deals with those areas where the platforms diverge – that is push notifications, in-app purchases, offline mode, and native modules. The US headquarters is needed due to time-zone compatibility and the terms of the contract, so all companies listed have their headquarters in the USA and provide an operational phone number and address on Clutch. For clients looking for Flutter development services in particular, it is recommended to hire Flutter specialists with examples of produced apps.

React Native and Flutter play a pivotal role in the mobile development strategy, as they have dedicated teams that manage the open source UI libraries that can be used for both frameworks. articles.title: Hackers norcoreanos usaron videollamadas falsas en un robo de 400 millones de dólares en criptomonedas, según el FBI
articles.text:
Hackers patrocinados por el Estado norcoreano se han llevado más de 400 millones de dólares en criptomonedas en los últimos 18 meses, y tal y como cuenta la BBC lo han hecho suplantando a los conocidos de sus víctimas en videollamadas falsas. El FBI, que ha bautizado el esquema como FaceStealer, dice haber incautado más de 900 vídeos de víctimas grabados en secreto.
Dinero para armas. Y es que ese dinero tiene destino. “El régimen norcoreano depende de lo que obtiene con robos de criptomonedas a gran escala para financiar su programa ilícito de armas, y ha robado miles de millones de dólares en los últimos años”, afirma Brett Leatherman, director de operaciones de la rama cibernética del FBI, en el comunicado del Departamento de Justicia.
El precedente de Binance. El aviso llegó nueve días después de que Binance contase, el 3 de noviembre, que hackers norcoreanos usaron una entrevista de trabajo falsa para llevarse unos 6.300 millones de dólares. Son unos 5.700 millones de euros al cambio del 12 de noviembre del Banco de España, y Reuters lo ha calificado de robo récord. Según el mismo comunicado de Justicia, el FBI atribuye ese ataque a actores vinculados a Corea del Norte, aunque Pionyang lo ha negado.
Una cara conocida. FaceStealer ataca “de forma agresiva”, en palabras de Leatherman, a quienes trabajan con criptomonedas y en el sector web3, y también a quienes desarrollan y mantienen software de código abierto. La trampa empieza con una invitación a una reunión que llega desde cuentas secuestradas a víctimas anteriores y que lleva a versiones impostoras de Zoom, Microsoft Teams o Google Meet, donde los atacantes reproducen vídeos pregrabados de gente a la que el objetivo conoce para que la llamada parezca legítima.
El arreglo que lo estropea todo. Pero el audio falla, o eso parece, y en la pantalla aparece un mensaje que invita a “arreglarlo” con un enlace. Ese arreglo es lo que instala el malware, según la misma alerta del FBI, y da a los atacantes acceso a los contactos y las aplicaciones de la víctima. Además, durante la espera de la reunión graban en secreto su webcam, y esas imágenes sirven después de cebo para engañar a sus conocidos.
“Explota nuestra confianza en unas plataformas de videoconferencia omnipresentes y en las relaciones personales que valoramos”, dijo Patrick Grandy, jefe de la oficina del FBI en Los Ángeles, en unas declaraciones recogidas por The Record el 12 de noviembre. Grandy, que define FaceStealer como “un esquema de ingeniería social muy eficaz, capaz de engañar incluso al usuario con más conocimientos técnicos y más concienciado con la seguridad”, añadió: “Si no eres capaz de imaginar un escenario en el que podrías ser víctima, no estás pensando con suficiente creatividad”.

articles.title: Pour le Black Friday 2026, ce vidéoprojecteur 4K XGIMI noté 5/5 perd 346,67 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le vidéoprojecteur XGIMI Horizon 20 "5 étoiles" à 1 290,00 € (-21%)
Actuellement noté 5/5 par notre rédaction, le vidéoprojecteur XGIMI Horizon 20 délivre une image 4K détaillée et facilite son installation grâce à son zoom optique et son pied sur balancelle. Le Black Friday 2026 fait descendre son prix à 1 290,00 € chez Amazon Marketplace, soit une baisse d'environ 21 % et 346,67 € d'économie.
Le Xgimi Horizon 20 est un vidéoprojecteur 4K tri-laser pensé pour simplifier les séances de cinéma à la maison sans sacrifier l'équipement optique. Il intègre un zoom optique, un lens shift et un pied sur balancelle pour faciliter son positionnement dans le salon. Ce modèle sous Google TV avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage sur notre banc d'essai.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le Xgimi Horizon 20 descend à 1 290,00 € chez Amazon Marketplace, soit environ 21 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (1 636,67 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 346,67 € sur ce vidéoprojecteur.
Une installation facilitée et une image 4K détaillée
Le Xgimi Horizon 20 dispose de la note maximale de 5/5 dans notre comparatif. Lors de notre test complet, l'appareil a brillé par son ergonomie d'installation. Son pied intégré sur balancelle, complété par un zoom optique et un lens shift, permet d'ajuster l'image au millimètre sans devoir déplacer physiquement le boîtier. Les automatismes se chargent de corriger le trapèze et d'assurer une mise au point nette dès le démarrage.
Sur le plan de l'affichage, ce modèle diffuse une définition de 3840 x 2160 pixels (4K) portée par une source tri-laser au pic lumineux élevé. Les contenus profitent d'une compatibilité avec les formats HDR10+ et Dolby Vision pour préserver les détails dans les scènes complexes. L'interface Google TV intégrée donne un accès direct aux services de streaming avec une navigation fluide, pilotable depuis la télécommande rétroéclairée fournie.
XGIMI Horizon 20
Points forts
- Design soigné.
- Pic lumineux élevé.
- Image 4K détaillée.
- Zoom optique et lens shift.
- Pied intégré sur balancelle.
- Correction du trapèze et mise au point automatiques efficaces.
- Google TV complet et fluide.
- Compatibilité HDR10+ et Dolby Vision.
- Input lag particulièrement faible.
- Télécommande rétroéclairée.
- Ventilation très silencieuse.
Points faibles
- Colorimétrie perfectible.
- Contraste encore limité.
- Audio correct, mais qui manque de coffre.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Quelques concessions sur la colorimétrie et le contraste
Malgré son statut de référence, le projecteur montre des limites sur la précision colorimétrique en sortie de carton et conserve un contraste limité dans les zones sombres. Sa partie audio manque également de coffre pour les pistes sonores explosives, ce qui orientera les amateurs de grand spectacle vers une barre de son dédiée. Ces compromis n'empêchent pas le vidéoprojecteur de convenir parfaitement à un salon familial recherchant une grande image sans installation complexe.
Dangbei Mars Pro 2 (DBOX02) : l'autre option face au XGIMI Horizon 20
Le Dangbei Mars Pro 2 (DBOX02) constitue une solution alternative pertinente sur le terrain des projecteurs 4K lumineux. Actuellement noté 4,5/5 par notre rédaction, il propose lui aussi un système d'exploitation complet avec les applications actuelles et un rendu vidéo très net. Il dispose d'un système sonore intégré plus efficace que celui de son rival, mais il souffre également d'un contraste perfectible.
Le Mars Pro 2 fait toutefois l'impasse sur le pied intégré sur balancelle, ce qui rend son placement moins souple que celui du Xgimi. Le Dangbei Mars Pro 2 coûte 90,05 € de moins que le XGIMI Horizon 20 au tarif du jour, mais le Horizon 20 conserve l'avantage de la note maximale et d'une installation bien plus flexible.
Dangbei Mars Pro 2 (DBOX02)
Points forts
- Qualité d’image 4K.
- Luminosité très élevée.
- Nombreux réglages disponibles.
- Compensation de mouvement très efficace.
- Interface Google TV avec Netflix.
- Connectique complète.
- Silencieux.
Points faibles
- Contraste limité.
- Retient les traces de doigts.
- Pied optionnel.
- Télécommande basique et non rétroéclairée.
- Pas vraiment dédié au gaming compétitif.

articles.title: El Black Friday es el momento perfecto para dar el salto a una tele más grande. Esta TCL Mini LED llega hasta las 98 pulgadas
articles.text:
Comprar un nuevo televisor es algo que no hacemos todos los años. Por esa misma razón, cuando llega ese momento, merece la pena pensar bien lo que vamos a adquirir, especialmente si tenemos en la cabeza dar el salto a uno con más pulgadas. Ahora que estamos en Black Friday, tenemos una muy buena oportunidad para ello, puesto que es posible encontrar modelos de gran formato a precios ajustados. Aunque eso sí: no todo es el tamaño.
TV QD-Mini LED 65" - TCL 65P8L, UHD 4K, TCL AiPQ Processor, Smart TV, DVB-T2, Dolby Vision·Atmos, 144Hz, Google TV, Negro

TCL P8L: un televisor QD-Mini LED disponible en hasta 98 pulgadas
Lo primero a destacar de esta tele TCL es que combina retroiluminación Mini LED con puntos cuánticos. Pero, ¿y qué ventajas tiene esto? En esencia, es una combinación que permite controlar mejor la iluminación de la pantalla, una gama de colores más amplia y un mejor contraste. El TCL P8L, además, incorpora el procesador AiPQ, encargado de optimizar aspectos como la nitidez o el color de lo que estamos viendo.
A esto hay que sumarle que es un televisor con una tasa de refresco nativa de 144 Hz, algo ideal para gaming y para escenas con movimientos rápidos. Además, cuenta con algunas tecnologías como el VRR, que adapta el refresco de la tele a los fotogramas que genera la consola o PC que estemos usando. De esta forma, se evita un desgarro en la imagen o el conocido como tearing.
Además de todo lo anterior, es compatible con HDR10+ y Dolby Vision e incorpora Google TV, que facilita el acceso a las principales plataformas de entretenimiento y ofrece funciones inteligentes de Google, con integración de Gemini según disponibilidad. También tiene Chromecast integrado (para mandar contenido desde el móvil, por ejemplo), funciones de control por voz y un sistema de sonido Onkyo 2.1 con subwoofer integrado en las versiones a partir de 65 pulgadas.
Tenemos la TCL A65K para completar la experiencia
Este sistema de sonido tiene lo necesario para rendir bien, pero podemos ir un pasito más allá si queremos una experiencia más envolvente. Ahí está la TCL A65K, una barra de sonido que incorpora un sistema de 3.1.2 canales físicos y que es compatible tanto con Dolby Atmos como con DTS:X.
La barra incorpora sonido Audio by Bang & Olufsen y ofrece una potencia máxima de 460 W, repartidos entre los 260 W de la barra y los 200 W del subwoofer inalámbrico, diseñado para reforzar los graves. Otro de sus puntos interesantes es TCL AI Sonic-Adaptation, una función que, a través de la aplicación TCL Home, permite analizar las características acústicas de la habitación y ajustar el sonido para ofrecer una experiencia de escucha más equilibrada.
Todo ello en un diseño ultradelgado, con una altura de aproximadamente 5,2 centímetros, que permite colocarla discretamente bajo el televisor. La tenemos disponible por 175 euros.
TCL A65K Barra de Sonido 3.1.2ch con Subwoofer Inalámbrico, Dolby Atmos | 460W de Potencia Máxima, Audio by Bang & Olufsen, DTS:X, AI Sonic-Adaptation, HDMI 2.1 eARC, Bluetooth 5.3
¿Qué tamaño de TCL P8L es el ideal para ti?
Volviendo al televisor, es muy importante elegir el tamaño correcto. Esto es algo que viene determinado por nuestro presupuesto, pero también por el espacio que tenemos disponible en casa. Por ejemplo, si nuestro salón tiene un tamaño medio, lo ideal sería adquirir un TCL P8L de 65 pulgadas, la opción más equilibrada. Ofrece una diagonal generosa, pero sin necesitar tanto espacio como sus hermanas mayores.
Si preferimos tener más pantalla, la versión de 75 pulgadas puede ser la indicada para nosotros, especialmente si tenemos una distancia de visionado aproximada de entre 2,5 y 3 metros. Si tienes un salón especialmente amplio o si directamente buscas montar un cine en casa, la versión de 98 pulgadas es entonces una opción interesante para ti. A continuación, el precio de todas ellas:

- TCL P8L de 98 pulgadas: 1.496 euros.

En definitiva, si estamos buscando este Black Friday renovar nuestro televisor, el TCL P8L es una opción que merece la pena tener en cuenta. Especialmente, si lo que estamos buscando es una tele con una diagonal generosa, puesto que MediaMarkt las tiene con un descuento bastante jugoso. Igual que ocurre con la barra de sonido TCL A65K.

articles.title: Jensen Huang talks succession, Trump, and therapy in his first all-hands meeting since returning
articles.text:
Big quote: Nvidia went 11 days without Jensen Huang as CEO, and his return hasn't changed the chipmaker's approach to succession: it still has no formal plan. At his first all-hands meeting since being reinstated, Huang told employees the company had shown it could operate without him and argued that the board should choose his successor based on what Nvidia needs when he leaves. But for a firm whose chips, deals, and investments give it influence across the AI industry, keeping the business running through a brief absence presents a different challenge than deciding who will set its next direction.
Nvidia's board accepted Huang's resignation after raising concerns about his conduct and candor, then reinstated him on Monday. Chief financial officer Colette Kress ran the company in the interim, but Huang's departure drew criticism from Wall Street over the lack of a clear internal successor. "All day long, this company can run autonomously, and you saw it," Huang told staff.
Huang pointed to the breadth of Nvidia's leadership to explain why he saw no need to designate a successor. He described his 60 direct reports as effectively running their own businesses within the company, giving directors a pool of executives to choose from rather than a single heir apparent. "The idea of succession planning is not flawed. What people think succession planning means is flawed," he said.
That approach gives the board room to decide what kind of leader it needs, but it leaves the choice open until a transition is at hand. One issue already facing Nvidia that its next CEO could inherit is the ongoing scrutiny of its compliance with US chip export controls.
Huang also addressed Washington's role in his return. He denied that senior government officials were responsible for his reinstatement and said the decision belonged to Nvidia's directors. However, it has been reported that President Donald Trump called into a board meeting to urge directors to bring Huang back. The CEO told staff he would advise Trump on policy and would do the same for a future president.
 – WallStreetBets (@wallstreetbets) November 23, 2026
Inside Nvidia, Huang acknowledged violating company policy and said managers would weigh the facts of each case, the same discretion he defended in explaining the board's decision to give him another chance. "But 'it won't be tolerated' does not mean the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door," he said.
Huang also said he was spending 90 minutes a day in therapy and acknowledged that his management style could undercut the people he relied on to run the company. "When I go too far, it hurts people, it belittles them, it disempowers them," he said. He told staff he would seek regular feedback from colleagues through a 360-degree review, a process he said he would undergo himself rather than make mandatory across Nvidia.

articles.title: Recap of Microsoft Ignite 2026: Copilot as the Work OS and Agent Governance
articles.text:
Microsoft Ignite 2026, held in San Francisco and online from November 17 to 20, centered on running AI agents in production, with Microsoft positioning Copilot as the operating system for work and extending agent identity, governance, and cost controls across Azure, Foundry, Entra, and Defender.
CEO Satya Nadella opened the keynote by acknowledging the November 12 Microsoft 365 outage, then positioned Copilot as the operating system for work, combining chat, coding, and autonomous agents in one experience. In his edited keynote remarks, Nadella argued that customers must be able to examine and independently verify what AI does, announced an AI Transparency Initiative aligned with NIST's Agent Standards Initiative, and rejected setups where models audit other models:
These nested black boxes are simply unacceptable.
The Book of News groups the announcements by product area, and many of them ship as previews rather than in general availability.
Compute and Infrastructure
Azure Cobalt 200 virtual machines are now generally available, a year after InfoQ reported on Microsoft introducing the chip at Ignite 2025 and two and a half years after the preview of Cobalt 100 VMs. According to the Azure announcement, the processor combines 132 Arm Neoverse V3 cores on TSMC's 3nm process, and the VMs run in 14 regions today, with 23 planned by the end of 2026. Microsoft claims up to 50% better CPU performance than Cobalt 100, plus up to 15% higher network bandwidth and 20% higher remote storage IOPS through Azure Boost. Customers can run cores at a fixed 3.2 GHz in Deterministic Mode or let them boost up to 3.6 GHz in Opportunistic Mode, and the lineup adds Mpsv4 VMs for high-memory workloads and storage-optimized Lpsv5 VMs. Amadeus reported more than 30% higher flight-search throughput than on Cobalt 100, and OpenAI's Vadim Filanovsky described a similar result:
We saw higher throughput and lower latency on Cobalt 200.
Confidential computing gains three previews: multi-GPU confidential computing on VR72 for models larger than a single GPU, Azure Confidential Enclaves with AKS Kata CoCo containers, and Azure Confidential Clean Room for multiparty analytics without exposing raw data.
Customers can now deploy Foundry open-weight models and agents to their own AKS clusters. At the same time, an Agent Sandbox extension provides VM-level isolation for agent-written code, and Agent Grid applies central policy to agent, model, tool, and service interactions. Flex nodes extend AKS clusters to servers outside Azure. According to the AKS team's Ignite post, managed GPU node pools, which handle GPU drivers, device plugins, and Azure Monitor metrics, are generally available, with NVIDIA GB200 and GB300 support and mixed multi-instance GPU in preview. Confidential VM node pools on Azure Container Linux are also generally available on both Intel TDX and AMD SEV-SNP VM sizes.
On the operations side, Azure Monitor health models are generally available and build a real-time health graph from telemetry, ranking incidents by business impact. The Azure Copilot deployment agent, also generally available, turns natural-language requirements into deployed workloads, and Azure SRE Agent picks up previews for customer-managed keys, Entra Agent ID integration, cross-agent communication, and multicloud investigations. For migration projects, Azure Catalyst is now generally available, with its agent (formerly the Azure Copilot migration agent) handling discovery, assessment, and planning. Separately, GitHub Copilot modernization adds a preview of BizTalk-to-Logic Apps migration.
Hybrid, Sovereign Cloud, and Windows Server
Microsoft now pitches Sovereign Private Cloud as a full stack on Azure Local, with VMs and AKS at the base, followed by data services, Foundry Local, GitHub Enterprise Local, and Microsoft 365 Local. Darryl van der Peijl, a Microsoft MVP for Azure Local, Hyper-V, and Azure Arc, listed what shipped in his Azure Local Insider newsletter: Foundry Local on Azure Local and GitHub Enterprise Local are generally available, while a Sovereign control panel, Blob Storage and DocumentDB on Azure Local, multi-tenancy, and rehoming are in preview. The control panel assesses data residency, encryption, network exposure, and business continuity for Azure resources without enforcing any controls, and during the preview it runs in European regions only, with the service hosted in Sweden.
Van der Peijl singled out rehoming, which moves an Azure Local instance from Azure management to local management while VMs, AKS clusters, and data stay in place:
Until now, going from connected to disconnected meant a migration project. Microsoft showed a script that does the rehoming in one run.
Azure Local also runs on arm64 for the first time, in public preview on the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor Development Kit, which hosts containers on bare metal without a hypervisor. Windows Server 2028 entered preview through the Windows Server Insider Program, bringing a hardened Server Core, post-quantum cryptography, native NVMe enabled by default, NVMe over Fabrics, and boot from ReFS. According to van der Peijl, Microsoft added inference as a new pillar for the release, calling on-premises inference servers token factories, and is moving network drivers from kernel mode to user mode as part of its Windows resiliency work. Windows Admin Center vMode is now generally available at no extra cost and manages up to 1,000 Hyper-V hosts and 25,000 VMs, which Microsoft described on stage as "kind of a replacement for SCVMM."
AI, Models, and Microsoft Foundry
Foundry's main theme was continuous improvement. Multi-turn evaluation and production insights that group recurring failures and rank fixes are now generally available, while the agent optimizer, human annotation, rubric evaluators, Managed Training, and Programmed Training for custom SFT and reinforcement learning loops on open-weight models are in preview. The optimizer adjusts an agent's instructions, skills, and model choice, with a human approving each change before it ships.
(Source: Microsoft blog)
In a separate engineering post, the Microsoft team behind the optimizer described how the loop works. They reported that the reflector, a separate model that reads failing traces and diagnoses why an agent scored poorly, influenced results more than switching the agent's own model, for example between gpt-4o and gpt-4.1-mini. Developers drive the loop from the Azure Developer CLI:
azd ai agent eval init                         # generate dataset & evaluator from a one-paragraph description
azd ai agent eval run                          # score the current version (baseline)
azd ai agent optimize                          # search over candidates
azd ai agent optimize apply --candidate <id>   # apply the winner locally
azd deploy                                     # ship as the next version
Writing on DEV Community, Hector Flores advised readers to treat Microsoft's claim that the model router saves up to 65% compared with a frontier model as a ceiling rather than a forecast, and he welcomed the human approval step in the optimizer loop:
Self-modifying agents with no review gate are an incident waiting to happen.
On the model front, Microsoft-Decision-1.1 is generally available in Foundry, OpenRouter, and Vercel. Built on Gemma 4 26B A4B with added image input, it scores 68 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1 and runs more than twice as fast as its predecessor, and Copilot uses it to route requests. MAI-Code-2 and MAI-Code-2-Flash are generally available on GitHub, MAI-Image-2.7 is in preview, and the model router now covers the top 50 models in a catalog of more than 11,000. OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol became generally available in Foundry, with Global Standard deployments covering 28 regions. On Standard deployments with short context, Sol costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, while Astra costs $8 and $40. Foundry IQ added knowledge graphs and an iterative retrieval model, Microsoft-Retriever-1, both in preview.
Microsoft also made Azure AI Gateway generally available as a standalone product, split out of the API Management AI tier, to govern, route, and monitor access to AI models and MCP tools across providers. It includes 10,000 free requests per gateway per month, with paid billing starting January 1, 2027, across 17 regions.
Microsoft IQ, which Nadella described as an externalization of the context system behind Copilot, is now generally available without a new SKU. It exposes Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ, and Web IQ context to Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Foundry, and MCP-compatible harnesses, and Web IQ is now available to all Azure customers at a lower price. Business plugins, which package reusable context, skills, and tools with hierarchical inheritance and governance, are available through the Frontier program.
Data
PostgreSQL got most of the attention on the data side. Azure HorizonDB is now generally available as a managed, PostgreSQL-compatible database with built-in vector indexing, and teams can lock it down with Entra ID, private endpoints, and their own encryption keys. Calling models from SQL through AI Functions and AI Pipelines is still in preview. The same holds for Fabric HorizonDB, a serverless variant inside Fabric that provisions in seconds and pauses when nobody uses it, and for a DMS path that moves existing Azure Database for PostgreSQL servers onto HorizonDB.
Teams moving off Oracle can test a new Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration in Azure DMS, also in preview. Cosmos DB developers now have a generally available Rust SDK and semantic reranker, and Cosmos DB Shell lets them query from VS Code or the portal with MCP support built in. On Azure Managed Redis, the Redis 8 preview folds JSON, search, time-series, and vector search into a single version. Anyone who wants to develop against Azure SQL Database on a laptop can pull a preview container that needs no Azure subscription.
Developer Tools
The Microsoft Copilot SDK 2.0 is generally available, built on a native Rust runtime, supported in six languages, and using the same agent harness Microsoft and GitHub run internally. The GitHub Copilot app now takes Azure DevOps repositories from clone to merge and runs tests in a real, signed-in browser. Copilot code review adds local reviews in the CLI and app, secret detection, adaptive review effort, and cross-repository context. Copilot Code, a natural-language app builder with cloud and local sandboxes, is in the Frontier program, with general availability planned for December and a macOS local sandbox still to come.
Copilot and Business Applications
The Copilot app now brings Chat, Cowork, Code, and Autopilot into one experience, and Office in Copilot puts Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside it as a generally available feature. Autopilot, a long-running personal agent with its own identity, memory, and tool access, is rolling out to Frontier customers. Salesforce in Copilot entered preview with more than 38 prebuilt sales skills, and zero-copy data federation between Salesforce Data 360 and Fabric OneLake is generally available. For spend control, Agent 365 FinOps previews cost visibility, policies, alerts, and Fabric-based chargeback.
Cost tracking also featured in practitioner reactions. In his newsletter, Microsoft principal AI apps architect Anurag Karuparti wrote that tokenomics is among the top challenges his customers raise, and he proposed a different unit for agent ROI:
The metric that matters isn't just tokens consumed. It's cost per successful business outcome. That's how I think enterprises should start measuring agent ROI.
Writing for business leaders, Aaron Reich, CTO of the Accenture and Microsoft joint venture Avanade, built his Ignite analysis around trust rather than speed:
Speed isn't the bottleneck anymore, trust is. As AI drives the cost of knowledge toward zero with apps being easier to build, agents doing more work, and abundant intelligence, the scarce things are hard and need more attention: institutional knowledge, judgment, accountability and trust.
Security, Identity, and Governance
At the Microsoft Hub, where he spent the week answering customer questions, Microsoft MVP Muhammad Atif noticed a change in what customers wanted to know:
How do we actually put this into production? How do we scale AI and agents across the organisation? How do we govern and secure them? How do we control the cost as adoption grows?
Entra now assigns Agent IDs automatically to discovered local agents, starting with GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code, and previews an MCP Firewall that controls access to MCP servers, tools, prompts, and transports. The Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise, which gives agents permission-controlled access to Entra data, is generally available. Defender's runtime protection for local AI agents on Windows is generally available to Defender for Endpoint P2 customers, while Intune previews local agent governance that marks devices with unapproved agents as noncompliant. Agent 365 now has a generally available tools registry that lists the plugins, skills, MCP servers, and connectors agents use; MCP governance is in preview through Azure AI Gateway and LiteLLM; and Dynamic Agent Risk combines runtime, posture, and blast-radius signals into risk levels for each agent. Microsoft Perception, formerly Project Perception, is now generally available, with its Triage Agent covering about 80% of alerts in a typical Defender queue.
(Source: Microsoft Tech Community, Agent 365 blog)
In her Ignite recap, cloud and identity consultant Shannon Kuehn warned against handling agents as ordinary applications:
Treat agents like apps and you'll spend 2027 cleaning up after them.
Conclusion
The complete list of announcements is available in the Microsoft Ignite 2026 Book of News, and Microsoft has made keynote and breakout session recordings available on demand on the Ignite website.

articles.title: Galaxy S27 : quatre ans après, Samsung copierait ce design iconique de l’iPhone
articles.text:
Depuis One UI 7, les Galaxy regroupent leurs activités en cours dans la Now Bar : musique, minuteur, itinéraire ou score en direct. La fonction vit sur l’écran de verrouillage et dans le coin gauche de la barre d’état, à bonne distance de la découpe de la caméra frontale. Une préversion destinée aux Galaxy S27 rebattrait ces cartes, d’une façon que les utilisateurs d’iPhone reconnaîtront au premier coup d’œil.
La pilule migrerait vers la caméra frontale
Dans cette version en fuite, les notifications en direct quitteraient la gauche de la barre d’état pour s’afficher au centre de l’écran, autour de la découpe. La Now Bar conserverait ses usages actuels, de la lecture musicale au suivi d’un itinéraire, mais occuperait la zone la plus visible de la dalle. Le geste changerait aussi : un balayage vers la gauche ou la droite ferait défiler les activités, là où la pilule actuelle se parcourt de haut en bas.
Des animations baptisées « Moment Effects » compléteraient le tableau. Elles se limiteraient au sport dans un premier temps, déclenchées quand une équipe marque ou remporte son match, avant une possible extension à d’autres applications. Les mises à jour en direct des applications tierces, ouvertes depuis One UI 8 grâce à Android 16, y gagneraient une scène autrement plus exposée.
Apple a installé une interface animée du même genre autour du poinçon de ses iPhone 14 Pro en septembre 2022, avant de l’étendre à toute la gamme sous le nom de Dynamic Island. Samsung présentait de son côté la Now Bar comme un « élément déterminant » de One UI 7 au lancement de la fonction, fin 2024.
Les Galaxy actuels y auraient droit, sans passer par un S27
Samsung a officialisé One UI 9.5 le 18 novembre, et sa première bêta circule depuis sur les Galaxy S26. La nouvelle Now Bar n’y figure pas. La bêta actuelle se concentre sur d’autres chantiers, du verrouillage natif des applications aux réglages photo retravaillés, et retire au passage les volets Audio brief et Moments du résumé quotidien Now brief. Cette mouture intermédiaire garde Android 17 pour socle et, comme One UI 8.5 avant elle, peaufine l’interface plus qu’elle ne la bouleverse.
Le calendrier supposé donne rendez-vous au début d’année 2027, quand les Galaxy S27 étrenneraient la refonte avec la version finale de One UI 9.5. Les Galaxy plus anciens suivraient ensuite, au fil d’un déploiement attendu avant la fin du deuxième trimestre. Le constructeur n’a confirmé ni le nouveau design ni sa fenêtre de sortie, et une interface aperçue si tôt peut encore changer d’ici la version finale.
Pour les propriétaires de Galaxy récents, l’affaire se jouerait donc dans une simple mise à jour, sans repasser par la caisse. Elle rapprocherait encore One UI de son rival, quatre ans après que la Dynamic Island a fait d’un trou dans l’écran une signature visuelle. Réponse au lancement des Galaxy S27.

articles.title: This Brother printer solved one of my biggest gripes with printers
articles.text:
I’ve got some major grievances with printers.
Over the years, I’ve tried a bunch of them, including multiple models from HP, Epson, and others. And I keep running into the same major headache: when I need to print something, they never work.
The central issue is that I don’t need to print often. Most of my job exists in the digital world, so it’s exceedingly rare that I need a physical copy of anything. But every once in a while, I do need to print. A shipping label here, a document there. And that’s always when my printer gives me a hard time.
See, most printers I’ve tried need you to print semi-regularly, or the ink dries up, and when you print, it’s splotchy and faded and missing parts of the document. Then I have to spend hours running calibrations and printing tests until the ink starts flowing properly again.
So when Brother reached out to me asking me to test one of its printers, I explained that exact problem. And Brother suggested I try its ‘Work Smart MFC-J1360DW Wireless Colour Inkjet‘ printer. Admittedly, I was a bit skeptical it would work, given it’s an inkjet printer and all the others that have plagued me with issues were also inkjet printers. But I figured, hey, they seem confident. Let’s see what it can do.
When the printer arrived, I set it up, calibrated it, and made sure everything was working as intended. Then I didn’t touch it for almost two months to see how it’d handle the first print job after a lengthy idle period. Much to my surprise, it printed perfectly on the first try.
Lots to love, even for infrequent printers
While that alone sold me on the Brother printer, there are plenty of other things to like about it. It’s got automatic duplexing, meaning it can handle printing on both sides of a page, borderless printing, and more.
I was also pretty impressed with the MFC-J1360DW’s printing speed and quality. Brother claims the printer takes less than seven seconds to start printing, and in my testing, that felt pretty accurate. Text quality was excellent, with everything being clear and easy to read. Image quality wasn’t quite as good, but certainly sufficient for my needs.
Beyond printing, the MFC-J1360DW boasts scanning and copying capabilities with both a letter-size flatbed glass for scans as well as a 20-sheet automatic document feeder (ADF) for loose stacks of up to legal-size paper.
In terms of controls, the MFC-J1360DW sports a 1.8-inch LCD display with physical control buttons, which you can use to access various printer settings. Additionally, the printer offers wireless and wired connectivity options. I found setting up the wireless printing was a breeze with the Android app, and once it was connected to my home internet, I could easily connect other devices like laptops, tablets, and my desktop to it for printing.
Even better, replacement ink cartridges aren’t obscenely expensive like some other brands. The MFC-J1360DW takes four cartridges: Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, and Black. Standard cartridges start at $15.99, and you can get a three-pack of the colours for $40.99.
Minor grievances
Brother’s MFC-J1360DW isn’t perfect, though my complaints are fairly minor. First, when I took it out of the box, I was disappointed to see that the packaging had slightly damaged the finish on the front. It’s not super noticeable, but there’s scuffing and wear, particularly around the control panel where the packaging rubbed against the printer.
My other complaint is that the MFC-J1360DW can be rather loud when in operation, and sometimes it makes noises for no discernible reason. On the first point, most printers are loud when printing, so it’s not that big of a deal. And with how fast it prints, it’s not loud for long.
But the seemingly random noises have given me a few jump scares now, so that has gotten on my nerves more. My best guess here is that the noises are part of a shutdown or start-up routine of some kind, and that they happen when the printer wakes up or goes to sleep, such as when it’s been idle after a print job or when it installs an over-the-air update.
Still, these minor grievances don’t outweigh the fact that this printer can seemingly handle sparse print jobs with ease. Even better, the MFC-J1360DW itself is decently priced. It costs $179.99, though at the time of writing it was on sale for $89.99 for Black Friday. While that deal ends on Nov. 26, there will likely be other sales on it during the holiday season, so watch out for those.

articles.title: Spotify quitó a Livi, la voz del DJ con IA, y usuarios de habla hispana se quejaron del cambio
articles.text:
El 10 de noviembre, Spotify anunció en su sitio oficial una ampliación de las voces de DJ, la función Premium que mezcla canciones recomendadas con comentarios de una voz sintética. Las nuevas opciones comenzaron a desplegarse ese día en los mercados donde la función está disponible.
La actualización suma siete voces en inglés, con acentos británico, estadounidense, irlandés, australiano e indio, y dos en español: Fabi y Nico, ambas identificadas como de México. La voz en inglés original, conocida como DJ X, sigue disponible, según la compañía.
En el anuncio, Spotify describe a Fabi como una voz ingeniosa, amigable y siempre un paso adelante, y a Nico como auténtico y presente. El comunicado no menciona a Livi ni explica qué ocurrió con ella.
Lo que respondió Spotify a las quejas
Según respondió a usuarios la cuenta de soporte SpotifyCares en redes sociales, Livi ya no está disponible y el DJ utiliza ahora la voz de Fabi. En otra respuesta, la cuenta explicó que la función sigue en fase beta y que la compañía seguirá desarrollándola para sumar nuevas voces en español.
Spotify no ha aclarado si Livi volverá. Tampoco explicó por qué decidió retirarla ni si la elección de voces en español cambia según el país, ya que el anuncio solo identifica a las dos nuevas como mexicanas.
Quién era Livi y cómo llegó
Spotify presentó el DJ en español el 17 de julio de 2024, en versión beta y para usuarios Premium de España y de países de Latinoamérica como Argentina, Chile, Colombia, México y Perú, entre otros. Antes, la función solo existía en inglés.
La voz de Livi se creó a partir de Olivia Quiroz Roa, entonces editora musical sénior de Spotify con base en Ciudad de México. Según la empresa, fue elegida tras un casting internacional porque los usuarios que la evaluaron la sintieron cercana, como recibir recomendaciones de una amiga.
Entonces Spotify afirmó que tenía millones de oyentes de habla hispana y que las conversaciones en redes sociales sobre el DJ en español habían crecido más de 215% en los meses previos.
Más control para quien no quiere comentarios
La actualización de noviembre incluye otra novedad: los usuarios pueden desactivar los comentarios entre canciones para que la música suene con menos interrupciones. El DJ solo interviene con mensajes breves al iniciarse o cuando el usuario toca el botón para cambiar el ambiente.
Para elegir voz, el usuario debe abrir Spotify en el teléfono, buscar DJ y tocar el menú de tres puntos, donde también se ajustan los comentarios. Spotify sostiene que el 80% de los usuarios de DJ vuelve a usarlo semana tras semana.
Las nuevas voces y los controles comenzaron a implementarse el 10 de noviembre para los usuarios Premium de los mercados donde DJ ya está disponible.
Spotify prepara para 2027 un servicio pago de remezclas con IA
Spotify planea lanzar en el primer trimestre de 2027 un servicio pago que permitirá a sus suscriptores crear remezclas de canciones con inteligencia artificial, con un posible estreno en febrero, según el Financial Times.
El complemento costaría entre USD 4 y USD 5 adicionales sobre el plan Premium y permitiría transformar el estilo de una canción o simular que un artista interpreta el tema de otro. Las regalías y reproducciones se acreditarían a los artistas originales.
La compañía ya cerró acuerdos con Universal Music Group, Merlin y Believe, pero todavía negocia con Sony Music y Warner Music. Según Music Business Worldwide, el codirector ejecutivo Gustav Söderström afirmó que Spotify podría avanzar sin el respaldo de todas las discográficas.

articles.title: IBM quantum computer solves problem classical computers can’t in just 15 minutes
articles.text:
IBM quantum computer solves problem classical computers can’t in just 15 minutes
- Date:
  November 23, 2026
- Source:
  IBM
- Summary:
  IBM and University of Chicago researchers have demonstrated that a quantum computer can complete an extraordinarily complex calculation in just 15 minutes, beyond the practical reach of leading classical computing methods. A novel error-detection technique also allows scientists to establish confidence in the accuracy of the results, overcoming a major hurdle in quantum computing.
- Share:
An IBM quantum computer has completed an extraordinarily complex computational task in just 15 minutes, while leading methods for simulating the calculation on conventional computers would require prohibitively long runtimes. Perhaps even more significantly, researchers were able to establish statistical confidence in the accuracy of the quantum computer's results, addressing one of the biggest obstacles in the field.
The achievement, led by IBM and researchers from the University of Chicago, satisfies the fundamental criteria for quantum advantage. This milestone occurs when a quantum computer performs a computational task beyond the practical capabilities of leading classical computing methods while producing results that can be trusted.
In their new paper, "Sampling hard circuits with verifiably high fidelity," the researchers demonstrated that both objectives could be achieved simultaneously using a novel design for encoded quantum circuits. The experiment represents one of the largest demonstrations of logical quantum computing to date. The researchers have also made their circuits and experimental results publicly available through the Quantum Advantage Tracker.
Solving Quantum Computing's Verification Problem
Unlike conventional computers, which process information using bits that represent either zero or one, quantum computers rely on quantum bits, or qubits. These can exist in combinations of both states and interact through a phenomenon known as quantum entanglement. These properties allow quantum computers to approach certain computational problems in fundamentally different ways.
For years, scientists have tested the capabilities of quantum computers using a benchmark called random circuit sampling (RCS). This technique involves running a series of randomly selected quantum operations and generating samples from a complex probability distribution. As the circuits grow larger and more complicated, reproducing their output with a classical computer becomes increasingly difficult.
However, this approach creates a fundamental dilemma. If a computation is too difficult for a classical computer to reproduce, how can researchers establish that the quantum computer performed it correctly?
As computational complexity increases, independently verifying the results becomes progressively more difficult and eventually impractical without making strong assumptions about how accurately the quantum hardware operates.
To overcome this problem, the IBM and University of Chicago team developed a more structured alternative to random circuit sampling. The researchers mathematically demonstrated that their approach preserves the same computational hardness criteria as conventional RCS while introducing a structure that allows errors to be detected during the computation.
"Verification remains one of the biggest challenges in firmly establishing experimental quantum advantage," said Bill Fefferman, Associate Professor at the University of Chicago. "This experiment develops techniques to better characterize the fidelity of hard quantum states under noise, increasing confidence that the quantum computer is solving a computationally hard problem."
Soumik Ghosh, PhD student in Fefferman's group at the University of Chicago, added, "Beyond strengthening experimental validation, advances in verification have the potential to unlock practical applications for the next generation of quantum computers."
70 Logical Qubits and Tenfold Lower Error Rates
One of the greatest challenges in building powerful quantum computers is their extraordinary sensitivity to errors. Quantum information can be disrupted by environmental disturbances, imperfections in hardware, and inaccuracies in the operations used to manipulate qubits. As computations become longer and more complex, these errors can accumulate and undermine the reliability of the results.
Quantum error correction addresses this weakness by encoding quantum information across multiple physical qubits to create more reliable units known as logical qubits. This approach allows certain errors to be identified and, depending on the technique, corrected or accounted for without destroying the underlying quantum information.
In one of the largest known demonstrations of quantum error correction, the researchers performed computations using 70 protected logical qubits. The experiment involved 2,415 logical two-qubit operations and 468 logical "T gates."
Quantum gates are the fundamental operations that manipulate quantum information, much like logic gates in conventional computers. Two-qubit gates allow qubits to interact, while T gates enable additional types of quantum operations needed for universal quantum computing. Together, these gate counts illustrate the considerable complexity of the experiment.
By encoding the quantum circuits, the researchers achieved effective logical error rates 10 times lower than the underlying physical error rates. This substantial reduction allowed the quantum computer to maintain remarkably high fidelity, a measure of how closely the actual quantum state matches the intended one, despite performing thousands of complex operations.
A New Era of Quantum Advantage
"We are now firmly in the quantum advantage era," said Jay Gambetta, Director of IBM Research and IBM Fellow. "We have demonstrated a quantum computation beyond the practical reach of classical computers that establishes, with statistical confidence, a lower bound on how faithfully it was executed. This milestone gives scientists, developers, and businesses a new foundation for trusting quantum computers as they scale to problems far beyond what we can achieve classically."
The researchers found that many leading classical simulation techniques would require impractically long periods to reproduce the computation. IBM's quantum computer, by comparison, accomplished the task in approximately 15 minutes.
Although the experiment was designed to demonstrate quantum advantage rather than solve an immediate real-world problem, it addresses two essential requirements for making large-scale quantum computing practical: controlling errors and establishing confidence in computational results.
By demonstrating both capabilities in a computation beyond the practical reach of leading classical methods, the researchers have taken a significant step toward a future in which quantum computers could reliably tackle scientific and industrial problems that are currently out of reach.
Story Source:
Materials provided by IBM. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Simon Martiel, Jay-U Chung, Alireza Seif, Soumik Ghosh, Ian Hincks, Abhinav Deshpande, Bill Fefferman, Jay M. Gambetta, Ali Javadi-Abhari. Sampling hard circuits with verifiably high fidelity. arXiv, 28 Jul 2026 DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2607.25941

articles.title: Galaxy Tab S12 Plus ainda é caro, mas atinge 41% OFF na Black Week
articles.text:
Galaxy Tab S12 Plus ainda é caro, mas atinge 41% OFF na Black Week
Tablet premium da Samsung, lançado em 2026, tem queda de mais de R$ 4 mil em oferta na Amazon há poucos dias da Black Friday 2026
O Galaxy Tab S12 Plus (512 GB) atingiu o menor preço desde o lançamento há pouco mais de um mês por R$ 10.499. O tablet premium da Samsung está custando R$ 6.189,08 no Pix com o cupom TABLETBLACK, disponível na vitrine.
A oferta histórica na Amazon, há poucos dias da Black Friday 2026, é uma excelente oportunidade para quem busca alto desempenho.
Esta oferta é o menor preço que já encontramos para o Galaxy Tab S12 Plus Wi-Fi 512 GB. Nas outras 1 ofertas publicadas desde novembro de 2026, o melhor foi R$ 8.449,10 (Magalu, 12/11/2026).
O dispositivo premium promete entregar o que há de melhor em termos de desempenho. De acordo com a Samsung, o chip Dimensity 9500 (3 nm) oferece otimizações de até 141% na NPU, 48% na CPU e 67% na GPU comparado ao Galaxy Tab S10+.
Isso significa que o Tab S12+ sustenta com mais facilidade recursos apoiados por IA, como resumo de e-mails, tradução de conversas e edição de imagens, além de apps exigentes. Além disso, a combinação de 12 GB de memória RAM possibilita executar tarefas simultâneas sem travamentos. O espaço interno de 512 GB ainda aceita expansão de até 2 TB.
Em relação ao painel, utiliza uma tela AMOLED Dinâmico 2X de 12,6 polegadas com taxa adaptável de até 120 Hz. A configuração possibilita experiência fluida tanto gráfica como em navegação, além de reprodução de cores intensas. Enquanto as imagens recebem resolução de 2.800 x 1.752 pixels.
O Galaxy Tab S12 Plus adota uma bateria de 10.600 mAh no qual promete até 21 horas de reprodução de vídeo, segundo a fabricante. Desse modo, o usuário deve conseguir autonomia para um dia intenso longe da tomada. Em relação a recarga, o carregamento de 45 W promete alcançar 100% em até 95 minutos.
O novo tablet sai de fábrica com o sistema Android 17 baseado na One UI 9. Entre os principais destaques, concentra agentes de inteligência artificial, como o Gemini, Bixby e Perplexty. Para quem busca escalar a produtividade, é possível dividir a tela em até três áreas para rodar apps em simultâneo. A Samsung promete até sete anos de atualizações Android e da One UI.
O Galaxy Tab S12 Plus, que inclui a caneta S Pen, está disponível por R$ 6.189,08 no Pix com o cupom TABLETBLACK na Amazon. Um preço histórico às vésperas da Black Friday 2026 que concede 41% de desconto.
Em razão da proximidade da Black Friday 2026, no dia 27 de novembro, a Amazon e outras grandes lojas do varejo já oferecem descontos especiais e preços abaixo da média praticada pelo e-commerce. O Achados reúne dia a dia as melhores oportunidades de itens de tecnologia para você pagar mais barato!
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Macarena Arnás, grafóloga, analiza la firma de Pedro Sánchez: "Es una persona con capacidad de resistencia, terquedad y mucho apego a la familia"
articles.text:
La firma de Pedro Sánchez ha acabado sobre la mesa de un programa de televisión en plena carrera hacia las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre de 2026. Ha sucedido en “La Comedia Nacional”, el programa de Héctor de Miguél en La Séptima, donde contactaron con la grafóloga Macarena Arnás para que explicara qué podría esconder la rúbrica del presidente del Gobierno, en la que dice ver desde capacidad de resistencia hasta terquedad. Es la misma que el candidato socialista deja, por ejemplo, en las cartas de propaganda electoral.
Una letra que se inclina. Arnás, que además de grafóloga es perito calígrafa y autora de un libro sobre firmas célebres, empezó destacando la inclinación de una de las letras hacia la izquierda, algo que, según ella, se puede ver a simple vista. Y es que en grafología, explicó, hay que tener en cuenta la izquierda y la derecha, y en este caso esa inclinación indicaría que Sánchez “puede tener muy buena memoria, capacidad de resistencia también por esos ángulos pronunciados y fortaleza tanto mental como física”.
Pero la misma inclinación tendría, siempre según la grafóloga, una segunda lectura, porque también apuntaría a alguien con “dificultad para olvidar el pasado y mucho apego a la familia”.
Todo en mayúsculas. La firma, según la describe el diario, se compone de una “P”, un punto y un “Sánchez”, todo en mayúsculas. Cuando le preguntaron si eso no le llamaba la atención, Arnás respondió que ese rasgo admite dos interpretaciones: “Una es que quiere dar claridad y legibilidad al escrito y otra podría ser que intenta mostrar a veces una imagen de mayor fortaleza de la que realmente posee”. En ese segundo caso, añadió, podría ser alguien que aparenta más fortaleza en la primera impresión, pero que luego tiene mayor sensibilidad, “porque hay algunas formas curvas también presentes en la firma”.
El subrayado y la P. También le preguntaron por la línea que subraya la firma y por una “P” que se parece más a una “D”. Sobre el subrayado, la grafóloga explicó que es muy habitual, ya que el apellido “está muy vinculado con la parte profesional, entonces puede indicar mayor necesidad de reconocimiento en la esfera profesional”. Y sobre esa “P” con poco “palito”, su lectura fue que “hay mayor ángulo que curva en ese caso”, lo que, en sus palabras, “sí podría indicar un exceso a veces de racionalidad y también de terquedad”.
Lo que dice la evidencia. Eso sí, todas estas interpretaciones son las de Arnás, y la grafología no ha conseguido demostrar que la letra sirva para medir la personalidad. La British Psychological Society (Sociedad Británica de Psicología) la sitúa al mismo nivel que la astrología, el más bajo de su escala de validez, según explica Maldita Ciencia. De hecho, un metaanálisis publicado en 1989 en ‘Personality and Individual Differences’ sobre su uso en la selección de personal concluyó que, con textos de contenido neutro, la validez de los grafólogos era prácticamente nula, y que psicólogos sin formación en grafología los superaban en todas las medidas. Vamos, que la evidencia no respalda que una firma revele cómo es quien la estampa.
El análisis encaja en una campaña en la que, según plantea el propio diario, además del programa electoral cuentan muchos otros recursos centrados en la figura de cada candidato, desde un gesto en un debate hasta una publicación en redes sociales, y en la que hay quien se fija en detalles que a muchos les pasan desapercibidos, como la forma de firmar.
Foto | @la_septima_tv

articles.title: A familiar Iranian hacking group has found a new way to cause chaos
articles.text:
One night in October, hackers staged one of the most unusual cyber attacks in history: cranking up the temperature in refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets across France and destroying millions of euros of food.
Hackers have targeted commercial fridges and freezers before, but never at this scale and never in the heart of Europe. The brazen attack left cyber professionals unsure as to who might have executed such a madcap operation. But French intelligence agencies found traces of Farsi and other clues in the digital trail pointing to an elite hacking unit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
The unit allegedly behind the hack, Shahid Kaveh, was already well known to Western intelligence agencies. Named after Mahmoud Kaveh, an Iranian commander who died during the 1980s Iran-Iraq war, it is one of several hacking units overseen by the Revolutionary Guards’ Cyber Electronic Command.
The group, which often goes by the online persona CyberAv3ngers, has a history of targeting critical infrastructure. In 2023 and 2024, it hacked Israeli-made industrial control devices inside water, manufacturing, and transportation systems across several US states. Operational disruption was minimal, but the attackers left a message each time: “Every equipment ‘made in Israel’ is CyberAv3ngers legal target.”
State-backed Iranian hackers have rarely targeted Europe in this way, however. October’s hacks, experts say, mark an escalation in the Islamic republic’s cyber warfare strategy and a new willingness to hit European infrastructure.
“Iran has very clearly messaged that the global economy will be disrupted as a consequence of it being shut out from the world,” said Ellie Geranmayeh of the European Council on Foreign Relations.

articles.title: Heroic Launcher 3.0 Gets Steam and Itch.io Support and UI Overhaul
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Heroic Launcher 3.0 Gets Steam and Itch.io Support and UI Overhaul
Heroic Games Launcher, the open-source game launcher and library management tool for Linux, Windows, and macOS, has officially been updated to version 3.0 in the latest beta release. The move to version 3.0 promises a number of new features and delivers a long-awaited UI overhaul, replete with support for several new themes for extensive customization. The new launcher also has a few added usability improvements, like a new backup system that can help back up logins, system settings, and game settings. 
More importantly, though, GOG has also received support for both Steam and Itch.io games, and there is a new built-in system to manage running Windows games installed via Itch and Steam via Proton and Wine. The launcher also adds Steam integration via Aurelia, an open-source headless Steam client, meaning players can lunch and run Steam games with lower overhead.There is also a new gamepad settings screen for configuring your gamepad, a new download manager, and a new "Add Game" button that has automatic EXE detection for simpler installations. Overall, the new version of Heroic Games Launcher does have a cleaner look, with its newly rounded corners and simpler layout, and the developers behind the project are seemingly aiming to streamline the program to grow its audience somewhat.It should be noted that Heroic Games Launcher 3.0 is still in beta testing, so it may be somewhat unstable. The announcement also comes with an acknowledgement that some of the known issues in V3.0 include that some Steam games, especially those with anti-cheat, will not launch. Native Linux games on Itch.io also aren't supported yet, and the new UI is still under development in Console Mode.

articles.title: Are Kindles better than Onyx, Kobo, and reMarkable ereaders? Here's how the best ereaders compare
articles.text:
Amazon Kindles vs non-Amazon ereaders: here’s how they differ, and which models I recommend this Black Friday
Get to grips with Onyx, Kobo Rakuten, reMarkable, and more
Ereaders are just as useful for working and relaxing at home as they are on holiday or while travelling. If you’ve been looking to buy one, you’ve probably been looking at Amazon’s excellent Kindle range, with Black Friday on November 27 stamped in your calendar as the day to buy.
Amazon dominates the portable ebook reader market, but it’s not a lockout reign: plenty of other brands like Onyx, Kobo, and reMarkable have growing fanbases thanks to their alternative E-Ink gadgets. And as someone who’s covered many of the best ereaders, I often recommend these alternative devices over Amazon’s Kindles.
In the Black Friday sales, you’ll see E-Ink devices of all shapes and sizes discounted, including Amazon Kindles and plenty of major rivals (we've got a dedicated Black Friday Kindle deals page, if you're interested). So it’s worth getting to the bottom of the big question: is a Kindle really the best ereader for you, or will an alternative suit you better?
Kindles
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Let’s make sure we’re on the same page, shall we? Here’s Amazon’s current Kindle range as it stands:
- There’s the base Amazon Kindle, which starts at $149.99 / £134.99 / AU$279 for the 16GB, ad-supported model.
- There’s the Kindle Paperwhite, which has a bigger screen with backlighting and a hardier body. It starts at $199.99 / £184.99 / AU$367 for the 16GB model.
- A big step up takes us to the Kindle Scribe, which is much larger and introduces a stylus, so you can use it for note-taking as well as reading. The 32GB model, the cheapest one, sells for $499.99 / £449.99 / AU$849.
- The most premium option is the Kindle Colorsoft, which, as the name suggests, has a color display (as well as the stylus). The base model is 32GB, and it sells for $629 / £569 / AU$999.
If you’ve seen mention of Signature, Aluminum or Kids versions, these are just alternative versions of the models listed above. Signature refers to a higher-storage variant, while Aluminum gets that name for the base Kindle, and Kids models are simply regular models bundled with kid-friendly software and accessories.
What makes Amazon's Kindles such a big draw?
Because of the varying definitions of what an ereader exactly is, exact ereader sales figures are impossible to find, but one thing is clear: Amazon Kindle dominates the market. It’s no insult to other models that ‘Kindle’ has become the proprietary eponym for any kind of e-book device.
So what’s the draw? To a certain extent, the popularity of a gadget becomes a self-fulfilling prophecy — Kindles will be the default ereader you consider buying — but there are a few appealing aspects to Amazon’s slate.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
One big draw is the simplistic design, carried over from Amazon Fire tablets. Kindles are the perfect size between a book and a tablet, so they’re unintrusive to carry around with you yet give you loads of reading space. They're also fairly durable and light.
The Kindle design also benefits from popularity; plenty of accessories and covers are available on the market, both from Amazon and other brands.
Another draw is Kindles' software, which Amazon has created. The user interface has been refined to give readers everything they need and nothing that they don’t; you won’t waste time playing around with different modes, navigating endless menus or trying to work out which app your books are hidden in.
Kindles are for reading, or for buying new books, with a convenient storefront and reading library (with some of the more advanced models offering some extra features).
Amazon also benefits from being one of the biggest book sellers out there. You can easily buy a book via its website and send it to your Kindle, so it’s ready to read at your leisure. That unique positioning offers ease of use that rivals can’t match.
Kindle alternatives
Kindle rivals have a few major selling points that ensure they’ll always have a space on the market.
To me, one of the most important factors is price: Amazon Kindles aren’t cheap, especially after several years of price hikes. Bear in mind, the entry-level model is roughly twice the price of the 2021 model, with each new iteration suffering from higher price tags.
Other brands have managed to undercut Kindle, so if you want a budget buy, they’re where to look. The Kobo Nia, for instance, still sells for $109.99 / £96.99 / AU$159.95, and in the US, Barnes and Noble’s Nook line offers similarly priced models that are more advanced in certain ways.
Over the last year, micro ereaders have become big, with names like the Boox Picco and Xteink X4 offering small-form e-reading gadgets for under $100 / £100 / AU$200. So the budget-minded have a range of options outside the Kindle world.
That diversity is one of the main draws of the non-Kindle ecosystem. Even if you don’t want a tiny ereader, there are options that make the normal Kindle look large, like the Boox Palma 2 Pro, which resembles a smartphone.
And while Kindles' closed user interface is a major draw for many, it can also put off people who want freedom. Options from Onyx like the Boox Go 7 offer Android, so you’re able to do far more with these devices than simply read or buy books.
Speaking personally, this is why I’d never use a Kindle. I have two ereaders, both from Boox, and the open infrastructure means I can install a range of apps and use them in different ways that’d never be feasible on a Kindle.
For note-taking, reMarkable has garnered a reputation for offering a stylus experience that’s second to none, with no other brand coming close to emulating the pencil-and-paper experience — its reMarkable Paper Pro also undercuts the Kindle Scribe by a hearty amount.
One final draw, which I’ve heard many people rave about, is buttons. Amazon used to put physical buttons on its Kindles so you could turn pages without touching the screen, but hasn’t for several years. However, some rivals do so, with the likes of the Kobo Libra Colour retaining this handy physicality.
What are the best Kindle rivals?
So, you had a particular Kindle in mind, but might be swayed by something similar? Let’s run through a few Kindle alternatives you might find interesting.
I haven’t picked these Kindle rivals based on their being better — they won’t exhibit every single one of the traits I’ve just listed above — but instead they’re similar models that will let you make an informed buying decision.
Let’s start at the bottom, with the base Amazon Kindle. In our list of the best ereaders, we rate the Kobo Clara BW as the best budget ereader, and it’s very similar to the Kindle in terms of its design. It launched for $129.99 / £119.99 / AU$239.95 back in 2024, but it’s gone down in sales, with Black Friday likely to see more discounts on it.
If you want a more premium ereader experience, instead of the Amazon Paperwhite, it becomes a little harder because most brands differentiate their products better than Amazon does. Perhaps a worthy consideration is the Onyx Boox Go 7, for $295.99 / £239.99 / AU$419.
With a stylus and note-taking apps, this isn’t just a reading device, but it still has the premium design and increased storage that you’d want for a step-up device.
As your Kindle Scribe alternative, I’m going to have to return to a smaller brand already mentioned in this article: reMarkable. It has options at a range of price points with its newest, the reMarkable Paper Pure, retailing for $399 / £359 / AU$629.
Finally, we reach Amazon’s color option, the Kindle Colorsoft. This is an interesting one to find rivals for; it’s the brand’s most expensive option, but most brands don’t put quite the same premium on color displays as Amazon does (perhaps because, judging by sales stats, color e-paper devices are way less popular than you’d imagine).
I’m assuming you want a device not just for reading things in color, but for working too, and so I’d opt for the Boox Note Air6 C (which we’ve not tested, but here’s our Note Air5 C review), which costs $579.99 / £499 / AU$919. I rely on Boox’s notepad ereaders for work (albeit a different model), and feel confident recommending them for people who want a note-taking and reading slate that offers color.
Black Friday
By now, you hopefully have an idea of which ereader model you should buy, so I feel a little bad about throwing a massive wrench in the works. But you should probably know this before you spend ages searching around in the sales.
Having covered Black Friday for almost a decade now, I can say with confidence that Amazon's discounts will be better than those offered by the likes of Onyx, Kobo and reMarkable.
There will be a range of discounts from various brands, but Amazon slashes massive amounts of money off its gadgets over Black Friday, with reductions that other brands struggle to match (we've rounded up the best of them in a dedicated Black Friday Kindle deals page).
If you have your heart set on a specific ereader, then that's more important than money. But if you've been sitting on the fence so far, perhaps this year's Black Friday discounts will make the decision for you.
