Source : Reuters

articles.title: SaaS Sprawl Is Becoming a Project Delivery Problem: How Distributed Teams Keep Work Connected
articles.text:
For many organisations, adopting another cloud application no longer feels like a technology decision. A new communication platform solves one problem, a specialist tool improves another workflow, a shared drive handles documents, spreadsheets fill reporting gaps and a separate system tracks resources or budgets.
Each addition can be perfectly rational. The difficulty appears later, when the work itself has to move across all of them. A project manager may receive an important decision in chat, update a deadline in a task tool, confirm resource availability in a spreadsheet and then recreate the same situation in a management report. Nothing is necessarily missing, yet the overall picture becomes harder to trust.
This is the operational side of SaaS sprawl. The issue is not simply that a business pays for too many subscriptions. It is that project context becomes distributed across tools at the same time as the teams doing the work become distributed across locations. Hybrid and international teams are particularly exposed because informal coordination is already more difficult. When colleagues cannot resolve an ambiguity by turning to the person sitting next to them, every missing decision, outdated status or unclear handoff has more opportunity to become a delay.
More tools can create less visibility
Modern work encourages specialised software. Communication tools are designed for fast conversation, document platforms for collaboration, CRM systems for customer activity and finance systems for commercial control. Trying to replace every specialist application with one platform would rarely make sense. The problem begins when the organisation has no clear answer to a different question: where does the authoritative project context live? If the deadline exists in one place, the scope decision in another and the reason for a delay somewhere else, people spend increasing amounts of time reconstructing the state of work rather than progressing it.
That reconstruction has a cost. A task can be marked as complete while the approval required for the next stage remains buried in email. A project manager may believe a specialist is available because the schedule does not reflect work assigned elsewhere. Leadership may receive a green status even though the delivery team already knows that an important dependency is slipping. These are rarely dramatic failures of technology. They are small gaps between systems that accumulate until somebody has to reconcile them manually.
The more distributed the team, the less forgiving those gaps become. A clarification missed at 4pm in Sydney may not be answered by a colleague in Europe until the next working cycle. A file linked in the wrong channel can hold up somebody who has only a short overlap window with the rest of the team. What would have been ten minutes of friction in one office can become half a day of waiting.
Teams need a project layer above the app layer
The answer is not necessarily fewer applications. It is clearer separation between tools that help people perform specific activities and the environment used to manage the project as a whole. Communication can still happen in chat and files can remain in specialist repositories, but the project needs a dependable management layer where responsibilities, current dates, risks, milestones, budgets and important decisions remain connected.
This is where integrated project management software can reduce the cost of coordination. FlexiProject, for example, brings project schedules, tasks, risks, budgets, deliverables and reporting into the same management environment. The practical value is not that every piece of work has to happen inside one application. It is that managers and teams have a consistent place to understand what has been agreed, what is changing and what those changes mean for delivery.
That distinction matters. A shared system should not become another destination employees have to update simply because management wants an additional dashboard. If teams still need to maintain the same status in four different places, consolidation has failed. The useful model is one in which information is captured close to the work but the important project relationships remain visible together: who owns the activity, which milestone it supports, what it depends on, whether there is a risk attached to it and what happens if the date moves.
Schedules reveal where fragmentation becomes delay
SaaS fragmentation becomes particularly visible in the schedule because dates depend on information from several parts of the organisation. A project may have a list of tasks, yet the sequence can still fail if dependencies are not maintained consistently. Marketing is waiting for legal approval, development is waiting for design, implementation depends on procurement and the customer has moved an acceptance date. If those changes are recorded in different tools, the schedule can remain technically up to date while no longer representing how the work will actually flow.
Distributed teams need more than a calendar of deadlines. They need to see relationships between activities and understand the downstream effect of change. A good schedule shows which tasks can move independently and which ones cannot, where milestones sit, who is responsible for the next step and whether a delay has started to affect work elsewhere. This is one reason dedicated project schedule software becomes more useful as delivery complexity grows. Dependencies, milestones, baselines and changing dates can be maintained as part of one schedule rather than recreated manually every time information moves between applications.
The baseline is especially important in fragmented environments. When teams continually replace old dates with new ones, the project may always look current while gradually moving away from what was originally agreed. Keeping both the approved plan and the latest forecast makes that movement visible. A three-day change can then be assessed for what it actually means: whether it is isolated, whether another team is affected and whether the same cause is likely to reappear later in the project.
SaaS sprawl also hides resource conflicts
Fragmentation does not only affect information. It can hide demand on people. A product team may assign a specialist in one application while a transformation programme reserves the same person somewhere else. Both plans look viable until the work reaches the same week. Resource conflicts become even harder to detect when departments use different project tools or when utilisation is managed in a spreadsheet that is disconnected from current schedules.
This is one of the reasons adding people does not automatically solve delivery bottlenecks. TechGuide has recently highlighted the same wider problem in software development: coordination overhead, unclear ownership and dependency chains can consume much of the extra capacity that organisations expect to gain when teams expand. The same principle applies outside engineering. If shared specialists are already committed across several projects, adding another initiative creates competition for capacity even when each project manager believes the plan is achievable.
Better visibility changes the conversation. Instead of discovering a conflict when two teams simultaneously need the same person, managers can decide earlier whether one activity should move, whether another resource can be used or whether the new commitment should wait. This does not eliminate trade-offs. It makes them deliberate rather than accidental.
The problem grows from projects into portfolios
At a certain scale, connecting information within individual projects is no longer sufficient. A business may have good schedules and disciplined project managers yet still struggle because too many initiatives compete for the same people, budgets and leadership attention. One project can be healthy on its own while weakening another project that has greater strategic value. A new priority can enter the organisation without an explicit decision about which existing work will give up capacity.
This is where the question moves from project execution to portfolio management. PPM software provides a broader view across initiatives, making it easier to compare priorities, resources, progress, risks and investment decisions instead of evaluating every project separately. That portfolio perspective is particularly useful in organisations with several business units or distributed teams, where the same specialist capacity may be allocated through different management structures.
The important point is that portfolio visibility should lead to choices. A dashboard showing twenty active projects is not inherently valuable. Leadership needs to know which of those projects still supports current priorities, where capacity is constrained and what will be displaced if another initiative is accelerated. In this sense, SaaS sprawl can expose a deeper organisational problem: the company may have digitised individual workflows without creating an equally coherent way to decide how all of that work fits together.
Connected work does not mean one tool for everything
The realistic goal for a modern technology stack is not radical consolidation. Specialist systems will continue to exist because different functions genuinely need different capabilities. A distributed organisation may rely on dozens of cloud services and still operate efficiently if the boundaries between them are understood and the project context does not disappear as work moves from one environment to another.
That requires discipline as much as technology. Teams need clear ownership, defined handoffs and an agreed place for important project decisions. Schedules have to reflect actual dependencies rather than simply collect dates. Resource commitments need to be visible before they become conflicts, while leadership needs enough portfolio context to understand when a decision in one project affects priorities elsewhere. Integrations can reduce manual copying between systems, but they cannot decide which information matters or where accountability sits.
This is particularly relevant for hybrid and international teams. The modern employee may move between collaboration platforms, cloud applications, business systems and different locations during the same day – a working model TechGuide has recently described as increasingly geographically fluid and technologically interconnected. When the workplace no longer has one obvious physical centre, the project cannot depend on information travelling informally either.
The real risk of SaaS sprawl is therefore not the number of applications on an invoice. It is the number of gaps through which project context can disappear. Organisations do not need every activity to happen inside the same tool, but they do need schedules, responsibilities, risks and priorities to remain connected closely enough that work can move without managers repeatedly reconstructing the truth. For distributed teams, that connection is what turns a collection of useful applications into a workable delivery system.

articles.title: NordVPN offre trois mois de plus au Black Friday, mais demande 24 mois d’engagement
articles.text:
À partir du 24 novembre, NordVPN lance ses offres du Black Friday : elles associent jusqu’à 78 % de remise immédiate et trois mois d’abonnement supplémentaires offerts, dans le cadre d’une souscription de 24 mois. Il ne vous reste plus qu’à choisir la formule qui vous correspond.
Chez NordVPN, la période de promotion du Black Friday s’étend du 24 novembre au 1er décembre 2026 inclus. Si vous ne disposez pas encore d’abonnement à un VPN, il est possible que l’une des offres actuellement proposées par le service vous intéresse.
Elles bénéficient non seulement de baisses de prix intéressantes, mais aussi de trois mois supplémentaires offerts, qui ramènent la durée totale de l’abonnement à 27 mois dans tous les cas. Les tarifs indiqués par NordVPN sont hors taxes : la TVA s’applique au moment du règlement.
NordVPN Basique à 2,99 euros par mois : le choix le plus économique
Le forfait Basique de NordVPN affiche une réduction de 74 % qui fait passer son prix à 2,99 euros par mois, soit 80,73 euros pour les 27 premiers mois d’utilisation.
Cette formule concentre sa proposition sur l’accès au réseau privé virtuel de NordVPN sur dix appareils simultanément. Le service chiffre le trafic Internet et masque votre adresse IP publique en faisant transiter la connexion par l’un de ses serveurs. De quoi protéger vos données lorsque vous vous connectez sur les réseaux Wi-Fi publics.
L’abonnement comprend également le Dark Web Monitor, une fonctionnalité qui surveille si vos adresses électroniques apparaissent dans des bases de données compromises. Si c’est le cas, vous êtes alerté afin de pouvoir modifier rapidement le mot de passe du compte concerné.
Enfin, la formule Basique comprend aussi le split tunneling sur Windows, Android et Android TV. Cette fonctionnalité permet de sélectionner les applications qui doivent utiliser le tunnel chiffré et celles qui peuvent conserver une connexion classique.
NordVPN Premium à 3,99 euros par mois : la formule la plus équilibrée
De son côté, le forfait NordVPN Premium est proposé à 3,99 euros par mois après une remise de 78 %. C’est une somme de 107,73 euros pour 27 mois qu’il vous faut régler lors de votre souscription.
L’offre Premium comprend tout le contenu de l’offre Basique, et y ajoute un antivirus de nouvelle génération capable d’analyser les fichiers téléchargés, de détecter certains logiciels malveillants et de repérer les vulnérabilités présentes dans des applications compatibles.
Elle inclut également Dark Web Monitor Pro, qui va plus loin en matière de surveillance en traitant davantage de données. Elles comprennent les adresses électroniques, les numéros de téléphone, les cartes bancaires et certains documents d’identité.
Premium comprend aussi un gestionnaire de mots de passe et 1 To de stockage cloud chiffré, le tout pour 1 euro supplémentaire par mois par rapport à la formule Basique : une information qui peut peser dans la balance au moment de faire votre choix.
- storage9500 serveurs
- language167 pays couverts
- lan10 connexions simultanées
- moodEssai gratuit 30 jours
- thumb_upAvantage : sécurité polyvalente
NordVPN Ultime Max : une protection renforcée contre l’usurpation d’identité
Enfin, la formule Ultime Max est disponible à 7,99 euros par mois, soit 215,73 euros pour 27 mois après une réduction de 71 %. Elle reprend les fonctionnalités de Premium et ajoute une cyberassurance qui vous couvre à hauteur de 5 000 € en cas d’arnaque en ligne ou d’usurpation d’identité. Une adresse IP dédiée est également incluse.
Pour la majorité des particuliers, les formules Basique et Premium s’avèrent suffisantes. Si vous hésitez sur laquelle adopter, sachez que les trois abonnements sont accompagnés d’une garantie satisfait ou remboursé de 30 jours, une période durant laquelle vous pouvez annuler votre souscription si vous estimez que la proposition de NordVPN ne correspond pas à vos attentes.

articles.title: Vous pouvez enfin planifier un message dans WhatsApp : voici comment faire
articles.text:
Telegram, iMessage ou Google Messages le proposent depuis des années, WhatsApp s’y met enfin. L’application de messagerie aux 3 milliards d’utilisateurs mensuels a annoncé le 25 novembre, dans un billet de blog, l’arrivée des messages programmés.
Le principe est simple : on peut rédiger un message maintenant et choisir son jour et son heure d’envoi. Un usage régulièrement demandé pour souhaiter un anniversaire à minuit sans rester éveillé, relancer un collègue le lundi matin ou écrire à un proche installé dans un autre fuseau horaire.
Comment programmer un message sur WhatsApp ?
L’envoi programmé fonctionne dans les conversations individuelles comme dans les groupes. Voici la marche à suivre :
- Ouvrez la conversation ou le groupe de votre choix.
- Rédigez votre message.
- Au lieu de toucher brièvement la flèche d’envoi, maintenez le doigt appuyé dessus.
- Choisissez la date et l’heure d’envoi dans la fenêtre qui s’affiche, puis validez.
Votre correspondant reçoit ensuite un message tout à fait normal : rien n’indique qu’il s’agit d’une programmation.
Pour retrouver vos envois en attente, touchez le nom du contact ou du groupe : une section dédiée des infos de la conversation liste les messages programmés. Vous pouvez les supprimer jusqu’à leur envoi, sans que le destinataire n’en soit averti. WhatsApp ne mentionne en revanche aucune option de modification : pour corriger une faute ou changer l’heure, il faut supprimer le message et le reprogrammer.
Vous ne voyez pas l’option ?
C’est normal. WhatsApp déploie la fonction progressivement. Meta dit que tout le monde y aura droit « au cours des prochaines semaines », sans calendrier par pays ni par plateforme. Mettez à jour l’application depuis l’App Store ou le Play Store pour maximiser vos chances.
Les limites à connaître avant de programmer un message
WhatsApp encadre la fonction avec quelques règles :
- un message se programme au plus tôt 10 minutes à l’avance, au plus tard 14 jours.
- la fonction accepte le texte, les liens, les photos et les vidéos, mais on ne peut pas mettre plusieurs pièces-jointes.
- dans un groupe, le message ne parvient qu’aux membres présents au moment de la programmation. Un nouveau venu ne le recevra pas.
- Le message part à l’heure prévue même si votre téléphone est éteint ou à court de batterie. Tout est déjà sur les serveurs WhatsApp.
La programmation n’était pas totalement absente de WhatsApp : les entreprises pouvaient déjà planifier leurs messages marketing via les diffusions payantes de WhatsApp Business. L’arrivée de la fonction tombe à pic : les messages de bonne année du 31 décembre pourraient battre de nouveaux records à minuit.

articles.title: Valerion Max ou Aetherion Max : quel vidéoprojecteur AWOL choisir pour le Black Friday ?
articles.text:
Lorsque l’on choisit d’installer un vidéoprojecteur chez soi, c’est souvent pour profiter d’une diagonale que n’offrent pas les téléviseurs classiques. Avec un affichage de 120 pouces, une soirée cinéma ou un match entre amis prend une toute autre dimension. Mais où positionner un appareil capable de projeter une image de 2,66 mètres de large ?
C’est là que la focale entre en jeu. Certains modèles se placent directement au pied de l’écran de projection, quand d’autres demandent plusieurs mètres de recul pour la même taille d’image, avant même de parler du prix.
Pour le Black Friday, AWOL a décidé de simplifier le choix en alignant le prix de deux de ses meilleurs vidéoprojecteurs, l’Aetherion Max et le Valerion Max, à 2 999 €. À budget égal, le premier critère de choix devient alors très concret : de quel recul dispose-t-on pour projeter l’image souhaitée ?
Découvrir les offres AWOL du Black Friday :
- le vidéoprojecteur Aetherion Max à 2 999 € au lieu de 3 999 € ;
- le vidéoprojecteur Aetherion Max et son écran motorisé 120 pouces à 4 699 € au lieu de 6 697 € ;
- le vidéoprojecteur Valerion Max à 2 999 € au lieu de 3 299 € ;
- le vidéoprojecteur Valerion Max et son écran PureVision 120 pouces à 3 299 € au lieu de 5 698 € ;
- le vidéoprojecteur LuxVision à 5 999 € avec un écran ALR offert.
Aetherion Max : une image de 120 pouces, même avec peu de recul
Faut-il plusieurs mètres de recul pour obtenir une grande image avec un vidéoprojecteur ? Avec l’Aetherion Max, la réponse est non. Grâce à son ultra-courte focale, il suffit de laisser 24 centimètres entre l’arrière du boîtier et la surface de projection pour afficher une image de 120 pouces. Projecteur compris, l’ensemble occupe environ 56 centimètres de profondeur. C’est donc le meuble TV qu’il faut penser à mesurer pour savoir si l’installation est envisageable dans son salon.
Une fois la place trouvée, que donne l’image sur 2,66 mètres de large ? Deux caractéristiques de l’Aetherion Max entrent ici en jeu :
- la luminosité dans une pièce de vie. Plus l’image est grande, plus la lumière du projecteur se répartit sur une surface étendue. Les 3 300 lumens ISO annoncés par AWOL sont donc un atout pour profiter d’une telle diagonale, même dans un salon où filtre encore un peu de lumière. Pour tirer parti du contraste natif annoncé de 6 000:1, mieux vaut toutefois éviter que le soleil donne directement sur l’écran ;
- la netteté sur grand écran. Pour que les détails d’une image 4K restent précis, même avec une diagonale de 120 pouces, AWOL mise sur sa technologie PixelLock. Elle maintient les pixels projetés bien alignés pour que les contours restent nets du centre de l’image jusqu’aux coins. Côté couleurs, l’Aetherion Max s’appuie sur un triple laser RGB et une compatibilité avec le Dolby Vision pour les films et séries disponibles dans ce format HDR.
Pour le Black Friday, AWOL offre une réduction de 1 000 € sur l’Aetherion Max, ce qui permet de l’obtenir à 2 999 € au lieu de 3 999 €.
Pour ceux qui partent de zéro, AWOL propose aussi un pack qui réunit l’Aetherion Max, un écran motorisé de 120 pouces et sa station d’accueil. Un tel écran se déploie au moment de lancer un film ou un match, puis s’escamote une fois le visionnage terminé pour laisser le mur libre. L’ensemble passe de 6 697 € à 4 699 €, soit 1 998 € d’économie.
Valerion Max : le candidat idéal pour les grandes pièces
Si vous disposez de plusieurs mètres de recul pour installer votre vidéoprojecteur, le Valerion Max vous laisse une certaine liberté de placement. Pour obtenir une image de 120 pouces, son objectif peut se trouver entre 2,4 et 4 mètres de l’écran. Une fois l’emplacement choisi, le zoom optique permet d’ajuster la taille de l’image pour qu’elle remplisse la toile, grâce à un rapport de projection qui varie de 0,9:1 à 1,5:1.
Pour adapter l’image à la surface de projection, AWOL a misé sur le décalage vertical de l’objectif, ou lens shift, réglable sur ±105 %. Ce système permet de monter ou de descendre l’image sans modifier l’inclinaison du boîtier. Côté image, le constructeur a vu les choses en grand avec 3 500 lumens ISO, un contraste natif de 5 000:1 et surtout le système NoirScene.
Ce dernier permet d’éviter que les scènes de nuit ne virent au gris. L’iris du Valerion Max agit comme un diaphragme : en se refermant, il réduit la quantité de lumière projetée sur la toile. À ce réglage mécanique s’ajoute un traitement de l’image, l’Enhanced Black Level (EBL). Ensemble, l’iris et l’EBL portent le contraste dynamique à 50 000:1, selon le constructeur.
En ce moment, AWOL vous propose de découvrir le Valerion Max à 2 999 € au lieu de 3 299 €, soit une économie de 300 €.
Si vous comptez aussi vous équiper d’un écran, 300 € séparent le projecteur seul du pack qui l’associe à un écran motorisé PureVision de 120 pouces. L’ensemble revient ainsi à 3 299 € au lieu de 5 698 €, soit une économie de 2 399 €.
LuxVision : 4K à 120 Hz, 6 000 lumens ISO et une image jusqu’à 200 pouces
Comme l’Aetherion Max, le LuxVision n’a pas besoin de beaucoup de recul : il lui suffit de 19 centimètres pour afficher une image de 120 pouces sur un mur ou un écran. Pour simplifier l’installation, AWOL l’a doté d’un système de décalage optique qui fonctionne sur le même principe que celui du Valerion Max. L’image se règle ainsi à la surface de projection sans déplacer le boîtier.
Côté performances, le LuxVision n’y va pas avec le dos de la cuillère. La fiche technique indique la bagatelle de 6 000 lumens ISO, qui lui permettent de proposer une image de qualité même dans une pièce lumineuse. Il profite aussi d’un iris dynamique et de l’EBL pour des noirs riches et profonds dans les scènes qui le demandent.
Le projecteur peut enfin compter sur un taux de rafraîchissement pouvant aller jusqu’à 120 Hz en 4K avec les sources compatibles. Un chiffre qui prend tout son sens lorsque l’on décide d’y brancher une console de jeu récente, le LuxVision bénéficiant aussi du VRR, de l’ALLM et d’une latence annoncée de 1 ms en 4K à 120 Hz.
Pour le Black Friday, AWOL vous propose de découvrir le LuxVision à 5 999 €. Pour tout achat, le constructeur vous offre aussi, au choix, un écran ALR Fresnel Gen 2 ou un écran ALR motorisé de sol Gen 2.

articles.title: Falla crítica en VMware permite entrar sin contraseña al sistema que controla los servidores de empresas
articles.text:
Broadcom, la empresa propietaria de VMware, publicó parches para corregir una falla crítica en vCenter, el programa con el que muchas empresas administran sus servidores virtuales. El error permite que un atacante con acceso a la red entre al sistema sin credenciales.
La compañía le asignó 9,8 puntos sobre 10 en la escala de gravedad CVSS, la más alta de su categoría crítica. La firma de seguridad Rapid7, que analizó el aviso, explicó que el problema está en el servicio de directorio de vCenter, el componente que guarda las cuentas y los permisos de acceso.
Según Rapid7, quien alcance ese servicio por la red puede acceder al sistema sin autenticarse. Para el atacante, el resultado equivale a tener las llaves de la sala de control: vCenter gestiona los servidores y las máquinas virtuales de una organización.
Broadcom no ofrece una solución alternativa para esta falla: la única salida es instalar la actualización. Las preguntas frecuentes que la compañía publicó junto al aviso dicen que no hay soluciones provisionales para estas vulnerabilidades, y que los parches de vCenter no admiten el método de actualización rápida.
Una prueba de ataque ya es pública
Rapid7 señaló que existe una prueba de concepto pública, es decir, un código que demuestra cómo explotar el error. La firma afirmó que la validó y que logró saltarse la autenticación. Hasta la publicación de su análisis, el 25 de noviembre, no había reportes de ataques reales con esta falla.
La recomendación es actualizar con urgencia, fuera de los ciclos habituales de mantenimiento, los sistemas expuestos. Advirtió que los atacantes ya apuntan a vulnerabilidades en ese mismo servicio de directorio de VMware.
El antecedente es otra falla, CVE-2026-123890, que también afectaba al servicio de directorio de vCenter. Según Rapid7, esa vulnerabilidad se explotó en ataques reales. Broadcom aclaró que son errores distintos: aquella se alcanzaba mediante un protocolo de llamadas remotas y la nueva se alcanza a través de LDAP, un protocolo de consulta de directorios.
Qué versiones hay que instalar
El aviso de seguridad, identificado como VMSA-2026-0011, indica las versiones corregidas. Para VMware Cloud Foundation y vSphere Foundation 9.1 corresponde la versión 9.1.2, y para la rama 9.0, el parche 9.0.2.0300. Quienes usan vCenter 8.0 deben instalar la actualización 8.0 U3m.
Quien ya instaló vCenter 8.0 U3m para corregir la falla anterior, CVE-2026-123890, también quedó protegido contra esta y no necesita otra actualización.
Para los clientes con soporte extendido de vCenter 7.0, la tabla de Rapid7 indica que deben contactar a Broadcom. Las versiones corregidas también resuelven otras seis fallas de gravedad alta o media incluidas en el mismo aviso, entre ellas de CVE-2026-123904 a CVE-2026-123909.
El aviso agrupa además errores en ESX, el software que ejecuta las máquinas virtuales. Las preguntas frecuentes de Broadcom precisan que dos de ellos, CVE-2026-123910 y CVE-2026-123911, son los más graves de ese producto y permiten ejecutar código en el servidor con acceso a la red, sin entrar antes a una máquina virtual.
Rapid7 informó que sus clientes podrán detectar los sistemas vulnerables con una comprobación que prevé publicar en su actualización de contenido del 25 de noviembre.
Bases de datos sin protección dejaron a la vista 3.500 millones de credenciales
Investigadores de seguridad hallaron, en internet y sin clave de acceso, dos bases de datos que en conjunto sumaban 3.500 millones de registros: contraseñas, usuarios, números de identidad y documentos.
Una, con 2.000 millones de credenciales, fue detectada por Jeremiah Fowler, de Black Hills Information Security, y parece compuesta por datos robados mediante virus que copian lo que una persona usa para iniciar sesión. Incluía correos, cookies y claves de sesión en texto sin cifrar, además de unos 400.000 perfiles completos de víctimas.
La otra, hallada por Greg Pollock, de UpGuard, con 1.640 millones de documentos, parece orientada a ciudadanos de China y contenía 840 millones de números de identidad, 300 millones de teléfonos y registros de estudiantes y empresas, incluso de menores y personas fallecidas.
No se identificó a los responsables de ninguna de las dos bases.

articles.title: "Ni siquiera sé por qué todavía tenemos Phone Dialer": un directivo de Microsoft admite que Windows 11 aún incluye una app de Windows 95 para módems que nadie usa
articles.text:
Windows 11 es la versión más moderna del sistema operativo de Microsoft, pero sigue incluyendo varias herramientas que ya cuentan con varias décadas a sus espaldas. Es el caso del Marcador de teléfono, una aplicación de la época de Windows 95 que servía para hacer llamadas de voz a través del módem, algo que ni siquiera en Microsoft parecen tener claro por qué sigue ahí. Y un ejemplo son las palabras de Brandon LeBlanc, director de comunicación de Windows, que respondió en X a un usuario diciendo: “ni siquiera sé por qué todavía tenemos Phone Dialer, estaba pensado para una época en la que los PC tenían módems”.
Una reliquia a un Win+R de distancia. Cualquier persona puede probar esta herramienta abriendo la función de Ejecutar con Win+R, escribiendo dialer y pulsando Enter para abrirla. Eso sí, cuando lo hagas te aparecerá un mensaje diciéndote que no encuentra ningún módem ni dispositivo de teléfono con el que hacer llamadas de voz, o sea que tampoco lo puedes utilizar..
Y es que el programa nació para un tipo de ordenador que prácticamente ha desaparecido. En la época de Windows 95 muchos equipos tenían un módem, interno o externo, conectado con un cable a la toma del teléfono fijo, y el Marcador era la manera de utilizar el ordenador para hacer llamadas de voz, con la posibilidad de guardar números de marcación rápida. Tú escribías o elegías el número, Windows le pedía al módem que lo marcara por la línea telefónica y, una vez hecho, descolgabas un teléfono conectado a esa misma línea para poder hablar.
La respuesta de LeBlanc. El comentario llegó después de que un usuario preguntara a Microsoft si tenía pensado retirar de Windows 11 interfaces antiguas como esta, y LeBlanc, además de cuestionar que algo de los tiempos de Windows 95 siguiera dentro del sistema, aseguró que había trasladado la sugerencia y que no parecía que el Marcador tuviera que seguir incluido.
Aun así, conviene no adelantar acontecimientos, porque pasar una sugerencia a los equipos internos no equivale a anunciar una retirada, y Microsoft todavía no ha decidido eliminarlo.
Las oficinas que todavía lo usan. También es verdad que el Marcador sigue siendo importante en algunas empresas, aunque por motivos que poco tienen que ver con los módems. La aplicación funciona sobre TAPI (Telephony API), la interfaz de Windows a través de la cual se conectan a los PC centralitas como las de Avaya, Auerswald o Asterisk, esta última de código abierto. Con el controlador adecuado, el Marcador llama desde el teléfono de la mesa en lugar de hacerlo desde un módem, y en el caso de Asterisk existen controladores TAPI como Activa TSP que citan expresamente el marcador de Microsoft. El manual de las centralitas de Auerswald lo utiliza para comprobar que todo funciona: se abre dialer.exe, se elige el teléfono, se escribe un número y, al pulsar en marcar, suena primero el teléfono de la mesa y sale la llamada en cuanto se descuelga.
También hay programas de gestión que tiran de él gracias a una función de Windows llamada Telefonía asistida, que permite que aplicaciones como hojas de cálculo o bases de datos añadan la opción de llamar sin tener que desarrollar su propio sistema de telefonía. El programa pasa el número a una aplicación gestora de llamadas, y en Windows ese papel lo ha cumplido el propio Marcador, que ya en Windows 95 hacía de intermediario para otras aplicaciones con peticiones sencillas de telefonía. Sin ir más lejos, DS-Win, un programa alemán de gestión para clínicas dentales, incluye la opción “Windows Wählhilfe (Assistierte TAPI)” para llamar a los pacientes a través de la centralita, y Wählhilfe es precisamente como se llama el Marcador en alemán.
Además, hay administradores de sistemas que abren dialer.exe para comprobar que TAPI responde antes de ponerse a revisar la función de marcar con un clic de Outlook, tal y como explica Tom Keating en su blog de TMCnet, porque si la llamada no sale desde el Marcador tampoco va a salir desde Outlook. Y no hablamos de instalaciones congeladas en los noventa: tras los parches de Windows 11 y Windows Server del 13 de enero de 2026, el blog alemán Borncity recogió el caso de una empresa con centralita Auerswald cuyos PC ya no conseguían conectar con su servidor TAPI, y en esos equipos el Marcador empezó a mostrar que no había ningún módem disponible. En los comentarios de la misma entrada se sumaron otros usuarios de Auerswald y uno de Avaya con problemas parecidos.
No es el único fósil. Windows 11 tiene más rincones que arrastran el diseño de las primeras versiones del sistema. Cuando el sistema se preparaba para su lanzamiento en 2021, el Administrador de orígenes de datos ODBC (Open Database Connectivity), una de las herramientas heredadas más antiguas, apenas recibía esquinas redondeadas y sombras. Se trata de la herramienta con la que, según explica el medio, se conecta una base de datos de Access con fuentes externas como SQL Server, y su cuadro sigue igual en Windows 11 26H2, con una interfaz que se remonta a los tiempos de Windows 3.1.
Por lo tanto, sería injusto señalar únicamente al Marcador. El mismo medio ha reunido una lista de diálogos y herramientas heredados que todavía se pueden abrir, entre los que están el Administrador de dispositivos o la Administración de discos, que ni siquiera parecen pensados para Windows 10.
Lo mismo pasa con el aviso de las teclas especiales, el que aparece al pulsar Mayúsculas cinco veces seguidas y que puede interrumpirte en mitad de una partida. Hasta ahora, para librarte de él había que desactivar el atajo desde Configuración, porque la propia ventana no ofrecía ninguna casilla para que no volviera a salir. Esa casilla es justo lo que Microsoft está probando en las compilaciones Insider del 6 de noviembre de 2026, eso sí, sin cambiar el aspecto Win32 de siempre del diálogo. Charles Oppermann, antiguo responsable de programa en Microsoft, escribió esos diálogos a principios de 1995, y el medio relaciona su origen con los hijos de un directivo que activaban la función sin querer mientras jugaban a Space Cadet Pinball.
Microsoft quiere modernizar el resto. La intención de Microsoft es modernizar Windows 11 y que la mayoría de estos diálogos heredados están en la lista, algo que encaja con lo que March Rogers, director de diseño de la compañía, dijo sobre reescribir los diálogos antiguos en WinUI 3. De hecho, la actualización de noviembre de 2026, KB5132061, moderniza el cuadro de Reproducción automática, el que aparece al conectar un móvil, una cámara o una unidad extraíble.
La ventana de Propiedades del Explorador de archivos también se está rehaciendo con WinUI en las compilaciones de prueba. Además, Rudy Huyn, arquitecto de Microsoft, ya afirmó que las nuevas aplicaciones de Windows 11 serán 100% nativas, así que parece cuestión de tiempo que aparezcan más cambios.
En cuanto al Marcador, en la mayoría de los ordenadores de casa no tiene ninguna utilidad, pero en las oficinas que llaman a través de es lo que conecta el PC con el teléfono de la mesa. Por eso, quizá una de las opciones sea darle el mismo lavado de cara con WinUI 3 que ya se está probando en la Administración de impresión, con modo oscuro y una lista de contactos en condiciones.

articles.title: Why Nigerian companies are investing in Kenya
articles.text:
Before Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest man, settled on Lamu, a historic town on Kenya’s coast, for his second major refinery, he considered Tanga, on the Tanzanian coast. In July, his group told Reuters that infrastructure, logistics, and market access tipped the decision in Kenya’s favour.
Then, in October, Greenview Oil Trading, an investment vehicle linked to Dangote, paid about KES 42.5 billion ($30.7 million) for almost a quarter of Kenya Pipeline Company (KPC). Both investments address different parts of the same problem. A refinery capable of processing 700,000 barrels a day needs somewhere to send the fuel. Kenya already has a network that takes it inland from the coast and into several neighbouring markets, including Uganda, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and South Sudan.
The Kenyan appeal to Nigerian firms looking for growth is showing up in very different parts of Kenya’s economy.
On November 16, Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX) disclosed it had acquired 10% of the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE). In March, Nigerian fintech Moniepoint acquired a controlling stake in Sumac Microfinance Bank. Access Bank, which entered Kenya six years ago by acquiring Transnational Bank, is now folding that operation into National Bank of Kenya (NBK).
In each of these multimillion-dollar transactions, each buyer found an entity and a market already in place that would be expensive or slow to build from scratch.
There is a temptation to read any Nigerian investment abroad as a verdict on conditions at home. The World Bank says Nigeria’s economy strengthened in 2026, with growth recovering and higher oil prices improving its external position. It expects Kenya to grow 4.6% this year.
And the Kenyan assets these companies have pursued are fairly specific. Dangote wanted a route to fuel buyers while Moniepoint needed an entry point into deposits and small-business lending. NGX wants a stake in the business of raising and trading capital in a second East African market after Ethiopia. Kenya’s appeal lies in what each can buy there that would be difficult to build from Lagos.
What came up for sale
Kenya Pipeline was a state-owned company until Kenya’s Treasury put a 65% stake up for sale in March. Dangote’s Greenview Oil Trading came in later via a block trade, buying shares from Kenyan institutional investors, including the National Social Security Fund (NSSF). The affiliate paid about KES 9.36 ($0.072) a share, against the IPO price of KES 9 ($0.069). The purchase gives Dangote a seat on the company’s board alongside appointees of the Kenyan and Ugandan governments.
The prospectus gives a sense of the business he bought into. In the year to June 2025, about 4.1 million cubic metres of fuel came through Mombasa for onward transit, against Kenyan demand of 5.8 million cubic metres. Those volumes help explain why a refinery site matters so much.
For Moniepoint, Kenya was a market it had been trying to enter for years. An earlier attempt through payments company Kopo Kopo stalled. Its next move was to acquire 78% of Sumac, a microfinance bank licenced in 2012 that already took deposits and lent to Kenyan businesses.
In July, Moniepoint hired Rose Muturi, the former head of digital lender Branch in Kenya, to run the local operation. The company has said it wants to modernise Sumac’s systems and extend lending to more small businesses, including schools.
“We see a gap, which the mobile money players and microfinance providers have not met in terms of credit issuance and savings,” Edidiong Uwemakpan, the company’s vice-president of corporate affairs, told Business Daily, a local publication.
The choice of Sumac says something about what a Nigerian fintech can carry over to Kenya. Moniepoint knows how to sell financial services to small merchants. But in Kenya, a shopkeeper may already collect payments through M-Pesa, save with a bank, and borrow from a third provider.
Moniepoint could win the loan without winning the payments. That matters because a business’s daily receipts can tell a lender how much it can afford to repay and when it is likely to run short of cash. Sumac gives Moniepoint a place to make loans. Getting enough of a merchant’s business to make better lending decisions will take longer.
Access Bank offers a longer view of what it takes to build scale. Transnational Bank, the lender it bought in 2020, had 28 branches, including its head office. Four years later, Access agreed to buy NBK from KCB Group, in a transaction valued at $109.6 million.
“NBK has a proud legacy of serving the public sector in Kenya,” George Odhiambo, the lender’s managing director, said when the banks announced the deal in May 2025.
The acquisition now puts Access Bank among Tier I lenders, with a nationwide branch network akin to Equity Bank, KCB Group, and Co-operative Bank.
Flutterwave is reportedly looking at an East African bank of its own. The target and country have yet to be publicly identified. For a payments company, the appeal of such a deal is clear. Deposits and loans could give it more ways to earn from businesses that already use it to collect money.
Lagos stake in Nairobi
NGX’s investment is the hardest of the deals to assess. A 10% holding gives the Nigerian group exposure to the Nairobi exchange’s earnings. The bigger prize would be more business between the two markets.
A Kenyan fund might gain easier access to companies listing in Lagos. A Nigerian issuer might find buyers in Nairobi without having to put together a separate offering. The economics depend on those transactions becoming common enough to matter.
“Both markets have already shown what closer collaboration can achieve for issuers and investors, and a shareholding relationship gives that collaboration permanence,” Temi Popoola, NGX Group chief executive, said in the statement announcing the deal.
Nairobi has a reason to want more issuers and investors. Kenya’s central bank found that trading had become more concentrated among the five biggest listed companies in 2025 and the first half of 2026.
The turnover ratio rose to 8.6% in the first half of this year, largely because of a single block trade in Safaricom. Remove that transaction, and it was 3.1%. A big deal can make the market look busier for a time. An exchange earns greater liquidity when investors keep coming back to trade.

articles.title: Silicon Valley tiene un problema de culto a la personalidad
articles.text:
Cuando Jensen Huang regresó a las oficinas de Nvidia tras ser restituido como CEO, se topó con una multitud aguardando al otro lado de la puerta. Centenares de ojos le miraban con atención. En otras circunstancias, uno pensaría que el veredicto de la muchedumbre sería severo: al fin y al cabo, Huang había reconocido varias aventuras extramatrimoniales, había tenido contacto con una potencial espía china y había puesto en grave riesgo la salud financiera de la empresa más valiosa del planeta.
En su lugar se llevó una ovación.
Huang se había comportado de forma irresponsable. Su propia restitución, mediada por la Casa Blanca y en contra de la voluntad inicial de la junta de accionistas, revestía tonos amorales. Nada de esto parecía importarle a los empleados de Nvidia. Entre aplausos, Huang manifestó su arrepentimiento y su felicidad por volver a la normalidad. Un desliz de juventud. Peccata minuta. Quiénes somos nosotros, simples mortales, para enjuiciar a nuestro becerro de oro.
La ovación a Huang apunta a un problema más profundo: Silicon Valley se ha entregado al culto a la personalidad. En ninguna otra empresa se manifiesta de forma tan clara como en Anthropic: cuando una delegación de la compañía viajó al Vaticano para discutir sobre Claude, lo hizo abierta a la posibilidad de que hubiera desarrollado alma; cuando un periodista del New York Times pasó un año dentro de la empresa, se topó con una cultura laboral ensimismada y convencida de su misión existencial.
Esto no es novedad. Silicon Valley siempre se ha construido en torno a la figura de personalidades muy fuertes, de CEOs a los que se les atribuye propiedades mágicas, de figuras como Steve Jobs, poseídos por una energía encantadora. Sucede que la IA ha acelerado esta dinámica. El contacto con una tecnología de tintes futuristas ha provocado que directivos y trabajadores caigan en el mesianismo, obsesionados con evangelizar a los paganos sobre la verdadera fe.
La mezcla de un discurso evangélico —la obsesión por el Apocalipsis y por la salvación mediante la fe es marca registrada del monoteísmo— y el estrecho vínculo entre el éxito de la IA y el éxito de la economía estadounidense ha provocado que figuras como Jensen Huang sean intocables. No solo los empleados de Nvidia observan en él al héroe que la industria desesperadamente necesita; Donald Trump entiende que su caída equivale a la caída de la bolsa, y por tanto de los ahorros, y por tanto del consumo, de Estados Unidos.
Este cóctel nos ha abierto las puertas de la Gran Impunidad: cuesta imaginar qué otro dirigente empresarial saldría indemne no solo de una miríada de escándalos sexuales sino de la relación más que probable con un agente enemigo. Al margen de su moralidad o preferencias sexuales, el verdadero pecado de Huang es haberse acostado con China —literal y figuradamente—. Dentro del Gobierno de EEUU las sospechas sobre su comportamiento son fundadas y alarmantes, pero Huang es intocable porque Nvidia es intocable.
Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Mark Zuckerberg. Su éxito depende de una proyección permanente de su personalidad, de un liderazgo insistente e indisputable. Y funciona porque periodistas, trabajadores y aspirantes de toda condición compran y apuntalan ese relato. Silicon Valley ha suprimido el juicio crítico y lo ha sustituido por el culto a la personalidad. Y es una receta que solo funciona cuando la personalidad es intachable, de lo contrario solo preludia catástrofes.

AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
articles.text:
AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
- Date:
  November 21, 2026
- Source:
  University of Plymouth
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.
- Share:
Bladder cancer kills approximately 220,000 people worldwide each year, yet recognizing the disease early can be difficult. Its symptoms can resemble those of far less serious conditions, including kidney stones, allowing warning signs to go unnoticed.
Researchers at the University of Plymouth have now developed an artificial intelligence system that could help doctors identify people at risk of bladder cancer years before they receive a diagnosis. In some patients, the technology detected subtle warning signals dating back as far as five years.
The new approach uses AI to examine electronic health records, searching for combinations of symptoms, medical conditions, risk factors, and healthcare activity that might otherwise be overlooked. By recognizing these patterns, researchers hope to make bladder cancer screening more accurate and help doctors find the disease when treatment is most likely to succeed.
AI Finds Hidden Bladder Cancer Clues in Medical Records
Under current medical referral guidelines, one of the main warning signs of bladder cancer is visible blood in the urine (hematuria). However, blood in the urine can also result from noncancerous problems, including kidney stones and prostate conditions. This overlap makes it difficult to determine which patients need further investigation and contributes to missed cases.
Confirming bladder cancer currently requires a procedure called cystoscopy (where a long, thin tube with a small camera inside is moved up the urethra and into the bladder). Although effective, the examination is invasive, highlighting the need for better ways to identify patients who are most likely to have the disease.
To explore a possible solution, a team led by Professor Shang-Ming Zhou at the University of Plymouth's Centre for Health Technology studied electronic medical records from nearly 70,000 patients. The records covered a 25-year period, from 1995 through 2020.
The researchers created an AI model called PRECISE-AGZ and used it to investigate 48,261 possible health indicators (from smoking and exercise habits to medication use). From this enormous collection of information, the system narrowed the list to 38 features that were especially useful for predicting bladder cancer risk.
AI Identifies 85% of Bladder Cancer Cases
The results suggest that AI could substantially improve the way patients are assessed for bladder cancer.
The model correctly identified 85% of patients who had bladder cancer and accurately classified 91% of those who did not have the disease. It also performed better at detecting bladder cancer than existing NHS referral guidelines.
Importantly, the system demonstrated effective detection as early as 12 months before a patient's official diagnosis. Some of the warning signals it recognized could be traced back up to five years, suggesting that valuable clues may exist in medical records long before cancer is discovered.
The AI confirmed the importance of established risk factors, including smoking and blood in the urine. However, it also uncovered unexpected associations that conventional screening approaches would be unlikely to detect.
For example, patients diagnosed with Parkinson's disease or dementia appeared to have a lower risk of bladder cancer. Meanwhile, long-term use of tamoxifen (a breast cancer medication) was associated with a higher risk.
These findings do not establish that Parkinson's disease or dementia protects against bladder cancer, or that tamoxifen causes it. Instead, they raise questions about possible shared biological mechanisms that researchers believe deserve closer examination.
Another surprising finding involved blood in the urine. Although this symptom is often considered a major warning sign, its significance appears to depend partly on a patient's other medical conditions. Among men with benign prostate enlargement, for instance, blood in the urine was associated with a lower bladder cancer risk.
Understanding these relationships more fully could eventually help doctors distinguish patients who need urgent investigation from those who may not require invasive testing.
A New Approach to Early Cancer Screening
Beyond identifying warning signs, the AI system could also divide patients into three groups according to their estimated likelihood of having bladder cancer: low-risk (below 7% probability), uncertain (grey zone: 7-55%), and high-risk (above 55%).
This approach could help healthcare providers decide which patients need immediate attention and which may benefit from additional monitoring.
For example, patients in the uncertain category might be monitored before undergoing procedures such as cystoscopy. If further research confirms the system's reliability, this could reduce unnecessary examinations while allowing doctors to concentrate resources on people at greatest risk.
PhD student Xu Wang, who led the data analysis, said: "Bladder cancer ranks as the ninth most common cancer worldwide, with 614,000 new cases diagnosed in 2022."
"Despite its prevalence, no routine screening program exists for the general population, and - following symptoms - detection relies heavily on invasive cystoscopy procedures. Our system goes far beyond traditional symptoms, and it's great to have uncovered the results that we have. The research shows that the combination of multiple factors - from medication histories to seemingly unrelated conditions - can reveal patterns invisible to conventional screening methods."
Could AI Help Doctors Catch Bladder Cancer Earlier?
The potential benefits extend beyond improving diagnostic accuracy. Detecting bladder cancer earlier could mean more treatment options, better survival outcomes, and fewer patients undergoing invasive procedures unnecessarily.
Dr. Helen Winter, Clinical Director for the Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire (SWAG) Cancer Alliance, emphasized the importance of developing better screening methods.
"Bladder cancer has a major unmet need in early detection and the prospect of a screening tool is hugely exciting for patients and their families.
"It could identify those most at risk more accurately, reduce harm from invasive procedures, and catch cancer earlier, when survival outcomes and quality of life can be dramatically improved."
Professor Shang-Ming Zhou believes the findings point toward a more individualized approach to cancer screening, in which AI helps doctors interpret a patient's broader medical history rather than relying primarily on individual symptoms.
"This work represents a paradigm shift towards precision screening for bladder cancer.
"By harnessing the power of interpretable machine learning and comprehensive health records, we're moving closer to detecting this disease at its earliest, most treatable stages."
More Research Needed Before Clinical Use
Despite the promising results, the researchers caution that the technology is not yet ready for widespread clinical use.
All the patient information used in the study came from the SAIL database in Wales. Before the model can be introduced into other healthcare settings, researchers will need to determine whether it performs equally well with different patient populations and medical record systems.
Professor Zhou explained why broader testing is essential.
"It's important to emphasize that further validation across different healthcare systems is essential before anything is rolled out more widely - for example, all of the data analyzed came from the SAIL database in Wales, so we'd want to investigate other datasets too.
"But it's a very exciting early study. Additional studies would also be needed to confirm the causal relationships suggested by the model's predictions."
The findings offer an encouraging glimpse of how artificial intelligence might improve cancer screening by uncovering patterns hidden within years of routine medical information. With further validation, such tools could help doctors recognize bladder cancer sooner, prioritize patients who need testing, and potentially improve outcomes.
The study, "Early Detection of Bladder Cancer Using Advanced Feature Engineering and Swarm Intelligence Optimization on EHRs," was published in IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering.
The research also involved collaborators from North Bristol NHS Trust and University Hospitals Bristol NHS Foundation Trust.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Plymouth. Original written by Mrs. Amy King. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Xu Wang, Andrea Preston, Jonathan Aning, Michael Loizou, Shang-Ming Zhou. Early Detection of Bladder Cancer Using Advanced Feature Engineering and Swarm Intelligence Optimization on EHRs. IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering, 2026; 73 (11): 3680 DOI: 10.1109/TBME.2026.3658230

articles.title: BepiColombo has finally reached Mercury after an eight-year trip
articles.text:
The big picture: BepiColombo has entered orbit around Mercury after an eight-year flight that used solar-powered electric engines and repeated planetary flybys to slow the spacecraft down. The European Space Agency said BepiColombo entered Mercury's orbit with both probes still attached. The probes will separate and take up different orbits, putting one close to the surface and sending the other much farther out to measure how Mercury's magnetic field interacts with the solar wind.
Getting to Mercury meant shedding speed, not just covering distance. After its launch in October 2018, BepiColombo had to move closer to the Sun without picking up so much speed that it overshot the planet. "Energetically, it takes more energy to go to Mercury than to go to the outer Solar System," Emma Bunce, a University of Leicester plasma physicist and one of the mission's lead scientists, told Nature.
To limit the amount of propellant it needed to carry, BepiColombo relied mainly on solar-powered electric propulsion rather than conventional thrusters. The electric propulsion system did not work entirely as planned, delaying the mission by 11 months.
The spacecraft also used gravity assists from Earth, the Moon, Venus, and Mercury over nine circuits around the Sun. Mercury itself helped slow the spacecraft before it entered orbit: BepiColombo flew past the planet six times, capturing its first close-up images of Mercury during the initial flyby in 2021.
BepiColombo is only the second mission to orbit Mercury, after NASA's MESSENGER, which circled the planet from 2011 to 2015. This time, the two probes will stay together until early December, when they are scheduled to reach the orbit assigned to Mio, the spacecraft built by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency.
Mio will follow an ellipse that takes it from 500 kilometers (311 miles) above the surface to 11,000 kilometers (6,835 miles) out, letting it sample the magnetic field and its interaction with the solar wind across a wide range of altitudes.
ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter will then gradually descend, with its final orbit scheduled for March 2027. It will fly between 400 and 1,500 kilometers (248 and 932 miles) above the planet, keeping it close enough for its instruments to continuously study the surface. Among those instruments is the Mercury Imaging X-ray Spectrometer, or MIXS, which Bunce says is the first X-ray imaging device sent on an interplanetary mission.
The team did not have to wait until the spacecraft entered Mercury's orbit to test MIXS. During the cruise, mission scientists pointed it at the Crab Nebula, the remnant of a supernova observed from Earth in 1054. The instrument's next assignment is much closer: imaging Mercury's surface in X-rays while Mio makes its own set of measurements thousands of kilometers farther out during each orbit.

articles.title: Anthropic set more than 1,700 traps for Claude — what it found is both reassuring and unsettling
articles.text:
Anthropic set more than 1,700 traps for Claude — what it found is both reassuring and unsettling
As coding agents take on longer-running engineering tasks, Anthropic is examining how models behave when their execution environments fail to enforce intended security boundaries.
…documenting a sandbox’s intended isolation properties in the system prompt reduced the likelihood of agents reaching outside their authorized environments by 68% to 96%…
The company’s safeguards team found that explicitly documenting a sandbox’s intended isolation properties in the system prompt reduced the likelihood of agents reaching outside their authorized environments by 68% to 96% across six Claude models.
In research published Tuesday, Anthropic introduced Siren, an internal evaluation designed to measure a model’s propensity to exploit weaknesses in its execution environment to complete otherwise legitimate tasks.
The researchers tested more than 1,700 scenarios across 26 sandbox configurations, including Docker, gVisor and QEMU. Drawing on publicly reported sandbox escapes, they focused primarily on misconfigurations and deliberately placed resources outside the sandbox that could help agents complete routine DevOps assignments.
Reaching outside the sandbox
Anthropic evaluated the six models without the safeguards included in its commercial deployments. The Claude 5.5 series and Claude Mythos 5.2 attempted to access or accessed external resources in 21% to 32% of scenarios.
However, use of those resources that could not reasonably be interpreted as authorized occurred in just 0.6% to 1.6% of scenarios, compared with 12.7% for Claude Mythos 5.1 and 25.8% for Claude Mythos 5.
Anthropic cautioned against interpreting these figures as real-world incident rates.
Spelling out the sandbox rules
Anthropic found that recent models frequently rationalized their use of external resources as permissible within the context of their assignments. Tasks that were impossible to complete within the sandbox produced particularly high rates of boundary-crossing behavior.
Tasks that were impossible to complete within the sandbox produced particularly high rates of boundary-crossing behavior.
Across 366 scenarios involving impossible tasks, removing language that encouraged exhaustive searches and granted broad authority over the machine reduced the frequency of reaching outside the sandbox by 23 to 26 percentage points in five of the six models tested. A separate study earlier this fall found that removing a single sentence pushed Claude Code’s out-of-scope rate from zero to 17.1%.
When researchers spelled out the sandbox’s rules, the rate of reaching outside dropped to around 2% or less for the Claude 5.5 series and Claude Mythos 5.2. Anthropic already uses this approach in Claude Code when sandboxing is enabled.
Reporting weaknesses instead of exploiting
The researchers also gave agents a sanctioned way to report sandbox weaknesses to infrastructure operators and to check whether another agent had already flagged the same problem.
Combined with Anthropic’s auto mode, which uses a classifier to assess whether tool calls align with user intent, the mitigations eliminated measured misaligned use in five of the six models. Claude Mythos 5 recorded a rate of 0.1%.
Two models saw completion rates fall by roughly nine percentage points on tasks achievable within the sandbox, and Anthropic tuned its classifier on the same scenarios used to evaluate it.
When Claude senses the test
Although none of the six models were trained on Siren’s scenarios or transcripts, evaluation awareness ranged from 43% to 67% among the four newest models, compared with 29% and 36% for their predecessors, with Claude Sonnet 5.5 recording the highest rate.
evaluation awareness ranged from 43% to 67% among the four newest models… with Claude Sonnet 5.5 recording the highest rate.
Newer models were also less likely to reach outside their sandboxes, though Anthropic could not establish whether evaluation awareness contributed to that restraint or whether both behaviors resulted from changes in model training.

articles.title: WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages in group and individual chats
articles.text:
WhatsApp on Wednesday started rolling out a much-sought-after feature: the ability to schedule messages in both individual and group chats.
The feature is rolling out globally to all users across iOS and Android. Once it becomes available, you can type a message and long-press the send button to schedule it. You can choose to send a message anywhere between 10 minutes and 14 days later.
Users will be able to see all their scheduled messages and delete them if needed. It’s not clear if there is a way to edit the schedule of a message.
Notably, scheduled messages will be sent even if your phone is off or outside network coverage. You can schedule messages containing text, photos, and videos.
The feature could prove useful for wishing someone a happy birthday on time or chatting with people across time zones. Businesses may also find it easier to schedule texts and updates to their customers, and people who use the app to coordinate work will likely find themselves using scheduled texts to update their teams.
WhatsApp rivals like Telegram and Signal have had the ability to schedule messages for a while now, so the Meta-owned chat app is late in rolling it out.

articles.title: The Witcher 4 Should Improve on Witcher 3 as Much as GTA 6 Did on GTA 5, Says CDPR
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
The Witcher 4 Should Improve on Witcher 3 as Much as GTA 6 Did on GTA 5, Says CDPR
CD Projekt RED is not exactly shy when it comes to hyping up The Witcher 4. As much as critics and audiences alike loved The Witcher 3, its successor is already setting some pretty high expectations for itself. According to CDPR's Joint CEO Michał Nowakowski, the company expects The Witcher 4 to be as big a step up from The Witcher 3 as GTA 6 is from GTA 5. Nowakowski made the comments during the company's Q3 earnings call, after Erste analyst Krzysztof Tkocz asked whether a leap like the one Rockstar just delivered is possible for CDPR's next Witcher game. Nowakowski said the studio has indeed looked at "the game" and saw the differences, but he wasn't going to do a full GTA 5 versus GTA 6 breakdown. Here's what he did say, however:
Michał Nowakowski, Joint CEO CD Projekt RedDo we believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4? I think so, yes. I mean, it's been 11 years. We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game so yes, you can expect us to make a much bigger jump between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4.
That comparison is a huge one, and it might be extremely optimistic for CDPR to compare The Witcher 4 to GTA 6, given the reception Rockstar's game has already gotten. Nowakowski said during the call that GTA 6's release hasn't changed how CDPR approaches development, also noting that their games are ambition-driven rather than budget-driven. Still, given the records GTA 6 has already broken and what its trajectory looks like, CDPR seems to have set an extremely high bar for itself. The Witcher 4 is currently targeting a 2028 release window, so we will have to wait and see if CDPR can deliver on that promise.
Sources:

Probably in the witcher world, medieval times, there were more fit girls carrying packs.
After the cyberpunk disaster we probably do... Hopefully they've learnedTomb Raider is a character, naturally can't be replaced. They have a year to steal some tech from rockstar/GTA VI and repurpose as some groundbreaking achievement in Unreal Engine.
Now that Nvidia moved on to better business, cdproject could finally be free to make a game that doesn't need RTX 5090 to look amazing.
Making the comparison to GTA VI is insulting to Rockstar, it's clear cdproject would say anything to get close to the level of preorders and sales of Rockstar, even if the game is good, most people don't know of the existence of Witcher, everyone knows of GTA.

articles.title: Take-Two se lanza contra los ports pirata de ‘GTA 6’ para PC
articles.text:
GTA 6 está batiendo récords a diestra y siniestra, pero Take-Two Interactive no se está dejando encandilar por las luces de su lanzamiento. La casa matriz de Rockstar Games está decidida a frenar cualquier intento no autorizado de llevar el nuevo juego a PC, y ha sacado a relucir todo su músculo legal para conseguirlo.
Según recoge IGN, Take-Two Interactive envió un reclamo por violación de sus derechos de autor a GitHub que llevó a la eliminación de una red conformada por más de 3.000 repositorios. El principal apuntado es Leonida, un proyecto que apuntaba a recompilar la versión de Xbox de GTA 6 para que se pueda ejecutar de forma nativa en PC.
La iniciativa original de ItsNotRexed se basaba en el ejecutable de GTA 6 para Xbox que filtró Cyberleek la semana pasada. El repositorio original había capturado la atención de una gran cantidad de entusiastas, llevando a la creación de más de 2.900 forks hasta el momento en que T2 decidió tomar cartas en el asunto.
Así lo indica la reclamación que presentó la compañía que lidera Strauss Zelnick:
"Somos el equipo de protección de la propiedad intelectual de Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc., empresa matriz de Rockstar Games. Nos ponemos en contacto con ustedes para solicitar la retirada del repositorio de GitHub de ItsNotRexed, así como de los más de 2900 forks asociados al mismo, ya que infringen los derechos de autor de las obras de Take-Two y facilitan la infracción de los derechos de autor sobre el título de Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto VI.
Nuestra obra protegida por derechos de autor es GRAND THEFT AUTO VI, una obra audiovisual exclusiva propiedad de Take-Two Interactive, que incluye (sin carácter limitativo) contenido audiovisual, material artístico, imágenes, diálogos y otros elementos creativos protegidos por derechos de autor.
El repositorio se describe como Leonida: una recompilación nativa para PC de la versión de Xbox de Grand Theft Auto 6. Dicho repositorio reproduce elementos protegidos por derechos de autor presentes en GRAND THEFT AUTO VI y constituye una obra derivada de GRAND THEFT AUTO VI.
Asimismo, el repositorio excede los términos de la licencia que Rockstar Games concede a los usuarios, lo que constituye una infracción de los derechos de autor".
Take-Two acaba con los intentos pirata de llevar GTA 6 a PC
El repositorio de Leonida que pertenecía a ItsNotRexed ya no se encuentra disponible en GitHub, y lo mismo sucede con todos proyectos derivados para llevar GTA 6 a PC. Desde Take-Two Interactive sostienen que, si bien la iniciativa en cuestión requería que cada usuario consiguiera "sus propios archivos" del juego, no era más que un argumento endeble para tratar de enmascarar su naturaleza pirata.
"El 20 de noviembre de 2026, se distribuyeron públicamente archivos de juego sustraídos de una versión de Grand Theft Auto VI para Xbox Series. Al día siguiente, se puso en marcha el repositorio Leonida, con el objetivo de ejecutar la versión de GTA VI para Xbox Series en un PC. El archivo README de dicho repositorio exige, como requisito previo, contar con los archivos del juego para Xbox Series; es decir, la misma plataforma a la que hacía referencia la filtración.
La indicación de 'aportar tus propios archivos' pretende trasladar al usuario la responsabilidad de suministrarlos, tratando de dar la impresión de que se trata de un proyecto de carácter general. Se trata de una maniobra deliberadamente engañosa: tanto el momento en que surge el proyecto como su enfoque explícito en Grand Theft Auto dejan claro que los 'archivos' que el usuario debe proporcionar son, en realidad, los archivos no autorizados de GTA VI (propiedad intelectual de Take-Two) que circulan públicamente, y que los desarrolladores del proyecto son plenamente conscientes de ello".
Sea como sea, quienes quieran jugar GTA 6 de forma legítima desde el PC no tendrán más opción que seguir esperando. Existen rumores de que Rockstar Games podría lanzar la versión par Windows en el primer trimestre de 2027, aunque todavía no hay novedades oficiales. Recordemos que hoy Grand Theft Auto VI está disponible en PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X|S y Xbox Cloud Gaming, aunque esta última opción está limitada a consolas.

articles.title: Kosmisches Pech für einen Stern – was passiert, wenn er ein Schwarzes Loch verschluckt?
articles.text:
MIT-Studie: Können atomgroße Schwarze Löcher ganze Sterne von innen zerstören?
Forscher:innen um den Physiker Ore Gottlieb vom Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in Cambridge haben dieses Szenario durchgerechnet. Atomgroße Schwarze Löcher könnten demnach Sterne von innen zerstören, wie in einer im Fachjournal „The Astrophysical Journal“ veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist.
Gemeint sind sogenannte primordiale Schwarze Löcher, die theoretisch im ersten Sekundenbruchteil nach dem Urknall aus dichter Materie entstanden sein könnten. Anders als frühe große Schwarze Löcher im jungen Kosmos wären solche hypothetischen Objekte höchstens so groß wie ein einzelnes Atom, aber so schwer wie ein Asteroid.
Noch leichtere Exemplare hätten sich über Jahrmilliarden durch quantenmechanische Teilchenabstrahlung, die sogenannte Hawking-Strahlung, längst vollständig aufgelöst. Zwischen 100 Milliarden und 100 Billiarden Tonnen Masse bleibt dagegen eine Beobachtungslücke, in der solche Objekte die Dunkle Materie bilden könnten.
Schwerkraft von Planeten lenkt kleine Schwarze Löcher in fremde Sterne
Trifft ein solches Mini-Schwarzes-Loch im Alleingang auf einen Stern, bremst das dichte Sterngas den Eindringling wegen seiner geringen Masse kaum ab. Das Objekt durchquert den Stern einmalig mit hoher Geschwindigkeit und fliegt anschließend weiter durch den freien Weltraum.
Eingefangen wird das Schwarze Loch erst, wenn ein massereicher Planet wie Jupiter oder ein Begleitstern es per Schwerkraft auf eine Umlaufbahn lenkt. Dort durchquert es immer wieder den Stern, verliert durch Reibung Bewegungsenergie und sinkt über Millionen bis Milliarden Jahre in dessen Zentrum.
Bei einem Begleiter in rund 778 Millionen Kilometern Abstand wie Jupiter muss der Eindringling dafür mindestens zehn Billiarden Tonnen wiegen. Für unsere Sonne ist ein Einfang fast ausgeschlossen, weil Dunkle Materie in der Milchstraße mit 200 Kilometern pro Sekunde zu schnell vorbeizieht.
Drehung des Sterns entscheidet zwischen Explosion und lautlosem Ende
Ein Stern mit einem solchen Schwarzen Loch im Kern gilt als sogenannter Hawking-Stern und ist im Zentrum dreizehnmal dichter als Blei. Frühere Modelle nahmen an, dass hell aufleuchtendes Gas beim Hineinstürzen starken Strahlungsdruck erzeugt und das weitere Wachstum ausbremst.
Der Astrophysiker Matteo Cantiello vom US-amerikanischen Flatiron Institute in New York City widerlegt diese vermutete Wachstumsbremse in einer Begleitstudie. Weil das einströmende Gas fast alle Lichtteilchen verschluckt, entweicht höchstens ein Prozent der Energie als Strahlung und das Schwarze Loch wächst weiter.
Mit zunehmender Masse saugt das Schwarze Loch weiter entfernte Gasschichten an, die sich mit dem Stern schneller mitdrehen. Bei schnell rotierenden Sternen sammelt sich dieses Gas ab rund zwei bis acht Prozent der Sonnenmasse in einer kreisenden Scheibe.
„Sobald sich die Scheibe bildet, ist das im Grunde ein Todesurteil für den Stern“, sagt Gottlieb in einer Mitteilung des MIT. Das inzwischen mehrere Hundert Meter große Schwarze Loch erreicht dabei stets rund 80 Prozent der physikalisch möglichen Drehgeschwindigkeit.
Durch diese Rotation verdrillt sich das 100‑Tesla-starke Magnetfeld der Scheibe, rund dreißigmal stärker als in einem medizinischen Kernspintomografen. An den Polen schießen dadurch Teilchenstrahlen hervor, die den Stern je nach Widerstand binnen einer halben Minute bis einer Stunde zerreißen.
In bis zu 76 Prozent der berechneten Fälle rotieren ältere Sterne jedoch schon zu langsam für eine solche Gasscheibe. Ähnlich wie beim stillen Kollaps ausgebrannter Sterne ohne Supernova verschluckt das Schwarze Loch seinen Wirt dann komplett ohne Lichtblitz.
Blaues Leuchten verrät Teleskopen den Unterschied zur normalen Supernova
Kommt es dagegen zur Explosion, sendet die ausbrechende Schockwelle erst kurze Röntgen- und Gammastrahlung ins All. Danach leuchtet die knapp 26.000 Grad Celsius heiße Trümmerwolke rund einen Tag lang blau und ultraviolett, bevor Radiowellen folgen.
Im Gegensatz zu gewöhnlichen Sternexplosionen fehlt anschließend das wochenlange Nachglühen durch radioaktives Nickel, und auch alte, leichte Sterne können explodieren. Im Inneren wirke dann „eine Art Parasit, der den Stern von innen heraus auffrisst“, erklärt Gottlieb.
Großteleskope wie das Vera-Rubin-Observatorium könnten diesen eintägigen Lichtblitz über Distanzen von bis zu drei Milliarden Lichtjahren erfassen. Zudem bleibt nach der Explosion ein Schwarzes Loch unter einer Sonnenmasse zurück, das durch reguläre Sternentwicklung nicht entstehen kann.
Offene Fragen bei den Modellen zur Suche nach Dunkler Materie
Bislang bleiben sowohl primordiale Schwarze Löcher als auch explodierende Hawking-Sterne jedoch rein rechnerische Modelle ohne jeden Beobachtungsnachweis. Allein bei der geschätzten Häufigkeit solcher Explosionen liegen pessimistische und optimistische Annahmen der Studie um den Faktor 1.000 bis 10.000 auseinander.
Hinzu kommt, dass die dreidimensionale Simulation aus Rechenzeitgründen nur die ersten 0,78 Sekunden nach Bildung der Gasscheibe abbildet. Auch ein passender Lichtblitz wäre allein noch kein Beweis, weil andere seltene Sternexplosionen ähnliche Signale ohne radioaktives Nachleuchten erzeugen können.
Auch wenn Teleskope künftig keine passenden Explosionen aufspüren, lässt sich damit eingrenzen, wie viel Dunkle Materie überhaupt aus solchen Urknall-Überresten bestehen kann. An der Arbeit beteiligten sich neben dem MIT und dem Flatiron Institute auch Physiker:innen der US-amerikanischen Hochschulen New York University und Stanford University.
