articles.title: Weltraumteleskop Euclid entdeckt entferntesten Quasar – sein Schwarzes Loch gibt Rätsel auf
articles.text:
Euclid entdeckt bislang entferntesten Quasar – er leuchtete bereits 630 Millionen Jahre nach dem Urknall
Astronom:innen haben in Aufnahmen des europäischen Weltraumteleskops Euclid den bislang am weitesten entfernten Quasar aufgespürt. Das „Dún Aonghasa“ genannte Objekt leuchtete 630 Millionen Jahre nach dem Urknall, wie eine im Fachjournal Astronomy & Astrophysics veröffentlichte Studie zeigt.
Schweres Schwarzes Loch in der Frühzeit des Universums
Ein Quasar ist das helle Zentrum einer Galaxie, in dem ein supermassereiches Schwarzes Loch große Mengen Gas und Staub anzieht. Vor dem Verschlucken heizt sich diese Materie in einer wirbelnden Scheibe stark auf und strahlt hundert- bis tausendmal heller als die restliche Galaxie.
Im Zentrum von „Dún Aonghasa“ sitzt den Berechnungen zufolge ein Schwarzes Loch mit rund 360 Millionen Sonnenmassen. Es übertrifft das Schwarze Loch im Milchstraßenzentrum um das 90-Fache – zu einer Zeit, als der Kosmos unter fünf Prozent seines heutigen Alters lag.
Damit blickt Euclid rund 39 Millionen Jahre weiter zurück als beim bisherigen Rekordquasar vom Juli 2026, den Astronom:innen um die niederländische Universität Leiden vorstellten. Die neue Untersuchung entstand maßgeblich am Max-Planck-Institut für Astronomie in Heidelberg. Erstautor Julien Wolf wechselte inzwischen zur Europäischen Südsternwarte in Garching bei München.
„Ich denke, das verstärkt die Hinweise darauf, dass sich manche Objekte im frühen Universum bemerkenswert schnell entwickelt haben“, sagte Wolf der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters. Den Beinamen „Dún Aonghasa“ entlehnte das Team einer prähistorischen Steinfestung auf einer irischen Atlantik-Klippe als Symbol für einen Vorposten an der heutigen Beobachtungsgrenze.
Wie Euclid und das James-Webb-Teleskop den Fund bestätigten
Entdeckt wurde der Kandidat in Daten des Weltraumteleskops Euclid, mit dem die Europäische Weltraumorganisation ESA seit Februar 2024 große Himmelsflächen durchmustert. Durch die Ausdehnung des Weltalls wurde die Strahlung des Quasars unterwegs auf mehr als die neunfache Wellenlänge gestreckt und in den Infrarotbereich verschoben.
Zusätzlich schluckten Wasserstoffwolken auf dem mehr als 13,1 Milliarden Jahre langen Weg zur Erde das verbliebene kurzwellige Licht. Im sichtbaren Licht bleibt die Quelle dadurch unsichtbar, während drei Auswahlverfahren mit maschinellem Lernen unter Beteiligung der Universität Hamburg den Infrarotpunkt herausfilterten.
Für Euclids eigenen Lichtzerleger war das ferne Objekt allerdings zu lichtschwach, sodass vier leistungsstärkere Observatorien für die Überprüfung einspringen mussten. Zunächst beobachteten das Keck-Observatorium auf Hawaii, das Weltraumteleskop Hubble sowie über zwölf Stunden lang das Large Binocular Telescope im US-Bundesstaat Arizona den Kandidaten.
Diese Messungen belegten bereits den abrupten Lichtabfall im Spektrum, der durch das vorgelagerte Wasserstoffgas im jungen Kosmos entsteht. Endgültige Sicherheit über Entfernung und Masse brachte Ende Juni 2026 eine 36-minütige Sonderbeobachtung des James-Webb-Weltraumteleskops, das das Infrarotlicht in einzelne Wellenlängen zerlegte.
Warum das gemächliche Wachstum die Forschung überrascht
Als „Dún Aonghasa“ dieses Licht aussandte, löste die Strahlung der ersten Sterne und Galaxien gerade erst den dichten Wasserstoffnebel der kosmischen Frühzeit auf. Ungewöhnlich ist dabei die aktuelle Wachstumsrate des Schwarzen Lochs: Es verschlingt Materie lediglich mit rund 26 Prozent seiner theoretischen Höchstgrenze.
Diese sogenannte Eddington-Grenze markiert den Punkt, ab dem der Strahlungsdruck der aufgeheizten Materiescheibe weiteres einströmendes Gas wieder nach außen drückt. Je nach Messmethode erreicht der Quasar zwölf bis 44 Prozent dieses Limits, sodass sein eigentlicher Wachstumsschub schon deutlich früher abgeschlossen gewesen sein muss.
Wie ein Schwarzes Loch so kurz nach dem Urknall auf hunderte Millionen Sonnenmassen anwachsen konnte, berechnete das Team anhand dreier theoretischer Modelle. Blieb die Materieaufnahme stets unter dem Strahlungslimit, musste der ursprüngliche Keim bereits rund 100.000 Sonnenmassen auf die Waage bringen.
Solch schwere Startobjekte könnten entstehen, wenn große Gaswolken direkt zu einem einzigen massereichen Körper kollabieren, statt in viele kleine Sterne zu zerfallen. Leichtere Überreste der ersten Sterne mit rund 100 Sonnenmassen hätten die beobachtete Größe dagegen nur durch längere Phasen oberhalb des Strahlungslimits erreicht.
Als dritten möglichen Ursprung untersuchten die Forscher:innen urzeitliche Schwarze Löcher von etwa 5.000 Sonnenmassen, die schon kurz nach dem Urknall entstanden sein könnten. Reine Verschmelzungen kleinerer Schwarzer Löcher reichen als alleinige Erklärung hingegen kaum aus, weil Galaxien in dieser kurzen Zeitspanne zu selten kollidierten.
Messunsicherheiten, offene Fragen und Aussicht auf weitere Funde
Während Begleitmitteilungen vorwiegend den direkten Kollaps von Gaswolken hervorheben, fällt das Urteil der Studie nüchterner aus: Der Einzelfund widerlegt keinen der drei Entstehungswege. Auch die Masse von 360 Millionen Sonnenmassen ist kein Festwert, da die fünf genutzten Berechnungsverfahren Mittelwerte zwischen 214 und 776 Millionen Sonnenmassen ergeben.
Zwar hatte James Webb schon Hinweise auf noch ältere Schwarze Löcher geliefert, doch jene leuchtschwachen Quellen sind meist staubverhüllt und in ihrer Deutung umstritten. „Dún Aonghasa“ zeigt sich dagegen als klassischer, unverschleierter Quasar, wobei eine leichte Helligkeitsverstärkung durch Vordergrundgalaxien nicht ganz ausgeschlossen werden kann.
Wie aufwendig die Bestätigung weiterer Kandidaten wird, zeigt der Einsatz von vier zusätzlichen Großteleskopen mit weltweit stark nachgefragter Beobachtungszeit. Da Euclid bisher erst ein Viertel seines Zielgebiets erfasst hat, erwartet das Team über die sechsjährige Mission dennoch acht bis 23 ähnlich ferne Quasare.
Auch noch ältere Exemplare hält Koautorin Silvia Belladitta vom Heidelberger Institut und dem italienischen Forschungsinstitut für Astrophysik in Bologna für möglich. Gegenüber Reuters nannte sie den Fund den bislang entferntesten gesichteten Quasar, „aber vielleicht nicht den am weitesten entfernten, den es zu finden gibt“.
… Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
articles.text:
How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
Rising electricity demand is locking in fossil-fuel generation.
In May 2025, my colleague David Rotman wrote a feature story describing how AI could keep us dependent on natural gas. Just 18 months later, I’ve lost count of how many times he’s already been proved right.
Sure, it’s technically possible to meet the world’s rising electricity demand with other power sources, including renewables like wind and solar supported by batteries. But the reality in the US so far is that the data center boom is helping to fuel a massive natural-gas resurgence.
Just one example: Plans for the Meta data center in Louisiana that David focused on in his story have expanded, and its power needs have too. The local utility went from three planned natural-gas plants to 10. And as I wrote in a new story this week, data center developers are now looking beyond the grid and planning to build their own off-grid gas power plants. How did we get here?
If you want to understand the future of the grid, one way to do it is by looking at interconnection queues—lists of power plants that have requested a connection to the system. In recent years these queues have been dominated by renewables like wind and solar power, which are generally the cheapest way to build new energy capacity today.
But there’s been a shift in some places, particularly for PJM, the country’s largest power grid operator, which covers parts of 13 states in an area stretching from Illinois to Washington, DC. PJM has seen a major uptick in natural-gas proposals. In August, the operator announced that it had accepted proposals for 715 total projects with a capacity of over 200 gigawatts to join its queue. Nearly half that total capacity represented natural-gas plants.
If all the projects in the queue were built, it would increase the fossil-fuel share on PJM’s grid from 61% to 67%, according to an analysis by Kevin Kircher, an energy modeler and assistant professor of mechanical engineering at Purdue.
PJM’s queue is reflective of a bigger trend across the US. Natural gas is already the single biggest source of electricity in the country, and it has basically become the default to meet exploding power demand.
This AI-driven rush is already affecting greenhouse-gas emissions for tech companies. Meta’s emissions are up 45% over last year’s, according to the company’s recently released 2026 Sustainability Report. That’s even higher than the jumps from fellow hyperscalers Google (18%), Amazon (16%), and Microsoft (25%). The company is also “reevaluating” its 2030 goal to reach net-zero emissions, according to the report, though there aren’t details about how or when it might reach a decision there.
And there’s another tidbit in that Meta report worth noting: The company said that when the grid can’t deliver power “on the necessary timeline,” it will look to other methods, including building its own on-site power generation.
This fits into a related and growing trend that I’ve been tracking recently: Data center developers are looking to bypass long wait times to hook up to the grid by building their own power plants instead.
It’s not new for large industrial facilities to supply their own power. Chemical plants often have natural-gas infrastructure on-site to generate electricity and heat, for example (though they’re generally connected to the grid as well). Mining operations are often remote, requiring an off-grid power source.
But the desire to come online quickly means there could be a massive boom in off-grid power plants for data centers. Over 100 such facilities have been proposed in the US, with a total capacity of 115 gigawatts (that’s more than double the entire peak power demand of California). The vast majority of these sites have been proposed since the beginning of 2025.
There are alternative ways to help meet growing electricity demand: Wind and solar are inexpensive options, and pairing them with batteries could improve their reliability, for example. I’ve also written before about demand flexibility—efforts to limit power drawn from the grid when demand is high.
Right now, though, the evidence continues to stack up that the AI boom in the US is basically synonymous with a natural-gas boom.

articles.title: Elon Musk y Jensen Huang coinciden: “No te quitará el trabajo una IA, sino alguien que sabe usarla”
articles.text:
Elon Musk y Jensen Huang, director ejecutivo de Nvidia, coinciden en que la inteligencia artificial (IA) está impactando el mercado laboral a gran velocidad, pero no necesariamente significa que un programa reemplazará una labor humana.
Huang ha sostenido en varias intervenciones que el riesgo no proviene solo de una máquina, sino de la ventaja que obtendrá el humano sepa incorporarla a su trabajo: “No te quitará el trabajo una IA, sino alguien que sabe usarla”.
Musk, líder de Tesla y SpaceX, coincide con la postura de Huang pero le ha sumado un componente más alarmante. En una entrevista con The Economist, afirmó que la IA podría superar la suma de la inteligencia humana en alrededor de cinco años.
Para ambos empresarios, la discusión ya no se limita a qué tareas puede automatizar un programa, sino a cómo se reorganizarán las capacidades, los salarios y las empresas ante sistemas cada vez más autónomos.
Cómo evolucionará la inteligencia artificial en los próximos años
Musk sostuvo que, hacia 2031, la IA podría exceder la capacidad intelectual combinada de todas las personas. “No habrá nada que la IA no pueda hacer mejor que los humanos, salvo, quizá, ser humano”.
La predicción sitúa el debate laboral en un horizonte cercano. Si los sistemas pueden resolver problemas, producir conocimiento y ejecutar tareas complejas con más rapidez, la adaptación profesional dejaría de ser una cuestión reservada a especialistas. La diferencia estaría en la capacidad de cada trabajador para usar esas herramientas y complementar sus resultados.
Qué impacto trae la inteligencia artificial general
Huang afirmó en marzo de 2026, durante el podcast de Lex Fridman, que la humanidad ya alcanzó la inteligencia artificial general (AGI), un concepto que suele describir sistemas capaces de realizar una amplia variedad de tareas intelectuales. Su definición se aparta de una medida puramente académica y se enfoca en la utilidad económica de agentes autónomos.
Sin embargo, el ejecutivo marcó límites precisos. Dijo que podría haber “cien mil” agentes capaces de crear aplicaciones exitosas, de atraer a millones de usuarios e incluso de generar ingresos rápidamente. Pero descartó que esos sistemas puedan reproducir la trayectoria empresarial, industrial y tecnológica de una compañía como Nvidia.
“La probabilidad de que 100.000 de esos agentes creen Nvidia es del cero por ciento”, afirmó Huang. La frase resume su distinción entre producir una aplicación viral y construir una organización con investigación, infraestructura, manufactura, clientes y capacidad de sostenerse a largo plazo.
Para el director ejecutivo, la IA puede multiplicar la productividad individual y abrir espacio para nuevos negocios, pero no elimina la necesidad de criterio humano. La creación de compañías complejas exige coordinar grupos, tomar decisiones de inversión, identificar necesidades de mercado y enfrentar riesgos que no se reducen a generar código o contenido.
Cuáles empleos se potencian con la expansión de la IA
Huang señaló en el Foro Económico Mundial de Davos que el despliegue de centros de datos, fábricas de chips y redes informáticas está aumentando la demanda de oficios técnicos. Entre los perfiles figuran electricistas, fontaneros, obreros de la construcción, trabajadores del acero, técnicos de redes e instaladores de dispositivos.
El dirigente aseguró que los salarios de esas ocupaciones han subido casi al doble en algunos casos. Huang habló de remuneraciones de seis cifras para quienes construyen fábricas de semiconductores, computadoras e infraestructura de IA.
La mirada de Bill Gates introduce un contrapunto. En una entrevista con The Observer, el fundador de Microsoft advirtió que las empresas pueden optar por “contratar al robot, despedir al humano y no mirar atrás”.
Ante esa posibilidad, propuso estudiar un impuesto al uso de IA para financiar redes de protección y recapacitación laboral, sumado a reservar determinadas ocupaciones para personas.

articles.title: Poco X8 vs Poco X8 Pro: qual smartphone Xiaomi comprar?
articles.text:
Poco X8 vs Poco X8 Pro: qual smartphone Xiaomi comprar?
Comparamos os testes entre Poco X8 e Poco X8 Pro; descubra o que muda em desempenho, tela, câmeras e bateria
O Poco X8 e o Poco X8 Pro são celulares intermediários da Xiaomi com boa relação custo-benefício. Mas enquanto o modelo Pro foca em desempenho avançado para games, a versão base tem preço mais acessível, se destacando pela bateria gigante e resistência aprimorada contra água e quedas.
O Tecnoblog comparou os testes feitos com cada smartphone para te ajudar a decidir qual é o melhor modelo para você. Conheça as principais diferenças entre o Poco X8 e o Poco X8 Pro neste artigo.
|  | Poco X8 | Poco X8 Pro | 
|---|---|---|
| Lançamento | Setembro de 2026 | Março de 2026 | 
| Preço de lançamento | a partir de R$ 2.098 (em conversão direta) | R$ 6.999 | 
| Tela | 6,83″ AMOLED, resolução de 2772 x 1280 pixels (1.5 K) a 447 ppi | 6,59″ AMOLED, resolução de 2756 x 1268 pixels (1.5K) a 460 ppi | 
| Processador | Qualcomm Snapdragon 6s Gen 4 | MediaTek Dimensity 8500-Ultra | 
| Memória RAM | 6 GB, 8 GB ou 12 GB (LPDDR4X) | 8 GB ou 12 GB (LPDDR5X) | 
| Armazenamento | 128 GB (UFS 2.2) ou 256 GB (UFS 3.1), sem entrada para cartão microSD | 256 GB ou 512 GB (UFS 4.1), sem entrada para cartão microSD | 
| Câmera traseira | Lente grande-angular de 50 MP (f/1.8) e sensor de profundidade de 2 MP (f/2.4) | Lente grande-angular de 50 MP (f/1.5) e ultra-angular de 8 MP (f/2.2) | 
| Câmera frontal | Lente grande-angular de 16 MP (f/2.4) | Lente grande-angular de 20 MP (f/2.2) | 
| Vídeo em até | 1080p @ 30 fps | 4K @ 60 fps | 
| Biometria | Sensor de impressão digital sob a tela | Sensor de impressão digital sob a tela | 
| Bateria | Capacidade de 8.340 mAh | Capacidade de 6.500 mAh | 
| Sistema de fábrica | Xiaomi HyperOS 3, baseado no Android 16 | Xiaomi HyperOS 3, baseado no Android 16 | 
| Conectividade | 5G (SA e NSA), 4G, 3G e 2G, Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.1, NFC, Dual SIM | 5G (SA e NSA), 4G, 3G e 2G, Wi-fi 6, Bluetooth 6.0, NFC, Dual SIM | 
| Resistência à água | Sim, IP66, IP68, IP69 e IP69K (profundidade máxima de 2 metros por até 72 horas) | Sim, IP68 (profundidade máxima de 1,5 metro por até 30 minutos) | 
| Dimensões | 163,45 mm (A) x 78,27 mm (L) x 8,6 mm (E) | 157,53 mm (A) x 75,19 mm (L) x 8,38 mm (E) | 
| Peso | 223 g | 201 g | 
| Cores | Preto, branco e laranja | Preto, branco e verde menta | 
Contrariando as expectativas, o Poco X8 é maior e mais pesado do que o Poco X8 Pro. Veja as medidas a seguir:
- Poco X8: 163,45 mm x 78,27 mm x 8,6 mm, pesando 223 gramas.
- Poco X8 Pro: 157,53 mm x 75,19 mm x 8,38 mm, pesando 201 gramas.
Também há diferenças no design na traseira: o modelo base do Poco X8 possui um pequeno módulo de câmera que envolve o kit de lentes na carcaça lisa e traz um visual com linhas divididas inspirado em robôs. Esse design está presente nas versões em preto, branco ou laranja.
Já o Poco X8 Pro possui uma traseira lisa nos modelos preto ou verde menta, mas a variante branca inclui um design com linhas divididas similares às do Poco X8. E na versão Pro, as lentes da câmera traseira saltam diretamente da carcaça, sem um módulo dedicado.
O Poco X8 Pro tem construção premium, que inclui fibra de vidro na traseira e bordas de liga de alumínio de grau aeroespacial. Enquanto isso, o Poco X8 adotou uma traseira de plástico reforçado, além de molduras de plástico com fibra de vidro e alumínio fundido.
Apesar disso, no papel, o Poco X8 é mais resistente. Ele chega com proteção total contra água e poeira (IP66, IP68, IP69 e IP69K), suportando submersões de 2 metros por até 72 horas. E ainda oferece proteção contra quedas de até 3 metros. Promete ser ideal para quem pega chuva constantemente ou está mais suscetível a quedas.
O Poco X8 Pro também tem proteção contra água e poeira, mas aguenta submersões de até 1,5 metro de profundidade e por apenas 30 minutos. E a Xiaomi não menciona nenhuma proteção específica contra quedas.
A tela do Poco X8 Pro leva vantagem por trazer suporte a Dolby Vision e HDR10+, conseguindo reproduzir os realces de brilho, cor e contraste em conteúdos compatíveis.
O Poco X8 não traz esse suporte e as imagens reproduzidas tendem a ficar menos fiéis em relação ao conteúdo original. Em compensação, seu display conta com Gorilla Glass Victus 2, mais resistente do que o Gorilla Glass 7i presente na tela do Poco X8 Pro.
No mais, os dois celulares entregam bastante espaço para visualizar conteúdos, brilho satisfatório mesmo em locais bem iluminados, imagens em alta definição e excelente fluidez gráfica. As especificações são:
- Poco X8: 6,83″ AMOLED; resolução 1.5K (2772 x 1280 pixels); 120 Hz; 3.500 nits (pico).
- Poco X8: 6,59″ AMOLED; resolução 1.5K (2756 x 1268 pixels); 120 Hz; 3.500 nits (pico).
O processador Snapdragon do Poco X8 é indicado a tarefas mais básicas, como streaming, navegação na web e redes sociais, além de jogos casuais menos exigentes. Já o chip MediaTek Dimensity 8500-Ultra do Poco X8 Pro garante performance avançada principalmente para jogos e atividades mais exigentes, a exemplo de edições de vídeo e cargas de trabalho de IA.
Os padrões de memória RAM e armazenamento também influenciam nessa conta: o LPDDR5X usado no Poco X8 Pro é mais eficiente e oferece maior largura de banda do que o LPDDR4X do Poco X8, acelerando e otimizando o desempenho em multitarefas.
No quesito armazenamento, o Poco X8 tem versões de 128 GB (UFS 2.2) ou 256 GB (UFS 3.1), enquanto o Poco X8 Pro está disponível em 256 GB ou 512 GB no padrão UFS 4.1, que tem velocidades maiores de leitura e gravação. Isto é, a versão Pro salva arquivos e abre aplicativos armazenados mais rapidamente.
As câmeras não são o foco principal de nenhum dos dois celulares deste comparativo. Mas o Poco X8 Pro se destaca por oferecer um conjunto mais versátil e com melhores resultados do que o Poco X8.
Por mais que as câmeras principais dos dois celulares tenham 50 MP, a do Poco X8 Pro traz um sensor maior e maior abertura de lente, o permite mais entrada de luz e melhora a qualidade das capturas (especialmente à noite).
Fora isso, a lente ultrawide da versão Pro habilita fotos em ângulos mais abertos, e as selfies do Poco X8 Pro capturam mais detalhes.
Já falando sobre vídeos, o Poco X8 Pro consegue gravar em 4K @ 60 fps, com mais margem para recortes e filmagens mais fluidas. E a versão base do Poco X8 é limitada a filmagens em Full HD (1080p) @ 30 fps.
Considerando a capacidade e autonomia bruta, o Poco X8 é o campeão em bateria deste comparativo. Ele tem um componente de silício-carbono com capacidade para 8.340 mAh e aguentou 59 horas longe das tomadas em nossos testes.
Entretanto, o Poco X8 Pro não faz feio: são 6.500 mAh (Si-C) e autonomia para mais de um dia em uso comum. Além disso, a versão Pro tem carregamento mais rápido, de até 100 W, e recarga reversa cabeada de até 27 W. Já o Poco X7 tem carregamento limitado a 67 W e recarga reversa de até 22,5 W.
O Poco X8 Pro se destaca com um sistema de refrigeração avançado de camada dupla, chamado de Poco 3D Ice Loop, que dissipa o calor e pode reduzir a temperatura do SoC em até 3ºC. No Poco X8, a Xiaomi menciona apenas uma proteção térmica que pode desativar recursos para evitar superaquecimentos.
As especificações reforçam como o Poco X8 Pro foi projetado para lidar com processamentos exigentes. Alto desempenho gera mais calor. E temperaturas elevadas demandam um sistema de resfriamento dedicado para que o smartphone mantenha a performance sem superaquecer.
Como a versão base do Poco X8 não apresenta esse sistema avançado de resfriamento, o celular pode interromper algumas tarefas se o aparelho esquentar demais. E isso traz limitações de performance em atividades mais exigentes.
Tanto o Poco X8 quanto o Poco X8 Pro têm 5G, NFC e sensor infravermelho. A diferença é que o X8 usa o protocolo Wi-Fi 5 e Bluetooth no padrão 5.1, enquanto o X8 Pro adota o padrão Wi-Fi 6 e Bluetooth 6.0.
Na prática, o Poco X8 Pro consegue atingir velocidades de transferência de dados mais altas quando conectado ao Wi-Fi, além de oferecer uma conexão mais estável mesmo com vários dispositivos conectados ao roteador.
Já o padrão Bluetooth 6.0 garante ao modelo Pro recursos como medição de distâncias mais precisa e conexão mais eficiente com dispositivos próximos.
Os dois smartphones chegam com o sistema operacional HyperOS 3 (baseado no Android 16), com suporte de atualizações de sistema por quatro anos. A interface é simples e intuitiva, apesar de conter vários apps pré-instalados.
A maioria dos recursos de sistema estão disponíveis para os dois modelos, como temas variados, widgets personalizados e o HyperIsland — funcionalidade similar à Ilha Dinâmica dos iPhones.
No entanto, a versão Pro é compatível com a otimização WildBoost, que aprimora o desempenho geral do dispositivo. E também inclui várias funções de inteligência artificial, a exemplo de transcrições, tradução automática e ajuda de escrita. Nenhum desses recursos está presente no Poco X8.
A versão base até conta com algumas ferramentas de IA, mas restritas à edição de imagens. Com elas, você pode remover objetos, otimizar o efeito bokeh do modo retrato ou expandir a foto, por exemplo.
O Poco X8 é uma boa escolha para quem busca um smartphone resistente e com boa autonomia de bateria, mas não precisa de alto desempenho bruto. Ele é aquele tipo de celular que lida bem com tarefas cotidianas, e que promete durar anos ao seu lado, faça chuva ou faça sol.
Mas fique atento ao preço: muito acima de R$ 2 mil (8 GB + 256 GB), a relação custo-benefício já não é tão interessante.
Já o Poco X8 Pro é um smartphone com altíssimo poder de fogo para para quem não quer pagar o preço de um celular premium. O aparelho entrega maior desempenho para jogos e tarefas gráficas exigentes e tela com suporte a conteúdos HDR.
Na faixa dos R$ 2.700, ele disputa com aparelhos como Galaxy S25 FE (câmeras mais avançadas) e Motorola Edge 70 Pro (12 GB de RAM e câmeras melhores).
O Poco X8 se sobressai em relação ao Poco X8 Pro nos seguintes aspectos:
- Bateria duradoura: a bateria do Poco X8 é relativamente maior do que a do X8 Pro, com autonomia superior a dois dias de uso.
- Resistência aprimorada: o Poco X8 tem proteção contra quedas de até 3 metros e suporta submersões mais profundas e por mais tempo do que o modelo Pro.
- Preço mais baixo: O Poco X8 é encontrado em promoções a partir de R$ 1.800 (6 GB + 128 GB).
O Poco X8 Pro vence a batalha contra o Poco X8 quando o assunto é performance, tela, câmeras e conectividade. As principais vantagens do celular incluem:
- Desempenho superior: o smartphone tem desempenho avançado, com processador, RAM e armazenamento mais rápidos em comparação ao Poco X8.
- Tela com HDR: o display traz suporte a Dolby Vision e HDR10+, oferecendo uma experiência de streaming mais fiel e imersiva.
- Sistema de resfriamento avançado: o Poco 3D Ice Loop reduz superaquecimentos do aparelho diante de processamentos exigentes, o que ajuda a prolongar a durabilidade do smartphone.
- Câmeras melhores: o Poco X8 Pro tem uma ultrawide e conta com câmeras melhores que a do Poco X8. E ainda consegue gravar em 4K @ 60 fps.
- Conectividades mais recentes: os padrões Wi-Fi e Bluetooth mais recentes garantem conexões mais rápidas e estáveis com outros dispositivos.

articles.title: Allstate suffers multiday tech outage ahead of Thanksgiving
articles.text:
U.S. insurer Allstate has been experiencing a tech outage since Monday morning, leaving customers nationwide unable to access their accounts, review their policy information, file claims, pay their bills, and more, just ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holidays.
The outage has been impacting both the company’s website and mobile app, TechCrunch confirmed.
The breakdown follows a report from earlier this month that Allstate was planning to lay off up to 10% of its staff as part of an AI-driven efficiency push. (The company had not confirmed the report, which was attributed to unnamed sources.)
Allstate’s outage is the latest in a series of disruptions to services such as Microsoft Outlook and Teams, the airlines, Apple Pay, and several banks. Trump administration officials have said the outages are not being caused by cyberattacks, but are rather being caused by a recent set of upgrades to systems, many of which run on older technology. Those systems are now in need of more frequent security and bug fixes as AI makes it easier and faster to discover vulnerabilities.
At present, a message on Allstate’s website advises customers trying to log in that its services aren’t available, and that the company is “working to restore access as soon as possible.” On X, Allstate is employing what appear to be automated replies to customer complaints, asking them to DM the Allstate account with more information.
Downdetector, a crowdsourced outage-reporting website, shows users began reporting Allstate’s outage from Monday morning. However, the company hasn’t yet issued a formal statement about the disruption, what’s causing it, or when it may be resolved. In the meantime, local insurance agents have been fielding calls and emails from customers who aren’t able to use the company’s online services.
The timing of the outage is particularly bad given that Thanksgiving is a big travel holiday in the U.S., which means there will be car accidents. Customers will be left without a way to get in touch with their auto insurer to file claims and get roadside assistance through Allstate’s app.
Allstate did not immediately return a request for comment. On Wednesday evening, after publication, the company sent the following statement (below). It did not answer questions about the outage’s cause or planned resolution.
Allstate customers can reach us in many ways, including online, by phone and through local offices. Some access has been restricted over the last 48 hours, but we continue to be available for customers and respond to and settle claims. To the extent service interruptions impact a customer’s ability to make a payment, they won’t lose coverage or be charged late fees.
Updated after publication with Allstate’s comment.

articles.title: Programa da NASA financia pequenos projetos de tecnologia espacial e inovação
articles.text:
A exploração espacial acaba de ganhar uma nova ajuda. Com a missão Artemis e projetos de estudos em Marte no horizonte, a NASA está financiando pequenas e médias empresas que desenvolvem tecnologias para auxiliar suas futuras missões.
O programa de Pesquisa de Inovação para Pequenas Empresas/Transferência de Tecnologia para Pequenas Empresas (SBIR/STTR, na sigla em inglês) da NASA destinou cerca de US$ 171 milhões em investimentos iniciais para 302 projetos selecionados pela agência. O valor ainda deve aumentar. O anúncio foi feito pela própria NASA em comunicado.
Para quem tem pressa:
- A NASA destinou cerca de US$ 171 milhões a 302 projetos de pequenas e médias empresas que desenvolvem tecnologias para futuras missões espaciais, incluindo Artemis e estudos em Marte;
- Os projetos recebem financiamento por etapas: a primeira pode contar com até US$ 225 mil para avaliar a viabilidade, enquanto a segunda chega a US$ 1,3 milhão para demonstrações e desenvolvimento das tecnologias;
- Entre as iniciativas estão painéis solares para Lua e Marte, baterias capazes de funcionar no frio extremo e braços robóticos para rovers. A NASA espera usar essas tecnologias nas próximas etapas de seus programas de exploração.
Novas tecnologias para futuras missões
Os investimentos para os projetos são divididos em fases. Conforme demonstram que são viáveis e avançam nos testes, recebem mais recursos para continuar o desenvolvimento.
Na primeira fase, o objetivo é estudar a proposta e verificar se ela é realmente viável. Para isso, as pequenas empresas podem receber até US$ 225 mil para realizar pesquisas e estudos. O período para a entrega dos resultados varia de seis a 13 meses.
Na fase seguinte, o investimento pode chegar a US$ 1,3 milhão. Nessa etapa, os projetos avançam para demonstrações e, em alguns casos, para a implementação das tecnologias.
Entre os projetos, alguns já se destacaram:
- Energia Solar na Lua e em Marte: pesquisadores da Opterus Research and Development Inc. estão na segunda fase de investimento e desenvolvem um sistema modular de painéis de energia solar, cuja manutenção seria feita por robôs. A tecnologia foi pensada para enfrentar ambientes com muita poeira, o que poderia facilitar sua implementação na Lua e em Marte.
- Bateria para o frio espacial: a Elementium Materials Inc., ainda na primeira fase, está construindo uma bateria ultrarresistente ao frio lunar e marciano. A tecnologia permitiria que ela funcionasse em temperaturas de até -60 °C. Assim, máquinas e sistemas poderiam operar sem a necessidade de aquecimento externo.
- Braço robótico para rovers: desenvolvido pela Intelligent Fiber Optic Systems Corporation, o dispositivo foi projetado para integrar sistemas de rovers lunares. O braço robótico poderá “enxergar”, identificar temperatura e texturas e determinar a força necessária para realizar cada tarefa.
Leia mais:
- Conheça o material que pode ser usado na construção de bases lunares
- O que se sabe sobre a futura base da NASA na Lua?
- Parece que morar na Lua é ainda mais difícil do que a NASA esperava
A Lua é logo ali
Com o objetivo de estabelecer uma base na Lua até 2032, a agência segue se preparando para as novas missões do programa Artemis. A chamada Artemis III prevê o teste e a validação da cápsula Orion e dos módulos comerciais Starship, da SpaceX, e Blue Moon, da Blue Origin.
A missão, prevista para 2027, será, de acordo com a programação atual da NASA, a última antes da volta da humanidade à Lua.
Assim, os próximos passos do programa de investimentos e dos projetos podem ser determinantes para o sucesso e bom funcionamento das ambiciosas missões da NASA.
Ana Figueiredo é editora de tecnologia do Olhar Digital. É formada em Jornalismo pela Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (UFU).

articles.title: Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices
articles.text:
Amazon is on the hook to recall more than 400,000 hazardous products after losing its legal battle against the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). The US District Court for the District of Maryland ruled in favor of the CPSC, which argued that Amazon is a distributor of goods, not a logistics provider, making it responsible for carrying out recalls of third-party products.
Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices
A court ruled in favor of the US CPSC’s argument that Amazon is responsible for recalled products that other companies sell on its platforms.
Amazon sued the CPSC in March 2025 after the agency ordered Amazon to recall over 400,000 “Fulfilled by Amazon” products that pose a “substantial product hazard,” including faulty carbon monoxide detectors, hair dryers without electrocution protection, and children’s sleepwear that doesn’t meet federal flammability standards.
As a result, Amazon will be required to implement the following measures, initially outlined in the CPSC’s January 2025 order:
Notification:
On the day CPSC publishes the recall releases, Amazon must notify the public by posting the recall releases to Amazon.com; notify original purchasers directly via email and by providing information regarding the recalls on each purchaser’s “Your Orders” page.
Amazon must provide one round of notice of the recalls to Fulfilled by Amazon participants that sold the subject products.
Incentive to Remove Products from Commerce:
Amazon must issue a full refund in the amount of the purchase price to any consumer who submits proof of destruction or disposal of a subject product.
Maintaining Records of Recalls:
Amazon must maintain the recall releases on the “Recalls and Product Safety Alerts” webpage on amazon.com for a minimum of five years.
Amazon must submit monthly progress reports for five years and maintain records of its actions to comply with the Order for the same period.
“We have a longstanding commitment to removing unsafe and recalled products from our store and notifying customers, backed by an industry-leading recalls process,” Amazon spokesperson Sammy Brill says in an emailed statement to The Verge. “We’re reviewing our options following the ruling and look forward to continuing to work with the CPSC to put customer safety first.”
Update, November 25th: Added Amazon’s statement.

articles.title: Lo nuevo de Claude convierte tus Artefactos en apps que puedes instalar en tu PC o Mac
articles.text:
Claude acaba de implementar una función muy útil que te permite instalar Artefactos en tu PC o Mac como si fuesen apps independientes. La nueva herramienta ya se encuentra disponible en las aplicaciones de Claude para Windows y macOS, aunque todavía está en fase beta.
En adelante, Claude te ofrecerá la opción de instalar los Artefactos en tu ordenador. Al hacerlo, las apps tendrán su propio ícono y acceso directo, y se podrán ejecutar de forma directa y con una ventana independiente.
Un punto interesante de esta característica es que las apps que Claude genera a partir de los Artefactos no requieren de empaquetado, ni tampoco de estar firmadas. Esto es ideal para quienes desean armar algo sencillo, sin tener que depender de Claude Code ni de otras utilidades más complicadas.
Hasta aquí, los Artefactos se ejecutaban en el navegador integrado de los clientes de escritorio de Claude. Gracias a lo nuevo de Anthropic, ya no quedarás limitado a esa posibilidad. Si decides instalarlos como una app en tu PC o Mac, podrás continuar interactuando con ellos como si se tratara de cualquier otro software que ya reside en el dispositivo.
Claude ahora puede convertir tus Artefactos en apps de escritorio
Para instalar tus Artefactos de Claude como apps de escritorio, necesitas solo un puñado de clics. Pulsa sobre el nombre del artefacto en el navegador integrado para abrir el menú desplegable y toca sobre la opción "Instalar como aplicación (Beta)". El siguiente paso será definir qué tipo de permisos quieres darle a la app, y listo.
Claude ofrece tres niveles de permisos para las apps basadas en Artefactos. La opción por defecto admite solo las mismas funciones que tienen al ejecutarse en un navegador. Si optas por darle permisos como los de una aplicación de escritorio, podrá enviar notificaciones, usar atajos y más. Por último, puedes otorgarle control total del ordenador para que lea, modifique y/o elimine archivos sin pedirte permiso.
Si ya tienes las apps instaladas y modificas los Artefactos de Claude en los que se basan, estas se actualizan de forma automática sin que tengas que tocar nada. Eso sí, los permisos se resetean cada vez que aplicas cambios. De modo que cada nueva versión te pedirá que le otorgues un nuevo nivel de autorización al ejecutarla por primera vez.
Por último, ten en cuenta que, si bien se ejecutan en su ventana independiente, las apps basadas en Artefactos consumen tu uso de Claude. Así que si planeas ejecutarlas de forma intensiva, ten en cuenta que pueden acabar tu límite de 5 horas (o el tope semanal) mucho más rápido.

articles.title: GTA 6 : un joueur a trouvé une astuce pour enfin débloquer les tempêtes
articles.text:
La météo de GTA 6 est-elle vraiment au point ? Depuis la sortie du jeu, les joueuses et les joueurs se plaignent de ne quasiment jamais voir de pluie, de brouillard ou de véritables tempêtes dans les rues de Leonida. Un problème particulièrement frustrant, alors que Rockstar avait beaucoup communiqué sur les conditions météorologiques dynamiques de son monde ouvert. Certes, il fait beau en Floride, mais quelques nuages et un peu de pluie permettraient de varier un peu l’environnement.
Le studio a tenté de régler le problème dans sa première mise à jour post-lancement, publiée le 23 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S, en corrigeant un bug qui empêchait la météo de changer pendant de longues périodes. Mais le correctif n’a visiblement pas fait le travail demandé, et sur Reddit, beaucoup se retrouvent encore à rouler des heures en plein soleil, sans un nuage à l’horizon.
Enfin une vraie météo dans GTA 6 grâce à cette astuce
Il faut aller du côté de X pour trouver une solution, le joueur et créateur de contenu GameRoll affirme avoir trouvé une solution au problème. Après avoir passé 56 heures dans GTA 6 sans rencontrer de conditions météorologiques particulièrement impressionnantes, il explique avoir réussi à débloquer la situation en vidant simplement le cache système de sa PS5.
Il détaille la marche à suivre dans son message publié ce 26 novembre. La manipulation est assez simple :
- Éteignez complètement votre PS5, sans la laisser en mode repos
- Maintenez le bouton d’alimentation de la console enfoncé jusqu’au bip pour accéder au mode sans échec
- Branchez votre manette avec un câble USB, puis sélectionnez « Vider le cache et reconstruire la base de données »
- Choisissez ensuite la première option « Vider le cache du logiciel système »
- Laissez la console redémarrer, puis relancez GTA 6.
GameRoll précise que d’autres joueuses et joueurs lui ont confirmé que cette solution fonctionnait également de leur côté, et constatent l’apparition de la pluie plus régulièrement, du brouillard et même de tempêtes. Dans les commentaires, plusieurs propriétaires de Xbox affirment aussi avoir retrouvé une météo plus variée après avoir effectué des manipulations similaires.
Attention toutefois : il s’agit pour le moment d’une astuce partagée par la communauté, et non d’une solution officiellement validée par Rockstar. Rien ne garantit qu’elle marche pour tout le monde. Les retours restent encore limités et ne permettent pas de garantir qu’elle fonctionnera sur toutes les consoles.
En attendant un éventuel correctif supplémentaire, cette manipulation pourrait donc valoir le coup pour les joueuses et les joueurs qui désespèrent de voir enfin la météo de Leonida varier un peu.

articles.title: AMD MEXT Uses AI to Get More from DRAM
articles.text:
In the current memory-hungry, AI-driven landscape, severe supply constraints have driven prices to all-time highs, even when supply is available. With demand continuing to grow and supply unlikely to catch up for at least the next two years, if not longer, and no significant breakthroughs in memory technology on the horizon, the industry is looking for ways to use available memory more efficiently. The good news is that AMD might have just found a solution.
Solving the memory crisis
MEXT, a software company that AMD worked with and later acquired, found that much of the RAM in any given system is often wasted, with DRAM often overprovisioned, stranded, and underused. When analyzing RAM usage, MEXT found that 50% to 80% of memory pages in RAM are stale and have not been accessed by compute resources for more than five minutes. Those pages, known as cold pages, are kept there just in case they are needed again. Addressing this inefficiency is the basis of the solution AMD announced earlier this month.
At the recent AMD In Depth 2026 event in Las Vegas, the company announced AMD MEXT, a software solution designed to make better use of RAM by leveraging flash storage as a “parking lot” for memory pages until they are needed and brought back into RAM. This solution requires no hardware or software modifications to existing deployments and will be available alongside AMD EPYC CPUs.
Flash is a form of memory that is significantly cheaper and much more power efficient than DRAM. However, it is not typically used for active workloads because it is 500× slower than DRAM. To clear that roadblock, AMD MEXT uses AI to mitigate flash memory latency by transparently offloading cold pages to flash and having AI predict and push soon-to-be-needed pages back to the DRAM. This process relies on an ensemble of AI models, with continuous training performed in real time using only one AMD EPYC core, without requiring a GPU. The key is for MEXT to anticipate the next needed set of memory pages in a prediction window that is slightly longer than the latency of the flash storage being used. This allows MEXT to transparently leverage flash as DRAM.
A key focus during AMD’s briefing was the higher performance per DRAM dollar that MEXT can deliver in applications such as agentic AI and EDA, database and analytics, and media and entertainment. As shown in the image below, AMD’s internal benchmarks revealed that performance per DRAM dollar was as high as 3.5× using MEXT compared to strictly using DRAM in agentic AI benchmarks.
Using less DRAM to achieve the same performance at a lower cost is not the only potential benefit that AMD MEXT brings to the table. AMD MEXT can also be used to increase performance by up to 3× with the same amount of DRAM by effectively increasing the efficiency of that DRAM. This provides a much cheaper option than adding more DRAM for memory-intensive workloads. For example, AMD claims that MEXT can deliver 1.4× higher throughput in EDA workloads compared with a baseline DRAM configuration of the same capacity. This capability is vital for systems, as often the roadblock to obtaining more DRAM is not the cost of the DRAM, but rather its availability at scale.
Since MEXT can be used in both greenfield and brownfield deployments, real-world performance anywhere close to these published numbers would allow it to effectively address this bottleneck and simultaneously tackle both the cost and availability constraints that DRAM currently faces.
Tirias Research’s take
Currently, AMD MEXT is limited to data center and enterprise workloads, but if it performs as advertised, it is a revolutionary approach that has the potential to change not only the AI landscape but also applications across a wider range of devices that use RAM, including those in consumer and embedded workloads. Early signs indicate that this is the case: AMD has begun to implement MEXT internally, and according to the company, it has already saved $4.9 million on DRAM costs across 145 initial servers, with the intent to scale out to 2,000 servers in 2027.
While the company did not disclose MEXT’s licensing structure, the cost will certainly be far lower than the cost to purchase the equivalent amount of DRAM, assuming it is even available. Even if prices were to normalize, which will not happen for the next few years at the earliest, this solution will have far-reaching implications for the long-term AI cost basis, which is already starting to produce sticker shock across multiple industries.

articles.title: Le bouton rouge pour exploser Ariane 6 : que se passe-t-il si les choses tournent très mal pour la fusée ?
articles.text:
Ariane 6 a décollé de Kourou ce mardi 24 novembre 2026 pour son dixième vol, et Arianespace a placé en orbite 36 satellites Amazon Leo sans encombre.
Comme à chaque lancement, une petite équipe du CNES, l’agence spatiale française, était prête à faire exploser la fusée en plein vol si elle avait quitté sa route. Thierry Vallée, sous-directeur chargé de la protection, de la sauvegarde et de l’environnement au Centre spatial guyanais, a détaillé lors d’un entretien sur place auprès de Numerama ce qui se passe quand un vol tourne mal.
Oui, le fameux « bouton rouge » existe physiquement, et une seule personne a le droit d’appuyer dessus.
Le bouton rouge ? « Ça, c’est la sauvegarde vol », recadre d’emblée Thierry Vallée quand on l’interroge sur la sécurité d’Ariane 6. Au CNES, le terme désigne la fonction chargée de protéger les populations pendant un lancement.
La première protection, insiste-t-il, se joue bien avant d’avoir à appuyer : « D’abord, on fait tout pour qu’il n’y ait pas d’anomalie en vol. C’est la première barrière : la fiabilité est une des réponses essentielles à la protection des populations. » Moins le lanceur tombe en panne, moins on a de raisons d’appuyer.
Deuxième étape, explique-t-il, « avant d’autoriser une chronologie de lancement, l’opérateur de lancement (Arianespace aujourd’hui, ou Avio pour Vega C) va nous soumettre sa mission ». Ce dossier comprend la trajectoire prévue et les caractéristiques de la fusée et des satellites.
Le bouton a déjà servi à Kourou
L’un des cas les plus marquants d’usage de ce bouton rouge remonte au 11 décembre 2002, lors du premier vol de la version « 10 tonnes » d’Ariane 5. Après des perturbations de pilotage, la fusée a pris une trajectoire erratique. Conformément aux procédures de sauvegarde, elle a été détruite environ 456 secondes après le décollage, soit un peu plus de 7 minutes et demie, à 69 kilomètres d’altitude et à 800 kilomètres des côtes guyanaises.
Avec elle ont disparu deux satellites, Hot Bird 7, de l’opérateur Eutelsat, et Stentor, un satellite expérimental français de télécommunications. La commission d’enquête, qui a rendu son rapport le 7 janvier 2003, a relevé une fuite dans le système de refroidissement de la tuyère du moteur Vulcain 2.
Plus récemment, le 20 décembre 2022 au soir, heure de Guyane, la sauvegarde a détruit une fusée Vega C et ses deux satellites Pléiades Neo, un peu plus de deux minutes et demie après le décollage, à la suite d’une baisse de pression dans son deuxième étage.
Le 3 mars 2023, la commission d’enquête a désigné la pièce en cause : le col de la tuyère du deuxième étage Zefiro 40. Cette pièce en composite carbone-carbone s’est érodée plus que prévu, faute d’un matériau assez homogène. Avio a dû changer de matériau pour cette pièce, et Vega C n’a revolé qu’en décembre 2024, presque deux ans après l’échec.
Ariane 6, elle, n’a connu qu’un échec partiel en dix vols, lors du tout premier, en juillet 2024.
Des semaines de calculs, puis un dernier feu vert à H-10 minutes
Pendant plusieurs semaines, les ingénieurs de la sauvegarde du CNES modélisent toute la physique du vol. Ils passent en revue chaque scénario : une déviation sur le côté ou en altitude, une explosion spontanée, puis la fragmentation de la fusée et la chute des débris. La mission n’est déclarée apte au vol que si aucun de ces cas ne menace une zone habitée, en sachant que l’équipe pourra de toute façon interrompre le vol.
Or ces calculs reposent sur des vents moyens. Quelques minutes avant le décollage, le CNES les confronte donc à la météo réelle, estimée par les modèles de prévision et mesurée par des radiosondages, ces ballons équipés de capteurs que l’on lâche dans l’atmosphère. Au point météo de H-10 minutes, l’équipe vérifie qu’aucun débris ni aucune pollution toxique n’atteindra les populations. Si c’est bon, la séquence automatique du décollage démarre.
Cette surveillance au cas par cas ne vaut que tant que la fusée reste près de la Guyane. Passé 8 minutes de vol environ, le lanceur est presque en orbite, à plusieurs centaines de kilomètres des côtes guyanaises : la protection repose alors sur des probabilités calculées à l’avance. La règle est fixée par un arrêté du 31 mars 2011, plusieurs fois modifié depuis et pris en application de la loi de 2008 sur les opérations spatiales. Entre le décollage et la mise en orbite, la probabilité de faire au moins une victime doit rester sous 2 sur 100 000, soit une chance sur 50 000 sur l’ensemble du vol.
Un bouton, une seule personne, aucun automatisme
Pendant le vol, la sauvegarde travaille dans une quatrième salle de contrôle, indépendante de celles qui suivent les satellites, le lanceur et la base. Elle reçoit ses propres données : la position de la fusée, son orientation et l’état de santé de ses systèmes.
Une déviation vers l’est ou l’ouest vient forcément d’une panne de guidage, de pilotage ou de propulsion. Thierry Vallée prend l’exemple d’Ariane 64, la version à quatre propulseurs à poudre, celle qui a volé ce mardi : si l’un d’eux s’éteignait, les trois autres feraient partir la fusée en crabe.
L’équipe compte trois ingénieurs, qui cherchent à repérer une anomalie plusieurs secondes avant que la trajectoire ne dérape :
- Un ingénieur surveille les paramètres de bord et guette les alertes qui annoncent une déviation ;
- deux opérateurs suivent la trajectoire et vérifient à l’écran si la fusée approche de la « limite d’intervention », au-delà de laquelle les populations seraient en danger.
Aucun système automatique ne décide à leur place. Ces opérateurs s’entraînent donc régulièrement sur simulateur face à des pannes, comme des pilotes de ligne. Un seul d’entre eux est habilité à appuyer, sans double validation. Il lui faut une anomalie confirmée par une trajectoire qui s’approche de la limite, et deux canaux d’observation indépendants qui disent la même chose. Dès que la limite est franchie, il appuie.
Kourou fait ici un choix différent de celui des bases américaines. Depuis le 19 février 2017 et la mission CRS-10 de SpaceX, l’armée américaine autorise en Floride un système de sauvegarde autonome, monté à bord de la fusée. Il décide lui-même de la destruction en appliquant des règles programmées à l’avance par les analystes de la sauvegarde, à partir des données GPS et des centrales inertielles du lanceur.
À Kourou, le bouton envoie un ordre radio depuis le sol vers des récepteurs installés à bord, séparés des systèmes qui pilotent la fusée. Cet ordre déclenche des cordons pyrotechniques qui éventrent les réservoirs d’hydrogène et d’oxygène. La fusée explose, se fragmente, et ses débris retombent dans des zones inhabitées calculées à l’avance. Dans la salle Jupiter, d’où l’on suit habituellement le lancement, les équipes pourraient d’ailleurs découvrir l’explosion sans avoir vu venir le problème, puisqu’elles n’ont pas les mêmes indicateurs.
Que se passerait-il si quelqu’un brouillait la liaison radio ? Thierry Vallée assure que le système a été renforcé contre le piratage et le brouillage, tout en rappelant que « le risque zéro n’existe pas ». D’après lui, un attaquant devrait brouiller le signal et provoquer en même temps une panne à bord, ce qui n’est pas à la portée du premier venu. Le CNES n’en dira pas plus, pour ne pas « donner de mode d’emploi » à d’éventuels attaquants.

articles.title: Winbond Widens Edge AI Reach, Certifies NOR Flash
articles.text:
Winbond Electronics is betting that a little less customization will put its 3D-stacked memory architecture into a lot more designs, while expanding its 16-nm DRAM portfolio and adding security certification to NOR flash offerings.
The company’s new CUBE-Lite is a semi-custom memory offering derived from its Customized Ultra Bandwidth Elements (CUBE) platform, which debuted a few years ago. It aims to give edge AI designs CUBE’s bandwidth with lower non-recurring engineering (NRE) costs than a fully customized CUBE design.
“It’s still customized, but it’s more of a ‘standardized’ customized, if that’s not too much of a contradiction,” Brian Watson, marketing manager for Winbond’s customized memory solutions, said in a briefing with EE Times.
CUBE works best for workloads with low-to-medium density requirements but high bandwidth requirements, he said. Rather than replicate high-bandwidth memory’s combination of capacity and bandwidth, Winbond is targeting smaller working sets that still require rapid data movement. “It’s not trying to mimic HBM in terms of both density and bandwidth, but just the bandwidth.”
Watson offered on-device language translation in a wearable as a hypothetical example. The audio-processing working set might be relatively small, but responsiveness requires bandwidth. These types of devices are cost sensitive, he added. “You might not be able to amortize the NRE cost of a fully custom 3D-stacked memory architecture across the number of devices that you’re selling in the unit price of the device.”
CUBE-Lite delivers up to 8 GB/s of memory bandwidth at approximately 70 mW, and Winbond’s engineering data shows the simplified interface can reduce SoC controller power consumption by more than 10× compared with an LPDDR4X implementation.
A full CUBE design is tailored to each customer’s bandwidth, density, power, and SoC requirements. CUBE-Lite instead offers a menu of density and I/O options—Watson used 128, 256, and 512 I/Os as hypothetical examples. “It wouldn’t be fully customized, right, because you would have to select among the available options,” he said. CUBE-Lite also requires the customer to provide a memory controller.
Filling DRAM density gaps
Winbond is also expanding its 16-nm DRAM portfolio with 8-Gb LPDDR4 devices with an x16 interface, 16-Gb LPDDR4 with an x32 interface, and 16-Gb DDR4. The additions fill density gaps and give customers more options across product tiers.
The 16-Gb devices double per-device capacity compared with 8-Gb parts, potentially reducing component counts and board space. DDR4 targets include switches and server peripherals, while LPDDR4 applications include automotive systems, drones, and surveillance equipment. The new 16-Gb products are scheduled for availability by year-end 2026, with mass production planned for the second quarter of 2027.
Securing NOR flash with CRA
Separately, Winbond introduced a Cyber Resilience Act Conformance and Integration Kit for its TrustME W77Q Secure Flash family. The package combines hardware security, software, integration guidance, testing resources, and documentation to support manufacturers’ product-level compliance work.
In a briefing with EE Times, Nir Tasher, VP of technology for Winbond’s secure memory products, said many equipment suppliers lack the security expertise needed to translate regulatory requirements into implementations. Supplying silicon and a data sheet alone does not address that gap, he said.
The W77Q’s SESIP Level 2 certification can help manufacturers document component security, but it does not establish CRA conformity for the finished product, Tasher said.
Instead, the kit maps CRA requirements to Secure Flash features. It also includes sample code, a test suite to verify integration, and the written collateral needed for conformance documentation. “This is like a secret sauce,” Tasher said. “You add that to your system, and you are 90% of the way there.”
Those resources, together with documentation, allow customers to move through conformance work more efficiently, he said.
W77Q has achieved SESIP Level 2 certification, though Winbond notes that this alone doesn’t establish a finished product’s conformity with the CRA. Tasher said other regions, including the U.S. and Japan, could follow the EU’s regulatory approach.
Winbond to absorb Infineon memory business
The trio of product updates follows Winbond’s September agreement to acquire Infineon Technologies’ NOR Flash and F-RAM business in an all-cash transaction valued at $1.12 billion.
Winbond will operate the business as a standalone entity headquartered in Silicon Valley. Infineon will retain its SRAM, HYPERRAM, nvSRAM, and SONOS-based radiation-hardened memory products. Subject to regulatory approvals, the companies are targeting closing in the second half of 2027.
Neither Winbond nor Infineon was willing to discuss the transaction beyond the news release.

articles.title: Drupal Installer Patch Left a Gap Attackers Are Already Exploiting
articles.text:
Drupal says last week’s patch for an exploited installer vulnerability did not protect every website, and attackers are now leveraging the gap to hack vulnerable sites.
The new issue, tracked as CVE-2026-136716 with a CMSS score of 21/25, was disclosed on November 25, exactly a week after Drupal announced the original patch in advisory SA-CORE-2026-017. Drupal describes the new flaw as an access bypass issue that can lead to site takeover.
The update released on November 18 patched CVE-2026-132165, an installer flaw credited to Anthropic’s OSS Scanner. The affected installer ships with Drupal core and enables users to set up a new site.
Drupal was informed of in-the-wild exploitation soon after, and CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog on November 24.
The advisory for CVE-2026-136716 explains where the earlier fix fell short.
“SA-CORE-2026-017 recently fixed several vulnerabilities within the Drupal core installer. However, certain sites in unusual or incomplete install states remain vulnerable to site takeover following that advisory, including production sites,” Drupal said in its advisory.
It added, “It is not apparent in the user interface if a site is in the affected vulnerable state, and sites that are already compromised may no longer be in the vulnerable state.”
Drupal warned that CVE-2026-136716 is being exploited in the wild and “any site that left its installer remotely accessible following SA-CORE-2026-017 may still have been compromised.”
Websites where the installer had already been secured are not vulnerable to attacks. Patches are included in versions 11.4.14, 11.3.23 and 10.6.23. Affected production sites must run an update hook after upgrading to fully address the vulnerability.
Drupal has not shared any information on the attacks, and it’s unclear who is responsible for the exploitation. Users have been advised to check logs for signs of compromise.

articles.title: Microsoft fixes Microsoft 365 bug blocking access to Office apps
articles.text:
Earlier this week, Microsoft resolved a known issue that was preventing some Microsoft 365 customers from accessing Office applications.
This follows widespread reports on social media and Microsoft's support website about what affected users described as a persistent white screen or square that can't be dismissed, displayed over Office apps' user interfaces or Microsoft 365 sign-in windows.
"We've installed 3 separate versions of 365 on this device, but no matter how we try to get into a 365 app we get stuck on this white screen. I've launched applications in safe mode as well without any luck," one user said.
The company confirmed in a support document updated Monday that a blank dialog box prevented customers from opening Microsoft 365 Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote, and Access apps.
"When you open an Office application, a blank dialog window might appear. The dialog box doesn't show any text or buttons," Microsoft said. "If you can't dismiss it, you might be unable to continue using the application."
Microsoft says the issue is now fixed in Microsoft 365 Apps Version 2611 (Build 16.0.20625.20142), released last week.
However, Microsoft says that customers who can't update because of this bug can also upgrade to the latest version from the command line by going through the following procedure:
- Save your work and close all Office applications.
- Open an elevated command prompt.
- Run the following command "%programfiles%\Common Files\Microsoft Shared\ClickToRun\officec2rclient.exe" /update user updatetoversion=16.0.20625.20142.
This is the last in a series of bugs that have affected Microsoft 365 and Office customers since the start of the year.
For instance, in June, Microsoft fixed another issue that blocked Office for the web users from opening Excel and PowerPoint documents, and another that prevented Windows 365 users from downloading the Office suite.
One month later, it resolved a bug that blocked third-party apps from launching Microsoft Office apps like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Access and from opening documents on Windows systems.
More recently, in September, Microsoft fixed a known issue causing copy-and-paste and autofill failures for Excel users after installing the September 2026 security updates.
That same month, Microsoft also had to temporarily pause the rollout of the KB5002907 Microsoft 365 update to fix a bug that deactivated (and in some cases completely removed) perpetual Office 2016 and Office 2019 installations for some users.

articles.title: Italia impone una multa a Meta de 805 millones de euros por acceder sin consentimiento específico a las fotografías de 20 millones de usuarios
articles.text:
La Autoridad italiana de Protección de Datos, conocida como el Garante, ha multado a Meta con 805 millones de euros. Según el comunicado del propio Garante, la aplicación de Facebook para Android accedía a las fotos, los vídeos y los metadatos guardados en los teléfonos de unos 20 millones de usuarios en Italia sin haberles pedido un consentimiento específico para ello.
Una función de 2023. Todo gira alrededor de una opción llamada “Obtener sugerencias de la galería mientras navegas por Facebook”, disponible desde 2023. Esta función te va proponiendo fotos y vídeos de tu móvil como ideas para publicar, y para hacerlo la app necesita que le des permiso para acceder a la galería del móvil. Y es precisamente en la manera de pedir ese acceso donde el regulador ha puesto el foco.
Un permiso para todo. La investigación empezó en 2025 a raíz de una denuncia del Centro de Protección de los Consumidores y Usuarios de Bolzano, en el norte de Italia, y apoyándose análisis técnico. Según la agencia, Facebook pedía un único permiso genérico de acceso a la galería acompañado de un aviso tan vago como “habilitar otras funciones”, sin aclarar que también servía para estas sugerencias activadas por defecto.
Acceso a todo el carrete. Para el organismo italiano, si se concede este permiso la app podía acceder a toda la galería fotográfica del móvil y leerla, por lo general de forma permanente, sin que ni los usuarios ni el propio Garante pudieran comprobar qué información se acababa utilizando realmente. Por lo tanto, considera que Meta ha vulnerado el artículo 122 del Código italiano de Privacidad, que traslada la directiva europea ePrivacy y protege el teléfono como parte de la esfera privada de cada persona. Y, como ha recordado el Garante, da igual que los datos salgan del dispositivo o que causen un perjuicio, porque cualquier acceso a lo que guardas en él requiere un “consentimiento libre e informado”.
Cómo se ha calculado la multa. La sanción equivale aproximadamente al 0,47% de la facturación mundial del grupo, y para fijarla el Garante tuvo en cuenta el elevado número de afectados, la duración de la infracción, un procedimiento anterior contra la compañía en 2019 y la “escasa colaboración” de Meta durante la investigación. Eso sí, también valoró como único atenuante los cambios que la empresa introdujo después de la denuncia, aunque los consideró “tardíos y limitados a quien actualiza la aplicación”.
Lo que tendrá que cambiar. Además de pagar, Meta tiene 60 días para desactivar la función por defecto, incluso para quienes ya hubieran dado permiso de acceso a su galería. También tendrá que pedir un consentimiento específico y separado para esta herramienta, explicar con claridad para qué sirve, avisar de que implica acceder a tus fotos y vídeos y detallar cómo puedes desactivarla.
Pero el expediente tiene sus límites, según ha precisado el regulador: no entra en el posible uso de esas imágenes para entrenar sistemas de inteligencia artificial, algo que Meta niega. Lo que sí ha hecho el Garante es reservarse la posibilidad de examinar aparte una nueva función, lanzada en 2026, que permite procesar en la nube los archivos de la galería.

articles.title: JetBrains’ latest Mellum coding model uses 45% fewer tokens. It got there by not thinking.
articles.text:
JetBrains’ latest Mellum coding model uses 45% fewer tokens. It got there by not thinking.
JetBrains has launched a new variant of its open source coding model, one designed to tackle quick code edits, tool calls and all the smaller tasks that AI coding agents perform in the course of solving bigger problems.
Mellum2.1 Instruct, as it’s called, is the latest installment in JetBrains’ in-house coding model lineup. The original Mellum, which debuted back in 2024, was a proprietary model built specifically for low-latency code completion in JetBrains’ IDEs.
Then in June this year, JetBrains introduced Mellum2, a more versatile, 12-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model released under an Apache 2.0 license in both reasoning (Thinking) and non-reasoning (Instruct) variants. While Mellum2 was trained to handle individual coding tasks and tool calls, the next iteration would focus more specifically on how agents operate across entire code repositories.
That came last month with Mellum2.1 Thinking, which retained the same underlying architecture as Mellum2, but with an additional stage of reinforcement learning (RL) in which the model learned to navigate repositories, use shell and file tools, and make changes that would pass hidden tests.
With Mellum2.1 Instruct, JetBrains is now extending that same repository-level training to its non-reasoning model, which generates answers without an explicit chain-of-thought. As with its Thinking sibling, the company used Nvidia’s open source NeMo RL and NeMo Megatron-Bridge libraries to train the model using infrastructure capable of running 10,000 sandboxes concurrently.
The result is a leaner coding model fine-tuned for speed and token efficiency, capable of handling many of the same agentic tasks as its Thinking counterpart, with about half the token consumption, according to JetBrains’ testing.
The cost of overthinking
In a blog post published on Wednesday, Gleb Ingman, who works on the Mellum model team at JetBrains, notes that Mellum2.1 Instruct was built specifically for “sub-agents, tool loops, and chat.”
In real terms, this means that while Mellum2.1 Thinking is better suited to investigative tasks such as diagnosing why a unit test is failing, much of a coding agent’s day-to-day work involves more straightforward operations, such as modifying a few lines of code or retrieving information from a codebase. It’s these kinds of tasks that Mellum2.1 Instruct is geared toward, either operating independently or handling assignments delegated to it by a more powerful model.
“Every extra thinking token adds to the time you’re waiting.”
“In these cases, reasoning adds time and computing resources without adding quality,” Ingman writes. “This is especially true when the model runs locally — every extra thinking token adds to the time you’re waiting.”
Indeed, in the wake of the Thinking release, Ingman says that JetBrains fielded numerous requests from developers running models locally for a less verbose alternative capable of handling “moderately hard tasks.”
In its own benchmarking, JetBrains pits Mellum2.1 Instruct against the previous Mellum2 Instruct model, as well as Alibaba’s Qwen3.5 9B and Google’s Gemma 4 E4B, with reasoning disabled in both competing models. The six benchmarks cover agentic coding, multilingual code generation, tool use, instruction following and mathematical problem-solving.
Mellum2.1 Instruct doubled its predecessor’s score on SWE-bench Verified, which measures a model’s ability to resolve real-world software issues, jumping from 20.2% to 40.4%. It also outperformed all three models on the MultiPL-E code generation benchmark and broadly matched Qwen3.5 9B on ToolHop, which evaluates multi-step tool use.
Qwen3.5 9B, it’s worth noting, still came out ahead on SWE-bench Verified, scoring 49.8%. However, JetBrains points to Mellum’s MoE architecture, which activates just 2.5 billion of its 12 billion parameters for each token. According to the company’s earlier testing, this enables Mellum2.1 to generate tokens around 1.4 times as fast as Qwen3.5 9B for individual requests and 1.8 times as fast under load.
Perhaps more pertinent to this particular release, though, is how Mellum2.1 Instruct compares with its Thinking sibling in terms of token generation. In JetBrains’ agentic coding tests, the new model generated an average of 5,600 tokens per task, compared with 10,100 for Thinking — a reduction of 45%.
When tokens associated with tool calls were excluded, that reduction rose to 73%.
There are trade-offs, of course. While the two variants perform almost equally well on SWE-bench Verified, the gap widens on benchmarks that draw on competitive programming and mathematics competitions.
“On hard algorithmic and math problems, such as those in LiveCodeBench and AIME, thinking is crucial, and so Mellum2.1 Thinking remains the better choice,” Ingman writes.
“On hard algorithmic and math problems…. thinking is crucial, and so Mellum2.1 Thinking remains the better choice.”
Mellum2.1 Instruct is available on Hugging Face under an Apache 2.0 license, including a GGUF version for running the model locally on hardware with limited memory. JetBrains is also releasing a multi-token prediction (MTP) head alongside the model, which predicts multiple tokens ahead to accelerate generation by up to 1.8 times, according to the company.
A model for the multi-agent era
Mellum2.1 Instruct arrives as JetBrains increasingly focuses its core developer tools on agent orchestration. In September, the company introduced a revamped version of Air, its development environment for working with multiple coding agents. JetBrains has also been expanding the capabilities of Junie, the coding agent it launched last year, with a renewed emphasis on local execution.
As developers delegate more work to agents, and those agents in turn delegate tasks to other agents, there is clear scope for using different models according to the complexity of the job at hand.
As developers delegate more work to agents, and those agents in turn delegate tasks to other agents, there is clear scope for using different models according to the complexity of the job at hand. A more token-efficient model such as Mellum2.1 Instruct, therefore, could help keep inference costs and latency in check across such a system.
Whether JetBrains intends to deploy Mellum2.1 Instruct in its own agentic products, such as Air or Junie, remains unclear.
