articles.title: Así es el centro de Ciencias de robótica, realidad virtual y prototipado en Colombia
articles.text:
Programar un dispositivo, probar un modelo, recorrer una simulación digital o producir una pieza audiovisual forman parte de las actividades que se pueden hacer en un centro de Ciencias en Colombia.
Este tipo de espacios reúne áreas de robótica educativa, realidad virtual con visores, experimentación científica, prototipado, creación tecnológica y trabajo colaborativo, con propuestas dirigidas a niños, adolescentes y adultos.
Qué se puede hacer en el área de robótica en el centro de Ciencias
La zona de robótica educativa está destinada a la construcción y programación de dispositivos. Allí, los participantes podrán aproximarse a los elementos que intervienen en el funcionamiento de un sistema automatizado: estructuras, componentes, instrucciones y respuestas frente a una acción determinada.
La zona de robótica educativa dispone de estructuras móviles armadas con piezas modulares, motores, ruedas y sensores. Algunos de esos dispositivos incorporan pinzas, brazos mecánicos y detectores de proximidad, elementos que permiten introducir nociones de movimiento, distancia y control.
Este tipo de práctica permite entender que detrás de un robot hay decisiones de diseño y secuencias lógicas. El aprendizaje no parte únicamente de un aparato terminado, sino de las pruebas necesarias para que un dispositivo cumpla una tarea.
“Queremos que la ciencia y la tecnología dejen de percibirse como conocimientos lejanos o exclusivos de especialistas”, señaló Camilo Roncancio, director de la Fundación Conecta +, detrás del centro de Ciencias en Bogotá.
Cómo se implementa la realidad virtual
El centro cuenta con puestos de realidad virtual integrados con visores, auriculares y asientos para experiencias inmersivas. Quien utiliza el dispositivo puede observar un entorno digital en 360 grados y modificar el punto de vista a partir de los movimientos de la cabeza.
Esta tecnología se diferencia de una pantalla convencional porque pone al usuario dentro de una simulación. Puede servir para recorrer un escenario, observar una reconstrucción, conocer la representación de un proceso científico o participar en una actividad que requiere interacción con elementos virtuales.
Por qué es útil el área de prototipado
El prototipado es la etapa en la que una idea se convierte en un modelo de prueba. Puede tratarse de un objeto, una estructura, un mecanismo o un sistema electrónico. El propósito no es obtener una versión final de inmediato, sino comprobar si la propuesta funciona y qué cambios necesita.
Un participante puede construir un vehículo, añadirle un brazo mecánico, probar cómo se desplaza y luego modificar la posición de las ruedas o el programa que controla sus movimientos.
Asimismo, este proceso incorpora el error como parte de la actividad. Un prototipo puede no girar, chocar con un obstáculo o fallar al tomar un objeto. En cada caso, el problema exige una revisión: puede estar en la estructura, en el circuito, en la programación o en la combinación de estos factores.
Qué aportan los espacios de experimentación científica
Las áreas de experimentación científica están enfocadas en la observación y la práctica. La intención es trasladar algunos conceptos de las aulas a actividades en las que los participantes puedan formular preguntas, contrastar resultados y conocer procesos a partir de la experiencia.
La ciencia, en este formato, es una práctica que requiere comprobación. Un experimento puede mostrar cómo se comporta un material, qué sucede ante una reacción o qué variables modifican un resultado.
La iniciativa se apoya en la Apropiación Social del Conocimiento, un enfoque que plantea que la ciudadanía no debe limitarse a recibir información científica. Debe participar en su comprensión, aplicación y construcción.
“La innovación adquiere mayor valor cuando el conocimiento se comparte y se convierte en oportunidades para las personas”, afirmó Roncancio.
El lugar tiene espacios de producción audiovisual y trabajo colaborativo que permiten relacionar la tecnología con la comunicación de ideas, la elaboración de contenidos y el intercambio entre personas con distintos intereses.

articles.title: AMD's graphics chief just pushed a Radeon 9060 XT to 4,837 MHz, reportedly the fastest GPU clock ever
articles.text:
In a nutshell: GPU overclocking records usually belong to seasoned pros who have spent years tinkering with liquid nitrogen. The newest addition to the list, however, is the man who runs AMD's computing and graphics business. Jack Huynh and a veteran overclocker pushed a Radeon RX 9060 XT to 4,837 MHz inside a new Micro Center in Austin. That's reportedly the highest clock speed any graphics chip has ever reached.
Huynh had come to town to celebrate the store's opening with local gamers and PC builders. On November 15, two days after the grand opening, he joined Bill "Sampson" Alverson and AMD's in-house overclocking team for a liquid-nitrogen session. He posted about it on X only this Tuesday, along with a video he says captures the exact moment the record fell.
On paper, the RX 9060 XT's boost clock tops out at 3,130 MHz, so the run pushed the chip roughly 55% past AMD's own spec. It's also nearly double the 2,530 MHz that AMD expects the card to hold in a typical game.
This is actually the third time this year that an RX 9060 XT has claimed a new high. AMD and overclocker Splave first pushed one to 4,769 MHz at the company's Markham office back in February. Then in June, Sampson and a South Korean overclocker called SoonHo edged past that with 4,789 MHz. Huynh's run tops their mark by just 48 MHz.
As for proof, Huynh's entry in overclocker SkatterBencher's OC World Record Museum rests on a single phone photo of a GPU-Z window. The catch, as PC Games Hardware points out, is that the photo shows 0% GPU load. Board power reads just 62 W, too. That's well below the card's 150-160 W rating, so the GPU likely wasn't doing much at that moment.
SkatterBencher's own rules say the clock has to be measured while the GPU is active. In fact, that's exactly why AMD's February claim never made it onto his leaderboard. Weirdly, the museum still lists Huynh's run at the very top of its GPU chart.
For anyone looking to buy an RX 9060 XT rather than freeze one, the bigger story this year has been pricing. The 16GB model launched at $349 in mid-2025. Since then, AMD has raised what it charges board partners for its GPU and memory kits several times as GDDR6 prices climbed. Another increase is reportedly lined up for this month, too.

articles.title: Des fours à 1 300 °C et des pièces de 450 tonnes : EDF investit 1 milliard pour le nucléaire français
articles.text:
C’est un virage stratégique pour la filière nucléaire tricolore. Détenue à 80,5 % par EDF et 19,5 % par le japonais Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, la filiale Framatome finalise un projet colossal baptisé Forge+ en Saône-et-Loire. Grégoire Ponchon, son directeur général, a confirmé à Bloomberg la validation prochaine d’un chantier étalé sur 10,5 hectares, soit la surface de quatre à six terrains de football. Initialement évaluée à 579 millions d’euros, l’investissement dépasserait finalement le milliard d’euros pour faire sortir de terre un complexe gigantesque capable d’usiner des composants jusqu’ici façonnés uniquement en Asie.
Un nouveau géant industriel de l’acier
Des halles de 40 mètres de hauteur abriteront des fours capables de porter des pièces en acier à 1 300 °C, couplés à une presse géante pour façonner le métal incandescent. Sur ce nouveau site bourguignon de 40 000 mètres carrés, les équipes travailleront sur des pièces pesant jusqu’à 450 tonnes, comme les couvercles de cuve qui équipent les réacteurs. Actuellement, ni la France ni l’Amérique du Nord ne possèdent les équipements nécessaires pour forger ces éléments critiques du circuit primaire des EPR. Seuls la Chine, le Japon et la Corée du Sud ont aujourd’hui cette capacité industrielle au niveau mondial.
À lire : Un réacteur nucléaire de nouvelle génération va alimenter l’IA de Google
Avec ce nouvel outil de production, Framatome a pour ambition de fabriquer, à terme, 200 pièces forgées par an. Un rythme élevé qui permettra de fournir l’intégralité des éléments en acier forgé nécessaires pour équiper deux nouveaux réacteurs nucléaires chaque année. En doublant ses capacités en France, l’entreprise sécurise ainsi son calendrier de construction tout en revitalisant le patrimoine industriel du Creusot.
Réduire la dépendance de la France aux géants asiatiques
Jusqu’ici, EDF devait faire appel à des sous-traitants étrangers comme le japonais Japan Steel Works pour acquérir ces composants lourds. Bernard Fontana, le PDG d’EDF, a expliqué au média local Creusot Infos qu’une telle incapacité de production représentait une vulnérabilité technologique importante. Le regain d’intérêt mondial pour le nucléaire risque de pousser les industriels asiatiques à privilégier leurs commandes nationales, retardant d’autant la construction des centrales françaises. Produire ces éléments en Bourgogne permet ainsi de garantir l’autonomie stratégique de la filière.
À lire : 60 ans d’attente : pourquoi la NASA mise enfin sur le nucléaire pour atteindre Mars
Près de deux siècles après sa contribution à la révolution industrielle, Le Creusot s’apprête donc à accueillir l’un des chantiers phares de la relance nucléaire française. Le projet Forge+ témoigne de l’effort financier et industriel consenti pour rebâtir la souveraineté industrielle du pays. Les bases sont donc posées pour ce chantier d’envergure qui sortira de terre juste à côté des installations existantes de Framatome.

articles.title: Windows 11 : Microsoft libère plus de 860 Mo de RAM… occupés par ses propres logiciels
articles.text:
Microsoft affirme avoir récupéré plus de 860 Mo de mémoire vive sur Windows 11 en allégeant ses logiciels.
Au printemps dernier, Microsoft a reconnu que Windows 11 consommait bien trop de mémoire. Quelque mois plus tard, l’éditeur avait promis une cure d’amaigrissement pour ses PC équipés de 8 Go de RAM. Une baisse de la consommation avait été également notée en octobre avec la mise à jour 26H2 du système d’exploitation. Microsoft vient enfin d’en dire plus sur ces gains. On fait le point.
Microsoft a fait le grand ménage dans ses applications
La dernière conférence Ignite, qui s’est déroulée le 18 novembre dernier, a été l’occasion pour Microsoft de faire le point sur ses promesses concernant la consommation excessive de RAM de son OS. Ian LeGrow, Vice-président en charge du coeur des systèmes d’exploitation, a notamment expliqué que les équipes de la firme avaient réussi à libérer plus d’un demi-gigaoctet de mémoire en se penchant sur les services Defender, Purview et OneDrive, qui fonctionnent en arrière-plan. Elles ont aussi réussi à réduire de 360 Mo la consommation de la suite Microsoft 365.
Pour en arriver là, Microsoft a dû faire des ajustements conséquents. La firme a décidé de ne plus lancer systématiquement des modules jugés superflus. Certains composants qui reposent sur les mêmes briques logicielles partagent désormais la même zone mémoire. Les équipes ont aussi pris le temps d’optimiser les applications. On salue l’effort, mais on aurait quand même préféré que Microsoft conçoive des outils sobres dès le départ.
Un effort motivé par la pénurie de mémoire
Bien sûr, l’envolée du prix de la mémoire n’est pas pour rien dans la prise de conscience de Microsoft. Ian LeGrow l’a d’ailleurs reconnu lors de la conférence : « le prix de la mémoire a explosé. Par conséquent, une plus grande capacité de mémoire dans les appareils a un impact considérable sur le coût de ces appareils. ». Il a notamment expliqué que « depuis janvier dernier, (la firme avait) consacré beaucoup de temps et d’efforts à l’amélioration de la mémoire sur toute une gamme d’appareils, en (se) concentrant particulièrement sur les appareils de 16 Go et de 8 Go. »
Le résultat ? Les applications Office seraient aujourd'hui 10 % plus rapides sur des ordinateurs possédant 8 Go de RAM et les tâches peuvent être réalisées 21 % plus vite. Afin de vérifier si ces promesses étaient véritablement tenues, l’équipe de Windows Latest a fait des mesures après avoir installé la mise à jour 26H2. Sur un portable de 8 Go, la consommation passe de 5 à 3,3 Go au démarrage. Sur un PC de 16 Go datant de 3 ans, le gain atteint même 2 Go. Seul bémol, dès que les widgets sont ouverts, la consommation repart à la hausse.
Microsoft a donc bien amélioré les choses, mais la route est encore longue.

articles.title: Les Peugeot 3008 et 5008 ne se vendent pas assez : 500 intérimaires en moins dans leur usine, mais l’électrique sauve les meubles
articles.text:
La crise frappe durement l’industrie automobile, et ce depuis plusieurs années déjà. Mais tous les constructeurs ne sont pas touchés de la même manière. Certains s’en sortent d’ailleurs plutôt bien, comme Renault, qui a même accéléré la cadence de production de sa R5 E-Tech. Il faut dire que la citadine rencontre un franc succès dans toute l’Europe. En revanche, côté Stellantis, c’est un peu la soupe à la grimace depuis quelque temps. Voilà que Peugeot a été contraint de prendre une décision assez lourde.
Comme le rapporte le Journal de l’Automobile, Stellantis a annoncé ce mardi 24 novembre qu’il réduira la cadence de son site historique de Sochaux, dans le Doubs. La raison ? Les ventes de ses deux SUV stars, les 3008 et 5008, sont trop faibles. C’est ce qu’admet à demi-mot le groupe franco-italo-américain, qui justifie sa décision par « le contexte économique actuel » ainsi que « l’état prévisionnel des marchés ». Mais concrètement, qu’a prévu la marque au lion ?
Eh bien, le constructeur a annoncé lors d’un Comité social et économique extraordinaire (CSE) la suppression de la demi-équipe de nuit. Une mesure qui entrera en vigueur dès le mois de janvier 2027. Ainsi, l’usine franc-comtoise reviendra à seulement deux équipes en journée pour produire les deux SUV. La cadence sera donc ramenée à 850 véhicules par jour, ce qui est « durablement soutenu » selon ses propres mots. Mais cette décision devrait avoir un impact social non négligeable.
Votre production solaire dépasse votre consommation ? Stockez le surplus au lieu de le revendre à bas prix. Le SolarFlow 2400 AC+ se branche sur votre installation existante, 100 % plug-and-play, et s’amortit plus vite grâce au Black Friday.
Des ventes en demi-teinte
Et pour cause, il faut savoir que 500 personnes travaillent actuellement dans l’équipe de nuit de l’usine sochalienne. Si les salariés en CDI seront déplacés en journée, les intérimaires ne seront quant à eux pas renouvelés à la fin de leur contrat.
Les salariés en CDI reprendront en effet des postes de jour aujourd’hui tenus par des intérimaires : près de 500 contrats d’intérim ne seront donc pas renouvelés, sur les 1 100 intérimaires que compte le site.
Stellantis rappelle que les 3008 et 5008 restent leaders de leur segment en France, leur principal marché. Mais le groupe invoque aussi, dans son communiqué, « l’arrivée d’une concurrence nouvelle et agressive ».
Il est vrai qu’en France, les deux SUV totalisent respectivement 30 172 et 15 448 immatriculations sur les dix premiers mois de 2026, selon la PFA, soit les 8e et 22e places du marché. La marque Peugeot recule toutefois de 4,9 % sur la période, dans un marché des voitures particulières en hausse de 4,4 %.
Mais d’après les chiffres de Dataforce pour l’Europe, la 3008 a vu ses immatriculations reculer de 2,3 % pour atteindre 101 612 exemplaires sur les dix premiers mois de 2026. Quant au grand SUV sept places, ses ventes ont progressé, mais le total n’atteint que 58 232 unités.
Cependant, les variantes électriques tirent encore leur épingle du jeu et permettent de sauver les meubles. En effet, elles permettent de maintenir une équipe de nuit dédiée à la préparation des batteries, indiquent Les Échos.
Une bonne nouvelle, alors que les usines de Sochaux et de Rennes avaient dû mettre leurs chaînes à l’arrêt fin octobre, faute de batteries pour les versions grande autonomie. La faute au fournisseur ACC, coentreprise de Stellantis, Mercedes et TotalEnergies, dont l’usine de Douvrin ne produisait pas assez de cellules pour répondre à la demande. Stellantis assure d’ailleurs avoir constaté de « nets progrès » chez ACC depuis septembre, sans donner de chiffres.

articles.title: The Download: AI swamping open records, and firefighting for permafrost
articles.text:
The Download: AI swamping open records, and firefighting for permafrost
Plus: Hackers reportedly used an AI tool to breach US spy agencies.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
AI is straining America’s open records systems
AI has intensified investors' interest in public records. Over the last few years, venture-backed startups have raised upwards of $100 million to collect data from thousands of agencies and turn it into AI-powered "signals" that help businesses sell to governments. At the same time, chatbots are making it easier for individuals to file requests.
As agencies struggle to tell whether they’re dealing with a citizen, a chatbot, or a sales pipeline, some states are passing legislation that makes it easier to deny requests. That could potentially make public offices less transparent.
Find out how AI is testing the limits of America's right to know.
—Matthew King
MIT Technology Review Narrated: Inside the quest to combat Arctic fires and save the planet’s frozen carbon
In July 2021, a wildfire burned through a forest on the University of Alaska, Fairbanks campus, stripping away the moss and soil insulating the permafrost below. Five years later, we followed researchers into the forest to investigate how fighting fires could help keep that carbon locked in the ground.
Their probe revealed an escalating problem: As climate change fuels more frequent and severe fires, they’re accelerating permafrost thaw and releasing greenhouse gases. Now, researchers are trying to break that cycle. But how much should we spend, and what risks are worth taking?
This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts. Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 Hackers reportedly used an AI tool to breach US spy agencies
The tool, Artex, was originally designed for cyber defense. (NYT $)
+ Sources suggested that China may be behind the attack. (CNN)
+ Officials say it exposed non-classified data. (Gizmodo)
+ A US financial crimes bureau has also disclosed a breach. (Verge)
+ AI is making online crimes easier. (MIT Technology Review)
2 Firms tied to Alice Huang financed $270 million of AI servers in China
It's unclear whether they contained chips restricted by the US. (Reuters $)
+ Chuck Schumer has accused Jensen Huang of export violations. (Guardian)
3 A powerful HIV vaccine may finally be within reach
“Super antibodies” blocked diverse strains in monkeys. (Nature)
+ Yet vaccine hesitancy is on the rise. (MIT Technology Review)
4 China’s Huawei has been convicted of stealing US trade secrets
It was found guilty on 10 of 12 counts, including bank fraud. (BBC)
+ The DoJ says it also helped Iran surveil protesters. (Guardian)
+ But it was cleared of the more serious racketeering charge. (CNBC)
5 Data centers have been linked to hundreds of premature deaths
The culprit is pollution from connected power plants. (Newsweek)
+ Data centers are getting their own gas plants. (MIT Technology Review)
6 Meta insiders warn its AI moderation is causing dangerous mistakes
They say the errors could have sweeping political consequences. (Guardian)
7 The ex-OpenAI engineer accused of spying has been freed
He’ll wear an ankle monitor after posting a $1 million bond. (CNBC)
8 An immune-calming pill has healed severe eczema in a clinical trial
Over a third of patients saw their symptoms improve. (Bloomberg $)
9 AI is forcing researchers to reconsider artificial minds
Some now think minds may not need bodies after all. (New Scientist $)
+ AI consciousness debates are a trap. (MIT Technology Review)
10 The US Army is about to blow up 10,000 pounds of unstable explosives
The old stockpile has become too dangerous to move or neutralize. (Verge)
Quote of the day
“All this guy did was cheat on his wife with two employees and a Chinese spy. Who hasn’t done that?”
—Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel skewers Jensen Huang's swift reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO.
One more thing
Kids outlearn AI—and we still don’t know why
Teaching a computer to use human language requires an inhuman amount of data. An LLM can easily churn through a hundred thousand times more words than a person will experience in the process of mastering their mother tongue.
This yawning divide between children and machines is called the data efficiency gap. It raises a tantalizing question for researchers: How can children learn so much with so little?
By reverse-engineering how they learn, scientists hope to create more efficient AI models—and perhaps settle enduring questions about language and children's developing minds. Here’s how they’re trying to close the data gap.
—Elise Cutts
We can still have nice things
A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line.)
+ Need a smile? Finland is livestreaming six newborn puppies around the clock.
+ Wes Anderson has stepped into the Criterion Closet and picked out the films he loves most.
+ A product designer has invented inflatable chopsticks that you unroll and blow up when it's time to eat.
+ The James Webb Space Telescope has captured a stunning image of stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron.

articles.title: Wave’s 25 million-user blueprint: How low fees disrupted Francophone West Africa’s mobile money ‘cartels’
articles.text:
As mobile money platform Wave crosses the 25 million active account mark, its Public Policy Lead, Awa Gueye, tells GODFREY GEORGE how the company forced down prices across the WAEMU region—and details the structural and regulatory hurdles that still prevent millions of informal businesses and women from participating fully in the digital economy.
A decade ago, digital payments in Francophone West Africa were still at an early stage, with adoption and the services available gradually expanding. Wave Mobile Money accelerated this development when it launched in the region by introducing a radically lower, flat-fee pricing structure.
The resulting price war forced established telecom-backed operators to slash their own commissions, fundamentally altering the digital payments landscape across the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). MTN MoMo eliminated withdrawal fees in Côte d’Ivoire in 2025, and Orange cut transfer fees to zero ahead of Wave’s launch in Cameroon.
For Awa Gueye, Wave’s Public Policy Lead, the true disruption is not merely in the pricing, but in the shift in consumer psychology.
“The biggest change is in what people expect,” Gueye says. “When someone sends small amounts several times a week, fees decide whether digital payments are part of daily life or reserved for emergencies. Once customers experience a low-cost, simple and reliable service, they expect that standard everywhere.”
That shift in expectation is borne out by the numbers. Wave now boasts 25 million active accounts, a figure Gueye uses to illustrate how rapidly unbanked populations will adopt digital financial services when the friction of cost and complexity is removed. This consumer demand has compelled the broader WAEMU market to pivot toward lower prices and improved product offerings.
For policymakers, however, the challenge is ensuring this new, competitive equilibrium is maintained. According to Gueye, regulatory frameworks must proactively protect the conditions that enabled this disruption, fostering a market where “providers compete on the value they deliver, and where the customer is the one who benefits.”
The Illusion of account ownership
While rising mobile money registration figures are frequently celebrated by governments and development agencies, Gueye cautions that mere account ownership is a flawed metric for evaluating financial inclusion.
“Opening an account is only the first step,” Gueye notes. “Inclusion is real when someone can use that account to receive income, pay a supplier, save a little, or deal with an unexpected expense, and when they trust it enough to do so every week.”
Genuine inclusion requires digital wallets to serve as gateways to savings, credit, and insurance—the financial instruments necessary for households and small enterprises to plan for the future and absorb economic shocks. However, several structural barriers continue to block this transition from basic access to active usage.
Cost remains a primary deterrent; for users making frequent, low-value transactions, even modest percentage-based fees rapidly erode capital, driving them back to the informal cash economy. Furthermore, stringent Know-Your-Customer (KYC) requirements disproportionately exclude rural populations and women, who frequently lack formal identification documents.
To overcome these hurdles, Gueye advocates for a shift in how regulators measure success, urging them to track user activity and economic outcomes rather than raw account numbers.
She also calls for the widespread adoption of tiered, risk-based KYC protocols that allow low-value accounts to be opened with simplified documentation. Governments, she suggests, could accelerate adoption by digitising the payment of civil service salaries, social welfare transfers, and supplier invoices.
Crucially, Gueye points to the potential of leveraging digital transaction histories to build alternative credit profiles, allowing individuals and small businesses without formal financial records to finally access responsible credit and insurance products.
Navigating the WAEMU regulatory labyrinth
Operating across multiple jurisdictions in Francophone West Africa presents a complex regulatory puzzle. While the WAEMU region benefits from a shared central bank (the BCEAO) and a unified framework for electronic money, friction arises when national regulations intersect with this regional base.
Rules governing taxation, telecommunications, data protection, and consumer rights often diverge from one country to the next. For a pan-African provider like Wave, a single product can be subjected to disparate compliance requirements across different borders, slowing the rollout of beneficial services.
Despite these bottlenecks, Gueye believes a balance between rapid innovation, consumer protection, and systemic stability is achievable, provided regulators engage in early, structured dialogue with industry players. She points to the BCEAO’s financial inclusion lab as a successful model, allowing regulators and providers to collaboratively test new concepts under controlled supervision.
Gueye argues that regulations should remain technology-neutral and risk-based, with clear implementation timelines and extensive industry consultation. “Regional coordination should keep a service built for one market usable in the next,” she says. “For any innovation, the same questions apply: who is accountable, how are customers protected, and what happens when something goes wrong?”
A cautious case for stablecoins
At recent industry gatherings, such as the Africa Financial Industry Summit (AFIS) and Moonshot by TechCabal, stablecoins have dominated discussions, particularly regarding their potential to streamline cross-border payments. While mobile money has successfully digitised domestic transfers, moving capital across African borders—especially between different currency zones—remains slow, expensive, and reliant on cumbersome correspondent banking networks.
Gueye acknowledges that stablecoins warrant serious attention, identifying cross-border settlement as their most credible use case.
“That gap is where stablecoins could help, for example in supporting SMEs to pay for their suppliers across borders or in faster settlement between regulated institutions to ensure business continuity for the end user,” she explains.
However, Wave’s approach remains pragmatic and compliance-driven. Gueye stresses that any integration of stablecoins would strictly require a clear regulatory framework and the explicit approval of relevant authorities in each operating market.
Designing for women’s economic agency
Perhaps the most persistent failure of Africa’s digital financial revolution is the continued marginalisation of women, both as consumers and as industry leaders.
For a digital financial product to truly serve a woman, Gueye argues, several prerequisites must be met: she must possess her own mobile device, hold her own identification, and retain sole control over her account. Beyond affordability, female users require stringent privacy protections, physical safety, and customer support accessible in their preferred language.
To close the gender gap, Gueye proposes targeted policy interventions. Chief among them is the implementation of simpler, tiered KYC requirements to address the identification deficit that disproportionately affects women.
She also urges regulators and providers to disaggregate their data by gender, providing a clearer picture of actual usage patterns rather than aggregate account ownership.
The digitisation of wages, social transfers, and market fees would also ensure capital is deposited directly into accounts controlled by women. Furthermore, the industry must design products tailored to the realities of female-led enterprises, offering affordable merchant payment solutions, savings tools, and digital transaction records capable of unlocking credit access. Increasing the number of female agents and frontline staff, who often establish trust more effectively with female customers, is also crucial.
Within the industry itself, female representation remains a priority for Wave, where women comprise 51% of the workforce.
“We believe diverse teams build better products for a wider range of customers,” Gueye says. “Women should help design products and shape the rules that govern them, as regulators, policy leads, engineers and founders. That means mentoring and sponsorship, transparent promotion paths, and making sure women have a seat at the table in consultations and industry forums.”
Ultimately, Gueye concludes, the success of these platforms should be judged by a single metric: economic agency—the tangible ability of users to receive income, make autonomous financial decisions, and grow their businesses.

articles.title: 1Password Breach Exposes Customer Data, Internal Source Code
articles.text:
Password management and identity security company 1Password revealed on Wednesday that a hacker stole customer information and proprietary source code. 1Password says customer vaults are not affected.
The company launched an investigation on November 19 after discovering that an employee’s corporate GitHub account may have been compromised.
The attacker used the account to deploy malicious code to backend services and exfiltrate customer records. The compromised customer records include names, email addresses, account identifiers, public cryptographic keys, authentication parameters, account activity times, and non-secret metadata.
In addition, the threat actor obtained source code from private repositories and accessed the company’s CI/CD system, potentially exposing infrastructure credentials.
According to 1Password, the hacker also obtained tokens from emails sent to users for account invitations, provisioning, and recovery.
A “small number” of individuals who were undergoing provisioning or recovery during the intrusion have been notified. However, the company noted that the exposed tokens cannot be exploited on their own and there is no evidence that the attacker hijacked user accounts.
A 1Password representative noted on the company’s community forum that the stolen authentication data included Secure Remote Password verifiers derived from user account passwords and Secret Keys. The verifiers cannot be used directly for authentication, and brute-forcing account passwords would require the associated Secret Keys, which 1Password does not store.
1Password highlighted that customer vaults and the cryptographic keys protecting them were not compromised. “We have no evidence that encrypted vaults were downloaded or accessed,” a 1Password community manager said.
The breach also does not impact client applications, browser extensions, and account recovery keys.
It’s unclear how many users are affected and how the hacker gained initial access to the corporate GitHub account.
In response to the intrusion, 1Password disabled the compromised GitHub account, invalidated a stolen token, replaced potentially compromised infrastructure credentials, and restored clean versions of affected services.
The company said its investigation, conducted with independent cybersecurity experts, is still ongoing. Customers do not need to take any action, but have been advised to watch for phishing attacks that could exploit news of the incident.

articles.title: Resumo do OD: Brasil na astronomia; perdão de Huang; China vs EUA
articles.text:
Em construção no Chile para liderar a próxima geração de megaobservatórios astronômicos, o Telescópio Gigante Magalhães (GMT) pode ganhar reforço da engenharia brasileira. Empresas da indústria pesada nacional deram os primeiros passos para disputar a construção do domo e das instalações de apoio dessa gigantesca estrutura científica.
Nos dias 3 e 4 de novembro, representantes da Brafer, Gerdau, MKRAFT e Vallourec participaram de um encontro técnico em Los Angeles, nos Estados Unidos, para conhecer as exigências da obra. O evento, chamado Industry Briefing Day, foi organizado pelo consórcio responsável pelo projeto.
Instalado no Observatório Las Campanas, no Deserto do Atacama, o GMT terá uma estrutura externa equivalente a um prédio de 22 andares. O domo terá cerca de 60 metros de diâmetro, 65 metros de altura e pesará aproximadamente 5 mil toneladas.
A humanidade já é capaz de evitar o destino dos dinossauros?
Há cerca de 66 milhões de anos, um asteroide atingiu a Terra e provocou uma das maiores extinções da história do planeta. O impacto contribuiu para o desaparecimento dos dinossauros não avianos e mudou o curso da vida. Se uma ameaça semelhante surgisse hoje, a humanidade teria como impedir uma catástrofe desse tipo?
A resposta ainda não é definitiva, mas estamos começando a descobrir. Nesta quarta-feira (25), conforme noticiado pelo Olhar Digital, a Agência Espacial Europeia (ESA) divulgou as primeiras imagens detalhadas de um asteroide depois que ele foi atingido propositalmente por uma espaçonave da NASA em 2022.
O experimento fez parte de um programa de defesa planetária que busca desenvolver meios de desviar asteroides que possam ameaçar nosso planeta no futuro.
Trump admite perdoar CEO da Nvidia e pede que ele não fique em silêncio no Congresso
O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmou que considera conceder um indulto presidencial a Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, caso o executivo enfrente problemas judiciais. Em entrevista ao New York Post, o republicano também aconselhou o empresário a não recorrer à Quinta Emenda da Constituição estadunidense durante os depoimentos que deverá prestar ao Congresso na próxima semana.
Saiba mais.
China acusa EUA de perseguir empresas do país após condenação da Huawei
A China acusou os Estados Unidos de impor obstáculos às empresas chinesas após um júri de Nova York considerar a Huawei culpada de roubo de segredos industriais e de crimes relacionados às atividades da companhia no Irã. Pequim criticou a decisão e afirmou que apoiará a fabricante na defesa de seus direitos e interesses.
Saiba mais.
Data centers poluem três vezes mais do que se estimava, aponta estudo
A poluição climática provocada por grandes data centers nos Estados Unidos pode ser três vezes maior do que estimativas anteriores indicavam. A conclusão é de um estudo da Universidade Harvard, que analisou 403 instalações de grande porte e identificou impacto ambiental superior ao calculado até então.
Saiba mais.
Mesmo sem quebrar, seus eletrônicos podem virar pesos de papel a qualquer momento
Cada um usa tecnologia de um jeito. Uns usam mais. Outros usam menos. Hoje em dia, é uma questão muito pessoal. Cada um tem seu punhado de dispositivos e aplicativos favoritos. E sua rotina com eles.
O que muitos usuários costumam não pensar muito sobre é justamente como sua rotina depende da boa vontade de empresas. Geralmente, essa reflexão vem à tona quando uma companhia anuncia o fim do suporte a algo que a pessoa usava muito.
A obsolescência digital acontece quando um aparelho eletrônico, como um celular, uma smart TV ou um eletrodoméstico que se conecta à internet, perde suas funções ou deixa de servir não porque quebrou fisicamente, mas porque a fabricante parou de atualizar o seu sistema.
Bruno Capozzi é jornalista, mestre em Ciências Sociais e editor executivo do OD.

articles.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
articles.text:
Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that’s designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users. The patent has been rejected, but unfortunately, Google might appeal or resubmit an amended version, and we could see this monstrosity come to market.
Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
Imagine an endless feed of AI slop in which you are the main character of every story.
First spotted by Patentlyze, the patent — which was filed last May and published last week — describes how My Channel would use a person’s demographic data and viewing history to create its own prompts that would then be fed into an LLM to help generate AI videos tailored to that person’s specific interests. In addition to factoring in what kinds of videos a user tends to watch, the system would capture contextual data from their device like IP addresses, GPS locations, and specific details about the user’s age. My Channel could also base its prompts on current news like sports scores and things happening on social media, and all of the video generation would take place on Google’s servers.
According to the patent, My Channel would be able to churn out entire movies of various genres. If a user watches a lot of videos about Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, the system might serve up something like Ash Koosha’s Odysseus: The Fall. The patent details how My Channel might be able to connect to other streaming services — which would give it even more information about users and, presumably, access to useful training data for video generation. It all seems like a convoluted way to whip up AI knockoffs of professionally produced art, but what’s most unsettling about the patent are its mentions of My Channel creating digital avatars of users and turning them into “the protagonist or lead character” in the content it pumps out.
Setting aside the fact that My Channel would use photos, videos, and audio clips of people to create these avatars, the system sounds like it is designed to generate a form of “entertainment” that is deeply at odds with what makes engaging with art a worthwhile, enjoyable experience. It can be fun to metaphorically project one’s self into fictional narratives to understand how characters feel, but what Google is proposing is giving people access to an endless supply of bespoke content that doesn’t at all encourage them to use their imaginations to empathize with or relate to the characters. The patent makes it seem like Google thinks that viewers would be entertained enough just by seeing themselves onscreen. That’s bleak in and of itself because My Channel sounds very much like an unholy cross between JibJab and the panoptic elements of Google.
My Channel feels like an even more depressing idea when you consider how the service would make it that much easier for its users to avoid broadening their horizons by being exposed to new things that exist outside their comfort zones. If Google were able to strike the right licensing deals with other streaming services, My Channel users could presumably gorge themselves on artless AI regurgitations of preexisting content. That might keep some people glued to the service — a goal that every streaming platform strives for — but it would also discourage them from engaging with entertainment that isn’t expressly crafted to appeal to their assumed tastes.
When people refer to AI-generated videos as “slop,” they’re talking about the fact that generative models are incapable of generating art with the same kind of creative intention that makes human-made stories compelling. Video generation models can mimic visual elements of the data (read: movies and series) they’re trained on, but they cannot truly think or feel in the way that directors, writers, and actors can. This reality is why it has been so baffling to see AI-boosting entertainment companies, streamers, and studios insisting that the technology will fundamentally revolutionize the industry for the better. It feels much more likely that gen AI is going to keep flooding the internet with garbage no one wants to watch.

articles.title: Plus d’un milliard d’euros : à quoi va servir la forge géante de Framatome au Creusot ?
articles.text:
Le chiffre a presque doublé en un an et demi. Lors de la concertation publique, organisée de mai à juillet 2025, le projet Forge+ de Framatome était évalué à 579 millions d’euros. Ce mardi 24 novembre, son directeur général Grégoire Ponchon a indiqué à Bloomberg que l’entreprise, détenue à 80,5 % par EDF et à 19,5 % par le japonais Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, était prête à approuver un investissement de plus d’un milliard d’euros. Selon nos confrères de BFM Business, ce serait tout simplement la plus grande forge du monde.
Après Canal+, Disney+ et Numerama+, la France accueille Forge+
Forge+ doit sortir de terre à côté de la forge historique de Framatome, en Saône-et-Loire, sur un terrain de 10,5 hectares. Les bâtiments occuperaient entre 30 000 et 40 000 mètres carrés, avec des halles de 40 mètres de haut, des fours capables de chauffer l’acier à 1 300 °C et une presse géante pour façonner des pièces pouvant peser jusqu’à 450 tonnes.
Le tout est très gourmand en électricité : plus de 80 mégawatts de puissance installée, dont environ 25 mégawatts pour la seule presse hydraulique, selon le dossier de la concertation publique. RTE doit tirer une ligne souterraine de 225 000 volts sur une dizaine de kilomètres pour que le site soit raccordé en 2029 (oui, pour fabriquer des pièces de centrales, il faut d’abord brancher la forge à une centrale).
À quoi vont servir ces pièces ?
D’abord aux nouveaux réacteurs EPR2. Forge+ doit doubler la capacité de production de pièces forgées de Framatome et lui permettre de fabriquer 100 % des composants forgés du circuit primaire d’un EPR : la cuve, son couvercle, les générateurs de vapeur, le pressuriseur. L’objectif affiché est d’environ 200 pièces forgées par an, de quoi équiper deux réacteurs chaque année.
Le calendrier tombe bien. EDF vise une décision finale d’investissement sur six nouveaux EPR2 d’ici la fin de l’année. Le même jour, venu au Creusot inaugurer un nouvel atelier d’internes de cuve à 100 millions d’euros, le ministre délégué à l’Industrie Sébastien Martin a évoqué la commande de huit EPR2 supplémentaires, sans avancer de date. Selon France 3 Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, il faut encore boucler le budget de l’État et obtenir le feu vert de la Commission européenne.
Mais la forge ne vivra pas que des EPR2. Le dossier de concertation cite aussi :
- les petits réacteurs modulaires (SMR) ;
- les chaufferies nucléaires de la Défense, comme celles des sous-marins et du futur porte-avions ;
- l’entretien du parc existant, dont une bonne partie se prépare à fonctionner au-delà de 40 ans et aura besoin de pièces de rechange ;
- l’export, vers l’Europe et les États-Unis.
Pourquoi la France, championne du nucléaire, ne sait pas déjà le faire ?
Les plus grosses pièces, comme les couvercles de cuve, ne sortent aujourd’hui que de quelques forges asiatiques. « Elles sont toutes situées en Asie, au Japon, en Corée et en Chine, alors qu’il n’y en a aucune en Amérique du Nord », a résumé Grégoire Ponchon. Framatome dépend notamment du japonais Japan Steel Works.
Tant que la demande mondiale restait faible, ce n’était pas un drame. Avec la relance du nucléaire un peu partout, et notamment en France, le risque est que ces fournisseurs servent d’abord leurs marchés nationaux, et que les chantiers français attendent leur tour. L’usine n’a pas attendu Forge+ et a été remise à niveau : elle a déjà travaillé pour l’EPR2, sur une pièce de 150 tonnes destinée à Penly qui y a été forgée au printemps.
Framatome prévoit de créer entre 190 et 240 emplois directs avec Forge+, et a ouvert cet automne une école interne d’usinage pour former ses futurs salariés. Il reste maintenant à transformer le milliard en usine, puis l’usine en pièces. Au Creusot, où la Fonderie royale a ouvert en 1782, on a un peu d’expérience.

articles.title: Wann hört KI auf dich? Wenn bei ChatGPT und Claude der Zufall entscheidet
articles.text:
Widersprüchliche Anweisungen: Wenn bei ChatGPT und Claude der Zufall entscheidet
Du hast in den Custom Instructions festgelegt, dass die KI angibt, wie sicher sie sich ist – bei manchen Aufgaben übergeht sie die Vorgabe jedoch einfach. Grund kann die Reihenfolge sein, nach der deine Eingaben priorisiert werden. Diese Erfahrung hat Prompt Engineer Susanne Renate Schneider gemacht.
Bestimmte Vorgaben sind gesetzt
Ganz oben stehen dabei die Sicherheitsregeln der Anbieter wie OpenAI oder Anthropic. Kein Prompt hebelt sie aus, außer gezielte Jailbreaks. Das sind Versuche, durch bestimmte Eingaben Sicherheitsvorkehrungen zu umgehen.
Danach folgen im Job die Vorgaben deines Unternehmens, etwa bei Microsoft Copilot. Auch diese umgehst du nicht per Prompt. Nutzt du KI jedoch privat, fällt diese Ebene weg.
Chat überschreibt mitunter Custom Instructions
Erst im nächsten Schritt kommen laut Schneider deine Eingaben. Dabei hat sie selbst eine Hierarchie überrascht: Die Chat-Eingabe wiegt schwerer als deine Custom Instructions. Das sind die Eingaben, die du in den Grundeinstellungen deines Nutzeraccounts hinterlegst. Mit ihnen forderst du ein bestimmtes Verhalten der KI dir gegenüber an. Die Custom Instructions sind demzufolge laut Schneider eher eine Grundhaltung, die einen einzelnen Prompt überlagern kann.
Außerdem können sich Regeln widersprechen, etwa „Antworte kurz“ und „erkläre jeden Schritt ausführlich“. In solchen Fällen kannst du nicht darauf vertrauen, dass ChatGPT oder Claude dich auf diese Eingaben-Kollision hinweisen. Möglicherweise entscheidet der Zufall, welche Eingabe dabei befolgt wird.
Wie du damit umgehen kannst und welche Eingaben in den Custom Instructions recht zuverlässig funktionieren, hörst du in der verlinkten Folge von t3n MeisterPrompter. In der Episode geht es auch darum, wie deine Eingaben durch Dritte manipuliert werden können, wenn du etwa unbekannte Dokumente hochlädst.
Hier hörst du t3n MeisterPrompter – auf allen Plattformen
Den Podcast hörst du über die Podcast-Plattform deiner Wahl. Gib dafür in der Suche „t3n MeisterPrompter“ ein. Alternativ findest du direkte Verlinkungen hier:
Du hast einen Vorschlag für ein Episoden-Thema? Schreib uns unter meisterprompter@t3n.de. Renate erreichst du außerdem über Instagram und Tiktok unter @renate.gpt oder du meldest dich auf Instagram oder Tiktok unter @t3n_magazin.

articles.title: Why you must read Jordan Himelfarb’s New Chess book
articles.text:
Why you must read Jordan Himelfarb’s New Chess book
Discover why Jordan Himelfarb's Interregnum is a compelling read about ambition, rivalry, young chess prodigies and the battle to become world champion.
Chess is often seen as a game of strategy, patience and intellectual ability. But behind every major tournament lies a world of ambition, intense preparation, personal sacrifices and the pressure to perform.
For elite players, becoming world champion is not simply about winning matches; it is about securing a place in the history of the game.
Jordan Himelfarb's Interregnum: Inside the Grueling & Glamorous Battle to Become the Next King of Chess explores this fascinating world through the stories of grandmasters competing for one of the most prestigious titles in sport.
The book follows a defining moment in modern chess: Magnus Carlsen's decision not to defend his world championship title for a fifth time. His announcement created an opportunity for other leading players to pursue a dream that had long seemed difficult to achieve.
Combining sports journalism, character studies and behind-the-scenes storytelling, Interregnum offers a closer look at the people competing at the highest level of chess.
Here is why this book deserves a place on your reading list.
Jordan Himelfarb’s new chess book: What makes it worth reading?
1. It takes you inside the battle for the world chess championship
For years, Magnus Carlsen's dominance made the race for the world championship particularly challenging for other elite players. His decision not to defend his title changed the competitive landscape and opened the door for a new champion.
Interregnum explores what happened next, following the grandmasters who saw an opportunity to achieve their lifelong ambitions. Rather than simply documenting tournament results, Himelfarb examines the competitive environment surrounding the championship race. Readers get a sense of what it means to pursue a title that can define an entire career.
For anyone curious about professional chess, this offers an engaging perspective on the competition beyond the board.
2. It explores the personalities behind the chess pieces
One of the most interesting aspects of Interregnum is its focus on the individuals behind the game. Elite chess players are often recognised for their ratings, tournament victories and playing styles.
However, they also have personal ambitions, insecurities, unconventional personalities and different approaches to handling pressure. Himelfarb explores the lives and mindsets of these grandmasters, showing how their backgrounds and experiences influence their journeys.
The book also examines the contrast between established players whose opportunities may be running out and younger prodigies determined to make their mark.
This makes the story about much more than chess. It becomes a study of ambition, competition and human psychology.
3. It introduces readers to the changing world of chess
Chess has experienced a remarkable resurgence in recent years, attracting new audiences through online platforms, streaming and digital communities. Interregnum explores this changing landscape, including the influence of younger, internet-savvy players who are reshaping how the game is experienced and discussed.
The book captures the contrast between chess's centuries-old traditions and the modern personalities bringing fresh energy to the sport.
For readers who have followed the growing popularity of online chess, this offers an opportunity to understand the people and developments behind that transformation.
It also highlights how an ancient intellectual pursuit continues to find new audiences in a digitally connected world.
4. You don't need to be a chess expert to enjoy it
One reason people hesitate to pick up books about chess is the assumption that they need to understand complicated strategies, openings and technical terminology.
However, Interregnum is not designed as a traditional chess instruction manual. According to the book's description, it combines elements of a sports chronicle, character study and celebration of the game.
Its storytelling focuses on the personalities, ambitions and rivalries that make the championship race compelling.
The book also uses technical details without overwhelming readers with chess terminology. As highlighted in reviews by The New Yorker and Deccan Herald, its accessibility makes it appealing even to those unfamiliar with the finer details of competitive chess.
You can therefore enjoy the human stories and competitive drama without being an experienced player.
5. It shows the psychological side of competition
Competing at the highest level requires more than intelligence or technical preparation. Players must also manage expectations, anxiety, setbacks and the pressure of performing when the stakes are high.
Interregnum explores these emotional dimensions through the experiences of grandmasters pursuing the world championship.
The contrast between experienced competitors and young prodigies also raises interesting questions about timing, opportunity and ambition. Some players are racing against time, while others are only beginning their journeys.
These experiences make the book relatable beyond professional chess. Anyone pursuing a demanding personal or professional goal can recognise the tension between ambition, uncertainty and the desire to succeed.
About the Author: Jordan Himelfarb
Jordan Himelfarb is a managing editor at the Toronto Star, one of North America's major newspapers. He oversees coverage across politics, national and international affairs, and opinion.
Before becoming managing editor, he served as the newspaper's politics editor and deputy editorial page editor. He has also received three National Newspaper Award nominations, recognising his work in journalism and editing.
Interestingly, Himelfarb was previously a competitive Scrabble player before turning his attention to chess and contract bridge.
His experience in journalism and his interest in intellectually demanding games come together in Interregnum, which approaches chess through reporting, observation and character-driven storytelling.
Final thoughts
Interregnum: Inside the Grueling & Glamorous Battle to Become the Next King of Chess offers a different way to experience the world of competitive chess. Instead of focusing exclusively on moves, strategies and tournament outcomes, Jordan Himelfarb explores the people, personalities and ambitions shaping the modern game.
Whether you follow international chess, enjoy sports journalism or simply appreciate stories about individuals pursuing extraordinary goals, this book offers an engaging reading experience.
Its biggest appeal lies in showing that behind every intellectual battle is a human story filled with ambition, uncertainty, rivalry and the desire to leave a lasting legacy.

articles.title: Todoist confirms 6% of customers' details were stolen in data breach
articles.text:
Task management app Todoist said on Tuesday that a hacker gained access to its production systems and stole customer data, including email IDs, password hashes, and account creation dates. The company said around 6% of its customers were affected and blamed stolen credentials for the breach.
Todoist said the attacker used stolen credentials to access the company’s version control system and source code between November 22 and 23. The hacker then changed employee access controls and reached the app’s cloud infrastructure via an employee’s work account.
The hacker downloaded credentials of early Todoist users whose passwords were stored using an older hashing method, but didn’t change any source code, the company said. Todoist said it has blocked the attack path and reset passwords as a mitigation step, as well as disabled the Todoist for Outlook email add-on.
For a small number of people, about 0.001% of its userbase, the hacker also searched through tasks, comments, and attachment names to look for credentials for other services, like API keys and access tokens.
The hacker also pulled Todoist API tokens and Slack integration tokens, and looked for emails, addresses, and attachment file names through the Todoist for Outlook extension if it was connected to accounts and had permission to read emails.
The company said it has sent a notice to those affected and asked them to reset their credentials and change their login details in other places with the same password. The company is asking users to also update API tokens, reconnect integrations, and revoke or replace any access keys, recovery phrases, or credentials they had stored in Todoist comments.
Todoist said it has also reset its internal access structure and how remote command execution works in its cloud environment to prevent such incidents in the future.
Todoist’s founder and CEO Amir Salihefendić apologized to users about the incident on X, and said the company will take a closer look at why it happened.
The to-do app’s data breach is the latest in a burgeoning list of data breaches in which hackers use stolen credentials to access data and systems at enterprises. So far this year, we’ve seen several companies fall victim to this form of attack, including Uber and Klue.

articles.title: Lo nuevo de BYD se llama Shark y es una pick-up híbrida con la mayor batería de su segmento
articles.text:
BYD sigue sus lanzamientos en la recta final del año. Si la semana pasada era el nuevo Seal U 2027, ahora es el turno de Shark, que llega con un nuevo modelo de tipo pick-up a un precio muy interesante y con la tecnología de hibridación de la compañía que tanto se ha aclamado.
El nuevo BYD Shark llega con una carrocería de doble cabina y unos impresionantes 5,46 metros, y, como decimos, lo hace con la tecnología DMO (Dual Mode Off-road) con hasta 90 km de autonomía 100% eléctrica (675 km en combinada) y grandes capacidades todoterreno con unos impresionantes 436 CV y 650 Nm de par. Una potencia que le permite, pese a su peso y tamaño, acelerar de 0 a 100 en solo 5,7 segundos y ganándose por el camino las 5 estrellas de Euro NCAP.
BYD Shark: dos motores eléctricos y una gran autonomía combinada
En su apartado de hibridación, cuenta con un motor de gasolina turboalimentado de 1,5 litros y cuatro cilindros (de 150 CV y 240 Nm), usado principalmente como generador de electricidad para los motores eléctricos y la carga de la batería, aunque también puede generar propulsión; y dos motores eléctricos: uno delantero de 231 CV (170 kW) y 310 Nm, y otro trasero de 204 CV (150 kW) y 340 Nm.
Complementa el conjunto una batería de tipo Blade Battery de 32,2 kWh, según BYD la de mayor capacidad del segmento pick-up en Europa, integrada en un chasis de largueros y travesaños, ya que usa la tecnología CTC (Cell-to-Chassis) y, como decíamos, homologa una autonomía eléctrica en ciclo combinado de 90 km y alrededor de 110 km en ciclo urbano y una autonomía combinada de 675 km. Esto supone unos consumos ponderados de 3,5 l/100 km² y de 9,6 l/100km a nivel mínimo de carga. Respecto a su carga, admite corriente alterna trifásica de 11 kW, con unos tiempos de 3,2 horas del 15% al 100%, y carga rápida en corriente continua de hasta 55 kW: sobre 21 minutos del 30% al 80%.
Respecto a su apuesta tecnológica en el interior, integra una pantalla digital para la instrumentación de 10,25” (26 cm), un Head-Up Display y una pantalla central para el sistema de infoentretenimiento de 15,6”.
Un detalle interesante de este BYD Shark es que incorpora la función Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) de 6 kW, que permite alimentar dispositivos eléctricos externos, bien para el trabajo o para el ocio en acampada, mediante dos tomas de corriente.
BYD Shark, precio y disponibilidad
¿Y su precio? Llega en una única versión llamada Design, que parte desde los 41.521 euros sin IVA (50.240 euros IVA incluido) y cuenta con una garantía oficial de 6 años o 150.000 km para el coche y de 8 años o 250.000 km para la Blade Battery. Y ya está disponible en los concesionarios de BYD.

Proton VPN Plus
Proton VPN es la mejor forma de navegar seguro por internet

Es decir, que podemos instalarla tanto en nuestro móvil como en nuestro portátil, pero también podemos llegar a tenerla instalada en dispositivos de nuestra pareja, para que ella también navegue segura.

El servicio cuenta con un total de 22.000 servidores repartidos a lo largo de 149 países, en 197 localizaciones diferentes. Esto, además de garantizarnos estabilidad y velocidad (hasta 10 Gbps), también nos permitirá acceder a los catálogos de servicios como Disney+, Netflix o DAZN si estamos fuera de España.
También es importante destacar la función NetShield. Prácticamente todo el mundo está de acuerdo en que navegar con publicidad acaba llegando a ser desesperante en según qué sitios. Esta función permite bloquearlos tanto a ellos como a los rastreadores y al malware de las páginas web. Además, es capaz de soportar los protocolos de P2P/Bitorrent.
Como podemos ver, se trata de un servicio realmente completo. Pero si aun así buscamos algo más, Proton también tiene rebajado su plan Proton Unlimited. Por apenas 6,49 euros al mes, además de la VPN, nos ofrece acceso a servicios como Proton Mail, Proton Pass o Proton Drive con un total de 500 GB de almacenamiento y Proton Docs y Sheets. Esto nos permitirá poder contar con hasta 15 direcciones de correo diferentes, etiquetas y carpetas ilimintadas y todas las funciones de pago de Proton Calendar. Es la opción perfecta para el que busque la suscripción más completa posible, y al mismo tiempo quiera una alternativa a los servicios de Google.

articles.title: 6 Best Affordable WordPress Hosts for Small WooCommerce Stores
articles.text:
A store with only a few orders a day can still lose an afternoon of work when a plugin update goes wrong. Restoring yesterday’s backup may bring the site back, while leaving today’s orders out of the restored database. Low traffic does not make that recovery problem disappear.
Small stores can find affordable hosting with useful recovery tools, but the costs and restore controls vary. Prices are in United States dollars. Taxes, optional extras and later domain renewals cost more.
Check checkout separately from product pages
Low-cost WooCommerce hosting needs to cover both shopping and the work of putting a store back together. Product pages can often use cached copies [1]. Carts, customer accounts and checkout [2] need fresh data as people shop. A fast catalog page alone says little about how checkout will behave. A useful test follows a customer through adding an item to the cart. It should include changing the amount, using a discount and paying for the order. That work should use the store’s actual plugins and a test payment method. Any plan can look right in a feature list while the store’s mix of plugins still needs work.
1. SiteGround GrowBig for staging and planned changes
SiteGround [3] GrowBig suits a small store whose owner expects to change plugins, layouts or payment settings often. Its staging tool gives the owner a place to test those changes before they reach the live site. On-demand backups also let the owner save a copy before a planned update. The store can keep that copy as well as its scheduled backups.
GrowBig costs $4.99 a month for the first 12 months, paid in advance, or $59.88 for that term. It renews at $29.99 a month, or $359.88 for a year at that rate. The owner needs to budget for that later bill from the start. A low first-year price does not make the plan cheap in later years.
The plan includes 50 gigabytes of storage, managed WordPress updates, caching, email and migration. StartUp costs less and can host a single small store, but GrowBig is the more useful comparison when staging and on-demand backups matter. The buyer should not assume StartUp has those tools just because both plans run WordPress.
Staging needs a careful store workflow. A test copy can fall out of date as live orders arrive. Replacing the live database with an older staging database can erase changes made by customers. The owner should decide which files or settings to move before making the changes live.
GrowBig still needs a checkout test with the store’s theme, payment method and plugins. Before upgrading, check whether the account can handle those requests well. The number of product pages alone will not answer that question.
2. GreenGeeks Premium for a small store with restore controls
GreenGeeks [4] offers Premium for busy websites and small stores. It includes 100 gigabytes of storage, LiteSpeed optimization and caching, automatic WordPress updates, daily backups and migration, subject to the migration terms. Live chat and ticket support are open around the clock.
The first-term rate is $8.95 a month with 12 months paid in advance. That makes the first hosting term $107.40. The plan then renews at $30.95 a month, or $371.40 for a year at that rate. A store looking at Premium needs to budget for that later bill as well as the first year.
Premium and Pro include on-demand backup and restore features. Lite uses a different restore process. The cheapest plan does not offer the same way to get a site back. For a store, the choice affects who can start a restore and how the work gets done.
Daily backups can still leave recent orders outside the available recovery point. Before opening the store, its owner should check how to restore an older site and keep newer order records. Caching also needs to respect carts and checkout. Premium is aimed at small stores, but that does not prove how fast checkout will be or how many sales it can handle.
3. Hostinger Unlimited when a long commitment fits the budget
Hostinger Unlimited offers daily backups and 50 gigabytes of storage, while the cheaper Premium plan has weekly backups. Unlimited is the more useful plan to compare for a store that changes throughout the week. With a weekly backup, the saved site can be much further out of date than the store’s records.
The advertised rate works out to $3.49 a month. To get it, the buyer must pay $167.52 up front for 48 months. That pays for the first four years of hosting, rather than just one year at a low price. The renewal rate shown is $16.99 a month for the same term. An owner should weigh that payment against how long the store may last and how much it may grow.
The low rate can suit a new shop that expects to use WordPress for several years. It is less useful when the owner is still testing the sales model or may need to move the store soon. A low rate does not remove the cost of paying early for years the store may never use.
Daily backups still need a restore plan. The buyer should check how to restore Unlimited before relying on its backups. That means knowing which saved copies are kept and what happens to recent orders. A saved copy helps only when the person in charge of the store knows how to use it. The hosting mailboxes are also free for only the first year. A store that uses them to email customers needs to budget for that later cost.
4. Bluehost eCommerce Essentials for included store tools
Bluehost’s eCommerce Essentials plan installs WooCommerce for the owner and includes store tools. It may be worth the cost when those tools replace extensions the store would have to buy on their own. A store that needs only a basic catalog and checkout should compare the package with the lower WordPress tiers before paying for the larger bundle.
The current offer is $14.99 a month for 36 months. The service costs $539.64 for that term. Renewal is listed at $21.99 a month. That is more to pay up front than the plans with a one-year term here, even if the monthly rate seems within budget. The value depends on which tools the shop will use.
The plan includes 100 gigabytes of storage, managed WordPress updates, a website security certificate, a content delivery network and a migration tool. These features help run the site, but its scheduled backups are weekly. A store with daily orders needs to decide whether to pay for an extra backup service. That cost needs to be part of the plan comparison.
The first upgrade may therefore be a recovery service rather than a larger hosting plan. Buying more storage would not close a gap between backup points. Before choosing the plan, the owner should price the extensions it replaces. Then add the cost of any backup or order-recovery service the store still needs. The business email offer is a trial, so staff mail may cost more once it ends.
5. DreamHost Launch for a low-cost starting account
A small WooCommerce store with modest needs can use DreamHost’s Web Hosting Launch plan, which supports WordPress. The annual offer costs $2.89 a month, with $34.68 paid for the first year. It renews at $10.99 a month. The first-year cost is easy to compare with other one-year offers. There is no need to divide a four-year payment to work out a price for one year.
Launch includes 25 gigabytes of storage, daily automated backups, a website security certificate and a first-year domain offer. Its limit of 25 websites does not mean it can host 25 equally busy stores. The account still has to do the work those sites need.
DreamHost also gives an estimate of how many visits a month the plan can serve. For a store, that estimate cannot replace a checkout test. Customers who search products, log in and place orders create a different workload from visitors reading cached pages. A store can need more resources before it reaches that broad visit estimate.
Launch is most useful here as a modest initial hosting purchase. Before changing a live store, the owner should check how long backups are kept and how to restore them. They should also check whether they need a separate staging tool. Included email lasts only for a 3-month trial, so the owner needs to budget for customer-service mail after that.
6. HostArmada Start Dock for a single-store account
HostArmada [5] Start Dock offers a single website with 15 gigabytes of storage and 7 daily backup copies, with free restores. An owner can use that history to judge how far back a restore could go. A fault discovered several days after an update may require an older copy, even when the website appeared to work immediately afterward.
The first 12 months cost $2.15 a month, for a first-year service total of $25.80. It renews at $11.95 a month, or $143.40 for a year at that rate. The account also includes cPanel and one website migration, with phone, chat and ticket support available around the clock.
The higher Web Warp and Speed Reaper tiers retain 14 and 21 daily backup copies respectively. Those older copies may matter more than extra storage when the store needs to fix a fault found days later. They still do not provide a fresh copy after every order.
Start Dock offers a low-cost account for one store with a set backup history. Before paying, the owner should check how to request a restore and how long it may take. They also need to know how to keep order records created after the chosen backup.
Choose the recovery window before choosing the plan
The store owner should decide how much missing order history the business could piece back together. A shop with a few manual orders may accept a daily backup and written steps for matching up its records. A shop with orders throughout the day may need database backups more often, or a service that records each change as it happens.
That requirement should become a test before launch. On a test copy, the person responsible for the store can create a sample order, take a backup, create another order and then rehearse the recovery. The exercise should show which records return, which disappear and what evidence remains with the payment provider. A successful page restore alone does not answer those questions.
The owner should also write down who can access backups, who contacts support and who decides when checkout can reopen. Once those steps are clear, the owner can compare plans with those needs in mind. The affordable plan is the one that fits the store’s workload and recovery needs at its ongoing cost, including any extra service needed to protect recent orders.

articles.title: I tested Philips Hue Essential and White & Color Ambiance smart light bulbs side-by-side — and this is the one I'd choose for my home
articles.text:
If you're shopping for Philips Hue lights this Black Friday, you'll notice there are two main types: the classic Philips Hue series, in their distinctive black and purple boxes, and Hue Essential, which are packaged in light blue. So what's the difference, and which should you choose?
Philips Hue Essential bulbs are a more affordable version of the company's standard smart lights, and they perform incredibly well considering they're less than half the price. There are a few limitations, though. For example, Philips Hue Essential bulbs offer a maximum brightness of 806 lumens, whereas standard Philips Hue White & Color Ambiance bulbs range from 800 to 1,600 lumens.
In most other respects, the two are very similar, and considering the huge difference in price, I'd recommend the Hue Essential series in most situations. Comparing the two side-by-side, there are only a couple of differences to be aware of.
US deals
If you want to expand your Philips Hue setup into more rooms without taking out a second mortgage, this is the Black Friday deal for you. Philips Hue Essential bulbs are excellent, work with all other Huge devices, and with this offer they're less than $11 each.
Knocked down to almost half price, there's a tempting $72 saving to be had on these white and color smart lightbulbs thanks to this Black Friday deal. That's just over $25 per bulb.
UK deals
This Black Friday, there's £23 to be saved on this four-pack of E27 Hue Essential bulbs. Whether a treat for yourself or a gift for someone else, at just over £10 each, they're a smart buy.
With 30% off, this is a respectable Black Friday discount courtesy of John Lewis, and better than Amazon's current offerings, but at just a whisker over £30, each of these bulbs is three times the price of its Hue Essential counterpart.
Responsiveness
To see how the two would compare, I set up a pair of lamps – one with a Philips Hue Essential bulb, and the other with an 800-lumen Philips Hue White & Color Ambiance bulb. I added them to the same room in the Philips Hue app, which would enable me to control them simultaneously, and directly compare and contrast their output.
During most of the tests I ran, it was difficult to spot any difference between the two. Both were equally responsive, and produced colors that were identical to my naked eye when I switched between scenes. According to Signify (the company behind the Philips Hue brand), Essential bulbs use different color-matching technology to regular Hue lights; but personally, I had a hard time telling the difference.
Having said that, I did notice a dark band at the top of the Essential bulb, which wasn't present on the premium bulb. This was most apparent with purple and blue light. Note that it isn't something you'll notice if you're using the bulb in a ceiling light or table lamp, and is unlikely to be a deal-breaker unless you're exceptionally picky.
Brightness
The two were equally bright (as expected), although if I'd used a higher-output White & Color Ambiance bulb, then it would have been appreciably brighter.
However, there's one important difference that you should be aware of, particularly if you're looking for smart bulbs that will produce a natural-looking sunrise and sunset to help you wake up feeling refreshed, or to create subtle ambient lighting in your living room.
With both bulbs dialled down to their dimmest setting, the Hue Essential bulb was much brighter than the more expensive White & Color Ambiance model, as you can see in the photo below. That's because the Hue Essential bulb can only be dimmed to 2% of its maximum brightness, whereas the regular bulb can drop to just 0.2%.
Color temperature
I also found that the Essential bulb tended to show a slightly warmer cast, due to its narrower white light spectrum (2,200–6,500K compared to 1,000-20,00K for a regular Hue bulb). Depending on your preferred light temperature, the difference could be apparent if you use the two different types of bulbs in close proximity,
I wouldn't mix and match regular Hue and Hue Essential bulbs within the same room. However, they're an excellent option for those wanting to setup a Philips Hue system but have previously been intimidated by the price. They're also great if you're looking to extend your existing system to more rooms in your home, without splashing too much cash.
Price
The Philips Hue Essential range is designed to be an accessible entry point into the world of smart lighting, with the bulbs coming in at a much cheaper price than standard Philips Hue ones.
One Philips Hue Essential bulb (either screw or bayonet) costs $24.99 / £19.99 (about AU$40) at full price. If you want several, you can save money by opting for a multipack. A twin-pack costs $44.99 / £32.99 (about AU$70), and a four-pack comes in at $59.99 / £49.99 (about AU$90).
During Black Friday, those prices drop substantially, and you can get Hue Essential bulbs for around $10 / £11 each if you buy them in a multipack.
For comparison, a twin-pack of regular 800-lumen Philips Hue White & Color Ambiance bulbs costs $98.99 / £84.99 / AU$149.25, and a four-pack is $185.99 / £169.99 / AU$290.50. That's the starting price for a maximum brightness of 800 lumens; brighter bulbs cost even more.
These bulbs also get price cuts for Black Friday, and during the sale period you can expect to pay around $25 / £30 each when you pick up a multi-pack.
