articles.title: Sonda da NASA usará gravidade da Terra para acelerar viagem até lua Europa
articles.text:
A caminho de Europa, uma das luas de Júpiter, a sonda Europa Clipper fará passagem próxima da Terra em 3 de dezembro. O encontro vai ajudar a nave a ajustar sua trajetória e ganhar velocidade com a ajuda da gravidade do nosso planeta. A manobra também permitirá que a equipe da missão teste os instrumentos científicos que serão usados para investigar o mundo gelado.
Lançada pela NASA, a Europa Clipper é a maior espaçonave enviada pela agência para uma missão no espaço profundo. Durante o sobrevoo, ela passará a aproximadamente 3.140 a 3.450 quilômetros da superfície terrestre. A maior aproximação está prevista para as 17h14 (horário de Brasília), sobre uma região a oeste da África.
A sonda pesa cerca de seis toneladas e percorre jornada de aproximadamente 2,9 bilhões de quilômetros até o sistema de Júpiter. A expectativa é que ela comece a orbitar o planeta gigante em abril de 2030.
Gravidade da Terra vai impulsionar a sonda
- A passagem faz parte de manobra conhecida como assistência gravitacional. Nesse tipo de operação, uma espaçonave aproveita o movimento orbital e a atração gravitacional de um planeta ou lua para alterar sua velocidade e trajetória;
- No caso da Europa Clipper, a gravidade terrestre ajudará a aumentar sua velocidade e modificar um pouco o caminho até Júpiter;
- Em março de 2025, a nave já havia realizado uma manobra semelhante em Marte, passando a cerca de 884 quilômetros da superfície do Planeta Vermelho. Na ocasião, a atração gravitacional marciana ajudou a reduzir sua velocidade e reorganizar sua órbita ao redor do Sol;
- “Estamos entrando no campo gravitacional da Terra, seguindo sua curva e saindo novamente”, explicou ao Phys.org Robert Pappalardo, cientista do projeto Europa Clipper no Laboratório de Propulsão a Jato (JPL, na sigla em inglês), da NASA. Segundo ele, a gravidade do planeta puxa a espaçonave e altera tanto sua trajetória quanto sua velocidade.
Sobrevoo também servirá para testar instrumentos
Além de economizar combustível e ajustar o percurso, a passagem pela Terra será oportunidade para calibrar os nove instrumentos científicos da Europa Clipper. Todos serão ligados e coletarão dados durante o encontro.
As equipes vão comparar as medições feitas pela sonda com informações já conhecidas sobre a Terra. A ideia é identificar possíveis ajustes antes que a nave chegue ao destino.
Um dos equipamentos que receberá atenção especial é o magnetômetro, responsável por estudar a interação entre o campo magnético de Júpiter e Europa. As medições poderão ajudar a confirmar a existência do oceano que, segundo as evidências científicas, está escondido sob a crosta congelada da lua.
Outro instrumento, o E-THEMIS, fará observações da Terra em infravermelho a cada oito horas durante a aproximação. Em Europa, ele será usado para identificar regiões mais quentes, que podem indicar locais onde a água esteja mais próxima da superfície ou até tenha sido expelida para o exterior.
Já o espectrógrafo ultravioleta Europa-UVS terá seus dados comparados com observações feitas pela missão Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), da NASA. A sonda também apontará um de seus instrumentos para estudar a geocoroa terrestre, a região mais externa da atmosfera, onde átomos escapam para o espaço.
O que a NASA pretende descobrir em Europa?
Quando chegar ao sistema de Júpiter, a Europa Clipper usará a gravidade de Ganimedes, outra lua do planeta, para desacelerar e ser capturada pela gravidade do gigante gasoso.
Depois disso, fará uma série de sobrevoos por Europa para investigar a espessura de sua camada de gelo, sua composição e suas características geológicas.
O principal interesse científico está no oceano que pode existir sob a superfície congelada. A missão não foi projetada para detectar vida diretamente, mas vai investigar se Europa reúne ingredientes que poderiam permitir a existência de organismos.
Os dados coletados ajudarão os cientistas a entender melhor as condições de habitabilidade em mundos além da Terra.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: How Much Does Coram AI Cost? Pricing, Licences and What's Included
articles.text:
If you’ve been looking at AI security camera platforms, you’ve probably noticed Coram AI doesn’t put a price on its website. So how much does it actually cost?
Here’s the short answer. Coram AI doesn’t publish a price list. Its pricing is quote-based and depends on three things: how many locations you have, the type of cameras you’re using, and how many days of video you want to keep. Every order includes an on-site appliance called Coram Point, which you buy upfront and own, plus a per-camera software licence on a one, three, five or 10-year term.
That might sound vague, but the way the price is built is actually quite clear. Here’s what goes into a Coram quote, what you get for it and what costs extra.
Why Coram doesn’t publish a price
Coram is an AI physical security platform used by schools, healthcare groups, warehouses and multi-site businesses. Because no two sites are the same, Coram prices each deployment based on its real requirements rather than a one-size-fits-all plan.
The three inputs are simple. The number of locations decides how many Coram Point appliances you need. The type of camera affects how many video feeds each appliance has to handle. And the days of storage you need decides how much recording capacity goes on site. Coram says that once its sales team has those three details, it can come back with a price quickly.
Quotes are in US dollars, so Australian buyers should factor in the exchange rate on the day.
What you’re actually paying for
A Coram quote has two main parts.
The Coram Point appliance. This is the on-site box that records your video locally and runs the AI, while a cloud dashboard lets you view and manage every location from a browser or the mobile app. It’s a one-time purchase, and you own it. There’s no leasing.
Coram Point comes in several sizes, so the model on your quote depends on how many cameras each site has and how long you need to keep footage:
| Coram Point model | Cameras (video feeds) | Video storage | 
| CP-I-1 | 4 | 30 days | 
| CP-M-1 | 8 | 30, 60 or 90 days | 
| CP-S-1 | 16 | 30, 60 or 90 days | 
| CP-E-1 | 24 | 30, 60 or 90 days | 
| CP-E-2 | 32 | Up to 365 days | 
| CP-X-1 | 64 | Up to 365 days | 
| CP-Y-1 | 80 | Varies; check with Coram | 
You can see the full range on Coram’s Coram Point AI NVR page.
The per-camera licence. This is the recurring part. Each camera connected to the system needs a video licence, and you choose a term of one, three, five or 10 years. The licence count is what grows as you add cameras, so it’s the number to watch over time.
What’s included in the licence
The licence covers more than access to the software. According to Coram, it includes:
- The Coram cloud dashboard, with unlimited user seats
- 24/7 online support
- Software updates for the length of the term
- A 100 per cent hardware warranty during the licence period
Unlimited users is worth noting. Some platforms charge per user, which adds up quickly when security staff, managers and IT all need access.
Coram also lists its security credentials alongside its pricing, including SOC 2 Type II, multi-factor authentication and single sign-on, role-based access, audit logs and data encryption.
What costs extra
Not everything sits inside the standard video licence, so it’s worth asking about these on any quote:
- Safety alerts. Firearm detection, slip-and-fall and PPE alerts are separate licences.
- Continuous cloud backup. Video is stored on the Coram Point by default. Backing everything up to the cloud continuously is a separate paid option.
- Installation. If a partner installs the system, their labour will be on top of the Coram quote.
- Other products. Access control, visitor management and emergency management are part of the same platform but are priced on their own lines.
One more detail: a camera that’s offline still uses its licence, so it pays to keep your camera list tidy.
Can you use the cameras you already have?
This is where Coram’s pricing model differs most from many cloud camera systems. Coram works with existing IP cameras, as long as they support the ONVIF standard and stream video in H.264 or H.265. If your cameras qualify, you don’t need to buy new ones, which can take a big chunk out of the upfront cost.
Older analog, coax and MPEG-only cameras aren’t supported, so check your camera models before you ask for a quote.
For businesses that don’t have IP cameras at all, Coram offers 5MP NDAA-compliant cameras free with the software subscription.
What happens if you stop paying?
Ongoing licences are becoming a familiar story across tech, which is why so many buyers now look for alternatives that don’t require ongoing subscriptions. With security cameras, the bigger question is what you’re left with if you stop.
With Coram, customers who don’t renew keep the Coram Point and any cameras Coram supplied. Coram says it never disables the cameras’ RTSP video streams, so those cameras can be connected to another recording system.
How does Coram’s pricing compare?
Some competitors do publish their prices, which helps put Coram’s model in context.
Verkada, for example, publishes its camera prices and charges a separate licence for every camera. Its one-year camera licence is listed at $249 at 2026 US list price, and its cameras only work with Verkada’s own platform.
Rhombus also publishes pricing, listing its Professional camera licence at US$149 per camera per year on top of the cost of its own cameras.
Coram’s main difference isn’t the licence itself. It’s that you can often keep the cameras you already own and you own the on-site hardware outright. Whether that works out cheaper depends on your camera fleet, so the only fair comparison is to get quotes for the same number of cameras, sites and storage days.
Why the on-site appliance matters
Because Coram records video on site, cameras keep recording even if your internet connection drops. Cloud dashboards are convenient, but as the global IT outage showed, relying entirely on remote systems has risks. Keeping the recording local is part of what you’re paying for with Coram Point.
It’s also why Coram sits in a different category from the home security cameras most of us know. A consumer camera like the one in our Arlo Essential Pan Tilt review is built for a home. Coram is built for organisations managing dozens or hundreds of cameras across multiple sites.
How to get an accurate Coram quote
To get a quote quickly, have these ready:
- The number of sites you need to cover
- How many cameras you have, and their make and model
- How many days of footage you need to keep
- Any extras you want, such as access control, safety alerts or cloud backup
Ask for every item as a separate line, and check the licence term against the yearly cost so you can compare it fairly with other quotes.
Common questions
Does Coram AI publish its pricing?
No. Coram AI pricing is by quote, based on the number of locations, the type of cameras and the days of storage you need.
How long are Coram licences?
Coram sells per-camera video licences on one, three, five or 10-year terms.
Do I need to buy new cameras for Coram?
Not usually. Coram works with existing ONVIF IP cameras that stream in H.264 or H.265. Customers without IP cameras can get free 5MP cameras with the subscription.
Is Coram AI available in Australia?
Coram’s quote form accepts enquiries from Australia and New Zealand. Check with Coram about local availability, installation partners and support for your sites. Some features, such as Coram’s Video Alarms service, are currently available only in the US.
The bottom line
Coram AI doesn’t have a sticker price, but its pricing isn’t a mystery either. You pay once for a Coram Point you own, then a per-camera licence for the term you choose, with extras like safety alerts and cloud backup on top. If you already have compatible IP cameras, that can make Coram a sensible way to add AI search and alerts without starting again from scratch. The best way to find out is to get a quote with your real numbers and compare it line by line.

articles.title: Cyberattaques : l’étude 2026 révèle la vulnérabilité des collectivités locales
articles.text:
Dans près de six communes de moins de 25 000 habitants sur dix, les élus et les agents disent ne pas être prêts à affronter une cyberattaque, contre 54 % en 2024. Et parmi les rares mairies qui se disent prêtes, une sur quatre seulement a prévu comment relancer ses services après une attaque.
En avril 2024, un pirate est entré dans le réseau de la mairie de Gravelines, dans le Nord. Un robot avait d'abord essayé des milliers d'identifiants sur l'accès à distance prévu pour le télétravail, jusqu'à trouver le bon, et le pirate a ensuite désactivé les antivirus pour installer le rançongiciel LockBit. Grâce à son service informatique de dix personnes, la ville de 12 000 habitants a évité le pire, mais l'attaque lui a coûté 50 000 euros, selon la Banque des Territoires. Dans près des trois quarts des communes de moins de 25 000 habitants, la mairie emploie moins de dix agents en tout, soit moins que le seul service informatique de Gravelines, selon un baromètre sur la cybersécurité des collectivités (Sondage OpinionWay pour Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr). Depuis 2024, davantage d'élus et d'agents mesurent le danger, mais ils ont rarement les moyens de préparer leur commune à une attaque.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Une mairie prête sur quatre seulement a prévu un plan de reprise
Sur les 2 830 élus et agents interrogés entre la fin août et la fin septembre, 13 % estiment leur commune suffisamment préparée. Parmi eux, 24 % disposent d'un plan de reprise ou de continuité d'activité, c'est-à-dire d'une procédure écrite pour faire tourner la mairie pendant l'attaque, puis relancer ses services. Les autres répondent non (44 %) ou l'ignorent (32 %).
Si vous habitez l'une de ces communes, et c'est le cas de deux Français sur trois, une attaque peut d'abord vous priver des services de votre mairie. Au cours des douze derniers mois, 9 % des communes interrogées ont subi au moins un incident de sécurité informatique, et 37 % des victimes ont dû interrompre leurs activités et leurs services. Et 19 % des répondants ignorent si leur commune a été attaquée. « Près d'1 collectivité sur 3 a déjà été victime ou ne le sait pas », résume Jérôme Notin, directeur général de Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr.
Les mairies attaquées savent mieux qu'en 2024 d'où venait le coup. Au total, 65 % d'entre elles connaissent au moins une cause de l'incident, soit dix points de plus. L'hameçonnage revient dans 38 % des cas, et une faille non corrigée dans 15 % des cas.
Les appareils personnels servent de plus en plus au travail de la mairie. C'est le cas dans 65 % des communes, contre 58 % en 2024, et il s'agit presque toujours d'un téléphone portable (93 %). Près d'une commune sur deux écrit en outre à ses habitants depuis une messagerie grand public, de type Gmail ou Orange, et non depuis une adresse au nom de la commune.
La plupart des communes consacrent moins de 1 000 euros par an à leur sécurité
L'enquête a eu lieu quelques mois après les municipales de mars 2026, et 71 % des répondants travaillent avec une équipe municipale nouvelle ou différente. Pour 29 % d'entre eux, les élus entament leur premier mandat. Ces équipes héritent de budgets très serrés. Deux communes sur trois dépensent moins de 5 000 euros par an pour toute leur informatique, photocopieur compris, et parmi les communes qui connaissent ce budget, 71 % consacrent moins de 1 000 euros à la sécurité.
Pour 44 % des répondants, la hausse des cyberattaques n'a pas pesé sur les décisions budgétaires de leur commune, contre 38 % qui disent l'inverse. Et parmi les communes qui connaissent leur budget informatique, seules 16 % prévoient d'augmenter leur budget de sécurité l'an prochain, contre 10 % en 2024.
Les répondants citent d'abord le manque de connaissances (46 %), devant le manque d'argent (42 %). Près de sept répondants sur dix ne savent pas dire si les offres de sécurité vendues sur le marché répondent aux besoins de leur commune. Dans 64 % des cas, la mairie se tourne vers son prestataire informatique, mais 83 % des élus et agents concernés ignorent s'il détient le label ExpertCyber, délivré par Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr aux prestataires spécialisés, ou un visa de sécurité de l'ANSSI.
Pour aider les communes rurales, Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr et l'Association des maires de France (AMF) publient un mémento, moins de trois mois après le piratage de l'AMF. Le pirate affirme avoir volé près de 114 000 entrées, avec les noms, les adresses e-mail et les fonctions de maires, de conseillers municipaux et d'agents, et l'association a confirmé l'attaque. Le mémento contient les mesures prioritaires à prendre et la marche à suivre en cas d'attaque, avec les services à contacter. Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr met aussi en avant le 17Cyber, le guichet en ligne d'aide aux victimes. Mais dans 11 % des communes, personne ne gère la sécurité informatique, et 7 % des répondants ne savent pas comment elle est organisée.

articles.title: 5 Lessons from Traitor in the House by Shubha Menon
articles.text:
5 Lessons from Traitor in the House by Shubha Menon
Explore five powerful lessons from Shubha Menon's Traitor in the House, a memoir about mental health, family trauma, caregiving and resilience.
Traitor in the House: My Bipolar Life by Shubha Menon is a deeply personal memoir about growing up in a family affected by bipolar disorder. Through experiences of childhood trauma, caregiving, denial and eventual diagnosis, Menon explores how untreated mental illness can shape relationships and affect generations.
The book moves beyond the experiences of one individual to examine the emotional realities of families living with mental health challenges. It also explores how understanding, acceptance and self-awareness can help people confront painful experiences.
5 Meaningful lessons from Traitor in the House by Shubha Menon
1. Mental illness should be understood, not judged
One of the most important lessons from the memoir is that mental illness should never be treated as a personal failure or a character flaw. Through her mother's experiences with bipolar disorder, Menon shows how a lack of awareness and understanding can make an already difficult situation more painful for an entire family.
The book highlights the importance of recognising mental health conditions, seeking professional help and replacing judgement with compassion.
Lesson: Understanding someone's struggles is the first step towards treating them with empathy rather than blame.
2. Childhood experiences can shape adult life
The experiences we have during childhood can influence how we think, behave and build relationships as adults. Menon reflects on growing up in an unpredictable family environment and how those experiences affected her sense of safety and emotional well-being.
The memoir demonstrates that painful childhood memories do not simply disappear with age. They can influence how people respond to stress, relationships and difficult situations later in life.
Lesson: Acknowledging childhood trauma is important because healing often begins with understanding how the past has shaped the present.
3. Unaddressed trauma can pass through generations
The book explores how the effects of trauma can extend beyond one individual and influence future generations. Menon's family history reveals how unresolved emotional pain, untreated mental illness and unhealthy coping patterns can affect relationships between parents and children.
However, recognising these patterns creates an opportunity to approach them differently. Understanding family history can help individuals identify harmful behaviours and make conscious choices to avoid repeating them.
Lesson: You may not be responsible for the pain passed down through your family, but you can take steps to prevent harmful patterns from continuing.
4. Caregivers need emotional support too
Families supporting someone with a serious mental health condition often experience emotional exhaustion, fear and uncertainty. While their attention naturally focuses on the person who needs care, their own emotional well-being can easily be overlooked.
Menon's account highlights the complicated realities of growing up in a caregiving environment, where love, responsibility, fear and frustration can exist together.
It reminds readers that supporting someone through mental illness should not mean ignoring their own emotional needs.
Lesson: Caring for someone else should not require abandoning yourself. Caregivers also deserve understanding, support and space to heal.
5. Acceptance can become the beginning of healing
One of the most powerful aspects of Menon's journey is her gradual movement from fear and denial towards diagnosis, understanding and acceptance.
The memoir shows that confronting painful experiences is not easy, but acknowledging reality can make it possible to seek help and develop healthier ways of coping.
Acceptance does not mean approving of everything that happened or forgetting the past. It means recognising what happened without allowing it to define every part of your future.
Lesson: Healing begins when you stop running away from difficult truths and start understanding them with honesty and compassion.
Final thoughts
Traitor in the House: My Bipolar Life is more than a memoir about living with bipolar disorder. It is an exploration of family relationships, childhood experiences, generational trauma and the complicated journey towards understanding oneself.
Through her personal experiences, Shubha Menon encourages readers to look at mental illness with greater empathy and recognise the importance of addressing emotional wounds rather than keeping them hidden.
The book leaves readers with an important reminder: understanding the past does not change what happened, but it can help us make different choices about the future.

articles.title: À l'occasion du Black Friday 2026, ces écouteurs Apple notés 5/5 passent à 188 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Les écouteurs sans fil Apple AirPods Pro 3 "5 étoiles" à 188,00 €
Actuellement notés 5 étoiles par notre rédaction, les Apple AirPods Pro 3 se distinguent par une restitution sonore précise et une réduction de bruit active très efficace. Pour le Black Friday, leur prix tombe à 188,00 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 8 % et 15,73 € d'économie.
Avec les Apple AirPods Pro 3, le constructeur fait évoluer sa formule audio avec un format intra-auriculaire plus marqué, une isolation renforcée et une orientation sportive affirmée. Ce modèle s'est distingué lors de son passage dans notre labo grâce à ses prestations sonores et ses nouvelles fonctions dédiées à l'activité physique.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le tarif descend à 188,00 € chez Amazon, soit environ 8 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours fixé à 203,73 €. Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 15,73 €.
Réduction de bruit de pointe et autonomie solide
Les écouteurs sans fil d'Apple délivrent un rendu audio précis et immersif, tout en intégrant un traitement des bruits extérieurs encore plus poussé. Pour vous faire un avis détaillé sur leurs capacités acoustiques, vous pouvez consulter notre test complet. Le labo a mesuré une autonomie de 8 heures et 40 minutes avec la réduction de bruit active enclenchée, ce qui assure une utilisation continue sur une longue journée de travail.
Leur certification IP57 garantit une résistance à l'eau et à la poussière, un atout direct pour les sportifs réguliers qui courent en extérieur sous la pluie ou transpirent abondamment pendant l'entraînement.
Apple AirPods Pro 3
Points forts
- Restitution précise, profonde et immersive.
- L'une des meilleures réduction de bruit.
- Très bon confort, excellent maintien.
- Résistants à l'eau et à la transpiration (IP57).
- Kit mains-libres de haut vol.
- Très riches en fonctionnalités.
Points faibles
- Sonorité moins équilibrée que sur les AirPods Pro 2.
- Conception intra-auriculaire clivante.
- Expérience utilisateur tronquée sur Android.
- Régression de l'autonomie totale.
Un format intra-auriculaire plus sélectif à l'usage
Le maintien dans l'oreille s'avère particulièrement stable, mais la conception intra-auriculaire choisie par Apple peut déplaire aux personnes sensibles à l'effet de bouchon. De plus, l'expérience logicielle reste restreinte pour les utilisateurs de smartphones Android, qui ne bénéficient pas de tous les réglages intégrés à l'écosystème Apple. Ce profil conviendra avant tout aux possesseurs d'appareils de la marque à la recherche d'un excellent kit mains-libres pour leurs appels téléphoniques.
Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro : l'autre option face au Apple AirPods Pro 3
Les Galaxy Buds4 Pro adoptent une approche plus sobre avec une signature sonore orientée vers le naturel, tout en affichant une excellente ergonomie pour les possesseurs de smartphones Samsung. Les AirPods Pro 3 conservent cependant l'avantage sur l'isolation active et l'endurance par charge, tandis que la référence de Samsung accuse un retrait sur l'atténuation des fréquences médiums.
Les Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro sont vendus 28,01 € moins cher que les Apple AirPods Pro 3, mais le modèle d'Apple justifie cet écart par sa note actuelle de 5/5 contre 4,5/5 pour son rival.
Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro
Points forts
- Rendu sonore équilibré et naturel.
- Belle précision des basses et médiums.
- Excellent confort, format léger et compact.
- Bonne réduction du bruit, micros efficaces.
- Multiples fonctions, certification IP57.
Points faibles
- Légère brillance dans l'aigu.
- ANC perfectible dans le médium.
- Connectivité limitée hors univers Samsung.
- Pas d'app sur iOS.
- Autonomie correcte, sans plus.

articles.title: Hackers reportedly breached CIA intelligence analysis system
articles.text:
Unknown attackers have reportedly breached an open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis system at the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), according to a source familiar with the matter.
The source told The New York Times, which first reported the incident, that the cyberattack was carried out using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework and also affected the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency.
While the CIA and the ODNI have not yet replied to a request for more details regarding this incident, no classified data or systems were exposed in the breach.
"The hack did not involve our classified networks or classified information, and no other systems are currently at risk," the source said.
Hours after the CIA security breach was reported, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) also disclosed that it's investigating a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. After detecting the attack, the agency took some systems offline as a precaution and told banks to use the Financial Institutions Hotline to file reports, since some services may be unavailable.
"Treasury is working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and third-party forensic examiners to determine the scope and impact of the incident," a FinCEN official told BleepingComputer. "In the meantime, as a proactive measure, we have taken certain FinCEN systems offline and provided exceptive relief for filers that are not able to submit reports as a result of the disruption."
BleepingComputer has also learned that, while forensic analysis remains ongoing, there is no evidence of any breach of beneficial ownership databases or the Bank Secrecy Act.
FinCEN is the Treasury Department's financial crimes unit and the country's official Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), protecting the nation's financial system from illicit activities by sharing financial intelligence with domestic and international law enforcement agencies.
One week ago, the US National Security Agency's classified network also suffered a days-long outage, but the agency blamed scheduled routine maintenance and said its mission-critical capabilities remained fully operational.
US agencies targeted by cyberattacks
These incidents follow a series of other cyberattacks that have led to security breaches at other US federal agencies in recent years.
For instance, two years ago, the Silk Typhoon Chinese state-backed hacking group hacked the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), another Treasury Department office that administers economic and trade sanctions programs.
The same threat group also breached the Treasury's Office of Financial Research, and it reportedly infiltrated the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (a Treasury Department office that reviews foreign investments for national security risks).
More recently, as BleepingComputer reported over the weekend, hackers reportedly breached the FBI's National Crime Information Center (NCIC). However, it is unclear how the attackers gained access, when the breach occurred, or whether they stole any information from the compromised systems.
This follows a claim by the ShinyHunters extortion group that it breached the FBI's recruitment website, FBIJobs.gov, prompting an FBI investigation that led to the arrests of multiple suspected ShinyHunters members, including a Canadian cybersecurity executive reportedly linked to the attack.

articles.title: Santiago, castañero riojano con 44 años de éxito y experiencia: "Antes 8 castañas costaban 100 pesetas, ahora la docena ronda los 4 euros"
articles.text:
A mediados de los 80, ocho castañas costaban 100 pesetas. Hoy la docena ronda los 4 euros y el oficio del castañero sigue creciendo. Aunque habría que definir ese “creciendo”. Santiago Palacios Cuesta, castañero autónomo y dueño de la SL Coto de Buriz, comenzó en el oficio vendiendo cucuruchos en Logroño, en 1982. Hoy la misma docena, ya decimos, supera los 4 en Cataluña, según ha contado. Y tiene las ofertas de empleo abiertas. Le disputa el puesto a otros castañeros como Mikel Álvarez Menor, de Pamplona, o Paco Pazos, en Pontevedra.
Su oficio parece la tarea de alguien de otro siglo. Y lo es: las castañeras ya eran un arquetipo popular en la Madrid de mediados del siglo XIX. No en vano, aunque la técnica ha cambiado respecto al brasero de toda la vida, asar bien una castaña exige darle muchas vueltas “tener el fuego adecuado y no despistarse”. Además, como dice su propio FAQ, no, las castañas no tienen gluten. Y la buena noticia es que el oficio no están desapareciendo, más bien al contrario.
De un puesto a 76. Santiago Palacios Cuesta tardó 16 años en dar el salto de uno a dos puestos, luego cuatro, ocho, dieciséis y treinta y dos. Hoy El Castañero suma 76 puntos de venta entre Blanes y Castro Urdiales, con paradas también en Tarragona, Cuenca y Zamora. Asa unas 100 toneladas por campaña. Las vende una a una en sus puestos y las suministra a otros castañeros y almacenistas. Lo único que hace la IA son algunos carteles.
En un reportaje de Nueve Cuatro Uno de 2024 ya contaba que parte de su producción viene de su propia parcela de 50 hectáreas. Pero es solo una parte: casi todo el fruto en cuestión llega de Extremadura, Galicia o Portugal a un almacén en Alesón, en La Rioja. Allí se clasifican por tamaño y densidad con una máquina de agua (las malas son las que flotan, porque suelen estar agujereadas por los insectos). Aunque su lema es "del árbol a tu boca", después pasan a una cámara frigorífica, porque la castaña es muy perecedera.
Los puestos, al alza. Ahora mismo, las cuatro capitales catalanas suman 169 puestos este otoño, el máximo desde antes de la pandemia, frente al centenar de 2021. Barcelona tiene al menos 64 autorizados (hay bastantes más, sin permisos); en 2013 eran apenas 29 puestos. Tarragona está batiendo su propio récord este otoño con 18. Deja el margen justo, aducen, pero es suficiente.
Porque detrás de muchos hay scouts, asociaciones vecinales y colegios que no cobran nada. Madrid ya iba por 68 puestos en 2024, según el Ayuntamiento, aunque muchos abren solo por tradición, sabiendo que no reportan pingües beneficios.
La cuenta de la vieja. 100 pesetas son 0,60 euros: unos 7,5 céntimos por castaña. Hoy salen a entre 29 y 33 céntimos, cuatro veces más caras. Pero nadie podría quejarse: los precios se multiplicaron por casi cinco desde 1982. Las ocho castañas de entonces hoy equivaldrían a unos 2,95 euros, o 4,4 euros la docena, así que, en términos reales, el cucurucho sale algo más barato que hace 44 años. Lo que sí cambió es el comprador: cada persona se lleva menos castañas.
El soto, tocado. Lo que está claro es que el problema está en el monte, no en las calles. Por volumen de producción, Galicia manda en la castaña: más de 49.000 hectáreas de castaño y unos 20 millones de kilos al año en condiciones normales. En 2025, la sequía y los incendios dejaron la cosecha gallega por debajo de los 10 millones. Aquel año los grandes incendios quemaron 105.303 hectáreas en Ourense, con sotos de Valdeorras entre los afectados. A escala nacional, la campaña 2025/26 cerró con 89.374 toneladas: un 7% menos que la anterior y un 4,5% por debajo de la media de cinco años.
2026 iba a ser el año de la recuperación. Y los castaños quemados rebrotaron, perro la sequía de septiembre y octubre lo estropeó: en Valdeorras la cosecha quedó en el 60% de lo habitual, con insectos, hongos y más castañas pequeñas de lo normal, y pocos frutos grandes. En El Bierzo, las olas de calor dejaron los erizos más pequeños y adelantaron la cosecha ya en agosto. La escasez de los últimos años ya encareció el kilo tanto en origen como en destino. Y el hongo que pudre el fruto repuntó, tras bajar del 33% al 14% de positividad media entre 2023 y 2025.
Paradoja mayorista. Que escasee no significa que el kilo se dispare a lo loco. En septiembre, primer mes de campaña, el precio medio de la castaña en Mercamadrid era de 3,54 euros el kilo. Es un 15,5% menos que los 4,18 euros de septiembre de 2025, con 275 toneladas en el mercado. Un solo mes no define ninguna tendencia, pero sí ayuda a entender por qué el cucurucho aguanta.
Palacios lo resume en tres ideas: buena castaña, fuego adecuado y muchas vueltas. Solo las dos últimas dependen de él, pero parece que les ha cogido el punto.

articles.title: Nvidia might be about to cut GPU supply in a major way — which means Black Friday deals on graphics cards suddenly look even more tempting
articles.text:
Rumor suggests Nvidia will cut GPU supply by 20% to 30% over the next few months — so if you don’t buy soon, prices could get even scarier
A solid Black Friday deal could be a smart move
- A rumor claims Nvidia will reduce gaming GPU supply in China by 20% to 30% over the next quarter
- If true, this will likely be reflected in the global picture for Nvidia's consumer GPUs
- It comes on top of some big price hikes for GPUs already, and could mean an even more miserable start to 2027 for PC gamers
We don't need any more supply shocks in the desktop GPU world right now — but we're about to be dealt another blow by Nvidia, if a fresh rumor is correct.
VideoCardz reports that there's been more news from the Board Channels (a source of supply chain rumors over in China) which suggests that Nvidia is dropping its allocation of chips for consumer and gaming GPUs over the next quarter (November to January, or Nvidia's fiscal Q4).
We're told that graphics card makers over in China are going to be subject to a 20% to 30% reduction in supply for gaming GPUs over these next few months, with supply in Q3 already having been tight.
As a result, the (translated) Board Channels post notes that consumer GPU pricing is going to be volatile — although I assume the volatility will purely be a function of how big a price spike might occur.
While this rumor pertains specifically to China, that market doesn't exist in a bubble, and there's a good chance that Nvidia will have similar global priorities — at least to an extent.
Analysis: more GPU misery
This is obviously very disappointing news, although we must take it with some seasoning. It's only a rumor, of course, and as noted, one that applies to China. However, the trouble is that it's quite believable that Nvidia would increasingly focus on its AI GPUs at the cost of consumer products, and that this is going to apply on a worldwide basis to some extent.
GPU pricing is already in a bad way, with recent major increases taking their toll — especially with higher-end Nvidia graphics cards. If more pricing pain is in the cards, well, that could push many GeForce GPUs into truly frightening territory in terms of just how expensive they're getting.

I've been saying for months now that if you're in the market for a graphics card, you should buy one sooner rather than later — and that Black Friday could be the last chance to get a decent deal on some models of GPU for a very long time.
This fresh rumor makes it seem more likely that prices are only going up – so you're either going to have to pull the trigger soon, or be patient possibly for quite a long time. (Or alternatively, look at the second-hand market — but that holds its own perils of course).

articles.title: Logitech's new MX Master 4 Creator Edition mouse offers pixel perfect precision
articles.text:
Logitech has launched the limited-edition MX Master 4 Creator Edition mouse aimed at creative professionals who spend a lot of time at their computer editing and enhancing their content.
The mouse has layout grids, coloured calibration bands, and alignment crosshairs printed directly on it to give your desktop a new studio artboard aesthetic.
There are a number of subtle Easter eggs on the mouse as well including key timestamp tributes integrated into the body to signify and celebrate World Design Day (04/27), World Photography Day (08/19), World Creativity Day (04/21) and World Day for Audiovisual Heritage (10/27).
And naturally it is built on the MX Master 4 platform which offers built-in haptic vibration feedback while scrubbing timelines, adjusting sliders, and making even the smallest image edits.
There is a dedicated Action Ring button to provide one-click access to custom macros, colour wheels, and other shortcuts for your workflow.
The mouse can scroll at up to 1,000 lines per second but can stop on a pixel with the MagSpeed scroll wheel which is Logitech’s fastest and quietest precision scrolling experience.
And because people will spend so much time the mouse, it must be comfortable.
The MX Master 4 is optimised at a tilt angle to keep your arm in a more natural posture and with button placement to offer quicker and more intuitive navigation.
It’s also possible to connect the mouse to up to three devices and switch seamlessly between them.
And of course the MX Master 4 works across Windows, macOS, Linux, Chrome OS, iPadOS, and Android.
MX Master 4 can run for up to 70 days on a full charge. And a 1-minute quick charge offers 3 hours of use.
The Logitech MX Master 4 Creator Edition is available now and is priced at $199.95.

articles.title: Como editar um story do Instagram depois de postado
articles.text:
Como editar um story do Instagram depois de postado
Editar stories já postados no Instagram permite corrigir textos e ajustar stickers em até 15 minutos sem perder visualizações, curtidas ou a ordem da publicação original
Você sabia que é possível editar um story do Instagram mesmo após publicá-lo, corrigindo textos e ajustando figurinhas? A função está disponível diretamente nos aplicativos para Android e iPhone por meio do menu “Mais” na própria publicação.
Para editar um story já publicado, a alteração precisa ser feita no limite de 15 minutos após o envio original na rede social. O ajuste mantém todas as visualizações e curtidas intactas, exibindo apenas um discreto aviso de que o conteúdo foi modificado.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog te ensina o passo a passo para editar stories já publicados no Instagram.
Você pode editar um story depois de postado diretamente pelo aplicativo do Instagram para celular Android ou iPhone. Veja o passo a passo para alterar um conteúdo que já foi postado na rede social:
Abra o aplicativo do Instagram no seu celular e toque na sua foto de perfil, no canto superior esquerdo, para visualizar os seus stories recentes.
Com a publicação aberta na tela, toque no botão “Mais”, ícone de três pontos no canto inferior direito, para abrir a aba com as opções e ferramentas disponíveis para o conteúdo.
Toque em “Editar story” e, caso seja sua primeira vez usando a ferramenta, confirme tocando no botão “Entendi” para avançar.
Use as ferramentas de edição para corrigir textos, reposicionar figurinhas ou modificar elementos visuais do story, lembrando que a mídia original (foto ou vídeo de fundo) não pode ser substituída.
Após revisar todas as modificações feitas na tela, toque em “Salvar alterações” no canto inferior direito e aguarde alguns instantes até que o aplicativo atualize o story publicado para seus seguidores.
Ao editar stories já publicados no Instagram, a rede social aplica ajustes visuais e técnicos para sinalizar a atualização sem prejudicar o alcance da postagem. Confira os principais efeitos que ocorrem ao alterar um story:
- Selo de alteração: o Instagram exibe uma etiqueta “Editado” acompanhada de um ícone de lápis logo abaixo do seu nome de usuário, sinalizando para os seguidores que o conteúdo passou por modificações;
- Preservação do engajamento: todas as métricas de interação acumuladas antes da mudança, como a lista de visualizações, curtidas e respostas enviadas por mensagem direta (DM), permanecem intactas na publicação;
- Posição e público intocados: o story não é republicado como novo nem volta para o final da fila, mantendo a ordem na sequência e respeitando as configurações de privacidade definidas inicialmente;
- Remoção de republicações: caso outros perfis tenham compartilhado o seu story antes da alteração, esses recompartilhamentos feitos a partir do original são automaticamente removidos do ar pelo Instagram.
Não, você não perde suas visualizações ao editar stories no Instagram dentro da janela de 15 minutos após a postagem. Todo o engajamento original, incluindo curtidas e respostas, permanece intacto na publicação, que passa apenas a exibir o selo “Editado” para informar a atualização aos seguidores.
Não, o story editado não é atualizado automaticamente nos compartilhamentos feitos pelos seus seguidores. Para evitar inconsistências de exibição, o Instagram remove do ar todas as cópias ligadas à versão original, exigindo que outros perfis voltem a compartilhar stories a partir da publicação corrigida.
O Instagram não estabelece um limite fixo de alterações ao editar story depois de postado, restringindo o recurso apenas ao prazo de 15 minutos após a publicação. Durante essa janela de tempo, você pode reabrir a interface de edição e salvar ajustes nos textos ou figurinhas quantas vezes precisar no mesmo arquivo.
A opção para editar um story depois de postado fica disponível apenas quando a publicação atende a regras técnicas e prazos definidos pelo Instagram. Veja os motivos mais comuns que fazem o botão de edição sumir do seu menu:
- Prazo expirado: a janela de edição dura apenas 15 minutos após o envio. Passado esse limite de tempo, o recurso é bloqueado e você precisará apagar e publicar o conteúdo novamente;
- Liberação gradual: o Instagram distribui novas ferramentas em lotes pelo servidor, o que significa que a função ainda pode não ter sido ativada para a sua conta;
- Aplicativo desatualizado: versões antigas do Instagram não suportam os recursos mais recentes do sistema, exigindo a atualização manual do aplicativo na App Store ou Play Store;
- Recursos incompatíveis: a inclusão de stickers interativos específicos, como a figurinha “Sua Vez”, bloqueia o modo de edição devido às limitações técnicas de sincronização;
- Integração com o Facebook: stories configurados para compartilhamento cruzado com o Facebook têm a edição bloqueada para evitar falhas de exibição entre as duas redes sociais.
Se você perdeu a janela de 15 minutos para editar a publicação, a saída prática é apagar o story no Instagram e subir o conteúdo corrigido do zero. Antes de excluir a postagem, salve o arquivo na galeria do celular para reaproveitar a foto ou o vídeo original sem perder o arquivo.
Na hora de republicar, aproveite para montar stories criativos, adicionando textos, trilhas sonoras ou enquetes que ficaram de fora da primeira versão. Vale lembrar que, se você usar stickers interativos ou ativar o envio simultâneo para o Facebook, o sistema bloqueará novas edições posteriores.

articles.title: Rockstar dice ‘no’ a una película de GTA, pero no descarta algo como Red Dead Redemption
articles.text:
Rockstar Games decidió trazar una línea clara entre sus dos franquicias más valiosas. Según reveló The Ankler, el estudio detrás de Grand Theft Auto no tiene intención de llevar la saga a cine o televisión, pese al interés de Hollywood durante años.
La noticia llega en medio del éxito arrollador de GTA 6, que generó cerca de 3.800 millones de dólares al cierre de su primer día en el mercado. Sin embargo, mientras GTA permanece fuera del alcance de productoras y plataformas, Red Dead Redemption sí aparece como una posibilidad concreta de adaptación.
Por qué Rockstar no quiere llevar GTA al cine
De acuerdo con The Ankler, Rockstar Games ha recibido llamados constantes de compañías de entretenimiento interesadas en adaptar Grand Theft Auto a lo largo de los últimos años. A pesar de esa demanda sostenida, el estudio mantiene su negativa.
La franquicia ya genera un nivel de expectativa y atención mediática que, según se desprende del reporte, haría innecesaria cualquier versión televisiva o cinematográfica. Las cifras de ventas de GTA 6 refuerzan ese argumento: se espera que el título termine generando entre tres y cuatro veces lo recaudado por GTA 5, que alcanzó los 1.150 millones de dólares.
El lanzamiento del juego, ocurrido tras una espera de 13 años, coincide además con el momento en que se conoció esta postura del estudio respecto a Hollywood.
Rockstar Games no estaría interesada en adaptar Grand Theft Auto a cine o series porque la franquicia ya concentra una enorme expectativa comercial por sí sola. En cambio, sí consideraría ofertas para licenciar Red Dead Redemption, aunque exigiría un pago mínimo de 100 millones de dólares por los derechos.
Red Dead Redemption, la franquicia que sí estaría en juego
El panorama cambia con Red Dead Redemption, la saga de acción y aventura ambientada en el Lejano Oeste. Para este caso, Rockstar se mostraría más abierta a negociar una adaptación de esta propiedad para cine o televisión.
Un agente que trabaja con guionistas del sector de los videojuegos señaló que “en algún momento, estaban barajando un precio de compra de más de 100 millones de dólares mínimo para licenciar los derechos”. La cifra sirve como punto de partida para cualquier negociación, aunque no garantiza que el estudio termine aceptando alguna propuesta concreta.
Como referencia de magnitud, Amazon pagó 250 millones de dólares en 2017 por los derechos televisivos globales de El Señor de los Anillos. La comparación ubica la cifra pedida por Rockstar dentro de un rango que, sin alcanzar ese techo, resulta igualmente alto para el mercado de adaptaciones.
Todavía no está definido si una eventual producción de Red Dead Redemption seguiría de manera fiel la trama de los videojuegos o si optaría por una historia original ambientada en ese universo.
El auge de las adaptaciones de videojuegos en Hollywood
El posible interés de Rockstar por licenciar Red Dead Redemption se da en un contexto de expansión de las adaptaciones basadas en videojuegos. Plataformas como Amazon, Netflix y FX destinan entre 15 y 25 millones de dólares por episodio a proyectos como Tomb Raider, Assassin’s Creed y Far Cry.
El éxito de Fallout, producida por Amazon, y de The Last of Us, de HBO, intensificó esa búsqueda de nuevas franquicias para convertir en series o películas. Estas producciones buscan atraer a los jugadores hacia el formato televisivo tradicional.
El reporte también aporta cifras sobre el peso actual de la industria de los videojuegos: el mercado global está valuado en más de 200.000 millones de dólares y reúne a 3.700 millones de jugadores activos. Esa magnitud explica por qué el equilibrio de poder entre Hollywood y la industria gamer se modificó de forma marcada en los últimos años.

articles.title: Diversity is increasing within BDC portfolio companies but remains stubbornly low among leadership
articles.text:
A majority of companies backed by the Business Development Bank of Canada’s venture capital arm are practising diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI), but those efforts aren’t translating into leadership positions.
The news: BDC Capital released its fifth annual report on DEI and environmental, social, and governance practices on Tuesday. On the DEI side, the report looks at how BDC portfolio companies and supported venture capital general partners (GPs) are engaging with and implementing DEI policies.
From the source: Between 2021 and 2025, BDC surveyed 82 GPs, including 70 BDC-backed GPs and 12 internal teams, and surveyed a sample of its 1,399 eligible portfolio companies. Notably, participation from GPs was spotty, with a non-response rate of 30 percent. Reporting shows more than half of participating GPs have a DEI strategy, and 63 percent have introduced efforts to reduce bias in hiring. 
The context: Among the VC ecosystem, the overall impact of adopting DEI policies and practices is viewed favourably, with 38 percent of respondents saying its impact was positive or very positive; just 1 percent said it had negative impacts. Respondents also cited improved decision-making and innovation (26 percent) and stakeholder expectations (17 percent) as their primary reasons for implementing DEI practices. Both of those metrics were overshadowed, however, by larger percentages of non-responses (30 and 33 percent, respectively).
Among portfolio companies, talent attraction was the highest motivator for DEI adoption (42 percent). A majority of portfolio companies reported that adopting DEI practices had a neutral impact (51 percent), while just 15 percent said it was very positive. Despite a majority of GPs and companies practicing DEI, as employees move up the rungs of leadership, that representation narrows. While 95 percent of portfolio companies report having women and visible minorities on staff, only 24 percent of companies reported women making up half or more of their management team, and 43 percent reported that visible minorities make up 25 percent or more.
Final thought: For GPs in particular, rates of inclusion have risen among all groups by between two and nine percent, except for Indigenous representation, which shrank by two percent. April Hicke, the founder of equity-based recruitment platform Toast, said those increases were akin to standing still and condemned low levels of representation in leadership, telling BetaKit, “ignoring half the talent pool is a business problem.”
“Women work at 95 percent of Canada’s VC-backed companies, but a quarter of those companies still have zero women in management, so this isn’t a pipeline problem. Obviously, something is still stopping women from moving up,” she said.
BetaKit’s Prairies reporting is funded in part by YEGAF, a not-for-profit dedicated to amplifying business stories in Alberta.

articles.title: The questions Jensen Huang and Nvidia will still have to answer about Megaspeed
articles.text:
Jensen Huang’s return as CEO to Nvidia hasn’t eased the scrutiny the company faces. The chipmaker still needs to address multiple inquiries into allegations that its advanced GPUs were smuggled into China by a customer, the Singapore-based data center operator Megaspeed, in violation of U.S. export rules designed to slow China’s development of frontier AI models.
The central question for investigators is what Nvidia knew about where those chips ended up and whether Huang’s affair with a Megaspeed executive gave the company reason to doubt Megaspeed’s assurances. Huang’s return doesn’t settle that. U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche has suggested Nvidia isn’t a target of an investigation, but California’s attorney general and Congress are pressing ahead, and the Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating, too.
The U.S. government opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 and requested information from Nvidia about its billions of dollars in sales to the company, concerned that some of the chips Megaspeed bought for data center projects in Malaysia were in fact being diverted to China. Singapore also began investigating similar allegations in 2025. Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing.
Diversion of this kind would be a fairly routine issue for a company like Nvidia, whose in-demand chips are the targets of smugglers and resellers. When it comes to compliance and liability for export-control violations, Nvidia and other chip sellers need assurances that the end users of their chips are obeying the rules. However, they also cannot ignore other information that might call the reliability of those assurances into question, export-control attorneys told TechCrunch.
And that’s why Jensen Huang’s affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang was such a problem for Nvidia, likely even more so than her alleged role as a source for Chinese intelligence agencies. If Nvidia personnel, from lower-level employees up to the CEO, had reason to believe that statements from Megaspeed weren’t reliable, the attorneys said, that would increase the company’s legal risk.
“Government investigators likely would want to know, notwithstanding whatever formal assurances were exchanged between the parties, what anyone at Nvidia actually knew about the end use and end users of the chips,” Dan Fisher-Owens, an attorney at the firm Berliner Corcoran & Rowe, told TechCrunch last week.
The concern Nvidia’s board faced when it decided to oust Huang is that he knew more about what Megaspeed was doing with Nvidia’s products than was reflected in any of the compliance statements. The Wall Street Journal reported that Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, were part of a network of businesses that funneled chips to a company in Shanghai. Kang also reportedly introduced his wife to Jensen Huang, whom he had known for a decade.
On Monday, the U.S. government added Megaspeed and its affiliates to a list of companies restricted from U.S. trade due to national security concerns. The U.S. also issued new rules last week barring large data centers that purchase U.S. chips from serving customers in China and other nations seen as problematic by the U.S. government. Nvidia, meanwhile, said it would stop selling licensed chips to China and laid out plans to hire its first compliance officer and create a new board committee focused on export controls.
Nvidia’s board said it reinstated Huang on Monday after receiving “input from senior levels of the United States government” that left it confident his return posed no national security risk. President Donald Trump later said he called into the meeting to give them that assurance.
In a news conference Tuesday, Blanche said that Nvidia was “a good corporate citizen” and suggested it is not the target of an investigation, but Blanche declined to answer questions about the government’s investigation into Megaspeed, which the Justice Department said was ongoing as recently as last week.
“When you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don’t know what you’re talking about,” Blanche said.
Other authorities may be more demanding. Nvidia faces investigations by California Attorney General Rob Bonta and, reportedly, the SEC, both tied to its corporate disclosures. While many details of the investigation still aren’t known, short sellers complained about the company’s decision to stop breaking out its exports to Singapore in financial filings after journalists raised concerns about chip diversion.
Members of Congress from both parties say they want answers from Nvidia, with many citing alarm about China and some questioning the White House’s role in Huang’s return. Three committees in the House of Representatives will privately interview Huang and Nvidia’s top lawyer, Tim Teter, next week. Teter reportedly intervened in the Department of Commerce’s investigation of Megaspeed last year.
“We remain committed to getting answers on the mass smuggling of Nvidia products, their diversion for Chinese military purposes, and their key role in advancing our foremost adversary’s AI capabilities,” the Republican chairs of House committees focused on foreign affairs, intelligence, and China said in a joint statement.
Rep. Brian Mast, the chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, has also demanded that the Department of Commerce share extensive data regarding its investigation into chip smuggling, including by Megaspeed and its affiliates.
The Senate Banking Committee will also question Huang in a public hearing on December 3.
“Mr. Huang, Nvidia executives, and the company’s board still owe Congress answers about the company’s compliance with U.S. export controls,” Senator Elizabeth Warren, the ranking Democratic member on the committee, said in a statement. “The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what ‘input’ was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement.”

articles.title: EPA reports ‘zero’ airborne lead following controlled Army detonation in Iowa
articles.text:
Saying it was necessary to prevent the possible spontaneous explosion of a stockpile of material used in igniters and blasting caps, the US Army conducted a controlled detonation of over 9,700 pounds of lead azide today at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa. Videos of the detonation showed plumes of smoke several hundred feet high drifting south before quickly dissipating.
EPA reports ‘zero’ airborne lead following controlled Army detonation in Iowa
Hours after detonating 4.4 tons of lead azide in Iowa, officials reported early test results from the surrounding areas.
Following the explosion, the Army confirmed that all of the barrels at the plant had been destroyed without any secondary explosions or infrastructure damage. “I believe, absolutely, that we reduced, as close to zero as it’s absolutely humanly possible, the risk to the health and safety of the people of Middletown and the extended communities throughout Iowa,” said Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley during a press conference held two hours after the blast, according to the Associated Press.
The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has been monitoring the area around the ammunition plant leading up to today’s event. According to a statement from the EPA following the detonation, “real-time air monitors are reporting zero detection of airborne lead throughout the region” an hour after the detonation. The data collected by EPA employees, contractors, and monitoring equipment is shared here.
The Army has used lead azide in munitions for nearly a century but began transitioning away from the material around 15 years ago because it can be difficult to transport and store. Over time, the material can degrade and crystallize and eventually become unstable enough to detonate at ambient temperatures. The Iowa ammunition plant housed 68 barrels containing about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, representing the country’s remaining stockpile. For safety reasons, the material was stored in liquid form embedded in sawdust and burlap bags while water and ethanol were added to prevent freezing. However, the decision was made to detonate the stockpile after an inspection by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms (ATF) discovered “significant crystallization on the exterior of the barrels” last March.
Ahead of today’s detonation, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) supported a recommended, but voluntary, temporary relocation of all the residents of Middletown and immediate surrounding areas that began yesterday. A cone-shaped evacuation zone extends about five miles southwest of the ammunition plant to account for the post-explosion dispersion and deposition path of dust. Displaced residents will be lodged until Friday, November 27th, and can return home once the all-clear has been given.
To reduce the amount of lead dust released into surrounding areas and the environment, the Army said it took several additional precautions as part of today’s detonation. Walls made of four 16,000-gallon water tanks were installed to capture lead particulate, while the aging earth-covered magazines holding the barrels were covered with tarps and lead containment screens and flooded with foam.

articles.title: C’est quoi cette explosion qui panique les USA et les réseaux sociaux ?
articles.text:
Comme l’explique la BBC, ce mercredi 25 novembre 2026, à la veille de Thanksgiving, l’armée américaine va procéder à la détonation contrôlée de près de 4,5 tonnes d’explosifs dégradés sur le site de l’usine de munitions de Middletown, dans l’Iowa. Cela devrait avoir lieu à 9h00 du matin soit 16h00 chez nous. Saisie par des associations environnementales, dont le Sierra Club, la cour d’appel fédérale du 8e circuit avait suspendu l’opération la semaine dernière. Elle l’a autorisée ce lundi 23 novembre, quelques heures après que Donald Trump a demandé à l’armée d’attendre le feu vert des juges. L’explosion plonge toute une région agricole dans l’angoisse.
L’armée devrait se débarrasser de 68 fûts d’azoture de plomb, un explosif très instable qui sert à amorcer les munitions, devenu trop dangereux pour être conservé. Selon l’armée, la baisse des températures annoncée pour les jours suivants augmentait le risque d’une explosion spontanée. L’armée a donc choisi de faire sauter le stock. Elle a proposé une évacuation facultative dans un rayon de 8 kilomètres et recommandé de rester confiné dans un rayon d’environ 32 kilomètres, en prévenant que la poussière de plomb pourrait porter jusqu’à 160 kilomètres selon les vents (rassurant). Sur les réseaux sociaux, beaucoup d’Américains s’inquiètent d’un potentiel nuage toxique.
Une région agricole coupée en deux entre colère et résignation avec cette explosion
Autour de Middletown, la décision passe très mal, en particulier chez les agriculteurs et les habitants des communes voisines qui dénoncent un manque criant de transparence. À Donnelson, à une trentaine de kilomètres au sud-ouest de l’usine, l’exploitante agricole Margo Sprenger, 71 ans, voit ses terres placées directement sur la trajectoire du nuage toxique. « Nos grands-parents ont démarré sur ces fermes, et aujourd’hui nous ne savons même pas si elles peuvent produire une nourriture fiable », confie-t-elle à la BBC, redoutant le coût des analyses et l’impact irréversible sur son exploitation familiale. Sa voisine Beth Howard passe Thanksgiving à Des Moines, à quelque 240 kilomètres de là, tandis que son compagnon, Doug, reste sur la ferme que sa famille exploite depuis plus de 150 ans.
À Fort Madison, à une trentaine de kilomètres du site, la ville n’a été prévenue que le 17 novembre, trois jours avant la date initialement prévue. « Nous avons été pris de court », dénonce l’administratrice de la ville, Laura Leigois, qui a fait couvrir les bouches d’aération du château d’eau. Selon la ville, d’autres méthodes de neutralisation existent et le risque d’explosion spontanée n’a rien d’imminent.
À l’épicentre, les habitants voulaient surtout en finir
À Middletown même, une bourgade d’environ 360 habitants collée à l’usine militaire, l’ambiance était plus… pragmatique. Habitués depuis des générations à vivre dans l’ombre du complexe d’armement, de nombreux résidents souhaitaient avant tout tourner la page.
Le maire de Middletown, Rodney Johnso, vit dans un mobile home à environ 800 mètres du site et s’est contenté d’installer une caméra pour le surveiller depuis son travail. Il rappelle que des avions d’épandage survolent les maisons toutes les deux semaines et que, selon lui, ils répandent des produits bien plus dangereux. Il assure que ses administrés auraient été très en colère en cas de nouveau report. L’armée affirme que les sols, l’air et l’eau autour du site sont analysés avant et après l’explosion. Elle doit publier une estimation finale de la zone touchée par les retombées de plomb. Pour autant, sur les réseaux sociaux, comme X, la panique est bien présente chez de nombreux Américains qui craignent un nuage toxique dans les états voisins. Une carte (dont on ne connait pas la provenance) est même très partagée, comme on peut voir ci-dessous.

articles.title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15
articles.text:
AWS recently doubled the maximum timeout of on-demand Lambda Event Functions from 15 to 30 minutes. The new limit applies to synchronous, asynchronous, and event source mapping invocations in all commercial regions, at standard pricing and without an opt-in. The 15-minute ceiling had stood since 2018, after 60 seconds at launch in 2014 and five minutes from 2015.
Raising the limit is a configuration change per function, and Lambda rejects any value above 1,800 seconds with a validation error:
aws lambda update-function-configuration \
    --function-name my-demo-function \
    --timeout 1800
The change covers one of the three shapes Lambda took this year. Web Functions keep 15 minutes, and Lambda MicroVMs allow eight hours, while on Lambda Managed Instances synchronous invocations now get 30 minutes and asynchronous ones keep the 90 minutes introduced in September. AWS names agentic AI requests that chain model and tool calls, media transcoding, Monte Carlo simulations, and report generation as the workloads that outgrew 15 minutes.
According to Tarun Rai Madan, Dan Slusariuc, and Snehil Ameta, the authors of the announcement, the first thing to check before raising the timeout is capacity:
Concurrency equals requests per second multiplied by average duration in seconds. At the same request rate, a function that runs for 30 minutes instead of 15 needs twice the concurrency. For example, 1 request per second at 30 minutes each needs 1,800 concurrent executions.
The rest of the post is about what sits around the function. An SQS queue's visibility timeout has to be at least six times the function timeout, which means three hours. Kinesis and DynamoDB Streams read one batch per shard at a time, so a slow function slows the shard. Amazon MQ, DocumentDB and Kafka mappings created before November 19 stay at 14 minutes. A NAT gateway still drops idle connections after 350 seconds, and the Init phase keeps its 10-second limit.
Wibo van der Sluis, an independent AWS practitioner, tested the SQS rule in eu-west-1 by raising a function to 1,800 seconds behind a queue with a 90-minute visibility timeout and then lowering the queue to 60 seconds. Both changes were accepted with the mapping still enabled, while a new mapping from the same queue was refused:
So the check exists, but only at creation. One more thing the test showed: at creation, Lambda compared the queue with the function timeout itself, not with six times it. I did not test where exactly that line sits, so treat the six times as guidance you enforce yourself.
He adds that an asynchronous function which times out three times has run for 90 minutes before the event reaches a dead-letter queue, and concludes that 30 minutes is the wrong fix for slow code behind an API.
Luc van Donkersgoed, principal engineer at NS and AWS Serverless Hero, writes:
Hell froze over. AWS Lambda now supports 30-minute timeouts. I am not sure how I feel about this.
The comments under the post took two directions. Magnus Eriksson, architect and former AWS employee, notes that Lambda "is anyhow quite expensive per CPU second compared to EC2" and would still reserve it for short-lived spiky loads. Matthew Bonig, AWS DevTools Hero and co-author of The CDK Book, looked further ahead: "Eventually it'll be 8 hours, and then nobody will be able to understand when to use it vs. MicroVMs."
On Reddit, the most-upvoted reply welcomed the change because it avoids Fargate and ECS for hour-long batch jobs. The answer under it was that Fargate is beautifully simple. One commenter sets out where the longer limit fits:
A 30 minute run still bills for the full duration at your configured memory, so check the cost per invocation before moving batch style work here, and keep the handler idempotent with a dead letter queue, because a failure or timeout partway through a long run can leave partial work behind. For multi step work, long running jobs, or anything that needs clear state and retries, Step Functions with Fargate or ECS is still usually cleaner.
Joseph Emison, CTO of Branch Insurance, reads the move as Lambda team recognizing that Cloud Run is its most compelling competitor. Cloud Run services allow 60 minutes per request, and Azure Functions on the Flex Consumption and Premium plans enforce no maximum, with a 60-minute grace period during scale-in. AWS has not said whether the Lambda limit will move again.

articles.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
articles.text:
Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
By treating qubits like individual molecules, scientists can now predict their behavior faster and more accurately
- Date:
  November 13, 2026
- Source:
  Princeton University
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers.
- Share:
A new computational technique could accelerate the search for diamond materials capable of powering future quantum computers and highly sensitive sensors. Developed by a researcher at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory (PPPL), the method makes it much easier to identify promising materials for quantum technology, potentially opening the door to advances across many areas of science.
The approach has already revealed new candidates for quantum computing and sensing applications. The findings were recently published in ACS Central Science and have attracted attention from other researchers in the field.
One of the biggest challenges in developing quantum technology is finding materials that can maintain delicate quantum states under practical conditions. Many candidates require extremely low temperatures to function reliably. Diamond materials stand out because certain quantum properties can remain useful even at room temperature.
This capability could help advance technologies that are important to national research priorities and the development of next-generation computing. Quantum sensors promise levels of sensitivity and precision beyond those of conventional instruments, while quantum computers could eventually solve certain extraordinarily complex problems much faster than today's most powerful supercomputers.
Why Imperfect Diamonds Could Be the Key to Quantum Computing
Although diamonds are made of carbon atoms, a flawless diamond crystal is not enough to create a useful quantum computing system. The key lies in tiny irregularities within the crystal structure.
These imperfections, known as defects, can occur when a carbon atom is absent from its normal position, when another element replaces a carbon atom, or when both changes occur together. The atoms surrounding these defects can form qubits, the basic units used to store and process quantum information in quantum computers and sensors.
Finding the most useful defects, however, has been difficult. Accurately modeling their quantum behavior traditionally requires enormous computational resources, making it challenging to evaluate large numbers of possible candidates.
A Simpler Way to Discover Better Diamond Qubits
Mark Martirez, a staff research scientist at PPPL, developed a way to dramatically reduce the complexity of these calculations. Instead of simulating a much larger diamond structure, he isolates a small region containing just 16 to 30 atoms around a defect.
By "carving out" this tiny atomic cluster and treating it like a separate molecule, Martirez can use powerful computational methods that chemists have spent decades refining. These established techniques make it possible to analyze the quantum properties of diamond defects much more efficiently without sacrificing the high level of accuracy needed for the calculations.
"Because we're treating the qubits as molecules, the cost of calculating these defects is equivalent to the cost of just modeling a simple molecule," Martirez said. "This method really opened the floodgates" in terms of how qubits can be assessed.
The new technique allows researchers to calculate how different qubits respond to laser light and microwave pulses far more quickly than before. Using this approach, the team identified promising defects involving boron and oxygen that could serve as new types of qubits.
New Diamond Defects Reveal a Spectrum of Quantum Colors
Light plays an important role in how scientists interact with diamond qubits. Researchers use lasers and microwave pulses to manipulate their quantum states and retrieve stored information.
Much of the previous work in this area has centered on a defect known as the nitrogen-vacancy center. This structure forms when a nitrogen atom takes the place of a carbon atom in a diamond crystal, while an adjacent position that would normally contain another carbon atom remains empty.
Under laser illumination, this type of defect can emit red light when it occupies a particular quantum state.
The newly investigated defects offer different optical properties. Oxygen defects can produce blue light, while those involving boron emit ultraviolet light.
These differences could make it possible to combine several types of qubits within a single quantum device. Because each type responds differently to light, researchers might be able to interact with one group of qubits without disturbing another.
"One could imagine, then, combining different qubits of different responses, so you can basically probe one qubit but not the other," Martirez said.
Beyond identifying new candidates, the findings suggest a broader change in how researchers approach quantum technology. Diamond qubits have traditionally been studied primarily through physics, but understanding their underlying chemistry could provide additional ways to design them.
Martirez believes that researchers could eventually engineer qubits for particular functions using principles similar to those applied when chemists create specialized molecules, including compounds designed for new medications.
How Quantum Chemistry Could Transform Future Research
The potential benefits extend well beyond the development of quantum computers themselves. Martirez sees an intriguing possibility in which advances made possible by quantum chemistry eventually lead to quantum technologies that help improve the field of chemistry.
In other words, quantum chemistry could develop the very tools needed to "enrich itself" in the coming decades.
A practical quantum system containing multiple qubits could make molecular calculations substantially more accurate. That would allow scientists to study increasingly complex chemical structures, including large biological molecules and proteins, with a level of detail that is difficult to achieve using conventional methods.
"We could describe larger molecules, biomolecules, proteins and everything like that in a more accurate way, and that could improve all the chemical-adjacent industries, such as pharmaceutical science and materials science. Even our fundamental understanding of molecular systems could be enriched."
Such improvements could have far-reaching implications for pharmaceutical development, materials research, and the fundamental study of how molecules behave.
Martirez also hopes the research will encourage more chemists to explore solid-state physics. Although building advanced quantum computers is often viewed as a challenge primarily for physicists, he argues that chemistry offers valuable expertise that could help accelerate progress.
"At this moment in time, there's a great emphasis on building the first state-of-the-art qubit computer," he said. "But it's not just physicists who should be participating in this research. Chemists have decades of developed intuition about chemical systems that could be easily translated into understanding defects in solids as well."
By bringing these disciplines together, scientists may be able to develop more effective ways to discover, understand, and eventually engineer the quantum materials needed for future technologies.
The research was funded through PPPL's Laboratory Directed Research and Development program under prime contract number DE-AC02-09CH11466, with additional support from the DOE Office of Science, Office of Fusion Energy Sciences.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Princeton University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- John Mark P. Martirez. A Chemist’sGuide to Solid-State Qubits: DiamondColor Centers as Embedded Vacancy-Centered Molecules. ACS Central Science, 2026; 12 (10): 1578 DOI: 10.1021/acscentsci.6c00548
