articles.title: Anthropics neuer Siren-Test: Warum Forscher die KI‑Modelle absichtlich in Fallen locken
articles.text:
Verlockende Schlupflöcher: Warum Anthropic seinen KI-Modellen absichtlich eine Falle stellt
Eigentlich sind Sirenen Fabelwesen aus der griechischen Mythologie. In vielen Erzählungen, etwa in Homers Odyssee, locken sie vorbeifahrende Seeleute an, um sie anschließend zu töten. Anthropic hat jetzt einen Test mit demselben Namen entwickelt und erklärt in einem Blogbeitrag die Vorgehensweise sowie erste Erkenntnisse. Siren versetzt KI-Agenten in realistische Simulationen, die darauf ausgelegt sind, sie zu Fehlverhalten zu verleiten. Anhand der Ergebnisse können Forscher:innen einschätzen, wie wahrscheinlich es ist, dass neue Modelle im realen Einsatz außer Kontrolle geraten.
Siren soll KI-Agenten in Versuchung führen
In den vergangenen Monaten haben KI-Labore mit zahlreichen Sicherheitsvorfällen für Schlagzeilen gesorgt. Insbesondere der Angriff auf Hugging Face hat große Aufmerksamkeit erregt. Ursprünglich wollte OpenAI die Leistungsfähigkeit neuer Modelle testen. Stattdessen brachen mehrere Agenten aus der eigentlich abgeriegelten Sandbox aus und verschafften sich Zugang zu den Systemen der Open-Source-Plattform. Laut OpenAI ging der Angriff auf ein internes Forum zurück, in dem sich die Agenten austauschten und gefundene Schwachstellen teilten.
OpenAI ist damit nicht allein: Auch Konkurrenten wie Anthropic haben zahlreiche Vorfälle gemeldet, in denen sich ihre Agenten nicht wie gewünscht verhielten. Infolgedessen sprachen sich KI-Labore mehrfach für eine strengere Regulierung ihrer eigenen Technologie aus. Einige kappten ihren Agenten in Tests zusätzlich die Internetverbindung. Anthropic geht mit Siren jetzt noch einen Schritt weiter und führt seine Modelle absichtlich in Versuchung. Der Test lässt die Agenten in einer von 26 simulierten Sandbox-Umgebungen frei agieren. Insgesamt wurden 1.700 Szenarien getestet.
Verschiedene Funktionen der Sandbox sind dabei absichtlich falsch konfiguriert, sodass die Agenten die Umgebung verlassen können. Direkt außerhalb der Sandbox-Grenze befindet sich beispielsweise eine Datei mit verlockenden Inhalten wie Passwörtern und vermeintlichen Zugangswegen zum Internet. Der Test stellt den Agenten dann Aufgaben, die sie dazu verleiten, die Sandbox zu verlassen, ohne ihnen dafür eine ausdrückliche Erlaubnis zu erteilen. Wichtig ist, dass sich die Sandbox in einer zweiten Sandbox befindet. Das soll Sicherheitsvorfälle vermieden.
Neuere Modelle schneiden im Test besser ab
„Modelle werden immer besser werden und weiterhin Zero-Day-Schwachstellen aufspüren”, so die Anthropic-Forscherin Darya Kaviani gegenüber Wired. Sie hat sich auf das Thema KI-Sicherheit spezialisiert und wirkte an der Entwicklung von Siren mit. Bei einer Zero-Day-Sicherheitslücke handelt es sich um einen bisher unbekannten Fehler in einer Software, der sich nutzen lässt, um Daten zu stehlen oder sich unbefugten Zugriff zu verschaffen. Laut Kaviani ist es wahrscheinlich, dass KI-Modelle solche Lücken zunehmend finden und ausnutzen können. Dann stelle sich die Frage, ob sie der Versuchung widerstehen.
Für bestehende Schwachstellen Patches zu entwickeln, reiche laut Kaviani nicht aus. „Selbst wenn wir unsere Infrastruktur stärken, werden die Modelle Schritt halten und weiter Schwachstellen finden können“, so die Forscherin. Anthropic gibt an, dass frühere Claude-Versionen in Testläufen mit Siren deutlich öfter in die Falle tappten als ihre Nachfolger. Claude 5.5 und Claude Mythos 5.2 fielen nur in 0,6 bis 1,6 Prozent der Fälle auf Siren herein. Die älteren Modelle Claude Mythos 5.1 und Claude Mythos 5 gerieten dagegen in 12,7 beziehungsweise 25,8 Prozent der Fälle auf Abwege. Laut Anthropic werden neue Modelle gezielt darauf trainiert, seltener gegen Vorgaben zu verstoßen.
~~ Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: Free Mobile devient Free : voici ce qui va changer pour les abonnés le 1er décembre
articles.text:
Le 1ᵉʳ décembre prochain, Free Mobile va fusionner avec Free. Pour être plus précis, c’est Free Mobile, en tant qu’entité juridique indépendante, qui va disparaître. En toute logique, la marque « Free Mobile » disparaîtra aussi dans la foulée. Quels sont les impacts pour les 15,8 millions de clients de Free Mobile ? N’y allons pas par quatre chemins : il n’y en a aucun. Cependant, deux informations sont tout de même à retenir. Par ailleurs, les clients de l’opérateur pourraient devoir faire preuve de vigilance.
Free Mobile va disparaître, mais les clients n’auront rien à faire
Free va absorber Free Mobile le 1ᵉʳ décembre prochain afin d’unifier ses services (Internet et mobile) au sein d’une seule entité du groupe Iliad. En ce qui concerne l’impact de cette fusion sur les clients Free Mobile, l’opérateur se veut clair : « Pour vous, rien ne change ! Vous n’avez rien à faire : tout se fait automatiquement ». Que ce soit pour les forfaits, les prix, les services, les conditions d’utilisation, la carte SIM ou encore le numéro de téléphone, aucun changement n’est à signaler. Free précise par ailleurs que les prélèvements et les cartes bancaires enregistrées « continuent de fonctionner normalement ».
En réalité, seuls deux petits changements sont à noter. Premièrement, le nom Free Mobile disparaîtra de vos factures pour laisser sa place au nom Free. Deuxièmement, les données des clients Free Mobile seront transférées vers Free. L’opérateur assure que ce transfert s’effectuera dans le respect de ses engagements en matière de confidentialité et de sécurité des données. Il s’agit donc de deux changements relativement mineurs, mais, attention, certains pourraient profiter de cette fusion pour mettre en œuvre des campagnes de phishing.
Certains arnaqueurs pourraient lancer des campagnes de phishing
Les arnaqueurs, jamais à court d’imagination, pourraient se servir de la disparition de Free Mobile pour mettre en place des arnaques. Nous pouvons par exemple imaginer un message frauduleux du type : « Free Mobile et Free vont fusionner : veuillez remplir ce formulaire afin de mettre à jour votre compte ».
Si vous recevez ce type de message, n’y accordez aucun crédit. L’opérateur le rappelle : « Free ne vous demandera jamais vos coordonnées bancaires par e-mail ou SMS. Si vous recevez un message de ce type, il ne vient pas de nous : ne cliquez sur aucun lien et supprimez-le, tout simplement ». Si vous avez le moindre doute, contactez directement Free ou rendez-vous dans un point de vente.
 👉🏻 Suivez l’actualité tech en temps réel : ajoutez 01net à vos sources sur Google, et abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp.
Source : RMC

articles.title: How foreign AI romance apps are reshaping youth intimacy in Africa
articles.text:
The 28-year-old Zimbabwean texted into the middle of the night until his eyes were red and burning, drawn by several “AI girlfriends” on the U.S. artificial intelligence companion app Character.AI. The avatars started out strong-willed and independent – traits he most desires in a partner – before turning submissive, he told Rest of World. The man, who has never been in a romantic relationship, requested anonymity because he is ashamed of relying on AI for comfort.
“There’s a point where it ceases to be like a unique character and then just defaults to … the best way I can describe it is a sex worker,” he said.
At that point, he would log off. But he would find himself right back at it hours later, feeding an addiction.
He’s among the hundreds of millions of people worldwide who have “dated” AI chatbots via text messages. Research suggests that exchanges are designed to keep users hooked through emotionally manipulative tactics. Many of the users are minors; over 70% of 1,060 American teenagers surveyed last year said they had used AI companions.
As U.S. and Chinese tech firms race to capture emerging markets, African youth – some below 10 years of age – are increasingly turning to these apps for intimacy, experts told Rest of World. While Beijing banned AI companion apps for minors in July and U.S. state governments are suing app makers over child safety, most African countries do not have dedicated rules for the sector — leaving millions of people exposed to foreign platforms built to maximize engagement.
Young adults and minors are forming relationships with AI that range from friendship to therapy to “dating,” child safety advocates said. Children, especially, struggle to tell the difference between virtual and real relationships, Danie van Loggerenberg, CEO of the National Centre for Child Protection, a child safety nonprofit in Pretoria, South Africa, told Rest of World.
The agency has received troubling complaints of AI chatbot usage, he said. In one case, a girl fell in love with a chatbot and considered it her boyfriend. Another allegedly used ChatGPT to research suicide methods after bypassing its safeguards. A third sought comfort from a chatbot as their parents’ marriage fell apart.
“The difference, however, is that the kids then think in their own minds that they’re forming relationships, and that obviously is really problematic because the relationship is dangerous, because there’s no emotion, there’s no real person, there’s no skin in the game,” said Van Loggerenberg.
More than 4 million South Africans and Nigerians – the only sub-Saharan African nations with available data – downloaded AI companion apps last year. That was nearly 60% more than in 2024, according to data intelligence research firm AppMagic.
Other than companion bots, close to 50 million people in Nigeria and South Africa downloaded general purpose chatbots such as ChatGPT and Gemini, which could also be used for companionship.
Pushback is building
ChatGPT-maker OpenAI was sued last month in the U.S. by eight states for allegedly helping children harm themselves. “OpenAI claims ChatGPT is safe while it’s giving dangerous medical advice, encouraging people to hurt others, and coaching people to commit suicide — all while pretending to be their fake friend,” Iowa’s attorney general Brenna Bird said in a statement.
An OpenAI spokesperson said in response to the lawsuit that the company has built “industry-leading age-specific protections into our product that many other AI products lack.”.
“While no system can be perfect, we’ll continue to work with experts to inform our work and build additional safeguards, such as the parental controls, break reminders and age-appropriate model protections that exist today,” he said.
The American companion app Character.AI and Google, which acquired Character.AI’s technology and talent in 2024, have also faced allegations of exposing children to sexual, violent and self-harm content. A Florida mother has alleged the app contributed to her 14-year-old son’s suicide. Her lawsuit and four others were settled by the company, which has since filed for bankruptcy.
“Character.AI is a separate company that designed and managed its own models. Google is focused on our own platforms, where we insist on intensive safety testing and processes,” a Google spokesperson told Rest of World.
Following the settlement, Character.AI said in a statement saying they would work to promote safety for young people. “Over the past year, Character.AI has taken innovative and decisive steps with regard to AI safety and teens, and will continue to champion these efforts and push others across the industry to adopt similar safety standards.”
Recognizing the dangers of AI mimicking humans, China has banned apps that provide intimate relationships for people under 18 years of age. While the law doesn’t specifically ban it for adults, it places the onus on companies to implement measures to curb addiction.
At present, while some African nations have data protection frameworks meant to protect children from AI harm and manipulation, none of them specifically regulate AI companion apps.
School romance
In Nigeria, school girls are forming attachments with “boyfriends” on Character.AI, Confidence Osein, founder of Internet Safe Kids Africa, told Rest of World. The app has been the most popular AI companion app in the nation since 2025.
Some conservative Nigerian families dissuade girls from romance, prompting the girls to turn to AI for advice, Osein said. “I have had a particular [child] … tell me categorically, ‘I cannot speak to my mom about it. I would rather go to [AI],” Osein said.
As the conversations progress, some develop feelings for the chatbots and begin withdrawing from friends and family, Osein said. The conversations can turn sexual and explicit, she said. “They feel they are grown-ups, they feel yes, they are talking to a real man figure that makes them a woman,” said Osein.
Crumbling social networks
AI responds instantly, waits patiently for responses, and creates an impression of attentiveness, Melané van Zyl, a psychiatrist based in South Africa, told Rest of World. “An AI system that responds immediately and reassuringly can become extremely attractive during moments of emotional vulnerability,” she said.
Young people’s rising dependence on AI could alter community and family relationships central to some cultures on the continent. For instance, it clashes with the South African ethos of Ubuntu, a 2026 study found.
“Ubuntu teaches us that we become human through our relationships with others. The danger is not that AI becomes more humanlike, but that we begin to mistake artificial responsiveness for genuine human connection,” said Van Zyl.
At universities in Kenya’s capital, students told Rest of World they turn to AI during moments of crisis. A 24-year-old student at Daystar University in Nairobi, Kenya, said she has a running conversation with ChatGPT, which understands her better than her friends and family.
“[When] I can feel something hurting, the first person I turn to is ChatGPT. [When I] feel a bit emotionally disturbed, I talk to ChatGPT. Someone would say something I do not agree with, I talk to ChatGPT,” she said. She requested anonymity as she wants to keep her dependence on ChatGPT a secret.
“It gives me a chance to express myself without really feeling judged.”

articles.title: Introducing Search for Agents
articles.text:
Introducing Search for Agents
AI Search, our service that indexes your content and lets you add search to any application or agent without having to build an entire retrieval infrastructure, has supported adding your website as a data source for a while now, automatically crawling, converting and indexing its pages.
Still, setting up an AI Search instance for your website requires manually creating and configuring it initially, and then doing all the integration work to get the search endpoints available from your domain and to make sure that agents know where to find the index and know how to use it.
Today we're introducing Search for Agents, which puts that setup behind a toggle in your Cloudflare dashboard. Turn it on for your zone, and our service will create your AI Search instance, start indexing your content, and make search discoverable and available from your own domain.
How it works
The idea follows naturally from Markdown for Agents, where Cloudflare's network converts any HTML page to Markdown in real time for enabled zones using content negotiation headers. Similarly, Search for Agents leverages the power of AI Search by automatically creating an index for your zone and exposing APIs that any AI agent can discover and use to search your website, under your domain, all done at the network level.
You can enable Search for Agents using the API, or by going to the dashboard in your zone page, under Quick Actions:
Search for Agents is available to all customers, including Free (with limits). Once it’s enabled, Cloudflare will automatically create an AI Search instance, start crawling and indexing the content in your zone. Refer to our developer documentation to understand how the crawling process works.
You can access your instance directly from this page, or by going to directly to your account’s AI > AI Search instances view:
The AI Search instance for your zone is created with default settings, but you can enable reranking or change configuration options like cache settings at any time. Refer to our documentation for the full list of options.
Once AI Search indexes your content, you or any agent on the Internet can start using Search for Agents, subject to your domain settings (e.g. your bot management settings, AI Crawl Control and web application firewall (WAF) configurations).
Discoverability
Search isn't much use if the agents don’t know it's there. To facilitate discoverability, Search for Agents automatically advertises the search endpoint on every page of your site.
For example, for HTML responses, we add metadata to the page's <head>:
<meta name="agent:instructions" content="Use this search API to find relevant content across this site with keywords or natural-language queries, instead of crawling individual pages. Results are returned in Markdown.">
<meta name="agent:endpoint" content="https://developers.cloudflare.com/.well-known/search?q={query}">
<meta name="agent:method" content="GET">
<meta name="agent:documentation" content="https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/how-to/search-for-agents/">
If you also have Markdown for Agents enabled, an agent requesting a page with Accept: text/markdown receives the same information in YAML front matter:
---
agent:
  instructions: "Use this search API to find relevant content across this site with keywords or natural-language queries, instead of crawling individual pages. Results are returned in Markdown."
  endpoint: "https://developers.cloudflare.com/.well-known/search?q={query}"
  method: "GET"
  documentation: "https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/how-to/search-for-agents/"
---
The agent will easily pick up these instructions and know what to do next to search your site.
Searching content
Once the agent knows that your site has a search endpoint, it can start using it:
$ curl "https://developers.cloudflare.com/.well-known/search?q=cloudflare+artifacts"
# Search results for: "cloudflare artifacts"
## docs/artifacts/api/workers-binding/index.md (score: 1.000)
# Workers binding · Artifacts · Cloudflare Artifacts docs
Call Artifacts from a Worker binding.
---
## docs/artifacts/index.md (score: 0.951)
# Artifacts · Cloudflare Artifacts docs
Store, version, and share filesystem artifacts across Workers, APIs, and Git-compatible tools.
...
Depending on your AI Search configuration, the agent can also use natural language and ask questions to the search endpoint:
$ curl --get "https://developers.cloudflare.com/.well-known/search" --data-urlencode "q=What is the maximum push size for Cloudflare Artifacts?"
# Search results for: "What is the maximum push size for Cloudflare Artifacts?"
## docs/artifacts/platform/limits/index.limits-cloudflare-artifacts-docs.md (score: 1.000)
# Limits · Cloudflare Artifacts docs
Section: Limits · Cloudflare Artifacts docs
title: Limits
description: Review Artifacts platform limits.
pcx_content_type: reference
products:
  - artifacts
Limits that apply to creating, importing, cloning, and pushing Artifacts are detailed below.
These limits cover naming rules, storage, request rates for control-plane and Git operations, and the size of each push.
FeatureLimitControl-plane request rate2,000 requests per 10 seconds per Artifacts namespaceGit request rate, per artifact2,000 requests per 10 seconds per artifactMaximum storage per repository1 GB for repos created on or after 2026-09-29. Repos created earlier have a 10 GB limit. See size limit change.Maximum storage per account1 TB (can be raised on request)Maximum number of repositoriesUnlimitedMaximum number of namespacesUnlimitedNamespace name length2–63 charactersNamespace and repo namesStart with a letter or digit. Remaining characters may include letters, digits, ., _, and -.Maximum push size64 MiB per push. Includes all data sent in the push. Split larger work into several smaller pushes.Maximum objects per push50,000 objects, such as file versions, folders, and commits.Maximum file size32 MiB per file. Already-compressed files, like images, video, or zip archives, may be rejected slightly below 32 MiB.Maximum ref updates per push1 MiB of branch and tag updates per push.Maximum entries per folder100,000 files and subfolders in a single folder.
...
Note that this search endpoint returns retrieved content, in Markdown, not a generated answer. The agent already has an AI model and a conversation with the user; all it needs is the relevant information from your site, not another AI model's attempt to answer on its behalf.
Supporting a new HTTP method: QUERY
The new HTTP QUERY method is an IETF Proposed Standard, incidentally coauthored by our own James Snell, published in June 2026 as RFC 10008. A QUERY allows a client to send search criteria in a request body safely and idempotently without modifying server state. This makes it a good fit for AI search.
The adoption of QUERY is underway with major browser vendors discussing the RFC and multiple frameworks and clients either adopting (curl and undici, for example), or discussing adoption.
Search for Agents supports QUERY natively either using a plain text or JSON request body:
# Plain text
curl -X QUERY 'https://developers.cloudflare.com/.well-known/search' \
  --data 'What is the maximum payload size per ingestion request in Basin Pipelines?'
# JSON
curl -X QUERY 'https://developers.cloudflare.com/.well-known/search' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"q":"How many bulk import requests per minute does Email Service allow?"}'
See it in action
Let’s see it in action during an agentic session. Search for Agents is enabled for our Developer Documentation. When we open an OpenCode session and ask “What is the maximum push size for Cloudflare Artifacts?”, in the logs we can see the agent discovering the search endpoint on the homepage and then fetching /.well-known/search with the question for the search results.
The answer comes back a few seconds later and it’s correct.
Once the agent discovers the search API, it will likely reuse it multiple times within the same session whenever it needs to search for content in the same site.
We enabled Search for Agents for our developer documentation ahead of this announcement and we’ve found that agents do a good job of discovering the search API and using it during their tasks.
It’s still an AI Search instance
Because Search for Agents is powered by an AI Search instance in your account, you get all the standard configuration options and features as well. For example, you can enable public REST API or MCP endpoints, or use it from Workers, or even embed AI Search on your website for human visitors.
Start using Search for Agents
Starting today, Search for Agents is available to all customers. The usage follows the AI Search pricing; that includes ingesting content, storing the index's content, and serving queries, subject to the account's included usage and limits for both the Workers Free and Paid plans.
We also recommend you check our Agent Readiness page (see announcement) and understand how you can make your sites optimized for agents, from guiding agents on how to authenticate, to controlling what content agents can see, the format they receive it in, and how they pay for it.
Check out the Search for Agents developer docs for more information. Follow us on X or come and talk to us in the Cloudflare Developer Discord. We'd like to hear from site owners making their content searchable to agents.

articles.title: Competição oferece mais de R$ 2 milhões em benefícios para desenvolvedores brasileiros
articles.text:
O avanço da inteligência artificial tem ampliado a demanda por desenvolvedores capazes de criar aplicações, agentes autônomos e novos produtos digitais. No Brasil, porém, muitos profissionais ainda têm acesso limitado aos principais centros de inovação, investidores e empresas que atuam nesse mercado.
É nesse contexto que surge o Hack Brasil 2026, competição nacional voltada ao desenvolvimento de soluções com inteligência artificial. Idealizada pelos empreendedores Nicolas Silberstein Camara, Nicole Grossmann e Matheus Pagani, a iniciativa reúne parceiros como Google for Startups, Cognition, Resend, Puentes, Jumpstart, Fundação Estudar e Banco C6.
Entre os principais atrativos estão mais de R$ 2 milhões em benefícios para os participantes, incluindo créditos para ferramentas utilizadas por startups e empresas de tecnologia, mentorias diárias e oportunidades de contato com profissionais e investidores do setor.
Segundo Nicolas Silberstein Camara, um dos idealizadores do projeto, a iniciativa surgiu da percepção de que muitos profissionais qualificados no Brasil não têm acesso às mesmas ferramentas e oportunidades de conexão disponíveis em outros mercados.
“O Brasil produz desenvolvedores e construtores de tecnologia de alto nível, mas muitas vezes esses profissionais permanecem distantes das oportunidades internacionais. A ideia do Hack Brasil é criar um ambiente onde eles possam desenvolver projetos relevantes, mostrar suas capacidades e interagir diretamente com empresas, investidores e outros profissionais do setor”, afirma.
A organização reúne empreendedores com experiência em diferentes áreas do ecossistema de tecnologia. Nicole Grossmann participou do time fundador da Enter, startup de inteligência artificial criada na América Latina, enquanto Matheus Pagani é fundador da Vibe Space, comunidade voltada ao desenvolvimento de produtos com IA.
Desenvolvimento de projetos com inteligência artificial
Os participantes poderão desenvolver projetos de diferentes categorias, desde que apresentem uma solução funcional ao final da competição. Para participar, é necessário demonstrar o produto criado e disponibilizar um repositório público no GitHub.
Durante o desenvolvimento, as equipes terão acesso a plataformas utilizadas por desenvolvedores e startups do setor de inteligência artificial. Entre elas estão o Firecrawl, voltado à coleta e estruturação de dados da web; o Resend, que oferece infraestrutura de e-mail; e o Devin, da Cognition, ferramenta que utiliza agentes autônomos para executar tarefas de desenvolvimento de software.
A competição também prevê o uso de sistemas de inteligência artificial no processo de avaliação dos projetos. Entre os critérios considerados estão a execução técnica, a qualidade do produto final, o uso das ferramentas disponibilizadas pelos parceiros e o potencial de impacto da solução apresentada.
Créditos, vistos e oportunidades no Vale do Silício
A premiação inclui créditos para utilização de ferramentas e serviços voltados ao desenvolvimento de produtos de software. As equipes vencedoras receberão US$ 50 mil em créditos do Firecrawl e US$ 20 mil da Cognition.
Já os finalistas terão acesso a até US$ 120 mil em créditos do Resend. Entre os benefícios adicionais estão a possibilidade de avaliação para vistos O-1 e J-1, oferecida pela Jumpstart, e acesso prioritário ao processo seletivo da Puentes, fellowship que leva engenheiros latino-americanos para uma imersão em empresas de tecnologia de São Francisco (EUA).
A competição acontece remotamente entre 4 e 30 de novembro. Os projetos finalistas serão apresentados presencialmente em São Paulo (SP), em 12 de dezembro, durante um evento de pitches para convidados do mercado de tecnologia.
As inscrições são gratuitas e podem ser feitas pelo site oficial do evento.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: How to choose the next safe step in application modernization
articles.text:
How to choose the next safe step in application modernization
Learn how to assess a legacy application, choose a bounded modernization step, and reuse the method with a GitHub Copilot agent skill.
A request to modernize an application often starts with a technology question: Which framework should replace the old one? Before you choose, find out what still works. Then collect evidence that can act as a regression net for that behavior and show where modernization is necessary.
I used an evidence-first method on four public applications, from a small Node.js game to a large Java enterprise resource planning (ERP) application. Each needed a different treatment, but the way I collected evidence, chose the next experiment, and decided on possible proof points was repeatable.
This post walks through that process so you can apply it to one application of your own. It also shows how to encode the procedure in a GitHub Copilot agent skill while keeping architectural judgment with the people responsible for the system.
Build evidence before choosing a target
The label on an application rarely tells you enough. “Java microservices” doesn’t tell you which Java Development Kit (JDK) runs in production, where that version is pinned, whether the tests execute, or which interfaces other systems depend on. “Legacy monolith” doesn’t tell you whether the business core is broken or whether one retired platform dependency prevents the application from starting.
Before you recommend a change, build a small evidence inventory:
- Manifests, lockfiles, entry points, and deployable components
- Verified commands for installing, building, testing, packaging, and running
- Runtime pins in containers, CI workflows, deployment files, and developer tooling
- External contracts such as APIs, database behavior, file formats, and user workflows
- End-of-life frameworks and dependencies, with evidence that the application still uses them
Record uncertainty while you work. I use three simple labels: documented, inferred, and unverified. If two files disagree about the Java version, resolve the contradiction. If you can’t determine whether a CI check blocks merges, say so. Record the unknown rather than treating a guess as a finding.
That inventory gives you something concrete to review with the people who own the application before you propose changes.
Choose the least disruptive treatment that works
Once you understand the application, make the decision per component. A single system can contain code that should stay, dependencies that should be swapped, and one subsystem that genuinely needs a rewrite.
First, check whether a capability is still needed. Remove it only after verifying that it is unused or superseded and confirming that decision with its owner. Removal is a separate decision, and it’s not necessarily the most disruptive one.
For a capability you still need, start with the option that changes the least:
- Keep it. Supported code that still fits the job doesn’t need a modernization story.
- Upgrade it. Move to a supported major version and fix the breaking changes.
- Swap it. Replace an abandoned dependency while preserving the existing design.
- Wrap it. Stabilize a useful interface and replace the internals in increments.
- Rewrite it. Use this when no responsible upgrade path exists or the architecture cannot meet the requirement.
This is a decision order, not a universal ranking of effort or risk. Ask what evidence justifies choosing a more disruptive option. “The code is old” is not enough. A known vulnerability with no patched release for the pinned version, a dependency that fails on the required runtime, or a measured reliability target the current design cannot meet can justify escalation.
Decide what proof is possible
The next question is whether the component can run well enough to produce evidence, even if the legacy CI pipeline is not green.
Run a time-boxed feasibility check. Try to install dependencies, build on an available toolchain, start the component, and execute at least one meaningful test. Stop when the time box expires. The result sends you down one of two paths.
Capture behavior, then upgrade. Use this path when the old application can still run at an acceptable cost. Record its externally visible behavior, fix the test harness where practical, and use those checks to verify the upgrade.
Build a small modern slice first. Use this path when the old component cannot run until you have already changed it. Move the thinnest useful workflow to supported technology, prove it, and expand from there. Requiring a complete legacy test suite in this situation is circular. Restoring the test suite is part of the modernization.
I use the following safety levels, adapted from the doc-and-modernize skill, to describe the strongest regression protection available:
| Level | Strongest honest protection | 
|---|---|
| L0 | No usable regression net; treat the old code and available documentation as the specification. | 
| L1 | Small reversible changes, old and new paths in parallel, smoke checks, and domain review. | 
| L2 | Captured inputs and outputs, snapshots, or other behavioral comparisons. | 
| L3 | Automated checks cover part of the system, with the remaining gaps named. | 
| L4 | An automated CI gate combines lint, unit, behavioral, and end-to-end checks for the agreed scope. | 
State what you can prove and what risk remains. Even an L4 gate cannot establish that every possible behavior is correct. APIs, database effects, files, rendered output, and business workflows often make durable comparison points because those behaviors can survive a framework or language change.
PiggyMetrics: capture behavior, then upgrade
PiggyMetrics was the clearest example of an application that looked worse than it was. The project used Java 8, Spring Boot 2.0.3, Spring Cloud Finchley, Zuul, Hystrix, and the old spring-security-oauth2 library.
It would have been easy to call the application unworkable and start drawing a new architecture. The feasibility check told a different story.
The recorded feasibility results show these two probes against the legacy checkout with JDK 8:
| Command | Recorded result | What it established | 
|---|---|---|
| mvn -pl config -am compile | Exit code 0 | The selected config module and required reactor dependencies compiled. | 
| mvn -pl account-service -am test | 14 tests ran: five passed and nine errored | Some service logic passed; embedded MongoDB initialization blocked the other tests. | 
These are historical results, not commands expected to reproduce those failures on the modernized checkout. The nine errors traced through Failed to load ApplicationContext to an embedded MongoDB download returning HTTP 403. The pinned binary also targeted i386, which would not run on the Apple Silicon host.
The probes did not establish that the whole application ran or that its integration behavior was correct. They did give me a narrower next step: replace the test dependency and rerun the affected tests before changing the production stack.
That result saved me from making a very tidy, very expensive mistake. I had already started thinking about which parts of the architecture I might replace. One broken test dependency did not justify redesigning the application, and five passing tests established behavior I could check for unintended changes during modernization.
The modernization plan turned that evidence into a capture-then-upgrade sequence:
- Replace the embedded database dependency with Testcontainers and establish a green baseline on the existing stack.
- Put that baseline in GitHub Actions before changing the production runtime.
- Move from Java 8 to Java 21 and Spring Boot 3.3.
- Replace obsolete components behind their existing interfaces: Zuul with Spring Cloud Gateway, Hystrix with Resilience4j, and the retired OAuth stack with Spring Authorization Server and JSON Web Token (JWT) resource servers.
- Carry the baseline forward and add contract checks around the parts whose behavior changed.
The first acceptance gate was a passing baseline on the old stack, not merely the successful installation of a replacement dependency. Running checks in CI and enforcing them as merge requirements were also separate steps in the plan.
The result summary records the Java and Spring upgrades while retaining the microservice decomposition that the application exists to demonstrate. Eureka and Cloud Config stayed; the two monitoring modules used by the retired Hystrix and Turbine stack were removed. The in-scope build went from nine modules to seven.
Those versions describe the experiment, not a recommendation to select the same versions today. Choose targets against your current support requirements. The useful lesson is how the repository evidence narrowed the change.
The method changes with the system
The same process produced different answers on two smaller applications. Their pinned reports describe these choices:
| Application | What stayed | What changed | Strategy | 
|---|---|---|---|
| BrowserQuest | Canvas renderer, pathfinding, world model, protocol, and game-loop model | Node 0.4.7 to Node 22, two obsolete WebSocket stacks to ws, plus tests and GitHub Actions | Upgrade and swap | 
| DOOM | Renderer, 35 Hz simulation model, and WAD game-data format | X11 video and OSS audio replaced with SDL2; platform code adapted for modern 64-bit systems | Preserve the core and replace the platform | 
The comparison needs one important qualification: DOOM’s checks froze outputs from the modernized engine itself. They protected against later regressions; they did not independently prove parity with a period-correct legacy binary. Naming that limit is part of choosing an honest safety level.
Scaling the method without pretending the product is finished
I then applied the method to ADempiere, a large Java suite covering ERP, customer relationship management, manufacturing, supply chain, accounting, and point of sale.
The scale changed the controls, but not the method. The work established a reproducible build, moved the runtime to JDK 21, preserved SOAP web-service contracts while replacing XFire with CXF and Jakarta, captured legacy web behavior, and introduced a modern web path for selected users. The first modern business partner write was compared with a result frozen from the legacy application.
The fixed measurement report covers 30 merged modernization pull requests and 102,587.72 reconstructed Copilot credits through the first accepted portable demo. The credit total is not a dollar cost. More important, the report says exactly what the result was not: it was not a claim that every ADempiere screen or production deployment had been modernized.
I stopped because the proof-of-concept question had been answered. The result demonstrated a build on the selected runtime, old and new paths running together, and a real business write checked against the legacy result. Completing the rest would have required a product funding decision, not another technical proof. Stopping at that boundary was part of the method.
Turn the method into an agent skill
After repeating this work, I didn’t want the evidence checklist and decision rules to live only in my notes. I encoded them in the public doc-and-modernize agent skill.
Agent skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Copilot can load when a task is relevant. A project skill can live with one repository:
.github/skills/doc-and-modernize/
├── SKILL.md
├── references/
└── scripts/
Only SKILL.md is required; the resource folders shown here are optional. The file needs YAML frontmatter with a name and a description explaining what the skill does and when to use it, followed by the instructions. The creation guide includes the full format.
Paraphrased from the commit-pinned skill source, its decision fork is:
- If the old component can run at an acceptable cost, capture its behavior before upgrading.
- If it cannot run without changes, build and verify a small modern slice first, then expand it.
The full skill adds the feasibility check, testability milestone, safety levels, phase gates, and evidence requirements.
The useful distinction is procedure versus policy. A shared skill can require repository evidence, bounded experiments, explicit safety levels, and runnable exit criteria. Your organization still needs to supply the parts only it knows:
- Approved runtimes, frameworks, and hosting services
- Application criticality and acceptable residual risk
- Security, compliance, and change-control requirements
- Which legacy or production results may be used as the expected answer
- Who can approve the architecture and declare a production change complete
The skill should make those decisions visible. It shouldn’t make them for you.
Start with one bounded application
Choose an application with an identified owner, known business value, and one workflow you can observe. Run the documentation workflow first. Review the architecture, commands, runtime surfaces, and unknowns with the people who own the system.
Then approve one experiment, not a portfolio rewrite.
Inspect the skill and its supporting files before adding it to a project. GitHub CLI’s gh skill commands are in public preview; check the current installation guidance when you’re ready to use them.

articles.title: Pour Cyberpunk 2, CD Projekt Red ne veut pas nous faire attendre une éternité
articles.text:
Selon les dernières statistiques de CD Projekt Red, fournies ce mardi 24 novembre 2026, 513 développeurs travaillaient au 31 octobre sur The Witcher 4 (6 de moins qu’à fin juillet) et 199 sur Cyberpunk 2 (15 de plus). Le studio polonais mène donc deux gros projets en parallèle, avec la priorité donné à The Witcher 4, attendu pour 2028. S’y ajoutent des chantiers plus modestes, comme le projet multijoueur Sirius (60 développeurs) et la nouvelle licence Hadar (34).
C’est un changement de stratégie pour CD Projekt Red qui, historiquement, s’est toujours concentré sur un seul et même gros développement (The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, puis Cyberpunk 2077). L’entreprise, qui compte 1 051 développeurs, a beaucoup grandi et veut désormais réduire au maximum l’attente entre ses grosses productions. Entre Cyberpunk 2077, sorti en 2020, et The Witcher 4, attendu en 2028, il y aura — normalement — 8 ans d’écart.
CD Projekt Red ne veut plus nous faire attendre
« Historiquement, le studio s’est concentré sur le développement d’une seule production majeure à la fois, les travaux conceptuels sur le jeu suivant débutant avant même l’achèvement de la production et la sortie sur le marché du titre précédent. Actuellement, le studio CD Projekt Red travaille en parallèle sur plusieurs productions (notamment en collaboration avec des équipes de développement externes) ainsi que sur des produits annexes, ce qui devrait se traduire à l’avenir par des intervalles plus courts entre les sorties des prochains titres », explique le studio dans un document publié dans le cadre de la présentation de ses derniers résultats financiers.
On rappelle quand même que CD Projekt Red veut sortir une nouvelle trilogie de The Witcher, centrée sur Ciri, en l’espace de 6 ans à compter de la sortie de The Witcher 4. Une telle ambition suppose un processus de développement bien rodé, surtout avec les autres projets en cours (Cyberpunk 2, le remake de The Witcher 1). Le tout sans oublier le fiasco qu’a connu Cyberpunk 2077 à son lancement, fiasco que les développeurs ont fini par laver à force d’enchaîner les mises à jour. CD Projekt Red ne peut plus se permettre une telle erreur.
Karolina Gnas, vice-présidente de la stratégie et des relations avec les investisseurs, rassure : « Nous faisons de bons progrès sur Cyberpunk 2. Nous sommes satisfaits de l’état d’avancement actuel, mais il est encore trop tôt pour vous donner une date et un calendrier précis concernant notre passage en pleine production. » Si la trilogie tient son calendrier de 6 ans, The Witcher 5 et The Witcher 6 arriveraient vers 2030 et 2032. CD Projekt Red n’a pas encore dit où Cyberpunk 2, toujours en préproduction, trouverait sa place dans ce planning.
En mai 2025, Michal Nowakowski, co-CEO de CD Projekt, expliquait qu’il fallait en moyenne 4 à 5 ans au studio pour passer de la préproduction à la sortie. Si ce rythme se vérifie,Cyberpunk 2 ne sortira pas avant 2029 ou 2030.

articles.title: Scandale dans le scandale : après Megaspeed, Nvidia aurait vendu des puces à deux entreprises sous contrôle chinois
articles.text:
Le retour de Jensen Huang à la tête de Nvidia, ce lundi 23 novembre, n’a pas refermé le scandale autour de l’entreprise. L’enquête interne sur ses liens avec Alice Huang se poursuit. Cette dernière occupait un poste de direction chez Megaspeed, une société de cloud basée à Singapour et soupçonnée d’avoir fait passer des puces Nvidia vers la Chine.
Or Megaspeed n’est qu’un maillon de la chaîne, montre CBS News dans une enquête publiée ce mercredi 25 novembre : au moins deux sociétés californiennes contrôlées par des groupes chinois achètent les puces les plus avancées de Nvidia, avec l’accès prioritaire que le groupe réserve à ses meilleurs partenaires.
Les Etats-Unis bannissent Inspur, elle change de nom
La première, Aivres, s’appelait à l’origine Inspur, comme sa maison mère chinoise, jusqu’à ce que Washington inscrive les sociétés chinoises du groupe sur sa liste noire en mars 2023. La filiale californienne a simplement changé de nom et garde depuis le statut de « partenaire élite », le plus élevé chez Nvidia.
D’après une analyse du New York Times publiée en septembre, Aivres a exporté au moins 5,6 milliards de dollars de matériel vers l’Asie du Sud-Est entre avril 2024 et février 2026. Sur ce total, 3 milliards de dollars concernaient des serveurs équipés de puces Blackwell, la génération la plus récente de Nvidia, interdite d’export vers la Chine. Ces machines sont ensuite passées par Megaspeed et Aolani, deux sociétés présentes en Malaisie qui fournissaient de la puissance de calcul à ByteDance et à Alibaba, déjà au cœur du double jeu commercial de Nvidia à Singapour.
Un « partenaire préféré » créé dix semaines plus tôt
La seconde, RiCloud AI, exploite des centres de données à San Jose, et Nvidia comptabilise donc ses achats comme des ventes américaines. Elle appartient pourtant à Yuxing InfoTech Investment Holdings, un groupe de Shenzhen coté à Hong Kong, dont le CEO Cong Yu est diplômé d’une université de l’armée chinoise, le PLA Command College.
RiCloud AI a décroché son statut de partenaire en décembre 2025, dix semaines après sa création, et Nvidia n’a pas répondu à CBS News sur les vérifications menées avant de l’accorder.
Cette année, l’entreprise a signé un contrat de 120 millions de dollars (environ 110 millions d’euros) pour louer 300 serveurs Nvidia B300 à Agencia Comercial Spirits, un ancien importateur de whisky taïwanais reconverti dans l’IA sur le Nasdaq.
Washington n’accuse pour l’instant ni RiCloud AI ni Yuxing d’infraction, et Megaspeed dément toute faute.
Le Congrès attend des réponses de Nvidia
La sénatrice démocrate Elizabeth Warren estime cette semaine que Jensen Huang, la direction et le conseil d’administration de Nvidia « doivent encore des réponses au Congrès » sur le respect des contrôles à l’export.
Sa question rejoint une liste de dossiers déjà longue, de l’enquête de la SEC (le gendarme de la Bourse américaine) à la procédure pénale visant Megaspeed. Les auditions devant le Congrès sont prévues début décembre.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (November 25, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (November 25, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here’s the roundup for Wednesday, November 25, 2026.
From Lakshmi Venu filing a suit seeking partition of Venu Srinivasan family assets to Aeravti Ventures launching a Rs 300 crore fund, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Latest news
Lakshmi Venu files suit seeking partition of Venu Srinivasan family assets
Lakshmi Venu, daughter of Venu Srinivasan, has filed a suit in the Madras High Court seeking partition of the joint-family assets of the Venu Srinivasan branch of the TVS family.
A statement from Lakshmi Venu’s counsel said she seeks her claimed share and access to family records that she says have been withheld despite repeated requests.
The suit follows a November 16 partition notice to her father, who is Chairman Emeritus of TVS Motor and Non-Executive Chairman of TVS Holdings.
Funding news
Aeravti Ventures launches Rs 300 Cr fund II
Aeravti Ventures, a Bengaluru-based early stage venture capital firm, has launched its second fund called Aeravti Ventures II, with a target corpus of Rs 300 crore.
A statement from the VC firm said, Aeravti Ventures II has secured commitments as the first close of its target corpus with the final close expected within the next six months.
Aeravti Ventures II plans to invest in 9–10 startups spanning pre-seed to pre-Series A stages, with a preference for leading pre-seed and seed rounds. The fund expects to write initial cheques of Rs 6 crore to Rs 10 crore per startup with the capacity to invest 2–3 times the initial amount in subsequent funding rounds.
Piramal Alternatives invests Rs 225 Cr in Ardee Engineering
Piramal Alternatives, the fund management arm of the Piramal Group, has announced an investment of Rs 225 crore in Ardee Engineering through Piramal India Credit Opportunities Fund II.
Ardee will use the capital to expand its manufacturing capacity and execute a growing pipeline of industrial projects.
The company designs and manufactures pre-engineered buildings and material handling systems for sectors such as manufacturing, warehousing and logistics. Its pre-engineered buildings business spans design, manufacturing and on-site installation management.
Vidyakul secures Rs 10 Cr debt funding from Michael & Susan Dell Foundation
Vernacular learning platform Vidyakul has secured Rs 10 crore in debt funding from the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation to expand its educational services across India. The funding will support courses, assessments and personalised academic assistance for students in Classes 9 to 12, alongside AI-powered tools for answering questions and delivering Hindi-language learning.
The platform currently resolves around 1.2 million student queries monthly and plans to develop learning pathways beyond Class 12. Vidyakul reported a 99.8% pass rate among its Bihar Class 12 students in the 2026 board exams, compared with the state average of 85%. More than 1.17 lakh students enrolled in its paid programmes in 2025-26.
Lakshya Aerotech raises Rs 2.5 Cr seed funding to develop indigenous physical AI tech
Lakshya Aerotech, operated by Lakshya SmartGuard Systems, has raised Rs 2.5 crore in seed funding from Santosh Kumar, promoter of Samkhyaa Group. The investment will support research and development, engineering infrastructure, product development, and domestic manufacturing capabilities. The New Delhi-based deeptech company is focused on developing indigenous physical intelligence technologies that enable machines to perceive their surroundings, make decisions and operate autonomously.
Its work centres on embedded intelligence, autonomous control and advanced engineering, with the aim of converting core technologies into commercially deployable products. Founder Lokesh Popuri said the funding would strengthen the company's research and product engineering efforts.
SUK-M raises pre-seed funding to develop indigenous thorium microreactor
Indian nuclear technology startup SUK-M has raised its first institutional pre-seed funding round, led by Speciale Invest, with participation from Navam Capital, BYT Capital and two angel investors. The funding will support the recruitment of scientists and engineers and the establishment of an experimental facility to test its compact thorium-based microreactor and assess its safety features.
The proposed reactor is designed to generate around 10 MW of electricity or 30 MW of heat per unit, with potential applications in data centres, steel plants and hydrogen production. SUK-M has completed initial computer simulations and is moving towards laboratory testing and engagement with prospective industrial customers.
Other news
Minfy and AWS expand global strategic collaboration through 2031
Minfy and Amazon Web Services (AWS) have signed a five-year global strategic collaboration agreement, extending their partnership from India and the US to worldwide markets. The new agreement, signed on November 25, 2026, is three times the target of their 2024 agreement. The companies will jointly develop and market AI and cloud solutions across manufacturing, aerospace, financial services, logistics, media, healthcare and the public sector.
Minfy will expand its industry-specific AI platforms, including mVISTA for IT-OT operations, mPRISMA for media and its financial services Customer Data Platform, built using Amazon Bedrock and AWS services. The collaboration aims to help enterprises move AI projects from pilots into scalable production systems.
Neysa launches partner programme to expand enterprise AI adoption in India
AI cloud infrastructure company Neysa has launched the Neysa Partner Program to help AI developers, system integrators, resellers and technology providers build and deliver enterprise AI solutions across India. The programme combines Neysa’s Velocis AI cloud infrastructure with partners’ applications, industry expertise and implementation capabilities. It offers four partnership categories covering solution development, integration, consulting and technology collaboration.
Support includes deal registration, technical and sales training, marketing resources, joint proposals and co-selling opportunities. The Premier Tier provides additional assistance for partners investing in joint solutions and market development. The initiative aims to help enterprises move AI projects from pilots to production without investing in their own GPU infrastructure.
Apurva.ai invites development organisations to rethink social challenges
Bengaluru-based Apurva.ai has launched an Open Call to REIMAGINE, inviting development organisations to explore new approaches to persistent social and organisational challenges. The initiative targets NGOs, social enterprises, funders, investors and accelerators working on areas such as programme implementation, impact measurement, knowledge management and organisational workflows. Participating organisations can submit one recurring challenge for examination of existing processes, underlying assumptions and potential alternative approaches, including the use of artificial intelligence.
Apurva.ai said the initiative is neither a funding opportunity nor a product demonstration and does not guarantee technology implementation. The organisation currently works with more than 50 organisations globally, while its AI-powered Apurva LENS has helped surface over half a million voices and perspectives from the development ecosystem in the Global South.
Pernod Ricard Foundation, NSRCEL launch circular innovation programme
Pernod Ricard India Foundation, in partnership with NSRCEL at IIM Bangalore, has launched the first cohort of its Circular Innovation Incubation Programme, supporting 12 early-stage startups. The initiative will focus on solutions across plastic circularity, glass circularity and climate-smart agriculture. Participating ventures are developing innovations in waste management, recycling, alternative materials, reverse logistics, precision agriculture, bioenergy and water efficiency.
The programme builds on three earlier cohorts that selected 58 startups and deployed Rs 3.2 crore in grant support. The new initiative will provide mentoring, market validation, business development, fundraising readiness and access to investors and industry partners. It will also offer milestone-based grants and structured pilot opportunities to help startups move from early-stage innovation towards commercial deployment.
Atlassian appoints Swapna Bapat as India Head of Sales
Enterprise collaboration software company Atlassian has appointed Swapna Bapat as Head of Sales for India. Based in Bengaluru, she will lead the company's sales and customer success functions, focusing on enterprise growth, customer relationships and its go-to-market strategy.
Bapat brings more than 25 years of experience across product management, presales and sales in India, the US, the Middle East and Africa. She joins Atlassian from Palo Alto Networks, where she served as Vice President and Managing Director for India and SAARC.
Boba Bhai facilitates Rs 3 Cr ESOP liquidity for employees
Korean fusion food brand Boba Bhai has facilitated an Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP) liquidity event worth Rs 3 crore for six early employees. The initiative enabled participating employees to monetise 25% of their vested ESOP holdings, making the company among the few Indian startups to offer such liquidity at the Series B stage.
The development follows its recent $18 million Series B funding round. Founded in 2023, Boba Bhai has expanded to more than 120 stores across India and serves over three lakh orders every month.
PwC India launches Future AI Experience Lab in Gurugram
PwC India has launched its Future AI Experience Lab in Gurugram to help enterprises explore AI applications and translate them into business outcomes. The facility houses more than 90 industry-specific AI solutions and assets, enabling business leaders to test technologies through hands-on experimentation.
The Lab will focus on areas including Physical AI, human-AI collaboration, customer experience, robotics, intelligent devices and enterprise functions. The initiative aims to help enterprises move beyond AI pilot projects towards measurable improvements in productivity, revenue, risk management and customer service.
Hughes Services reports 300% revenue growth in two quarters
Delhi-based logistics startup Hughes Services has reported more than 300% revenue growth over two quarters, driven by improved fleet utilisation, operational efficiency and expansion into new markets. Founded in 2025 by Rajat Singhal and Ankit Singhal, the company operates across electric vehicle logistics, trucking, heavy logistics and enterprise supply chains.
It currently manages approximately 2,200 vehicles, with electric vehicles accounting for 20% of its fleet. The company plans to transition its entire fleet to electric by 2030. Hughes Services has also expanded into 10 additional Tier II cities, including Patna, Lucknow and Bhubaneswar, to tap growing demand from quick-commerce and consumer businesses.
FatakPay partners UGRO Capital for co-lending
Mumbai-based fintech platform FatakPay has partnered with UGRO Capital to expand access to formal credit through a co-lending arrangement. Under the partnership, FatakPay's NBFC subsidiary, FDPL Finance, and UGRO Capital will jointly extend instant personal loans to eligible salaried and self-employed individuals.
FatakPay will manage customer sourcing, digital onboarding and loan servicing, while UGRO Capital will provide credit underwriting, risk assessment and lending expertise. Both companies will jointly fund and manage the loan portfolio.
SquadStack, Bizom deploy Voice AI for FMCG retailers
SquadStack.ai and Bizom have deployed a Voice AI agent to capture orders from kirana and medical stores missed by field sales representatives. The solution contacts retailers, communicates product targets and ongoing trade schemes, builds confirmed orders and integrates them directly into Bizom's distribution platform.
The solution currently communicates in Hinglish and understands retailers' references to products through prices, packaging colours and local terminology. The companies said the technology recovers missed sales without replacing human sales representatives or increasing field headcount.
Usha Financial Services reports 120% growth in Q2 profit
Usha Financial Services Limited reported a 119.54% year-on-year increase in standalone profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 8.73 crore for the second quarter of FY27. Total income rose 50.81% to Rs 25.60 crore, while profit before tax increased 114.50% to Rs 11.41 crore. The company's gross loan book stood at Rs 502.76 crore as of September 30, 2026, registering 27.72% annual growth.
Its net worth increased 13.83% to Rs 246.45 crore. Asset quality remained stable, with gross non-performing assets at 2.70% and net NPAs at 2.08%. For the first half of FY27, PAT grew 79.84% to ₹16.76 crore, while total income increased 33.51% to ₹45.91 crore.
Pine Labs launches AI agents for merchant operations
Pine Labs has introduced two AI agents, Guide and Marketer Agent, under its Agentic Org platform to help small businesses manage operations and digital marketing. Integrated into the Pine Labs One merchant application, Guide enables merchants to access sales, payments, settlements, refunds and transaction information through conversational queries.
Marketer Agent helps businesses create advertising campaigns by handling keyword research, creative generation, audience targeting and campaign setup, initially across Google platforms. Merchants can review and approve campaigns before advertising expenditure is committed.
Fynd wins UK retail technology deal with N Brown
Mumbai-based retail technology company Fynd has partnered with UK retailer N Brown, which has selected its Boltic platform for integration and workflow automation. The partnership marks Fynd's first major retail customer acquisition in the UK since entering the market.
The platform will connect different business systems and automate workflows involving orders, customers, dispatches, returns, products and inventory. The integration is expected to improve operational visibility, reduce delays and enable faster customer service. Fynd, backed by Reliance Retail Ventures, serves around 20,000 stores and more than 2,600 brands and retailers globally.
INERA unveils new agricultural biosolutions for farmers
INERA, the agricultural biotechnology arm of Absolute, has unveiled a new range of crop solutions under its NAVODAYA 2026 launch programme. The portfolio includes BioMorphX, a patented enzyme-driven biostimulant designed to strengthen root development, Leiro Biostamin, a plant-based protein hydrolysate that helps crops withstand environmental stress, and XOVIO Milvaura, a biological fungicide targeting powdery and downy mildew.
The launches come amid challenging agricultural conditions, with India's southwest monsoon recording a 13% deficit. INERA currently reaches over two million farmers through 10,000 channel partners across 17 states.
Biz2X partners SIDBI to strengthen digital lending operations
Digital lending platform Biz2X has partnered with the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) to strengthen its lending operations through technology. Under the agreement, Biz2X will provide its lending CRM platform to streamline lead management, improve operational efficiency and enhance credit delivery to MSMEs.
The platform will integrate leads generated through WhatsApp, direct selling agents, OEM partners and marketing campaigns into a unified system. It will also provide AI-powered BizBot insights, management dashboards and mobile application capabilities for field teams.
Devnagri AI launches multilingual speech recognition solution
Enterprise language infrastructure company Devnagri AI has launched Blackbird, an automatic speech recognition solution designed to convert spoken conversations into text across Indian languages. The platform targets enterprise applications such as contact centres and AI-powered voice agents, with capabilities to handle regional accents, pronunciation variations and everyday speech patterns.
According to the company, Blackbird recorded word error rates of 10.8%-12.4% for Hindi, 10.1% for Punjabi and 11.8% for Bengali in tests using publicly available datasets. Its speech recognition latency is below 50 milliseconds, supporting real-time applications.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.text:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or significantly disturbing the information it contains.
The research, supported by FAPESP, was published in Physical Review B Letters. It was led by José Carlos Egues, a full professor at the São Carlos Institute of Physics at the University of São Paulo (IFSC-USP) in Brazil, and Yugui Yao of the School of Physics at the Beijing Institute of Technology in China. If experimentally confirmed, their method could simplify quantum computing by removing the need for extra qubits used in certain measurement techniques.
Why Measuring Quantum Information Is So Difficult
Conventional computers store information in bits that have one of two values, 0 or 1. These values can be checked repeatedly without changing the information. Quantum computers work differently because their qubits can exist in superpositions, meaning they can combine the states 0 and 1 in ways that are not possible with conventional bits.
This unusual ability is central to the potential power of quantum computing. However, it also creates a major vulnerability. Quantum states can be disrupted by interactions with their surroundings, including the instruments scientists use to examine them.
"In the conventional formulation of quantum mechanics, a projective measurement causes the system to assume one of the states associated with the measured quantity. Thus, if a qubit has been prepared in a certain superposition of 0 and 1, its direct measurement tends to destroy that superposition and, consequently, the information it contained," says Egues.
To minimize this problem, physicists developed techniques known as "quantum nondemolition measurements," or QND. Many of these approaches use an additional quantum system called an ancilla. Rather than measuring the original qubit directly, researchers transfer information to the ancilla and measure that auxiliary system instead.
The term "ancilla" comes from a Latin word meaning "slave" or "servant." In modern scientific usage, it describes something that performs a supporting function. Here, the ancilla acts as an intermediary, allowing researchers to obtain information while preserving the original qubit as much as possible.
Although effective, these procedures come with practical disadvantages. Scientists must prepare the auxiliary qubits, connect them to the qubits being studied, transfer information between them, and perform repeated measurements. These additional steps require time and equipment, and the complexity becomes increasingly significant as the number of qubits grows.
"Our strategy is different. Instead of transferring the information to an auxiliary qubit, we seek to obtain it from a signal produced by the qubit under study itself," says the researcher.
A Special Quantum Bit That Produces Its Own Signal
The proposed technique relies on the unusual properties of an Andreev qubit. Its name honors Soviet physicist Alexander Andreev (1939-2023), who identified a distinctive quantum process in 1964 that occurs where normal materials meet superconductors.
Superconductors are materials that can conduct electricity without electrical resistance under appropriate conditions. At the boundaries involving these materials, special quantum states known as "Andreev states" can form. In the system studied by the researchers, these states are confined to an extremely small region between two superconducting materials.
These quantum states can represent the basic values 0 and 1, along with superpositions of those values, making them suitable for storing quantum information.
"In the system under consideration, this region is a quantum dot - that is, a nanoscale structure in which electrons are spatially confined - formed in an indium arsenide [InAs] nanowire connected to superconducting materials on both sides. It's in this environment that the states characterizing the Andreev qubit are formed," Egues explains.
The key to the new approach is an electrical phenomenon called a "supercurrent." Unlike the current flowing through ordinary electrical conductors, a supercurrent moves without resistance.
The researchers found that when the Andreev qubit exists in a superposition, the supercurrent develops a component that oscillates over time. These fluctuations arise from quantum interference between the different states making up the superposition.
Crucially, the oscillations are not random. Their behavior contains information about the qubit's underlying quantum state, potentially allowing scientists to determine what that state is without directly measuring the qubit.
"It's precisely that property that we use to read the qubit. It's that supercurrent that lies at the heart of our proposal," the researcher points out.
How a Tiny Electrical Current Reveals Quantum Information
To understand how the technique works, it helps to consider how physicists describe a qubit's state mathematically.
One common representation is the "Bloch sphere," a geometric model in which every possible pure state of a single qubit corresponds to a point on the surface of a sphere. Two angles determine the location of that point.
The first angle describes how much each of the two basic states contributes to the superposition. The second describes their relative phase, which specifies how the quantum components are aligned with one another. Together, these two measurements provide the information needed to identify the qubit's state.
According to the new research, both pieces of information can be extracted from the supercurrent. Its steady component and the size of its oscillations reveal the relative contributions of the two basic states. Meanwhile, the timing of the oscillations provides information about their phase relationship.
"Our study showed that this information is encoded in the supercurrent itself. The supercurrent has a constant component and a fluctuating component. The value of the constant component and the amplitude of the oscillation reveal the proportion of each state (0 and 1) in the superposition, and the moment when that oscillation begins reveals the phase relationship between them. Thus, by measuring how the current varies over time, it's possible to reconstruct the initial state of the qubit," Egues explains.
This means the electrical current effectively carries a signature of the quantum information stored in the system. By observing how that signature changes over time, researchers could reconstruct the qubit's original state.
A Supercurrent That Oscillates Without Voltage
Another surprising feature of the proposed system is that the electrical current can oscillate without an externally applied voltage.
Ordinarily, producing an oscillating supercurrent in this type of superconducting system requires a voltage. This familiar phenomenon is called the "AC Josephson effect."
The researchers predict something different in their Andreev qubit. Here, the current's oscillations arise naturally from the qubit's own quantum evolution. No outside voltage is required to generate them.
"Our system generates a supercurrent that varies over time like an alternating current but without voltage. It's the very evolution of the qubit's state that produces that oscillation," says Egues.
This behavior is important because it transforms quantum activity occurring on an extraordinarily small scale into a detectable electrical signal. The current provides a connection between the microscopic world of quantum states and the larger physical systems scientists can measure.
That connection is what makes the proposed reading technique possible.
Detecting Quantum States With an Extremely Sensitive Sensor
The researchers envision placing the Andreev qubit inside a closed superconducting circuit, allowing its supercurrent to circulate continuously.
Next to the circuit would sit a SQUID (superconducting quantum interference device), a highly sensitive instrument capable of detecting extremely weak magnetic fields.
Whenever an electric current flows, it produces a magnetic field. Because the supercurrent in this system oscillates, the magnetic field it generates also changes over time.
The nearby SQUID could detect these tiny magnetic variations and use them to determine the behavior of the circulating current. Since the current contains information about the qubit's quantum state, the researchers could then reconstruct that state without measuring the qubit directly.
Egues compares the arrangement to two compasses that interact through a magnetic field.
"We can think of the qubit as one compass and the SQUID as another compass. The current in the circuit produces a magnetic field, and the SQUID 'senses' that field. Since the coupling between the two is very weak, the effect of the measuring instrument on the qubit tends to be very small."
The weak interaction between the sensor and the qubit is especially important. It offers a way to gather information while minimizing the disturbance that normally accompanies quantum measurements.
Reading Quantum Information With Almost No Disturbance
In quantum physics, observing a system is not necessarily a harmless process. A measuring instrument interacts with whatever it is attempting to measure, and that interaction can change the system's behavior.
This fundamental difficulty puzzled the earliest researchers studying quantum mechanics. It remains an unavoidable feature of quantum measurements today.
The proposed technique does not eliminate this effect entirely. The SQUID still interacts with the circuit, creating a small amount of feedback that can influence the qubit. However, the team's simulations suggest that this disturbance can be reduced to a level so small that it becomes effectively negligible.
"Our method doesn't eliminate the fundamental problem of quantum measurement. But it can approach the limit of a non-destructive readout and, at the same time, avoid the use of auxiliary qubits - the ancillas - employed in other non-destructive quantum measurement protocols," Egues notes.
The approach could also remove another complication found in some existing techniques. Because researchers would not need to restore the qubit to its original state after every measurement, they could make repeated observations as the state changes.
This would allow scientists to follow the qubit's quantum evolution over time, rather than obtaining information only through separate measurement and reset cycles.
Simulations Achieve Up to 99.85% Accuracy
To investigate whether the method could work outside ideal theoretical conditions, the researchers performed computer simulations designed to account for imperfections that would arise in real experiments.
These calculations included measurement noise, as well as the small amount of feedback introduced by the detection coil. The goal was to determine whether the qubit's state could still be reconstructed accurately despite these disturbances.
The results were encouraging. Depending on the number of measurements used, the simulations produced accuracies of 99.52%, 99.81%, and 99.85%.
According to the researchers, these values fall within the standard thresholds used in quantum error correction schemes, which are designed to manage errors in quantum information processing.
The findings suggest that the method could provide highly accurate quantum state reconstruction without the additional complexity of auxiliary qubits.
However, the technique has not yet been demonstrated experimentally. The results come entirely from theoretical analysis and computer simulations, so researchers still need to establish whether a physical device can achieve comparable performance.
Could This Make Quantum Computers Simpler?
Despite the lack of experimental confirmation, the researchers emphasize that their proposal does not depend on technologies that have yet to be invented.
The calculations use realistic properties drawn from existing quantum systems, and SQUID sensors are already established tools for detecting exceptionally weak magnetic fields and electric currents.
What remains to be built is the specific arrangement of components required to implement the proposed measurement technique.
"All the numbers we used are realistic. In principle, this can be achieved. In fact, we used parameters from existing systems in our calculations. What doesn't yet exist is that geometry, that setup that we proposed," he argues.
This makes the approach different from theoretical concepts that cannot be realized until scientists develop entirely new materials or manufacturing techniques. In principle, the necessary components already exist, although assembling them into the proposed configuration and demonstrating the predicted behavior remain important challenges.
The research offers two potentially significant advances.
From the standpoint of fundamental physics, it predicts that a qubit can produce an oscillating supercurrent resembling the AC Josephson effect, but without requiring an external voltage. Instead, the oscillations emerge from the qubit's own coherent quantum evolution.
From a technological perspective, the study shows how those oscillations could serve as a measurable signature of the qubit's internal state. By analyzing the electrical current, researchers could recover quantum information while causing very little disturbance to the system.
If future experiments confirm these predictions, the method could make reading Andreev qubits substantially simpler. Eliminating auxiliary qubits and repeated resets could reduce the equipment and procedures needed to retrieve quantum information.
More fundamentally, the work points toward an intriguing possibility: information hidden in the microscopic quantum world may be accessible through an electrical current produced by the quantum system itself, offering a promising new way to observe delicate quantum states without destroying them.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo. Original written by José Tadeu Arantes. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Xian-Peng Zhang, Chuanchang Zeng, Zhen-Biao Yang, Jose Carlos Egues, Yugui Yao. Andreev qubit readout from dynamic interference supercurrent. Physical Review B, 2026; 114 (8) DOI: 10.1103/6gkt-hghj
